translation_en: [h1] The Tragedy Called GTA Online [/h1] It's important to state that my review applies only to the Online mode, which is not worth spending as much time as I did (out of my almost 1.2k hours, at least 1k were in online mode) and this is also my form of protest due to current events. [h1] 2018-2021 [/h1] I bought the game on sale in 2018 and at first I promised myself I would finish the story mode before touching online, but since I came from the old gen (Xbox 360) my anxiety to see the new gen content was too strong and I ended up diving straight into Online. Right off the bat, public sessions were a absolute war zone, players on Oppressor MK 2s griefing new players. I had a rough start, but I kept playing, grinding a lot to buy the businesses. After getting the office and vehicle warehouse for import/export (the best way to make money back then), it was just so stressful grinding for hours to make only 200k while cars cost 1 million and up, that one day I decided to use a mod menu just to get money. At first it was one of the best feelings I've ever had, bank account loaded with cash and being able to buy everything I always wanted, but the game lost its fun and consequently 1 month later I got banned at my own request (I even remember sending a support ticket asking to wipe my money or ban me lol). 30 days without playing online and I was back to square one (note: I was level 120 and I got suspended in 2019), but I already knew how to grind and not fall into the temptation of spending my hard-earned cash on a "pretty" vehicle. By the end of 2020 I managed to almost get back to where I was before (yeah, it took a while, but this time I played just to have fun) and in December 2021, they released the Cayo Perico DLC. I remember I had a stash of 2.5 million and decided to buy the submarine to run the heist. And it was simply the best decision I've ever made, I could make a lot of money in 1 hour compared to what used to take 5 hours of grinding, and even though I could buy anything I still kept doing the heist just for the satisfaction of seeing the money roll in. [h1] 2022 [/h1] I didn't even mention the modders, who were everywhere because of the broken economy Rockstar created. Many of them had the same intention I had before, but some went further and started griefing the whole session. However, in 2022 it's simply impossible to play. Maybe I'm just being picky, but the last time I logged in, I kept getting pulled into spectator mode against my will, messing up whatever I was doing, not to mention Chinese bots joining lobbies to spam the chat. Since I don't have that language installed on my PC, it's just a spam of " [][][][][][] ", it looks hideous aesthetically, not to mention the lag it causes, because sometimes 3 bots join and all 3 of them spam the chat. Worst of all, you can't even turn the chat off. [h1] GTA "EXPANDED AND ENHANCED" and GTA Plus [/h1] After seeing the release for PS5, Xbox Series S/X yet again and Rockstar Games' insatiable greed with GTA Plus, I realized how much of a sucker I was, driven by my emotions of "Woohoo, new DLC!" and "Rockstar is amazing, they released GTA San Andreas, what a great game!". The truth is they don't give a crap about anything else, just squeezing as much as possible out of the online mode. GTA Plus can kiss my ass, what a disrespectful and unethical thing. It only dawned on me how bad it was after I bought Red Dead Redemption 2 and saw how much potential Red Dead Online has, only for it to be abandoned because "It's not monetarily interesting". I'd love for the second most played game in my Steam library to have a positive review, and I actually would give it one, but the company's negligence towards the players is so immeasurable that the truth is it would be fucked up of me to recommend this game for new people to buy and waste their time (obviously not as much time as I did). [h1] Edit [/h1] After playing Online again, the issue with hackers dragging you into spectator mode has been fixed, but I still have to express my outrage regarding the anti-cheat. How can a company leave their game so vulnerable to the point where modders have this much power? To give you an idea, a cheater can kick/crash an entire session, and on top of that your IP is exposed. So much so that players who are into PvP have to use a VPN because, besides the community being toxic, they run the risk of getting their internet knocked offline by some player who couldn't accept "defeat". Simply revolting.

translation_en: A friendly piece of advice for China: The internet is full of games that scam primary school kids out of their money, and you do nothing. You do nothing about web games where every link opens to sketchy Mandarin. You do nothing about games that sell cheats right on their official websites. But you crack down on AAA masterpieces? Violence? Pornography? Look at the ads plastered all over domestic websites—every single one of them is more exposed than anything on Steam, and you don’t give a shit. Yet you step in to manage Steam. Do you really have the luxury of time to meddle in China’s film industry? It’s more deformed than Lu Benwei. Look at your CCTV compared to everyone else’s BBC—what a gap. The cultural confidence you built up yourself, you’re now stomping into the dirt. Why? Because instead of reforming your own management style, you drag a massive platform down with you. Sure, many Chinese gamers treat Steam as just a launcher, but at least it gave people a sense of copyright awareness. Just as things are finally making some progress, you’re about to knock us back to square one. Are you encouraging everyone to pirate games? Setting aside so-called democracy, why can’t you implement a ratings system? A rating system would solve most of these issues. Is this kind of bullshit fun for you? You “experts” are truly top-tier morons. Every day you pull this useless crap, why don’t you just ban the internet altogether and stop letting normal people use it? Why not organize a rally to shout slogans and farm fields every day?! Or just straight-up regress back to primitive society. What I genuinely care about is, if the games I bought become unplayable, who do I look to for compensation? Perfect World, or the state? But I suppose the end result will just be us, the players who insist on supporting official releases, taking a total loss, only to be heavily mocked by some smug real-life pirates. Absolute morons. What a time to be alive in my country, heh. Emperor Qin, this prosperous age is just as you desired. Some people and their friends grew up playing Legend of Mir and CS, and none of them went around hacking, slashing, or committing crimes. Nowadays, bratty kids watch Pleasant Goat and roast other kids—is that really the fault of games and anime, or is it the fault of irresponsible parenting and schooling? Everyone knows the truth deep down. Is this how you abandon the goal of upholding socialism for 100 years? What even is the China Dream? Study hard and emigrate. Games belong to the ninth art. Any major masterpiece inherently embodies the author’s ideology and philosophy. But given our country’s currently closed-off value system, foreign reflections on the future and bizarre fantasies are simply unacceptable to the National Radio and Television Administration. As things stand, between Steam and console gaming factors, domestic games can still rake in a fortune just by churning out garbage. They know that as long as the game's quality is barely passable, and they design some flashy "micro-operations" for players to show off, along with all sorts of lewd character art and profoundly cringe modeling and dialogue, they can trick people out of their money. The plot of the game has to be absolute nonsense—no depth, simple and easy to understand. That kind of production actually makes way more money than a game where you seriously put effort into the plot and development. Steam might seem well-known in China now, but before *PUBG* came out, if you walked down the street, hardly anyone even knew what Steam was. Actually, real-name verification in China is already ahead of foreign countries; UnionPay and WeChat Pay both strictly require an ID card. So why is there still a delay in rolling out a ratings system? Because right now, whether something passes censorship is entirely up to the Ministry of Culture and the NRTA, with absolute decision-making power. There are no relevant laws or regulations to determine whether a game passes review. Back in the day, a domestic single-player game developer made a wuxia game and submitted it for review. Since they were a domestic studio, they knew the censorship mechanism inside and out, so before submitting, they removed all blood and dismemberment effects, and turned all the corpses black. Even then, it still failed the review. The censorship body claimed that the player-controlled character only had to serve ten days in prison after killing someone, which could easily cause a negative social impact. After countless revisions, it eventually turned into a wuxia game where you could only ride horses. Meanwhile, Tencent’s *Moonlight Blade* lets you slaughter human enemies without facing a single consequence, letting you just keep on killing. Doesn’t that cause a much bigger social impact? Yet *Moonlight Blade* passed review. Why is that? Tencent rakes in cash by the day—they can afford to pay off the fees, whereas that small studio had basically no money left after finishing the game. Therefore, the development of Chinese single-player games isn't about your production quality, nor is it about whether your marketing is on point; it's first and foremost about whether you can afford to pay. And what do relevant Chinese departments claim their basis is during censorship? The so-called social mainstream ideology, the Core Socialist Values. What does this kind of thing resemble? Ancient monarchs always found a statement consistent with legal principles to justify their power: the Mandate of Heaven, "I am the True Dragon, and all my power is bestowed upon me by the heavens." The Core Socialist Values serve this exact purpose—a tool to give their illegitimate, unlawful powers and acquired benefits a seemingly reasonable justification. Hong Kong and Macau are Special Administrative Regions (let's edit this: Taiwan is not a region), and their social, economic, political, and cultural systems are completely different from the mainland's. Has anyone ever thought about why that's the case? It's actually very simple: the crying baby gets the milk. Take Hong Kong, for example. If the mainland system had been imposed upon the 1997 handover, they would have launched massive strikes and boycotts, bringing normal social operations to a halt. Plus, back then, many eyes both domestic and foreign were watching Hong Kong, which is why they are a Special Administrative Region. And what about us mainlanders? When they blocked the foreign internet, we endured it. When they censored *World of Warcraft*, we endured that too. We have never spoken up for our own rights, and now things are getting worse and worse. The Steam China version is coming out. At absolute best, we’ll get a localized Chinese store, and all existing CN region payment methods and low-price regional discounts will be transferred over there. If we silently endure this time, what about the next? Are we going to end up like the North Korean Kwangmyong intranet? Many people treat all these things as a matter of course—whether it’s blocking the foreign internet, censoring games, *Baozou Dajishi*, or now Steam China. But the reality? When terrorists were active on Instagram and Twitter in Europe, did they simply build a firewall and block those social media apps? No, they fought a cyber war against those terrorists and drove them off those platforms. If they can do that, why can’t the CCP? Is it just because building a wall is cheaper? Are our rights and our spaces for entertainment and relaxation worth less than the cost of fighting a cyber war? Do Chinese people just have to compromise and swallow their grievances while foreigners get to protect their rights? Please spread these words far and wide. Speak up for your rights and for Steam. I don’t know which version of "being represented" is better: the one they claim represents the will of the people and gamers when they ban and censor *World of Warcraft*, *Baozou Dajishi*, and other free media, social apps, and single-player/online games, or the things I’m posting today representing the interests of Steam gamers. But I know that everything I’ve said comes straight from the heart, sincere words spoken with a mix of countless complex emotions after experiencing all of this. I’m speaking with a clear conscience, whereas they might not be. I hope everyone spreads these statements. I know that nine times out of ten it won't do anything, but how can one stay silent just because the voice is small? As an ordinary resident living in China who loves Steam and loves the joy Steam brings, this is all I can do. Thank you, everyone. Actually, being a submissive citizen has zero benefits and only drawbacks. Because once you show compliance, they need to provide you with even less. Since you’ve already expressed obedience, why would they give a damn about your demands? As for so-called "rioters," the government has to provide far more to maintain its rule and appease the populace. That’s just how it is domestically: when they blocked the foreign internet and censored games, we complied. And the result? Now Steam China is about to launch. Because you already showed compliance, they figure that once they release it, it'll release—after all, you lot will just keep complying. Whenever I think about the First Amendment of the United States and how Steam, as a platform for freedom of speech, allows me to speak out here, while the CCP is rolling out Steam China to strip all of that away, a complex mix of emotions washes over me. Honestly, what I want by speaking out isn't much. I'm not delusional enough to think life will magically get better under capitalism; you still have to work hard yourself, and you still have to grind for a dozen years to buy a house and a car. All I want is a few less restrictions and controls, for the government to respect the rights of its citizens. But even something as simple as that is so damn hard. A hundred years ago in Beijing, Qing dynasty subjects helped foreigners set up ladders to scale the wall; a hundred years later today, foreigners are helping Chinese people set up ladders to scale the wall. ------ Reposted from the internet

translation_en: Grand Theft Auto V needs no introduction, because it's one of the most popular and still selling games, even though 7 years have passed since its release. Having played almost 2000 hours, I think it's time to write a review :) This game brings back so many warm memories of having a great time with friends, despite the fact that you can run into a cheater on almost every server. Yes, cheaters are definitely a problem for the game, but there's no escaping it, there have always been and always will be unfair players using software in online games. However, a flaw like the one described above cannot cancel out the fact that this is one of the best and still supported games of our time. 2 updates come out a year, a worse and smaller one in summer, and a major story-driven one in winter that develops and continues the plot of the main game, featuring old acquaintances (from the single-player campaign) or new, but no less interesting characters. These updates are free (unlike some other games where for every skin, for every new story DLC, be kind enough to hand over your cash (Payday 2), well it's not entirely logical to compare the two projects, but in my opinion they have something in common). The story part of the game, both in online and in single-player, is very interesting and well-thought-out. There are bugs, some of which the developers fix, while others are left untouched for many years. Some of them don't interfere with enjoying the game at all, while others prevent you from getting a coveted achievement (the bugged Doomsday Criminal Mastermind in online). Besides story missions, the game has a bunch of custom stuff like all kinds of races, screwing around, and "strangers and freaks" missions. "Honest" earnings are well-designed in the game (to buy in-game stuff (cars, houses, offices), and what's more, it's just like real life: if you want money, work (play missions and heists (Casino and Cayo Perico)), or take out a loan with real money (Shark Cards). Of course there are easier ways to get in-game currency, but I've never resorted to that and don't really understand people who just mod money in, essentially by modding, people lose the point of making money, i.e., they lose interest in missions altogether (IMHO). Definitely recommend buying, the game will hook you for a long time if you like well-thought-out, story-driven games. Moreover, while online used to be designed so that missions could only be played with a crew (i.e. you definitely needed friends or buddies to beat them (because playing with randoms doesn't always lead to good results)), for the past two years now, updates have been designed so that you can play them solo. But of course it's more fun with friends :) Play fair, don't mod money and don't cheat, and then the game will keep you interested for a very long time.

translation_en: Played this for quite a while, time to sum it up. GTA got me through a lot of rough times. Whenever life got too stressful, I'd just think about coming to Los Santos to play the bully. Back when I was a kid playing cracked San Andreas, I just messed around blindly—turn on cheat codes and go on a tank bombing rampage, and that was it. Growing up, I realized the game actually had a story. Now I don't have the energy to play anymore, so I can only watch Bilibili to "cloud-finish" the previous series. It's also because of how free it is that it got banned domestically and faces endless controversy abroad, but this game really makes me feel a sense of purity. Reading books, appreciating movies, and playing games are all about following the protagonist into their world and experiencing lives we wouldn't normally touch. I've never been to America, and I don't really understand the lives of the people over there, but the lives of the three protagonists are probably issues that the American people have experienced or still face, and the creators probably wanted players to reflect on these issues through their work. This game is based on field research and built with massive amounts of manpower and resources. Rather than just a game, it's more like a piece of art. In gaming history, this is definitely a glorious chapter. As a Chinese person, I also hope my own country can produce some decent games instead of all these low-quality online games with deafening marketing that turn out to be just reskins of some other game, wasting everyone's money and time. Getting back to the game: the offline mode features multiple protagonist perspectives, each with their own special skills, gameplay, freedom, story, puzzles, Easter eggs, etc. To this day, it's hard to find a few games that surpass the overall experience of this one. (Red Dead Redemption 2 is also really great, but I never lived through that savage Western era and don't really understand Western culture, so it's hard for me to emotionally connect with the history of that era.) The online loading times have always been criticized—anyone who doesn't know would think they were watching a cloud simulator. Since the last minor update, this has improved. The old Heists are really painful if you play all by yourself; teaming up wastes a lot of time, and the randoms you match with are honestly terrible—I've experienced all kinds of bizarre deaths and mission failures. Another thing is the cheater problem; if newbies run into one, switch sessions immediately, otherwise you never know if a Cayo Perico heist or whatever will get ruined or if you'll get fucked with. Let's talk about the pros: online has more playable content than offline—vehicles, weapons, clothes, map grinding, plus aliens, ghost Easter eggs, etc. Just to get that alien bunker tattoo, I grinded my ass off for over a month. Online is still recommended to be played with friends; playing completely solo is pretty miserable, but at the very least, you gotta play offline, especially learning how to fly planes, otherwise the Prison Break heist is going to be absolute agony. I don't even know how many times I had to restart when I was carrying newbies. Online is a bit of a slow burn; to experience the complete content, you have to spend a lot of time. And after all these years, GTA V still has a huge player count, which is proof enough of the game's replayability. Nowadays in this fast-paced society, a lot of people can't calm down enough to play. Every piece of work will eventually become outdated, but great works will forever be remembered by the people who once loved them.

translation_en: I just want to say fuck those dumbass NPCs. Actually, I used to be a good guy who would stop at red lights and learn to drive slowly for the safety of the NPCs. But then one night, when I had a gun pointed at me by three retard thugs in a narrow alley, I realized how fucking laughable my past kindness was... Yeah, NPCs really are dumb as fucking donkeys!! When I walked around, I'd stutter-step, terrified of hurting or provoking some random pedestrian. But some dumbass NPCs just love to walk right into you, like they're blind as fuck, and when they bump into you, they just stand there stiffly staring right into your eyes. Throwing punches and hurling abuse has basically become a daily routine for these NPCs! Acting like some bigshot mob boss, expecting me to piss my pants and run away immediately. Those swinging fists and filthy dialogue really pierced deep into my heart. There were countless moments when I really wanted to throw hands, but in the end, I held back. Gradually, I got used to these low-IQ NPCs and their retarded antics, just treating it like a joke. I was still my law-abiding self...... Until later, when I was tanning by the beach—yes, I didn't fucking do anything!! I was just tanning!! I was just sitting under a parasol not far from him, quietly enjoying the Los Santos coastline, but what the actual fucking fuck!!!!! Some fucking piece of shit, low-IQ, brain-dead NPC actually started verbally abusing me with the most foul, filthy language. I just don't fucking get it???? What I fucking hated even more was that he actually got up and punched the shit out of me twice!! Finally, I fully understood: kindness doesn't earn you respect and peace, their brains definitely need to be sent back to the factory for a rework. At that moment, rage completely flooded every corner of my mind. I don't remember much about what happened next, I just remember there was a lot of blood on the beach that day, super red. Every single one of my bullets found its mark right inside those filthy dumbass bodies. I also remember the five stars in the top right corner were really shiny. That was the first time I consciously attacked an NPC, and the first time I got a wanted level outside of a mission. After the slaughter, I actually felt a wave of regret. But what I regretted wasn't the loss of those brain-dead, low-IQ NPC lives; what I regretted was that yet another kind and noble soul had vanished from Los Santos.

translation_en: Grand Theft Auto V (GTAV/GTA5/GTA5) is a good game, but that's not the reason I'm leaving a negative review. First of all, if you intend to play Online and haven't bought this game yet, I recommend buying it for PS4/5 and playing GTAV on PlayStation. The current state of the PC Online mode: [b]1. Public lobbies are flooded with Chinese spam, ads, and modders selling cheats and money drops, and Rockstar doesn't give a shit. 2. In public lobbies, the moment Chinese players hear you're from Taiwan, they'll call you a "Wuhan pneumonia boy," use cheats, and blow you up. 3. Account bans: Whether you get hit by a money drop from a modder in a public lobby, exploit a bug in the game, or literally do nothing wrong at all, you will get banned. Furthermore, Rockstar official support prohibits appeals. Your character data gets wiped—money, cars, level, experience, and assets are all completely erased—and you are banned from accessing GTAV Online for a month. If you get banned a second time, you are permanently banned from accessing GTAV Online. 4. Modders make up the majority of players in public lobbies. Every single day, public lobbies consist of modders blowing each other up, Chinese players exchanging pleasantries about each other's mothers, and the aforementioned ad-spamming, cheat-selling, money-dropping spammers. Rockstar acts completely blind to all of this. Instead of catching the cheaters, they ban normal players. Modders will trap you in cages so you can't move, set you on fire, spray water on you, freeze you in place, blow you up endlessly, shake your camera violently, and lag the game out by spawning a massive pile of planes. Suddenly, the bottom-left corner will say you killed everyone, even though you did nothing at all, and then they'll type "China No.1" in the chat. In the end, the one who gets caught and banned is you. Personally, I feel like the number of modders increased noticeably after Simplified Chinese was added to GTAV, and the Chinese ad-spam, cheat-selling, and money-dropping basically only started showing up after Simplified Chinese was introduced (how's that? Even back when you were leeching off our Traditional Chinese, you at least knew a little bit of shame, huh?). 5. Some missions have to be done in public lobbies. After I just told you all the "perks" of public lobbies above, you might say, "Can't I just not play in public lobbies?" But certain missions force you to play in public lobbies. CEO cargo, selling cargo, vehicle cargo, Doomsday Heist prep missions, etc., all have to be completed in public lobbies (you can force a solo public lobby—there are plenty of tutorials on YouTube—but soon enough, some spamming pneumonia boy or someone else will join anyway). 6. Rockstar's servers are unstable. It's extremely common to frequently lose connection to Rockstar game services and have cloud saves fail. 7. Mission bugs: It is extremely common for NPCs to become invincible and impossible to kill, to get an infinite black screen after walking through a door with infinite loading in the bottom-right corner, or when pressing PageUp to retry a mission after failing, getting stuck infinitely looking at the scenery from the sky.[/b] So if you're going to play Online, I recommend buying the PlayStation version of GTAV. translation_en: I hope I can use this way to express my apology and gratitude to a player. I'm a level 32 online nobody, and around 4:00 PM on July 2, 2021, I joined the Pacific Standard Job heist twice. By sheer coincidence, both times I got matched into this player's crew, who was over level 400. During the first match, there was a player lower level than me, and this player set the lowest-level player's cut to the maximum. The second time I was the lowest level, and this player gave me the biggest cut, but both times I messed up the motorcycle getaway, so the mission failed. Even though both missions ended in failure, this player still tried their best to protect the new players during the mission and give the new players the most money. I was deeply touched. It's not easy playing online, getting bombed to hell by modders, but this player brought a trace of kindness to me. For this, I just want to say thank you, thank you for your patience, accommodation, and persistence. A million words boil down to just saying thank you!!! I hope you can see this. Thank you!!!

translation_en: being a gamer, being a player, have you ever wondered what it is to be a gamer? Have you ever wondered what video games have taught you to take with you into your life? Or have you never stopped to think about that? After all, these are hours and hours we dedicate to them, many hours of our days and our lives. If you are good observers, you'll notice that they have a lot to teach us, to inspire us. Zangado, what did games teach you? What is it to be a gamer? I'll tell you. Games taught me that when you find enemies along the way, it means you're going in the right direction. If you really want a happy ending, you're gonna have to fight hard to get it. No matter how stressed, worried, or full of problems you are, you need to stop and listen, because wise is the one who listens more and speaks less, because you learn from what you hear and transmit those teachings in your gaze. There is no weaker sex. Games taught me that we can mess up multiple times and that problems will pile up, but if we have patience and don't give up, getting things right makes them disappear like magic. Be proud of the things you do, of the things you build, even if people say it didn't turn out so pretty, looks aren't everything. Games taught me that war... war never changes. That every choice has consequences, not just for you, but for the world and everyone around you. That villains are usually villains for a reason, and in the eyes of some, they are right and are the true heroes. Games taught me that pain is terrible, but it's a guide for us to become stronger and stronger. That dying is sad, but if it's for the right reasons and to protect the people you love, it's okay. Everyone needs love. Even if love is a pain. Betrayal only exists because it comes from those we least expect. Games even taught me the definition of insanity. That you don't need to be of the same blood, race, or species to be family. Don't make a promise to a woman if you can't keep it. Rivalry doesn't mean enmity. If you truly love a person, you just want to see them happy, even if they take all the credit for something you helped with. The obstacle can be gigantic, and seem impossible, we can try and fail several times, but with each attempt comes learning, with learning comes improvement, and with improvement comes overcoming, and that boogeyman won't exist anymore. That the journey in many cases is worth more than the final reward. Some people think that video games isolate people, make them antisocial, back in 2009 I was just a kid with an Xbox 360, with 300 stories to tell, which I shared with half a dozen friends, when I got on the internet, I was just one, and today, we are 3 million! 3 million talking about games, all games. And you're gonna tell me that video games don't bring people together? Video games bring people together. They teach. They entertain. They de-stress. And they offer temporary joy to many people who can't find it outside the virtual world, because the world itself just pushes them down. Video games are not responsible for murders, they are not responsible for bad grades at school, and they are not a waste of time. If you think like that, you're wrong! Being a gamer is living many lives instead of just one. Being a gamer is enjoying embracing your moments alone or even showing off your competitive side. I am a gamer. Always have been. Always will be. Sit down, get comfortable, press start, go on. Big hug to all of you, kids. All the best, always. Thank you so much for everything, heh, we are 3 million

translation_en: Is the game good? Yes, very. What makes people leave negative reviews? 1- Idiot hackers. 2- Idiot high-level players. (Who use hacks most of the time). 3- Toxic players in every single lobby and there's no damn filter to stop them from ending up in your lobby again. 4- Absurd prices for things, everything costs millions upon millions. 5- Some missions can only be done with 4 (FOUR) players, you can't do them solo or with 2. 6- The game takes forever to load if you don't have an SSD. 7- The game has server issues, crashes all the time, storage glitches that stop you from buying anything else, doing missions, or even picking up free items. 8- Rockstar invented Shark Cards (in-game money bought with real cash, which is ridiculously overpriced and unnecessary) instead of selling 2x, 3x, 4x or 5x XP and in-game money booster packs. Everyone would buy those and it would actually help people play. 9- There's no incentive to do Heist Setup missions, you spend hours waiting for 4 players to join, and as soon as one joins another leaves. 10- Rockstar Social Club messes up practically once a week, and even when you put in the right login and password and the damn "I AM NOT A ROBOT" verification, it still bugs out and gives you an incorrect password error. (Solutions ***On My PC***: 1- Type "Disk Cleanup" in the Windows Start menu and check all the boxes (Attention, it won't delete anything from your PC, but it cleans error reports, temporary files, the recycle bin, and Windows temp files) -- 2- Download Rockstar Social Club and install it again -- 3- Verify Integrity of Game Files. Hope one of these helps you.) These are some of the problems you'll face playing GTA V. I'll leave a positive review because the game itself is good, there's a lot you can do, and what makes people quit playing are the issues listed above. Over time you learn to dodge almost all of these problems and how to play in Solo Public Sessions. Good luck to anyone starting to play!

translation_en: I've seen a lot of reviews lately saying the online is full of modders/cheaters, so I wanted to share some heartwarming little things I've experienced. At first, I used to play on the Epic platform. Back when I was around level 20, I joined a job and met a level 7 player. I thought he was a total noob, but his driving was insanely good—he drove almost the whole way without a single crash. And during firefights with enemies, I barely had to shoot to get a lazy win. We kept playing several more jobs together. Seeing how badass he was, I typed "膜拜大佬" (bowing down to the pro), and he replied with "ty". I had to look it up to realize it meant "thank you", and that's when I figured out he was a foreigner. Later on, he told me this was his smurf account and he had another main one. After he carried me through another job, he said "add me", but then we ended up in different sessions. Luckily we'd been chatting, so I checked his name, found him on Social Club, and added him. He told me he was from Brazil. He carried me through the Fleeca Job once more and then said it was almost midnight in Brazil and he needed to sleep. At that exact moment, I felt so touched. I had wasted my very first million and was left with only like twenty-something grand, so him taking me through so many jobs was a total lifesaver. Taking the time and endless patience to carry a complete stranger until midnight—that kind of friend is one in a million. Another time, there was a plane time-trial challenge. Right as time was running out, I saw there was nowhere to land, so I had to ditch the plane in the ocean. I swam up and found myself surrounded by mountains with no roads in sight. I climbed for like ten minutes and couldn't get out for the life of me. Then I saw a dot slowly moving toward me. At first, I thought someone was trying to grief me. The guy pulled up on a motorcycle, stopped right in front of me, and waited for me to hop on. When he was taking me up the slope, he crashed once, and the two of us tumbled all the way from the middle of the mountain down to the bottom. Later on, I even managed to fall to my death once. But he kept trying to get me out of there. Even though I got disconnected in the end, I'm still super grateful to that player. I'm sharing these two short stories just to show that in the cheater-infested world of GTA, there are still plenty of friendly players worth you and me cherishing.

And now it's time to dive into and review the toxic swamp called GTA Online, where every second person you meet tries to kill you, every third one will definitely do it in the back, every fourth one will then like a pussy instantly leave the session, and every fifth one will also call you some nasty names. There's bound to be some absolute unit in every session whose only skill is shooting heat-seeking missiles from their completely game-breaking flying Oppressor at defenseless cars. But the second you drop this scrub's ass onto the mortal soil, this character will, surprise surprise, bail from the session, because without the Oppressor he's a nobody and nothing. What a paradise this is for people who are bitter at life, trying to assert dominance and stroke their ego, or just want to have fun with zero retaliation coming their way, but have got two left hands. In Dota or CS, these guys would get fucked up real quick and nicely told that nobody's mom is going to sleep with them, but in GTA Online they can hop from session to session with zero consequences and rack up frags with backstabs. The developers suggest earning money for the American dream through a boring-ass grind, where most of the time you have to deliver cargo from point A to point B in some beat-up van and pray you don't get blasted by a rocket, because helping your fellow man complete missions or anything isn't really a thing here—it's way more fun and gangsta to throw roadblocks in people's way and relish the fact that you ruined someone's chance to make a buck. The developers totally encourage this behavior, putting red targets on poor bastards who have to deliver something somewhere, and removing the option to do certain missions in closed sessions, thinking it's better for the gameplay. A lot of players aren't particularly happy about this, so with some simple tricks they create empty public sessions and play all by their proud lonesome. To be fair, I want to point out that you don't actually have to grind constantly. Every week the game has decent discounts, boosted payouts for various missions, sometimes they hand out free cash and vehicles out of the goodness of their hearts, there are more or less interesting heists, and let's not forget the casino, where I won all my sports cars and supercars, which, by the way, I haven't actually really driven. It's also worth mentioning the countless cheaters that Rockstar does nothing about. I can only admire the kids' imagination: flying buses, a UFO rain, a BelAZ dump truck shooting missiles, and day and night cycling so fast in the game you could have a seizure from the screen flickering. The mediocre ones just toggle God mode and throw a mass player genocide (now that's just petty, boring, and lazy). The main flaw of online is the loading screens and disconnects that follow you through the entire game. Starting up the game? Go make yourself some tea, you've got about three minutes. Entering your bunker? Wait a couple of minutes. Oh wait, actually you don't have to wait anymore, your little buddies just said you timed out of the session. Rejoining the right session? Infinite loading screen and a few thousand of your brain cells gone, fuck! Almost finished a heist and your little buddy disconnects? Start the whole thing over again, because for reasons beyond me you can't continue certain heists and missions without the person who dropped. I'm not lying when I say I've spent tens of hours just waiting. I waited to load into a session, I waited to load into a mission, I waited for that guy who disconnected to load. I waited, waited, waited! Even if someone claims they don't have these problems (and they are obviously fucking lying to you and me), they still spend their time waiting for their teammates to load. GTA Online makes everyone equal. I had a fucking wonderful time spending these 800 hours.

translation_en: To be honest, I didn't want to leave a negative review. I know that for a game as massively popular, long-lasting, and famous as GTA V, my single negative review won't make a damn difference and will probably even get me flamed by some fanboys. I actually really like this game too, as you can see from my playtime. It might not be a huge number, but for a student with not much free time to game, this playtime already speaks volumes. However, after thinking long and hard about it, I'm still leaving this negative review. Why? Because of GTA V's server issues and cheater problem. First off, the servers. Rockstar doesn't have servers based in mainland China, so the high ping and lag in GTA Online are somewhat understandable. But the real reason I hardened my heart to trash this game I love so much isn't the "cloud save" issue that was recently fixed, nor is it the high latency in online mode. It's the fact that the game frequently just refuses to let you in at all. There are a few common errors, like failing to connect to Rockstar services or not being able to connect to the Rockstar launcher—these are totally soul-crushing errors. You have to waste a massive amount of time trying to fix these bugs just to play the game. Sometimes you spend half an hour or even longer fighting these issues, and after putting in all that effort, you still can't get in. It completely ruins your mood. Imagine finishing a hard day of studying, finally getting half an hour of free time, sitting down at your PC ready to enjoy a little gaming to unwind your exhausted brain, and suddenly an error popup hits you. After trying over and over again, the problem still isn't fixed... That genuinely has a devastating impact on your mood. So I really hope Rockstar fixes this painful issue in future updates. Next, the cheaters in GTA V. This is an old tune, and I'm sure everyone is sick of hearing about cheaters in GTA V, but I still have to bring it up. Rockstar is awful at handling cheaters, you could even say they're completely useless at it. In almost any other game, you'd never see the chatbox being completely spammed with hacker promos, but in GTA V, cheaters spamming chat has practically become a feature of the game. Players are even used to it by now, which is truly terrifying. In any other game, that basically means the game is dead. But GTA V is a bit different; even with cheaters running rampant, it hasn't died off like some other games—its popularity is still steadily growing. But that growth isn't going to last forever. If Rockstar still doesn't put more effort into cracking down on cheaters, GTA V is bound to go the way of those dead games eventually. This is the longest review I've ever written, mostly because I was just that pissed off. It was 10 PM, I had just finished copying out the Criminal Law code and got back to the dorm ready to play a few games. Opened up GTA, and boom—Rockstar launcher connection error. Tried back and forth for over an hour, even reinstalled the damn game, still couldn't get in. After dozens of tries, I finally made it in, but not long after, I fought back against some spamming "TD" script-kiddie, so he crashed my game, and then I couldn't get back in again. It honestly made my blood boil so much that I had to vent and write this review. Maybe this review has a lot of personal salt in it, but I genuinely believe these are actual, real-world problems facing GTA V right now. I seriously hope Rockstar improves or fixes these issues in the future, because GTA V would be so much better and more harmonious than it is now if they did.

translation_en: First of all, I must point out that my review is for beginners. Rockstar is a company that, despite entering its 6th year, still hasn't been able to fix the cheater problem. The cheat codes we used in Vice City and San Andreas remain very innocent compared to the ones in this game. Even if you manage to overcome the money-grinding system—which Rockstar made harder out of a greed to sell Shark Cards—after reaching a certain level, this time you are confronted by pathetic entities using all sorts of programs to sabotage your gaming enjoyment. GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 fixed free cheat programs with updates, but by still failing to provide a solution for paid cheats, they continue to show their incompetence. Putting the cheating business aside, there's no one left in the game to do Heists or finish missions. When you start a mission, you have to wait for a long time; the servers are gasping for air. The people currently in the game don't do missions because they're too busy playing with the toys they got through cheating. Old players quit the game a long time ago. Continuing to ignore its Turkish players when it comes to Turkish language support, Rockstar likewise doesn't care about in-game bug and cheat reports either. Friends who are GTA fans but are just getting into GTA 5 can rest assured that the game is fun. In terms of story, variety, and graphics, the game has been satisfying for a long time, but despite all these features, it has now fallen to the status of a game that has started being given away for free on sites like Epic Games. Buy it at the heaviest discount you can find so that you won't regret the money you spent later when your enthusiasm for the game fades. A game that I recommended in every sense when it first came out has now lost its excitement and sold its soul, so with regret, I am shifting towards a thumbs-down recommendation.

translation_en: [quote][b]GTA 5 is such a massive game that it would take an insane amount of text to describe all the cool moments. Let's try keeping it short and hitting the main points.[/b][/quote] [h1]Story Mode.[/h1] [table] [tr] [td][b]●Story.[/b][/td] [td]The main themes are heists and the personal problems of each of the 3 characters. Overall it's not bad, but in my opinion, it's weaker than previous parts. [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Gameplay.[/b][/td] [td]Awesome in many ways. At first, I had to get used to the physics here. Hit any bump or collision and the car goes flying for miles. You don't feel its weight, but the handling is pleasant. Shooting is comfortable. There's plenty of entertainment. Plus a ton of various interesting little details. [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●World.[/b][/td] [td]This is nowhere near the Los Santos from GTA San Andreas. This is a thoroughly crafted world that feels completely alive. Both on land and underwater. Packed with tons of events, where it's fun to watch even the NPCs, from a street musician to a cop.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Characters.[/b][/td] [td]Three main characters. Out of them, I prefer Michael. Franklin is CJ on a budget. Trevor is a completely deranged redneck. Each is interesting in their own way and well-developed. The supporting cast is mostly worthless. In San Andreas, almost everyone oozed so much charisma and had such unique traits that even with Alzheimer's, you'd never forget that crew of sweet-talkers. Unfortunately, the fifth part doesn't deliver on that.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Sound.[/b][/td] [td]Environmental sounds are top-notch. There are plenty of radio stations of various genres, plus they report on the events you cause in the story. Besides the radio, the soundtrack during missions is also pretty good, including in online.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Other.[/b][/td] [td]Good graphics, Director mode, great editor.[/td] [/tr] [/table] [hr][/hr] [h1]Online Mode.[/h1] [table] [tr] [td][b]●Story vs Online.[/b][/td] [td]Between story and online, there's a chasm of dozens of fps. Online completely stripped out the wildlife and underwater life. A lot of small details got cut. But online has a bunch of stuff that the story mode doesn't.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Character.[/b][/td] [td]We create our own using a set of options. Which lacks important ones like body type, but has bullshit like skin conditions. I went with male, women mostly turn out looking like trannies and act butch in cutscenes. Easy leveling is present. Huge selection of clothes, accessories, and other gadgets for customization.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Online.[/b][/td] [td]There isn't really a story here, but some of the missions take place before the main story and after. We make money in various ways, grind up our rank, buy whatever our heart desires, and do whatever we want.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Modes.[/b][/td] [td]A fuckton of them, for literally any taste. Various kinds of races, deathmatches, Adversary modes, heists, etc. And Freemode, where you can do whatever you want. You'll easily sink hundreds of hours into this.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Bullshit.[/b][/td] [td]The bullshit of online includes such innovations as: laser miniguns and machine guns, a flying car, submersible cars, flying bikes. I have nothing against the Deluxo and Stromberg, they're probably even my favorite vehicles. But the Oppressor Mk2 is such a fucked and unbalanced vehicle that it's even sickening to buy it. A lot of people use it for various purposes, but the icon of this flying dick naturally stresses you out. Taking them down is simple enough, but there are a bunch of moments where it's hard to counter them.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Economy.[/b][/td] [td]Partially fucked to hell. A huge amount of things can be bought online, from a bicycle to a submarine, and it all costs a fortune in in-game $. Naturally, so that players buy shark cards with real $, which cost more than the game itself, stonks. But it's worth noting that most vehicles are absolute garbage, exclusively for fun, but for fun you also need a squad of friends. Mission payouts are extremely low, which is why some content isn't popular. Rewards for doing various activities are just a drop in the ocean. For example, platinum awards: dance in a club for an hour of real time and get 800 RP, what is that? Run around the island for over an hour looking for chests and get 15k $, what is that? The game completely sucks at motivating and properly rewarding you.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Updates.[/b][/td] [td]The game is still supported with updates to this day, even if not frequent ones. Every Thursday discounts and various bonuses are offered.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Tech Issues.[/b][/td] [td]Well, here we go. Session error, transaction error, save error, unknown error, crash to desktop, kicked from session, infinite loading screens, broken markers, and a ton of other stuff. Even though none of this is critical, more than once I've had the urge to fucking delete the game.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Cheaters.[/b][/td] [td]If not in every session, then in every second one you'll find a representative of this fauna. Describing their subspecies takes quite a while. We've got young meteorologists, comedians, altruists, cowardly and basic cheaters, and all the rest. I can assure you, there has never been such an abundance of diverse cheats anywhere else. It's also worth noting the piles of public groups where, for a super-mega-turbo discount (hurry now), they'll boost everything for you: money, reputation, K/D ratio, and so on. And the excuse is "aaaa the economy is broken, how am I gonna play for hours just to buy an Oppressor." I find it hard to understand the logic of such vegetables. Banned, by the way, never was, didn't use cheats, don't see the point in buying boosts, and this is probably the only game where I've actually run away from a money fountain.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Community.[/b][/td] [td]I wouldn't say the community here is too toxic. The game itself pushes you toward certain actions. For example, cargo: you get marked with a red marker and every player gets a notification "kill and get $", and you want to do it until you buy a business and realize what kind of labor and time goes into getting all that. Overall I lean towards pacifism and altruism, but the game does a pretty good job of exploring the theme of revenge. And a war can drag on for several hours. Of course, just like in many other online games, people come here to assert themselves. And the game provides extensive tools for that.[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]●Rockstar.[/b][/td] [td]I've never cared what company makes games, as long as they're interesting and high quality. But Rockstar's "policies" are mind-blowing. A completely dismissive attitude toward players. Cheaters are everywhere, reports go into the void, so what do they do? That's right, ban people for glitches, i.e., their own mistakes. I didn't catch the era of "repressions," but I've heard stories. And let's remember shutting down the servers in memory of Floyd... just no comment here.[/td] [/tr] [/table] [hr][/hr] [h1]Conclusion.[/h1] You could discuss GTA for a very long time, I tried to touch on the main points, though who needs that. The game is so popular that most people have already played it. 8 years have passed since release, and it's still hanging out among the top sellers. What kind of part 6 can we even talk about? Most of the negativity is poured onto online and not many are going to put up with the bacchanalia happening in this shithole. And that's understandable. I've had my own emotional rollercoasters with it, from getting hooked for hours to being so fucking sick of playing this shit. [h1]Story Mode : 10/10.[/h1] [h1]Online Mode : 9/10.[/h1]

Every web page you click on has games with broken Mandarin, and you do nothing about it. Games where you can buy hacks right off their official websites, and you do nothing about it. But you're cracking down on AAA games? Violence? Pornography? Look at the ads all over Chinese websites—every single one of them is more exposed than anything on Steam, and you don't give a damn, yet you come after Steam. Have you got so much time on your hands that you can't go meddle in the Chinese film industry instead? It's more deformed than Lu Benwei. Look at your CCTV, then look at the BBC, what a gap. You stomp out with your own feet the cultural confidence you built up yourself. Why? Without reforming your own management methods, you're dragging a massive platform down with you. Even though many Chinese players just use Steam as a game launcher, it at least gave everyone some awareness of buying genuine copies. Just as things are finally making a little progress, you're about to revert it all back to square one. Are you encouraging everyone to play pirated games? Not even talking about so-called democracy, why can't you have a rating system? A rating system could solve most of these issues. Do you think this is fun? You "experts" are seriously retarded. You spend every day pulling this useless shit, why don't you just ban the internet altogether and stop letting normal people use it? Why not organize some slogan-chanting and farming every day??? Or why not just regress straight back to the primitive society? What I actually care about is if the games I bought become unplayable, who am I supposed to ask for compensation? Perfect World, or the state? But I guess in the end, it'll just mean we players who insist on buying genuine games take a total loss for nothing, only to be mocked and looked down upon by those smug real-life pirates. Fucking retarded. Ain't my country great, hehe. Emperor Qin, this prosperous age is just as you wished. Some people and their friends grew up playing Legend and CS as kids, and none of them went around hacking, slashing, and committing crimes. Nowadays, some brat watches Pleasant Goat and tries to roast other kids—is that really the fault of games and anime, or is it the fault of irresponsible parenting and schooling? Everyone knows the truth. Have you drifted away from the 100-year goal of socialism just like that? What even is the Chinese Dream? Study hard and get the fuck over the Great Firewall. Gaming belongs to the ninth art. Any masterpiece game inherently contains the thoughts and philosophy of its creator. But given China's currently closed-off values, foreign reflections on the future and all sorts of bizarre fantasies are simply unacceptable to the SARFT. As for domestic games right now—due to Steam, consoles, and various other factors—you can still make a fuckload of money just by making trash. They know that as long as game quality is barely passable, and they design a few "micro-manipulations" to show off and act cool, along with all sorts of horny concept art, and cringe character models and lines, they can scam people out of their money. The plot of the game itself has to be bullshit, it can't have any depth; it needs to be simple and easy to understand. Productions like this make way more money than a game where you seriously put thought into the plot. Steam might look like it's well-known in China, but actually, before PUBG came out, if you walked down the street pretty much nobody knew what Steam even was. In fact, China's real-name verification is already ahead of foreign countries; both UnionPay and WeChat Pay require an ID card. So why is there still no sign of a game rating policy being rolled out? It's because right now, the final say on whether culture passes censorship rests entirely with the Ministry of Culture and the SARFT. There are no relevant laws or regulations to determine whether a game passes review. There was once a domestic single-player game developer that made a wuxia game and submitted it for review. Since they were a domestic developer, they knew the censorship system inside and out, so before submitting, they removed blood and dismemberment effects, and turned all the corpses black. But even then it failed review. The censors said that the player character in this game could just serve ten days in prison after killing someone, which could easily create a bad social influence. Later on, after endless revisions, it turned into a wuxia game where you can literally only ride horses. Meanwhile, Tencent's Moonlight Blade lets you slaughter humanoid enemies without facing any consequences, you just keep right on butchering. Doesn't that create an even bigger social influence? Yet Moonlight Blade passed review. Why does this happen? Tencent makes a fortune every day, they can afford to pay up, whereas that small developer had pretty much no money left after finishing the game. So the development of Chinese single-player games isn't about your production standards, nor is it about whether your marketing hits the mark—it's about whether you can afford to pay the bribe first. And what do relevant Chinese departments claim their basis for censorship is? It's the so-called social mainstream melody, the Socialist Core Values. What does this kind of thing feel like? Ancient monarchs would always find a statement that sounded legally and theologically sound to justify their power: the Mandate of Heaven, I am the Son of Heaven, all my authority is bestowed upon me by the heavens. And the Socialist Core Values act as that exact kind of tool—giving their illegitimate, legally baseless power and acquired benefits an ostensibly reasonable justification. Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Macao are Special Administrative Regions; their social, economic, political, and cultural systems are completely different from the mainland. Has anyone ever thought about why that is? Actually, it's simple: the crying baby gets the milk. Take Hong Kong, for example—if they had been handed the mainland system back at the '97 handover, they would have gone on massive strikes and student boycotts, completely paralyzing society's normal operations. Plus, back then, many eyes both domestic and international were watching Hong Kong, which is why they are a Special Administrative Region. And what about us mainlanders? When they blocked the foreign internet, we endured it. When they censored World of Warcraft, we endured it again. We have never once spoken up for our own rights, and now it's getting worse and worse. Even a China version of Steam is on the way. The best-case scenario is that a China-only store pops up, and all existing mainland region payment methods and regional pricing discounts get migrated over to it. If we silently endure this time as well, what about after that? Are we gonna turn into the North Korean Kwangmyong network? A lot of people treat all these things as if they're only natural—whether it's blocking the foreign internet, censoring games, *Baozou Dashijian*, or now the China version of Steam. But the reality? When Europe has terrorist activities happening on Instagram or Twitter, do they just simply build a firewall and ban these social media apps? No, they fight a cyber war against those terrorists and drive them off those platforms. If that's the case, why can't the CCP do it? Just because building a firewall is cheaper? Are our rights and our spaces for entertainment and relaxation worth less than the cost of fighting a cyber war? Do Chinese people just have to compromise and swallow their shit while foreigners get to protect their rights? Please spread these words far and wide. Speak up for your own rights and for Steam. I don't know which kind of being "represented" is better: the kind they claim when they ban and censor World of Warcraft, *Baozou Dashijian*, and other free media, social apps, single-player games, and online games, claiming it's the will of the people and the players; or the kind where what I'm posting today represents the interests of Steam players. But I do know that everything I'm saying comes straight from the bottom of my heart. It's heartfelt, spoken with a mixture of all sorts of bitter emotions after going through all this bullshit. I'm saying this with a clear conscience, whereas they certainly aren't. I hope everyone will spread these words. I know that nine times out of ten it won't do shit, but how can you refuse to cry out just because your voice is small? As an ordinary resident living in China who loves Steam and loves the joy Steam brings, this is all I can do. Thank you everyone. Actually, being a docile citizen has zero benefits and all the drawbacks. Because if you show obedience, they have to provide you with even less. Since you've already expressed compliance, why would they give a damn about your needs? On the other hand, the so-called rabble—for the sake of their own rule and to appease the masses, they're forced to provide a lot more. You see this domestically all the time: when they blocked the foreign internet and censored games, we complied. And the result? Now a China version of Steam is on the way, because since you always comply, they figure if they launch it, they launch it—you'll just keep falling in line anyway. Whenever I think about the First Amendment of the United States and how Steam, this platform for freedom of speech, allows me to speak out here, while they're about to roll out a China version of Steam to strip all of that away, a flood of mixed emotions hits me. Honestly, I don't want that much when I speak out. I'm not delusional enough to think life will magically get better just because of capitalism. You still have to hustle yourself, you still have to grind for a dozen years to afford a house and a car. All I want is a few less restrictions and controls, for the government to respect the rights of its citizens. But even something as simple as that is so fucking hard!

translation_en: The story of GTA 5 came out five years ago, and I've also grown from some clueless kid who only knew how to go on killing sprees in the game into an adult who actually enjoys game storylines. When I booted up GTA 5 again, I realized the whole game's story isn't as exhilarating as before anymore; it's much more about the helplessness of life. The people caught in this helplessness are Michael, Trevor, and Franklin. [h1]I gave everything for this family, but my wife is cheating, my son is a total NEET, and my daughter's an easy girl.[/h1] Mid-life crisis is the psychological anxiety that permeates the entire game. When you reach middle age, life loses its drive, room for upward mobility shrinks, and relationships gradually become fixed. A teenager's soaring ambitions slowly fade away, leaving you with nothing to emotionally invest in except your family. Michael is exactly this kind of character. Dressed in the leather shoes and suit of a successful man, sitting in a therapist's office, he complains about his bitch of a wife and kids while calling himself an even bigger asshole. Now, besides blowing money on venting furiously to a shrink, nobody at home is even willing to talk to him seriously. Michael is like that old-school guy who's great at his job but never gives a shit about his family. Back in the day, he was full of swagger out there, and he settled down early hoping to have a happy middle-and-old age after all his hustle. Once he actually achieved his dream, landed smoothly, and bought a mansion in his favorite city—Los Santos, the movie capital—he left his neck-risking days behind. He thought the life ahead would be blissful, but he never expected to constantly face the gritty, raw reality of life and the petty bullshit of everyday trivialities. He found he had no place in his home. Once the intense life—where everyone worked toward the same goal and a single mistake meant getting killed or arrested—relaxed into ease, he didn't know what to do with himself. He started finding everyone around him annoying: his wife who liked messing around, his daughter willing to trade her body to climb the social ladder, and his stay-at-home son who lacked an ounce of manhood. But he knew they were his family, the only people who wouldn't betray him, so he could only shut himself off and hide. That's why when Franklin came to steal Michael's car, he wasn't sitting on the living room sofa; he was hiding in the backseat just to get some peace and quiet. Therefore, the second time Franklin came to his house, even though his daughter and wife were constantly arguing over whether to take in some hobo, he just smoked, drank, and sunbathed in the yard wearing sunglasses and headphones, as if that arguing world had nothing to do with him. I fucking relate to this feeling so much. Life is a total mess—there's no order, only chaos, and after the chaos, it naturally settles into a compromise. Since the final outcome is just a compromise anyway, what the hell difference does it make whether you participate or not? Michael was just waiting out his aging and death in this kind of life. So when Franklin came to him for guidance, Michael repeatedly emphasized that he was a retired man and rejected his past life. That's why he told Franklin: "Go get a college degree so you can legally exploit people and make a fucking killing." Michael rejected his past chaos because nowadays he craves order. Of course, while he successfully escaped society's chaotic disorder and stopped doing illegal work, he also jumped headfirst into family disorder. But the sad part is that people seem to have their destinies decided from birth. No matter how much Michael yearns for a peaceful life, his true nature isn't peaceful, and the family supported by his illegal enterprises won't let him have peace either. That's why we see Michael having to save his son after he sold his yacht and got scammed, having to stop his daughter from hooking up with gangsters, and getting revenge on the tennis coach when he caught his wife cheating. And because of this, Michael racked up massive debts and had to go back to his old ways. So the gears that should have rusted started turning again: contacting his old pal Lester, training a new crew for a heist, finally pulling it off, and dropping that line he always muttered unconsciously: "You forget a thousand things every day, pal. Make sure you forget this one." Back then, Michael retired for the sake of his family; now, Michael came out of retirement for the sake of his family. He had to do evil to sustain his current life, but continuing to live like this would sooner or later drag the whole family down into the abyss. Nobody in Michael's family is a "good person" in the broad sense. Just like later in the game when the whole family goes to the original therapist's office for a family session, Michael and his wife scream at each other about each other's faults while the son and daughter sit nearby looking down at their phones. Then the argument, which should have escalated to a breaking point, just stopped because the therapist looked at his watch and said time was up. I used to not get how the fuck these people could still stay together, but now I understand: Michael and his wife are the exact same kind of person. It's precisely because they're the same kind of person that they stay together. Everyone in that family knows about Michael's shady past, and they know why they came to Los Santos to live under fake names. They all accept their own wickedness and then blame each other for not understanding them. That's just how reality is. I might not love you anymore, but we can't split up. Wanting to stay together—wanting to stay together as a complete unit—is way more important than shallow, untried love. Michael represents the side of us that compromises with reality as we grow up. We gradually accept our own bad sides, gradually accept the bad sides of the world, and adapt to each other. [h1]I always gotta fuck somebody, you want me to fuck you?[/h1] If Michael represents compromise with reality, then Trevor is the other side of middle age—preserving qualities we practically only see in textbooks: loyalty, simplicity, and the desire for others' approval. Generally speaking, during the process of growing up, people divide the world into two types: one where the world is just "me" and "everyone else," and another where the world is "us" and "them." These two states can switch back and forth in a single person. For instance, when Michael is dealing with his family, he uses "us" and "them," but when he's all by himself, it becomes "I" and "everyone else." So when Michael was in hiding and Franklin asked him and Trevor for help, Michael's first line was, "We're keeping a low profile!" Trevor shot back, "You only care about yourself, you didn't even ask what kind of trouble Franklin's in!" What makes Trevor interesting is that in his world, there is no "me" and "everyone else"—only "us" and "them." That's exactly why, when he found out Michael was still alive, he didn't hesitate for a second to find him and see him. As for the reason behind the fake death back then, it didn't matter; as long as the guy was still alive, that was enough. It's not like Trevor didn't know there was a mystery there; he just refused to unravel it. If Michael going back to his old ways had his family as the fuse and Franklin as the spark, Trevor was the lunatic who dumped a pile of bombs in front of Michael and made him light them one by one. Trevor barged back into Michael's life like a rabid dog, dragging him right back into his old madness, making him find that old thrill within the insanity, getting hopelessly hooked, and finding a track back to life right on the edge of a cliff. No matter when you meet a guy like Trevor, you'll think he's sincerely adorable. When you're young, you want to hang out and mess around with him; when you're older, you might think a guy like that is an idiot, but you'd still want to be friends because he'd never stab you in the back, he wouldn't steal your girlfriend, he wouldn't let anyone talk shit about you, and he'd be down to face the storms of this world right alongside you. The drive and fearlessness of youth can make your blood boil with a guy like Trevor, charging forward fearlessly. But when you hit middle age, you've got your own family, your own kids, your car, your house, your bank account. Everything's going smoothly; you're just missing that reckless wildness of your youth. You clearly don't need to put yourself out there anymore, braving the wind and sun—you could be sitting in a high-end mansion drinking the most expensive booze and enjoying top-tier service. But you're still missing that tiny sliver of nostalgic passion. You feel like you should summon back your old rush, feeling like everything around you isn't worth holding onto. Yet you still don't dare casually change your track; you're too used to being comfortable, and you refuse to let yourself change anymore. And that's when life starts feeling like it's reaching its end. Living steadily, aging steadily, watching your kids get married and have kids steadily. That sense of loss and helplessness just bubbles right up. What people fear the most is this feeling of losing their edge, leaving behind only the chill of old age. As the saying goes: A real man should die in the wilderness, wrapped in horse hide and buried—how can he just lie in bed and die surrounded by women and servants? Trevor is the kind of guy who can awaken that spirit in someone too used to comfort. He wakes up blood that has long since gone cold. Even if you can get fired up and passionate again, you're still not your old self. You're no longer that carefree kid partying all night. Your body is starting to age, your mind is failing, and you've got a wife and family. You worry about them; even when they annoy you, you're still worrying about them every second. That's who you are now. But you realize Trevor is still the exact same as when you first met him—still rolling solo, still wild and unrestrained, still without a single worry in the world, still rocking that live-for-today swagger. You find yourself constantly envying Trevor, yet constantly hating him, too. In the end, Trevor's actions and words strip away the superficial comfort you thought you had, layer by layer. You start to panic, hesitate, and suffer immensely, but just like your initial choice, you end up betraying Trevor at the very end when everything wraps up. A guy like Trevor is just so infuriating—just when you think you're gonna die of sheer boredom, he suddenly pops up and tells you, "Pal, you can't just fucking go out like this, you've got one more score in you, and I've got your fucking back, brother!" Every single one of us has a Trevor inside us, constantly reminding us that you should live for yourself, go crazy for yourself, and be happy! But every single one of us also has a Michael inside us, constantly reminding you that you're not young anymore, you need to grow up, don't go wild, and you have a family along with responsibilities you have to bear for them. The success of Trevor's character is because we all need to project our regrets and lost emotions into some artistic work—even certain things we fantasize about doing in our heads but can't actually pull off due to real-life constraints. That's precisely why, when Trevor pops up in GTA—this sloppy, thinning-haired, foul-mouthed, greasy middle-aged uncle who wakes up God knows where every day—he leaves such a lasting impression on us. He's fucking beast living in modern society; he can sprint down the middle of the road like a madman, while the best we can do is just glance over from the sidewalk. [h1]I want to escape my living situation[/h1] Franklin is the only protagonist without a mid-life crisis, but he's also the only one who wants to escape his living situation. Michael wants to keep his broken family from derailing; Trevor wants a world that won't accept him to derail immediately—if we're going down, we're taking everyone with us. Franklin just wants to ditch his lifelong family, friends, and relatives to find happiness in a new life. Who does Franklin have around him? An aunt who does nothing all day except boost her feminine charm; Lamar, who has a screw loose, plays by his own rules, and constantly gets into trouble; and Tanisha, who grew up with him and whom he wanted to marry. But Tanisha thought nothing of Franklin and married a doctor who could give her a stable life. Franklin eventually escaped the neighborhood he grew up in, bought a big house, and got a luxury car, but besides himself, not a single soul ever came over. Franklin cut away from his roots, but he didn't get any fruit to comfort his soul either. Until Tanisha showed up, begging him to save Lamar. This time, it was Franklin's own choice: do you want this empty, bone-chillingly quiet big house, or do you want that noisy old neighborhood and those old buddies who always gave you a headache? Franklin chose the latter. But even so, he still couldn't understand Lamar's actions. Lamar's logic was: "I messed up, sure, but we're brothers, so you gotta come help me." This is the reality of Franklin's life: we either rise together or fall together. Nobody gets to escape alone. And even if you do escape, what of it? You'll still endlessly yearn for your old life. This isn't just Franklin's reality; it's Michael's and Trevor's too. Otherwise, why else would they still be dragging their aging bodies around in their forties and fifties, doing neck-risking dirty work? All three of them understand that one day, in some operation, they'll either heroically or silently be killed by someone else. But until then, they can only keep pushing forward. Back then I had no choice, now I want to be a good guy? No, the moment I was born I was only ever meant to be a bad guy. Because the path of a righteous man doesn't have what I want—besides, are there really no bad guys inside the righteous FIB? [h1]Finally[/h1] Playing GTA 5 again, I found myself with a brand new understanding of this story. In my view, the game's narrative perspective is genuinely unique. A single story told entirely from three different perspectives lets us see the entire heist process from start to finish. In the end, the three of them go off to kill their respective enemies, bringing the story to its absolute climax. Then the ending features all three of them pushing their enemies off a cliff together—none of their hands are clean anymore. When they leave, the three of them still have their own friction. Trevor and Michael are still bickering, which has become their own twisted way of showing affection. Franklin can't stand the middle-aged geezers' nagging, waves his hand, and is the first to leave. Right after that, Michael drives off into the sunset, while Trevor saunters away from the camera. It feels as though this was just the end of yet another ordinary job, and tomorrow they'll gather together again to pull off one more fucking score. GTA 5 definitely has skewed values—it's about crime, about destruction, and we're obviously all law-abiding citizens. When we see Michael's wife cheating, we wouldn't pull someone's house down with a car. But if I actually got cheated on, I'd fucking want to do exactly that. Even if I don't have the capability, you're not even gonna let me *want* to? Games are literally things designed to fulfill human fantasies! I also deeply felt how brutally realistic this game is. The people in it can never escape their inner desires: they want to protect, but don't know how; they want to escape, but keep clinging to the past. As I inch closer to middle age right alongside Michael and Trevor in the game, I've similarly discovered how my reality is getting less and less free. The drive of my youth is gone, leaving only the sighs of old age. The pain of our youth is embodied by Franklin—escaping the first half of our lives. The pain of our middle age is embodied separately by Michael and Trevor—wanting the warmth of a family, yet refusing to be shackled by it. Wanting to get others' approval even when you've achieved nothing. At a time like this, I just gotta drop a poem. *If you win, sing high; if you lose, call it quits. So many sorrows and hatreds, let them drift away.* *Drink today's wine while you have it today; let tomorrow's sorrows wait for tomorrow.*
