translation_en: First time in Los Santos, your driving is shit, so shit that ten minutes out of the house you casually catch a one-star wanted level, a once-in-a-history online road menace, that is literally you, until finally, you tearfully switch to getting around Los Santos on a motorcycle and a moped. One day, you as a absolute noob find a pro at Los Santos Customs just honking and spinning in place with god-tier driving skills (or rather, he finds you), and the pro asks you what you want to do. Trembling, you say: Can we just go for a drive? Then that day is the first time you see all of Los Santos at the speed of wind. Before saying goodnight and logging off, the pro drives you to a stop by a coastal highway. Like a bumpkin entering the city for the first time, you make a fuss opening your phone, clumsily figuring out GTA 5's selfie mode. He just quietly stands by your side, patiently tolerating your squeaking and squawking, so after taking a selfie of yourself, you sneakily snap one of the pro too. ...... You've had another shitty day in real life. You open your computer, stare at the desktop for ten minutes having no idea what to do, so you go back to Los Santos. By this time you already have a dozen hours of online game experience, finally figuring out some ropes, and your ride out has finally evolved from a two-wheeled motorcycle to a four-wheeled quad bike. The days of dominating Los Santos in your battle wagon are just around the corner. Wobbling over to the barbershop, after scrolling up and down the list for ten minutes, you give yourself some gorgeous pink and blue hair, swap to a slightly sickly eye makeup, disable passive mode, and with a baseball bat you stole from a job—your most treasured weapon—you aimlessly wander the streets of Los Santos, pretending to be some free-spirited Harley Quinn. Except this time you didn't run into some pro to help you play the role of Joker. You follow the map all the way along, and find that up on some godforsaken mountain in the middle of nowhere, there's actually a level 10-something player standing totally still. Dragging your bat, you walk up the mountain in confusion, and finally discover someone even more bored than you: some little shit staring blankly at the sky. The level 10 noob makes eye contact with you, doesn't say a single word to you in the chat, and gets back into his car. Channeling the thick-skinned energy you used to hitch rides with back then, you uninvitedly cram your way into his car, and the noob slowly drives you down the mountain. Passing a gas station, the mute noob silently parks the car right in front of the convenience store door and pulls out a pistol. You understand what he means almost instantly, and excitedly pull out your precious baseball bat, locking eyes with him— You two robbed the gas station store. Unsurprisingly, you instantly get reduced to Los Santos wanted targets, but what you didn't expect is that this little shit actually has god-awful driving skills, driving in a way that carries a fair bit of your own signature flair. Before getting far, under the watchful eyes of the law, he very slickly manages to crash the car with you inside. And just like that, you, the Los Santos Harley Quinn, are left dumbfounded as you get busted on the spot by the cops, blown to smithereens by the fuzz. Tears of regret. You cried, but you were faking it. You were laughing your ass off. ...... At first you said this game is so fucking fun, even tourist-type players like you with shit driving and garbage aim can find the purest joy in it. Surely you can just keep playing forever, right? You just didn't expect that until one day, after logging on and off over and over again, and clicking the Home key to open your friends list time and time again, you finally realize those guys—whose real names you didn't even know—are never coming online again. Just like that, your Los Santos life abruptly ground to a halt on some ordinary, uneventful day.

translation_en: For the longest time I kept putting off its campaign. Unforeseen events or even other games would make me push aside one of the most incredible stories in the GTA series. And something always dragged me back. Sometimes, an old friend inviting me to play online. Sometimes, pure nostalgia for exploring the streets of Los Santos. And even the sheer desire to listen to Mirror Park, Radio Rock, Non Stop Pop radio stations, which introduced me to yet another incredible soundtrack. It's worth remembering that when you buy the game, you're actually buying two games. The story mode (singleplayer) and Online (multiplayer), which are basically two different games that take place on the same map. In both, you'll have countless missions, many, many hours of gameplay, a shitload of random things to do, and enough chaos to break the world three times over. In Story Mode, you play with 3 pre-defined characters. Franklin, Trevor, and Michael. Michael and Trevor already share a certain past, but Franklin shows up in the campaign to act as the glue between the two. I know the game is 'old' by now, but I don't want to drop any more spoilers. Each character has a unique personal behavior, with their own problems, their own quirks, and their own craziness. When together, fun and plenty of laughs are always guaranteed. During the campaign, a lot of stuff is going to happen, including you—as everyone's probably heard by now—having to choose between Trevor and Michael at the end of the game. Which is not an easy choice, nor a very pleasant one. During the campaign, you can switch characters during or outside of missions. Each character has a unique special ability that comes in super handy when shit hits the fan. To this day, for me, the best campaign was always Vice City's, but GTA V managed to create something significant with plot twists that will make your jaw drop. Seriously, go for it. As for Online Mode, you can create one or more characters. In this mode, there's a gigantic range of missions and possibilities to climb up in the criminal underworld. There's also a co-op mode that works during heists or missions. Drug operations, forgery, theft, and another bazillion things you can be or do. The only problem is that Rockstar is greedy as fuck, you know. So, whenever you finally get everything, something else pops up for you to buy. And so on. There's also the issue with insanely long loading times, connection problems, and hackers that will make you shit copies of yourself across the map and then blow your head off inside your base. However, above all, what really hooks me to this game is the sense of freedom. The map is gigantic, extremely well-designed, featuring urban, rural, flat, vertical areas... man, it's incredible. Sometimes I just really wanted to drive my car while waiting for my favorite song to play on the radio. There are dirt trails cutting through the mountains. Trailers in the middle of the desert with shady locals. Poorly lit outskirts. Fancy neighborhoods. Psychos. Strip clubs. Hookers roaming the streets at night. Homeless people living under bridges. Communities of armed survivalists living in mountain fortresses. Religious cults scamming weak-willed, pathetic rich people. Gang wars. Rampages. Street racing. Cycling. Triathlon races. Swimming. Damn, there's just too much stuff, man. And keep in mind, I'm only talking about story mode here. So stop being a dumbass and go enjoy one of the best and most fun campaigns ever made. GTA V - 9/10

translation_en: [h1]1046 hours. All achievements unlocked. All challenges completed, rank 410 character. I do NOT recommend.[/h1] [h1]Story Mode[/h1] The story mode of this game is what the game SHOULD be. This is that very Grand Theft Auto – car thefts, chases and shootouts, an engrossing story, interesting missions, and superb graphics. Every element of this game is meticulously fine-tuned and lovingly placed into the world, from cave paintings in the Altruist cave or a megalodon skeleton to the ghost of a dead girl or UFOs. It's a living, breathing world full of secrets that you can explore over and over again. But alone. And then we have [h1]GTA Online[/h1] The online mode has NOTHING to do with GTA. When I first went online, I had huge hopes for it, and now they are all doomed to be crushed. Let's look at what you can do online: [h1]Races[/h1] There are over 500 official race tracks in the game, and thousands more are constantly being created by players. But what kind of people play races? They are: 1. Absolute noobs who don't know how to do anything except slam the gas pedal. 2. Unreal pros who use all the features of the game engine for their advantage (such as curb-boosting), and they won't leave you a chance. 3. Cheaters. [h1]Deathmatches: TDM, CF, FFA, Survival[/h1] Everything is simple here – you will NOT FIND anyone. The days when everyone grinded deathmatch missions for money and fun ended 5 years ago. [h1]Contact Missions[/h1] Nobody plays them unless it's an x2 week. They are extremely simple and unbalanced, with zero payout. [h1]Heists[/h1] Without a doubt, there is a certain section of players who are thrilled with heists. They are extremely difficult, require teamwork, and ultimately bring in huge revenue. I am one of the heist-runners – the so-called heist grinders. My specialization is the Doomsday Heist, and Act III in particular, on which I spent about 800 of my 1050 hours, beating it hundreds of times and even setting a world record for the fastest elite challenge completion time on it that held for about a week. I earned all my money and friends right here, and it is with this team of aces that I prefer to save the world over and over again. [h1]Businesses[/h1] Here I will include import-export work, the bunker, motorcycle club businesses, vehicle warehouses, Terrorbyte missions, hangar missions, the nightclub, the casino, VIP work, any supply and sell missions. This is all a grind. No, even worse than that. [b]THE GRIND[/b]. During a 4-hour gaming session, I can earn about 2-5 million from these missions. But they are disgustingly boring, do not reward players for helping you at all, but instead attract griefers. It's better to do them in a solo public session, and that's basically single-player. I've tried them all, some I like more, some less. But the game isn't designed for doing them, the ecosystem itself contradicts them. [h1]Community[/h1] GTA is one of those games infamous for the worst side of its gaming community. These are: 1. Noobs – they will do absolute wild shit, getting in everyone's way, ruining the game for themselves and others. 2. Cheaters – in every lobby of 10-20 people, at least one will be cheating. The moment they don't like something, you suddenly start burning, tanks and Molotov cocktails fall on you, you can't move, or even worse, you get kicked from the server, and sometimes you can get banned for that too. 3. Griefers – that exact guy who donated/cheated for money and bought an Opressor Mk2 and flies around shooting rockets at everyone just because he can. The game is built in a way that it practically encourages this behavior. 4. Grinders – the ones doing business missions. It's better not to touch them, they won't touch you, but what's the point of them playing next to you? 5. People who just fuck around. They might set up parachute jumps, ride bikes on the beach, shoot flare guns at each other, or organize a sports car meet. And then they all get wiped out by an orbital strike (read points 3 or 2). [h1]Conclusion[/h1] All these groups (except for cheaters) should be in balance, but the game is built in such a way that right now only grinders and griefers (and cheaters) are left. Do you think it's fun to do a thousand identical missions to buy a new car? Do you think it's fun to fly around shooting rockets at a guy who is hauling cargo in a truck that he spent 10 hours making? If not, then this game is not for you right now. Now it's not for me either...

Franklin Clinton, a street hustler, an ordinary car thief... Michael De Santa, a once-famous master thief across America, taking lives and pulling off heists with ease... Trevor Philips, a psycho, who vanished into the desert after a bank robbery in North Yankton with Michael ten years ago... Now, the three protagonists cross paths in the largest and most bustling city in the world—Los Santos. For their own survival, and even more for money, they embark on countless criminal journeys against the corrupt US government, the powerful Chinese mob, and the terrifying Merryweather... Yes, ten years ago in North Yankton, because of a setup staged by Michael, his partner-in-crime Brad died. Even though Michael faked his death by getting shot, Trevor refused to leave him behind... Just when everyone thought Michael was dead, and his funeral was being held in North Yankton, the person inside the coffin was actually the dead Brad... For the sake of his family, he had to abandon his brother, betray the friend he had committed crimes with for years, change his name, and go into hiding with his family in sunny Los Santos... Even though his wife cheated on him, even though his kids hated him, and even though his life for the past decade was miserable. He loved his family, he loved everything he lived for, and if his family was in the slightest bit of danger, he would eliminate the threat without a single hesitation... Walking on the edge of a blade, standing against the government, opposing the nation... Corrupt eunuchs, a rotten government... We are not their puppets, we need freedom. They must never get a hold of our dirt to let us live pathetically... Even if Ending C was a white lie... Still, all three protagonists had their own stories, and their own unspoken hardships... They loved and killed each other, yet each had their own bottom line... Even though Michael's fake death had tricked Trevor for ten years, upon meeting again after a decade, Trevor still treated him as his best friend... Michael led Franklin into a life of crime, but he cared for Franklin like a surrogate son, their bond was that strong... Even though Trevor was a cold-blooded, psychotic monster, because he valued brotherhood so much, even after finding out the coffin held Brad—the friend he thought had been locked up in prison—he didn't shoot Michael... Michael's ruthlessness had once broken Trevor's heart. Yet he loved his family dearly, and even though his family hated him, he still treasured them like precious gems, forbidden for anyone to violate... Each of the three had their own strengths, and each had their own flaws... But after raiding the Union Depository for hundreds of millions in gold and breaking through the army's blockade... Franklin is faced with three choices for the ending... Do you choose Ending A to kill Trevor, to get rid of this lunatic, only to end up controlled by the FIB forever... Or choose B to kill Michael, earning the hatred of Trevor and Michael's family, and returning to the life of a street hustler... Or maybe? C? Fight like hell? Wipe out everyone lording over you doing whatever they please, and let the three of them start over with a wealthy, carefree, and free life? Of course! My choice is! Nobody dies! C! The three protagonists team up and fight together once more... Breaking through the heavy sieges of the FIB... Killing everyone who needed to be killed, every last one of them... Even if it wasn't realistic... Still, nobody wants to see any of the three protagonists die... Not a single one of them can die... This is Mike's mercy, Franklin's humanity, and Trevor's loyalty. This ending is the most perfect ending, and at the same time the most unrealistic one... But I just couldn't bear to watch any of them die... Even if I had to replay it a hundred times, I would never choose A or B... All three of them need to live well... Living freely, in this city... Even if Franklin might just be watching TV alone in his mansion, even if Michael is still arguing with his family, and even if Trevor is still howling out in the wilderness in women's clothes, at least they have their freedom... And they have friends... Their story will go on... The legend of Grand Theft Auto never stops... This is the charm of GTA!

translation_en: Pre-ordered it back in 2015, and before I knew it, five years have passed. Today in 2020, after getting exhausted from playing all sorts of games, I still love coming back to log in and check out the familiar and bustling Los Santos. I don't know if I've just gotten used to polite citizens screaming a stream of profanities, or if I actually miss the endless harassment calls from "English Dave." Seriously, my phone in real life has never been as busy as it is in GTA. Driving my favorite off-road vehicle to the top of Mount Chiliad yet again, the last time I drove up to the peak was back in 2015. A dozen or so people lined up, everyone making a ruckus and taking pictures—what a lively scene. Walking into the barber shop wearing a white sports outfit; the last time, it was two people chatting, laughing, and pointing fingers. Some friends don't get it, and don't know what's so fun about this game. To be honest, I don't either. But it really is a world that is quiet yet loud and explosive, whether you're sailing off into the distance, or drinking tea and hitting a nice birdie with an old friend; whether it's three or five buddies trash-talking and messing with each other, or driving an Insurgent together to blow up endless waves of coming helicopters. I believe this game has way too many different ways to play, and what I've experienced is just one in ten million. A couple of years ago I was really looking forward to the release of GTA6, but now I don't seem to care as much. I don't know if I'm starting to get old, or if I'm just a sentimental person at heart. Five years ago, I was a clueless nobody; Five years later, I'm still a clueless nobody. It feels like everything has changed, yet actually nothing has changed. I love GTA5, this great game full of memories.

translation_en: So many great emotions this game gave me, especially online (I've been playing since the online mode launched on PS3). It's such a shame that such a cool and ambitious project turned into microtransaction bullshit. Every new update just makes things worse. Maybe some people actually like this "content", but definitely not true fans of the GTA series. >GTA came out on PC along with heists, and man, how fucking cool was that. Everyone enjoyed playing the game, running around doing missions, putting in the effort. Public sessions were packed with players who weren't just grinding, but actually enjoying the game. That's when you could really feel the GTA vibe. >2015 - The "Lowriders" update drops. Everyone loved it. Everyone was running Lamar's missions, setting up lowrider meets, and just having a blast with the game. >The "Executives and Other Criminals" update comes out, and at that point it became clear that you sure as hell wouldn't easily make enough money for all this, but even so, everyone liked it again. That was the first warning sign of what the game is like now... >2016 - "Further Adventures in Finance and Felony" update. At first everyone thought it was a cool update, and it was. Offices were added, along with the ability to grind money easily with crates, but the expenses were always actually higher than the income from this crap. You had to spend DAYS to break even on all this shit. >A bit later, "Bikers" comes out. It was a breath of fresh air after all those "cool" and expensive supercars, houses, etc. There were lots of cool MC missions, and various businesses were added. Everyone kept enjoying the game. They could have kept moving in that direction, but........ >December 13, 2016 - the date of the patient's death, namely the release of the "Import/Export" update. Now it became obvious to everyone which direction the game was heading. Whoever has the cash rules the public session, because the vehicles were fucking expensive and fucking overpowered. Moving away from the street theme toward futurism. Wow! Of course fucking futurism reflects the game's atmosphere way better, while street turf wars, heists, and stuff are total bullshit.... >2017 - "Gunrunning" update. Public sessions started getting flooded with military hardware, but that was half the trouble. The worst thing that could possibly happen to the game was the arrival of the Oppressor. A motorcycle with rockets, fucking awesome, just super-duper, 10 pieces of shit out of 10, thanks.... >Then "Smuggler's Run" came out. They added a lot of aircraft, but most of the vehicles were just useless. I especially liked the Lazer jet for 7 million, even though you can easily get it for free. Basically, the update was just another outrageous price tag and a whole lot of sweaty grinding. Total old junk, basically.... >The "Doomsday Scenario" update. After this update, I stopped playing online. All the game's atmosphere vanished, players were hiding from each other in solo sessions. Yeah, there were some heists in this update, but flying tanks, seriously what the fuck? Like, c'mon. >The "After Hours" update drops. Seemed like there was a small chance for the game to make a comeback, but once again, spend money on this and that... Expenses outpaced income, the missions are boring, nobody plays them, but that's only half the trouble. TA-DAAAAM. Let me introduce the Oppressor Mk II. Balance destroyed, sessions empty, and Rockstar doesn't give a fuck. >The "Arena War" update comes out. Just more expenses, useless cars, the arena, etc. Old players are sick of everything, and new ones are just losing their minds over how much money everything costs. Personally, I found this update completely uninteresting. >The last major update, as of writing this review, is "Diamond Casino & Resort". And what did we get out of it? Almost nothing, but we sure got screwed. Expenses, expenses, and more expenses. The casino heist turned out to be more crap, not fun to play. They added arcade machines. I don't even want to comment on that.... And what happened to the game after all these updates? Sessions are rarely even half full (it's pretty much the same on PS4). They DEMAND that you buy all kinds of crap from the updates, every 2 seconds your phone rings and they say: "Hey sweetie, spend your hard-earned cash on this useless piece of old garbage." Tons of modders in the game. Massive prices for EVERYTHING. Balance is ruined. With every new supercar, the other cars get slowed down so that next to the slow piece of junk, the new 100500 million dollar ride looks better (great strategy by the way). Playing is no longer fun, and the whole "GTA" vibe is completely gone. In the end, Rockstar didn't just eat shit, they fed it to us too. Now the game is a microtransaction dumpster fire. Thanks, Rockstars! Great job! p.s. Rockstar is even giving away GTA for free on the Epic Games Store, arigatou gozaimasu. It's not like we were lacking cheaters already...

translation_en: Actually GTA V is a really well-made game, the story is good, the graphics are too, and the online mode is basically good as well, it has a big sandbox and generally offers a lot of variety. However, there's the problem that there are no new updates for offline mode, so as soon as you've beaten it, you can barely have any fun in it anymore. But my biggest criticism is the online mode; it's infested with flying motorcycles that will bash your face in with their hyper-aggressive missiles the second you sit in a jet, heli, or car, and even if you actually manage to dodge the missiles in a jet, you'll be shot out of the sky by the next best explosive sniper a minute later at the latest. If you're really looking for a fair game, you're in the wrong place. Speaking of fair, another essential problem with the game is that on PC in every lobby with over 10 players there is at least one modder, and if you look at them sideways you're out of the lobby real quick. Unfortunately, nowadays there are more free mod menus than new affordable and efficient vehicles, which is straight up my next point. Sadly, it has become a reality in this game that current vehicles cost way too much, usually offer way too little variety because many cars don't really differ from each other except in design, and even new content like the casino contains paywalls which cost way too much and don't actually give the player anything outside of a few missions (the yacht is the best example). Maybe you've also heard about the endless loading times in GTA. As far as loading times go, it's not as bad as it used to be, but unfortunately there's a whole new problem. If I want to play GTA for 4 hours straight, I unfortunately have to factor in 2-4 game restarts every time, whether due to modders, or simply because I walked into my hangar and for inexplicable reasons got stuck in an infinite loading screen. Combined with the long loading times, this is AIDS and ruins a lot of the fun. And now to finish, I just want to get to Rockstar's attitude. Rockstar Games has stopped caring about the community of the game, they don't give a shit about the game anymore unless there's money involved, because glitches would naturally lower Shark Card sales. And that's exactly where the problem lies, GTA is like a dying dog whose owners don't give a crap about it, yet they still parade it around on YT to squeeze the last bit of money out of it before it dies. Rockstar doesn't give a damn about their community as long as every brain-dead casual keeps pumping money into the game, and that won't change unless Rockstar finally gets a proper kick in the teeth from their community, on whom they've been taking a shit in GTA for years now. If you're thinking about buying GTA, don't do it, buy Battlefield 4 or if you hate planes, Battlefield 5. Better wait until GTA 6 maybe comes out, although I don't have all that much hope for that either, and if you play it anyway then don't put any money into the game so Rockstar realizes they did something wrong. Thanks

translation_en: Played for a full month, nearly 300 hours as a totally legit player. I pretty much have everything I want by now, and I've played through all the game's content and mastered it. The game itself is good, but the player base is just so fucking toxic. If they can't beat you, they hack—God mode, modded models, infinite explosions, spawning shit to strip your weapons. Honestly, I genuinely love GTA 5. Looking at the sights of Los Santos, standing on top of Mount Chiliad watching the sunset with friends, taking a boat out to sea, chilling in the yacht hot tub, doing missions and street racing together—these are all such amazing memories. But of course, this beautiful Los Santos is ruined by a huge portion of cheating players. Yeah, that's right, in this game they cheat like it's totally natural, totally righteous. If you ask them about it, they'll righteously tell you "who told you to attack me" with all sorts of toxic trolling. On average, I’d spend 10+ hours a day in GTA; I really love this game. You have no choice but to switch sessions. GTA is an eternal legend in the gaming world, but its players are also its biggest failure—specifically Chinese players. First off, as a Chinese person, I'm proud of it, but as a Chinese gamer, I find it so fucking shameful and disgraceful. translation_en: I want to point out right away that this is about GTA Online. I'm one of the oldest Grand Theft Auto 5 players and, alas, my patience has run out. It's not that I'm complaining that it's hard for me to save up for something, no. translation_en: The first thing I did after getting a new PC was buy my dream game, GTA. But right after launching it, I noticed some stuttering. I spent a few hours Googling, following all the pro tips from various gurus to tweak the graphics settings step-by-step, lowering the effects and whatnot, but it still stuttered. translation_en: [h1]Hello everyone....[/h1] The reason I don't recommend buying this game lies in its absolute shit online mode. Grand Theft Auto V itself turned out to be really good. I played through it when it came out on the PlayStation back in 2013. I liked the characters, the story, the soundtrack, the graphics, and everything else that people love this game for. I beat the single-player campaign and had a blast doing both main and side missions. Two years later, I played the PC version (thanks to pirates). And finally, my hands reached GTA Online. However, the online mode of this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ garbage dump filled with representatives of every possible sexual minority. I'll break everything down in order: 1. Cheaters. Well, you already know everything. A broken anti-cheat has spawned a ton of cheaters, and there will always be one or 2 or 10 cheaters in your session. Some are harmless, quietly farming money for themselves and bothering no one (I have no complaints about them), but others can wipe out the entire lobby with the press of a single button. Rockstar tries to fight them in the most disgusting way possible—ban waves. When I first went online, nothing hinted at trouble, when suddenly all players in the session, including me, got teleported to Eclipse Towers and a cheater started happily gunning all of us down with a minigun (you absolute piece of shit). I also ran into smartasses who start a gunfight with you and turn on God Mode. Wonderful! Amazing! Brilliant! A cheater can throw a complete freak show on the server, and neither the anti-cheat nor Rockstar will do a damn thing. Stop cheating. Don't shame your mother! 2. The community. Do you like causing people pain? Do you get bullied at school and did your mommy yell at you for getting a D? Then welcome to GTA Online. Your rotten nature can run completely wild here. Especially for you, the devs introduced a flying motorcycle, motherfucker. Yeah, yeah, it's OP and has auto-locking rockets. Oh, it's gonna be so much fun! Eternal knife fights, murder sprees, and neo-Nazism are guaranteed. I wouldn't wish this whole amusement park on my worst enemy. The only way to deal with these guys is to buy this oppressor yourself in the hope that they won't mess with you. 3. Loading and waiting simulator. In general, it usually takes me about 10-15 minutes just to get into online (lifehack: go into single-player first, since there's a 50% chance online will just freeze while launching). When it freezes on the loading screen, you have to exit via Task Manager and load it up all over again. Also, 5-minute loads after every single mission, heist, or adversary mode. There is also often abnormally high ping and minor bugs, like empty sessions. 4. Updates. GTA has finally turned into Saint's Row in the worst possible sense. Mad Max cars, fighter jets, jetpacks, all kinds of weird weapons, flying and swimming cars straight out of 007 movies. None of this fits the GTA setting at all. The atmosphere and setting have been completely murdered. Not to mention, if all this crap didn't mess with the open world, I wouldn't have any questions, but no! There's always going to be some guy who wants to blow you up in a jet-propelled flying piece of junk equipped with rockets and machine guns. Now the devs might have realized what kind of monster they created and are releasing more down-to-earth updates like the casino. The next update is supposedly in January, we'll see...... 5. Ticket to banana islands. Lots of people just get banned for no reason, and I'm one of them. Back in July, I got my account suspended for a month, even though I hadn't even played this shithole for 2-3 weeks at that point. "How's that possible?" you ask? Well, just like that, I didn't use any cheat menus, didn't accept any dropped money. What the ♥♥♥♥!? As a result, all my 80 hours of progress went down the drain. The anti-cheat is absolute garbage, so why the hell not, let's keep banning regular players because that's obviously the right thing to do!! And if I get banned a second time for no reason, what do I do, buy the game all over again? Hell no, thanks!!! 6. Broken economy. All hail this casino, shiny! Those were my first thoughts when I saw the one-and-a-half million price tag on a remote-controlled car. If you play the honest way, it's going to take you a very, very long time to grind. You have no choice but to farm. For a very long time and very stubbornly. The prices for new cars, weapons, and properties are out of this world. But kind Rockstar gives you the opportunity to get money. By paying real cash, of course. And what's left for players when prices go up, but mission payouts don't? ̶C̶h̶e̶a̶t̶. It's absolute audacity to shove microtransactions into a full-price game and deliberately break the economy for it. As a result, I see no point in this broken online mode. At first it was awesome, but right now it's a pay-to-win and cheater-infested pit, and I see no point in playing GTA Online right now. If for some reason you haven't played the single-player, I strongly advise you to do so, you won't regret it! Try the online component at your own risk. What am I even explaining to you here, you already understand everything: online is the plague and sepsis, single-player is a panacea; online is jacking off, single-player is high morals, ethics, and family values; single-player is a living grandpa, online is a dead grandpa. 𝒯𝒾𝓃!

translation_en: Played so long I guess I've 100% completed all of GTAV. Before quitting for good, I'm gonna write a review for the whole game. Actually, GTAV and GTAO are practically two different kinds of game products. Don't know why Rockstar had to shove them together, probably for sales, which ended up causing a ton of derivative issues and making player reviews of GTAV completely polarized. Let's talk about GTAV first, the offline single-player part. Compared to GTA IV, the optimization is top-tier. Using the RAGE engine, they made the game world insanely close to real-life Los Angeles and parts of Southern California, making it super easy to get immersed in the world of GTAV. Unlike the dark and gritty realism of GTA IV, GTAV presents players with a neon-lit, vibrant Los Santos and a bunch of distinct, vivid characters. It uses the character-swapping mechanic to tell a story of three very different guys—their love, hate, and life together. Even though the plot isn't as deep as GTA IV's, the overall story experience is amazing. You get to experience the whole story from three different angles at the same time. This was what initially drew me to the GTAV trailer, and I hope GTA VI keeps this feature. Now onto the GTAO part. Although I'm not big on MMOs/online games, it feels like GTAO suffers from the common disease of online games on the market: the balance is absolute garbage. One of the biggest design failures in GTAO is the introduction of the Oppressor MK II. To this day, there's still no foolproof strategy to counter it (even after getting the backward-flight 180 bug nerfed, it's still way too strong, a total noob killer, kinda like Doomfist in Overwatch). Another huge failure is the game environment. Maybe when you get this many players it really starts feeling like a microcosm of society; in GTAO, arguing, drama, shaming people, cheating, and selling menus are everyday occurrences. This online game gives players way too much negative energy (though positive examples do happen on rare occasions, that still depends on everyone's own self-awareness—what goes around comes around, hope every player tries their best to be decent). As an online game, GTAO is not very friendly to newbies in the beginning. There's a dazzling array of fun, cool-looking vehicles and weapons, but they are stupidly expensive, and the money you grind from jobs runs out instantly. To put it bluntly, in Online you're experiencing going from working odd jobs to becoming a tycoon, and the middle part is a process of hard work and struggle. If you think Online is just a game where you get to experience all sorts of fun shit without having to pay a certain price, you are dead wrong. Closing thoughts: I sincerely wish all players have fun. Whether you're a player amazed by the offline story, or grinding cargo in Online amidst a war of cheaters, I wish you joy in your gaming. Goodbye, charming Los Santos, I'm gonna hop on a westbound train and go experience the final days of outlaws in the Wild West....,,,

translation_en: What the fuck kind of launcher are you releasing, Rockstar? Social Club was already working just fine—you could play single-player, drive cabs, go skydiving, play online, grind some money, or just cruise around and look at the scenery if you're a casual player. Endless updates, connection lost, game verification failed. So basically, if I don't have internet, I don't even have the right to play single-player? Living in this country means I don't even get to drive a cab or go for a run in-game? I finish a hard day's work, exhausted as fuck, take a shower, and just want to cruise the map for half an hour. Now playing this game is like playing a fucking escape room—can't get in, can't open it, can't connect. I'm here to play a fucking game, not to be played by one. I'll change this review when you actually fix these network issues.

translation_en: (Whether you're online or offline, you need an internet connection to play, and even if you're connected, you still might not be able to play.) (QQ email addresses cannot receive Rockstar verification emails. If you registered with a QQ email and don't want to quit the game, good luck dealing with Rockstar's customer support.) (Go to Baidu's GTA5 bar and search for "can't get online" and filter by "OP only"—there are a full 70 pages of results, and that's just from July to October 2019.) (I typed my email wrong at the beginning, but thankfully I could verify it later, so I played for over 300 hours. This morning, it locked me out, even offline. I thought I could just contact them through that email, but I found out QQ email doesn't receive verification emails.) I just fucking don't want to deal with customer support. Don't give me that bullshit about being too lazy or finding it a hassle. I bought a whole year of VPN for this game, I even tried downloading those sketchy virus-filled maps from my collection. But if a game forces you to rely on a support team that takes two or three days just to tell you what the fuck to do next to recover your account, I draw the line. What the fuck, a game is literally unplayable without customer support now???? Who the fuck buys a game expecting they have to contact customer support? As far as I can remember, I've never had to deal with customer support in my life. Why the fuck did I buy the game only for you to ask me for an email, a serial number, and a verification code, and if I mess up a single character I have to deal with customer support and wait two or three days for a reply? What the fuck. In my book, if a player is always contacting support, it means the player sucks. But if most players of a game have to contact support, it means the game sucks. It means this game is absolute trash. Whoever buys it is forced to act like a submissive little bitch in front of customer support. I can't be that bitch, and I don't fucking want to be. Just a few words: if you want to know what it feels like to buy a game, have an internet connection, and still not even be able to launch it, go buy GTA5. What the fuck, playing a game has more steps than scaling the Great Firewall. Buy the game, download the game, download the launcher, register a Rockstar account on their official site, link your email, verify your email, stare at the fucking cloud for half an hour. If a single step goes wrong, your money is down the drain. Every single step filters out a massive chunk of players. Don't think for a second it won't happen to you. When you realize Steam is launching the GTA5 launcher instead of GTA5, and you still have to verify your shit inside the GTA5 launcher. When you realize the email the launcher wants to send the verification code to isn't the one you originally entered. When you realize half an hour has passed and your inbox still hasn't received the verification email. When you realize your product key was already used by someone else. When you realize QQ mail literally cannot receive verification codes. When you realize your email was hacked, you forgot the password, it got auto-deleted from inactivity, or you just can't use it anymore. When you realize some random fucking moron typed a digit wrong and used your email so now neither of you can log in. When you encounter: "Incorrect email or password, or this account does not exist on this machine." "An unknown error occurred, please try again later." "Uh oh! You have never successfully logged in on this machine." Not to mention countless saving failures. Even when you do get in, it's one hour of gameplay and half an hour of staring at clouds. You don't even dare accept missions or jobs, because entering a job means staring at clouds for an unknown amount of time, and finishing a job means getting stuck on the loading screen for who knows how long. Getting your money and level modded by a cheater causes Rockstar to think *you* are the cheater and ban *your* account. You buy a new account, report the cheater, and the cheater counter-reports you, so Rockstar bans you instead of the cheater. You used to be able to play offline without the internet, but now even with internet and a VPN you might not be able to play offline, and without internet you can forget about it. And countless people get banned for no fucking reason, treated as cheaters without even knowing what they did wrong. I can only blame myself for being a dumbass to buy this piece of trash. Just treat it like I got scammed by an old lady. All my effort is completely gone. I'm never playing this again. Uninstalling right the fuck now.

translation_en: [h1] Grand Theft Auto V [/h1] GTA V was definitely one of the most hyped games of the generation. It won several awards worldwide and managed for a long time (if it still isn't) to be the best-selling game on Steam, and for good reason! The game is actually really good, but unfortunately, Rockstar has been slowly killing this game bit by bit and I don't know if I'd recommend buying it nowadays. [b] Really good story, but zero replay value [/b] The game's story is good. It has captivating characters, unfolds in an interesting way and, coupled with the game's gameplay, flows very smoothly to follow along. But make no mistake; it's not a story that'll make you cry at the end, and it's certainly not one you'll want to play again. The replay value is almost nil, with the only thing that'll encourage you to play again being a trophy to get 70 gold medals in missions. [b] The atmosphere is simply marvelous [/b] We are graced with a huge map of all San Andreas; ranging from a massive city with various buildings, luxury cars and billboards everywhere, to rural environments with farms, mountains and waterfalls. The atmosphere is fantastic and there's nothing to complain about on that front. [b] The soundtrack is spectacular [/b] Aside from the original soundtrack being very, very good; there are various radio stations in the game, each with different music styles, ranging from pop and jazz to indie and heavy rock. The variety of music is huge and all of them are very good and combine gracefully with the game's atmosphere. [b] The gameplay is marvelous, but there's a huge problem with Online missions [/b] The story mode has 3 characters: Michael, Franklin and Trevor; each of them has a distinct personality and each has an exclusive ability. For example, Michael has the ability, while on foot, to enter a slowmotion mode, which makes it much easier to take down pilots and drivers by shooting them, and speaking of shooting... Shooting in this game is one of the coolest things about it. Whether inside cars, helicopters and jets; shooting is simple, fast and very easy to get used to. Both in first person and third person; it flows very well and leaves nothing to be desired compared to other games. [h1] Okay, I get that the gameplay is good and intuitive, but what's the huge problem you mentioned in the title? [/h1] The enemy spawns in online missions are totally broken. I've lost count of how many times I've been blessed by an enemy popping up right next to me with a shotgun, right in my face and killing me in the process, and the worst part is that on hard difficulty, these enemies are buffed and instead of dying with 1 headshot like all the others, they take up to 5 shots (even with the strongest weapon in the game); besides that, their weapons are also buffed and even the pistols that normally kill you in 5 to 7 shots, kill you in 3 or 4. I recommend you look up videos on the internet of the [i] Doomsday [/i] Heist (the last part of it) where enemies literally spawn right next to the player. It's grotesque, it's unfair, it's pathetic. [b] GTA ONLINE [/b] GTA ONLINE in the beginning was simply a test of patience: The missions rewarded you very poorly and everything in the game was (and still is) expensive, and it stayed that way until the HEISTS update. From that point on, the game started being much more rewarding, but this update also brought what would become one of GTA ONLINE's biggest problems in the future: Armored vehicles. Armored vehicles were definitely a pain in the ass for anyone fighting them, but they all had one thing in common: they had a weak spot. The Kuruma for example, a car with completely bulletproof windows, but it couldn't take a single missile; the Insurgent could take multiple missiles and still had a roof machine gun, but in exchange, it left the driver and gunner exposed. All the updates tried to do something similar later with other vehicles, but you know that common trait that armored vehicles had? Rockstar completely forgot about it. We've got everything from flying cars that shoot homing missiles; cars with totally armored windows and bodywork (which you have to spend AT LEAST 4 missiles to destroy); cars with jet engines; cars that emerge and submerge [spoiler] Seeking out Bikini Bottom, I guess [/spoiler] (kind of like those old GTA cheat codes). But, there is one vehicle, 1 fucking vehicle that for me and several other players signed the death warrant for PVP and public ONLINE missions, and dear readers, let me introduce you to the Oppressor MK I and MK II. The first Oppressor could fly, but for a short period of time and it was slow, but it could shoot up to 20 homing missiles and get this, some hackers buffed these missiles and instead of shooting 1 missile per second, the Oppressor would fire 3 and before you knew it, there were 200 missiles heading your way with the ferocity of a thousand kids watching the Fortnite black hole. The second Oppressor has unlimited flight, is as fast as most planes in the game and guess what, it shoots 20 missiles too, but with an accuracy as sharp as your mom throwing a flip-flop, and get this² it can also be hacked to unleash a fleet of missiles as big as the US arsenal right at your face. On top of all that, this bike is practically uncounterable. It destroys every other vehicle in the game and in the end, the target is left with no choice but to activate passive mode, and even if the poor bastard is lucky enough to knock the guy off the bike and destroy it, the bike's respawn has no cooldown so, pretty soon the player will be back in the skies. It's not uncommon to see friendly sessions being totally ruined by players using this bike, and even less uncommon to see a player lose 5 hours of gameplay because some guy on a flying bike destroyed their cargo during a sale. I recommend you reader to watch this video (in English) to get up to speed regarding the Oppressor MK II and the problems it brings to the game's online. [url] youtube.com/watch?v=SwXYt7Vw72I [/url] For me and thousands of players, this bike was the burial of GTA ONLINE's PVP. [h1] Conclusion: [/h1] I'm going to ask a series of questions, answer them honestly: - Do you have friends to play with? - Do you have the time? - Do you have the patience to put up with griefers and toxic players ruining the game? - Do you have the patience to endure grinding? If you don't care about online, like good gameplay and an interesting story, buy this game. If you have some friends willing to help you out in the game, or simply cruise around exploring the map, buy this game. If you don't have friends, are a masochistic monk and want to play a totally unbalanced and frustrating online mode, buy this game. But, If you don't have friends and want an interesting and rewarding multiplayer game, save your money. If you can't stand toxic players in every match telling you they fucked your mom for the twentieth time, nor do you like wasting 5 hours of gameplay because some guy destroyed your cargo, save your money. If you don't have the time or patience to keep grinding in a game to buy the things you want, save your money.

translation_en: The offline story is amazing, and the game has a high level of freedom. After finishing missions, I still love driving around, hunting, doing some part-time Uber driving, and taking in the views from a plane. When I have free time, I like to hit the golf course with Michael. I'd give the single-player story five stars. As soon as I registered for online, I was labeled a bad sport for 2 months and 2 days. But the issue got sorted out in the end. After submitting an appeal on the Rockstar website, it took them a day to investigate and fix my online problem. Some cheater had modified my player info, applying bad sport data to my account, and they restored me to a normal player. So I think the company's attitude is really good, and they genuinely care about the player experience. Cons: Hackers are completely out of control, openly advertising hacks in public chat. Money and level drops are just the basics, which wouldn't really affect other players' experiences, so I'd say that's totally fine. But malicious hackers who grief, kill people, and trap them in object models seriously ruin the experience for everyone else, leaving players with no choice but to switch sessions, force a solo session, or log off. All in all, though, I fucking love this game. Both online and offline feature a massive open world with absolute freedom—aside from heists, you can buy properties, run businesses, manage gunrunning operations, and more. You can fly a plane around with your associates to sightsee, cruise down the street in a sports car honking at hot girls in the night, hot tub with bikini babes on a yacht, or just pick a fight in some alley if you're pissed off. You can play this game as a story game, a heist game, a truck-sim cargo-grinding game, a shooter, a PvP game, a parkour game, a gambling game, a racing game, a flight sim, a golf sim....... That's just what I've experienced so far, no idea what other ways there are to play. Lately, I've been wanting to grind out all gold medals offline. I've already beaten the offline story once, and it is truly fucking fantastic! I'm in love all over again.

translation_en: In itself, an absolutely commendable product. The gameplay is unique, the possibilities of how you can spend your time with GTA are limitless. Story mode, deathmatch, survival against AI, racing, one of the other dozen game modes, founding a motorcycle club and smuggling drugs, becoming a CEO and smuggling cars, smuggling weapons via a bunker, hanging out in the casino and blowing your money on gambling, doing the heists together with friends or just playing individual missions. Or just driving around in the open world ... shopping in a clothing store and getting new clothes, hitting the bong and watching TV at home, getting a tattoo or getting a new haircut at the barbershop, getting a blowjob from a hooker in a low-income neighborhood or just casually going on a rampage and having a police chase. All of that is possible in GTA and it's fun ... Another thing to praise, of course, is that Rockstar has been delivering continuous and free new content for half a decade. Why I don't recommend this game? Because the developers know how easy this game is to hack and, also for half a decade, nothing has happened. Just recently heard from 3 guys in Teamspeak who all cheated themselves $600,000,000 and a level boost (if you were to buy this money with Shark Cards, it would cost over 5000 Euros) and said that was normal ... everyone does it, anyone can do it, has no consequences. They even showed me the link and recommended I do the same. It feels like more than half of all players cheat there. I couldn't care less if someone cheats themselves a billion dollars. But then these players fly around in their hundreds of priceless vehicles and kill whatever they want, without any regard for their own financial losses, since they have infinite amounts of it anyway. Then, of course, there are also aimbot users who rack up like 50 kills each with a single shot and die 0 times, but that's not even all. What's really annoying then, as happened just yesterday, are the cheaters who take it to the extreme by using hacks to teleport all players to them and kill them, control the weather, are invincible and all that kind of stuff. The hack also implied that any player who reports the hacker gets kicked from the server themselves. And that can be done in GTA and is done. And as an honest player, you just have to take it. The fact that the hacker openly admits to it in global chat is just an indication that you have nothing to fear yourself, even after such stunts. And no matter what this game has to offer, as long as you continually draw the short straw just because you're honest and have to flee to closed servers to be spared from such actions, GTA naturally gets a thumbs down from me.

translation_en: I got banned for the second time, a permanent ban, and I feel totally numb. Did I cheat? No. Did I mod money? Yes. I grinded from level 1 to over 100, I bought shark cards, I legitimately grinded cargo, but every single time, modders came to grief me, blew up my cargo, trapped me in cages, fucked with me in every way possible. Was I in the wrong? I couldn't take it anymore so I modded money. I also occasionally killed people, occasionally helped noobs, but time and time again I got messed with by modders, dying over and over, and whenever I saw a modder I'd just report them and switch sessions. At this point was I in the wrong? Yes I was, I modded money. Then the first ban, one month. Fine, I accepted it, I modded money. But it had already been 2 years between when I modded money and the ban, so I thought maybe I got reported for using an invisible jet by some clueless noobs thinking I had an invisibility cheat. Whatever, unbanned and keep playing. I got unbanned, and I modded money again. There was no way in hell I was going to grind all that money back from scratch, my level 190 character got wiped to level 1, but whatever, time to start over. I didn't go around killing people, I bought the casino garage, parked my favorite cars in it along with a few bikes, would just drive around the map, wait at red lights in the city, and when other people killed me I didn't yell at them. As long as they weren't cheating it was fine, I didn't get mad. There was just one time they pushed me too far, and I went on a rampage in a jet. After that things were peaceful again, except running into modders was super fucking annoying, though of course I'd just casually report them and switch sessions. These days I bought another game and have been playing that, but just a moment ago, my QQ email tells me I'm permanently banned. Other players mod money and don't get banned, but I get banned, and I just don't get it. Sure, you guys can think I modded money and deserved to get banned. Yeah, I modded money, getting banned for that is what I deserve, but I got banned because I reported modders. Modders nowadays are really next-level. Kicking people, trapping them in objects, teleporting—those are just the basics. Now they've even evolved anti-report features. As long as you report them, they have ways to avoid getting banned, and on top of that, they'll counter-report you. You heard that right, they'll report YOU. At this point, what the fuck can I even do? I can't report modders, report them and I get banned. Even if I didn't mod money and played legit, I'd probably still get banned. Honestly, playing this game is just too mentally exhausting. Back then I downloaded a cracked copy for offline, and later bought the legit version for online. I got griefed to hell and back when I was level 1. My first car was that Bumblebee knockoff, my second car was the Kuruma, my first plane was the Hydra, my first bike was the Nagasaki Chimera, my first property was the garage by the Arena, my first heist was Fleeca, my first motorcycle clubhouse was out in the desert, and my first business was down by the mountain. From having trash aim to hitting headshots every time, from dying all night on Lamar's missions to getting the Criminal Mastermind achievement on Doomsday, I didn't have a ton of time to play the game so I modded money, but I genuinely cared about playing the game. I'm tired, I don't want to play anymore. Sure, I'm a Taobao warrior [bought cash/accounts online], but I don't show off, I don't lead other people into modding money. I'm tired, genuinely fucking tired. Over 1,000 hours, I'm just too exhausted. Playing legit gets you banned, reporting modders gets you banned, I just don't understand. At the same time, I am firmly against actual cheating—even if I suck so bad I smash my computer and mouse, I will never cheat. Whatever, goodbye Los Santos, hope you get rid of modders soon. Wish you guys a fun gaming experience, never fucking cheat, never fucking cheat, never fucking cheat. Hope Rockstar fixes the cheater problem soon, and hopefully GTA 6 will be better without any cheaters... though I know that's impossible.

translation_en: Having played 100 hours of GTA, I'm writing this review: (Everything said below is purely the author's opinion and is not forced on anyone. Trigger away at your own risk) -------------------------------------------------------------------------- Pros: - Lots of varied missions and campaigns - The game isn't abandoned, meaning new content keeps dropping (weapons, vehicles, clothes, locations, minigames, jobs, campaigns) - Pretty low system specs, so more people can play ==> bigger online base - Stable servers (personally I've had very few server issues, or none at all) - It's still good old GTA, with its occasional madness - The casino update made things more interesting, since you can randomly hit the jackpot or win a car. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- Cons: - There are microtransactions (Can't call it a massive con, but it's still there) - A huge chunk of the community (not just the Russian one) is toxic. I mean constant random killing, intentionally failing missions, and other bullshit that keeps you from playing in peace - A decent amount of cheaters; in 100 hours I ran into around 10-20 cheaters. They'd blow everything up, drop massive amounts of cash (which could get you banned), freeze players, and crash people's games. - (This is a very subjective opinion) With recent updates and the addition of flying bikes (Oppressor), cars (DeLorean), laser miniguns, alien pistols, and alien/laser weaponry in general, the game started to strongly resemble its satirical clone brother: Saints Row. - Even though the player base is huge, matchmaking for specific jobs can be a real test of patience and luck. Players might join, sit around waiting (maybe even start the mission) and just leave... out of nowhere. They can ruin and troll in missions just because they feel like it, and don't give a crap that someone actually wanted to finish the job properly and get that in-game cash. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Bottom line: All in all, I can say that after 100 hours in GTA I don't regret the time spent, because it was fun. It's got both a single-player campaign and online mode. You can create your own custom maps (races, parkour, hell, even a whole separate game mode). You can make some sort of acquaintances and friends (maybe even of a different nationality). GTA V still remains a classic GTA game, with all its quirks, features, annoying and funny moments, and of course a dash of madness.

You're in the middle of a mission in Online, or you're about to finish it—you know, that mission you spent 40 minutes sweating over, putting in all that effort and getting tired—and you're literally 100 meters away from the destination and BAM. Connection lost, mission canceled. If it were just you, they might show some humanity, but whoever else was on your team got fucked over too, so tough shit. And if that were the only thing (which it fucking isn't), you jump through a thousand hoops just to get into the game (I'm exaggerating, you just wait, which is boring as hell) and the game goes, "Bro, connection lost, how about we put you in story mode so you can try again later." And you try again, and again. Oh, and sometimes the game just freezes and you're like, "Ah fuck, here comes a connection drop," and even if it doesn't drop, the game is acting so retarded that you just close it and reopen it (oh boy, time to wait to connect to online all over again). 3- I strongly recommend getting the game with your friends instead of playing solo. You need 4 people including yourself for these heists. But if you're like, "Fuck outta here, as if I can't do shit on my own, I'll just mess around by myself," well, you gotta grind like a dog to make money. Okay, let's say you don't have friends and you bought it anyway. You get a text (an invite) to jump into some damn mission with other randoms, but there's no voice chat, like, you can't even say "dude, eat shit." Your teammates on the mission need to play just as carefully as you because in most missions either you only get 1 death for the whole team (not everyone gets one life each) or you get zero. Some people in the GTA V community are good, some are bad. Meaning, while doing a mission there are players who type in chat like "wait, be careful, come over here, we're coming," but there's also the chance that someone—after you busted your ass struggling for an hour—reaches the destination before you (a thing that has happened and keeps happening), types "ugh I'm bored," and kills themselves just to make you restart the mission from the very beginning. The guy does it just for the lulz. He ruins your gaming experience. There's so much more shit like this. 4- You'd think your manual dexterity, aiming skills, or playing smart would get you far in this game, but believe it or not, it only gets you so far. The person who wins in this game is the one with the high level, or let's put it this way, the most money. You're like, "Let me just pop this motherfucker's head off and school him!" but guess what? The guy is level 100-plus, and before you can even aim, he's drilling laser miniguns or an armed flying motorcycle right into your skull, and next thing you know, you're dead. Now you might say, "Well, what am I missing, I'll just buy one too." You can't, those weapons are way too expensive. Buying a house, a car, a weapon, an office, a motorcycle, a plane, a helicopter... Okay, you finally decide you're gonna buy one, buuut they are all insanely, super fucking expensive. Your whole life's purpose in GTA Online is either gonna be grinding for money or hacking and completely breaking the economy. Missions give you money, yes, but not that much. So when you factor in the mission difficulty, teamwork, length of the mission, connection errors, bugs (yeah, critical bugs where you're forced to restart the game, even if they aren't super frequent), it's a long-ass journey, my friends. 5- There are cheaters in the game. While you're trying to grind missions and do heists, some guy drops a cheat and completely ruins the server. I shit you not, within 1 second you can experience all 4 seasons in the server. 6- You can't just look at pictures of the game (ooh, flying car, helicopter, bunker, laser gun, oh so pretty, I'm gonna buy it right now and play) and expect that to be it. These things are a bit pricey, you don't just get them easily. The game's story is good, yeah, but if you're gonna buy this game, you should get it for Online, play on RP servers (which I've never tried, but I just assume they're more organized... God knows why I trust my gut on that), and buy it keeping all this shit I said in mind. It's not cheap money, you're gonna pay like 80-something. Rockstar, the game came out in 2013, man. As many good things as this game has, its flaws and bullshit are overwhelmingly massive. I don't get how a game that made this much revenue hasn't fixed this stuff. Anyone thinking about buying it or wanting to vent can drop a comment. If you read this far, props to you, friend who actually cares about Steam reviews :)

translation_en: For those friends who can't play online: First of all, don't blame R*. Yeah, it's not that the servers are trash, nor is it poor optimization. This kind of multiplayer game just requires a certain amount of computer knowledge and network know-how. If you have to blame something, blame China's network environment, especially around 8 or 9 PM—after all, there are only so many submarine cables, and it's impossible for this game to host servers locally in China. Master some tech knowledge and you'll be able to enjoy the game to the fullest. Don't just blame the game developer whenever you can't play. Alright, here is the real practical stuff, a summary of my experience getting into online mode, kept as simple and easy to understand as possible. First, you need to download a software called NatTypeTester. Run it and click "Get". If it shows "Full Cone", "PortRestrictedCone", or "Restricted Cone", you should be totally fine and able to play normally. Occasional disconnections are just network issues and considered normal. But if it shows "Symmetric", you basically can't play normally at all—either you can't get into the game, or once you're in, you create a session and no one's there, or people join and immediately drop out. Solutions: If your optical modem is doing the dialing, you have a wireless router, and your PC is connected to the wireless router, please unplug your network cable and connect directly to the optical modem. If you *must* connect via a wireless router, call China Telecom, China Unicom, or China Mobile, and demand that they change the optical modem to bridge mode and have the router do the dialing. They will send someone to handle it; if they don't, file a complaint immediately. Set your PC as the DMZ host inside your router settings (please Google this based on your specific router model). Note that if you have multiple devices at home, set your PC to a static IP, set your DNS to your local ISP's DNS, and use 8.8.8.8 as the backup. Also, it might be due to the firewall; add GTA 5 to your firewall whitelist or turn off the firewall. By now you should be able to play normally. If you still can't, please download UsbEAm Hosts Editor (Multi-platform hosts modifier) V3.47. Of course, this still doesn't work super well under China's network environment, but try pinging the GTA 5 server latency and pick the one with the lowest ping to apply. If that still doesn't work, you should take a good look in the mirror, my friend. Hahaha... Hope the above helps you guys out.

translation_en: The single-player campaign is an undisputed masterpiece and needs no introduction, so this review is about the online component. The online mode here is an endless grindfest for money. I'll list the obvious flaws that make GTA Online not worth playing: [h1] The Grind [/h1] 90% of all online missions are about delivering something from point A to point B for a pathetic $20,000, occasionally with a shootout thrown in. Every new DLC has brought us new money-making businesses. Absolutely all of them are built on the same template: steal supplies --> sell supplies --> get a little bit of money. The only difference is the supplies themselves; sometimes it's crates of weed, sometimes crates of shiny stuff, sometimes car parts, and sometimes stolen cars. All these money-making businesses cost a lot of money, around $5-6 million. Sure, you can buy one a couple of million cheaper, but then your business will be in the furthest corner of the map — a ghetto neighborhood where NPC gangbangers will gladly gun you down the second you try to visit your shack. [h1] Excessive Futurism [/h1] They went way too far with the futurism. If completing a heist used to be a pretty tough challenge, now you just grab an alien ultra-plasma gun (that's actually what it's called, btw) and blast everyone in sight without a second thought. I won't deny that parachute cars, flying cars, bikes, and jetpacks look cool, but they don't fit into the game at all. NPCs don't react to cars flying over their heads, and they have very little practical use. You can only use special vehicles in free roam; you can't take them into missions. Just think of how many cool and interesting missions you could design around a jetpack, a submersible car, or a flying bike, but no — every special vehicle in the game got exactly one five-minute mission that feels more like a vehicle test drive than a proper assignment. [h1] Escalating Prices [/h1] Vehicles in this game are insanely expensive. You'll shell out around $2 million for a single decent stock car, and don't even get me started on tuning. See, after buying a good sports car, you have to buy the sports transmission, brakes, turbo, and engine separately for a couple of hundred grand because they come "standard" as shit. As for special gear like flying bikes and cars, their prices range from $3 million to $10 million, not even counting the cost of mounting weapons on them. On top of that, every new piece of tech added to the game costs way more than the previous vehicles. A glaring example of this is the Hydra versus the Military Jet. The Hydra was added to the game a long time ago, back when you couldn't even buy a military jet. This plane outperforms it in speed and has a vertical takeoff system — cost: $3 million. The military jet loses to the Hydra in every way, plus any player can just steal one from the military base, yet it costs $7 million. Why? Because they added it to the store later. [h1] The Community [/h1] A controversial con for games, but this is a different story. Because of the flaws listed above, special vehicles here can only be owned by whales, no-lifes, cheaters, or exploiters. The microtransactions are so steep that 2,000 rubles ($20-30) is only enough for one decent little plane or a couple of cars. So you're unlikely to run into regular payers. No-lifes have a few good cars on their accounts after breaking their backs, and nothing more. That leaves just cheaters, who are thriving here. As you know, cheaters aren't known for good behavior. So it turns out that whenever you see someone on the map with a flying bike, you instinctively bail to another session unless you want to get nuked along with the crates you're trying to grind honestly. By the way, the game has an orbital cannon where you can blow up any player for $750,000. So if a cheater gets pissed at you, get ready to die on loop because there's no escaping it. (Sure, there's Passive Mode, but you can't do any work in it.) [h1] Instability and Loading Times [/h1] One of the biggest flaws that completely kills the urge to play. Server-wise, the game runs like absolute garbage. Connecting to online usually takes over 5 minutes. Loading screens are agonizingly long and happen everywhere; you might decide to walk into your garage and hit an infinite loading screen. Sometimes you spend 10 minutes connecting to online, only to get an error and get dumped back into single-player, where you have to try connecting to online all over again. 4 years after the game's release, loading screens have only gotten longer. Technically, the game is so full of holes that people have built entire YouTube channels just around abusing glitches in this game. The anti-cheat feels like it doesn't even exist; cheaters here are practically game admins. They can do whatever they want with you, from teleporting across the map to spawning random objects and instantly blowing up every player in the session with a single click. A couple of months ago, a cheater dropped a couple of money bags on me against my will. As a result, my account got banned for 30 days followed by a wipe of all my honestly and dishonestly earned cash. That's all you need to know about GTA Online.

By chance, you met Martin, a guy who led you down a life of crime, and later you met Franklin, Michael, and Trevor. Hope one of these helps you.) These are some of the problems you'll face playing GTA V. I'm leaving a positive review because the game itself is good, there's a lot to do, and what makes people quit playing are the problems listed above. Over time you learn to dodge almost all the problems and play in solo Public Sessions. Good luck to anyone starting to play!

translation_en: I've played for almost 2800 hours, GTA 5 has kept me company for a solid 6 years. It was my first legit game, and the first one I ever cared this much about, but it disappoints me time and time again. First of all, the ban system: I wasn't even online, got flagged for cheating, and got permanently banned. I tried appealing, but the reply is always the exact same. Then there's the dogshit game balance—heavy sniper, Oppressor MK2, macro-suicide and other bullshit tactics have made the game lose its original meaning. I've guided so many newbies, maxed out my friends list at 255 people, but in the end, the only one still sticking with it is me. The newbies think making money is too slow and go get modded money, while the veteran players feel like there's nothing left to do and quit, only logging in for occasional updates. Actually, I originally wanted to leave a positive review because this game is genuinely amazing. It's not the hackers that ruined this game, it's Rockstar's own retarded practices. Hackers spoof our player models, our stats flag as abnormal, and *we* get banned. Actually, I've thought about buying a new account and going back to Los Santos, but if I go back, what the fuck do I even have left? I don't really expect anyone to read this review, I just can't get over this hurdle in my heart. Because the character I customized stayed with me for six years, and she was completely forced out of my life just because of Rockstar's wrongful ban. I honestly just can't accept it.

translation_en: A game released in 2013 that came to PC in 2015 and has stayed a Steam top-seller fixture ever since tells you it definitely has something special going for it. First off, let's talk about where it all starts: the story mode. GTA 5's story mode doesn't actually feel much like an open-world game. In fact, it lacks the branching dialogue affecting the plot that various game studios do nowadays; basically, it just lets you choose the ending at the very end. The story mode feels more like a linear game—you can only do what the missions tell you. The two ways to pull off a heist are essentially pretty much the same, and you can count the different crew members on one hand. But hey, the writing in GTA 5 is just genuinely good. Even though it falls short of some pure narrative games, breaking away from the formulaic open-world mold is no easy feat, especially with the innovative three-protagonist story mode. Combined with graphics that still hold up today, you definitely need to experience the story mode. Then comes the reason most people buy this game: online mode. Before buying it, you've probably heard about random ban waves and stuff like that. Honestly, you don't need to overthink it—just fucking buy it. False bans are a low-probability event, and if you're really scared, just don't log on during a ban wave. Then there's the money-grinding issue. To be honest, I cheated in money, and I used hacks myself. I'm a cheater, and there's no denying that. In today's online environment (out of 30 people, 5 are cheaters), it's hard to survive without anti-kick and godmode. Still, I'd advise against using cheats, especially in the early game. What a newbie should do is experience the complete process of working hard to make money. Even if it's exhausting, it's a process, an experience. Only by going through that process will you know how to get through Pacific Standard, how to use a CEO office, and where to buy warehouses. After three or four hundred hours of playtime, you can consider experiencing the other half of the process: the billionaire lifestyle. But beginners shouldn't cheat in too much money; remember to leave yourself a goal, or else you'll get bored of this game real fast. If a newbie is going to get into modding money, I suggest 200 to 300 million is plenty, or even under 100 million is enough to buy all the real estate. Don't ever think that having billions like some people is great—what do you think they even do with that much money? It's nothing more than going into lobbies and randomly griefing people. -------------------------------------------------28/04/2019--------------------------------------------------------- After I posted this review, two or three people abused and insulted me because of the cheating I mentioned in it. If that makes you feel better, I don't give a shit, but I just want to say: I wasn't advocating for cheating. Also, regarding someone asking how I have the fucking nerve to admit I cheated—I want to say this is a review, and since I used cheats in the game, that was part of my personal gaming experience, so of course I'm going to talk about it. I hope you guys can look at this objectively. My account got banned ages ago anyway, and I stopped using cheats a long time ago. That's it.
