translation_en: I bought GTA 5 during New Year's and have been playing for a bit over a month now, clocking in around 70 to 80 hours total. I've pretty much finished the main story, and here's my quick little review. To be honest, I've always had a deep nostalgia for the Grand Theft Auto series, from Vice City, Chinatown Wars, San Andreas, all the way to Episodes from Liberty City. Every single one left a huge impression on me. The first time I ever experienced GTA was at a classmate's place—it was Vice City. Back then, playing it felt like opening the door to a whole new world. I realized games could actually be played like this: you could steal cars, beat people up, and do whatever the hell you wanted. My heart was completely hooked. As soon as I got home, I downloaded it, and bit by bit I learned about San Andreas and Episodes from Liberty City. Back then, my family's PC was absolute garbage and could barely run Vice City at best. So that ended up being the one I played the most. I played Vice City for several years, going from only knowing how to do missions at the start, to learning how to use cheat codes, and then following pro tutorials to install mods, adding all sorts of supercars, planes, and character skins. I started with just the simple stuff, but eventually, I could modify the map myself, adding the Akina Mountain map into the game. I'm sure this is a path a lot of people have taken, squeezing every last drop of fun out of Vice City. Facing pressure from teachers and parents back then, I could only cut loose in Vice City on Sundays. It accompanied me through several years of my youth. Later on, I got into high school and got a new PC that could finally run San Andreas, though somehow it never felt quite as satisfying. I spent days downloading Episodes from Liberty City only to find out it wouldn't run, and I could only watch enviously as other people played it. My biggest dream at the time was just to own a gaming laptop. Now I'm in college, I've got a gaming laptop, I've got the money to buy legit copies on Steam, and there's basically no game I can't run. Yet, somehow, that initial passion is gone—that hot-blooded excitement of reading reviews over and over and hunting all over the place for download links. Nowadays I don't spend much time on games anymore; it feels like it has all become a dream of my youth. The boy has grown up, things are different, and playing this game five years after its release, every mission feels both unfamiliar and strangely familiar since I'd already watched streamers play almost all of them. When I first opened up that in-game phone, which now looks kind of outdated, I still couldn't help feeling a rush of excitement. The graphics and the story hooked me into playing day and night. From having to penny-pinch just to buy ammo at the beginning, to ending up with more money than I could possibly spend after doing all sorts of missions. In the end, when it came to killing Trevor, I just couldn't bring myself to do it. I couldn't bear to picture that scene—brothers turning against each other. When the credits finally rolled, it felt like the curtain call of my youth. I really respect Rockstar. They take ten years to sharpen a sword and actually make real games. I hope to get a PS4 soon so I can play Red Dead Redemption 2. Finally, thank you Grand Theft Auto, thank you Rockstar, for walking through my youth with me. While you're young, go do what you want to do. Just like it says in *Eat Drink Man Woman*, life isn't like cooking; if you wait until all the ingredients are fully prepared before you start, it'll be too late. Hurry up and do what you love!

translation_en: Let me tell you about my history with the GTA series. When I was in elementary school, my family just got a PC. Because our broadband connection was unstable and kept dropping, my cousin downloaded Red Alert, Road Rash, GTA VC, and Blood War: Shanghai for me. GTA VC was my absolute favorite. Back then, being able to play a 3D sandbox game with such ultra-high freedom as GTA could only be described as mind-blowing. Ever since then, our family went through several generations of PCs, and GTA also upgraded through several generations—from VC to GTA 3, then to GTA SA, later to Liberty City Stories on the PSP handheld, and then to GTA 4, which used the next-gen graphics of the RAGE engine. Finally, five years ago, I saw news about GTA 5 on 3DM, and after watching the trailer, I was hyped for days. When the pirated version finally hit the net, I downloaded it only to find out my PC specs weren't enough. So I had to download it, copy it to a portable hard drive, and run to an internet café to play. Later on, it was actually GTA that got me into understanding computer hardware specs, which spiraled out of control and led me to major in computer science (actually a trashy vocational school, though I blame myself for not studying hard back then, but whether you study well has nothing to do with computers or games). Later on, I learned about Steam, and learned about genuine games versus piracy. Even though at the time I could only play cracked versions at the net café, I still bought GTA 5 on my own account. Not for anything else, I just wanted to pay back the genuine copy ticket I owed Rockstar from my childhood. GTA 5 is a milestone representative, and its biggest feature is undoubtedly the massive open world of nearly 130 square kilometers. In this huge open world, players can do multiplayer PVE or PVP. Leaving aside the server stability issue, being able to play online with friends in such a huge map while doing missions together—and even if players don't like PVE or PVP, they can just play the lifestyle way, driving sports cars around Los Santos, buying clothes, cars, and houses... I bet most games can't satisfy that kind of demand. So it makes sense why GTA 5 is so popular. Aside from the massive open world, GTA 5 is also a brand-new revolution for the GTA series itself. The RAGE engine used in Rockstar's own AAA games like GTA 4 and Red Dead Redemption is still used in GTA 5. And in GTA 5, the power of RAGE is fully unleashed, letting players experience what it feels like to "really do whatever the hell you want in a game." As for why it feels that way, the reason is simple: RAGE makes all the sensory content presented in GTA 5 way too realistic. Realism is also one of GTA 5's biggest traits. Besides the huge open world and insane realism, most players have another major source of fun in GTA 5: installing a series of highly playable mods, as well as graphic enhancement mods. Speaking of mods, people might think of The Witcher or Skyrim, where adding mods makes them feel like a completely different game. GTA 5 is the exact same way. Whether you're talking about upgrading graphics or game replayability, GTA 5's mods are equally top-notch. For graphics, GTA 5 has Redux, The Pinnacle Of V, and even stacking tons of 4K ultra-HD mods together will make you unable to tell the difference between a game, a movie, and a real photo. And in terms of gameplay, GTA 5 has countless options: Thanos snapping his fingers, Attack on Titan giants trampling the city, Iron Man, Spider-Man... So whether it's graphics or gameplay, GTA 5 can definitely satisfy your desires. But now, the official crackdown on mods has made many players who love both online and mods hesitate, leading to wave after wave of negative reviews. Unjustified bans, refusing to unban false positives, cheaters running rampant, and other reasons have made many players with thousands of hours quit the game for good. Rockstar is kind of shooting themselves in the foot. All in all, GTA 5's biggest feature is that everything about it is a feature. The story has twists and turns, the gameplay is extremely versatile, the graphics have room for improvement, and you can just wander around the massive open world... translation_en: [h1]"Every day you forget a thousand little things. Let this be one of them."[/h1] [u]My subjective opinion:[/u] Grand Theft Auto 5 is an open-world action-adventure game released in 2013 on consoles and in 2015 on everyone's beloved PC. As a devoted fan of this franchise, I eagerly awaited the release of the new installment, which at the time seemed very promising. I rewatched the trailers over and over, counting down every week and every day until the scheduled release, and when the PC version got delayed, I even managed to beat the single-player campaign on a buddy's Xbox 360 in the meantime. The story campaign turned out to be genuinely good and deserves a separate review; however, most of this review will be dedicated to GTA Online, because the vast majority of players (including myself) spent most of their time in the online mode, which has a massive amount of flaws. Overall, it's a game with huge potential that Rockstar themselves buried because of their greed, their desire to grab quick cash, and squeezing the last drops out of the online mode. It's really sad to watch such a promising project go down the drain. [h1]Grand Theft Auto 5[/h1] [u]Story:[/u] The story of this game is as old as time, telling the tale of three buddies trying to make a big score together, survive, and achieve that very American dream. All the characters are caricatures of typical US social strata. You've got Franklin — the typical representative of the African-American ghetto in Los Angeles; Michael — the typical well-to-do white guy with a criminal past and a messed-up family; and Trevor — the typical American lowlife living an antisocial lifestyle, doing various substances, and having an unstable psyche. Practically all the story moments and characters poke fun at one social phenomenon or another. Overall, the story is decent, comedic, but still not the best in the series in my opinion. [u]Gameplay:[/u] There's not much to add here, it's the same classic GTA gameplay with the same features, but also quite a few new additions. For the first time in the series history, there are three playable protagonists right away, each with their own special ability and skills. The rest of the features are either carried over or refined since GTA 4. [h1]Grand Theft Auto Online[/h1] There are so many flaws in the multiplayer that I don't even know where to start. I started playing GTA Online on the very first day the PC version came out. At first, the online hooked me from the first minutes and kept me engaged for hours; it was genuinely good and interesting. Tons of PVP modes, adversary modes, races, and cars that completely fit the game's theme. It was fun to host car meets with friends, show off the tuning on our rides, and just explore the open world. It was magnificent. Gradually, Rockstar started rolling out various updates, some of which were harmless and minor, others genuinely interesting and didn't stray from genre standards, and then there were those that simply destroyed the game's balance, dragging the game away from a car theft and heist simulator into Call of Duty-style futurism. Yeah, there were actually good updates, like "Heists," "Bikers," "Lowriders." I have no complaints about updates like those, they fit the genre well, but I'll describe the most idiotic updates and my specific complaints about them below. [u]"Import/Export" - December 13, 2016 update:[/u] Another tedious warehouse grind, but this time for cars instead of crates. A bunch of useless new zombie-apocalypse-style vehicles that cost unreal amounts of money. For example, the Ruiner 2000 — a car with rockets that can jump and deploy a parachute (a reference to the "Knight Rider" series), costs over five million dollars, is completely useless in combat because it gets blown away by a single RPG shot and is slow by itself. [u]"Cunning Stunts: Special Vehicle Circuit" - March 14, 2017 update:[/u] Maybe someone actually liked this update, but I think it doesn't fit the game's theme at all. The game's first step toward futuristic trash. Yet another mass of meaningless, unremarkable, and overpriced cars. The only plus is that this update doesn't affect freeroam sessions. [u]"Gunrunning" - June 13, 2017 update:[/u] The introduction of a bunch of military, game-breaking equipment for astronomical amounts of money, including a FLYING MOTHERFUCKING MOTORCYCLE with homing missiles. Freeroam sessions are swarming with cheaters and masses of military gear that make it impossible for regular players to play. The game turned into Call of Duty. [u]"Smuggler's Run" - August 29, 2017 update:[/u] Even more military tech, but this time in the air. Even more tedious warehouse grinding. [u]"The Doomsday Heist" - December 12, 2017 update:[/u] More military tech, a new tank, a jetpack, and other stuff that ruins the game's concept and balance. New heists where we suddenly turn from criminals into heroes, Marvel-esque saviors of the world. [u]"After Hours" - July 24, 2018 update:[/u] The biggest flaw of this update — the introduction of the even more upgraded FLYING MOTHERFUCKING Oppressor Mk 2 motorcycle. You can't shoot it down with anything, it has homing missiles and insane speed. It's from this exact moment that GTA Online finally buried itself. [u]"Arena War" - released December 11, 2018 update:[/u] A pile of expensive futuristic vehicles and outfits + absurd Mad Max-style arena battles. P.S. A ton of updates for the Online mode came out over all this time. Some were quite decent, like the casino heist or the Cayo Perico heist, but the overall problem with the online mode unfortunately remains the same. [u]Pros:[/u] - Good story campaign, worthy of a separate positive review. - Great graphics, visuals, lighting. - Plenty of references and attention to detail from Rockstar. - Pleasant soundtrack. [u]Cons:[/u] - A huge number of cheaters in GTA Online, with zero effort being made to fight them. - Unbalanced equipment in GTA Online. - Departure from the classic genre theme towards some kind of futurism in GTA Online. - The infamous ban wave in GTA Online where many honest players, with zero ties to cheats or bug abuse, got banned. - Less realistic car physics compared to GTA 4. - Ruined economy in GTA Online due to endless tedious grinding, microtransactions, and cheaters dropping cash on everyone. - Overpriced vehicles in GTA Online that often turn out to be useless. - The promised story DLC that was never released to this day. - Long loading times between sessions in GTA Online. - Apathetic attitude towards regular players. [u]My rating for the Grand Theft Auto 5 story mode: 9/10[/u] [u]My rating for Grand Theft Auto Online: 4/10[/u]

translation_en: Even though I just bought this game and haven't played a single minute of it, I specifically came back to buy it today to support the developers, and I'm feeling pretty emotional about it. Because, if I remember correctly, I've been a "cloud gamer" [spectator] of GTA 5 for almost five years! Yep, you heard that right. I'm actually kinda ashamed it took me almost five years to finally buy the game. Back in 2013, I was scrolling through Youku on the couch one day and stumbled upon an up-and-coming creator with only about 30,000 subscribers (if I remember correctly)—Lao Dai Zai Ci (Old Dai Is Here). He happened to be uploading a walkthrough series for this game. My first thought at the time was: Holy shit, the graphics on this game are so damn cool! (My impression of PC game graphics was still stuck back in the Vice City era, talk about being outdated). After that, I totally got hooked. I realized this game wasn't just all looks—the story was also amazing. What left the deepest impression on me were the three ending choices where Franklin has to decide whether to kill Michael, kill Trevor, or choose the "deathwish" option where they all survive. Even though I watched all of them, personally, I felt like the deathwish ending was the true home for the three of them (I've just got a personal bias for happy endings), while most of the other plot details have slipped my mind. Back then, whenever I got on Youku, I'd check to see if Lao Dai's GTA 5 walkthrough had updated. Haha, I really miss those days. This made me fall in love with GTA 5, and fall in love with video games. Because my PC at the time was total crap (the kind of crap where teamfights in LoL would lag). Plus, for various reasons, I was never able to buy it. Later on, GTA 5 Online dropped, and I was still just a cloud gamer on Lao Dai's channel. After that, whether it was the Heists or those bullshit races, I watched all of it on Lao Dai's channel (haha, I really love "Mama Dai," his commentary is so damn entertaining). I'll play through the whole story myself eventually. After all, that's going to be my very own trip to Los Santos. Thanks to GTA 5 for blowing my mind, and thanks to Lao Dai for bringing me so many laughs. ("The most badass pro in the commentary scene, the most badass commentator in the pro scene"—I can make jokes out of this meme for the rest of my life). Hahaha, nothing much left to write. I just threw this review together randomly, just read it for a laugh, guys. Happy Year of the Pig everyone!!!

translation_en: [h1] A few tips for online noobs [/h1] [h1] 0. Don't mod money or exploit cut glitches [/h1] Same old tune. When money becomes totally worthless, making money loses its meaning too. I've got no interest or right to police you guys, so I can't be bothered saying much else. Just chew on that quote yourself. [h1] 1. Find an active crew [/h1] As an online multiplayer game, playing as a lone wolf forever is clearly not how the game is meant to be played. Whether it's early-game guidance, rounding up players for heists, or mid-to-late-game mutual aid and chilling out, a group always has a massive advantage over going solo. And in GTA V, starting out as a newbie is rough, tutorials are lacking, finding people for heists is a pain, and random lobbies are an absolute dumpster fire. So joining a crew is pretty much a must. [h1] 2. Play through all the old heists if you can [/h1] Even though some of the old heists are pretty hard and the payouts aren't great, I personally suggest doing all of them if you have the chance. As the most appealing part of the game, heists not only help noobs bag their first pot of starter cash, but the rich content also lets newbies fully experience the fun of the game and quickly get into the vibe, which is really important for fresh noobs who are totally lost. Also, it's recommended to do heists with people; with communication and teamwork, you'll get twice the result with half the effort. [h1] 3. Don't be too impatient [/h1] After stacking your first pot of gold from heists, most noobs will own a vehicle warehouse or cargo warehouse and start the grind life. But for a noob who just went through the thrilling experience of heists, grinding is undoubtedly boring and tedious. And even though cargo and I/E are the fastest ways to make money normally, it still feels like a million miles away from becoming a high-level player just by doing that. This is honestly the stage that makes people quit the most. A lot of players either resort to modding money or just quit the game here. The initial accumulation of capital really does suck, but once you have that starting capital, making money becomes way easier, so don't give up so easily. [h1] 4. Make good use of double cash events [/h1] Why do rich players make money so easily while noobs struggle? It's not because veterans are special; it's just because veterans have a full-blown business empire and can exploit most 2x events to rake in crazy cash. No matter if you're a noob or a vet, making smart use of double payouts can make you rich overnight. 2x events usually update every Tuesday, and the corresponding properties go on sale too. This is the ultimate chance for noobs to get rich. Bunker 2x, cargo 2x, I/E 2x, biker business 2x, all kinds of heist 2x—these are all worth paying attention to and investing in. Of course, to profit from double events, you naturally need some starting cash on hand to set up properties first. That's the whole point of the grind mentioned earlier. Leveraging double events to invest in various properties over and over, breaking even or making profit during double weeks, and finally gradually building your own business empire—that's the path to becoming a rich veteran. As long as you keep grinding, one day, you'll be a boss too.

translation_en: This year's summer update is of abysmal quality, goes in the wrong direction, and crosses the line for players, hence the negative review. 1. Lazy new content 2. Nerfed old vehicles 3. Removed existing vehicles and locked them behind a paid membership 4. Increased cooldowns on old money-making methods 5. Abandoned a ton of existing custom maps when upgrading the map creator ----- The following is a review originally posted on February 5, 2019. Regarding point 1: the starter pack is now included when buying the base game at no extra cost, so you don't have to choose between them anymore. Regarding point 4: there is now a pretty solid weapon hiding feature, so you generally don't need to worry about this. ----- Welcome to the Lunar New Year sale, here are a few tips for newbies. [b]1. The starter pack is worth buying on sale[/b] You can play online and offline with any version on Steam; the difference is that more expensive editions come with extra freebies, which aren't that hard to get once you get on your feet. The starter pack is too expensive at full price, but the sale price is okay. You have to "buy" the included items for $0 using the in-game phone's internet. Oh, and the bunker included in the starter pack is in a terrible, remote location, I'd recommend swapping it for another one. [b]2. Get a VPN / game booster if you can't connect[/b] The servers are all overseas, so trying to play raw from China is pure RNG, a booster is basically mandatory. Even if you just want to play offline mode, you still need an internet connection for the first login. As for which booster is best, local network conditions vary so you'll have to test them yourself. By the way, if you get stuck on the "Are you a robot" verification while using a booster, try turning it off and on again. [b]3. Lamar's online missions are NOT beginner missions[/b] After finishing the tutorial, you'll get a series of 4-player missions from Lamar, the NPC who welcomes you to online. This mission line is NOT for beginners, it's super hard, added way after the game launched, and meant for veterans. Missions better suited for beginners are solo-capable ones from other contacts, heists unlocked at rank 12, and treasure hunts. Also, that mission from Lester asking you to buy a facility is definitely not for newbies either. [b]4. Don't buy unnecessary weapons online[/b] There's no way to delete weapons online once you buy them, they're permanent and will clutter up your weapon wheel. Some people have even remade their characters because of this. It's recommended to check out veteran guides and only buy the guns that actually suit you. Also, early on, only buy apartments with 10-car garages; other low-end apartments and standalone garages are useless. [b]5. Don't cheat or mod money[/b] Setting aside how this ruins the game for other players, there are at least three negative impacts on yourself: it kills the fun of the game, you lose some friends, and you risk getting your account hacked or banned. Seriously, if you're broke, you can find a veteran to carry you. There's a heist called Doomsday Act 2 (Bogdan) finale that's great for carrying people, netting nearly 1 million per run, and plenty of vets are willing to help newbies out. [b]6. Don't click the "boost" button after launching the game[/b] Game boosters work by closing some background processes and forcing others to free up RAM. You can click it before launching the game, but doing it after launching might get flagged by the game's anti-cheat system as memory modification, leading to a wrongful ban. By the way, based on what I've seen on Tieba, normal players practically never get wrongfully banned—80% of the people crying "false ban" are just cheaters and modders putting on a performance. [b]7. Don't ignore the offline story mode[/b] Even though most of the updates nowadays are for online, the core of the game is still the story mode. If you haven't played it, it's totally worth experiencing. Plus, jumping straight into online might just lead to you griefing your teammates because you don't know the controls yet.

translation_en: First off, GTA 5 is genuinely a great piece of work. Rockstar basically made their name on this series, and I'm sure a lot of you are like me—started with Vice City and fell in love with the game. I played GTA 5 to chase that old feeling back, but honestly, you just can't find it anymore. Back then, you had dumb NPCs that wouldn't even fight back, and you explored every tiny corner of the map until you knew where every road led, like you actually lived there. Tommy, who couldn't swim and barely spoke; CJ, with his crazy backstory yet goofy-ass animations and lines. Man, the nostalgia. GTA 5 coming out extended my childhood with Michael, Trevor, and Franklin. Sometimes I'd walk past a spot and instantly remember, "Oh shit, isn't this where old man Mike did such and such?" I'm not the kind of gamer who's into mindless slaughter, and I don't play games just for the sake of playing. Games are about emotion to me, not just toys. As for the offline single-player, there's really nothing to say—it is what it is. People who love it *really* love it, and people who hate it will never be satisfied no matter what. What I actually want to talk about is the Online mode. People who love griefing and killing other players, hackers everywhere, and money glitchers—there are seriously so many of them. One time, this guy ran up and started tossing me around, and I knew it was a hacker. I thought, "Great, another vet coming to bully a noob." But then it felt weird; the guy just kept dropping money bags on me, and my cash kept going up. I was sprinting away for dear life, and he chased me down just to keep spawning money. It scared the shit out of me, and I Alt-F4'd out of there immediately. It's gotten a lot better now, fewer hackers, but those freaks who get off on killing other players are seriously disgusting. Makes me wonder if they're absolute psychopaths. I don't want people thinking everyone who plays this game is a psycho. I've never killed another player in OL unless they started shit and came at me first. But most of the time, some dumbass just rolls up and kills you over and over and over again. Look, I get wanting to have some fun, but killing someone once should be enough. These assholes will just keep spawn-killing you infinitely. Did they get bullied in real life or are their brains just warped? Honestly, compared to those people, hackers are small potatoes—modders usually keep to themselves and don't affect anyone else, but griefers completely ruin other people's gaming experience. Those are the ones who actually deserve to be banned. I've played less than 30 hours online and I've been killed over 40 fucking times???????????

translation_en: A friendly suggestion to China: The web is crawling with games that scam kids out of their money and leave, but you do nothing. Every web page you click on has games with broken-ass Mandarin, but you do nothing. Games where you can buy hacks right off the official website, and you do nothing. You crack down on AAA games? Violence? Porn? Look at the ads plastered all over domestic websites, every single one of them is more naked than anything on STEAM. You don't manage any of that, but you come after STEAM. If you've got so much damn time on your hands, why don't you do something about the Chinese film industry? It's more deformed than Lu Benwei. Look at your CCTV, then look at the BBC. What a gap. You crush the cultural confidence you built up yourselves right back into the dirt. Why? Without reforming your own management methods, you still gotta drag a massive platform down with you. Sure, many Chinese players just treat STEAM as a game launcher, but at least it gave people an awareness of buying legit copies. Just when we're finally making some progress, you're about to beat us back to square one. What, you encouraging everyone to play pirated games now? Never mind about so-called democracy, why can't you just have a rating system? A rating system could solve most of these problems. Do you think this shit is fun? You "experts" are seriously retarded. Day in and day out you pull this useless crap. Why don't you just ban the internet altogether and stop letting normal people use it? Organising everyone to shout slogans and go farm fields every day??? Or why don't we just straight up regress back to primitive society? What I actually care about is if the games I bought become unplayable, who the fuck is going to compensate me? Perfect World, or the state? But I guess in the end, it'll just mean we players who insist on buying legit games take a total loss, and then we'll get mocked and smugly looked down on by the piracy snobs in real life. Retarded. Awesome job, my country, haha. Emperor Qin, this prosperous age is just as you wished. Some people and their friends grew up playing Legend of Mir and CS as kids, and none of them went around hacking people, killing people, or committing crimes. Nowadays, some brat watches Pleasant Goat and tries to roast other kids, so is that the fault of games and anime, or is it the fault of irresponsible parenting and schooling? Everyone knows the damn truth. Have you abandoned the goal of sticking to socialism for 100 years just like that? What is the Chinese Dream? Study hard, and leap the Great Firewall. Games belong to the ninth art. Any masterpiece game inherently contains the thoughts and philosophy of its creator. But given our country's currently closed-off values, foreign reflections on the future and bizarre fantasies just cannot be accepted by the NRTA. As things stand, between Steam and the various console factors, domestic games can still rake in mountains of money just by making garbage. They know that as long as the game's quality is barely passable, and they design some "micro-operations" for flex value, along with all kinds of horny character art, and cringe character models and lines, they can scam people out of cash. The plot of the game itself has to be ridiculous—it can't have depth; it has to be simple and easy to understand. Productions like this make way more money than games where you actually put serious thought into the plot and execution. Steam might seem like a lot of people know about it in China now, but before PUBG came out, if you walked down the street, hardly anyone even knew what Steam was. Actually, real-name verification in China is already ahead of foreign countries—UnionPay and WeChat Pay both strictly require an ID card. So why is there still such a delay in rolling out a game rating system? Because right now, whether something passes censorship is entirely up to the Ministry of Culture and the NRTA, who hold absolute decision-making power. There are no relevant laws or regulations that determine whether a game passes review. Back in the day, a domestic single-player game developer made a wuxia game and submitted it for review. Since they were a domestic developer, they knew the censorship system inside out, so before submitting they removed all the blood and dismemberment effects, and turned all the corpses black. But even then, it still failed review. The censors said that after killing an NPC, the player character only had to serve ten days in prison, which could easily cause a bad social impact. Later on, after endless revisions, it basically turned into a wuxia game where all you could do was ride a horse. Meanwhile, Tencent's *Moonlight Blade* lets you slaughter human enemies without facing a single consequence, letting you just keep on butchering. Doesn't that cause an even worse social impact? Yet *Moonlight Blade* passed review. Why does this happen? Tencent makes a fortune every single day; they can afford to pay. That small developer didn't have much money left after finishing the game. So the development of Chinese single-player games isn't about your production standards, nor is it about whether your marketing is on point—it's about whether you can afford to pay off the censors first. And what do the relevant Chinese departments claim their basis is when reviewing? It's the so-called social mainstream, the Core Socialist Values. What does this kind of feel like? Ancient monarchs would always find a statement that sounded legally and theoretically sound for their power—the Mandate of Heaven, "I am the True Dragon," claiming all their authority was bestowed by the heavens. And the Core Socialist Values serve this exact purpose: a tool to give their illegitimate, unlawful power and acquired benefits a seemingly reasonable justification. Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Macao are Special Administrative Regions; their social, economic, political, and cultural systems are completely different from the mainland. Has everyone ever thought about why that is? Actually, it's very simple: the crying baby gets the milk. Take Hong Kong, for example—if they had been handed the mainland system back at the '97 handover, they would have launched massive strikes and school boycotts, bringing normal society to a halt. Plus, at the time, many eyes both domestic and international were watching Hong Kong, which is why they are a Special Administrative Region. And what about us mainlanders? When they blocked foreign websites, we endured it. When they censored *World of Warcraft*, we endured that too. We've never once raised our voices to speak up for our own rights. And now they're escalating: the Steam China version is about to be launched. Best case scenario, a Chinese store drops, and all existing mainland region payment methods and low-price regional discounts get migrated over there. If we silently endure this time, what about the next? I'm afraid we're going to turn into North Korea's Kwangmyong. A lot of people treat all these things as a matter of course—whether it's blocking foreign websites, censoring games, *Baozou Dashijian*, or now Steam China. But what's the reality? Terrorists were active on Instagram and Twitter in Europe, but did they just lazily build a firewall and block those social media apps? No, they fought a cyber war against those terrorists and drove them off those platforms. If they can do that, why can't the CCP? Just because building a firewall is cheaper? Are our rights and our places for entertainment and leisure worth less than the cost of fighting a cyber war? Do Chinese people just have to compromise and swallow it, while foreigners get to protect their rights? Please spread these words far and wide. Speak up for your own rights and for Steam. I don't know which kind of "being represented" is worse: the kind they claim when they ban and censor *World of Warcraft*, *Baozou Dashijian*, and other free media, social platforms, and single-player/online games, claiming it's the will of the people and the players; or what I'm posting today representing the interests of Steam players. But I do know that everything I'm saying comes from the bottom of my heart. It's heartfelt, spoken with a mixed bag of feelings after going through all this bullshit. I'm speaking with a clear conscience, whereas they certainly aren't. I hope everyone spreads these words. I know 9/10 times it won't do shit, but how can you stay silent just because your voice is small? As an ordinary resident living in China who loves Steam and loves the joy Steam brings, this is all I can do. Thank you, everyone. Honestly, being a docile subject has zero benefits and only drawbacks. Because if you show obedience, they have to provide you with even less. Since you've already expressed compliance, why the hell would they care about your demands? As for so-called troublemakers, the government has to provide a lot more to maintain its rule and appease the populace. We see this right here at home: when they blocked foreign sites and censored games, we complied. And the result? Now Steam China is about to drop. Because you expressed obedience, they figure they can just push it out anyway since you'll just keep on complying. Whenever I think about the First Amendment of the United States and how Steam, this platform of free speech, allows me to speak out here, while the CCP is about to roll out Steam China and take all of that away, I get a flood of mixed emotions. Honestly, the things I want by speaking out aren't much. I'm not delusional enough to think life under capitalism is automatically going to be sunshine and rainbows. You still have to work hard yourself; you still have to grind for a dozen years to buy a house and a car. All I want is fewer restrictions and controls, and for the government to respect the rights of its citizens. But even something as basic as that is so damn hard. A hundred years ago in Beijing, Qing dynasty subjects helped foreigners set up ladders to scale the walls; a hundred years today, foreigners are helping Chinese people set up ladders to scale the firewall. A copy-pasta from an old R6 bro.

translation_en: At the end of 2018, thanks to sales, several of my friends got into the fifth part of GTA at once, and against the backdrop of their comments, I decided to roll out this review on how GTA 5 plays nowadays, in 2019, and whether it's worth checking out the 5th part of the series, which is already a synonym for computer and video games in general, alongside Mario, Tetris, and CoD. The game's story campaign, even in its sixth year of existence, looks and plays just great. It's very cinematic, all characters are brilliantly voiced and portrayed by Hollywood actors, on whom Rockstar didn't spare tons of cash. Here you will find an indecent number of brilliantly staged and seamless missions – from the opening tasks touching on the characters' personal problems that simply let you enjoy the game, to incredibly dynamic and well-thought-out heists. And even though the storyline itself is full of inaccuracies and presented in fragments – this doesn't interfere with the overall perception at all. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1066274440 But at the same time, you need to remember that GTA 5 is a satirical game that harshly mocks the lifestyle of modern man and consumer society itself, so despite the extreme brutality and Rockstar's signature don't-give-a-fuck attitude towards censorship, this game is a comedy, so you shouldn't expect a believable plot or realistic character personalities from GTA. There are no genuinely interesting characters here. Of course, watching them is very interesting, but it's impossible to empathize. Well, maybe with Michael) And what a city this is... Los Angeles, pfft, I mean Los Santos is fantastically huge and detailed. It's just amazing how a game from the PlayStation 3, albeit with the support of extra PC goodies, manages to deliver in 2019 the biggest, most beautiful, and most saturated city out of ALL currently existing games, where the content doesn't suffer from the size at all. You fall in love with this city at first sight. And note – not a single centimeter of copy-paste. It's just a magnificent sandbox. You can immediately see where almost three hundred million dollars of the budget and five years of development went. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1084633352 Even just driving around here is cool. Of course, you shouldn't expect car physics on the level of Project CARS, but nobody promised you the most plausible simulation either – right from the start, the game positions itself purely as an arcade, the goal of which is the maximum amount of your gaming pleasure. Considering that the game has one of the largest buying audiences in the world, I doubt it would have been a smart decision by Rockstar to make the car physics model more complex than it currently is. I don't want to learn how to drive in a game like this either – I want to sit down and go. And it works – you just need to find some rock among dozens of radio stations and drive off into the sunset. Graphically, everything is wonderful. Rockstar didn't skimp, and on PC the game arrived with a bunch of graphical goodies and even now looks simply remarkable. Moreover, there are even ultra-detail settings that can stun even modern graphics cards, but at the same time, everything is flexibly customizable – optimization here is top-notch, unlike the PC launch of the previous numbered installment. GTA Online is very controversial. On the one hand – playing with your kill team is genuinely fun and you can easily get lost in this world for dozens and hundreds of hours. On the other – with randoms, it's a pain in the ass, and that's if you can endure the constant long loading screens. In general, having your own team is welcome, but not mandatory. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1094846948 To date, the game has passed the threshold of 100,000,000 copies sold. Rockstar and GTA are still a genuine mark of quality in modern gamedev. In its genre, GTA still dominates like a busty broad in latex, thigh-high boots, and with a whip, who completely doesn't give a fuck about your safe word. This game has way too many pros to pay attention to any flaws. If you want to find out how one game can do more for the popularity of the gaming industry than ALL other games combined – just try Grand Theft Auto 5.

translation_en: [b]GTA: Online Review[/b] The title of this game is actually wrong. The correct name is GTA: Grindiest-Shit. I'm not kidding, if you don't want to pay-to-win, but actually want to buy anything in this game, you'll have to work your ass off 24/7. But first things first. The game has two main problems: greedy-ass developers and retarded players. [b]The game is hostile to beginners.[/b] You create a character, and... they just drop you into the city. That's it. What do you do? Where do you go? Why are you even here? Figure it out yourself. There are dozens of random icons scattered across the map, and your phone instantly blows up with hundreds of invites to join heists, missions, adversary modes, etc. Across the edges of the screen, you're constantly bombarded with messages offering you to take part in business battles or blow up someone's cargo. For the first while, you just feel totally lost online, with no clue what you're supposed to be doing. There's no clear goal, nobody explains a damn thing to you. You have to Google and YouTube everything about what you're supposed to do, how, and why. Getting your bearings on your own is an absolute pain in the ass. And that doesn't do the game any favors. [b]Phone calls.[/b] They will call you constantly. And it's fucking annoying! Every single time you log into the game, a bunch of bots will immediately call you demanding you buy various properties. And it doesn't matter if you're in the middle of a gunfight, or typing something in the game chat—the call will come through at the worst possible moment, throwing off your aim or wiping out whatever text you just typed. An in-game call is apparently more important than anything else. The only way to turn off this spam is to buy everything these bots are offering, and nothing else works. [b]Economy.[/b] Something tells me Rockstar's favorite Ninja Turtle is DONATello. The entire game is rigged around microtransactions. According to the devs, we should pay, and pay a whole fucking lot. And how do you force us to pay? That's right, skyrocket the prices on everything while driving earning potential down to absolute zero. Missions pay absolute peanuts, barely enough to cover your ammo costs. You can try making money through businesses, but first you gotta buy them for a shitload of cash, and then spend two more shitloads upgrading them because they're completely useless without upgrades. And then... hours upon hours of dreadful, mind-numbing routine. You have to endlessly haul supplies to your businesses from all over the damn map. The devs will conveniently mark your supplies on the map so literally anyone can see them. And if those "friendly players" blow it up, you start all over again. Then you gotta wait for the supplies to process into stock, and then you have to sell it. During the sale, other players can blow that up too. If your product gets destroyed, you get zero cash. And, once again, you start all over from hauling supplies. Incredibly fucking thrilling. You can buy a special cargo warehouse and haul crates. Not only is this the most profitable gig in the game, but it's also the most soul-crushing. Try filling up a medium-sized warehouse and you'll die of sheer boredom. And, again, if some trolls blow up your crates during a sale, instead of money you get a big fat dick. You can buy a vehicle warehouse and export cars, but super-aimbot NPCs will instantly turn them into Swiss cheese, severely cutting into your profits. Basically, the whole economy is designed to make you earn as little as possible while making everything cost as much as humanly possible, all to push you toward buying Shark Cards. The developers' greed is one of the two main problems with the game. The second main problem is… [b]Retarded players and cheaters.[/b] You'll say, "There are retards in every game, you can't hold that against the game itself!" I agree, but not in this case. You can't blame a game for idiots when the developers actually try to stop them. But Rockstar Games took their own special route, and instead of fighting the retards, they fucking reward them! You blew up someone's cargo? Here's some cash and RP. You messed up someone's session mission? Good job, buddy, here's your prize. The funniest part is that the reward is a cool 2000 bucks. Meaning, basically less than nothing. Yet, at every single opportunity, a horde of morons rushes to blow up everything in sight just for those pennies. And don't even get me started on session deathmatches, pointless and merciless. There's always some asshole on an Oppressor or a Hydra flying around and griefing everyone indiscriminately, making life miserable for everyone. And all this gay behavior is justified in chat with the classic excuse: "lol it's GTA bro!!!" Acting like a total piece of shit? Totally fine, it's just GTA, anything goes and it's practically encouraged. Normal games actually crack down on this kind of behavior, but not this one. And you know what else normal games crack down on? Cheaters. But not this one either. I have no idea what measures they take against them, but cheaters in GTA feel right at home. They can change the weather and time of day. They can hang UFOs in the sky. They can teleport players, lock them in cages, or attach random objects to them. Like a burning campfire, for instance. Cheaters can force-feed you millions of cash and RP, and all you can do is pray you don't get banned for it (you, not them). Steam reviews and internet forums are flooded with screams of people getting banned for absolutely no reason, or because cheaters forced a bunch of crap onto them. I'm sure a lot of those reviews are legit, there's just way too many of them. If not for the "Resource Monitor" trick that lets you clear out a session and play solo, GTA: Online would be completely unplayable. What kind of online game is it where one of the most satisfying things in the world is seeing the message "You are alone in this session," huh, Rockstar Games? Care to explain? https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1568200719 Playing heists with randoms is a whole separate saga. First, the game will spend half a day matching you with three absolute morons, each of whom is desperately gunning for a Darwin Award. Teamwork? Never heard of it. Someone fucks up—mission restart. Restart again, then someone quits and the whole heist falls apart. Back to square one, looking for players. Beautiful. Judging by the fact that people quit two out of every three missions, there is zero penalty for abandoning them. I honestly wish the game let me just hire bots... Running heists normally is only fun if you've got friends, then the game completely turns around and you actually start having a blast. But let me ask you: do you always have three friends lying around who happen to want to play GTA right this second? [b]Flying sci-fi bullshit and miracle weapons.[/b] Why, just *why* the hell did they add flying cars and rocket bikes, laser guns, and sniper rifles with explosive rounds to the game? All of this completely kills the atmosphere, turning the whole thing into a madhouse. This isn't Star Wars, for Christ's sake. On top of that, sessions are now flooded with this rocket-spitting flying trash, where a handful of griefers terrorize everyone, blowing up supplies, players, and your last remaining nerves. The community is howling for blood, begging the devs to yeet these vehicles out of the game, but the developers have never given a single shit about what sane players think. Though, I guess that's nothing new. [b]Aim-bot NPCs.[/b] In a lot of missions, the AI has been turned straight into Terminators. Instead of making missions actually difficult and well-designed, Rockstar just cranked up the NPCs' health, damage, and gave them god-tier aimbot. Everybody already knows what goes on in "Doomsday". But how about the bodyguards in the CEO "Headhunter" mission who can tank three sniper headshots (three fucking headshots from a sniper rifle, Carl!)?! Or those little Legolas wannabes who can bullseye you through the tiny window slits of an armored pickup with a full-auto burst while driving at top speed from a mile away? If a mission calls for a chase, enemy cars always spawn in a way that makes escaping literally impossible. They spawn right in front of your face and instantly open fire. You know what, why even bother, just teleport them right into the passenger seat next to me. GTA: Online isn't a bad game. It's got good, interesting ideas, and it's fun to play at its core. But it is fundamentally built around microtransactions. So thoroughly built around them that they didn't just tack monetization onto the game—they built the entire game *around* the monetization, with all the lovely consequences that come with it. And that completely overshadows all its good points. But as long as players are willing to finance the developers' greed, the devs are going to keep being greedy. Money ruins everything, as usual.

translation_en: I'll start by saying that I like GTA 5. A big open world, lots of vehicles and character abilities, and good graphics even today, despite the game being far from new. But what the developers are doing to it is, to put it mildly, disappointing. I'll try to do without swearing, although that's not easy in this case. Not only is the game turning more and more into "Star Wars," with all these flying motorcycles, the Deluxo flying car, the Batman car, jetpacks, and other bullshit—we're basically missing blasters for complete "happiness"—but the devs also failed to create a worthy counter to these "wonders of engineering." Just like it was back in the day with the Hydra, when any squeaker in that plane could ruin the mood even for experienced players, and back then there weren't any decent weapons to fight back, the Hydra easily dodged even homing missiles. Later on, the devs finally fixed their act by adding explosive ammo for the sniper rifle, and playing became more comfortable. Later they added the Oppressor, and the "angry" squeakers got all excited again because they once more had the chance to troll and kill players with impunity, but back then it wasn't so cut and dry, since experienced players could deal with that evolutionary mistake of a vehicle. But the developers felt that wasn't enough, and in an attempt to spark the interest of mindless little kids, they created the Oppressor MKII. Only they stepped on the exact same rake and forgot to add counter-weapons. As a result, life-offended "Jedi" fly around on these space motorcycles and blow everyone up, ruining the game for the whole session. Now, because of these dev screw-ups, session missions get ruined by these "cosmonauts." I don't give a crap about all these futuristic flying novelties; I bought GTA to drive ground vehicles, but the devs are forcing me to fly this fucking Oppressor just so I don't get attacked by these bottom-feeder flyers every 2 minutes. Plus, it all looks pathetic, straying further and further from reality. And as for cheaters, well, I honestly can't do without swearing there. Do I recommend this game? That's a tough question, I've personally lost the desire to play. I'll give it a No, until the devs come to their senses.

translation_en: A friendly suggestion to China: The web is full of games that scam schoolkids out of their pocket money, and you do nothing. You do nuthin' about web ads with sketchy-ass Mandarin. You do nuthin' about websites selling hacks. But you're cracking down on AAA games? Violence? Porn? Look at the shit all over domestic web ads—every single one of 'em is more exposed than anything on Steam, and you don't give a flying fuck, but you gotta stick your nose into Steam. If you got so much free time, why don't you do somethin' about the Chinese film industry? It's more deformed than Lu Benwei. Look at CCTV, then look at the BBC. What a joke. You crush your own cultural confidence that you worked so hard to build. Why? Refusing to reform your own management style, and dragging a massive platform down with you. Sure, a lot of Chinese players just use Steam as a launcher, but at least it got people realizing what buying legitimate copies means. Now that we're actually making some progress, you're dragging us back to square one. What, you wanna encourage piracy? Forget about democracy for a sec—why the hell can't we just have a rating system? A rating system would solve most of these issues. Is this shit fun for you? You "experts" are some real galaxy-brain geniuses. Since you spend all day doing useless shit, why don't you just ban the entire internet and forbid normal people from using it? Spend all day organizing rallies to shout slogans and farm the damn land?? Might as well just take us straight back to primitive society. What I actually give a shit about is if the games I bought stop working, who the fuck is gonna compensate me? Perfect World? Or the state? But let's be real, at the end of the day, us folks who insist on buying legit games are just gonna take it up the ass with heavy losses, and then get smugly mocked by some real-life piracy elitist douches. Real big-brain geniuses. Fucking impressive, my country,呵呵. Emperor Qin, this prosperous age is just as you wished. Some people and their friends grew up playing Legend of Mir and CS back in the day, and none of them went around hacking people to pieces or breaking the law. Nowadays, some brat watches Pleasant Goat and tries to roast another kid, so whose fault is it really—the game/anime, or the irresponsible parenting and schooling? Everyone knows the damn truth. Is this how you abandon the goal of sticking to socialism for 100 years? What even is the Chinese Dream? Study hard, flip the great firewall. Gaming is the ninth art. Any major masterpiece inherently contains the author's thoughts and philosophy. But given our country's currently closed-off values, foreign reflections on the future and bizarre fantasies are just too much for SARFT to handle. As things stand, between Steam and console restrictions, domestic games can still rake in a fortune just by churning out trash. They know that as long as the game quality is barely passable, and they slap in some "micro-operations" to flex on people, along with all sorts of horny character art, cringe character models, and cheesy dialogue, they can scam people out of their cash. The story has to be total nonsense—no depth whatsoever, kept nice and shallow. Making garbage like that actually makes way more money than a game where you seriously put thought into the plot. Before PUBG blew up, you could walk down the street and barely anyone would even know what Steam was. Actually, real-name verification in China is already way ahead of foreign countries. UnionPay and WeChat Pay both require a national ID card, so why the fuck are they still dragging their feet on a rating system? Because right now, the final say on whether culture passes censorship rests entirely with the Ministry of Culture and SARFT. There are zero relevant laws or regulations defining what actually passes censorship for a game. Back in the day, a domestic single-player dev studio made a wuxia game and submitted it for review. Since they were local devs, they knew the censorship system inside out, so before submitting it they stripped out all the blood and dismemberment, and turned all the corpses black. Even then, it still failed review. The censors said that since the player character in the game only has to serve ten days in prison after killing someone, it could easily cause a negative social impact. After going through round after round of changes, it eventually turned into a wuxia game where all you could do was ride a horse. Meanwhile, Tencent's Moonlight Blade lets you slaughter human enemies without facing a single consequence, letting you just keep on butchering. Doesn't that cause an even bigger social impact? Yet Moonlight Blade passed review. Why does this happen? Tencent is raking in cash hand over fist—they can afford to pay. That small indie studio was broke after finishing the game. So the development of single-player games in China isn't about how good your production quality is, nor is it about whether your marketing hits the mark. It's about whether you can afford to pay up first. And what do the relevant Chinese authorities claim their basis is during reviews? The so-called socialist mainstream melody, and core socialist values. What does this kind of shit remind you of? Ancient monarchs always found some pseudo-legal justification for their power—the Mandate of Heaven, "I am the True Dragon," claiming all their authority was bestowed by the heavens. Core socialist values are just acting as the exact same tool, giving their illegitimate, unlawful power and extracted benefits a veneer of reasonableness. Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Macao are Special Administrative Regions. Their social, economic, political, and cultural systems are completely different from the mainland. Has anyone ever thought about why that is? Actually, it's pretty simple: the squeaky wheel gets the grease. Take Hong Kong, for example—if they had been slapped with the mainland system back when they were handed over in '97, they would've launched massive strikes and school boycotts, bringing society to a grinding halt. Plus, back then, plenty of eyes both at home and abroad were watching Hong Kong closely. That's why they got to be a Special Administrative Region. And what about us on the mainland? When they blocked the foreign internet, we sucked it up. When they ruined World of Warcraft with censorship, we sucked it up again. We've never once raised our voices for our own rights. And now they're escalating. They're even rolling out a China-specific version of Steam. Best-case scenario, we get a dedicated China store, and all current mainland payment methods and regional pricing discounts get migrated straight over there. If we swallow this silently again, what the fuck comes next? Are we gonna turn into North Korea's Kwangmyong network? A lot of people treat all this shit like it's just the natural order of things—whether it's blocking foreign websites, censoring games, *Baozou Dashijian*, or now Steam China. But what are the facts? When terrorists are active on Instagram and Twitter in Europe, do they just lazily block those social media apps? No, they fight a cyber war against those terrorists and drive them off those platforms. If they can do that, why the fuck can't the CCP? Is it just because building a firewall is cheaper? Are our rights and our spaces for entertainment and relaxation really worth less than the cost of fighting a cyber war? Do Chinese people just have to compromise and take it up the ass while foreigners get to protect their rights? Please spread this message far and wide. Speak up for your own rights and for Steam. I don't know which kind of "representation" is better: the kind they claim when they ban and censor WoW, *Baozou Dashijian*, and other free media, social apps, and online games, claiming it's "the will of the people and players"? Or whether the stuff I'm posting today represents the interests of Steam players. But I do know that every word I'm saying here comes straight from the bottom of my heart, filled with a bitter mix of emotions after going through all this bullshit. I'm speaking with a clear conscience, which is more than I can say for them. I hope you guys will spread these words. I know it's 90% likely going to do fuck all, but how can you stay silent just because your voice is small? As an ordinary resident living in China who loves Steam and loves the joy Steam brings, this is all I can do. Thank you, everyone. Honestly, being a docile subject has zero upside and all downside. Because once you show compliance, they have to provide you with even less. If you've already made it clear you'll just roll over and take it, why would they give a shit about your needs? But those so-called "rioters"—the more they have to maintain control and appease the public, the more shit they actually have to provide. You see this all the time at home: when they blocked the foreign internet and censored games, we complied. And look where that got us? Now Steam China is on the way. Because you acted like obedient little sheep, they figure if they roll out a localized version, they can just shove it down our throats since we'll keep bending over anyway. Whenever I think about the First Amendment of the United States and how Steam, as a platform for free speech, allows me to vent here, while the CCP is rolling out Steam China to strip all of that away, I get this horribly bitter, mixed bag of feelings. Honestly, the things I want by speaking out aren't even that grand. I'm not delusional enough to think capitalism magically fixes everything and life instantly gets better. You still gotta bust your ass. You still gotta grind for decades just to afford a house and a car. All I want is a few less restrictions and controls, and for the government to actually respect the basic rights of its citizens. But even that's too much to ask. A hundred years ago in Beijing, Qing dynasty subjects were helping foreigners set up ladders to scale the walls; a hundred years later today, foreigners are helping Chinese people set up ladders to scale the firewall. translation_en: September 17, 2013. Grand Theft Auto V saw the light of day, the brainchild of Rockstar Games, which has since managed to end up in the hands of 80 million gamers. I have no complaints about the story mode—atmospheric, interesting, fun. This review will be about GTA: Online, not all that successful, by no means atmospheric, full of bad things, and with very little that is good. The Community. I think, just like in any online game, it’s basically awful. Screaming kids, people who just want to kill you for no reason, blowing up your cargo, hardly to get $2,000, but just for the "fun" of it, messing with your deliveries. If you just want to cruise around on an Imperator, for example, you won't be able to. Some animal on a super-duper canonical bike will fly in and shoot you until you leave the session. There are so many toxic players just itching to destroy you using the Oppressor Mk II, a futuristic flying motorcycle with homing missile artillery. Almost everyone wants to destroy you, and the flying cars, motorcycles, and post-apocalyptic vehicles from the latest update help them do it. Every action has a reaction, you'd think, and explosive rounds can help, but not against the Mk II. Small, nimble, relatively fast, chaff flares, and a bunch of gadgets to make it invincible, and it is. However, there are those ready to compete with them and even shred them to atoms—cheaters. Cheaters. There are a lot of them, in almost every session. And these aren't your ordinary aimbotters or wallhackers like in a bunch of other online games; these are demons incarnate. They can do anything: teleport anywhere, be immortal, rack up levels and money not just for themselves but for other players too (after which you'll get banned), blow objects up, set them on fire, annihilate every player in the session in a split second, blow up all vehicles, spawn any object anywhere on the map, make their vehicles invincible, spawn objects inside you (I even have a screenshot where they spawned a giant ball inside me and every car I got into blew up), spawn you in cages, and worst of all—crash your game. Yep, just like in good old SA-MP. And probably something else besides; all this is from my personal experience, over 300+ hours. But what forces them to cheat? There's no anti-cheat at all, they create anarchy, and normal players who are grinding are forced to switch sessions. The Grind is the next problem. The Economy. It is broken. Completely. A normal vehicle, a sports car without any tuning, will cost you $400k+; military vehicles like flying cars and bikes and rocket bullshit cost $2 million+. Want an Mk II to fight back? Buy a Terrorbyte for $1 million and then the Mk II for at least $3 million. Grinding via VIP Work—$100,000 an hour. Through heists and selling cars—up to 400k an hour (if you mix in CEO missions, but you still have to save up for an office and a vehicle warehouse first). Heists—depends on your luck (more on that in the next point). You won't make much on Adversary Modes, except when they have double payouts. The most profitable thing is grinding Doomsday Heists (stating the maximum possible income). By going against the game's mechanics, you can rake in up to $5,000,000 an hour on "Bogdan," and about $3,000,000 on the first act. However, this requires a facility, as well as completing setup missions, which needs more or less competent people, because the bots in this heist are broken, made of metal and blood. The hardest ones are stealing the Avenger (I did it on the second try without thermal vision, whatever; lots of comments saying this mission is too hard) and the Data Breaches, where you have to be careful, and you can't do that with randoms. Only after that can you monotonously and boringly grind away, buying various trinkets. Or through the quick job menu, so to speak, but nobody is going to give you more than 20-25%, plus you have to catch the exact final stage. I'm tired of writing, so I'll spell out why heists (except for Doomsday) are actually a bad way to make money. Heists (earnings if you aren't the heist leader; the numbers are a bit higher for them, of course): 1. The Fleeca Job. They give you peanuts, on average you get about $40-80k. An easy heist, but 90% of the time you'll get paired with either newbies or idiots who will spend half an hour hacking the bank vault via the Lester app on their phone, and I am not exaggerating. I remember waiting 20 minutes for a teammate to drill a bank safety deposit box; it was fun just standing there. 2. Prison Break. They give you more, but it's still small, around $100k on average. Better not play it with randoms, it drags out. I remember trying to beat it for 2 hours, considering I didn't die once and did everything right. Someone kept crashing the plane or helicopter, someone just died, someone crashed their parachute into the rocks, someone got run over by the cops, someone got blown up by their own teammate's helicopter—in a word, not fun at all. 3. Humane Labs Raid. They give you even more, the money actually feels like something now, around $150k. But the heist is no walk in the park, and that's the problem. Your teammates will drop like dominoes, though it's somewhat manageable. From experience, teammates didn't die *that* often, it's tolerable, but I think I just got lucky. 4. Series A Funding. The setups aren't the most interesting, but at least the finale actually tells you that this is GTA. Explosions, heavy machine gun fire, and chases. You get about $120k, the premise of the finale is very simple and banal—just kill the guys they tell you to kill, but often your drivers simply die, or the guy on the turret has such terrible aim that you have to help him out of the cab with a pistol. That's it. 5. The Pacific Standard. The most profitable and the hardest, you can get a whopping $300k, but you need to stock up on armor, miniguns, ammo, RPGs, and grenade launchers. In my experience, a lot of leaders quit the lobby because our guys just couldn't make it to the bikes, someone was always dying, and someone kept blowing themselves up. The fools carrying the money go first, losing 50% of the loot by the end. People blow themselves up, just die, crash their bikes into poles, cars, buildings, fly off mountains and smash into the ground, or just drop onto a ledge, die, and lose the money. And if you actually make it to the cliff you're supposed to jump off, someone will crash into the rocks a couple of times, and that's it, back to the start. As soon as someone gets in the boat, they get killed, back to the start again. Sure, you can grab a SWAT van and shortcut through the canyon, but apparently not everyone is that smart, and they still try to ride the bikes, losing more and more. Every day you forget a thousand things, let GTA Online be one of them.

translation_en: After clocking 300 hours, I think it’s time to write a review. A negative one... Let me explain. GTA 5 is Rockstar's brainchild that once made a huge splash in the gaming industry. If we're talking about the single-player game, everything is great there. But GTA Online is a sad mess (I don't want to lump single-player and online into the same garbage bin). This review is dedicated exclusively to the multiplayer game. The community. The main component of this game is its audience. I've played a lot of GTA Online, and I can state with confidence that the servers are overflowing with toxic players, angry kids, and absolute tryhards. I mean, if a player with unclear intentions heads your way, turn on passive mode or kill them, because in 90% of cases you won't be wrong. Sometimes it's impossible to buy clothes in a store without just getting shot. In every single session, you're guaranteed to find some ghoul on an Oppressor Mk II. Back in the day, you could at least somehow defend yourself against the tapeworms in tanks and jets. With the addition of the first Oppressor, the balance took a hit, and the Oppressor Mk II just ate the balance and shat it out. Cheaters haven't gone anywhere either... A few words about the updates. The updates are pointless, clownish, and not what people want. The latest update with the arena really tanked the FPS (maybe it's my PC, but the fact is that everything ran smoothly before the update). The updates have totally perverted the online mode, turning it into a pay-to-win piece of crap. It's very hard for a beginner to progress. Veterans shouldn't let their guard down either, since a random ban can fly your way at any time. To sum it up, we will never see the old online mode again, we can only watch it slide, regress, and degrade... UPD. I shared my opinion about GTA Online, don't take my criticism so personally. I had to close the comments because of one furious defender and shit-eater rolled into one. I don't want to start a war in the comments, totally annihilating this clown would take up too much space. To the rest of you crying about me ruining the game's rating just because of the online mode: grow some balls for fuck's sake and have some self-respect.

translation_en: Actually a great game. If you know the older GTA titles and love the story mode and the possibilities GTA offers, you'll be pleased. The world is top-notch, graphics in classic GTA manner, everything is super. GTA ONLINE: "Well, you wanna get punched in the face?!" Now, there is also the online mode, which is supposed to offer incredible multiplayer fun. Well, let's say maybe it did once... or rather, it's not for everyone... for players who want to kill everything and everyone, it's a super mode! For peaceful players who want to play with each other instead of against each other, probably much less suitable. After I bought the game two years ago, I celebrated it, playing missions together with friends or just with random people, wow.... was super fun. But even back then, there were always players who enjoyed just killing everyone running around in the open world, or maybe doing a 5-on-1. Then there were always cheaters, or as they're called in GTA Online, "modders" — which is an insult to any real modder. All the cheaters and griefers often just made it annoying. Ultimately, I needed a 1-year break from GTA. Now I thought to myself, let's play GTA again. Currently, as of Dec. 2018, I've been playing it again for 14 days. You'd think the game climate would be significantly better, or that it couldn't get any worse... But... MERCILESS. No matter what session you join, you will always find several players who love to use you as their punching bag, following the motto, fresh and new in GTA Online: "Hello I'm new here, fu—" BANG dead, "... Hey wait, stop" Bang dead. And these aren't fights, more like a slaughter. It's not about having fun, it's about crushing people. Either you're the victim or the perpetrator. And when you're down on the ground, even more so. Without skill, easy to become a super killer. Since release, Rockstar has continually brought new vehicles into the game. Update after update, there was always a new overpowered vehicle (e.g., the NoobBike / MK2). You don't even have to be good to kill all kinds of people like a psychopath. Like in a civil war.... It doesn't matter if you have a weapon or are a match for me, you are my victim now. Without Passive Mode, it's often completely impossible anymore. Passive Mode means people can't actually kill you, but if someone puts a bounty on you, you can't go into Passive Mode... but at best hide in your apartment, which is then the only safe place for you. But if the apartment is very far away, you might die 20 times on the way there, sure a great experience ^^... PAY TO WIN It's not 100% pay-to-win, but very much heading in that direction. Everything is very expensive, especially as a newbie it's not easy to grow in this world. Anyone under LVL 30 is often mercilessly kicked from lobbies during missions because such a low rank is sure to mess it up, etc. In demanding missions, players under LVL 100 are also gladly kicked. So getting to good missions that drop a bit more money is not that easy. Just a small example: for 80€ you get 8,000,000 GTA $. As an example, the MK2 (NoobBike) costs 2.9 - 3.8 million. To equip it with missiles, you have to buy the Terrorbyte truck for 1.4 million, the workshop for the truck 250k, and the missile upgrade costs extra on top of that... then a little bit here and there, and 80€ is gone fast... To achieve that without real money, you really have to grind for a long time, good stuff all costs a lot! HACKERS / CHEATERS / MODDERS As if that wasn't enough, there are also several cheaters every day that you meet in GTA who want to make life harder for you, e.g., spawn objects, set everyone on fire, manipulate the weather, etc., and lag everything out. Speaking of modding, if you still remember modding from GTA San Andreas, you'll be disappointed, because as far as I know, due to all the abuse of modding tools in the online mode, modding is completely forbidden and you quickly catch an online ban for it. LOADING TIMES The loading times are an absolute piss-take. Sometimes it takes 10 minutes to go from 0 to GTA Online, just to get kicked right back out. In-game, it's also unbelievable how long you sit in front of a loading screen over and over again. Or during so-called Heists (missions like robberies, bank jobs). You sit in lobbies waiting to start a heist. Now you sit there for 2-15 minutes waiting to get 4 players together, hoping the people who show up won't mess around or sabotage the mission, or just leave in the middle of a mission, causing it to fail for everyone. If everything goes well and you beat the mission, you hope (A) you don't get a disconnect during the loading screen for 1-4 minutes, and (B) the crew you just played the heist with doesn't want to just kill you right after as a pastime, which is why you always see people running away after a heist. No help is to be expected from Rockstar itself. Bugs or problems are never fixed with updates, unless you can get your hands on GTA$ too easily. The sad thing is that GTA offers so much potential, which isn't utilized in the slightest. It seems Rockstar has acquired a taste for pay-to-win. After the seemingly huge financial success with the overpowered vehicles in GTA Online, you can also see a big leap in that direction with "Red Dead Redemption 2". However, in my opinion, the fun of the game falls by the wayside... Therefore, I think no improvement to the current situation can be expected for GTA V Online. New missions, new vehicles, new nonsense, new modes... will certainly still come... but the conditions remain. That was a very negative view; there are also players who think the game is great as it is, but before buying, you should know what you're getting into. From my point of view, a game should generate excitement, relaxation, fun / joy, etc. But not frustration, and GTA is frustrating on so many points. That's why I can't recommend the game.
