translation_en: Video is in the works, stay tuned. If you found this helpful, feel free to give it a thumbs up. Picked up the game during the Summer Sale, played about a dozen hours of single-player before moving over to online. From a level 1 noob who didn't know shit and kept getting spam calls every day, to someone about to hit rank 100 as a faux-noob, it definitely took a lot of effort. Because I hate reading guides, I learned a lot of things the hard way. So, I'll share some small details and a beginner's guide. When you first start out and buy an apartment, I recommend Eclipse Towers—well, the cheap apartment near the slope by Eclipse Towers, should be around 100k or so. Just buy this one, worry about the others later (if you aren't planning to buy the bedroom in the office, I recommend the 1M office right next to that one; if you do want the bedroom, you can buy the one behind the Arcadius Business Center, Integrity Way I think, buying that one lets you do heists too). Why buy this cheap apartment by the slope? Because if you run around the building, you can steal a specific car, the modded version of the "Ubermacht Sentinel XS." There's a yellow one and a purple one. The yellow one sells for around 15K, the purple one for about 18K. Doesn't matter which, just steal it when you see it. The garage has six slots, so just steal them and store them. Car sell cooldown is 48 minutes, so let's say you play for an hour. If you grind 10 hours a day, you're guaranteed to make 130k–150k, making your money back instantly. After I bought the apartment, I just kept grinding Martin's "Dispatcher" mission series. I highly recommend the one at the airport where you blow up the planes; it's quick and convenient. Slap a suppressor on the default pistol and you can solo it. I was doing it stealthily like that when I was level 9. Random teammates are seriously annoying as fuck—they have more guns and firepower than me, but you guys end up scaring the targets away?! Every time I have to chase them down in a jet, what a waste of time. Secondly, the ones with multiple assassination targets are fine too, two people is enough. One goes to the mansion area, the other starts on a motorcycle. The mansion guy strikes first, once that's done, the motorcycle guy moves in. Then wait for the mansion guy to head back into the city, find a place with a plane, and fly over. The motorcycle guy can chase and kill the sports car target while waiting. Once the two meet up, you can take out the remaining targets: one is on top of a construction site roof—remember to use third-person, first-person sucks for that. The last one is a helicopter, just fly up in front of it and take out the pilot. There's also the one where you whack some gang; you can go through the back door to take out their boss and leave through the back door too, very fast. Of course, if you think doing assassinations with teammates is too much of a hassle, you can also do solo missions like "Out of Court Settlement," or "Repo I, II," which can all be done by one person. Do one or two assassinations and you'll差不多 have enough to sell a car. Combine these two methods until you can buy an Armored Kuruma. Once you have the Kuruma, you can solo any mission. Save up some money and buy the high-end apartment mentioned earlier, then you can grind heists. Just a heads up, if you're under level 40, the farthest you can get is Series A (correction: The Humane Labs Raid), the later heists have level requirements. Now let's briefly talk about some beginner pain points for heists and some essential gear. Gear: Buy a Heavy Utility Vest from the clothing store to reduce damage taken. Weapons: - Pistol: Armor-Piercing Pistol (buy at rank 36), or you can buy some revolver [spoiler](once the R8 speaks, your parents' efforts go up in smoke)[/spoiler], customize it yourself. - SMG: Micro SMG (the one on the left wall; due to translation issues, there are two micro SMGs with the same name, but I recommend the left one. Upgrade it with an extended mag and grip, leave the rest for later); optional choice: Combat PDW (comes with a suppressor and upgradable 100-round drum mag), Gusenberg Sweeper (upgradable 50-round drum, high damage, massive spread, can tide you over until the Combat MG, but not super useful, I mainly bought it because I like the gun, wouldn't really recommend). No need to buy any other SMGs. - Assault Rifle: Type 95 (QBZ-95/Bullpup) or Special Carbine, or buy both. Both of these have MK2 upgrades. I mainly recommend the Special Carbine because you can buy it at rank 1. - Rifle: Marksman Rifle (semi-auto sniper), Heavy Sniper (unlocked at rank 90). - Shotgun: Free Sawed-Off (okay for assassinations), Assault Shotgun. None of the others are recommended, especially the Heavy Shotgun—it hits like a single point, not an area. Because I love shotguns, I bought them all, and in the end, I used the Assault Shotgun the most. - Heavy Weapons: All of them. - Throwables: Sticky Bombs (there's a way to get them for free, and they're great), maybe add grenades or jerry cans for grinding "Repossession" (Blow Up). - Melee Weapons: Uh, does this really matter? Fine, the Easter egg hatchet and the knife, that's it. Fleeca Job: Only tricky part is getting the car, but if you wear heavy armor and use a car as cover to shoot heads, it's easy. Nothing else to it. Prison Break: No real difficulty, just a few details. For the police cruiser and sports car setup, just get a wanted level and steal a cop car—who has time to search around for one, seriously? For the cargo ship, you can climb the tower next to it, snipe from a distance, and parachute down (left click). As for the finale, just fly the plane head-on against the other plane, easy to dodge. Humane Labs Raid: Only one tricky part, the Key Codes setup. 4 spawn points, two on top of the building, two at the bottom. Guys *will* come out of the alley to the right of the buyer, and they have heavy firepower. Toss a grenade over there the second the cutscene ends. Grenade launcher is even better for the rooftop guys. Series A Funding: Nothing difficult here, smooth sailing the whole way. Pacific Standard: Doesn't seem hard either, nothing special to watch out for. PS: Once you finish playing, you'll realize Online is a prequel to the single-player story, and a lot of details in single-player match up with this. For example, in Mike's first heist, when he goes to see Lester, Lester mentions having some unruly guys—those are the players. Later on he calls us mutes, psychos, and stuff, which are all descriptions Online used for players. Plus, through Series A Funding, you find out why Trevor is so "attached" to that action figure, why he's broke as hell, and why he has to wipe out nearby gangs: because Trevor basically wiped most of them out in Series A! Not to mention, just the Series A finale alone takes out at least 75 Lost MC members. Get your heists up to Humane Labs, sell some cars, mix in some grinding, and you'll have over a million. At this point, you have two paths for progression. If you have friends, you can start a Motorcycle Club (MC); if not, stick to being a CEO. Of course, if you want to buy the Oppressor, you'll still need an MC even if you're a CEO. For CEO, I personally just bought a cheap small warehouse for cargo, felt pretty decent. You're gonna need to buy Special Cargo anyway, so getting a small warehouse doesn't hurt. To source cargo, either use the Kuruma or a motorcycle. Buy 3 crates at a time—no matter what, you're guaranteed to get at least 2, and most of the time you can grab all 3 in one go. Once you hit 1.5 million, buy a Vehicle Warehouse and start import/export. Selling a car has a 20-minute cooldown; I recommend keeping the Standard and Mid-range cars and only selling Top Range. After that, you can save up for the Buzzard attack chopper. Once you have it, you can combine cargo and car sourcing. Like buying a large warehouse... Next up is saving for a bunker and all that stuff. At this point, the Online portion of the game is basically wrapped up, and I'm about ready to quit. It's too exhausting, you can't just play this one game forever, and it's super grindy. For bunker upgrades, just the first two. If you're going to go AFK/idle, get all of them. Installing the shooting range lets you restock throwables like grenades and RPGs, can install that later though. The quarters are a must-buy. If you want to buy the Caddy, get the cheap one; the expensive one handles like shit. For the Mobile Operations Center (MOC), just buy the second cab and the Personal Vehicle Storage + Weapon/Vehicle Workshop. If you want to sweat and grief people in free-roam, change the living space into the Command Center. Let's talk vehicles: - Kuruma is a must-have, used for grinding missions and heists. - APC, Insurgent for free-roam PvP. - The absolute peak of PvP is the Hydra; if you're good at flying it, you don't need to care about anything else. - Try out other vehicles as you play, no need to buy everything. If you're interested and have the cash, go ahead, otherwise forget it. Anyway, that's GTA Online for you. Play until rank 120, buy a bunker, upgrade key vehicles and weapons, then play through the Doomsday Heist to experience it, and finally try out all the contact missions, and you're pretty much done. There's nothing else to do. Sure, you can go buy yachts and stuff, but I don't think spending too much time on that is a wise choice. There are other much better virtual worlds waiting for you. As far as Online goes, you've pretty much beaten the game at this point. If you found this helpful, feel free to give it a thumbs up. If you think there's too much text and it's hard to read, feel free to leave a comment, and I'll try to make a video out of it (even though similar ones already exist). Update, my thoughts after buying the bunker and upgrading weapons: First off, nobody needs to buy any SMGs, because MK2 weapons let you upgrade the default pistol to have stats similar to the AP Pistol, plus it doesn't even have that high AP damage, so it's awesome. Do not recommend buying the Special Carbine; once upgraded, you get stuck with an awkward 60-round mag limit. I pick the Type 95 instead. For the Heavy Shotgun, recommend adding explosive rounds before buying. In the SMG category, just buy the Combat MG. Better to leave the slot empty than buy the others, they suck. Snipers can all be upgraded, not sure what the muzzle brakes and stuff actually do yet. The heavy revolver, once upgraded, rivals the Heavy Sniper in damage. It finally redeems the R8 and Desert Eagle from being relegated to just "scout" snipers in CS:GO. That's it.

translation_en: [quote=] Home sweet home [/quote] Grand Theft Auto V, also very well known as "GTA 5", is an action-adventure game set in a completely open world, being the seventh game released in the Grand Theft Auto series, launched in 2013, re-released with a remastered version in 2014 for the new generation of consoles and PC, published by Rockstar Games. [h1] Story [/h1] This game shook up the story mode by having not just one character, but three. The game takes place in the fictional city of "Los Santos", which represents Los Angeles. Franklin, Michael, and Trevor are fed up with their lives and end up teaming up to pull off multi-million dollar heists. [b]Michael:[/b] He's a professional thief who left the criminal life many years ago, and, sick of his life and family, ended up making a deal with the FIB, getting back into crime. [b]Trevor:[/b] He is what we call pure insanity in the flesh, someone with nothing to lose, a drug addict, a massive hothead, and also Michael's best friend—or at least he was before they quit the criminal life. [b]Franklin:[/b] He's a young, ex-gangster, very skilled with cars, though not as much with crime, but he's super ambitious for money. That's when he met Michael, who helped him get into the criminal underworld. [h1] Graphics [/h1] The game's graphics are really nice and got even better in the remastered version. The problem is that with every new game released nowadays, GTA V's graphics start to look a bit dated, but I still consider them excellent. Of course, when GTA came to PC, the famous mods arrived too, and there are graphic mods like Redux, NaturalVision, VisualV, Reshade, among others... that make the game look surreal. The only downside to these mods is that they can't be used in GTA Online, even if it's just a minor tweak. [h1] Gameplay [/h1] GTA's gameplay features either a 3rd-person or 1st-person perspective, runs very smoothly, and got a lot of improvements over Grand Theft Auto IV. The player can use melee attacks with close-combat weapons or firearms, and can also use cars, motorcycles, bicycles, aircraft, airplanes, helicopters, boats, speedboats, jet skis, and go on foot. [h1] Settings [/h1] The game features incredible settings, like the beautiful city of Los Santos, with tons of places to explore. There's also another small town, also known as "Trevor's town": Sandy Shores, which is more rural, with fewer urban areas, inhabited by a community with a more country culture. [h1] Open World [/h1] This is one of GTA's richest aspects—the open world. The attention to detail is incredible, and since the map is huge, there are tons of things and possibilities for you to do. It's almost surreal how closely each location and landmark matches the real city of Los Angeles. And one of the best things to do in GTA is just messing around and having fun with your friends in this open world, or even in single-player with some mods; it's guaranteed fun. [h1] Soundtrack [/h1] The music inside this game is fantastic, just like in all other GTAs. They picked out awesome tracks that don't get old easily. Another neat little detail is that there are Brazilian songs on the in-game radio stations. I've only heard one so far, but in YouTube videos, I've noticed a few different ones, and that's really cool to see in GTA. If you want to buy the game, I recommend waiting for a sale because it gets really cheap. Anyway, Grand Theft Auto V is a masterpiece that you need to have in your library, that needs to be appreciated, and definitely played a whole lot.

translation_en: A friendly piece of advice to China: The internet is full of games that scam kids out of their money, and you do nothing about it. Web ads open up to games with terrible Mandarin, and you do nothing about it. Official websites selling cheats, and you do nothing about it. You're cracking down on AAA games? Violence? Pornography? Look at the images on domestic web ads everywhere; every single one is more exposed than Steam, and you don't give a shit, yet you come after Steam. You have the luxury of time, why not go manage the Chinese film industry? It's more deformed than Lu Benwei. Look at your CCTV, then look at the BBC. What a gap. You crush the cultural confidence you built up yourselves, and for what? Instead of reforming your own management methods, you drag a massive platform down with you. Even though many Chinese players just use Steam as a launcher, it at least gave everyone a sense of copyright awareness. Just as we're finally making some progress, we're getting hammered back to square one. Are you encouraging people to pirate games? Never mind so-called democracy, why can't we have a rating system? A rating system could solve most of these issues. Is this fun for you? You "experts" are seriously retarded. You spend your days pulling this useless bullshit—why don't you just ban the internet altogether and stop letting normal people use it? Go organize some slogan-chanting and farming instead? Or just straight-up regress back to a primitive society. What I actually care about is if the games I bought become unplayable, who do I go to for compensation? Perfect World, or the state? But at the end of the day, it'll probably just mean us players who insist on buying legitimate copies take a total loss, only to get mocked and smugly looked down upon by the real-life piracy elitists. Fucking retards. You're awesome, my country, haha. Emperor Qin, this prosperous age is just as you wished. Some people and their friends grew up playing Legend and CS as kids, and none of them went around hacking, slashing, or breaking the law. Now you've got spoiled brats watching Pleasant Goat and trying to roast other kids—is that really the fault of games and anime, or is it the fault of irresponsible parenting and schooling? Everyone knows the damn truth. Have you abandoned the goal of sticking to socialism for 100 years just like that? What is the Chinese Dream? Study hard, get the fuck out of China. Gaming belongs to the ninth art. Any major blockbuster inherently contains the author's thoughts and philosophy, but given our country's currently closed-off values, foreign thoughts on the future and bizarre fantasies are just not acceptable to the State Administration of Press and Publication (SAPPRFT). As for domestic games right now—between Steam and console factors—you can still make a fuckload of money just by making trash. They know that as long as the game quality is barely passable, they can design some "micro-operations" to flex with, along with all sorts of lewd character art, edgy-ass character models, and cringe dialogue, and they'll still scam people out of their money. The plot of the game has to be absolute garbage, lacking any depth, making it brain-dead simple. Making shit like this actually earns you way more money than a game where you seriously put thought into the plot. Before PUBG blew up, even if Steam seemed widely known in China, if you walked down the street, hardly anyone actually knew what Steam was. Actually, real-name verification in China is already way ahead of foreign countries; both UnionPay and WeChat Pay require an ID card. So why the fuck haven't they rolled out a rating system yet? Because right now, whether something passes censorship is entirely up to the Ministry of Culture and SAPPRFT, and there are no relevant laws or regulations to determine whether a game passes review. Back in the day, a domestic single-player game developer made a wuxia game and submitted it for review. Since they were a domestic studio, they knew the censorship system inside out, so before submitting, they removed all blood and dismembered limbs, and turned all the corpses black. But even then, it still failed the review. The censors said that the player character in this game could just serve ten days in prison after killing someone, which could easily cause a negative social impact. Later on, they kept modifying it until it turned into a wuxia game where you could literally only ride horses. Meanwhile, Tencent's *Moonlight Blade* has zero consequences after slaughtering human enemies—you can just keep on massacring. Doesn't that cause a much bigger social impact? Yet *Moonlight Blade* passed the review. Why does this happen? Tencent makes a fortune every single day; they can afford to pay up, whereas that small developer had no money left after finishing the game. So the development of Chinese single-player games isn't about your production standards, nor is it about whether your marketing hits the mark; it's about whether you can afford to pay the bribe first. And what claim do relevant Chinese departments base their censorship on? The so-called "mainstream melody" of society, the core socialist values. What does this kind of thing feel like? Ancient monarchs always found a legal-sounding justification for their power: the Mandate of Heaven, "I am the True Dragon, and all my power is bestowed upon me by the heavens." The core socialist values just act as a tool for that exact purpose—giving themselves a seemingly reasonable justification for illegitimate, illegal power and the benefits they reap. Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Macao are Special Administrative Regions; their social, economic, political, and cultural systems are completely different from the mainland. Has anyone ever wondered why that is? Actually, it's very simple: the crying baby gets the milk. Take Hong Kong, for example—if they had been handed the mainland system back during the '97 handover, they would have gone on massive strikes and student boycotts, bringing society to a complete halt. Plus, back then, many eyes both domestic and foreign were watching Hong Kong, which is why they are a Special Administrative Region. And us mainlanders? When they blocked the foreign internet, we endured it. When they censored *World of Warcraft*, we endured that too. We've never spoken up for our own rights, and now it's getting worse and worse. The Steam China version is about to drop; the best-case scenario is that a localized Chinese store comes out, and all existing mainland region payment methods and regional pricing discounts get transferred over to it. If we silently endure this time too, what's next? Are we just going to turn into North Korea's Kwangmyong intranet? A lot of people treat all this as if it's completely normal, whether it's blocking the foreign internet, censoring games, *Baozou Dajishi*, or now the Steam China version. But what are the facts? In Europe, there are terrorists operating on Instagram and Twitter—did they just simply build a firewall and ban these social media apps? No, they fought a cyber war against those terrorists and drove them off those platforms. If they can do that, why can't the CCP? Is it just because building a wall is cheaper? Are our rights and our spaces for entertainment and relaxation worth less than the cost of fighting a cyber war? Do Chinese people just have to compromise and suffer in silence while foreigners get to protect their rights? Please spread these words far and wide. Speak up for your own rights and for Steam. I don't know which version of "being represented" is better: the one they claim represents the will of the people and gamers when they ban and censor *World of Warcraft*, *Baozou Dajishi*, and other free media, social apps, and online/single-player games; or the things I'm posting today, which represent the interests of Steam players. But I know that everything I'm saying here comes straight from the bottom of my heart, spoken from genuine emotion and a kaleidoscope of bitter feelings after going through all this bullshit. I'm speaking with a clear conscience, whereas they certainly aren't. I hope everyone shares these words. I know it's 9 out of 10 times useless, but how can you stay silent just because your voice is small? As an ordinary resident living in China who loves Steam and loves the joy Steam brings, this is all I can do. Thank you, everyone. Actually, being a submissive citizen has zero benefits and only drawbacks. Because if you show obedience, the things they need to provide you with become even fewer. Since you've already expressed submission, why would they give a shit about your needs? On the other hand, the so-called "rioters"—for the sake of their own rule and to appease the public, the things the government has to provide will naturally be much greater. You see this domestically all the time: when they blocked the foreign internet and censored games, we complied. And what happened? Now the Steam China version is about to roll out, because since you always submit, they figure that once they launch it, you'll just take it because you'll keep bowing down anyway. Whenever I think about the First Amendment of the United States and how Steam, this platform of free speech, allows me to voice my thoughts here, while the CCP is about to launch Steam China and take all of that away, I am overcome with a complex mix of emotions. To be honest, what I want when I speak out isn't much. I'm not delusional enough to think life under capitalism would magically be better; you still have to put in the work yourself, and grind for a decade just to afford a house and a car. All I want is a few less restrictions and controls, and for the government to respect the rights of its citizens. But even something that simple is too damn hard. A hundred years ago in Beijing, Qing dynasty subjects helped foreigners climb ladders to scale the wall; a hundred years later today, foreigners are helping Chinese people climb ladders to scale the firewall. ------ *Reposted from the internet*

translation_en: I want to point out right away that this will be exclusively about GTA 5 Online. Where should I even start? I'll probably start with the fact that the team that developed and continues to support the online mode made a huge number of small (and not so small) oversights and completely fucked up what could have been one of the juiciest online modes in the world. And I will provide concrete examples of this: 1). The most important oversight, in my opinion, is that cheating, modded money drops, and so on are completely unpunished. Yes, my little buddy, go order a cash drop from Diletanta, oopsie-daisy, nothing will happen to you for that. Bans are handed out randomly. And since GTA 5 Online is a breeding ground for cheaters, the next problem stems directly from this, which is the game's community. It is, without exaggeration, disgusting. In public lobbies, all players (not just Russians, by the way) completely fail to see the difference between PvP (mutual consent for a 1-to-1 competition) and "what the fuck are you bugging me for, you unhinged animal" (here, I think, everything is clear). And the most insulting part is that Rockstar themselves egg players on into this scumbag behavior. Here's an example: you're carrying your little crates around, making some money, and out of nowhere some greaseball in a Deluxo screams like Papich and blows you the fuck up because a message pops up across his whole screen saying: "Player [Your Gamertag] is transporting cargo, interfere with them to get money and RP," and he's fucking happy with this option, he doesn't even give a shit that because of him you might lose 2,220,000 in-game dollars. And yes, I know you can cut your internet for 10 seconds and stay in the lobby all by yourself. I have a problem with the way things are set up in the first place. Because some of the people who read this are gonna go run and Google right now: "GTA Online how to stay in a lobby alone." 2). The second problem with Online is probably those very same "small (and not so small) oversights." All my disgust for the online mode is basically built on them alone. 2.1. One of the most annoying things is the weapon wheel layout. In a public lobby you can run around with whatever weapons you actually need, but in missions and, most importantly, in Heists, your custom weapon loadout is not available. You have to walk around with all the junk you've ever bought, and there's no way to fix this (Americans are shocked too, this true problem still hasn't been fixed). 2.2. Fucked controls. In the Doomsday Heist, during the mission to rescue the IAA agent, my character was climbing down a ladder (on the tower) and stepped onto the railing instead of the platform, which of course he didn't like. The animation triggered as if the character had stumbled, after which he enthusiastically face-planted all the way down. When getting on and off ladders, you have to do it either in aim mode or in first person, so you don't smash your head against the wall, or whatever else is nearby. It also happens frequently that the character, while in aim mode, doesn't zoom in (using the mouse wheel), but thinks he hasn't started aiming yet and scrolls through the weapon wheel instead. The character can't get into vehicles normally, runs around them multiple times, stalls in place, and even when holding F still gets into the driver's seat. I won't even mention the underwater controls. And there's a metric fuckton of this kind of bullshit. 2.3. When calling in a Buzzard (via the Boss menu), it can spawn halfway inside a building (that happened to me near LSIA, if anyone decides to pick a fight over it). Bikers lose their minds when you start up a chopper's engine, blindly ramming right into it while shouting that overused-as-fuck "OH MY GOD." 2.4. Now this is not a small oversight. Since there are 3 main things you can do in the game, specifically: grind businesses, play jobs (races, adversary modes, and other such bullshit), and grind again, but this time on heists. Therefore, 33% (or even more) of the game is just grinding for money. (Based on this, I have a separate question for cheaters: "What the fuck are you even playing for?") So, supply theft and sale missions, etc., are retarded. They are either boring (Special Cargo, biker business money laundering), or difficult (Special Cargo, Bunker). All this bullshit, according to Rockstar's logic, is supposed to be done in groups of three or even four. NPCs spawn on the opposite side of the road 10-15 meters away from you and shoot accurately, painfully, and nonstop. A regular NPC in these missions can kill you with an Uzi while you're trying like a fucking invalid to lock onto him with the Buzzard's retarded-ass missiles, which sometimes can't even hit a stationary target. There were times when I was sitting in a barely moving "motor home" (you sometimes have to use this piece of shit to haul special cargo to the warehouse) and killing 8-10 cars of rabid NPCs. NPCs also completely don't give a shit that the Kuruma is unbulletproof; their hit system is calculated by percentages, just like in fucking old games, and they shoot right through the doors and any armor plating on the Insurgent Pick-up. They don't give a flying fuck that players are supposed to break bulletproof glass before getting to your head. You can find yourself dead inside a bulletproof car where every single window is intact. To wrap up the grind in GTA Online: you often need help with grinding; you can only grind adequately in a bugged lobby (without players); the most profitable business in the game is Special Cargo, which is super tedious, and the NPCs on those missions are super annoying; for selling large batches of stock, particularly for the MC and bunker, you need at least 3 players (you physically won't have time to do it all yourself; I'm talking about cases where you have 3-4 delivery vehicles, and even then sometimes you barely manage to deliver 2 yourselves). I'll stop talking about the grind here, or the flashbacks are gonna start rolling in. 2.5. Civilian NPCs. This is fucking insane. I'm just speechless. They were intentionally made wildly annoying and stupid. God forbid someone is shooting nearby, they will start screaming obscenely, pulling a U-turn across a double yellow right in front of your nose, crashing into you, and they also just love breaking traffic laws (for no reason at all, meaning you don't have a pursuit going, no cops on your tail, the bots just love pulling dumb shit). It's especially fucking awesome when you're delivering a shipment of weapons from the bunker to some run-down neighborhood, and right there to the sound of heavy machine gun fire from military jeeps, exploding charges, and the thumping of Buzzard rotor blades, a bunch of pissy Vagos show up to join the war. And they sure as fuck won't attack the aggressors (meaning Merryweather), they'll definitely shoot at you instead. There was another case: I was riding down the highway on a chopper, just chilling (no pursuit, no stars, nobody else in the lobby) and some dumb cunt driving right toward me crosses the double yellow line and head-on fucking plows into me, followed by: "Oh my god! Are you okay?" WHAT THE FUCK?! WHAT KIND OF ORDER IS THIS?! Phew, damn! (Sorry for the swearing). Well, I think you understand that there is an uncounted number of situations like this. Okay, let's move on. 2.6. Stores. Excessive "attention to detail" in convenience stores — they can literally run out of food. One question — what the fuck for? By the way, there were times when the clerks completely disappeared from the gun shops. 2.7. Annoying bullshit. The weapons workshop inside the MOC or Avenger becomes unavailable. Helmets disappear when walking indoors. When trying to drive an Oppressor into the MOC/Avenger, you first use the boost, and while the boost meter hasn't refilled yet, you have to manage to press E to get inside, and the exact same bullshit happens with vehicles that drop mines (the outcome there, I think, is pretty obvious). The sniper rifle's zoom resets every time you exit aim mode. You can't return your personal vehicle if you're standing right next to it, and you can't call a new one either, plus there's a cooldown on this piece of shit; you can only bypass this nonsense using the MC menu. I can't remember anything else right now. 2.8. Customization and character creation. The character creation tool is absolute trash. Every player looks like a clone. No matter who you try to make, they still look like an ugly freak. There's a ton of clothing, but that's just because Rockstar loves to take one field jacket, slap about 10 different camos on it, make open and buttoned-up variants, and boom—you've got 30 jackets in every clothing category. Some military boots and flight boots exclusively match the heist crew pants. Why? Well, fuck knows. 3). Support (like, customer support) and the developers' attitude toward the game. "Where's the support? There it is, right there, wrapped around a dick" (Sam Houser). And that's no joke. The team of guys working on Online doesn't give a single solitary fuck and they couldn't care less about your complaints. This is probably the root of all problems. Well, I guess that's about it. All the venom is out of my system, thanks to everyone who read this toxic eruption. So, basically, what am I getting at all this for? Guys, don't play GTA Online, practice brain hygiene.

translation_en: It's genuinely absolute bullshit by now how some companies treat their players, but up until now it hadn't affected me, so only now have I had the "pleasure" of experiencing Rockstar's horrific support. Here's how it went:.....I played online a bit again and then disconnected totally normally like always. When I want to keep playing the next day, the game tells me I'm banned until August 1st (almost a full month) and that on top of that all my online characters have been reset.....gee, thanks. I'd like to point out that I have genuinely never modded in GTA V, I don't cheat, I have no add-ons installed etc., everything is 100% vanilla for me. On top of that I've never trolled or insulted anyone, it never goes beyond a "gg" after a successful round at most, voice chat usually runs through Team Speak. So I look for the support page and find a somewhat clunky form, type my problem into it and hope for the best. The reply actually comes within 24h as promised, which doesn't mean it's good. Some support woman writes to me curtly that a ban is unavoidable and that my characters are reset, that's it. It's not like you can select "I don't want to be banned" in the form. If she had even looked at my profile, she easily would have noticed that I neither own much nor have a high rank or anything like that... I earned everything honestly and the hard way. She apparently didn't even read my email either, since I expressed that exact thing in it again. I then looked around the net a bit and found out that some hackers can flag you for the ban filters and the BattleEye filter or whatever the fuck that is just kicks you out. You don't have to be a rocket scientist to research something like that, but Rockstar simply doesn't give a single fuck about these losses. I've seen enough hackers flying through the city making it rain money... or spawning Avengers everywhere. Rockstar apparently does fuck all against that, they'd rather kick out the players who did nothing. For a game that still costs 60 Euros after YEARS, you should expect support that can actually make three mouse clicks to realize that I definitely didn't do anything that would even remotely justify such a ban, but no, as a response I just get told the exact same thing the game already told me itself. I'd get a refund for this joke of a game, but you can be damn sure Rockstar has stuffed enough cotton in both ears there too. You get more intelligent support on some abandoned ARK or Minecraft servers than at this money-laundering operation called GTA V. If you have 60 bucks in your hand, you're better off buying three Early Access survival games that get abandoned by the developers after a year, or something like Just Cause 3 (which also has a great multiplayer mode) or Fallout or something, just not this joke of a game. By GTA VI at the latest, it'll probably be over anyway, then the only thing left in support will be Yahoo chatbots and ENDLESS loading times, and if you don't use cheats you'll genuinely stand out. Generally, there are enough programs online that easily bypass GTA Online's ridiculous filters and let you happily cheat everything in. Maybe I should just do what Rockstar accuses me of, maybe I should really just happily load up on mods and cheats and then get on everyone's nerves just like hackers do. That way Rockstar definitely wouldn't find me and maybe I could also make sure that other players who played honestly just get completely obliterated with a ban they didn't deserve. Is that what you want, Rockstar? Or do you not give a single shit anyway? Real piece of shit game.

translation_en: My first time writing a review. I just want to tell a sad story, a sad fact. The online mode's anti-cheat in this game is so maliciously incompetent. As someone who has never even used mods, rarely interacts or fights with people in online sessions, and has never been toxic or malicious in any other game either—someone who basically never used a single bug except for solo public sessions, and even actively avoids any potential bugs because I play on eggshells every time just to avoid getting banned— I hadn't logged in for a while, and this time, just because of some minor events and playing occasionally with a classmate, apart from selling a batch of bunker goods, dying while riding the Oppressor a few times, and getting weird pop-up prompts after being hacked recently, I didn't get shit. Looking at how there are no successful appeal cases online, and how appealing often just turns it into a permanent ban or a character reset anyway, I am heartbroken and desperate. Where is my innocence? /w\ It's not just about the time and money invested in this game, but the fact that I can't properly play with my buddies anymore. I don't know if anyone will see my first review here, but I strongly DO NOT recommend this company. Even though the game is well-made and the optimization is great, as long as they keep this kind of attitude toward handling issues, I still strongly DO NOT recommend this company or any of their PC games. Period.

My solution if you still want to play with friends: Set up your own dedicated server that you and your friends can then join. For some inexplicable reason, I still haven't completely lost the fun of playing this game. Most of the time I start the game and watch a series while walking around Los Santos. Works like a charm.

translation_en: 20 hours offline, 150 hours online, 106 hours in the past two weeks. I busted my ass grinding during the sale to buy an office and a bunker, and before that I was constantly grinding sales just to save up for a Buzzard. I held back and didn't buy the electric sports car I wanted, and I resisted buying the Pegassi BF400 motorcycle I liked, just buying a cheap Bati 801RR for deliveries instead, without even upgrading it much. All that self-control and grinding was so I could become like the high-level players as soon as possible, with a full set of properties and vehicles. But all of that came to an end yesterday. I left my PC on all night the night before to let the bunker stock produce, and when I got home yesterday afternoon, my account was banned. I'm not one of those casual players; I'm a player who strives for the competitive scene. I used to play CS:GO, which taught me to seize every single second to improve in games. Cruising around to sightsee, buying sports cars, and griefing can all wait until after I become a man who owns Los Santos. I wrote a ticket to support yesterday, choosing "Ban Appeal" as the topic. The support bot replied to me within 10 seconds, just copying and pasting Rockstar's ban policy. Today, I wrote another ticket under the topic "Other" explaining that my account was falsely banned. This time a real person replied, but the response was still just a pre-copied-and-pasted ban explanation saying basically that I'm banned for a month, my characters and everything are gone, if I get banned again it'll be permanent, followed by a list of things that can trigger a ban, and finally emphasizing yet again that GTA:O bans are non-appealable. I'm tired, and I don't have the will or energy to grind for that long all over again, especially without any property sales going on. Goodbye, GTA. To end it with a famous quote from the Steam review section: "The game is a great game, but the game company is a bunch of fucking cunts."

translation_en: Due to the massive amount of negative reviews, potentially new players are wondering: - Is it even worth buying the game when everything is so fucked up? Friends, I'm gonna tell you how things actually are, specifically for you. And let the money-glitchers go fuck themselves. Let's go! [i]This is gonna be exclusively about the online mode.[/i] Back in 2013 when the gameplay trailer for GTA and GTA Online dropped, I was hyped out of my fucking mind. Me and my friend talked about how we'd have the sickest cars and houses in online and how we'd be the kings of the business world. I spent all 5 years waiting for the moment I could play GTA. I didn't even spoil myself on the story, didn't watch let's plays on YouTube, all so I could experience it all myself. Hell, I bought a new PC just for GTA. But after looking at the Steam scores and negative reviews, I genuinely didn't understand how that was possible? Everyone was saying the online is unplayable because of cheaters and insane prices, basically hinting right away that there's no point playing without getting money glitched. My attitude toward the game was pretty repulsed right from the start. But now, with level 200 in GTA Online under my belt and just over 400 hours (at the time of writing this review), I can tell new players what the deal is and what you shouldn't be afraid of. But first things first. There is just a massive amount of content in the game. When you first step into online, you have no clue what to do, where to start, and you have to figure everything out. You've got all these bunkers, facilities, offices, etc., different missions/jobs, races, adversaries, a ton of cars and bikes, and loads of military tech. Gradually you start to progress, level up, and everything becomes dead simple. After many hours in the game, I can say that playing online definitely requires buddies, because trying to pull off anything on your own here is pretty tough, and sometimes impossible. But you can always invite players, say, from the public session, or just ask for help in game communities. The game has bugs, obviously. For example, I lost 50k when I bought ammo in the lobby. The money vanished, but I didn't get any ammo. Lost 500k when I was delivering weapons in a buggy, but they bugged out and wouldn't drop the cargo (ended up just wasting my time). Lost 300k when the delivery truck spawned on a fence and blew itself up. And 6,000 assault rifle bullets just straight up disappeared. And sometimes it pisses you off so much when you're hauling cargo/supplies, and not only do enemy bots and cops mess with you, but traffic starts acting retarded and flies right at you like a magnet. And in moments like those, you just want to punch every single resident of Los Santos right in the fucking face. Now for the most interesting part. There's this connection between cheaters, in-game prices, and making money in GTA Online. To get anywhere starting from scratch, you gotta grind your ass off. It's daily farming on repetitive missions. You gotta sit in online for hours, have zero social life, and completely neglect school/work. But that's all relative. I mean, nobody's stopping you from hopping on for an hour in your free time, playing with friends, and making some cash. It'll just take longer to reach your goals. But as soon as you save up even a little bit for your first business—any business—it'll start bringing in income. And with every cargo sale, it gets easier to level up and make millions. Plus, there are double-money events sometimes where you can rake it in. And just playing heists can net you decent cash. Well, I don't need to tell you how to make money, there are tons of guides on YouTube for that. As for the prices of in-game stuff, at first glance, they seem completely fucking insane. But if you actually level up your businesses, you'll easily be able to make big bucks and buy whatever you find interesting. Plus, unlock wholesale prices and it gets even easier. You can also wait for developer sales and grab things at a great price. That's actually what I did. High prices are what spawn the glitchers. They're the cheaters. Little shits who want everything right now and don't want to put in a single drop of effort. Those same little kids who bitch about high prices in the game and pay real money for level or money boosts in GTA. Because of every fucking kid on YouTube advertising modded lobbies, new players don't see the point in playing fair and want to buy out everything the second they join the game. Anyone would envy their success. Level 20 on GTA Online and already annoying everyone on an MKII Oppressor. But that's only at first glance. As soon as that vegetable joins a heist, they constantly fail. Because they had enough brains to buy a boost, but they're too damn cowardly to build up any skill and level up legit. Sure, you glitched billions for yourself, bought everything available. But what's next? What's the point? They get bored of playing and at best they'll log on just to fuck around or ruin things for other players. They justify it by saying they don't want to grind to achieve anything, they just want to play "normally." But then those exact same guys are the ones crying that "online is dying." Here's what I say: -As long as there's interest, online will live. But you know why else the game has such bad reviews? It's from those exact same glitchers, but completely fucked in the head. After the massive ban wave hit, hordes of angry kids swarmed the game with negative reviews. All they can do is cry that they didn't use cheats or exploit game bugs for personal gain. In reality, they got what they fucking deserved. But life doesn't teach these motherfuckers a lesson and they still order modded lobbies anyway. So 70% of the negativity towards the game comes from pathetic kids who first bought the game, then bought a cash drop, and got permabanned. I talked about harmless cheaters. But there's another caste of cheating kids. Level two, so to speak. The exact ones who are bored of playing and just mess around and grief other players. I've seen reviews saying there are cheaters in every single session blowing you up or dropping trains on you. You switch sessions and it's the exact same thing. Cheaters do exist in the game. But they are extremely rare (specifically the ones who blow up the whole lobby). Most of them keep a low profile (aside from being level 8,000), unless you run into them face-to-face. Sure, it sucks when you're, say, hauling weapons for a sale and all your money goes down the shitter. But nobody's immune to that. Because besides those cheaters, there are other assholes who will mess with you. Mostly, cheaters hang out in full sessions because they desperately need to bother someone. In those cases, it's better to look for an empty or half-empty session right away, and thankfully those pop up pretty often. A separate topic is "long loading screens." Seriously, guys, can't you wait a couple of minutes? For everyone saying it takes 10 minutes or more to load into online, there's a lifehack. Log into online through single-player. Your total load time in that case is around 4 minutes. As for post-mission loading screens, it's not a big deal to me at all, which is why I didn't include load times in the review originally—simply because I didn't even notice them. Yeah, sometimes a load screen glitches out and hangs for over 5 minutes. So what, are we gonna shit all over the game now? Still, it's a fantastic game that can keep you hooked for dozens of hours. Buy the game on sale and play for your own enjoyment. Unlock wholesale prices, wait for discounts, and don't waste money on useless crap (tattoos, clothes, expensive cars, etc.). Play with friends and don't fall for the tricks of these fags offering money drops or whatever. Then patience and hard work will pay off. Sure, you want to buy everything right away, but what's the point of the game then? It feels way better when you actually grinded YOURSELF from a street rat to a slum-dwelling millionaire! Cheaters are rare. And for those posting [strike]bullshit[/strike] in their reviews, just stop bothering everyone and nobody will mess with you. I recommend avoiding them entirely, or better yet, just switch sessions as soon as you see an 8000 level. [b]Huge thanks to everyone who read to the end and supported my review![/b]

translation_en: Time to write an angry review. I don't know what the problem is. Why Rockstar hates me so much, but here we are. WHO DOESN'T WANT TO READ ANGRY BAN RANTING, PLEASE SKIP TO THE SECOND PARAGRAPH Back in May, I was playing GTA Online, peacefully driving around when suddenly I get hit with a a month-long ban. Not understanding what's going on, I rush to support, and this is where Rockstar tells you to go fuck yourself for the first time. Support exists, there's even a "Ban Appeal" topic, but you know what? IT'S FUCKING USELESS. Because no matter what you write, no matter how you prove you're right, dear Rockstars will tell you to go fuck yourself, because a bot automatically closes the ticket, politely leaving a link about the policy update and saying that any ban is final and cannot be appealed. Okay, I think, and I start reading what you can get banned for. Turns out, you get banned for any interaction with cheaters. Meaning, a cheater kills you — you get banned. You're in a session with a cheater, and you don't even know it — you get banned. Yet for some reason, there aren't any fewer cheaters. People on the forums say you might get scrutinized more if you report other players. I don't know how true all of that is, but a fact is a fact. Actually, there was one moment I could have gotten banned for, but it's very sketchy. I find a regular military Lazer jet, hop in, start flying, take out psychos (red players), mess with rival cargo deliveries, and they start accusing me of cheating, while I naturally have no clue what's going on. They go on for a long time about how I'm gonna get banned, kiss my account goodbye, swearing at me and so on and so forth. At the same time, there was zero resistance from their side. Well, I thought, probably noobs, let them whimper. But it turns out, after they told me my plane was invisible and missiles were coming out of nowhere, I realized something fishy was going on. I landed the plane right away, but landed badly and it should've blown up, but it didn't, after which I was finally convinced that the jet was a cheater's. In my defense, I had no idea what they were talking about until the very last moment and that this bullshit wasn't spawned by me. Plus that was a long time ago. I don't know if I got banned for that or not. Anyway, don't steal other people's planes, just to be safe. But back in May when I got banned, literally 5 minutes before the ban a cheater killed me, I filed a report and changed sessions. Maybe that's the reason. BUT NOW THE MOST IMPORTANT PART, DEAR FRIENDS After the month-long ban, I got unbanned, a bit disappointed but already cooled down, and I log into GTA Online. I see a snarky message from Rockstar like, "Do you like the policy changes? Now all cheaters will be banned, next time you'll get banned too if we catch you doing anything." I'm like okay-okay, I'll be careful, I'll try to avoid cheater scum. I create a character, go through the tutorial, everything is fine and dandy. I start soaking in the atmosphere of wonderful Los Santos, looking for a car to keep for myself AND BAM RIGHT IN THE FUCKING FACE, YOU BITCH. PERMANENT BAN. THANKS A FUCKING LOT. I hadn't even reached level 5 yet, and I get instantly banned. FUCKING AWESOME, LET ME APPLAUD. CLAP CLAP CLAP. My verdict: the game is good, ROCKSTAR'S POLICY IS SHIT, ROCKSTAR IS SHIT. IF YOU SEE THE ROCKSTAR LOGO — THROW SHIT AT IT. Permanent ban. Thanks. They said players from past-gen are more trusted. My fucking ass. Permabanned an hour into a new game? Thanks. And what now? Permanent ban. Banned for nothing. Non-appealable. Buy a new game just to get banned again? No, go fuck yourselves.

translation_en: Mixed feelings. How can I put it? The game's story is genuinely great, the details are super rich, and in the end, I could still pick the happy ending. Unlike Ubisoft and their disgusting endings. Really good. The online part isn't nearly as good. I really miss when it first came out, a few of us playing the Prison Break heist, encouraging each other and figuring things out together. Now public sessions are practically full of flying cheaters everywhere, plus people spamming ads for modded money drops. The game environment is terrible, though you can still play with friends, and updates aren't too slow, so it's alright. Before, whenever I saw people talking about getting banned, I thought, "I'm just a hoarder player, I'd never dare to cheat, I'll play carefully and I should be fine." Now I've got 3,121 hours in the game, about 3,000 of those online, saved up 76.8 million in-game dollars, both characters have the most expensive yachts and all properties, and one of them owns almost every car. My first character is level 400+, and the second is level 200+. On Thursday, May 17th, I got banned for a month, and all my account assets and character info were completely wiped. Completely wiped. Completely wiped. I tried reaching out to customer service, but it's all automated bot replies, and they refuse to review ban appeals. Refuse ban appeals. Refuse ban appeals. Just like that, a whole week has passed, going from initial shock to searching everywhere for customer service and Rockstar support, until now I'm just dead inside. I'm really tired. Back in 2016, when cars disappeared from my garage or couldn't be sold, I contacted customer service and they were super helpful in fixing it. But this time, I seriously wonder if Rockstar pulled all their human staff away and left only a robot repeating over and over: "Please refer to our terms of service, if you have questions please visit support." I literally got this reply *from* support, orz. If there's any way to actually contact Rockstar, please help me out. Not recommended right now.

translation_en: [h1] Great game quality, potato servers that will drive you nuts [/h1] [b] If you're a single-player lover... [/b] Way-ahead-of-its-time graphics [spoiler] RAGE engine, San Diego black magic [/spoiler], a staggeringly complete sandbox world [spoiler] Three American idiots on a road trip, you know? [/spoiler], distinct and fully fleshed-out characters [spoiler] Chop is a boy dog! [/spoiler], a one-of-a-kind massive vehicle driving experience [spoiler] Bati 801 going to heaven and hell [/spoiler], and a plot full of twists and turns, absurd yet rigorous [spoiler] Resourceful old Lamar, more harm than good Lester [/spoiler]. These exceptional qualities are enough to make people fork out their hard-earned cash for GTA V ever since its 2013 release—whether you're a Vice City swimming champ, a Grove Street homie, a law-abiding East European, or a newass attracted by the rustic charm of Los Santos—to embark on the most authentic American democratic tour. What? It's already 2018 and you still haven't bought it? Given the sheer scale of this game, even buying it at full price is a steal, let alone how R* drops prices down to almost 80% off now. The only way to atone for not owning this is to immediately buy a copy for your grandpa and grandma as an early New Year's gift so you might just be forgiven. It's worth noting that [b] the best part of GTA V is its brilliant single-player campaign [/b]. Compared to the series' past single-perspective linear narratives, the bold attempt to seamlessly switch between three protagonists and follow multi-layered plotlines yields fantastic cinematic results. Not to mention the well-paced action and car chases, while in the shining Heists and gang crimes, the criminal details are handled with utter professionalism [spoiler] laundering money in online counterfeit factories is apparently meant to make fake bills look aged [/spoiler]. The balance between entertainment and realism is just right, the difficulty is moderate, and you can choose to skip missions after failing multiple times so it doesn't halt your progress [spoiler] Ah, the accursed SA Flight School [/spoiler]. To sum it all up in one sentence: playing it is pure bliss! All you newasses who haven't jumped in yet, buy it and see for yourselves! [b] If you're here for online play... [/b] If you're not [b] living overseas [/b], [b] lack special VPN tricks [/b], and have village internet that [b] sucks playing raw [/b], then [b] DO NOT BUY IT! DO NOT BUY IT! DO NOT BUY IT! [/b] [b] Sucky "Cloud Servers" [/b] When you haven't fucked the Great Firewall over or your VPN ran out of credit, loading into online is often so sluggish that doing a 10-minute mission means staring at clouds in the sky for 2 minutes just to get back to the session, and if the timing's off, it might just crash to desktop outright. (Network police might just become the biggest help to Los Santos law enforcement). Playing with your buddies, these are thoroughly ball-ache-inducing, frustrating experiences. [b] Mysterious Session Environments [/b] Online sessions are magical places. Here, you can run into peace-loving CEOs quietly grinding cargo and chilling—newasses, please try not to bother them, because firstly, grinding cargo and making money is genuinely hard, why go out of your way to block someone's bag? Secondly, once you piss them off, a one-shot Orbital Cannon from a thousand miles away and Oppressor MKIIs hunting you across the entire map are guaranteed. Sometimes you'll run into good-hearted bros who carry you through heists from start to finish. When you meet such a bro, hit the HOME key to open the social menu and add +1 to your harem, wouldn't that be wonderful? Once you have your own heist crew and a few hired guns, making it big is just a snap of the fingers. But keep in mind, what rules the top of the Los Santos food chain isn't guns or money, but the sheer power of technology! [spoiler] Science and technology are the primary productive forces! [/spoiler] Hackers come in two flavors: god-mode little fairies and all-powerful grand Buddhas. For the former, just press M to open the M menu and use R*’s strongest shield—Passive Mode—while talking shit and calling them a motherfucker. The latter are truly terrifying; they are masters of model-spawning and dropping garbage on you. When you run into such immortals, you can stalk them through your apartment TV, press F1 to record evidence (not strictly necessary), go to the ESC menu, select the Players tab, and report and kick them all in one go. Then send a quick greeting to their ancestors 18 generations back before switching sessions—it couldn't be more thrilling. [b] A little advice for newasses [/b] 1. Use the M menu to turn on passive mode often when being hunted, but if you went looking for a fight and got owned, then accept the loving education from the old-timers! 2. When you run into hackers, whether it's a session-wiping Kratos or a charitable God of Wealth, don't overthink it—switch sessions immediately for the sake of your level 189 character! Remember, getting money bags feels good for a moment, but getting banned is a one-way ticket to the crematorium. We criminals are respectable folk, money dropped from the sky cannot be accepted. 3. Brothers united can snap iron bars! If you're lucky enough to have some good homies (preferably four) to play and explore with, cherish the journey. You should know that the greatest charm of GTA isn't the extra 250k in your account after every Pacific Standard, but the strategic mind games with your homies, plotting how to make each other eat friendly jetwash and drafting behind one another. 4. Make clean money and you won't have to worry about false bans. My dozen or so homies and I have over 4,000 hours in GTA V combined, and only I got hit with a character reset and a one-month ban package when I got tempted after a slow delivery and tried using Cheat Engine to modify the delivery time, which miserably failed. None of the other homies were falsely banned. If you genuinely run into trouble and need support, appealing in English makes the process go a lot faster. [b] A little dramatic flair [/b] A short story adapted from personal experience—Player The layout of the banks in Los Santos is different from other places: they all have a square counter right on the street, with cash prepared inside, ready to be robbed at any moment. The robbers, finishing work around noon or dusk, would often spend 500 bucks to buy a lap dance—that was twenty patches ago, now it's gone up to 1000 bucks—and stand outside the stage, watching it heat up. If you're willing to spend another 1000 bucks, you could buy a hot chick or a jacked dude to get hands-on with. If you shelled out hundreds of thousands, you could buy a badass top-tier super car, but these customers were mostly poor cargo-grinding CEOs, generally not that well-off. Only those who bought Shark Cards would stride into the room next to the storefront, asking for cars and boats to slowly customize them. I've been a clerk at the Pacific Standard bank at the town entrance since I was twelve. The manager said I looked too stupid and might not be able to serve the Shark Card whales, so I should just do odd jobs outside. Although the CEO customers outside were easy to talk to, quite a few of them were nagging and pedantic. They often wanted to watch the cash being physically taken out of the warehouse, check if the payout difficulty multiplier was 1.25x, and personally watch the players change into saved outfits before feeling at ease: under this intense supervision, glitching money was pretty difficult. So after a few days, the manager said I couldn't handle this job either. Luckily, my recommendation letter had heavy backing and I couldn't be fired, so I was reassigned to the mind-numbing job of managing the Los Santos Customs. From then on, I stood all day in Los Santos Customs, doing my job. Although I didn't neglect my duties, it always felt a bit monotonous and boring. The manager had a fierce face, and the customers had no pleasant tone either, making it hard for anyone to feel lively. Only when Player came to the shop could I chuckle a few times, which is why I still remember him to this day. Player was the only person who bought Shark Cards while driving an armored Kuruma to heists. His build was very average; wearing outdated Deadline light-up suits, his clothes often stained with scars; holding an unupgraded MKII heavy sniper. Even though he bought Shark Cards, they were just a few loose Red Shark bills; it seemed he hadn't done cargo or deliveries for a dozen updates. Whenever he spoke to people, he always used a mouthful of archaic, pretentious language that left people half-confused. Because his name was simply "player," people took that half-understood phrase from copybooks—"despicable outsider player"—and gave him a nickname: Player. As soon as Player arrived at the shop, everyone drinking would look at him and laugh, some calling out, "Player! You've added another new Elegy to your garage again!" He wouldn't answer, instead telling the counter, "Change to two matte paint jobs, and I want a 2000-dollar horn." Then he'd plop down 9,000 big ones. They would intentionally shout louder, "You must have fucked up your Pacific Standard payout again!" Player would open his eyes wide and say, "How can you frame someone's innocence out of thin air..." "What innocence? Day before yesterday I saw you with my own eyes drive the getaway boat onto the shore and get farmed." Player's face would turn red, the veins on his forehead bulging, and he'd argue, "Running aground doesn't count as failing... failing! ...Can a CEO's matters be called failing?" Following that would be incomprehensible jargon, like "bunker research metaphysics" and "glitching solo public sessions," causing everyone to roar with laughter: the inside and outside of the shop were filled with a joyful atmosphere. Hearing people talk behind his back, Player had actually won Criminal Mastermind once, but in the end he didn't buy any new vehicles, nor did he know how to export cars in a public lobby; thus he grew poorer and poorer, eventually reaching the point where he was about to collect Rockstar's 2000-dollar welfare check. Fortunately, he was good at heists, so he would carry other people through them to earn a bowl of rice. Unfortunately, he had another bad habit: he loved to embarrassingly crash and fail. Barely a few days passed before he and a delivery Titan would smash into a telephone pole together. After happening a few times, no one would ask him to do cargo or heists anymore. Player had no choice, so he couldn't help but occasionally do embarrassing things. But in our shop, his conduct was better than everyone else's; he never defaulted on payments. Even though he occasionally had no cash and temporarily put it on his Maze Bank tab, within a month he would definitely top up a card to pay it off, erasing Player's name from the utility bill delinquency list. Player ordered a batch of cocaine, and his flushed face gradually returned to normal. Someone would then ask, "Player, are you actually any good at heists?" Player would look at the person asking, showing an expression of disdain for arguing. They would then continue, "How come you can't even get past half of Fleeca?" Player would immediately look dejected and uneasy, a layer of gray washing over his face, muttering some words; but this time it was all archaic nonsense, completely incomprehensible. At this moment, everyone would roar with laughter again: the inside and outside of the shop were filled with a joyful atmosphere. During these times, I could chime in and laugh, and the manager would never scold me. Moreover, whenever the manager saw Player, he would often ask him these same questions to provoke laughter. Player knew he couldn't converse with them, so he had no choice but to talk to the kids. Once, he said to me, "Ever griefed in a public session?" I nodded slightly. He said, "You have... well, let me quiz you. When you run into a flying Oppressor, how do you grief him?" I thought to myself, a beggar-like person is qualified to quiz me? So I turned my head away and ignored him. Player waited for a long time and said earnestly, "Can't do it, huh? ...I'll teach you, remember it! You should remember these tricks. You'll need them for session prep when the Doomsday Heist comes out." I secretly thought the manager and I were way higher level than him, and our manager never used the Oppressor as an anti-infantry vehicle anyway; finding it both funny and annoying, I lazily replied, "Who needs you to teach me, don't you just get out of the car and whip out an RPG?" Player would show an extremely delighted look, tapping the counter with his long fingernails, nodding and saying, "Right, right! ...Do you know the four ways to use Stinger missiles?" I grew even more impatient, pouting and walking away. Player had just used the interaction menu to register as a CEO, wanting to call in a Deliverator Ruiner 2000 through SecuroServ, and seeing my total lack of enthusiasm, he sighed again, wearing an extremely pitying look. A few times, newasses in the session drawn by the sound of session warfare would rush over to join the fun, surrounding Player. He would hand each of them a Stinger missile. After eating the missile, the kids still wouldn't disperse, their eyes staring at the Avenger boss standing nearby. Panicking, Player would spread his fingers to cycle through the weapon wheel, look at his remaining ammo count and say, "1500 a shot, there's not many left, I don't have many left." He would stand up straight, look at the Stinger missiles again, shake his head and say, "Not many! Is it many? Not many." And so this group of newasses would scatter amidst the sounds of explosive airstrikes. Player was such a joyful presence, but without him, everyone else just went on living the same way. One day, probably two or three days before the Independence Day update, the manager was slowly balancing the books, took down the chalkboard, and suddenly said, "Player hasn't been here for a long time. He still owes 190k!" That was when I realized he really hadn't been around for a long time. A prison break runaway said, "How could he come? ...He broke his leg." The manager said, "Oh!" "He's always making a fool of himself anyway. This time, he lost his mind and actually tried to mod Agent 14. Can you mod bunker stuff?" "What happened after?" "What happened? First he acted like an idiot searching for cheat tables, failed to mod it, and then got hit with the ban package hammer, banned for over half a month, and then got his character wiped." "And then?" "Then his character got wiped." "What happened after his character got wiped?" "What? ...Who knows? Maybe he made a fool of himself and got permanently banned." The manager didn't ask any further and slowly went back to calculating his books. After winter, it snowed in Los Santos more and more every day, looking close to Christmas; I was grinding vehicle cargo all day and had to drive my Avenger out. One afternoon, when there were no heist invites, I was sitting there with my eyes closed. Suddenly I heard a voice: "Change to a Bati 801." Although this voice was extremely low, it was very familiar. When I looked, there was nobody in sight. I stood up and looked outside, and there was Player, sitting under the counter facing the Los Santos Customs shop. At first he was wearing a scrub vest and flip-flops, looking an absolute mess; driving an unmodded Elegy, hiding in a 2-car garage on Popular Street, holding a free SMG. When he saw me, he said again, "Change the respray." The manager also poked his head out and said, "Player? You still owe 190k!" Player dejectedly looked up and replied, "This... I'll pay it back next time. This time it's cash, the Pisswasser livery is better." The manager, just like usual, smiled at him and said, "Player, you made a fool of yourself again, huh?" But this time he didn't argue much, just muttered a single sentence: "Don't make fun of me!" "Make fun of you? If you didn't make a fool of yourself, how'd you get banned for a month?" Player said in a low voice, "Monitor data, mon, monitor..." His expression was very much like he was begging the manager not to bring it up anymore. By this time a few people had gathered, and they and the manager all laughed. I changed the paint job, carried it out, and placed it on the threshold. He fished four thousand bucks out of his tattered pocket and put it in my hands. I saw his pockets were full of sticky bombs—so that's what he used those sticky bombs for, to blow up cars. After a bit, once it was customized, amidst everyone's jokes and laughter, he sat on that 801 and slowly drove away. Ever since then, I haven't seen Player for a long time. When the Summer Sale arrived, the manager took down the chalkboard and said, "Player still owes 190k!" By the Independence Day of the following year, he said again, "Player still owes 190k!" Halloween rolled around and he didn't say it, and by Christmas he wasn't seen again either. To this day I still haven't seen him—presumably Player is indeed dead. Written in the summer of 2018

translation_en: Cheaters are a problem, but they just keep pumping out new cars every time just to sell Shark Cards, so nobody's going 'Oh! Fresh! Amazing! Incredible!' anymore. People get sick of grinding Shark Cards and the exact same repetitive missions, so they either go look for cheats or just quit the game entirely. I feel like if it had been paid DLC instead of in-game microtransactions, it wouldn't have come to this. That said, it's still undeniable that it's a great game for messing around with friends. Honestly, I wish they'd add more fishing or leisure-related updates, or make better use of the elements already on the map. They call it open-world and free, but it's a game where you can't even sit on a park bench, you can't touch a basketball even though there's a court, and there's a huge ocean but you can't fish. It lacks attention to detail.
