translation_en: I've played GTA 5 for almost 1000 hours now, and running into cheaters is an everyday occurrence. I'd advise fresh noobs not to go into public lobbies; you don't yet realize the metaphysical power of cheaters—basically, they get you falsely banned. If it were half a year ago, I would definitely give this game a positive review, because whether it's the graphics, controls, worldview, or replayability, it's faultless and even exceeded my expectations for the GTA series. Yeah, exactly half a year ago, the emergence of cheaters and anti-cheat mechanisms started changing all of that. Back when I was a noob, I often got wasted by PVP tryhards, and back then I used to think, "Man, it'd be great if I could just use a cheat to take him out." Later on, as my skills improved, I never had that thought again, but someone actually went and turned that thought into reality. I don't know when it started, but public lobbies began to see money spawns, god mode, and even "clashes of the gods." To other players, these people are just bugs ruining the gaming environment, but having once had the thought of cheating myself, all I saw was a bunch of losers circlejerking. Cheaters became more and more rampant, to the point where Rockstar, who had never operated a large-scale online game before, finally started doing the bare minimum to crack down on modders. Yeah, I said the bare minimum, because Rockstar's approach was to find a few of the most blatant show-offs, ban them for 15 days, and then let them back out. For quite a long time, players could only tear modders a new one through forums. Later, the modders' activities started getting out of hand, and Rockstar finally realized that the existence of cheaters didn't just affect the players' gaming experience, it affected their own revenue. Games like DayZ next door are a living example of this. Rockstar's management slapped their foreheads and decided to design an anti-cheat system and throw it into the game. Ever since then, my frame rate has never gone above 30. Rockstar's method was super crude: ban any player detected by the anti-cheat system. Yet this system could not only detect modders, but also normal players who had money dropped on them, were killed by, or even got carried through missions by modders. And as the saying goes, while the Tao is one foot high, the demon is ten feet tall; cheats gradually evolved anti-detection mechanisms, so Rockstar's anti-cheat turned into an anti-player system. That's why so many players are crying about getting false bans. Plus, the anti-cheat hogs so much computing resource that a game with normally smooth-as-butter performance started stuttering and dropping frames—a game famed for its god-tier optimization started lagging. What does that even mean? Thanks to Rockstar's inaction, cheaters grew so rampant they even took over forums to publicly claim that cheating is not a crime. Over the past half year, I don't know how many players have had their hearts broken, silently deleting the game and choosing to quit for good. As a hardcore Rockstar fanboy who's been playing since GTA 2, I obviously can't bring myself to rage-delete the game. Even so, from January of this year until now, it's been a long time since I even logged on. The other day I had nothing to do, so I logged in and played for a bit. Fearing I'd get caught up in Rockstar's recent self-destructing random ban wave, I chose to go into an empty invite-only session. Sitting on an empty Ferris wheel, looking down at an empty city, my nose suddenly started stinging. Not long ago, my friends and I were still giving it our all to complete the Criminal Mastermind challenge, racking our brains over some sudden burst of inspiration. Now, the friends I knew have either deleted the game or haven't logged on in ages. Of the people still holding out on this game, I'm the only one left. Sorry, when I came to Los Santos a year ago, I never thought I'd write a review like this. If it were me back then, I probably would have written: 1. Great gameplay, 2. Exquisite graphics, 3. Online is super fun—stuff like that which fills 9 out of 10 reviews if you scroll down. But now... I'll end with a White Album quote format: GTA 5 or whatever, it doesn't matter anymore. Because there is no longer any content worth playing. An empty friend session is no longer needed. Because there's no longer anyone to play with.

translation_en: I felt the need to write this review because I can't stand the low scores and comments. First of all, let me state that I played 400 hours in 3 months and I spent all 400 hours in online mode. I want to touch upon a couple of issues that are talked about as disgraceful in the reviews. First, let's start with the cheaters. Yes, it's not like there are no cheaters, but they don't fuck up the servers as much as people exaggerate. Most of them chill passively, doing it just to make their own missions easier or for money hacks, and this doesn't really harm you much. Besides, most cheaters get banned. Let's come to another problem: long loading times. Folks, what were you expecting? Even LoL makes you wait 3-4 minutes to get in, and pardon my French, it has a tiny map and 2 monsters. Here, you have square kilometers of area, hundreds of cars, hundreds of NPCs, dozens of players, and the list goes on with these players' items, cars, planes, etc. I hope you aren't expecting all this stuff to load in 30 seconds. Since it only loads other players' items when switching servers, changing servers is quick once you're in. So it only makes you wait a bit at the start. Don't exaggerate and say "I played for 4 hours and 3 hours were spent waiting." Another problem is that grinding money is hard. Of course, it's going to be hard to earn, especially in a game like this. Guys, you don't need to buy any DLCs in this game. Not even a single one. I mean, the devs have no other income besides in-game currency sales. Naturally, they sell in-game cash, but since you can also earn it by playing, they need to nudge you toward purchasing it. That's why the earnings are a bit low. However, if you have 3 other friends, heists go like hotcakes—I know for a fact I've finished 8 or 9 heists in a single day. If you don't have friends, finding a Discord channel for GTA V isn't that hard. If you can't find one, I'll help you out. In most other games, you pay 100 bucks, then another 100 bucks for DLCs, and they keep asking for more money as new ones come out. In this game, if you are eager to play, you can have everything you want without spending another penny. Please don't take the bad reviews seriously, don't cheat, and play as much as you can. Because this game deserves it. Have a good game. Current Link ; https://discord.gg/Q67tWG4

translation_en: Where to start. Grand Theft Auto V is a really good game on which I've racked up over 1500 hours of total playtime between the PC and PS3 versions, and yes I bought the game twice at 60 euros because it was worth it, and I emphasize the past... GTA V had and still has excellent potential in single-player and with mods, just like its predecessors. But the core of this opus is focused on GTA Online, which USED to be well-made and isn't really anymore, and I'll explain why. Having known GTA V since the very beginning when there were only about 10-15 buyable cars, the game is driven by the economic side so you earn money doing missions, etc., anyway you get it, but several things ruined this GTA Online. First, the cheaters, or modders as you prefer, who make money spawn just because it suits them, but who will mostly try to annoy the hell out of you as much as possible without you being able to do anything about it, like GodMode etc., without ever getting banned by Rockstar. Then the updates, which started off original (the start of heists, new missions, businesses, biker clubs) and then turned into military-style updates with things like the hydra, and bunkers that make free roam unplayable with all the war machines on the map. Then the community, full of the aforementioned cheaters, kids who kill you on a loop for no reason and scream in voice chat (blessed be the mute button), and big assholes who stalk you and insult you over nothing, calling you a cheater just because your aim is better than theirs. And finally, the holy grail: the anti-cheat system that supposedly bans cheaters, whereas I got banned myself for no reason after over 1500 hours of playtime and never having put a foot out of line, but a permanent ban because otherwise it wouldn't be funny, an INSTANT permanent ban while I was just quietly grinding my businesses. And Rockstar's super helpful support that replies to you "this is not contestable" even though they have a tab for it on their support site, so basically buy the game again to play GTA Online. Having a huge amount of playtime, I'm saying what I think about the only game where I've spent over 1500 hours only to get a permanent, uncontestable ban for nothing, while cheaters get banned for 1-3 months MAX. So no thanks Rockstar, I'm stuffed. In conclusion, GTA V is a good game as long as you're ready to get banned from GTA Online at any moment on a whim from the Bot that manages the whole thing, and that makes up 75% of the game itself. I've told you my experience and my POV, do with it what you will.

translation_en: In 9 days, it will be a full year since I started playing GTA 5, but I'm not the same person I was back then. I still remember watching my friend play this wildly popular game. It looked amazing, but his PC was too trash to run it properly, capping out at 30 FPS. So, when it went on sale, I bought it and figured things out on my own (my friend was a casual player who modded money and rarely did missions). When I first arrived in Los Santos and looked at my empty pockets, I made a silent vow to make a ton of money. So, I frantically joined every money-making activity I could find—heists, adversary modes, whatever paid decently. That’s how I ground my way up to level 80. Later on, I learned that CEOs and MCs made good money too, so with my saved-up cash, I bought an office and a vehicle warehouse. From then on, every time I logged in, it was just import and export. Through the money from selling cars, I slowly built up my empire, until now, when I log in, there is only one thing left to do: source cargo. When I first started, my friend already had 500 hours in and didn't want to play anymore, so I had to grind in silence by myself. Back then I heard about money drops and modders and stuff, but I genuinely wanted to experience the game, so I chose the grind. The process was fulfilling, but also painful. To buy the Hydra, I literally ran crates for three straight days, and by the end, I almost gave up. Later, when the biker businesses and bunker came out, there were more cargo missions, so I just got used to it. Struggling every day for the things I wanted to buy—I just loved that feeling. But today, I’m genuinely tired. Ever since the bunker stuff dropped, I’ve felt more and more overwhelmed. Without friends to help, no matter how huge the daily workload is or how much money I make, the price tags on the vehicles are still miles away. On top of that, when the MC businesses and bunker are full, I have to sell solo, and there’s often not enough time to finish. With this latest Smuggler's Run update, my bunker research isn't even done yet (yep, I chose to let it research passively), and to buy a hangar, I had to drop 400 bucks on a Shark Card because the in-game money just wasn't enough. I honestly feel like playing this game has lost that original magic. Now, it just feels like a grinding simulator. Rockstar's game quality is indisputable, but the online mode nowadays makes me feel like Rockstar has turned into Tencent. Of course, it could also be that I just can't find friends to play with anymore. I did find a group of like-minded people online later on, but everyone gradually ran out of time, leaving just me working away in this city. As for why I don't look for people around me: it's simply impossible to pitch it to them. The environment I'm in is completely surrounded by Tencent games, and trying to get people into non-Tencent games is brutally hard. To the point where now, whenever I check out a new game, I just don't even bother mentioning it to them. I originally wanted to leave a negative review, but for the sake of the nearly 1,000 hours I'm about to hit and the time I spent grinding over the past year, I'll give it a positive one. After all, this is the first game I've ever put 1,000 hours into. Lastly, a few words for newbies thinking about getting into it: if you don't want to grind, you can mod money, but it's best to only do it when you're burnt out. This game is worth experiencing properly. Also, using cheats to blow up lobbies and griefing the whole server doesn't prove you're badass, because this isn't an FPS game, and PvP isn't the core of it. One day when you run into a cheater, all you can do is switch sessions—unless you can record a video to report them, save yourself the trouble with the in-game report button, clicking it does fuck all. Los Santos is a beautiful city, but now, it's time to leave...

translation_en: [h1]Charming![/h1] [b]Initial Info:[/b][list] [*]Personal rating: [b]10/10[/b]; [*]Review date: 28/10/17; [*]Last edited: 22/11/17; [*]Developer/Publisher: Rockstar North/Rockstar Games; [*]Genre: Action-adventure; [*]Platform(s): Xbox (360/One), PS (3/4) and PC (Microsoft Windows).[/list] Pleasant, stunning, magnificent and immersive, as well as crazy and astonishing, are just a few words that define this game. After years of development, [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockstar_Games]Rockstar Games[/url], a subsidiary of [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take-Two_Interactive]Take-Two Interactive[/url], has once again managed to deliver a work of art with the game's single-player mode (campaign) and win the hearts of many gamers around the world. It might sound like an exaggeration, but it isn't—especially for players who have already experienced [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/12120/Grand_Theft_Auto_San_Andreas/]GTA SA[/url], for example, or other games by [b]Rockstar Games[/b], and therefore know the potential this developer has when delivering their games. Just like in any GTA, you'll get a chance to get caught up in the story. And it's incredible. The content the game features is immeasurable and can keep you entertained for over 50 hours, seriously. And all of that just from the single-player mode. The world is huge, highly detailed, and very immersive, with everything wonderfully well-connected, featuring dynamic events (traffic, robberies, shops, housing, etc.), breathtaking views, and a fantastic job of making it all feel as real as possible. Making the player get involved. Well, it does, and it does that really well. [b]I didn't play the single-player mode on PC[/b] (only online mode) and I don't even care to, but my hours spent on the campaign via Xbox 360 were exceptional. I played for over 50 hours and the engagement just kept growing. All the attachment to the characters, the tough choices, the well-unfolded story, unusual missions (all of them), and interesting events made me love the whole experience, which is why I don't plan on replaying the campaign. I want to preserve my one and only astonishing encounter with the game. The game's optimization is phenomenal; after all, almost two years passed before it was released on PC. It was initially released on Xbox 360 and PS3, then on PS4 and Xbox One, and finally on PC. Take the system requirements as a baseline and check them first, you'll most likely be able to run it. As far as I remember, I had no issues with anything related to the single-player mode when I played. The game always delivered great quality, with extreme care given to everything related to the campaign. On top of all that, it's fair to say you'll witness a very good AI—moody, cynical, or troublesome—as you roam the streets of Los Santos and Blaine County. And don't worry, the entire game is in Brazilian Portuguese, except for the voice acting. The online mode is the only reason I bought the game on PC, and I have a lot of fun playing with a friend, so if you're going to play it, always try not to be alone. Bearing in mind that it wasn't Rockstar Games' original goal to make GTA V's main focus online, that mode ended up becoming so popular and profitable for the company that they focused more on it, leaving their initial plans for campaign expansions by the wayside. That's not a complaint, I'm just mentioning it so you know the story mode is unique. Take-Two Interactive, the owner of Rockstar Games, has been involved in scandals, which is why the game has received a lot of negative reviews. Therefore, even though the company has proven to be so predatory with in-game prices, I emphasize that it's not my goal to keep bashing them or to review GTA V through the lens of the online mode. All I can tell you about GTA Online is:[list] [*]It's incredible and features tons of fun content, meaning many, many more hours of gameplay; [*]Recommended for playing WITH friends; [*]There are predatory in-game prices charged for cars, properties, or anything else related to old or new content in the game—always pushing you to spend cash by buying Shark Cards via the Steam Store; [*]Playing casually with friends makes online play much more fun than playing alone, plus you don't have to worry about cash since you can always earn money in the game, even if it's just a little bit; [*]The servers aren't the best, nor are they the worst, but they could definitely use some more attention; [*]There's a heavy focus on it, so new content is always bound to pop up soon; [*]There are reports of unfair bans and sudden cash wipes unrelated to cheats—I don't know if these have been resolved or how support handles them, but if you need to contact support, go [url=https://support.rockstargames.com/hc/pt-br/requests/new]here[/url]; [*]As mentioned above, this is caused by cheaters you might run into during sessions, which unfortunately tends to happen in any online game—so far I've run into one who glitched my entire character (in this case, just restarting the game was enough).[/list] It's VERY HARD to describe GTA V to you within the review space I have here, but I can assure you that, regardless of your purpose for playing—campaign or online—what you'll play has great content for many hours of fun, truly many hours, so the asking price, even without a discount, is worth it. Big time! An interesting fact is the game's price on PC: since its release, it has always been R$ 99,99, with discounts maxing out at 50%. A great price! The rest is up to you. [i]GTA V[/i] is therefore highly recommended to any fan of the series, new or old, who loves action-adventure games, an open and dynamic world with tons and tons of content, plus an exceptional story, regardless of what you want to get out of the game. Call a friend, or more, and have fun with the online mode. Even if it has some issues or makes you feel forced to spend money, laughing with friends always makes gaming sessions better. Be the good guy or the bad guy, create your own fun and interests, and make GTA V a new love of your life. Play it! [b]Final notes:[/b][list] [*]If I made any mistakes, whether about the game or spelling, let me know politely below; [*]All URL shorteners are safe, I'm not here to screw anyone over, I just prefer using the "url" tag, please understand; [*]Read a review, it will help someone else the same way it helps you; [*]Thank you very much for reading, I hope this was helpful and have a good game![/list] [h1]Review endorsed by the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/groups/magnaway]Magnaway[/url] group curator.[/h1] [h1]Support us by following our [url=http://store.steampowered.com/curator/26745635/]Curator page[/url] for future reviews.[/h1]

translation_en: First of all, I want to warn new players! A lot of players in Online mode are not very friendly to newbies! There is a Passive Mode in Online mode that prevents other players from killing you once you turn it on! So avoid fights whenever you can! But I actually ran into some hackers dropping a Ferris wheel from the sky right on top of my head. I was totally speechless! Now let's talk about getting banned! Why are bans so harsh? Because a lot of people use cheats online! I don't recommend those who actually cheat at all! They deserve to get banned! Besides, those people usually don't even care about getting banned! They're usually just losers who want to use cheats to harass other players and vent their own frustrations. Pathetic! You're no different from the people in real life who pressure you! Then there's the thing called false bans! No wonder so many people leave negative reviews, especially regarding bans. Let me explain: you can't run antivirus software while playing GTA5 Online. Because their anti-cheat will mistake certain programs for cheats. So don't have anything related to antivirus running around. Normally I don't run antivirus when playing games. But one time my PC felt a bit laggy, so I used 360 Boost Ball to clear the cache! A little while later, I got banned! That was my first ban. Afterward, I saw a lot of different theories online. Pondering over it back and forth, I finally summarized from experience that you cannot run antivirus software while playing the game, nor can any programs related to antivirus. So I strongly advise against running them! If you don't want to get falsely banned! The gameplay is actually pretty good. After all, GTA5 is a series I've been playing since past titles. Speaking of how long, probably since I was a kid. The biggest problem with the game is that it keeps getting screwed over in our country time and time again. GTA5 became super popular because of streaming! And it's very suitable for streamers to stream. But I'm sure many people know the game got banned from streaming in China! And this year even racing and biker activities got banned from streaming too! So it's a pity! But I can't in good conscience leave a negative review! At least this game gave me a lot of happy times and I met quite a few friends, even though they're ultimately just GTA5 friends. I think the biggest appeal of this game is its freedom and replayability! Even if you can't find friends, you can make your own fun in the city, whether it's offline single-player or online. I gotta say, this game has killed a lot of my happy hours. Also, let's talk about how the optimization is indeed very great. A finely crafted masterpiece! Mid-range PCs can run it, as long as you don't turn the settings up too high, so the system requirements aren't very high. It's just pretty memory-heavy, needs at least 8GB of RAM! 8GB of RAM is recommended. Of course, high-end PC specs are great for maxing out graphics, and if your rig is badass you can add an ENB graphics mod. But I haven't tried that online; I just like how ENB looks, it's a blessing for graphics snobs. I believe long-time players will support the GTA series! Looking forward to GTA 6! Even though that sounds pretty far away—毕竟 (after all), following Rockstar's tradition, we'll probably have to wait a few more years for the next installment. But I really hope it won't be too long.

translation_en: A year later, somewhere near a peak on Mount Chiliad. Trevor’s grave. Michael hands Franklin a cigarette... The two of them just look at each other, gazing at "Trevor"... —————————————————————————— Michael's daughter went to college. The house slowly started to feel like a real home. Franklin became stinking rich. A lonely man among rich men. He had long since cut ties with Lamar.. He cycled through girlfriends, always feeling none of them were the one he originally wanted. For a while, he even got addicted to strip clubs. "Maybe the time spent in the club is the only real home Franklin has left." —————————————————————————— The FIB's final mission for Michael: "make Franklin disappear from this world." And they threatened him with Michael's family... After the cigarette burned out... Michael pushed Franklin off the cliff. Listening to Franklin's screams, Michael raised his gun. Aimed it at his own head. "Bang!"... Blood splattered onto Trevor's grave.. The last thing he heard. Was Trevor saying to him: "Welcome back, brother." —————————————————————————— Lamar is running his auto shop... Business is booming. Thinking back to the first day I met Lamar. He handed me a gun. And told me one thing. "Welcome to Los Santos." —————————————————————————— Right after getting off the plane and walking out of the airport, Facing this friend who I wasn't even sure was a friend, He handed me a gun that I wasn't sure was well-intentioned. Anyway, that's how I ended up in Los Santos. On the first day, I slept on the streets, nobody knew me. On the second day, I robbed a random passerby and took all his money. Finally, I didn't have to starve... On the third day, I went to Ammu-Nation. The owner told me: "In this world, only money is almighty." —————————————————————————— Robbed god knows how many convenience stores... Offed countless people.. Kicking open the doors of Pacific Standard over and over again. From Lester to the FIB... From having nothing, to supercars, mansions, businesses, bunkers, hangars... Sometimes parking a luxury car on the side of the road and letting pedestrians take pictures. Or soaring through the sky in a plane. Hunting game deep in the mountains. Swimming through the undersea world in the ocean. Dressed in a suit and tie walking into an office building by day. Heading out to a yacht to enjoy the peak of life by night. —————————————————————————— The rain washes over Los Santos every single day. As if it's the wailing of those wronged souls. Restless every single night, Nobody knows if they'll still see tomorrow's sun when they wake up. Sometimes I really want to go back to the beginning, with just that one pistol to protect myself. Work a legitimate job. Help out strangers in need. Have a home of my own and a car that runs. And a woman I deeply love. Living a plain and simple life. Not worrying about money, just happy because of love. —————————————————————————— On this day, the sunlight is shining down on the top of Mount Chiliad just like always. Me, standing in the sunlight.. With a sports car parked beside me. Facing the distant peaks, I ask myself. Can I still go back to the past? By chance, I spotted a gravestone. Perhaps, The owner of that gravestone. Can't go back to their past either.

translation_en: After over 1,300 hours of playtime I uninstalled GTA, even though I really liked the game. Here is my factual report on why: I had bought Shark Cards, farmed massive amounts of heist missions for cash, and had over 30 million in my GTA account. Now my account balance was wiped by Rockstar for supposedly hacked/cheated money. First of all, I never cheated or used an exploit. I then opened a ticket, also referencing the bought Shark Cards, I can absolutely prove where the 30 million came from. On the first ticket I got the standard response that my account was wiped because of hacked/cheated money. I opened a second ticket, and got the exact same response. On the third ticket I asked for some proof report or something, as to why Rockstar gets the idea that my money was cheated. Here I got the reply that Rockstar does not give any further information on this. Aside from the time I put into the farming missions, I also suffered an unjustified loss of real-life money due to the bought Shark Cards. My conclusion: Don't get pissed—uninstalled GTA—hands off all Rockstar games in the future.

translation_en: Edit from 2017-12-08: I wrote this review a month ago and had no idea so many people would see it, or that I'd get this much support (though there's been no shortage of haters talking shit either). At the time, I just kept seeing wave after wave of negative reviews complaining about "false bans," and I wanted to share my own real experiences and thoughts. I wanted to let newbies thinking about buying the game know that GTA has a ton of amazing content to look forward to, instead of everyone instantly associating it with unfair ban waves. Judging by the comments, plenty of veteran players saw the review too and shared their two cents. There are a lot of reasons for this update. One old-school player reached out and shared his false ban story with me. Unlike some of the commenters talking crap who don't even own GTA on their profile and claim to be "falsely banned," this guy bought GTA even earlier than I did. After talking with him, we both realized where we each needed to make adjustments. Because he loves GTA so much, the despair he felt after getting banned was unimaginable. Putting myself in his shoes, if my false ban wave appeal from late last year hadn't gone through, I'd probably be just as hopeless as him. Following his advice, to make sure newbies stepping into Los Santos don't walk into the trap of a false ban—even if the odds are super low—I need to share some proper ways to play. At the same time, I want to clean up my wording. If anyone who was genuinely falsely banned felt hurt by my review, please accept my apologies. Please interpret my phrase "false bans don't exist at all" correctly. If you were banned for cheating or money drops, just fuck off. Because a few safety tips were mentioned in the previous comments, and to help players with thousands of hours, I'm bundling them into one big update here: 1. DO NOT use cheats or money drops!!! 2. If a hacker drops money on you, DO NOT bank it and DO NOT spend it! Get into the habit of taking screenshots with F12 regularly, especially when money is being dropped on you. Press Z once to show the session player list and your cash, and the first item under Online -> Stats in the Pause Menu will show your income and expenses. Screenshots are super useful for reports and appeals; check out the specific method below. 3. If you get messed with by a hacker: getting props attached to you (roadblocks, oranges, toilets, trash cans, even flags), getting teleported with the whole lobby to one spot (the ocean, the sky, other sketchy places), getting blown up repeatedly and dying in flames, having your ID used to blow up the lobby (that one's seriously fucked up)... your first reaction should be to switch sessions (Pause - Online - Find New Session). If the props are still stuck on you after switching, quit to single-player and log back in; that usually fixes it. If it still doesn't work, restart the game. Hackers are disgusting, but they aren't worth ruining your mood to enjoy the game. 4. There's also a theory, which is pretty much a fact: having hackers in your friends list is super dangerous. When you look for a new session, it prioritizes sessions with your friends and crew members in them. So it's best not to join massive public crews like IGN. There are way too many people in them to guarantee that a cheater won't ruin your game. 5. Before launching Online, shut down software with optimization boosters like 360 Security or Master Lu, and completely uninstall pirated versions of GTA, single-player mods, trainers, and anything else that might make Rockstar think you're cheating. Game boosters are fine, but try not to use VPNs (I've never used a VPN for Online, but there's a rumor that constantly changing your IP can get you banned). These are unconfirmed ban risks, but if you really care about your account and feel super paranoid, just take care of these too. 6. How to report and appeal (the ID blowing up the lobby might not be the actual hacker, so report carefully—focus on the ones specifically griefing you or the ones you're 100% sure about): If you're in-game and in the same session as the hacker and know their ID, you can go passive first (to stop hackers from messing with you, though some hackers bypass passive mode anyway), then hit ESC - Online - Players - find their ID - Report - Exploit. You can report them multiple times, but you have to be sure they're cheating, because another reason Rockstar bans people is for abuse of the reporting system. Switch sessions immediately after reporting and gathering necessary evidence. There's no point hanging out with a hacker; don't forget you have your own game to play. The second method is way more effective: email Rockstar directly. Attach the screenshot of everyone in the lobby by pressing Z, and ideally include a short video clip of the cheater. Briefly explain the situation (time, cheater's ID, type of hacks used) in Traditional Chinese or English (doing both works even better). You can easily find their support email with a quick web search. The third way is through the official website at www.rockstargames.com/support where you can file reports and upload screenshots or video clips, pretty much the same as email. This kind of report is still most effective if you report them in-game first and then follow up with an email. Whether it's a report or an appeal, the first reply you get via email will most likely be an automated bot response, but there *is* follow-up. For example, with reports, once Rockstar sends you an email saying something like "Thank you for contributing to a fair gaming environment," it means there's a strong chance another "falsely banned" player was just created somewhere out there. The official website and support section are like the game itself—the servers are overseas so the pages load a bit slow. As long as your internet isn't completely trash, you'll eventually get through, you just need a little patience. That should be about enough. This updated review is aimed at newbies just getting into the game. If any veterans see this and want to add anything, you're always welcome. Anyone talking trash, acting superior, or flexing gets deleted—don't waste space in the comment section. ---------- Divider ---------- 2017-11-07 Original: 1000+ hours online, beat offline 3 times (twice on cracked versions, bought the legit version and beat it in first-person). If any Chinese players are hesitating about whether to buy the game and happen to stumble across my review, forget every other review out there and just focus on mine. Also, seriously, don't read reviews before buying games. Reviews will ruin this game. The GTA series is pure nostalgia for me. From Vice City back in elementary school, to San Andreas later on, and then GTA IV and its episodes—every game is a story, a piece of my own memories, even if I could only play cracked versions back then. Rockstar is an amazing company. Every single one of their titles was insanely massive for its time, and GTA V is no exception. The offline mode alone is worth the full price. Offline mode is genuinely, truly, suuuuper amazing! Online mode is basically just a bonus. For a lot of players, if there was no online mode, they'd just go play a cracked version. They only bought the legit game for online. Since online is so massively popular, let's talk about a few practical issues: 1. Network issues. Rockstar's servers are overseas, so they can't provide lightning-fast connections for most areas and networks in China. The best workaround is to get a game booster. I use Netease UU (others like Dolphin, Panda, or QiYou work too), though I could connect natively at first—it really depends on your own specific setup. If you're too stubborn to buy a booster, can't connect natively, and refuse to use other methods, there's really nothing that can be done, and your gaming experience naturally won't be good. 2. The "false ban" issue. Hearing about this makes me want to punch someone. Because "false bans" do not exist. Every single sob story, cry for help, and act of playing the victim you see is just a cheater or money-drop scrub putting on a stellar acting performance, without exception. Are there players who actually get falsely banned? Yes. But if you are the one-in-a-million-billion case who genuinely gets falsely banned, the correct move isn't running to forums or dropping a negative review on Steam; it's bravely emailing Rockstar to appeal. Every single account that goes through the proper channels gets unbanned (the truth fears no investigation), and Rockstar replies to emails very seriously. So next time you see posts and comments crying about being falsely banned, just silently look down on them. If you're curious enough to click on their profile and check their post history, you'll probably find them advertising cheats and money drops in some other thread. I once had over 1 million in cash dropped on me by a hacker, and I immediately emailed Rockstar with screenshots of my balance, income/expenses, and everyone in the session, explaining the situation. Rockstar replied telling me not to worry, and the illegal funds were wiped in the next update. Cheaters, legitimate players move with this kind of confidence. 3. Newbies hitting the road. What's the very first thing you do when you buy the game? Play offline, obviously. A lot of newbie friends haven't played GTA-style games before, and since GTA V added an online mode, player-to-player interaction raises the skill requirement for everyone. Offline mode will teach you the absolute basics hand-in-hand, like driving, flying, and parachuting—things that online completely skips, assuming you already have them mastered. If you want to avoid dragging others down and actually have fun yourself, go experience the super-duper fun offline mode first! Once you're familiar with the controls and ready to jump into online, I recommend hitting up the forums (like the GTA5 Baidu Tieba) and checking out the pinned newbie survival guides. Because the freedom in online is unimaginably huge, you can do literally anything, which ironically leaves a lot of newbies totally lost on what to do. Join a friendly, cheat-free QQ group; there are patient veteran players in there willing to carry you through leveling up and making money, plus other newbies stepping into Los Santos for the first time who want to grind together for the future. If you're playing all by yourself, the online mode is honestly pretty unfriendly. It's way more fun to find a crew you can actually play with, make a bunch of diverse gaming buddies to run heists with, and just take in the scenery together~ Seriously, do not use cheats, money drops, or any other rule-breaking bullshit! Stick to being a legit player and you will never get "falsely banned." All of this is just to clear the names of GTA and Rockstar. I'm not riding Rockstar's dick; I just can't stand cheaters. You got banned? Go appeal! What, too scared? Then stop showing your face and whining about a false ban, alright?! At the end of the day, I hope players who love GTA just as much as I do can find their own fun in Los Santos!!

translation_en: Anyone planning to play online honestly and without cheating should not buy this game! This review was updated on December 8, 2017 (addendum at the very bottom). I last quit in the autumn of 2015 because hackers were everywhere. I bought it on my own account during the 2017 summer sale and jumped in with great joy, but what do I see? Hackers, hackers, and more hackers... man, and it pisses me off when people call them "modders." It's like calling a prostitute an "escort"—people constantly typing "any modder here???". These motherfucking "modders" ruin your online game and, even if you have passive mode on, they can jam a guitar up your ass and make you do backflips in the air. Even after 2 years, they haven't cleaned up the hackers nor have they improved the game's matchmaking speed... Even if you have a top-tier PC, you'll connect slowly, mark my words. Making money is also very hard, let me point that out. In short: buy it if you really want to, but keep this in mind; if you want to wait 3-5 mins while loading into the game just to have hackers ruin it for you... suit yourselves. ------------------------------------------------------------------ October 13, 2017: In about 2 weeks I ran into 24 hacker motherfuckers; I reported them, I switched servers to get away from them, but what's the result? Result: I ran into hackers on the server I escaped to as well. Heyyyyy Rockstar! I hope your servers get a virus and you can never launch your game again. ------------------------------------------------------------------ October 27, 2017: I'm writing this again for those who want to buy the game and see this negative review; the game is great, driving around anywhere on the map at night in a customized car with ultra settings is amazing, the sea view is great and watching the city view from the mountain is a different kind of great, however, in the online game, especially in servers with more than 20 people, you inevitably run into a hacker, and no matter how patient a person you are, you eventually lose your mind. I looked at the reviews and there are people low-key praising the hackers; stay away from those who say "buy the game without thinking twice" instead of telling people the truth. I've been playing this series since GTA 2, and despite this review, I continue to play GTA 5 day by day because the game is good and high quality. Let me share a small observation I made about the game: the time that passes from Rockstar Games' opening video until the game is fully loaded and you can start controlling your character is 3:30 minutes. If you're lucky, the game throws you into a solo server (which shortens this time a bit), and if you get bored there, you can connect to other players using the find new server option (the loading time is long because the game loads its massive map as a whole). If you've installed the game on an SSD, this loading time might get a bit shorter, but matchmaking speed is up to Rockstar. I apologize to the decent human beings for my swearing-filled text, and I state that those who thumbs-down my review and move on are connected to the person or persons who are "modders." Wish you good games, regards. ----------------------------------------------------------------- November 2, 2017: Because the negative review got so many views, it was immediately pushed to the background. Go ahead, push it back, keep driving this many people to spend their money. ----------------------------------------------------------------- December 8, 2017: For some reason, there has been an incredible increase in the number of hackers lately. Hackers were already plentiful, but I don't know what happened, these bastards have increased massively. So much so that the moment I switch to a new server, the number of hackers gets even higher (I ran into 5 hackers in 1 server). Man, I'm doing a yacht defense mission, the guy instantly teleports to my yacht and finishes the mission. Reporting doesn't do shit either. I'm hiding during the executive search mission; you are not visible on any player's radar while on that mission, but a hacker bastard teleports right next to me, throws a rocket, and kills me. They managed to wear me out—level 157, 2.78 K/D, who doesn't let a fly buzz by in the game—so I've got nothing to say (what else is there to say anyway?). You made a legendary game, but you didn't back up its online support (player support). This success is yours, dear RPG-minded ROCKSTAR GAMES EMPLOYEES! Be proud of your creation. Take the map of GTA 5 and S H O V E I T U P Y O U R A S S !

translation_en: Great game, Rockstar's game quality is always top-notch, and getting the Online mode bundled with the single-player makes it super consumer-friendly. If you're buying this game just for the Online mode, I'd suggest checking out the negative reviews first before making a decision, because there are way too many toxic trolls, griefers, and straight-up hackers online, just to save yourself the headache. As a beginner you're squishy, so I suggest turning on Passive Mode right away. Change sessions immediately if you run into a cheater, and go buy a heavy utility vest (at a clothing store) first—you'll need it for heists. Also, keep your snacks and armor fully stocked. Don't try to face-tank everything; hide when you're low on health and let the high-level players handle it. The higher your level, the harder you are to kill. You'd better avoid Lamar's missions; the success rate is insanely low, they're not fit for beginners, and the payout is trash. You can press Esc -> Online -> Jobs to play some contact missions, or use Quick Join on your phone. For example, Simeon's repo missions and Blow Up I-III (hosting requires you to unlock certain levels) have very low difficulty. The latter can be soloed. Don't rush to turn the mission in once it's done; wait a bit and the payout will increase, maxing out at around $19,000. Once you're a higher level, go play 1-6 player missions like Titan of a Job. You're likely to run into high-level veterans, so you basically won't fail, and you can just chill and get carried while making decent cash. You can keep replaying them right after finishing, which is super convenient. Money is tight in the early game, so you better spend it wisely. Save up to buy a high-end apartment for around $200k (I bought the one next to Maze Bank; you can teleport home using the job teleport trick with Lester's phone, and it's right next to the office). This lets you start heists. After beating the Fleeca Job, you can buy the Armored Kuruma at a discount—pretty much everyone owns one. It massively boosts your survivability and makes doing missions way less nerve-wracking. Other vehicles, apart from the Buzzard which is a cargo-grinding essential, can be bought depending on your financial situation. Once you're somewhat established, you can move on to the later heists. It's best to have a fixed crew, because you never know how your random matchmaking teammates are going to die. Having a veteran carry you through Pacific Standard is amazing. If you don't have these conditions met, you're better off just grinding as a CEO, because waiting for people and failing missions is just a waste of time, and you can easily end up making nothing after hours of playing. Just buy the $1M CEO office. Location is literally non-existent (tan90°), because you can teleport so it doesn't matter where it is. If you're rich and feeling fancy, you can buy the $2M one in downtown. For warehouses, you should get medium warehouses—at least two, so you can bypass the cooldown. If you only have one, you can do CEO work to wait out the timer. Only upgrade to a large warehouse if you're confident you'll stick with it long-term. I don't have many insights on specific warehouse locations yet, I'll figure that out later. You can also try vehicle cargo for I/E, but I'm too broke to buy it yet. I feel like a fake level 100, broke as hell and haven't even finished Pacific Standard. PS: Haven't been falsely banned yet, leaving a positive review for now.

translation_en: I was born in a city, full of curiosity about everything online. I was driving my stolen car down those familiar streets, but suddenly a missile flew in and the screen just showed wasted. At first, I didn't understand, but that guy kept chasing me down and killing me. Back then I didn't know about levels, I only knew a player kept hunting me, and I had no choice but to turn on passive mode, then slowly do missions alone. As my playtime grew, I got my first apartment, a 10-car garage near Maze Bank, which wiped out all my savings of 200k. Having my own home felt so reassuring, being able to put the cars I stole inside. I also got my very first truly own car, the Elegy (lol). Later I found out I could host heists myself, but my level was too low back then, and nobody wanted to carry me, so just finishing a heist once made me feel quite satisfied. I remember it very vividly, the Prison Break finale took over three hours, and all four of us were newbies. I'm still very grateful to the three guys who accompanied me through that mission back then. Gradually, I found people to play with, joined their group, and we did heists together, helped me level up, immediately jumped into sessions to talk trash and fight back when I got bullied, and helped me source cargo and steal cars. I still remember during a double money event, we ran the Pacific Standard for over a dozen hours. I just tagged along and slacked off, didn't know how to glitch the plane or the cut. Just like that, one day I had my own office and the long-awaited yacht. A long time later, I was finally close to "graduating," having my own CEO office and sports cars. But the people who used to grind missions with me all stopped playing. Now they play PUBG every day, and I became alone again. With nothing better to do, I drive around the city, lounge on my yacht, hover a helicopter over Los Santos, turn on passive mode and watch them bicker, which I think is pretty entertaining. In the end, I played through single-player mode once, and haven't touched this game since. Thanks to GTA V for letting me experience that feeling of living together with many players, that time was truly happy. Regarding cheaters: Actually, in all my time playing, I haven't encountered that many cheaters. It wasn't as bad as other players say with hackers flying everywhere. Maybe I was just lucky. If you run into a cheater, just find a new session, that's what I've always done. Regarding bans: I have 200 hours so far and have never been banned, and my money has never been adjusted either. To sum it up in one sentence: don't do stupid shit, and don't be greedy. If you run into a cheater, just leave the session. If you're hoping someone will mod money for you or whatever, you can't blame anyone else if you get banned. Finally, a bit of advice for newbies: before buying the game, please make sure you have friends to play with in voice chat. This game is really hard to play solo; you'll get griefed by all kinds of people, for no reason at all. I used to see people fly a Hydra to spawn-kill a whole lobby and just say "I'm having fun." True, it's just like real society, everyone has their own way of living. Also, newbies must not be snowflakes, do not be a snowflake, DO NOT BE A SNOWFLAKE! When newbies join heists, because your health is low and you can't buy heavy armor, it's easy to die, and when you die the mission restarts. Don't blame others for kicking you either, it's best to find someone to carry you. In the early game, save up to buy an apartment first, then buy the Kuruma—you must remember to buy the armored one. That car is bulletproof and is an absolute god-tier tool for many missions. After that, buy an office, a warehouse, a garage, and then buy the Buzzard helicopter for deliveries. Pay attention: early on, don't waste a lot of money on expensive apartments and cars, and you'd better not buy a yacht (I suffered a huge loss on that myself, once you buy the yacht it basically just sits there collecting dust). You need to make your money work for you, you'll get all these things eventually. That's my take on GTA V. No matter how much other people trash it, I still think it's a piece of art. The mechanics, the environment are all flawless to me, especially the driving feel, which no other game can compare to.

When I started playing GTA Online, there was at least some kind of balance between newbies and regular players. The c*nts in Kurumas, Hydras and other abomination could be killed, albeit with difficulty. But now, besides those past idiots, there are new idiots in: APCs, rocket bikes and jets that you simply cannot kill, because by the time you manage to kill them, they will have killed you 10 times over. Also, there used to be this "fun and chaotic vibe" which got completely ruined by f*cking "Businesses", because now players either grind money just for the sake of grinding, or stop others from grinding. Yeah, when the first "business" update came out it was interesting and fresh, and it also gave you an easy way to make money, but with one catch: YOU had to pay at least a fucking MILLION AND A HALF just to start! Now to the point: what did the "Smuggler's Run" update bring us? Here's what: Another "business", boring tattoos, retarded clothes (that quad-lens helmet totally killed me), new multicolored masks... I'm not one of those guys who scream "BACK IN THE DAY IT WAS BETTER, NOW IT'S SH*T!", it's just the fucking truth if you remember what great global updates we used to get: Heists, Lowriders and so on. And what do we get now? "SMUGGLER'S RUN" is just another "business" update, right after another identical "GUNRUNNING" update... Bottom line: As always, no complaints about the story mode, but serious questions about online. The latest updates are a spit in the face of the community that's waiting for a story DLC or at least some decent online updates, though online can't be saved anymore...

I immediately contacted Rockstar Games support to check if it was a mistake and requested that if I actually violated any rules, they disclose what those were. It was completely unacceptable, so I replied asking them not to send a template email and to disclose what caused it. Then, 'precisely 3 days later,' the exact same template email was sent to me again. It seems they intend to play "see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil" and just run away from it. After ignoring anti-cheat measures for so long, they bothered to adjust in-game balances just a few days before a major update, and the content added in that update is (in-game) astronomically expensive... If you are thinking of buying this, please consider very carefully that the fruits of your honest, steady grinding might one day be unreasonably snatched away without any explanation. Also, the online mode has totally inadequate anti-cheat measures. God mode and auto-aim go without saying, but other unimaginable cheats run rampant, like being suddenly teleported and blown to death, or having cages dropped from the sky to trap you. You can only play the new content in a world swarming with these ghouls and goblins. If you are considering buying this because you're drawn to the new update, please understand that you will be forced to play with these kinds of freaks. translation_en: I've always been amazed by GTA V reviews where people in online say "I was just playing and then got banned for no reason." Well, my turn has come, but I wasn't banned "for no reason." Played 440+ hours in 2 years, never once used cheats, glitches, etc. Sometime in early summer 2017, there was an episode when a cheater appeared in the session and started teleporting players. He teleported me out of my Hydra into the desert at the airfield in the north. He disabled normal walking, I could only move by jumping. He dropped some money on top of me, somewhere around $10k, after which he blew everyone up and left. I hadn't launched the game after that for about a month. Today (27.08.2017) I launched it and saw that after starting a session, there was a message saying "we adjusted your account balance," and they took all my money, about ~$4.6 million. A tiny amount honestly earned from missions. They didn't ban me, didn't take away my real estate or vehicles, just wiped my bank account. I wrote to support about this. Judging by reviews, I'm sure they'll either reply with a boilerplate response or won't reply at all and the situation won't be resolved. Meanwhile, absolute hell continues in sessions. Cheaters are flying, teleporting, God-moding, dropping money, etc. Those cheaters I used to report are safely continuing to play. GTA Online is like a cheater state where all conditions are created for them, they're given perks, and are encouraged in every possible way. After the money wipe episode, I'd download cheats and use them myself, but I don't want to ruin my Steam reputation and profile. And seriously, Rockstar is still incapable of dealing with cheaters. Their anti-cheat measures feel like carpet bombing a city with napalm just to kill some roaches. I don't think anything will change in this situation, so: [b]Strongly not recommended to buy for GTA:Online. One (1) talentless R* employee out of ten (10) cheaters.[/b]

translation_en: GTA, a memory of my childhood. First off, I gotta say this review is just my personal opinion, so forgive me if it triggers you. Everyone's entitled to their own thoughts, right? Jokes aside, GTA 5 was the first game I ever bought on Steam. To be honest, I played a pirated copy on console first, and came to Steam to buy it legally after beating it. The story mode is seriously top-notch. Anyone who's played it won't deny that. Whether it's the plot, the graphics, or the handling, it's an absolute masterpiece of a game. The online mode—doing heists with crewmates, street shootouts, being dropped into a free world like Los Santos where you're above the law and anyone can be king—how satisfying is that? Remember back in the day, when I first started out online and didn't know what the hell to do, just stealing cars and killing NPCs, all the way to becoming a filthy rich veteran heist expert? From noob to badass, we went through a lot. I remember busting my ass, working hard and diligently on countless jobs, scraping together 100 million, pouring that hard-earned cash into Lamar's Benny's workshop, collecting every single lowrider I could trick out, driving my favorite ride down to the beach to dance battle with friends, blasting music on the radio and busting out totally rhythm-less moves. The genuine happiness from deep inside was just spilling out. Later on, I ran into those sweaty-ass hackers (cheaters) going mental in the lobbies. As if cheating and killing people wasn't already trashy enough, they gotta hop on text and voice chat to say hi to everyone's moms and families in the whole lobby. Chinese, foreigners, I'm not singling anyone out, I'm just saying all hackers are absolute garbage. Maybe you guys are just so insecure in real life that you have to use these game-breaking ways to comfort yourselves? And then later on, the game kept updating, pumping out new cars and new modes, and I slowly lost my passion for it. Now when I log back in, lobbies are crawling with hackers, endless wrongful bans, good guys getting screwed over while the bad guys walk free. Luckily, as a clean player, I've never been falsely banned. Do no evil, fear no ghost knocking. Plus, Los Santos isn't the pure Los Santos it used to be anymore. Flying bikes everywhere, cars driving on the ocean surface. It makes me wonder, is this future tech? Is the next step giving characters superpowers? Why not just go play Saints Row instead? This Los Santos is no longer the Los Santos I wanted, or at least it doesn't give me that original GTA vibe anymore. At the end of the day, it's a good game, worth a play. It's just not where my nostalgia lies anymore. Nuff said. 700 hours. Loved it. But you changed. You turned into someone I don't even know. You're not the GTA in my memories anymore. Since it's come to this, we walk our separate ways. Plenty of people will still love you, but you've lost one of me. PS: The above is purely my personal opinion. I don't deny the game's strong points, so I sincerely hope you guys won't take things out of context. Thanks a lot!

translation_en: After almost 600 hours, I feel like I can say a few things about the game, specifically for those who haven't bought it yet and might still be unsure. Let's start. Pros: - They haven't abandoned the game, updates are still dropping to this day. The new expansions, aka DLCs, are all free, and they also try to keep the cheaters away. - The game runs even on weak PC setups, though it's more recommended to have 8 GB of RAM and a 2 GB—or rather 4 GB—graphics card, and a decent processor wouldn't hurt either, maybe a higher-end i3. (I played 537 hours with a hard 30 FPS, but it's such an entertaining game that it takes your attention right away from the lagging.) - The graphics are genuinely like the teaser videos here on Steam, though I suspect those are on ultra settings, but even if you turn them to the lowest, the game doesn't lose much of itself, it's just more FPS-friendly. - Tons of missions in the ONLINE part, heist-wise the game totally delivers, but if someone isn't really into roleplay, it's worth trying out the freeroam as well as adventure and FUN maps, which obviously let you earn money and XP. But while we're on the topic of missions, let's go back a bit to the roleplay side: on the server, you can start your own supply missions, like within a CEO office where you can buy a cargo warehouse. Don't go thinking we're filling it with legal stuff, of course, it's all illegal business here. Then there's also the vehicle warehouse, which is pretty hard to pay off for a beginner, but totally pays off over time. Anyone who has played the GTA series knows we've returned to the core genre of car theft, only here you have to steal tuned vehicles from gangsters and deliver them to our warehouse. Just watch out not to smash and crash them because the game docks your pay and that's lost money. To sell them, you also have to tune one or two other things, and that costs money too, but unlike Los Santos Customs where you pay per part, you pay a fixed price and can slap anything on there—don't forget to put offroad tires on, otherwise you'll spin out on the road, which isn't great especially when gangsters are chasing you. There's also the biker gang, which is pretty neat; basically you buy a motorcycle club and through the laptop you can buy drug businesses and a money laundry, which you have to manage in terms of supplies and equipment since upgrading for + profit doesn't hurt. Putting up security cameras isn't a bad idea either, so that enemy gangsters/cops don't raid/confiscate the products in our labs and laundries. - Anyone who loves the GTA series knows this game is worth 60 euros, and you only have to pay it once since, as I mentioned, the DLCs are free. Unless the person wants to buy in-game money, in which case it definitely won't be just 60 euros... Cons: - There was only one thing I hated in the game, unlike others it's not their ban system. Back in the day, the system worked by having people review reports about cheaters, and players who were given money/XP by them would also get a 1-month suspension or more, or even a permanent ban from the online mode, so back then a lot of players said a permanent goodbye to the game way too easily.. Fortunately, they've fixed this nowadays with a so-called anti-cheat system that only punishes the cheater, while the money given to a player is just subtracted from them—there are also rumors floating around the internet that the game can put you into the negative. So it's good to pay attention and not really accept money/XP in those situations, purposefully leaving the given session and joining another one. (session = server) I hope I managed to answer a few questions in this review, and I trust I managed to help many of you in making your decision. If you'd like to play with me or have any more questions, feel free to add me as a friend on Steam and ask away!

translation_en: Bought GTA V two years ago, over 1300 hours on record, online level over 200. A game that cost over 260 million and took 5 years to develop is undeniably a masterpiece that Rockstar Games put a lot of heart into, but once the game is sold, do they just not need to give a shit about after-sales service anymore? The online gaming experience is really bad. I don't give a fuck if players use cheats, but please don't be a dick just to ruin other people's fun when you gain nothing from it either. I had a time when a cheater was attacking me, I shot back, the guy didn't lose a single drop of health, and then he used cheats to kill every single player in the session using my name, followed by quitting the lobby while I didn't do a damn thing. This kind of gameplay that ruins the game balance is totally pointless. On top of that, there's the disconnection issue. I ran into this problem right from the start, but I wouldn't run my mouth without being sure whether it was my own internet acting up. However, based on the long-term gaming experience of me and my friends, as well as reviews on Steam, the disconnection issue definitely exists, and after all these years it's still never been fixed. I currently live abroad and occasionally go back to China, but whether I'm in China or abroad I still keep getting disconnected constantly. Every now and then it hits you with "connection to the server lost, returning to Grand Theft Auto V," and constantly prompts that connection to the game services failed so you can't launch a Heist. All these problems ultimately boil down to the game devs just not giving a shit. And honestly, I probably aren't the only one hoping for new Heists, right? The devs can come up with so many creative things like CEOs, Biker clubs, and Bunkers, so I honestly find it hard to believe they lack the creativity to make new Heists. Personally, it just feels like the devs are just milking the game for cash now. After saying all that, I still gave it a negative review, but it's not because I don't like this game. If GTA V only had a single-player mode, based on the actual single-player experience and out of respect for the developers, I would definitely give it a positive review. The devs put a lot of thought into single-player; both the story and the graphics are on par with almost all AAA game companies and even surpass some of them. But do players only play single-player and never touch online? Online is the main reason why the game still maintains its popularity years after release. So, to sum it all up, I can only give a negative review due to the devs' lack of care for the game in its later stages.

translation_en: The biggest problem with this game is false bans. I got banned back in early January. Come to think of it, there are probably three reasons why I might have been banned: 1) I once got caught in a money glitch lobby, but I didn't know the host was glitching money at the time. As soon as I realized, I immediately quit. 2) I was playing with a friend who was cheating and straight-up teleported to the destination during a heist. 3) I killed a random player on purpose, but only once. Those three points are the most likely reasons I can think of. At the time, I got so pissed I wanted to leave a negative review, but then I figured I'd already put 300+ hours into the game, so I just let it go for a while. So, chalking it up to just having bad luck, I decided to play again this summer. When I logged on, I noticed a few noobs I used to carry were already level 200 or 300, and they all said they modded their levels. When I started playing with them again, I saw they were using a bunch of cheats and heavy-duty mods. When I asked if they weren't afraid of getting banned, they said if they were gonna get banned, it would've happened ages ago. So I immediately decided I'm done playing again. This game's ban system is such a pain in the ass. Law-abiding players like me get hit by stray bullets and banned, while those cheaters and modders who use them every single day are still online. I gotta ask Rockstar, do you guys just think this game is so popular that you can randomly ban people to prove how many players you have, figuring banning one person doesn't matter, and now that you feel players are starting to drift away, you've loosened up again? Upvote my review so people wanting to buy this game get a warning. With so many people playing this game, the next one to get banned might just be you.

translation_en: First off, I gotta recommend GTA 5, this game is seriously so much fun. The single-player story is super, super touching. Finishing it feels like watching an ultra-long movie, and then for days after you feel like something's missing...... That alone is totally worth the price, plus the crazy variety of online gameplay: buying cars, houses, planes, yachts, living the high life, bye-bye real life. Seriously, nobody needs to hesitate on buying this. ٩(˃̶͈̀௰˂̶͈́)و BUT! There's a but...... What's up with all these negative reviews about false bans lately? Are there actually false bans? Yeah, there fucking are! And you get banned completely out of nowhere......(´･ω･`) Let me make one thing clear first: false bans in GTA Online aren't like what those Rockstar fanboys think. People who get banned genuinely might not have done a damn thing, because me and my friend are two of them (or should I say two of the victims?). Nearly 300 hours in the game, never used a cheat, but when I got banned I kind saw it coming. Because twice during heists with friends, a teammate was cheating. The first time I had no idea at first, only realized near the end when I saw he was using a teleport cheat... so basically our mission got completed with a cheater, which I guess technically counts as "benefiting from cheating." The other time was right when we loaded into a mission session, some Chinese guy typed in chat that he was cheating to carry us, and my friend and me instantly quit the game. Then, during the ban wave a month ago, both of us got hit ˊ_>ˋ. But two days later, Rockstar emailed him saying it was a mistake and unbanned him that day, while I had to wait a whole month until the day before yesterday to get unbanned. Also, the fact that they send emails admitting to false bans and unbanning people proves that Rockstar isn't like you guys think—they DO false ban, and a ban doesn't automatically mean you did something wrong. Due to game mechanics, having a cheater in your session or accidentally triggering a bug during a mission can get you falsely banned... (One time doing a mission I got out of a car and instantly fell right through the map. If you don't believe me add me, I've got screenshots as proof, not sure if that played a part in getting banned......) (P.S. To the actual cheaters, don't the fuck come whining under my review with that "yeah right, you're just wrongfully banned" bullshit. I can just check your playtime and what else you have in your library. I refuse to believe anyone plays this game just to cheat, one-shot everything, use remote control, teleport, and infinite money hacks for hundreds of hours and actually finds it fun. People with hundreds of hours have already built their own empires, they don't need to cheat. But if you really can cheat for hundreds of hours without getting banned, I honestly tip my hat to your luck and persistence （−＿−；）) (P.P.S. Gotta say one more thing, I just despise you little shits who cheat for money, but for the griefers who use hacks to remotely fling players into a spiral or blow them up on the spot: do you just have miserable real-life problems, get looked down on, and act like absolute life failures so you have to come vent online by cheating? (╯°Д°）╯︵ /(.□ . \)) Right now I haven't left a negative review because I can understand how hard this situation is for Rockstar to handle. translation_en: It was September 18th, 2013, the first time I got to play this game on my Xbox 360. I was so hyped that I pre-ordered it. I remember how good and balanced GTA Online was in 2014, the DLCs that dropped and broke the internet, companies delaying their games so they wouldn't release on the same day as a DLC for this game. Then they released the Next Gen version, holy shit, everyone went nuts over the incredible graphics of this game running at ultra 1080p. But what about now? What has this game become? Back in the day, having a simple PvP fight was amazing, balanced for both sides, it was just you, your gun, and your skills. Today, whoever has the most money wins, along with anyone who can use "tricks" like killing themselves quickly so the enemy doesn't get the kill, tanks that shoot 60 rounds like it's an assault rifle, armored vehicles, "broken" options to get ammo without having to go to Ammu-Nation, an advantage through Bullshark Testosterone that doubles your damage and gives you way more bullet resistance, more armored vehicles, packed with modders and glitches, an extremely toxic community and above all, the game has become EXTREMELY PAY TO WIN. My dear friend planning to buy this game right now, give up if you want to play fair: yachts for almost 10 million, ridiculously expensive apartments, ridiculously expensive bunkers, ridiculously expensive cars, ridiculously expensive WEAPONS. And of course, I couldn't forget the new MK II sniper with explosive ammo that destroys helicopters and jets in two shots. Like the old-gen vehicles? Entity XF? Osiris? Zentorno? Forget about them, they're obsolete in races and all the vehicles that are better than those are ridiculously expensive. Maybe you'll get lucky and land in a session with a hacker and he'll give you money. But maybe you'll get unlucky and get banned because HE used hacks and gave you money. Rockstar Games broke this game, and with each passing day they destroy it more and more. They took away car insurance for now, but when and if it comes back, be even more prepared to empty your pockets: every time you destroy another player's vehicle, you'll have to pay their car insurance and get branded as a "Bad Sport." And get this, that's not even all—if you destroy a heavily armored vehicle, like the ones from the latest DLC, you'll easily pay 20 thousand GTA dollars. Now imagine that annoying player where all you do is destroy their vehicle, they pull out another one, and it stays in this loop until you leave the session? Yeah, even if you have millions, it won't last long. What made me hate this game the most on the new generation is precisely how unbalanced it has become. On Xbox 360, Rockstar Games literally ABANDONED the game, ALL sessions are CROWDED with modders, extreme tryhards, invisible players with infinite ammo and infinite rolling. This game is no longer what it once was. EDIT: Orbital Cannon... I don't need to say anything else. EDIT²: The game is currently infested with hackers, every single session has some blatant or low-key hacker to ruin your game, some just because they think they're doing justice by kicking or crashing a player who has a habit of killing others in sessions... and the consequence of that is in every session people are calling each other hackers, when in reality most of the time none of them actually are. Everyone is paranoid and any lucky shot gets you called one. On top of that, the game is getting heavier by the day. Those with mid-range PCs who used to play without any stuttering and with stable FPS now struggle to run the game "smoothly" like before. This just proves once again that Rockstar doesn't give a shit about the players, they only care about rolling out expensive and useless DLCs instead of fixing the problems THAT THE ENTIRE COMMUNITY complains about.

translation_en: Now GTA is overwhelmingly negative, and as a player with over 400 hours, I find it kind of unbelievable, so I'll just express my thoughts here for new players to take a good look at. 1. Regarding the bandwagon hate The latest wave of people bashing GTA are all complaining about mods being banned. Let me ask you, how many players in the entire GTA community actually use mods? And how much would those who genuinely know how to use mods actually be affected by the official game forbidding them? Most people are just jumping on the bandwagon. Besides, mods are the direct breeding ground for cheats. Let me ask you, what game company would ever allow cheat-generating software for a game they're currently operating to exist? 2. Regarding getting banned for no reason I've only experienced one ban myself, back in the summer of 2016. I hadn't played for a few months, and when I came back, my CEO office and warehouses had no money left to buy things. So I found a few friends and exploited a bug to grind the Criminal Mastermind challenge, farmed a few million, and got banned a few days later. I was pretty pissed back then too, but I didn't come here to bitch about it. Personally, I feel that if Rockstar bans your account, you definitely did something against the rules. Otherwise, are the people at Rockstar fucking retarded? Why would they ban your account for no reason just so you can come here and curse out their game and hurt their sales? Is that even possible? And would those "so-called" genuine players with hundreds of hours actually quit the game forever just because of a 10-day ban? 3. Regarding connection issues My home is in a tier-2 city in Northeast China, using a 20Mbps China Unicom connection, and I never use a VPN/accelerator. Sure, there are disconnections sometimes, but they're all within an acceptable range. Once or twice every half month isn't enough to ruin the gaming experience. 4. Impatient and fickle people When you buy GTA V, you're actually getting two games: GTA V single-player and GTA Online. The story mode in single-player is damn well-made, and there are lots of interesting side missions. Even if you don't like doing missions, the super high freedom lets you play however you like. But right now, so many reviews don't even mention this. Because a lot of people buy the game just to play Online, just to get a big house, sports cars, and a yacht in Online. But what do you do when you just made a character and have no money? You look for all sorts of ways to cheat/grind. Once you get banned after exploiting, "Oh man, I'm so pissed, let me write a negative review and trash them." Killing and getting killed are normal competition in the game, but a lot of people just yell "cheater!" the moment they can't beat someone. So the problem isn't with the game itself, it's with people's mindsets. Get a few good friends together to play some toxic stunt races, grab a helicopter for a high-altitude random-spot parachute jump, take an old rifle up the mountains to go hunting—a game with high freedom has all kinds of ways to play. If you choose the most exhausting and boring way for yourself, don't bitch about the game being trash. One last thing, even if the Online operation is trash, it's still only half of GTA V. If you're going to leave a negative review for a game, you should at least have played the game completely before posting it, and your review should at least mention the single-player part of GTA V. That is the bare minimum respect a game and its development studio deserve.
