translation_en: I'll add fuel to the fire. You can see a lot of negative reviews here, but the latest wave of them happened because of Take-Two's policy regarding modding. Let me warn you right away, there won't be another word about modding here, because I don't give a shit about mods. Instead, you can get a huge dose of "pleasure" from plenty of other things: * Cheaters - pure classic. I don't even need to describe how they blow you up, teleport you, and spawn props on you more often than they give you money. Anyway, dirty money is useless anyway since the system tracks it and just removes it in about a week. There's no point in spending it, but you don't get banned for it. * Single-player without support - also a pretty popular topic, especially if you read the foreign forum. People are begging for single-player DLC, but all to no avail. The plot and gameplay are not bad, most will dig the single-player. But don't even hope for expanded content. * PvP - if you love PvP in the GTA series, starting from SA:MP, ending with hanging out through the crappy Games for Windows LIVE in GTA IV, then I'll disappoint you. Here, PvP is essentially jerking off to first-person animation bugs, macros, and heavy vehicles, ranging from armored cars to APCs with missile launchers and fighter jets, which are best shot down with explosive sniper rifle rounds, but you still have to grind to get those first. Want PvP? Go to specially designated adversary modes, which, to be fair, aren't that popular anyway. * PvE - no, I won't describe the missions and actions. What's more interesting is the combat against NPCs, which looks pretty clunky. In multiplayer, most PvE battles will be played on high difficulty if you want to get at least some reward. When you shoot an NPC in the body, they fall down. On the one hand, pain shock, fine, but even with that, people don't fall like limp rags to the floor. As a result, you have to waste a decent amount of ammo on a downed target if your hands couldn't manage to hit the target's head. Elements like ragdolls hinder the game rather than embellish it. But you can get used to and adapt to this situation. * Audience - it's no surprise that GTA is a pop product, so the audience is broad, which means we shouldn't even stutter about its quality. Illiterate people, aggressive underage players, local jokers who think it's funny to create a guide on how to get into a car in Steam Guides. In general, all of this is absolute hell. In the foreign community, it's not much better, actually. And playing heists with those same Asians is equivalent to jacking off with pliers. Players readily join open official crews like IGN, LSB, or MP3. Most players from such crews can be safely ignored, as they generally have nothing of value to offer, although there are exceptions. * Earning money - another ladle of tar in a sea of excrement. Desperate players have already realized that the best way to earn money is to beg from cheaters. But as I said before, this makes no sense. In the end, you're left with heists, which require a good team of 4 people to avoid wasting time, or doing other forms of "grinding." You can export/import cars using the 10/10/12 scheme to sell only top-range cars, or sell drugs or weapons through biker club warehouses or the bunker. But there's not much fun in that either. Doing missions in a session often attracts some dumbass who has plenty of money thanks to a shady past, but is very much bored, so he will pester you with his entire bought-up arsenal, preventing you from reaching your goal. In such cases, of course, you can resort to "session-emptying" methods to remain alone in them and/or with friends. In general, R* did everything so you would donate for local currency instead of earning it yourself. * Pricing policy - I won't even mention that 2000 rubles is a questionable price. It's a AAA product that entered the stratosphere with a deafening bang, so everything's okay. Relatively tolerable. However, adding to the previous point about earning money, there's another minor detail. Look at the in-game item prices. They won't show you any mercy, so you'll have to reach your goal with blood, sweat, and diarrhea if you please. Prices for items are probably logically fair, but the game's economy won't let you earn such sums in a relatively short time. Besides, buying that same yacht, which is practically of no real use, will result in having to pay its upkeep every 24 in-game hours. (Along with the upkeep of all other real estate and the mechanic's services). * Loading times - GTA V is a pretty heavy game, so it's no surprise that loading takes a long time. Everyone already knows this, but get ready for another surprise. The loading can turn out to be eternal, while the game thinks you've already joined the session, judging by the active chat. This phenomenon is often typical when playing with those same laggy Asians. More suffering! * Content - since the single-player game was left without content, you're probably wondering what the multiplayer content is like? Actually, not the worst. However, R* spends a lot of energy creating unpopular and useless adversary modes that are forgotten instantly as soon as the double payout ends after a patch release. They also add stunt races, which, subjectively, go into the same garbage bin, but people might object to this point, so maybe there is some activity there. The most significant content of all time was generally relatively "global." I'm talking about the introduction of offices, vehicle warehouses, bunkers, biker clubs and their warehouses. All of these were introduced in separate updates, yet not a single new heist was added, even though the groundwork was there. So, something like that. * Community - basically, an evolution of what came out of the "Audience" section. In the Russian-speaking environment, everything is cluttered with ads about what creative guys they are. They do "themed meetups" in open sessions, where they dress up as some military guys or lowrider fanatics and take screenshots for Steam and Snapmatic. Basically, this is the only thing that sets them apart from the game OUTSIDE of such communities. If you read the Discussion forums, you can also find out that Russian-speaking communities manage to sneak into each other's open sessions and ruin the party, staging cockfights, as mentioned in the PvP section. And then they whine to each other on the forums, accusing certain people of cheating, dishonesty, and other sins, for which Satan rubs his hands, dreaming of making yet another schoolboy his personal executioner in the domains of hell. Despite everything I listed, I continue to play. (Actually, I haven't for a long time) But so that my nerves don't kill me by the time I'm 35, I generally play only with my circle of acquaintances in voice chat. And as a rule, in empty or sparsely populated sessions. The game can still somehow bring some pleasure, but keep all these factors in mind. Do not play this without regular friends, otherwise, I strongly advise against buying it. UPD: Joined the group of people who also got banned, on top of everything else. Rockstar hasn't commented on the situation after all this time and doesn't give a shit about the audience. That pretty much sums up the state of the game and the company.

translation_en: Well, seeing as a lot of people don't have a clue, I decided to write this review based on the facts of what happened with Take Two - Rockstar: If you're wondering why there are so many negative reviews recently, I'll give you a brief summary: Rockstar, hand in hand with Take Two, declared "illegal" the tool that modders used to develop mods (better known as OpenIV). The community was obviously pissed off (myself included). What they did was bomb most of the company's games with negative reviews. That happened right on June 14, 2017. To this day (June 24, 2017), Rockstar re-enabled the OpenIV tool, which means mods are back, so everything is fine there. The problem is that a lot of people gave this game a negative review just because someone else did. If you go and read them, 90% of the reviews are nonsense or people repeating things like parrots. And what happens now? Well, those "parrots" aren't going to change their review, no no no. On the contrary, the game went from having 86% positive reviews (Very Positive) down to 64% (Mixed). And it looks like it's going to stay that way because, like I said before, they're parrots who repeat what others do without having enough arguments of their own. I currently have 533 hours in this game, and I have to say it's one of the best games ever made to date (I'm speaking with reason, not like your typical "fanboy"). A story mode that pulls you in and hooks you into the plot, and makes you feel like it never ends. As for the multiplayer, I think it's obvious you're never going to get tired of it because of the massive amount of activities to do, and content they add for FREE (something almost no company does nowadays, and it's appreciated). Also, like any game, it'll have its problems from time to time: server crashes, your usual run-of-the-mill hackers, or some funny guy coming in a tank to annoy you for a bit. But you get used to it. I didn't think it was right that they took away mod creation, since that's what makes us PC gamers stand out. But that's not why I came to join the long list of people who gave this game a negative review. Why? Simple. The game isn't to blame for having its tool taken away, the company is. The right thing to do would have been to spam their inbox. But hey, who am I to make those decisions? In conclusion, if you feel like buying this game, DO IT. It'll be totally worth it and you'll get hours and hours of fun. And as for those who already play it, I ask you this: Do you really think this game deserves those reviews? Speak with reason, not just to go along with whatever everyone else is doing. I know a lot of people will think this comment is useless, but I'm writing it because many people who want to buy the game have no idea what was going on. And it's not fair that because of something that happened and got fixed (for now), people who want to try new games are robbed of that opportunity. P.S. Mods will remain allowed as long as they don't affect the online mode or use content from other companies and pass it off as your own. Greetings to everyone, and if you made it this far, I hope you have a great day and thanks for putting up with this whole essay.

New business? 3-4 million. New transport? 3-4 million. And of course, the repetitiveness of the missions as has been said more than once. Drive there, kill that guy, pick up this shit, bring it back. Conclusion: As a player who previously considered GTA to be the gold standard of all games, I am in a state of absolute fury, depression, and disappointment. Waiting so long for an update, and getting such a, to put it mildly, "pile of shit," with unreal price tags for everything, cheaters (who are wiping out entire servers in godmode using the new vehicles), and the exact same repetitive missions and business system. I have zero desire to play anymore. Thanks, Rockstar, for ruining my favorite GTA.

translation_en: There was a time when game developers cared about quality, delivered finished games (without pieces missing) and listened to player feedback, besides encouraging community content creation. Remember that time? Yeah... It's been a while. Everything was so great, until some guys in ties saw in this thing called "multiplayer" a way to cash in on "luckier" players willing to blow their hard-earned money on "exclusive and extremely rare items" or simple game "shortcuts" (after all, why actually play, right? ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ ). "But why limit ourselves to multiplayer? We spend millions on explosive campaigns, insane quality, cinematic stuff! No, no, we gotta rethink this shit, are we gonna hand over a masterpiece for just 100 bucks? We're sleeping on the job." And then came DLC endings, pre-order exclusive content, platform-exclusive content (damn), paying to play beta, paying to play alpha, paying to play something that doesn't even look like a game (early access), and all the rest that anyone who has ever bought an Activision or Ubisoft game already knows all too well. And remember player feedback, free community content, and the game that actually felt like yours? Well, my friend, times have changed, and so has Rockstar. For a company that once openly supported (and benefited just as much from) MODs and player-created content, banning modifications is a step backward and an INSULT to those who supported it WILLINGLY all these years. Rockstar has been S.H.I.T.T.I.N.G on PCs, and not just since yesterday. You know why GTA V came out on PC? I'll tell you why: GTA Online and its Shark Cards. After all, which platform has the highest concentration of players willing to buy the same game multiple times just to "mess around" (also known as hacking) with other players (hi CS:GO). If many players were taking advantage of modifications and anti-cheat flaws to hack, the right thing to do would be to find solutions that don't screw over those who play clean (who paid for the game like everyone else) and weren't hurting anyone with their work. Rockstar should, first of all, remember who made their games so popular, especially back in the GTA San Andreas days, where the vast majority of players used MODs, which contributed even more to its spread and sales. It makes me sad to see a company of such high quality following the same path as some others in the industry. Today, what dictates the work of these companies (Valve included) are microtransactions and the naivety of many players who don't understand the evil they are supporting. I really hope Rockstar reconsiders this attitude. The game belongs to them, and they make the rules, but remember that a game is made of players and a company has a reputation to maintain. I'm not gonna tell you whether or not you should buy GTA V, after all, the money is yours and you do whatever the fuck you want with it. But if you read this far, I just ask that you be aware of what is happening to the industry and see if this game really deserves your money.

translation_en: Review strictly for Online. The whole game is built around Shark Card microtransactions. According to the devs, players are supposed to donate—donate a whole lot. Why are we supposed to donate? That's right, prices for everything here are hiked up to the skies, while earning money is reduced to a minimum and dreary grinding. You can try making money with businesses, but first you have to buy them for a crap ton of money, then upgrade them for another two crap tons of money, because without upgrades businesses are useless. And, once again, if those fun-loving players blow up your crates during the sale—instead of money, you'll just get wrecked nerves. You can buy a vehicle warehouse and import/export cars, but the aimbot bots will instantly turn them into Swiss cheese, severely cutting into your income. Basically, the whole in-game economy is designed so that you earn as little as possible while everything in the game costs as much as possible, which is supposed to push us toward paying real money. The developers' greed is one of the main problems with Online.

translation_en: [h1] Why do we love Rockstar? [/h1] [b] Yep, exactly for the quality. [/b] Backstory. I remember back in 2013, rocking a PS3, eagerly waiting to buy this masterpiece. And then, a miracle happened: two months after its official release, GTA 5 finally arrived in our remote little town. After that, my console forgot what sleep and rest even were. Not only did I beat the story mode 3 times, but I also grinded my online character up to around level 110. It was insanely interesting and absorbing. But time goes on, and everything eventually gets boring, even a game as cool as this one. And one day, I saw a 50% discount in the Steam store and couldn't resist. I transferred my character from PS3 to PC, and here we go again. Beat the story mode once more, though this time just skimming through it, and started "partying hard" in online. But the joy quickly turned to boredom, because it was the exact same game in front of me, just with better graphics and slightly more features... So: + Story mode 10/10, I'd even say 12/10. The writers are absolute legends. + Gorgeous visuals. I've never seen a more beautiful sunset or sunrise in any other game than this one. + Incredible attention to detail. In the best traditions of Rockstar. + Huge and diverse map. Smaller than in San Andreas, but way more interesting. + Online, which all fans of the series had been waiting for so long. An entire city with loads of players hanging out in it at the same time. A generation of people who grew up on GTA 3, Vice City, and San Andreas could only dream of this. Not to mention the fans of the very first parts of the series. - No Russian voice acting. There's so much interesting dialogue during driving missions that sometimes you just stop to read the characters' lines to the end. And then, once they're done, you keep driving. - Online mostly expands in terms of new missions, cars, weapons, etc. That gets boring pretty fast. Playing it for a really long time will only be fun with friends. - Not very strict punishment for crimes in online. You basically get away with "accidental" murder. As a result, the whole map turns into a warzone between local factions, or a sandbox for some "crazy" player in a tank. In my opinion, that's messed up. - Unjustified online bans when you don't have fast internet. On this point, I can only note that my fiber-optic internet speed is around 6-7 MB/s, and I haven't been banned yet. Most of the time this happens when using a USB modem. P.S.: Having read a lot of negative reviews for the game, I can say that most of them are about unfair bans for using cheats. The lack of support feedback from players, who completely ignore honest players' requests to restore their accounts, is super frustrating. As a result, the player is left with either buying a new GTA or giving a massive crap and moving on. Either way, Rockstar keeps rolling in cash for their product, while the consumer gets hung out to dry. That is a really shitty way to treat your customers, guys... To sum it up, I can say that this game is very good, but it has run its course. Only worth buying for the story. 9.5/10

The events of the fourth and fifth GTAs, as is known, take place in a new reality where there was no Claude, no Tommy Vercetti, and no Carl Johnson. It turned out much like J.J. Abrams' Star Trek reboot or comic book series reboots: the names are the same, the places are the same, but everything else is different. Therefore, returning to Los Santos is somewhat soul-crushing. Remade for the new generation, the city has kept some external features, but overall has become completely unfamiliar. For example, of the old Grove Street, where Carl Johnson and his gang lived according to the story of San Andreas, only a musty courtyard remains, and its former inhabitants act as if they never even existed. Now the purple Ballas live here, and if you manage to show up here on foot, the guys from the whole neighborhood will rob you. An entire era of San Andreas history was simply erased, and the state itself was rebuilt from scratch. Out of three cities, only Los Santos remains, but it has transformed and expanded so much that it finally looks like a real city. INTERESTING FACT: References to GTA IV are met at every turn: sometimes fleeting mentions ("There was this guy from Eastern Europe in Liberty City, but he kept his head down..."), and sometimes even characters. And the fact that they forgot about the events of San Andreas might actually be the right call. After the madhouse that CJ's story ended with, Los Santos should have been left in absolute ruins. The entire territory (the city itself is the size of the new Liberty City from GTA IV plus the surrounding countryside with twice that area) is, for once, open right from the start: no excuses like "bridges are closed due to a terrorist threat." And everywhere, absolutely everywhere, you can stumble upon something interesting. First of all, this is what distinguishes GTA V from its genre peers — the sandbox here is so vibrant, well-thought-out, and unpredictable that you can get into a scrape at any minute. Bandits steal purses, motorcycles, and cars (and you can help the owner get the stolen property back), cops are in firefights with street gangs and rednecks (participating is not forbidden), forest deer run out onto the road (a good deer is a hit deer), accidents happen at construction sites, people curse, fight... Every single second, something is happening somewhere. These aren't just backdrops (since you can intervene in any random event), nor are they "Potemkin villages" built specifically for you — Los Santos manages just fine on its own. GTA is no longer just territory you have to drive through from point to point according to the plot, occasionally breaking for mass murder when you get bored. Rockstar, having passed through the thorny path of evolution, has achieved an almost ideal game space, creating a real ecosystem almost without rules and conventions. And also very beautiful and cozy. It has never been so pleasant to just drive down the highway in GTA. Some Gerry Rafferty plays from the stereo, cars rush past in a continuous stream, trees and some shacks, the sunset peeks out from behind the mountains, the car bounces on road bumps, and you can even feel the wind resistance — not a game, but a happiness generator. The last time it was like this was in last year's sunny Forza Horizon, but that's still a narrowly specialized racing game. So, you could say GTA V has no competition in generating happiness. When it became known that GTA V would have three main characters instead of one, many had doubts — back then Rockstar barely managed even with one. But the doubts vanished — this is the best thing they could have come up with to diversify the gameplay. Essentially, it turned out to be three different GTAs that not only coexist but complement each other. Franklin is a typical righteous "nigga" with a clear value system and a hyperbolized sense of gang loyalty. He is young, inexperienced, but surprisingly sensible, steals cars to order, and dreams of scoring a serious gig. He doesn't like taking unnecessary risks, but for friends he's ready to do anything. Michael is a hardened robber who retired and lost himself at the bottom of a bottle. Unlike previous protagonists, he has long since settled into adult life: a mansion in Vinewood, a garage full of cars, an unhappy wife, a daughter hanging out with porn moguls and lustful showmen, and a post-pubescent son who does nothing but smoke weed, troll trolls, and play the local equivalent of Call of Duty. And Trevor... Trevor is simply a psycho (he even has a doctor's note for it). He lives in a dirty trailer, cooks methamphetamine, yells obscenities for any reason and none, exterminates bikers, and at the first opportunity — punches people in the face (and women, women too!). Completely out of control, insolent, quarrelsome, and socially dangerous. Just like in previous parts, the main storyline in GTA V is tangled and disjointed — but this is no longer perceived as a flaw, but rather as a hallmark of the series. But the routine has decreased by an order of magnitude — mainly due to the fact that you can switch between characters. When, say, Michael has to lay low, we switch to Trevor, whose agenda features another massacre or crazy stunt. Mandatory races or the infamous flight school from San Andreas don't even come to mind — everything that used to seem like tedious "filler" remains in GTA V at best as optional extracurriculars. Even the intrusive dates from GTA IV stopped being intrusive. No more "Nico, let's go bowling!" with hurt feelings if you refuse. Want to invite companions for a walk — go ahead. As a bonus, you'll get an adorable episode with, say, a hammered Michael and Franklin. But no one will demand anything from you. Few games treat additional content the way GTA V does. Rockstar, fully aware that many players won't notice even half of the side activities, secrets, and charming details, has built a true paradise for explorers. You are reminded that there are scuba gear in the game during a single story mission, and you can easily miss that moment. But if you don't miss it, you'll discover an entire underwater world with its own secrets, valuable loot, and biting sharks. Flying in a helicopter on another errand, it's hard not to notice another interesting spot and make a mental note to "drop by in my free time." It's even harder to resist not dropping by during work hours: there's so much around that it's almost impossible to focus on just one thing. At home on the TV, they show programs and cartoons (we'll talk separately about the satire, of which there is really a lot in GTA V, because the local jokes are simply impossible to retell), and there are dozens of interesting pages on the local internet. Besides, you can mess around with yoga in the yard, and if you don't like it — run off to, say, the nearest tennis court. Mini-games like yoga have almost no practical value: they improve character stats, but this has a minimal impact on the game's progress. But the main thing is that such activities exist, and they are entertaining. So let them be. To make life in Los Santos feel even more real, Rockstar tries to instill a sense of private property in players, and in places it even works. Each character has a personal car: Trevor has a redneck, eternally filthy pickup truck, Franklin has a "gangsta" sedan resembling a Dodge Charger SRT8 and a stolen green motorcycle, and Michael has something like a prestigious Audi A6. Only these cars are worth upgrading: they won't go anywhere and will always be with you. Tuning the engine, transmission, and other things is expensive, and a random car can easily disappear if you don't put it in the garage (and sometimes even from there) — money down the drain. You can also invest money in real estate, like in Vice City, or play the stock market.

translation_en: The game is honestly close to perfection. Writing this review a year later, maybe if I hadn't randomly thought of it today I never would've again. I got into console gaming in the first place because of Assassin's Creed. Back then I didn't know much and bought an Xbox 360 just because I wanted to play GTA. Later on, finding out that next-gen consoles had better graphics, I bought a PlayStation 4, but due to various reasons I ended up getting into a bunch of other exclusives and didn't touch GTA for about half a year. But I knew I'd definitely play it eventually (tried to buy the physical disc multiple times in between). Until late 2015 when I built a PC, and I realized a game with graphics this insane is meant to be played on a computer. When I was still using Intel HD 530 integrated graphics, I finally bought it during a sale! Couldn't wait to grab a used reference GTX 780 Ti, maxed out all settings at 1080P, and finally felt pretty damn good. (Played a whole summer with that card, and even though I later upgraded to a 1070 and played in 4K, nothing could touch those happy times.) At first, I played with an old classmate for a bit, grinded through the beginning, and played with randoms for a while. I just remember one time taking on the Prison Break heist with two randoms. It was my first time doing it, no experience, and it took forever to barely finish the mission. The guys on the other end hopped on mic to "criticize," super embarrassing. Gradually I started proselytizing, getting a few classmates to jump into GTA with my hype, and even the ones I didn't convert bought in on their own—after all, the game's quality speaks for itself. Of course!! Isn't that how online gaming experiences are built in the first place? Back then, public lobbies were a total mess, so the importance of private invite-only sessions goes without saying. We'd hop on QQ voice chat (a group chat with twenty-something college classmates), fire up heists with a squad of four. The regret was constantly dealing with getting disconnected or infinite loading screens!! Sometimes half a day would just get wasted like that, totally killing the vibe, but we still managed to play a decent amount. I figure, if it weren't for the SARFT, if it weren't for systemic issues, if our country could just sort out the server problems, who knows how much better it would be than it is now? Los Santos, this city—no, this whole world, the life everyone yearns for. If only... but there are no "ifs," you just gotta use your limited time to experience and feel it. What, you want to quit the game? No way, not a chance in hell I'm ever quitting, I fucking love it in here, everyone's got great banter and the music slaps, they're all absolute legends. Aside from literally anything you could ever think of in the game, I think what touches me the most are the details and the views (every time I grind the "Titan of a Job" mission, I get to immerse myself in the bustling downtown nightscape), (saving up enough cash to buy a supercar and drive up the mountains and along the coast just taking in the scenery), listening to the saxophone playing on my personal radio station. Seriously, it's so chill. Though it probably loses a lot of impact on a laptop; gonna set up a triple-monitor display later (tried dual monitors already, it was insanely good). Actually, a 21:9 ultrawide monitor works in a pinch. Hardware is pretty much a necessity for this game, even though optimization is decent. Let's talk about the previous ban wave panic. I think people just need to pay attention to what background software they have running and keep it clean, and they'll be fine. As for VPN acceleration, teaming up with a buddy to buy a shadowsocks setup and using it properly with Proxifier makes you happy as a clam. China Mobile broadband is decent, but sadly this game just won't let you connect raw, China Telecom works much better though, other than that no major issues. The only problem is that sometimes after a system update (or maybe it's not even system updates), GTA starts stuttering or hitching every few seconds (completely not a hardware issue, it was still doing this after I upgraded to a GTX 1070 + Core i7 7700K, VRAM wasn't maxed, using an SSD, and a freshly reinstalled system had zero problems). Wonder if anyone has figured out the root cause? A few of my classmates ran into the exact same issue. Planning to snag another 1070 in the second half of 2017 to run SLI, crank settings to ultra, and rock a smooth 60 FPS. Played Battlefield 1 for the last few months, but occasionally I'll head back to Los Santos to enjoy life. Truly enjoy it, I won't even do anything, just watch the seconds tick by second by second... Hope there's a chance to properly play something like this again in the future. Edited again.

translation_en: Sorry, if you don't take the game environment seriously anymore, you'll lose even more veteran players. I've reported software exploit abuse multiple times with no response, and the other person hasn't even been banned. Looking at the anti-cheat efforts of other online games in recent years, they apparently only do a massive banwave right before a sale. To ask a question with no answer: isn't customer support supposed to exist to solve consumers' problems? Even when I sent complete videos, screenshots, and all the evidence, customer support's reply was just simply that the most effective method is in-game reporting—probably just to reduce the workload for email support? Big company game developers won't read every single review word for word like some indie developers do, whether positive or negative, which is understandable. Every single generation of Grand Theft Auto has been mind-blowing and set the trend for open-world games, and this generation is no exception. As a game that squeezed every drop of performance out of the PS3 and Xbox 360 eras, its incredibly rich gameplay got many players hooked. Back then, when the PC version unlocked, I skipped class to play it and was so hyped—I'd never played such an amazing game. Time flies. The Online mode, as one of the highlights of this generation, has always been loved by players for its rich replayability. Of course, the premise of loving it is being able to actually play it normally. At the start, there weren't that many cheaters using third-party programs; at least for the first year, I didn't run into any. Early on, Rockstar's attitude toward cheaters was just like NetEase's early days publishing Overwatch. I've been so pissed off by cheaters lately that I just uninstalled the game and quit for good. It's not that the game isn't fun; it's because of the dev team's attitude and the state of the game environment. At least I've never seen anything as spectacular as a 20-shot rapid-fire RPG barrage taking down a helicopter—especially when I was just trying to do a simple cargo delivery.

translation_en: The Party secretary slapped the desk and asked, "Who told him to come?" The student who was speaking was struck dumb. The counselor and head teacher sat in the corner, not daring to make a sound. At that moment, the class monitor spoke up. "The school rules state that changing dorms requires going through..." "You wanna leave?" the secretary asked again. The class monitor's body shook, and he stopped talking too. After a long while, the class monitor finally dared to speak again. "Why should I want to leave?" "If you feel the school's environment isn't suitable for you, you can withdraw voluntarily." "I didn't say I wanted to withdraw." "I said, you're withdrawing voluntarily." "......Then I can't do this class monitor job anymore." "Can't do it? Fine, find someone to replace you. But if no one replaces you, you keep doing it." "Then I can't do anything about this dorm issue." "Whoever doesn't want to switch, report your name to me. Those who find new roommates first get to decide their dorm." "Then we class committee members can't function." "Class committee members change last, gotta lead by example, right?" This dorm-switching mobilization meeting ended with four class monitors voluntarily resigning and a bunch of dorm heads sitting in silence. "I want to murder and burn things down." When there was no one else around, I said this to myself. There are always times in a person's life when you want to vent without any restraints, but you can't. You can't do a damn thing; if you rebel, you get wiped out, sometimes even "voluntarily wiped out." So I opened up GTA V, thinking that here I could vent freely. I could punch that secretary right in his disgusting dog head, grab him by the collar, and let him know his power and authority meant absolute shit compared to my fists. But I was wrong. In GTA V, I was still powerless. Michael's son stole his yacht trying to make a deal with gangsters, and as a result, the gangsters kidnapped him. Michael drove there, barely managing to save his son, only to be met with unreasonable blame and complaining. He caught his wife cheating with the tennis coach at home. He angrily chased the guy to his house and ruined his outdoor balcony. But the result? He pissed off a mob boss. He got beaten to the ground with a baseball bat at his own front door, got up in a pathetic state to apologize, and even promised to pay him a sum of money. How powerless, how utterly stifling. A once-legendary, fearsome master thief now had to submit to this fucking world just like me. Yet, when you drive the car following Lester's instructions and rob that jewelry store, everything changed. "You forget a thousand things every day, pal. Make sure you can't forget this one." When Michael said those words, time seemed to trace back to the very beginning. Michael's most successful heist to date: he had betrayed his crew, reached a compromise with the FIB, and got a huge pile of cash and a stable life. At the jewelry store, when he said those words once again, his life took another turn. Not far away, Trevor learned the news that Michael was still alive. On a rainy night, he wiped out a gang in his territory that he already had bad blood with, and then drove all night to Los Santos to find Michael—who was going through a midlife crisis, had gotten severely fat, and was fantasizing about retiring early from the stage of life. "Michael, let's go commit murder and arson." Fuck it all—the FIB, the IAA, fuck this world. Let's rage, let's go back to those days. Trevor, wearing women's clothing, tried to flip the middle finger to all power and authority. But once again, power won. Trevor was forced to return the nuclear weapon, Michael still had to do dirty work for the FIB according to their wishes, and even the naive Franklin was bossed around like a little bitch by the capitalists. Ah, even in a game like this, we still have to compromise with things. No, no, I admit it—we have to compromise, we have no choice but to compromise. But they will definitely pay the price for our forced compromises. Yeah, we've compromised for half a lifetime; today we're pulling off a big one. "The Federal Reserve System, commonly known as the Federal Reserve, is responsible for fulfilling the responsibilities of the central bank of the United States..." Fucking awesome, let's hit it, let's hit the Federal Reserve!! After making the plan, it was still a copy-paste of classic Hollywood movie tropes. Get the planes going, get the muscle cars going, prep the ammo, raise your guns. Oh ho! *The Italian Job*, *Speed*. We succeeded. Even though the world beat us down, we still bit a massive chunk right out of its flesh. It was worth it. At the end of the game, Rockstar ultimately gave players a chance to dream—Option C. That satisfying plot of revenge and loyalty, just like an old Hong Kong movie. In the end, the three of them declared their official retirement in the setting sun. I let out a long sigh of relief. Their problems were finally solved, the people who humiliated and threatened them died by their guns, and they had enough US dollars to last a lifetime. And me? ...I still have to move dorms.

translation_en: This review will focus exclusively on GTA Online (GTAO), as that is the cornerstone of all complaints about the game. After all, all the [u]"BANNED FOR NO REASON"[/u] guys have already beaten the single-player on torrents, and grabbed it on sale with a [u]"why the hell not buy it"[/u] attitude. So, since Steam is having a sale on this product again, it means the game is about to be hit with another wave of negative reviews like: "banned for no reason." I've read quite a few reviews about the game, and here are the conclusions I've come to regarding the timeframes of experiencing GTAO: [h1]NUMBER ONE[/h1] - from 0 to 30 hours of gameplay. The player is happy with the game, having fun with friends or solo, liking everything. [h1]NUMBER TWO[/h1] - from 30 to 230 hours of gameplay. The player is pissed off – they've realized: "To afford a house, an office, and cool cars, I'm gonna have to grind my ass off in online." And at this point, the options are either to grind or.... continued below. [h1]NUMBER THREE[/h1] - from 230 to INFINITY hours of gameplay. The player has probably saved up for everything they wanted and seen the game from all angles, playing exclusively with friends and in some casual modes. Now, about the specific types of banned players falling into these timeframes. [h1]NUMBER ONE:[/h1] - [b]80%[/b] are some kid who thinks he's smarter than everyone else and especially smarter than Rockstar Games and their crappy anti-cheat, which is definitely not gonna catch *him*. - [b]19.99%[/b] are guys who bought a second account and think that *this time* they definitely won't get caught because they messed up while cheating before, but this time things will be different. - [b]0.01%[/b] okay, you got banned by accident, but you won't have to be upset for long—with [u]THAT[/u] kind of luck, an icicle is gonna fall on your head this spring, so don't worry :) [h1]NUMBER TWO:[/h1] - [b]99.99%[/b] are people who realized that grinding the game takes a hell of a lot of time and they just don't have that much of it, so cheating is their choice. translation_en: Seeing everyone complaining about false bans, I want to give some advice to anyone planning to get the game. Register your Social Club account on the official website, registering in-game pretty much never works. When registering the account, do *not* select regions like China; pick the US, and even if you mod/cheat they barely check. When going online, it's best not to enter public lobbies, going passive mode is a great idea. You can't make huge purchases all at once, 200k is the absolute limit. If you want to make big purchases, go to a invite-only or trusted friends-only lobby. When doing missions, don't try to glitch stuff; like with the Pacific Standard this time, a lot of people glitched the Kuruma and ended up getting banned. Also, things like VPNs and game boosters, avoid using them if you can, otherwise your IP address changes too frequently and Rockstar will ban you. Make sure you completely delete single-player mods when playing online, some people got banned because of that. Don't be scared if you run into a cheater in a public lobby, but *do not* report them—those guys are arrogant for a reason, if you report them you'll get banned instead. Also don't pull your ethernet cable or disconnect your VPN, just switch lobbies, as long as it doesn't save, nothing happens. If you can do all this, you shouldn't catch a false ban, unless you pissed off a cheater. If you actually do get falsely banned, look up online how to unlink your GTA V Steam account from your Social Club account. Once you unlink it, make a new account and have fun.

translation_en: Today is March 14, 2020, White Day. Today I got an email from Rockstar saying my account has been unbanned and my privileges restored!!! I tried logging in, and yep, it's still my original account!!! In other words, my wrongful conviction from 3 years ago has been overturned, I guess that's a good thing. But it took them 3 years to clear my name, so I really don't feel like changing my negative review to a positive one for Rockstar. At the same time, this is also proof for all those sarcastic smartasses down in the comments. I am so fucking hyped right now, duck yeah ================================================================= This negative review goes out to GTA Online and Rockstar Support. Back in 2013, I played the single-player mode of this game for the first time on my cousin's PS3. I was still in school back then. Spent two whole weeks of summer break at his place playing GTA. The game genuinely blew me away, I had an absolute blast, and I kept saying I gotta buy my own PS3 to play at home (but how's a broke student supposed to afford that). In 2015, I heard GTAV came to Steam. I dusted off my ancient Steam account covered in thick layers of dust and bought the game on day one for 60 bucks. Even though the China region later got a super generous price drop to 30 bucks, I still have that 60-dollar purchase record, and I'm damn proud of it (felt like I caught some underpaid intern's pricing mistake, though looking back it feels so fucking stupid). When linking my Social Club, I found out my regular email was apparently already used to register an account. Checked the creation date—October 2008—and the only thing in it was Max Payne 3. The single-player mode kept me company for over 100 hours. Whenever my graduation thesis gave me a headache, I'd open GTAV to relieve the stress. Everyone in my dorm was super envious that my ancient-ass PC could actually run this game. All the physics collision effects and shit still hold up amazingly well today. Gradually, I started venturing into Online. Even though I'd already heard people saying Online was a total shitshow with all kinds of hackers and tryhards screaming at each other, I still decided to keep my nose clean and carve out my own path. At first, everything was great. Me and a few buddies spent every day grinding various jobs and heists. I remember it took us two nights just to beat the Prison Break heist. I really enjoyed the grind, and I really enjoyed that sense of achievement. Slowly, my friends drifted away from the game because of real-life stuff, and eventually we could never scrape together 4 people to play anymore. That's when I started playing as a lone wolf. That was right when modders were running rampant. I'd just casually drive around in passive mode in public lobbies, chilling and watching the tryhards blow each other up—it had its own unique charm. Suddenly, some guy with a minigun started shooting at me. But instead of bullets, the guy was shooting out money bags. I was so happy, thinking making money in Online was actually this easy. After a short while, I made a few million, and happily quit the game. That night I had a dream where I bought a bunch of stuff: an apartment I couldn't afford, a car I couldn't afford, guns and clothes I couldn't afford, and I became a badass boss! Then I woke up, checked my email, and got banned from Online for a month.... AFK... In 2017, a coworker bought GTAV, and I said "Hey, I have it too, let's play together!" So I downloaded it again. My coworker was looking up guides and using all sorts of glitches (got flamed for this in the comments below, looking utterly clueless. I looked it up online and saw there were a lot of malicious money glitches. I feel like I need to make a distinction here—what we did, to put it nicely, were just little tricks, totally different from those malicious glitches, how could that get you banned? For example, in certain missions when you get on a motorbike, enemies won't shoot from inside their cars). We leveled up fast. Right at that time, abusing the solo public session trick for CEO work became a thing, and slowly, I could afford a garage and started getting into car importing/exporting. Watching my hard-earned character grow stronger day by day, I decided to go back into a public lobby to check out the hustle and bustle of the world today. Just doing my daily drive... amazed by how many new cars they'd updated, and public lobbies now had random events pop up from time to time. Aside from joining that stunt race thing just to grab a first place, I didn't participate in any murder or PvP since I was in passive mode. Right before logging off, I exported a car, marveling at how cheating players were gone and the environment had gotten so much better, and that you could actually enjoy this game properly now. The next day, I got an email: Permanent ban... Appeals not accepted... My friend, do you know what despair tastes like? My friend, do you know what it feels like to have your hard-earned sweat and tears instantly wiped out? Played Online for about 50 hours in total, spent the whole time just getting griefed and killed... A peaceful player with a 0.03 K/D. Put me in a truck and I'd be your dedicated driver for a fucking year, yet they banned me just like that... I feel so bad for my Social Club account created in 2008, nearly 10 years old. I feel so bad for the 50 hours of effort put into my Online character. I feel so bad that my account won't even be able to use community features when GTAVI comes out in the future. I feel so bad that I used to say those wrongful bans only happened to cheaters, only to get my own karma bite me in the ass. I feel so bad that when I sent an essay to customer support, all I got back was a bot reply saying "Appeals are not allowed." At this very moment, I'm giving a negative review to the otherwise 10/10 GTAV. The devs helped me finally quit for good, how could I not thank them? P.S.: Through email exchanges with support, I learned that for future GTA titles—like GTAVI or GTVII—I will be permanently blocked from using Online and cloud services, though other games won't be affected. I really gotta thank Rockstar for this stellar customer service. Quitting GTA for good starting today, isn't that just wonderful? Part 2: This negative review goes out to Rockstar's red-headed stepchild, the retail version. Aside from the Steam version, I also own a Rockstar retail version. But after fucking around with it for ages, I still couldn't get it to run. Wonder if any Steam players have had a similar experience. First, the installation. The installer downloaded from Rockstar's official site takes forever and a day to read files after installing—took about an hour and a half on my PC—and then a pop-up appears: "Failed, please retry." After retrying 3 or 4 times, I gave up, copied my Steam game files over, and tried again: Failed, please retry... Fucked around with it even more, downloaded a retail .exe from some foreign site, and finally it started downloading. So I left it downloading overnight and went to sleep. Woke up the next morning: downloaded a tiny bit, error, please retry. So then I had to stare at the download progress. The download took about 15 hours (since it wouldn't max out my speed), but because it kept stopping and forcing me to retry, it took me three whole nights... Alright, now for the main event: download finished, Social Club tells me I can start the game. Excited as hell, I click play. It asks me to log in and enter a CAPTCHA image. I select the images, and it hits me with: "Selected verification image is incorrect." I thought maybe I went blind, so I picked a new one, still incorrect... Retry... Retry... What the fuck, can't even log into my account? I turned on my VPN, and same shit. Time for bed! Tried again the next day. This time I didn't even need to type my username, logged straight in, sweet! Loading screen, Social Club pops up again—still with the fucking image CAPTCHA, followed by endless retries... I spent five whole nights just trying to get past the retail GTAV login screen, and the exact moment I finally loaded into the game's story mode, I... chose to leave Rockstar a negative review! Right after that, a chunk of the map had a broken ground texture, and walking onto it made me fall through the map infinitely. So I spent time redownloading the whole damn thing, still didn't fix it, guess I'll just delete and redownload again... Am I trying way too hard just to play a video game? With all this time wasted, why the fuck didn't I just go enjoy a nice life instead?

translation_en: Played on Steam for so long, and this is my first ever review. First blood goes to GTA 5. Here is some reminiscing, feel free to skip if you find it annoying. [spoiler]Back in 2014, despite my wife's skepticism and my wallet and stomach protesting, I scrimped and saved, went to a certain electronics market in Zhongguancun, and grabbed an Xbox 360. That's right, purely for GTA 5 which was already sweeping the globe at the time. I played a cracked version, strictly single-player, no online. When buddies came over to my place, all they could do was watch. It felt like being a kid again, haha! I blitzed through the main story in a little over a month, and experienced a good chunk of the side missions and random events. My addiction to it only grew stronger. Then came the revolutionary year of 2015. After stubbornly playing World of Warcraft for 8 solid years (from high school straight through 5 years of working life), I felt like I just couldn't keep going. When I saw the Steam pre-order for GTA 5, my buddies and I bought in on day one! Since it was the first Steam game I ever bought (I'm sure a huge number of Steamers started their journey with the GTA 5 era), it was a real pain in the ass. Not having a Mastercard or Visa, we could only pay via online banking for domestic Steam back then. Plus, none of us had any idea how to activate the game after buying it. I remember seeing a bunch of people posting on Baidu Tieba asking for help, and some idiots accidentally posted screenshots with their activation codes visible... Those are really memorable times. I was the first among our group to successfully buy, activate, and get into the game. Then I started getting the hang of it, buying houses and cars, and running heists. Back then, modders/cheaters weren't as common or as hardcore as they are now, and ban waves weren't this heavy either. If you jumped into a random lobby for a heist and had a cheater on your team, you were seriously lucky—you might clear all 5 major heists in a single night. And the most disgusting thing back then was the network connection, which is probably still true today.[/spoiler] I'm based in Beijing, and I've tried GTA 5 Online under all kinds of network environments. My conclusion so far is: in the Beijing area, absolutely none of the tier-2 internet service providers can connect to the game bareback (without a VPN). Some of these broadband providers even block VPNs. Names like Great Wall, Founder, Dr. Peng, and Guangda Tong are pretty well-known tier-2 ISPs. As for China Unicom, China Telecom, and China Mobile, those three tier-1 ISPs I know of can all connect to GTA 5 Online natively without issues. To play GTA 5 Online, I switched my home internet to Unicom starting in 2016, and up until now, I can play GTA 5 and other Steam games normally. Let's talk about some solid, practical advice. GTA 5 Online is not a very friendly gaming environment. When you're out and about, get good at using Passive Mode (press M, up arrow, Enter), and watch out for cheaters. If anything abnormal happens—like having toilets, chairs, or other models attached to your body, getting randomly teleported somewhere to kneel and dance, everyone in the lobby suddenly blowing up, giant UFOs or Ferris wheels appearing in the sky, or having loot bags, cars, clowns, your own character, or buff guys dropped on your head—all of that means someone in the lobby is running a cheat menu. When that happens, immediately press Alt+F4 to forcefully quit the game, relaunch it, load into Story Mode first, and then go from Story Mode into an Online lobby. Generally speaking, when a lonely new player enters the game and finishes the tutorial mission with Lamar, they'll only be around rank 2 or 3, and then the game just leaves you to your own devices. Everything is open, which can be a bit confusing for newbies, and you'll just get killed by random people. At that point, you can actually pull out your phone and join someone else's Jobs to play together. Of course, you can also host your own Jobs (press Esc -> Online -> Jobs -> Play Job -> Created by Rockstar). I recommend playing plenty of Race-type Jobs because you don't need weapons, there are no kills or deaths (except for Vehicular Deathmatches), and it won't tank your K/D ratio too much. Nowadays the game has Stunt Races and a ton of other Jobs open, with plenty of people playing, so it's super easy to queue into someone else's Job. After messing around, getting a feel for the game, and clumsily grinding your way to rank 15, Daily Objectives unlock. If you're playing completely solo with no homies and no e-girls to carry, you must insist on doing your Daily Objectives every single day. Daily Objectives reset at 2:00 PM Beijing time, split into three small tasks. Try your best to complete them. Doing so awards $25,000 in-game cash and 3,000 RP every day. Keep it up for a week for the weekly bonus: an extra lump sum of $100,000 and 15,000 RP. Stick with it for a month for the monthly bonus: an extra $500,000 and 50,000 RP. Whether you're trying to make money or level up, this is by far the safest, most reliable, and easiest method. Search for "GTA 5 Online Daily Objectives" on Baidu; there's a very detailed guide and explanation on Gamersky (Gamersky.com) that you can reference. Once you've built up a certain amount of progress, you can consider buying some really good vehicles (the Armored Kuruma for around 500k is an absolute must-buy; you can use it for daily objectives, killing people in free roam, or heists). Buy a high-end apartment—the main perk of a high-end apartment is that it lets you host Heists. Heists are a major highlight of GTA 5 Online. Aside from the first heist which is for two players, the other 4 heists all require 4 people to pull off together. However, if you're playing solo, I advise against randomly queuing with randoms. Not only might you fight over the cut, but everyone's skill level and game sense are different. You could end up spending the entire night failing a simple setup mission, making zero money, and leaving with a belly full of frustration. Honestly, just grinding out Jobs and doing small tasks by yourself is pretty decent too. Another thing is selling cars, which is also a pretty important source of income. Every 40 in-game minutes, you can sell one vehicle stolen off the street. Supercars or special vehicles can't be sold. Currently, the best method is to farm the Lampadati Felon GT over by Eclipse Towers; the yellow ones sell for $13,000, and the blue ones sell for $18,000. You can look up the exact method on Baidu. Most of the stuff above can be done in Solo Sessions or Invite-Only Sessions, where you can grind slowly by yourself with zero worries about other players messing with you. Once you've stacked up some cash, you can buy an office on the web browser to become a CEO, or buy a Motorcycle Club. Whether you want to do missions or sell cargo, your options open up even more. A special note here: when playing the CEO mode, whether you're sourcing or selling cargo, you *must* force yourself into an empty public lobby before starting. So much CEO beef and griefing happens purely because people blow up each other's cargo. The method to force a solo public lobby is very simple: once you enter a public lobby, open 360 Security Guard, find "Traffic Firewall," and throttle the network speed for the GTA 5 Online process. Set both upload and download limits to around 10KB. Go back into the game and wait a bit. If other players in the session are still moving normally, lower the speed limit further until everyone else drops out of the lobby and you're the only one left—that means you've successfully forced a solo public lobby. Also, if you set the speed limit too low (like 3KB or 4KB), it might drop your own connection, so just readjust it to a different number and try again. Once you're rich, you can buy some offensive vehicles, like the Insurgent Pick-up Custom, the P-996 LAZER fighter jet, or the Valkyrie attack helicopter. I recommend getting the LAZER, as it comes in handy for a lot of solo CEO work, whereas the Insurgent and Valkyrie both require teammates to operate their weapons. I'll leave it at that for now. I'll update when I have time in the future, or maybe I won't. Regardless, GTA 5 is a damn good game. -------------------Manual Divider---------------------------- Today is 2017-6-26. I haven't logged into GTA 5 for about a month now, and my daily, weekly, and monthly reward streaks are all broken. Playing completely by yourself is just too damn boring... Day in and day out of the same grind, and the rewards serve zero purpose. I bought nice cars and gorgeous houses—who am I even showing them to? Back in the day, the goofball friends I used to play with would even flex a humble bicycle. Now supercars are parked on every street corner, but my buddies are nowhere to be seen. I haven't logged on once since this latest update. Heard they dropped some gunrunner DLC—don't even need to think about it. Ever since the CEO era, it's just been endless grinding (gan, gan, gan), I'm way too tired. [spoiler]Time to quit for good. GTA 5 doesn't belong to me anymore.[/spoiler]

translation_en: Taking advantage of the current sale, I'm writing a review. First of all, this game is worth buying right now, and I'll list both the pros and cons. Pros: 1. By far the third-person sandbox game with the highest gameplay value. 2. Buy one game, get two: one single-player, one online. 3. It has freedom, scenery, and progression systems. 4. Beginner-friendly (this is debatable, but in my opinion, it is friendly to beginners). 5. The game comes with Traditional Chinese, it has Chinese, it has Chinese!! Cons: 1. Getting banned isn't based on whether you're cheating, but on whether your game data is abnormal (99% of negative reviews are from bans). 2. There are tons of modders/hackers in the game; often you switch lobbies several times in a row and they're all cheaters. 3. Many features in the game are not fully unlocked (this isn't really a con per se, just that a lot of stuff can only be played in designated modes or at certain times). 4. Direct connecting is up to luck; sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. Now let's focus on the [Cons]. Situations where you'll get banned: 1. Clicking memory boost/turbos (including Tencent Manager, 360, etc.), any software that optimizes memory. If you use this while playing online, it will cause data anomalies. Clicking it makes your game lag, forcing you to force-quit, which results in an instant ban (don't ask me how I know, it's all tears). 2. Doing the finale replay glitch. This exploits game mechanics to grind money. This is controversial; some people say it gets you banned, others say it doesn't. 3. Picking up money bags. This happens when a cheater drops money bags and you pick them up, leading to a ban. This is also controversial—some people say you can't bank it and must spend it immediately. Last time a cheater dropped money bags on me, since the game defaults to spending money from the bank, I didn't spend it. After an afternoon (or a day, I don't remember), Rockstar cleared it themselves. 4. Buying modded money. If you join GTA groups or check Taobao, there are all kinds of people selling modded money, like tens of millions for 10 RMB, or hundreds of millions for 20 RMB. These are real, you actually can use cheats to grind money, but it gets you banned. It's up to luck; some people get banned, others don't. If you're already planning to buy it, I can give you some advice: 1. Once you enter online mode, don't click any memory-clearing software, otherwise you'll get falsely banned. 2. Don't do the finale replay glitch. If you're doing heists with randoms and see someone's cut is 0, walk away immediately, otherwise you might get banned. 3. Don't bank money bags you pick up; spend them immediately or leave them for Rockstar to clear out themselves (this is controversial, I did the latter). 4. If a modder attaches a model to you (like having a box on your character, a bunch of torches, doing weird animations, having a muscular guy behind you, seeing a bunch of yourself fall from the sky, etc.), you have a few options: 1. Switch lobbies 2. Switch to single-player and back to online 3. Force-quit the game. 5. Don't play with cheaters; switch lobbies the moment you see one. 6. Other (1-5 are avoidable situations; doing 1-5 can very effectively prevent bans. 6 is up to luck—if your luck is bad, there's a chance you'll get falsely banned). Now, some advice for beginners [things in this game are not always better just because they're expensive]: Weapons: - Special Carbine (unlocked at level 1), Uzi (unlocked at level 1) - Armor-Piercing Pistol (unlocked at level 33) - Heavy Sniper (unlocked at level 90) - Marksman Rifle (unlocked at some level I forgot) - Homing Launcher/Stinger (unlocked at some level I forgot) - RPG (unlocked at level 100) - Minigun (unlocked at level 120) - For melee, just buy brass knuckles (the absolute god-tier melee weapon) - Assault Shotgun (unlocked at some level I forgot) It's best not to buy any other weapons; you'll find out why later. Cars: - Armored Kuruma, Insurgent. Supercars don't matter, just get whatever you like. Apartments: - The $205,000 one is pretty good; great location, everything is nearby, and there's a subway tunnel right outside the entrance where you can lose your wanted level. Or Eclipse Towers, Apt 31, seems to be around $330,000, nice view. Office: - The $3 million beachside office (first, great view; second, it's close to where you spawn your tank or Insurgent truck, which is useful for PvP later on, though doesn't matter early game) or the cheapest $1 million office. Aircraft: - The Buckingham Valkyrie—wait, no, the Buzzard attack chopper, also known as the "Little Bird." Once you buy an office, you can register as a CEO and summon the Little Bird directly, spawning right in front of you. Other aircraft spawn at helipads by default. No other aircraft are recommended at all; you can buy the Hydra later on. To wrap it up, this game has a ton of fun. I recommend joining a few GTA groups. Go street racing together, do heists together, do outfit glitching together (doesn't get you banned), go griefing/PvP together, and just cruise around enjoying the scenery. Adding one last thing: getting banned is a major issue with this game, but the gameplay and everything else are beyond reproach.

translation_en: The game itself is fucking awesome, the years of development the devs put into it really paid off. The story isn't anything super special, but I liked it, I managed to get immersed and was looking forward to seeing how it ends. And then I went to play online......At that exact moment, my whole enthusiasm for single-player went completely down the shitter. After about a 15-minute wait for everything to load, I was finally playing. The fact that everyone griefs you the second they see you and that you get kicked from every activity because you don't have the level you're currently trying to grind for, I could still kinda stomach. But the fact that you own the game for a month, go play online for the first time, and by the next day you have a one-month ban and you don't even know why, well I'd honestly shit all over Rockstar's backs for that. Then I found out those motherfuckers had a problem with the Czech translation I installed for the single-player. Fine, I wait a whole month horny as a dog to play, yesterday was the day, the last day of the ban. I'M GOING TO PLAAAAY................Alright, I'll ignore again the fact that Fuckstar deletes all the characters you previously had (meaning if you're an honest player and had a lot of progress saved up, you're fucked and can start all over again). I played for about 4 hours before some hacker shoved every single weapon into my inventory. As soon as I noticed—because you notice that pretty damn quick—I quit the session and started a new one. Everything was running fine, I thought cool, he didn't ruin it for me. But what happens? Today I want to play and what do I find out.....You ain't playing this game anymore, asshole.... Permanent ban. If you think like I do that since you're totally innocent, you paid 400 crowns for the game which you didn't find on the street, and because of someone else's cocksucking behavior you can't play anymore, that Rockstar Support will help you?? Not a fucking chance. Online support works in a way that no matter what you write to them, you get a reply in the form of a pre-written email from which you learn nothing more than from the RS website. So with this, I'd like to warn all future buyers—if you're planning on buying this game, I'd rather not. I know everyone needs to get their own experience, I didn't believe my friends either and look how I ended up :D My opinion is that the people at RS are greedy and want to make an even bigger business out of it, because otherwise I don't understand why they use a ban system that doesn't ban modders and cheaters, but bans everyone including innocent players. Secondly, why a PERMANENT ban? I bought this game, a normal purchase, so how is it possible that they practically take the game away from you, but don't refund your money? I think what RS is doing is not a legal business, and I'm surprised nobody has filed a class-action lawsuit yet. And thirdly, contributing to this suspicion of mine is the attitude of RS support that I wrote about, which refuses to deal with their customers about anything, neither by phone nor email—if you don't believe me, there are a few videos on YouTube of people calling them. So if you even read this far, think carefully about what you're buying, especially from Rockstar Games. I wouldn't take even a free poster from them anymore.

Is this really okay? Then a black screen with yellow text told me: WARNING ⚠️ Unable to load Online session. I read it again, is this seriously okay? * The very first time I got into a public lobby, someone modded a money bag onto me, and I still have the video. Back then, I thought it was Rockstar's starter pack... Is this really okay? * Done countless missions, mostly Heists of course. Some used cheats, others had barely been playing for two hours. Had to wait a few days before I even dared to play. Is this really fair to us normal players, huh? * The Cheater Era: In the latter half of 2015 and the first half of 2016, it was the wild west of cheaters, with all sorts of freaks running rampant. "Wars of the Gods" in lobbies were a common sight. Practically every public lobby had unkillable people raining cash—you're a cheater, I'm a cheater, society style—casting a shadow over the otherwise gorgeous GTA5. Our conversations turned into: 1. Cheaters driving chrome invincible cars with pink headlights, capable of endlessly firing countless rows of missiles—eight per row—unbeatable. When you see a cheater watching the map, hehehe. You know what's up. 6. Once, I was in a solo public lobby and stepped away to use the toilet. Came back to find someone had dropped 2 million on me. The next day, I got a little red warning letter saying I exploited vulnerabilities. Yet the Taiwanese guy was completely fine. 7. Must have been around November 2015. As a total noob, I was cruising around the side street near Maze Bank in a chrome tank I picked up off the street. Suddenly, a pig came charging at me, followed by no less than ten green-skinned aliens 👽. What the hell is going on (´⊙ω⊙`)! I raised my cannon and fired, boom, boom... Even worse, the pig flew up into the sky right along with me while I got launched... (The pig was actually just a player wearing a custom skin model) Cheaters back then were seriously out of control. * The False Ban Wave In mid-2016, they started an unprecedented crackdown on cheaters. But shouldn't we also reflect on ourselves—were we using cheats way too excessively? * The Cross-Strait Flaming Wars No one claims #1 just by running their mouth; in GTA, you settle it with bullets! While I don't advocate starting shit, we aren't afraid of it either! A month ago, I joined a lobby with seven Taiwanese players and myself. Someone asked: "Are you from the mainland?" "Yeah," I replied. "Where from?" "Jiangsu, what about you guys?" "We're from Beijing, you Jiangsu morons." "Right, we're from Beijing, you Jiangsu 87s." "Did I provoke you? Can you watch your fucking language?" "Just a joke, don't take it seriously." "That wasn't just a joke." What's an 87? I wondered. Sounded like Taiwanese slang. "All Chinese people are morons, Taiwan No.1!" "Long live the Japanese Emperor, Taiwan is an independent and sovereign country!" "China belongs to Taiwan!" "Is this fun?" I said. To that tiny fraction of extreme Taiwanese players in the GTA world, I want to say: mainlanders aren't incapable of beating you, we just can't be bothered arguing with you. Teammates basically don't need to coordinate; missions entirely rely on one carrying veteran. Newbies walking down the street with passive mode off will get spawn-killed in every possible way by other players. You say just turn on passive mode? Players who just bought the game probably start off wanting to go in and experience it slowly, enjoying the fun and the process—after all, human nature is good, right? Don't give me that bullshit about the chance of a false ban being tiny; I got falsely banned while sitting inside my own in-game apartment, and I'll explain the details below. After you get falsely banned: 1. Character reset. All the cash you earned as a newbie, the cars you spent time and thought customizing, the houses you saved up for by grinding missions seriously—all of that is gone. Let me just say that starting out in the Online mode, missions are pretty hard and making money is really slow, since the game has huge openness and isn't very friendly to newbies. You care a lot about how you budget your money. Well, everything you busted your ass doing missions to earn is now gone. 2. If you're lucky enough to get a 30-day ban (instead of a permanent one), would any player seriously keep playing a game after getting falsely banned by it? When you play this game again with a reset character, are you still going to bust your ass doing all kinds of missions, leveling up slowly, and making money slowly? I fucking won't. Using mods to grind cash is now the best and most correct choice. 3. Speaking of false bans, the weirdest thing is I got banned while inside my own house. So as a newbie, you never know when you're going to get falsely banned. Let me go over the details of the ban. Just six hours ago, I logged into the game. My character got up from bed, and I found two NPCs standing in the second-floor living room of my house. No matter what, I couldn't get rid of them, so I ran into them, trying to shove them out of my house. Still didn't work, so I gave up. After a bit, someone else's sports car suddenly appeared in my living room. I tried to drive it out of my house, still didn't work. Later I went to the garage and found a female NPC corpse inside. At the time I didn't give a shit, since it was just my own house in the game, and there were no huge money transactions or anything, so getting falsely banned was impossible. After logging off and getting some sleep, Rockstar emailed me saying I violated the service agreement, slapped me with a 30-day ban, and reset my character. Fine, 30 days. With so many great games coming out non-stop these days, I probably won't have any interest in GTA V 30 days from now. When the ban lifts, I'll spend three days slowly cheating in a few hundred million game bucks, buy all the top-tier cars and top-tier houses, and hack my level up to the hundreds. As long as you use mods low-key enough, you won't get banned, and even if you do get banned, who gives a fuck? It was all obtained through illegitimate means anyway, so what if it gets wiped? Just use illegitimate means to get it back. Would you care if you wrecked a supercar you carjacked from some NPC? Saying all this isn't an appeal to get unbanned, nor is it a complaint that GTA V isn't fun. I just want to say that your random banning bullshit, Rockstar, is going to bring in even more modder players. (Just waiting for the unban so I can mod.)
