translation_en: [h1] Feb 4, 2017 2nd edit, if you're thinking of buying this game, read my post [/h1] Jan 28 1st edit, Feb 4 2nd edit Let me break it down for you cleanly. I've been playing since patch 1.32 and had 3 GTA accounts. One got permanently banned for hacking, and the other two were false bans. This is one of those. 1.32 Modders started showing up here and there. Saw them during heists, saw them hanging out in sessions. They didn't cause massive damage most of the time, but you'd frequently see them going on random rampages. 1.33 There were so many hackers. Hacking was possible online, clean players were suffering, and it was a time when money was hard to come by. Back then, hackers were so powerful they were practically called "admins." This was the era when hacking blew up and went completely through the roof. 1.34 Rockstar finally started cracking down on hackers to some extent. They figured out most hacks modified scripts, so if a file had modified scripts, the system filtered it out automatically. If your version didn't match, you couldn't play with non-cheaters. Plus, bans for 15 days started happening—as fast as 2 hours, or within a week at the latest. 1.35 New hacks were developed. They came out as `.exe` client versions, meaning people didn't need to use scripts anymore. Online hacking was back. Most of the hacks we knew back then were script modifications (Jordan Menu, Infamous, Hempus, etc.). Supposedly these existed before too. 1.36 The ban policy for hacking changed. It went from a 1st offense 15-day / 2nd offense 30-day / 3rd offense 20-year-to-perm ban, to a 1st offense 30-day / 2nd offense permanent ban. Accounts got suspended within 2 hours to 2 days on average, and if hacking was confirmed, characters were wiped. 1.37 Present day. A massive ban wave hit in late December 2016. This is where the false bans people keep talking about in reviews started happening. Even Dr. Kim, a famous member of the Ulsan Big Whale crew, got falsely banned. [h1] Feb 4, 2017 Edit [/h1] The criteria for getting banned changed a bit. 1. Using hacks 2. Griefing/bad sport behavior 3. Sharing hacks 4. Being suspected of hacking 5. Making money too fast 6. Being a newbie These 6 are the main ones. #3 is a bit broad: if you received money or gained XP abnormally, a ban is basically guaranteed. Since this applies even if you're just in the same session, running into a modder means running away is the only option. #4 and #5 prove that this is a game where you should want to slap the developers across the face. For #4, if you level up too fast or get a lot of money in a short period, you are banned unconditionally. Well, maybe not unconditionally, but your chances of getting banned are sky-high. For #5, I'm writing this based on the fact that I got suspended *again*. I cleared Criminal Mastermind ($10M), Loyalty ($1M), and All in Order ($1M) for a total of $12M+ plus heists on the side, cleanly, in one go taking 6 hours. And the next day, I was permanently banned. #6 has been added. We don't know the exact reason, but what's certain is that false bans are mainly targeting newly started players. It's not an absolute ban, but word is that if you do jobs like heists with older players, you get banned. There are other reasons too, but this is the most common cause and it somewhat connects to #5. [h1] Customer Support Issues [/h1] The problems are patch 1.37, the ban criteria, and support. I already wrote about 1.37 and the ban criteria, so I'll skip further explanation. Support issues: When your account gets permanently banned or suspended, you naturally submit a ticket, but doing this is completely pointless. 1. Automated macro replies. 2. I have never once seen them lift a ban. When you send an inquiry, the closing phrase always says: "This is a final decision and will not be overturned." This essentially brands every user as an absolute cheater and locks them out. It's their silent way of saying: "We consider you a cheater, so we're not dealing with you." They haven't lifted bans in the past either. Back then, they only banned actual cheaters, so I won't bring up the old days. However, the situation right now is completely different, and for obvious reasons. Rockstar is stuck between a rock and a hard place: if they lift all the bans, they unban the cheaters too; if they don't, players keep quitting. Yet, cheaters are still active right now, and they're going to keep sticking around in *Grand Theft Auto V*. If those cheaters had their accounts permanently banned, they lost something too, so wouldn't it make more sense to just unban everyone? I have a history of using hacks in the past, and I have an account that got permanently banned after the 1.34 patch for hacking. But after that, I played completely clean, yet two of my accounts got banned at the same time. [h1] I Do Not Recommend This Game [/h1] If you want to buy this game, read my post. This is what I wrote before my initial review. If you played *San Andreas* out of the GTA series, drop those expectations and go find another game. If you want to shoot guns, there's the first-person FPS CS:GO; if you want a third-person game, there's The Division. If you're looking for high freedom, there's *Garry's Mod* which is way cheaper. The entry barrier for this game is absurdly high compared to other games. Helicopter handling that's a pain unless you have hundreds of hours, differences in max health depending on your level, shooting stats, strength stats—you'll realize just how pathetic you are. If you're thinking, "Isn't this one of Rockstar's legendary masterpieces as always?", get that thought out of your head. I'm being dead serious. Don't waste your time on this piece of shit game. When patch 1.38 drops, it's going to be managed even more like dogshit. If Rockstar keeps running things this way, I'm never touching another Rockstar game again. The 1.33~1.35 patch era, when this was worshipped as a masterpiece, is gone. People say *The Division* bombed at launch and then climbed back up, but this game went from a masterpiece to having its credibility drill straight through the earth's crust because of botched anti-cheat. [h1] If you don't understand what this all means, read this [/h1] I am not going to recommend buying this game. I don't want to create any more victims. This isn't the GTA series of the past. With a steep entry barrier, rampant cheaters, constant microtransaction pushes, an extreme gap between old players and newbies, and bad blood between the company and the players, this game is no longer a masterpiece—it's hurtling toward its end. If you still want to play it after reading my post, go ahead. I'm just giving you advice, I'm not outright telling you not to do it. It is certain that this game used to be truly amazing and awesome. But it's a former masterpiece that management completely ruined, not a masterpiece today. If you've played *GTA San Andreas* before, you know how fun it was, and you probably tried *Grand Theft Auto IV* to feel that fun again. If you want higher quality and a finished product than that, go for it. But I strongly urge you not to play *Grand Theft Auto Online*. I can't deny that there's more content in Online. But don't throw away 65,000 KRW just to enjoy that content for a brief moment.

translation_en: Hello. I am BeaBoy, and since I don't see many quality reviews for this game here, I'll take the liberty of reviewing it myself as well. To introduce myself and my relationship with GTA V: I started playing GTA V back in 2013 when it came out on the Playstation 3. Outside of Steam, I have around 600 hours played on the game and have finished the campaign a total of 3 times. GTA V is one of those hardware-demanding games. [h1]Minimum HW Requirements[/h1] Operating System: Windows 8.1 64 Bit, Windows 8 64 Bit, Windows 7 64 Bit Service Pack 1, Windows Vista 64 Bit Service Pack 2* (*NVIDIA video card recommended if running Vista OS) Processor: Intel Core 2 Quad CPU Q6600 @ 2.40GHz (4 CPUs) / AMD Phenom 9850 Quad-Core Processor (4 CPUs) @ 2.5GHz RAM: 4GB Graphics Card: NVIDIA 9800 GT 1GB / AMD HD 4870 1GB (DX 10, 10.1, 11) Sound Card: 100% DirectX 10 compatible HDD: 65GB DVD drive [h1]GTA V itself As a story mode (singleplayer)[/h1] You don't have to play previous installments to understand the plot because, apart from a few easter eggs, this part has its own storyline. I estimate the playtime of all missions to be around 24-30 hours + plenty of side missions. The game is high quality both in terms of graphics and the story, which immediately manages to draw you in. This is also indicated by the fact that the game managed to make back its development costs within 24 hours of release. GTA V is also unconventional in that instead of one main character, you can play as three main characters right away. [h1]GTA Online (Multiplayer)[/h1] I'll venture to say that GTA Online is one of the best multiplayer campaigns regarding games in general. To start with, I'd like to state that the online system here isn't based on classic servers, but so-called sessions, of which there can be an infinite number and players from all over the world can join them. I believe the capacity in one such session is around 30 players, and via so-called Crews, which I'll talk about more in a bit, or via your friend list, you can play with your friends in sessions. All jobs are joined through a lobby, to which you can also invite players outside your session. Any player can create their own private sessions, which are divided into: SOLO: You play here alone and there are no other players INVITE: Only players invited by you play here CREW: Only players from the same Crew as you play here PUBLIC: Any player from any corner of the world can play here. Online contains countless missions that you can play with your friends. Countless so-called Adversary Modes, which you could say are mini-games within the GTA game itself, plus plenty of maps for deathmatches, races, stunt races, arm wrestling, etc., which are not developed only by Rockstar itself, but through the Rockstar Creator function, you can create maps and races yourself and publish them into the game using the Social Club service, where every player must be registered. Besides that, Online includes the already familiar Heists, which are big robberies aimed at making a larger amount of money. I haven't mentioned plenty of other entertainment branches such as minigames like golf, tennis, darts, and others. The GTA Online game has been continuously improved for several years, and new DLC updates are released that are part of the game and are not paid, and there are many ways to earn in-game currency. Through the mandatory Social Club service for Online, it is also possible to create so-called Crews (groups), where you can unite yourself and your friends and thus be better connected; it's also worth mentioning that each crew can create its own logo through Social Club, whatever they want as long as it doesn't conflict with the rules. You can then stick these logos on your cars in the game, for example. [h1]Cons[/h1] A big downside of the whole Online is that with how huge updates are constantly being added, like Executive and Other Criminals, Import/Export, and many others, where there are private yachts, giant residences, drug farms, cash, large offices, and many expensive but nice cars, there is also the problem of... where to get the money for it? Yes, we have countless ways to earn, but when one mission or a bigger race yields something around $20,000, it's relatively little, and it's impossible to earn enough for all the content of all updates this way. If I roughly calculate that if you were to own all the content of the added updates, it will cost you up to 100 million $ in game currency, which is a damn big amount and it's impossible to earn it all the honest way. That's why illegal features like various Mod Menus emerge, which are simply cheats, and you don't always run into a cheater who gives money to players, but they might also ruin the game by spawning big objects on the map, or by godmode. Nevertheless, despite all of this, you can still enjoy the game and even after your first thousand hours played, the game can still surprise you and be immensely entertaining. [h1]Evaluation[/h1] It is very difficult to write a hundred-percent review for this game because the game has so much content that simply describing everything is impossible, and you just have to try the game. I won't describe here how you can do anything you can think of. Yes, you can, and that's why this genre is also called Sandbox... I guarantee that if you give it time, you will experience the best gaming moments in the game.

translation_en: My first time experiencing this game was playing a pirated copy on a classmate's PC. Back then, we called it "Three Men and a Dog" because you couldn't search for its real name on Taobao and other shopping sites. I'm ashamed to say that basically all the games I played before that were pirated, or else fast-food games from Tencent and the like. But GTA V truly was the first masterpiece I ever encountered, and ever since then I've been proud of having played this game and recommended it to people everywhere. It's also because of this game that I've pretty much bought legitimate copies of every game I've played since. My classmate downloaded it from Ali213. Back then, my mind was blown when I saw a game was 50GB. Why was it so damn big? How much stuff could possibly be packed into a game? Then entering the game, starting with a flat-topped brute (Michael) and a constantly screaming idiot (Trevor) in a nonsensical robbery in North Yankton, I fell deeply into this game. The scene shifts to Los Santos, Michael doing therapy, Franklin and his black homie Lamar going off to steal cars. I hesitated for a long time back then choosing between the white car and the red car, followed by all kinds of stealing motorcycles and cars, gang wars, and then the protagonists meeting. Michael pisses off Martin, Franklin helps out, and they pull a jewelry store heist together. After succeeding, the scene cuts back to the psycho, who was going crazy as usual. I hated his guts back then, but when he also made it to the city and met up with Franklin and Michael, I started loving Trevor's wild ideas for heist planning, and happily played through the whole game. Later, seeing online that you could make money in the game through the stock market, I copied the game over to my PC and started a new playthrough. Then I found out some stocks were on a different interface, so I bought a legit PC game for the very first time in my life. Later on, when a game glitch happened, I deleted and redownloaded it, beating the offline story for the fourth time, but I didn't feel bored at all. Every time I watched the dialogue between the protagonists, I got a new feeling or a new understanding. Later I egged my friends into buying legitimate copies too, since after all, heists are a 2-player or 4-player game. After my friend bought it, he only played Online mode, so I secretly helped him beat the offline story too, haha. I could say that out of my 700 hours of playtime, a good fraction was spent wandering around offline. After finishing the main story and side quests, I'd go online to search for other offline achievements. The remaining time was spent waiting for friends to come online to do heists and mess around, and I also met some veteran players online. In a heist, one guy would charge ahead, and by the way we slowly moseyed over, he had already cleared out the entire Humane Labs. I really cherish the time playing Online with these friends. Whether due to the PC or the network, doing a mission required our computers to struggle to sync up for a long time, otherwise we'd run into all kinds of sudden issues. However, good times don't last. Last month, while doing the Pacific Standard job, I queued with a random public squad. Someone among them apparently used high-tech hacks. I didn't quit in time, and at the settlement screen I got bugged out of the game. Logging back in resulted in a 1-month ban. I can honestly say I've never used a cheat in my life. From the Eclipse Towers to the stilt apartments to all the supercars and weapons, and the yacht I accidentally bought on my secondary character—every single one of them was earned grinding missions and gigs. The face sculpting for both characters was carefully picked out to be what I thought was the most handsome and pretty, yet a few days ago when the ban was lifted and I logged in, I found that both of my accounts had been wiped. Creating a new character and jumping into an online session showed that everything was gone, leaving behind just a Level 1 alt with over 4 million in the bank... I've been looking for ways to fix this for the past few days, but I can't even log into the official website platform, haha. I honestly don't know what to say. I still deeply love this game; otherwise, I wouldn't have beaten the offline story 5 or 6 times without getting sick of it. My friends often say I've wrung every last drop of value out of these 200 RMB, squeezing it dry over and over again, but this ban really makes me feel so tired. The money is secondary; I modified those cars so many times, and every color scheme and interior I agonized over was the result of thoughtful time spent. Now they're telling me it's all gone—what kind of logic is that? I recommend this game from the bottom of my heart, but even more so, I don't want many people to pour in tons of time, effort, and money only to find out all their stuff is just an illusion. Rather than getting and then losing, it's better to have never possessed it at all.

Rather than doing this via DLC, asking for €5 or €10 regularly (and given the additions they could totally get away with it), Rockstar delivers these updates to us for free, and has been doing so since the game came out. It's just so inconceivable nowadays from a big studio that I had to mention it. To give you an idea, I'll take the most recent update as of writing this, the Bikers update. Which adds: → a phenomenal amount of bikes, sometimes highly customizable, very high-performing, very enjoyable, depending on the models of course. Two-wheel fans will be thrilled, GTA is no longer just about cars given the variety of two-wheelers now available. → the ability to buy a sixth property, meaning up to 60 vehicles in total for multiplayer. Just 60. Actually no, because: → the ability to buy a clubhouse to start your own motorcycle club and get into all kinds of illegal businesses: drugs, fake IDs... A brand new gameplay style, unfortunately restricted to public sessions (I'll come back to that). Your base can also store up to 10 bikes, making it a total of 70 vehicles with the 6 properties. You can even customize them on-site. Just like with the Yacht (a previous update), the base is slightly customizable. → New multiplayer game modes. There was already a ton of them, and well now, there are even more. Anyway, end of the list. All of that for free. How is the game even profitable despite being free? Well, first off, through account repurchases. The online mode is crawling with cheaters, and Rockstar's anti-cheat system is getting more and more efficient, sometimes even a bit overzealous. But you always get a second chance, so hey, it's fine. Still, some cheaters are forced to recreate accounts after a permanent ban. I'm saying this so you understand that despite themselves, they contribute a bit to keeping the game alive, so oh well... The situation has clearly improved regarding cheaters, and public sessions are generally playable (though it's still about as calm as Baghdad, but hey), which is all the more important since two updates (the one allowing you to start a business and the biker club one) require you to be in a public session (which isn't mandatory for the rest of the game) to enjoy them. Alongside that, there are shark cards, which let you get quick cash for the online mode. So, is it worth it? Not really, it's not actually that hard to make money in the end. But just because this model is so much better than having a ton of paid DLC... Don't hesitate to grab one on a day when you have money to burn. Just so that when they release GTA VI, they think this business model works, and that they don't need to charge for updates. The multiplayer mode is an atrocious time-sink, thanks to the monstrous amount of things to do. The casual activities (golf, darts...), co-op missions, heists, PvP modes, races... And of course, the story is as well-directed as ever. The numerous references are proof, if any were needed, that Rockstar left NOTHING to chance. Everything is controlled, in a good way. A masterpiece, plain and simple. If you like the universe and the style, there's no need to hesitate. You're already years behind, so it's high time you fix that! PS: don't forget that the baby is over 60 GB.

First of all, I feel like Rockstar doesn't stand in the players' shoes at all; they just act like money-grubbing businessmen who don't give a crap about player feedback. A good game company must first put themselves in the players' shoes and consider their feelings. Even No Man's Sky just dropped another update, so I want to ask why Rockstar doesn't have that kind of sincerity. I'm not going to bother pulling up exact statistics, but I genuinely feel like GTA Online is the game that falsely bans good players the most. Why can't Rockstar take a page out of Blizzard's or Ubisoft's book? Even though we jokingly call one a CGI studio and the other a bug factory, when it comes to cheaters, they'd rather risk not banning someone than falsely ban an innocent player. That's one of the reasons why we call Blizzard "daddy" and why we're still willing to buy Ubisoft games. But looking at Rockstar, they'd rather issue false bans and offer zero appeals. With an attitude like that, who the hell is going to buy their games anymore? Oh right, I think I originally got banned just because I looked down on modders, fought back against a few of them, and launched a few heists in a row. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -Divider: The text below is the original review from 11.11, the text above was added on 12.8- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - [b] First off, I'm writing this purely out of dissatisfaction over getting falsely banned [/b] I pre-ordered GTA. Back then I actually wanted to buy Dying Light, but I ended up choosing GTA. Everything felt so mind-blowing when I first started playing, and GTA Online in particular felt insanely fun. I can't even describe the sense of wonder I felt back then, probably because it was the only AAA game in my library at the time. My PC specs were trash back then too, and it lagged like hell when I first started playing, but I remember an optimization patch about 2 months in that actually made it run pretty smoothly. I really wish Rockstar was still that considerate of players instead of being the greedy, money-obsessed freaks they are now. When I bought it, they were giving away 1M cash for online, which was a huge sum back then. As an old-school player, I genuinely love this game. Even though my playtime isn't super high, it still kept me company for a really long time. From using Cheat Engine to grind money back in the day, to exploiting car-selling glitches later on, to dealing with all the modders—I've seen it all and lived through it all. I was even tempted to use cheats myself, but my conscience stopped me. I admit that Rockstar wants to stamp out cheating, but I have never once used a cheat, and now I'm the one who's permanently banned. All I did was launch a few heists back-to-back. I don't want to swear, but with Rockstar pumping out all this new content, can't they clear the names of us innocent players? To anyone thinking about buying it later on: you're better off not getting this game, because the online mode is completely unplayable. This is my first review, but it'll probably be my only negative one. Only when Rockstar gives us our innocence back will this review actually start praising the game.

translation_en: When the news about GTA 5's upcoming release came out, I was so excited and thrilled. As soon as it hit Steam, I pre-ordered it right away, counting down the days and hours until this game of my dreams would unlock... Finally, on April 14th, 2015, the game unlocked, and I couldn't wait to download the decrypted files and jump in. When the familiar opening screen appeared, my heart started beating faster and faster, and I couldn't contain my excitement. After waiting a bit, I finally got into the game, into the prologue. When I finally gained control, I was shaking so much I could barely hold my mouse. After the prologue, I controlled Franklin for a few missions, got used to the controls, and then went into Online mode to make my character. Once everything was ready, I started playing Online. After a while, summer vacation rolled around, and my friends started playing too. We cruised around together online, did missions, and had an amazingly happy time. Back then, you didn't just get banned randomly; none of us got banned, and we happily played like that for a while... Until one day, when my friends weren't playing, I was bored and just wandered around online for a bit. When I came back, it told me I was banned. I didn't really understand why, but since it was only for a few days, I didn't care too much... After a while longer, I was just cruising around again, and when I came back, it told me I was banned—this time for a month... I was so furious at the time, I filed an appeal, but nothing came of it. Whatever, I had other things to do during that time, so if I couldn't play for a month, fine. So I didn't touch the game for a long time. A long time passed, and I suddenly felt like playing again. I opened the game, did some missions, and for a few days nothing happened, aside from constantly getting disconnected (I gotta say, the servers are absolute trash). But the ban happened anyway. And this time... yep, permanent. I was completely blank. What the hell did I even do??? Get disconnected while doing a mission, log back in, and get told I'm permanently banned? I was so pissed. Go appeal on the official website, that's what everyone says, so I did. I looked up a bunch of appeal posts and methods, and spent a long time writing out my appeal to them. I was so nervous after submitting it, wondering if they'd unban me. But not long after I submitted it, they replied to me. I thought, wow, Rockstar's customer service is so efficient, that's at least pretty cool... Yeah, super efficient, except it was a fucking bot!! Right, as long as they reply to you, it's all good, they don't even need to read it carefully, just brush you off. After calming down, I figured maybe my appeal method was wrong, so I tried a bunch of other ways again, but it was still useless. Later I just emailed them directly, and after a while, they replied. It didn't look like a bot this time; they said they'd help me check. They were finally willing to talk to me! So I waited patiently. After a little while, they messaged me back saying I had been "convicted" and they wouldn't accept any more appeals. I was so mad I lost my mind. Bro, if you're gonna convict me, at least tell me the fucking reason? Saying I'm convicted without giving any reason at all—not even knowing what killed me, it's enough to make a guy die with infinite grievance! I just want to say, if Rockstar puts out any more games in the future, I'm really gonna have to think twice about whether I'll get banned the second I touch it... Finally, a piece of advice for those who haven't bought it yet but want to: think carefully about whether you want to spend nearly two hundred bucks on a game with an online mode that basically forces you to only play offline... Get your shit together, Rockstar. You're going from greatness straight to ruin.

translation_en: "The best GTA ever made" - wait, that statement only holds true if you consider graphics and a living city, which people complained GTA IV lacked. OK. Yes, in that regard GTA V is truly a masterpiece of a GTA. The city is gorgeous, alive, with plenty of hobbies and pastimes to do, and the best online mode - in my view, where they invested the most to hook casual players. In the online mode, there have been a lot of updates to keep the game alive and playable for a long time. OK, that's understandable and even plausible for a game that was produced for many years with a high investment. But... Well, a lot of people might disagree with me, but the story mode of this GTA is, to me, the poorest one, the one that leaves the most to be desired... Everything is a cliché and Trevor is the only thing that saves the game, hands down. I miss the feel of plots and settings like the ones in Vice City, IV, San Andreas, and III. I really don't care about a sandbox full of things to do; to be honest, it's nice to have some things, but I soon get tired of so many places to go, discover, and interact with. Maybe it's a flaw from having grown up with very objective games, but that's how I feel. Don't get me wrong, the game is by no means bad! But I can't help comparing the feelings brought on by the predecessors to this one when it comes to the campaign. Vice City - my favorite - made me feel like I had opened a door to the '80s and was living in the Miami of that era, making contacts to find out who sabotaged me and how to recover the damage done. III made me feel like a prisoner who got a lucky break and now had to rebuild himself while hunting down the whereabouts of the person who tried to kill him. San Andreas (everyone's favorite) put me in the shoes of a fallen gangster who had to slowly rise back up and beat a corrupt police force in the middle of the '90s, and IV made me feel the wrath of a Serb who didn't want to, but got dragged into a mess with the Russian mafia, and then had to deal with them with the help of some friends in a modern New York. To me, those feelings are more important than a pretty sandbox with an OK story as a backdrop. Maybe also, GTA V and its story dealing with such current themes... the rich valley girl who wants to be famous and has an annoying voice, the middle-aged guy having a midlife crisis, the hater/gamer/troll/useless/frivolous guy, the unfaithful wife who cheats because she feels neglected (note: I had several urges to kill Michael's family during the game); continuing... the poor guy who wanted to get out of the ghetto and get rich, and the psychopath just because, since he had a hard childhood, but he's misunderstood and sensitive too... Well, maybe it all became too contemporary and common to the reality we live in... Maybe the others were cooler because they provided feelings and settings we hadn't lived through. That's just my point of view. This is a GTA for everyone, casuals or fans... that's why I have to recommend it. But there's just that little observation. Fun: 8 Graphics: 9 Story Mode: 7 (it's cliché, but it has some cool heist parts that are even diverse since you can choose how you'll do them) GTA Online: when everything works out with Rockstar's server connection it's a lot of fun, but nothing is perfect, there are too many hackers and assholes. Even as a modest fan of this franchise, this was a critical and respectful review for all the magic of this GTA V.

translation_en: Old review: Written on January 12, 2017. Still a negative review and I'm not changing it. I saw this coming. Ever since I got slapped with a random 30-day ban for no fucking reason, I knew the next one wouldn't be far off. Bought the game on November 26, got banned for 30 days on November 28, and got unbanned on December 28. A few good buddies of mine had been waiting for me to get unbanned so we could go run some heists together. Spent two fucking weeks finally becoming a half-decent veteran, mastering all the heist strats, and even bought an office to become a CEO. Still no mods, no cheats, no griefing innocent players. I was literally two steps away from completing the Criminal Mastermind challenge. I was smoking a cigarette while doing vehicle cargo, and right as I parked the car in the warehouse, a big fucking banner popped up: "You have been permanently banned from GTA V Online." The inevitable finally happened. I knew that once you get false-banned, there's a first time for everything and a second time coming. Rockstar, you ruthless pricks, we are never seeing each other again. Got nothing left to say. Game is getting uninstalled. Finally, I wish all you readers safety and that you manage to stay the fuck away from false bans. A quick heads-up for anyone still on the fence about buying: Rockstar is a bunch of scamming assholes, think twice before throwing your money at them. —————————————————————————————————————————— Old review: Written on November 28, 2016. First of all, I want to say GTA is a great game. An amazing franchise that's been with a lot of us from childhood to where we are now. However, Rockstar is just a good game developer, not a good game publisher. I used to be a pirate back in the day because of reasons and didn't have the channels or the chance to buy legit software as a kid. Now I have a job, I make my own money, and the Online mode of this generation is super appealing, so I chose to buy the legit version to support Rockstar. Reality is harsh, though. I deeply regret not thoroughly reading everyone's negative reviews before buying, naively thinking that as long as I didn't cheat, I wouldn't get banned. Until I got kicked offline just two days into owning the game with a total of 20 hours played, right after scraping together enough cash to buy a 270k apartment, and got hit straight with a 1-month ban. I know damn well I didn't use cheats, mods, or even aggressively attack other players. I was just honestly grinding missions to make money. So I went everywhere looking for help on how to appeal. Tried Rockstar's web appeals, email appeals, everything. All I got were cold-ass automated replies: "Thanks for reaching out, but account bans are final and cannot be appealed. Thank you for your support of Rockstar." Are you shitting me? Is this how you thank players for their support? Putting aside the fact that I didn't cheat, even if I got screwed over by some cheater, why the fuck do I get a 30-day ban on my very first offense? Isn't the first offense supposed to be 10 days? You ban me for 30 days after I've only played 20 fucking hours, do you really think I'd ever play again once unbanned? The next false ban would be permanent. How the fuck are you guaranteeing my rights and my interests? My time is fucking valuable, you know! Now let me talk about the current state of the game. Online is still crawling with a shitload of hackers. They spawn money, drop planes, tanks, and UFOs killing everyone on the street, and force money onto your character! Which gets *you* banned. Meanwhile, their mods have data-spoofing features, making Rockstar's kindergarten anti-cheat system completely blind to their abnormal data. But regular players who happen to be in the same public lobby get dragged down with abnormal data and end up getting banned for 10 days, 30 days, or even permanently. Let me break down the types of players right now: 1. Normal players who got false-banned during normal gameplay, or have been false-banned before. Now they can only cautiously play in invite-only lobbies, keeping anyone else away from their world. A proper open-world online game turns into a fucking LAN co-op game. 2. Cheaters. Whether out of need, curiosity, or whatever random bullshit reason, they hack, spawn money, and kill people. Some of them even do it out of spite toward society, forcing cash onto normal players to get them banned, while they themselves stay scot-free thanks to their cheats being more advanced than Rockstar's monitoring system. 3. Lucky players who still believe false bans are a real thing. They've either witnessed it or had friends experience false bans, so they're too scared to join public lobbies and are stuck grinding missions in their own little bubble with one or two friends. 4. The last group, and also the most disgusting ones! The people who don't believe Rockstar hands out false bans and loudly scream, "Everyone who gets banned deserves it and is a cheater." I can't even be arsed to cuss out these people. Short-sighted, ignorant, schadenfreude-loving, zero-IQ, petty narrow-minded brainless pricks. Get the fuck out of here and don't come stinking up my feed, or I'm gonna light up some firecrackers on your ancestors' graves. If you read all that and are still super interested in this game, keep reading: 1. Rockstar bans purely through system monitoring, so false bans are everywhere. If they ban 100 players, maybe only 2 of them were actually using cheats. To avoid getting caught in a false ban yourself, see rule number two. 2. Stay the fuck out of public lobbies! Stay out of public lobbies! Stay out of public lobbies! Important shit needs to be said three times. Find friends to play in invite-only sessions, and tell your buddies to never use mods or cheats so nobody gets dragged down innocently. 3. Aside from staying out of public lobbies, it's rumored that frequently switching VPN nodes, running PC cleaners like 360 or QQ PC Manager, or having massive cash inflows or outflows on your account can all trigger abnormal account data and get you banned. Since you already bought the game, you better tread carefully. That's all the help I can give you. Now about Rockstar—not like they'll ever read this. Rockstar makes decent games, but they are guilty of crimes. Console versions came out two years ago published by Sony, and they didn't learn a damn thing from Sony's publishing experience. When they finally opened up the PC version to self-publish, they got completely blindsided by hackers. Hackers everywhere, flashing lights, flying into the sun with a single rocket explosion. They chose the absolute dumbest approach: the piecemeal tactics. They didn't upgrade their monitoring systems, nor did they reinforce their anti-cheat and anti-piracy defenses. Instead, they let the hackers lead them by the nose. Wherever the hackers went, since they couldn't accurately pin them down, they just used a half-assed monitoring system to check for data anomalies and handed out bans in droves, while the actual cheaters slipped right past data detection. This monitoring system is absolute trash, it's fucking infuriating. You run the Pacific Standard Heist? Made some money? Cool! Your data is abnormal! You're banned. You saved up to buy a car? Bought a house? Great! Your data is abnormal! You're banned. Rumor has it Rockstar used to have actual customer support agents who would seriously read player appeals and offer replies or even compensation. And now? All automated replies. I submitted feedback ten times through different channels, and what did I get back? 10 identical automated responses with different signatures, word for word, not a single letter changed. Do Rockstar's support staff only know how to copy and paste? If you're not even gonna read the appeals before auto-replying, why the fuck don't you just dissolve the support department altogether? Too big to care about customers, aren't you? Not scared of bad reviews, are you? Rockstar, you really fucking broke my heart. The eyes of millions of Steam players are sharp as fuck. Open your eyes and look at your own GTA Online! Hackers running rampant, normal players surviving in the cracks, terrified that one day their hundreds or thousands of hours of progress will get banned. One day, you're gonna wipe out every single normal player with your false bans, leaving servers full of nothing but cheaters having a god-mode anime battle and crashing your fucking servers! Anyway, I'm never buying a legit Rockstar game ever again. The stuff is good, but I can't accept your attitude and service! You don't give a single flying fuck about consumers' feelings, so how the hell are we supposed to defend our rights? You want to cash in, fine, but at least don't make it look so fucking greedy and shameless!

translation_en: Apologies to anyone whose replies were deleted ====================================================================== Please tell me if GTA's false bans ever stop being this ridiculous, and I'll change my review immediately and come back to GTA. While I'm not some pro with thousands of hours under my belt, I've still played a good hundred hours or so. I'm not writing this review on a whim or just after starting the game, dropping an angry rant and leaving. Would I randomly leave a negative review for a game I've played 100+ hours if something genuinely unfair wasn't going on? Before you guys come at me (even though I'm already going off), please actually think about it first. Finally, I'm writing this negative review for two reasons: first, to tell Rockstar; second, to tell people who haven't bought it yet to think twice and see if they can stomach the high chance of getting falsely banned, so fewer people get screwed over. This isn't just to shit on Rockstar, so keep it civil, everyone. ============================Original Review======================== Let's get this straight first: until the wave of false bans stops, the negative review stays. I picked up GTA 5 in early 2016. At the very beginning, only one of my friends had GTA 5, and he already had 150 hours on it, so right off the bat, I got to experience the best part of the game: Heists. I've got around 150 hours now, and aside from the opening prologue, every single second of it was spent in Online. GTA 5 has easily given me the most fun I've ever had on Steam. I don't go out of my way to add people, so I only have 14 friends on my list to this day, and 12 of them played GTA 5 with me. During the times we played the most, we'd be doing heists all day long. The moment you hopped into a party chat, you'd see a bunch of people on the mic. Aside from heists, we wasted tons of time griefing each other (back when I was level 30, I managed to get my 400k down to 100k through PVP, which was a huge deal to me at the time). To be honest, I never really ran into the cheater problems everyone in the review section always complains about, so I had a really long, amazing run. And all of that ended when the first person I played GTA with got banned. I don't remember the exact date, probably around when the CEO update dropped. He must've been part of the first big wave of false bans. Not that there weren't random bans before, but it was only after him that GTA turned into what it is now, where you're basically guaranteed to get banned if you play for more than 10 hours on average. Ever since then, my friends slowly started giving up on GTA 5. Not just because the late-game gets a bit repetitive (though that's definitely part of it—anyone who's hit level 50 or 60 in GTA Online knows how repetitive it gets after finishing those few heists, it's just endless grinding; if I didn't have friends playing with me, I probably would've quit around 100 hours instead of 150), but because none of us dared to play anymore. A level 20 noob who didn't even own an Armored Kuruma or any real estate got his account banned twice. Falsely banned twice in under 20 hours of playtime (and no, it wasn't me), which completely scared all of us away from the game. We started looking for other multiplayer games to play, but came up empty. There are no recent games that match GTA 5's mix of so many different elements while being exceptionally high quality in every single aspect, including the online stability (man, that's probably a broken sentence). We still haven't found a game to replace GTA. It gave us the most fun gaming memories, only to snatch them right back just because of the massive wave of false bans later on. In GTA, you used to be able to roll out with a few friends in a convoy of Monster Trucks just to take in the views, go skydiving out of a plane, or have all-out tank battles. But you can't experience any of that anymore. If you want to play with your friends now, all that's waiting for you is ban, ban, and another fucking ban. The last time I even logged into GTA was just to test out a ping booster. I genuinely hope we get to go back to GTA someday, because it represents my memories. I'm writing this right before bed when my brain is totally fried, so logic and grammatical errors are bound to happen, my bad. To sum it all up in one sentence: GTA is a great game—don't let it get ruined by bullshit reasons, and don't let it ruin our once-happy memories.

I'm not entirely sure, but it was around 10 minutes. I quit right after the first racing tutorial. But an hour later, I got an email saying I was hit with a 2-week ban. ? There was one other guy who did the racing tutorial with me, so I thought, maybe he was a cheater? Since it wasn't a permanent ban, I didn't think much of it. At the time, I was playing through the game's main story, so I figured I'd just play the main story for about 2 weeks and hop back online when the ban lifted. When the ban was lifted, I started playing online for real. I met 3 strangers in a public session and played a 4-player job together. Surprisingly, it was damn hard, and unlike the main story, your character dies after taking just a few bullets. We kept failing so it took a lot longer than I thought to beat it. I think we played for about 2 hours, and I was exhausted so I quit. Then, 1 hour later, I get an email saying I'm banned for 2 weeks. This pissed me off a little. Those Rockstar motherfuckers just notify you that you're banned without telling you *what* you got banned for. If there was a cheater among the 3 guys I did the job with, we wouldn't have struggled and died so much trying to beat it. I was pissed, but I figured there must have been some issue and let it go again. The third time I played online, I enjoyed it by myself. I did the most basic money-making stuff like robbing convenience stores and selling cars I stole from pedestrians, made about 20 grand, and called it a day. I think I played for about 4 hours this time. And right on cue, 1 hour later, a 2-week ban notice lands in my email. I played alone this time, so what the fuck again? Since they don't give you a reason, there's no way to know what the problem is or fix it. I got sick of it and quit. I didn't log on for several months. And yesterday, because of some event where they give you $250,000 if you log on to online, I logged on once. The money in my possession was still just $20,000. There wasn't a trace of hacking. It felt pointless to just log off immediately, so I went to Vinewood, took a selfie with the Vinewood sign in the background, and quit. And this time, an email arrives saying I've been permanently banned. Still no fucking reason given. Fuck Rockstar. P.S. : A lot of people are asking, so I'm adding this. I didn't use any cheats, trainers, or hacks in single-player either. I didn't install any weird patches or mods—I played single-player completely pure vanilla. And of course, multiplayer was the same, pure vanilla. I've never gone AFK while playing either. Also, people said that just playing Heists online is worth the money... Heists my ass... I couldn't even play online properly. P.S 2 : A lot of people keep arguing with me, so I'm adding this too. I am a Rockstar hater, but I'm not a GTA hater. As you can see from my account, I own GTA 4, San Andreas, Vice City, Liberty City, all of that. I've never had any complaints. I really love the GTA series itself, and I had a blast playing GTA 5 single-player. I just have complaints about online, and I have no intention of ruining the mood for people who are enjoying GTA 5 Online, nor am I calling for a boycott telling people not to buy the game. I'm just telling my experience and giving my opinion. A lot of people are asking if I'm a GTA hater, but like I said above, I'm not. I'm a Rockstar hater. If you're gonna buy the game and have fun, go ahead. I think I even left a comment saying it's worth the money just for the single-player if you buy it on sale, though it might not be on the first page of comments anymore. If you're a fan, or even if you're not, GTA 5's single-player alone is more than enough. Buy it and play it. I just want to say that Online is a total gamble. I just want to bash Rockstar's management style.

translation_en: GTA 5 I took my time reviewing GTA 5. This allowed me to get an accurate picture, as I've already spent a lot of hours both on- and offline in Los Santos. Offline: Singleplayer GTA 5 is very different from its predecessors. The characters and the setting deviate strongly from previous ones. This fresh coat of paint does the overall picture a lot of good, and for the first time you have more than one character you can partly identify with, which in turn also made me, as a player, shake my head in incomprehension. I don't mean that in a negative way at all, because Rockstar takes a very clear moral stance in GTA 5. This stands above all for the badness of crime. This is depicted primarily through one of the three characters, who mostly acts in a morally reprehensible way. Even though this character isn't held fully accountable in the game, he most embodies the "nobody wants to end up like this" character. And even if the characters sometimes act short-sightedly and thoughtlessly and you as a player can only influence that to a limited extent, it is precisely this behavior that makes them feel alive and ensures that they grow on the player. Moving away from psychology to the game itself. The setup probably doesn't need explaining anymore, since GTA 5 was controversially discussed in the media when it was released. The world in itself feels gigantic and alive. Even after playing through the story and the numerous side and extra missions, there is always something new to discover in Los Santos. Be it a dam behind which the entire city lies, a peace mountain painted by hippies, or a cougar on the hunt. GTA 5 is unbelievably diverse and looks gorgeous while doing it. Even after almost 200 hours of playing, I'm still regularly taking screenshots of the impressive landscapes, sunrises, or the outstanding rendering in the rain. You can just tell that the entire game didn't just have a lot of money poured into it, but above all, attention to detail and stories. The story is very diverse and lets you feel the poverty and resentment in a ghetto with Franklin, empathize with first-world problems but also the abandonment anxiety of the upper class with Michael, and just live out the aggression and raw conflict potential with Trevor that can otherwise only be seen in weird dreams or on TV. Even Trevor, who in my eyes is the most difficult character to design, never feels forced. Even during critical missions, like the torture scene for instance, the game uses just the right amount of degradation so that the player finds it not belittling, but thought-provoking. To a certain extent, the game does degrade people, but mostly to underline the protagonists' character and give them even more depth. Bottom line for the story mode: it's very motivating and guarantees you'll play the game all the way to the end. Online mode: Multiplayer The online mode is also a blast and obviously shines less with character depth and more with the great possibilities of GTA 5. You have the same world as in the story mode and consequently a lot to see and experience again. The heists in particular are a lot of fun and bring in a lot of money, which you can then invest in vehicles (land, water, and air), weapons, real estate, and your appearance (no claim to completeness). But the online gameplay is not without flaws. For example, there are frequent problems with cheaters who kill you without being nearby or shooting, and the matchmaking isn't the best either. For example, you can join a heist, but if a player isn't particularly good, or the host is super eager for a bit more money (higher difficulty), even simple missions can sometimes get annoying with frequent retries. Nevertheless, the online mode is also very motivating, and once you've picked out a car/loft/yacht that you'd love to have, the hours just fly by while you scrape the cash together. If that takes someone too long, they can speed it up with real money (everything is optional, nothing is forced). A pay-to-win mentality doesn't arise from this, because an expensive weapon/vehicle or whatever still doesn't make you a good shooter/driver. Overall: All in all, GTA 5 is an unbelievably good game where, unlike Destiny for example, you can be sure that the huge sum that went into development is a good investment. It was one of the best games I've played in recent years, and I will definitely drop by Los Santos every now and then to have fun. I would also like to give special praise to Rockstar Games. I think it's brilliant that there are still developers who deliver a complete game for one price, that gets by without DLCs and yet leaves nothing to be desired (cough... EA, Ubisoft... cough). And after playing through, I'm treating Michael, Trevor, and Frank to a little rest after they gave me an insight into their world in nearly 100 hours and can finally live in a bit of peace after a whole lot of hardship. Because gangsters essentially just want peace and quiet, and after all the hustle and bustle in Los Santos, all that's left for me to say is: I'm looking forward to an equally outstanding GTA 6, where (hopefully not too soon, but at the same time as the console version would be nice) I will have just as much fun and joy as I did with GTA 5. Thumbs up Rockstar Games, keep it up exactly like this!!!

translation_en: Aside from human and worldly factors, gaming itself is a meaning and a faith to players, and like all of you, I love and respect every single title in the GTA series. However, I don't feel like playing the rational guy here, nor do I want to waste my breath with a long-winded, euphemistic negative review. With 1,000+ hours of playtime and over half a year of companionship, the ship of friendship sank just like that. We were in an uproar over the consequences of GTA Online's anti-cheat mechanism swinging wildly like a drunken master, but this wasn't just about mourning a lost game account. It was because we heard the voices of too many innocent players, and watched consumers try hard to defend their own interests to no avail, which is when we started reacting. But what followed next made us feel helpless and terrified: Rockstar Support completely ignoring us, treating our feedback and appeals with a passive attitude. Meanwhile, GTAO is still crawling with modders everywhere you look, and the system mechanism still operates with a "one size fits all" blanket ban approach. If things keep developing this way, batch after batch of innocent players who received permanent bans will quit Los Santos for good, while players who survived being falsely banned the first two times will just have to tip-toe through every single day in GTAO, knowing that one tiny slip-up will face another ruthless ban. At worst, you end up having to bow your head and act submissive in a game that's supposed to let you be wild and lawless, until you lose all your love and interest for the game. Now my 500-hour account has been banned for the second time, completely without reason, and absolutely no explanation. I really don't want to play this game ever again; it's been tainted by Rockstar's attitude. Are they abusing their market dominance to bully customers, or are they blinded by money? Actually, you can tell from many of their commercial (cash-grabbing) tactics: every time there's a ban wave, there's a price cut, followed by various big updates designed to get you to drag your friends into the pit right before they ban more people, and then after the update drops for a bit, they cut the price again. Of course, as consumers we buy it because we love it, so my review isn't trying to stop you guys from buying it, just serving as a reference. Although I'm certain I won't be playing this game anymore—because when you get unbanned and log back in, even dropping out of a session makes your heart race, and you have no idea what to do anymore—I hope my friends can keep playing happily and avoid false bans. Update: Today is October 26th. As everyone knows, the Bikers DLC dropped not long ago, and the game's price in the China region has dropped to 113. I'm not surprised by this at all, because I still see comments from falsely banned players popping up in the review section, many of them with under 100 hours of playtime. Whether they'll keep using this tactic to milk money in the future remains to be seen. My intent in slamming Rockstar isn't malicious, just venting. I have to say the genius devs at the studio really have a heart of gold—the single-player story is closely tied to modern society, the online gameplay is high, there are tons of customization options, and the optimization is famously good. But their upper management decided to push the Online mode, which means preparing for a long-haul war. So why not come up with a more comprehensive way to sustain this long war instead of burying their heads in the sand, rigging the game behind the scenes, and reaching into players' pockets, tying the reputation of the game itself and the company's image together in such a shallow way?

translation_en: First wrote my GTA review in 2016, then updated it twice, and it was always a thumbs down. Even after updating it for the latest After Hours DLC, it's still a thumbs down. ------------------------------------------------ My previous negative reviews were mainly about toxic online players, cheaters, and false bans. As of August 2018, the false ban issue seemed to have improved, but with the new update, cheaters are flooding the online lobbies all over again. Sticking to the advice of warning newcomers, this review emphasizes: unless you have close friends to play with long-term, do not buy this game just for the online mode. If you've never played GTA before, wait for a sale. Just play the offline story mode and don't let the online mode ruin your mood. Without friends to play with regularly, logging into online mode will just make you want to quit immediately. ------------------------------------------------ Now let's talk about R*. As their ways of making money have increased, their tactics for milking players have become increasingly ugly. Out of nowhere, a single car or plane costs two to three million, and the P-996 even sells for a staggering 6.5 million. The worst part is you can't use the CEO menu to spawn it right next to you, and your personal vehicle can't be driven while going to get the plane. Pegasus makes you go all the way to the airport. It's utterly heartless, cashing in by exploiting players' nostalgia. A $400 shark card barely fully upgrades two cars. Grinding your ass off all day and leaving the game idle all night only gets you 2-3 million. And the new Nightclub DLC? Making money is slow as absolute shit; it takes 10 hours for just over 600k, and you have to sink 5 to 6 million into it first just to fully upgrade it. The grind is exhausting, so give me a single reason to keep playing : ( ------------------------------------------------ Next, for those who have been playing online for a while, here is how to spot cheaters and money hackers: 1. God mode, obviously. If you shoot someone and they don't lose any health, just report them and switch sessions, don't waste your time. 2. Aimbot. This is hard for beginners to spot. Most people who sweat in PvP play in first-person; if someone in third-person is hitting every single shot, they're basically using an aimbot. In third-person, when you're not aiming, you can't strafe left/right or backwards, and when you are aiming, the strafing range is small and slow. Another way to spot god mode: if there isn't much lag between both parties—meaning you can see bullet tracers and health draining in real-time—it means low latency. Under low latency, if your corpse gets continuously shot after you die, there's a high chance the other guy is using an aimbot. 3. Under level 100, constantly rotating through armed vehicles, and casually dropping orbital cannons? 90% chance they're a money hacker, report them. 4. Level 1000+, 90% are hackers who boosted their rank and money. Of course, you can't rule out legit players, but in this case, hit ESC -> Online -> Players -> [Player Name] -> View Profile, and check when they joined the game. As far as I know, no one has grinded to level 1000 within a year. Report them decisively. If they don't have obvious cheating tendencies and have a low KD ratio, most of them probably aren't playing with cheats, so no need to rush to switch sessions—just report them. 5. People driving vehicles that are currently unobtainable through normal methods. Definitely cheaters, report and switch sessions immediately. ------------------------------------------------ If you actually got false-banned, don't panic, submit a ticket to Rockstar. The first 2-3 responses will be automated, just keep sending them, don't write too much, stick to the point, don't curse, stay calm and your account will be back in a few days. What is a false ban? Never hacked money, accidentally got fucked over by a cheater (like having money bags forced on you, in which case you can ask R* to confiscate the illicit funds), or got banned just by accidentally playing in a job with a cheater. That's a false ban. If you're out here acting like a money-hacking piece of shit and crying about false bans, my foot up your fucking grandma's cunt. ------------------------------------------------ If your PC specs are good enough or you're just playing normally, and any issues happen—like frequent abnormal stuttering or frame drops, or having illegal weapons on you (like the railgun, stun gun, fire extinguisher, etc.)—quit the game immediately, restart, and check if the issue persists. If it does, force-quit immediately and verify integrity of game files. ------------------------------------------------ Money hackers and god mode users are just excuses for absolute morons and weaklings. A bunch of motherfucking orphans. No defending it, cheating is absolute shit, parentless orphans. Those cunts using aimbot, god mode, and blowing up lobbies—their family members have already been fucked to death, and they themselves have broken hands and legs, late-stage paralysis, and terminal cancer with not much time left. When you run into them, just report and switch sessions, don't stoop to their level, let them rot away in loneliness. Motherless, fatherless, stinking piece of shit cunts are less useful than a placenta thrown out in a hospital.

But I still felt it had nothing to do with me, yet I started dreaming about the world of GTA:O. Chapter 2 High school. Forgot all about GTA. We played however we wanted, street racing, arm wrestling, shooting RPGs into people's backs while they browsed clothing stores, calling in Insurgents on the street to start shit. We were just a dozen ordinary students, hanging out in the hallway talking about which car was best after upgrades, talking about which job let you glitch the Kuruma. We had level 100+ pros, we had level 10 noobs, and before this, he used to play all by himself. He said he was almost able to afford the most expensive jetliner, while my daily cash hovered between 8,000 and 20,000, but I loved every second of it. Then, he got permanently banned because some godmode asshole was in his session. Now, we play some Overwatch, some CS:GO, and nobody brings up GTA anymore. Criminal Mastermind not finished yet, T20 not bought yet, spent more money on Shark Cards than the game itself, but nobody plays it anymore. I got a new PC in the second semester of my junior year, but the summer of junior year was spent playing Overwatch and MC, which means none of us even played for half a year, or even played continuously during the break. I've seen plenty of shady devs, I get that they're cash grabs, I get that the optimization is trash, but I seriously don't get Rockstar. I've played a lot of horror games, but GTA is the only one I don't dare to play. The funny thing is, it's not a horror game. The funny thing is, I don't dare to play it anymore. Poured nearly two grand into Shark Cards. Welcoming wave after wave of noobs, watching wave after wave of noobs modding money. Because of him, I don't mod money. I don't cheat. When there's new stuff, I grind. If I can't grind enough, I pay to win. I bought this game for him, and I am not going to cheat.

translation_en: Pros and cons of GTA 5: Pros: 1) You don't need the most powerful PC. The game's optimization lets you play it on a mid-range and even a weak PC. 2) Updates for Online come out very often. The updates are super cool and massive, Rockstar adds a lot of new stuff to Online. And these DLCs are completely free, and the update downloads to your PC automatically. 3) An open world where you definitely won't get bored and will find plenty of things to do to suit your taste. (Both in single-player and Online). 4) They put effort into adding a lot of secrets. There are many Easter eggs in the game that still haven't been fully solved. 5) There is a 1st-person view. And in the Next Gen they made the graphics more detailed, in 1st-person you can enjoy a drive in a car or a flight in a plane, and the control panel is qualitatively detailed. The speedometer will show the exact speed you're going, the dashboard will show whether the headlights are on or off, etc. 6) Good graphics. Even though I don't pay much attention to graphics, still, this can't be overlooked. They did such a good job with vegetation, well-crafted weather, for example, during rain puddles gradually appear, etc. 7) Very interesting Online, with lots of possibilities. Cons: 1) GTA 5 Online sometimes crashes, or just won't let you in. But such cases are rare, and with each update the chances of crashing get smaller and smaller. 2) If they don't update Online for a long time, cheaters appear in it, and there get to be more and more of them until an update comes out. Cheaters are the biggest problem in GTA 5 Online. If the cheater is nice, they might shower you with money or help you rank up, give you weapons. But if the cheater is evil, then pray, because they can take away all your weapons, start setting you on fire, attach all sorts of objects to you, kill you, take away your whole GTA Online level and can even break your game, and after that you'll have to reinstall it. Because of these cheaters you totally don't feel like logging into Online. 3) The physics in the game are bad. You can use a tank to knock down very sturdy lampposts, crush cars, but then if you hit a tiny twig sticking out of the ground, your tank will crash into it and stop. If your tank just crashes into it, you're lucky, otherwise its barrel might touch the twig and because of that your tank will be repelled with huge force and you'll fly way up into the sky. And car damage in GTA 5 is poorly developed too. Cars are hard to wreck, they'll just get small dents. Sometimes, that's really annoying. My rating: 8.6 out of 10. P.s I put together the pros and cons based on my own view. If you found anything else, write it in the comments.

translation_en: Foreword: The following content is my personal opinion, for reference only, please do not repost. (This review is suitable for newbies to use as a reference before diving in. Just a reminder, I'm not writing this review for anything, and it's only thanks to the support of so many people that it got voted up to serve as a reference for you guys. Most of the content is complaining, and I'm not holding a knife to your throat telling you not to buy GTA. Please read it slowly if you're going to read it, and look at this review rationally. To those who want to flame and show off your IQ, please click the thumbs down and hit the top right, thanks!) ———————————————————————————— 1. Game false ban issue. False bans on PC are pretty severe, and some boosters and antiviruses will trigger bans. (Player precautions in the comments; interested newbies can go take a look. Note: The "HAIdun" booster—cutting off connection in a session will change your IP address, which has a certain chance of causing a ban.) 2. OL's late-game management is pretty underwhelming. (Since you're doing free updates, do it right, otherwise I'd rather pay for a season pass.) Once you start playing, if you don't do the Criminal Mastermind challenge and don't buy Shark Cards, if you're broke you have no choice but to grind slowly. The payouts Rockstar gives are so pathetic, I'd rather go grind the overwhelmingly negative-reviewed The Division. Because GTA Online really forces you to grind money to buy things you like, and the process is extremely boring. For example, a normal Pacific Standard heist run gets you 200k. If you're skilled at cut-glitching, you can knock it out in 15 minutes. If you have no friends, don't glitch cuts, and rely solely on random lobbies, there are way more accidents and it takes way more time. It's totally a loop (Rockstar wants to sell Shark Cards for profit, they won't give you massive profits in the game itself). As things stand, only Pacific Standard is efficient, which leads to almost all money-making methods being limited to Pacific Standard. Other methods can reduce the boredom, but their efficiency can't compete with Pacific Standard. If you happen to need money, you become super passive. In the end, it leads to boringly grinding maps massively just for money, which seriously drains the fun out of the game. With all the updates to GTA Online, the 12 million Criminal Mastermind reward is nowhere near enough to spend. Plus, you can't repeat Criminal Mastermind, and any random sports car in Rockstar's later updates costs 1 or 2 million (modding cars is even more ridiculously money-burning), not to mention various planes and yachts. If you want the full experience, go bust your ass working the bricks. Among the money-making DLCs, Further Adventures in Finance and Felony has an entry cost: Office + gun locker + 2 large warehouses, no discounts, starting at around 4 million. Delivering goods starts out pretty fun, but the routine gets super repetitive. Selling a full batch of goods gets you around 2 million (under normal circumstances), but you have to stockpile those 111 crates first, and doing them 3 at a time on average takes at least 10 minutes at best. But Rockstar forces you to sell in a public lobby anyway (though you can glitch a solo public session, the session often lags out so friends can't join, some VPN glitches easily catch bans, and if you use third-party software to mess with your network speed, you better hope they don't wipe your memory), and you constantly get forced into griefing wars. You play games to have fun—would it blow your asshole apart to give people the option to sell in a private lobby? (This DLC has zero story, it's just about adding ways to make money, and that kind of stuff should be as convenient as possible. P.S.: The Division caused a ton of PVE players to quit early on because you could only farm the Dark Zone and were forced into PvP griefing, thankfully later updates nerfed the value of the Dark Zone.) 3. You can watch out for bans, and if you're low on cash and don't want to pay, you can at least grind slowly; if you don't want to grind and it's not fun, you can quit. (The main team for OL was pushed out and disbanded internally by Rockstar, which leaves the whole game feeling empty after finishing Criminal Mastermind.) Everything in the later updates requires huge amounts of cash, and even just wanting to experience the new money-making content has a ridiculously high entry cost. What? Don't want to grind? Well, as long as you're having fun :-D Alright, onto the main point. Please, for the love of god, let players permanently drop weapons. (People have been bitching about this issue since the game first came out, yet Rockstar completely ignores it. P.S.: This single thing shows what a shitty attitude Rockstar has, coupled with the false bans, tons of cheaters, and underwhelming late-game updates.) Plus, PS4 can do it, but PC somehow can't. Changing guns often takes forever cycling through them, and most of the time you switch to a gun you don't need, causing a fuck-up. I started an alt character, and I didn't dare buy weapons casually; with so many weapons out there, I can't even buy them. Is this just here to annoy players? Well, since you added the weapon locker, how about refining it so it actually works in basic PVE missions and heists? Is that really so hard? (Don't give me that bullshit about heists needing complete preparation—anyone going into a heist empty-handed is a fucking retard!) 4. Back in the day, Rockstar was a famously exemplary game dev company, mind-blowing back-to-earth generous, especially with SA—couldn't praise it enough. But now they just constantly reek of corporate greed, and the content in the later updates burns cash like it's nothing. It'd be fine if the experience scaled up with it, but the OL experience just falls painfully short; they simply refuse to let you have a smooth, fun time. For a character-creation addict like me, so many stylish clothes can't be bought, new body armor can't be worn properly, glasses + mask while wearing a hat afterwards won't let you wear a scarf, military gloves won't pair with a lot of outfits, and other normal clothing combinations like that literally require you to glitch them. Did this somehow violate your precious balancing, or is it just your retarded game design? 5. Even though OL has overwhelmingly positive reviews, playing it in the later stages feels extremely uncomfortable. For linear or semi-linear players, the longevity of the online mode is very mediocre. The playable content might look like a lot, but as far as PVE missions go, most of it is brutally repetitive, though some of the forced co-op missions are pretty fun. Once you finish the heists, you're pretty much in the late game. If you don't have other hobbies (like BMX, obsessive street racing, group griefing, or bro-dating with your homies), you completely run out of subsequent fun. There are very few tasks with any replay value (job content is poorly made, no new heists), though looking at the scenery is still pretty nice. 6. The entry barrier for the game is quite high, and the core heist mode requires 4 people. If you don't have homies, or can't find friends to roll with and just want to rely on random lobbies, it's not a long-term solution. Matchmaking in randoms takes forever because you need 4 people to gather, plus heists require a certain level of player skill, and the chances of random squads wiping are extremely high. It is strongly recommended that newbies starting out drag a few friends along to learn the ropes and experience heists together. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Review Update 12.14: This update brings Import/Export. Rockstar is still continuing to scam people out of money. New money-making content: a 3M car, sell payout is 200k, money-making efficiency is still trash. New sports cars, stock cars, new military vehicles—you already know the drill with purchase price + upgrade costs. Also the CEO garage where you can store military vehicles: buying and decorating the CEO garage costs over 6M, and if you don't own a CEO office, you have to shell out another 2M just to buy that first. Still completely lacking any substantial game content. People who haven't saved up cash still have to waste a massive amount of cost-inefficient time and money just to get this stuff. Aside from using it as a money-making channel, griefing sessions, or playing house, I literally cannot feel any more gameplay value. To put it bluntly, it's just official mods pulled out to milk cash. (No wonder Rockstar bans mods the second they see them.) I experienced this update on a whale account. Even on discount, an 8M Shark Card costs 250 RMB, while most AAA games can be had for 250 flat, not to mention season passes that only cost around 100-something. Unless you are deeply passionate about this game, buying it is not recommended because it has zero value for money. I'd rather go grind The Division than waste a ton of time constantly grinding virtual bricks just to buy official mods. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I wrote this review so that everyone can look at this work rationally instead of blindly hyping it up. Given Rockstar's industry standing, the late-game service and experience of GTA Online only deserve a negative review. The game isn't expensive, and if you aren't hard up for cash, it's totally worth picking up. Fast-paced sandbox, beautiful Los Santos, interesting story, and eye-catching heist mode can all be reasons to buy it. But you must know that GTA Online is not a game focused on clearing missions for rewards; a lot of the fun relies on the player's imagination to sustain its lifespan. However, money is the barrier to experiencing the late-game content. Grinding is exhausting, and if you don't grind, you'll eventually AFK for good—it varies from person to person. GTA 5 can provide around 100 hours of basic playtime. Of course, playing the game to have fun is what matters most. But Rockstar's basic PVE missions like jobs and heists are supposed to provide players like us—who just want to have fun with friends, randoms, or even solo—with the fastest and simplest joy, yet Rockstar fails to do that. Rockstar gave us a sandbox world, but they also only gave us a sandbox world. If you want to experience the thrill of making money through missions in GTA Online? You're better off buying Watch Dogs 2. If you want to grief, race, tea-bag, and cause general mayhem in Los Santos, then Online might just be the home for your next 1,000 hours.
