So it's not like you can just buy all the properties, cars, and weapons and then the game is over and you get bored. With every update, at least 2 vehicles are added. Right now, my guess is there are roughly around 70-80 purchasable vehicles in the game. The number of properties is around 20-30-something. As for weapons, there are 20-25-something. Until 4-5 months ago, players used to complain that they couldn't find mansion-style places instead of just apartments when buying properties, but Rockstar added mansion-style properties to the game as well. The most used property by players is the "Eclipse Towers". If you start the game with bonus money and don't know which house to buy, this might be the building to buy. For weapons, there are various customizations like skins, silencers, lasers, and flashlights. When it comes to clothes, there are dozens of outfits in the game. Especially for the female character, there is tons of customization available. Hair, makeup, you name it. Just because the customization options are better, I personally play as a female character, and she has a much nicer vibe than the male character ^^ So don't sweat this part too much, you can dress and customize your character in any color or style you want. For a small fee, of course. Character, vehicle, and weapon customization is probably one of the areas Rockstar put the most effort into regarding variety. [h1]Heists;[/h1] I mentioned that GTA is a pretty tough platform. Once I give you a few details about heists, you'll understand better. First of all, buying in-game money falls into the luxury category, and I think even people with money will steer clear of such expensive prices and won't buy in-game cash. 8 million cash was somewhere around 130-150 [liras] if I remember correctly. There are 5 heist missions in the game. Some of these 5 missions consist of 4 setups and 1 finale, while others consist of 5 setups and 1 finale. The first mission is for 2 players, with 2 setups and 1 finale; you can view this as training. All the other heists consist of 4 players. Before getting into how much money they pay, I have to say that if you don't have friends, it'll be a bit hard to find people for heists. As for how much cash you'll rake in from heists, I'll only list the payouts for "Hard" difficulty because if you play on "Normal" or "Easy", you won't get anywhere with the money given. [u]-The numbers are based on a single person's 20% cut out of 4 players, and the numbers might vary slightly-[/u] [b]1. Heist: Setup Missions:[/b] 3-5k Final: 60-70k Completing the whole thing "without dying": 25-30 mins [b]2. Heist: Setup Missions:[/b] 20k Final: 100k Completing the whole thing "without dying": 1 hour - 1 hour 20 mins [b]3. Heist: Setup Missions:[/b] 20k Final: 125k Completing the whole thing "without dying": 1 hour - 1 hour 20 mins [b]4. Heist: Setup Missions:[/b] 20k Final: 100-125k Completing the whole thing "without dying": 1 hour - 1 hour 20 mins [b]5. Heist: Setup Missions:[/b] 25k Final: 180k-200k Completing the whole thing "without dying": 1 hour 10 mins - 1 hour 30 mins For those wondering why I wrote it based on a 20% cut instead of 25%: unless the friend who opens—meaning hosts—the heist is extremely kind or filthy rich, they won't split 25% evenly among 4 people. Normally, 3 people get 15% and the host gets 55%. So while 15% is the norm, expecting the host to hand out a 25% cut is absurd, but players who give 20% are quite common. To sum it up for those saying, "Bro, dude, you're explaining this too complicated, make it simpler": let me put it this way. The most expensive car in the game is the X80 Proto, and it's also the fastest. Its price is around 2m 700k, let's say 3m with upgrades. Assuming you play 4-5 hours a day, you'll need to grind for about 2 weeks just to buy this. [h1]Playlists & Fun & Mini-Games;[/h1] I talked a lot about money in the heist section, which might have put a damper on some potential buyers' moods, but I kindly ask those people to read this section too. There are thousands of races in the game and these races are super fun. In these races, all players are equal, meaning the player with the fastest car doesn't just floor it and leave everyone in the dust. You can only make a tiny difference if you do minor upgrades to a car you already own. You select from certain vehicles, and you even have the right to choose vehicles you don't own. As for mini-games, I mean things like golf and tennis. These games are surprisingly detailed. Friends who love golf and tennis can spend a lot of time here. Rockstar didn't just phone these in; they actually put work into them. Aside from that, there are TDM matches, different game modes, survival modes, and tons of other stuff. So basically, even players with no money can have a blast in this game. Just cruising around the map, even in a car you found on the street, will give you immense pleasure. [h1]Map;[/h1] As most of us know, the GTA V map is way bigger than the GTA: SA map, but here's the thing: GTA: SA consisted of 3 cities, while GTA V consists of just 1. Most of the GTA V map consists of mountainous areas, but they didn't just lazily slap flat mountains down. There are different details at every step, and the more you explore, the more different things you discover. [h1]Cheaters;[/h1] 6 months ago, the game was crawling with cheaters, plain and simple. Everyone was doing money hacks, ruining the game for other players, etc. But Rockstar cleaned up almost 90% of the cheating players. Seeing cheaters pop up at every turn is very rare now. This might upset people looking for a quick buck, and they might even resort to cheating themselves to get rich quick, but I'll share some info about bans under the "Bans" heading for that as well. Hundreds of new players join every day, and there are plenty of players who don't use cheats, so you don't need to feel bad. [h1]Bans;[/h1] [b]1st Ban duration:[/b] 1 week. Trust me, staying away from a game like GTA is a long time. [b]2nd Ban duration:[/b] 1 month. When GTA fans spend 1 month without GTA, they swear off cheating forever ^^ [b]3rd Ban duration:[/b] 20-30 years or permanent. As far as I know, the 20-30 year one only applies to minor offenses. Those caught cheating get permanently banned straight up. Permanent or 20-30 years... what's the difference? ^^ I've written a lot, and trust me, there's even more to write about GTA. When it's on sale, it drops to around 110-120 TL, I say buy it and don't miss out. You might even find a cheaper 2nd-hand account on forums. I've seen and know hardcore hagglers who managed to find it for as low as 40 TL. Other than that, though, it doesn't look very likely to drop below 80-100 TL on Steam or anywhere else anytime soon.

translation_en: Sourced from the internet and others: 1. Trevor hates country music, easy listening, and classical music. If you are driving as him and these radio stations come on, he’ll bitch and moan and change the station himself. 2. If Franklin is driving and nobody is in the passenger seat, he can take Chop out for a cruise. 3. While Michael is kidnapped, switching to Trevor will increase the probability of him waking up drunk in some alley or some goddamn weird place. Even though Trevor is full of complaints about Michael, he's the one who truly loves Michael... 4. When stealing cars on the street, Trevor's short temper basically has him elbowing the window out. Franklin is an experienced thief so he has special lock-picking skills. But whether it's smashing the window or triggering a car alarm, the reactions of pedestrians on the street vary: some scream and run away, some take out their phones to take pictures, and others call the cops right away! (You can rush over and punch the guy calling the police, otherwise you'll get a wanted level in a bit). 5. Later in the game, Trevor will encounter a stranger mission on the side of the road—a woman with a hiking backpack talking a bit incoherently and rambling on. Be careful not to take her to the Altruist Cult; take her home instead, and she will become Trevor's regular FwB. You can call her for hookups, and she will occasionally send Trevor a pornographic photo for him to feast his eyes on... 6. When waiting at a red light at an intersection, if there is a car in front of you, you can honk the horn to rush them. Different people have different reactions: some flip you off from inside the car, some get out to curse you out, and timid ones get so scared they just run the red light. The most hardcore ones will get out and pull out a gun to shoot... (NPCs have a breaking point, you know!) 7. You can call the other two protagonists in the game to go out for drinks (or other entertainment) by calling one immediately after the other, otherwise you can only invite one at a time. The lines they have in the car together have a few variations, and they are also different before and after the main storyline is completed. 8. The three of them use phones with different operating systems, which everyone already knows: Michael has iOS (representing the upper class), Franklin has Android (representing the lower-middle class), and Trevor has Windows Phone (representing the 1% of users...). In the next-gen and PC versions, Trevor's phone screen is cracked (Trevor couldn't care less about fixing it). 9. The radio stations in the game will occasionally broadcast breaking news during programs, and the specific content is related to missions you just completed or chaos you just caused in the game... 10. The three protagonists also steal cars on the street differently: Michael sometimes politely asks people to get out of the car; Franklin steadily pulls people out and puts them on the ground; Trevor's hot-headed ass just starts beating them, sometimes shoving their heads into the steering wheel, sometimes dragging them straight out and throwing them on the ground, while mouthing off, "It's just a carjacking!" ================================== 1. If you don't do any inputs in the game, the three of them will have their own habitual movements, like waving their hands or stomping their feet. Only Trevor has the most movements and the most... disgusting ones, like picking his ass and then smelling the hand he just used, or picking his nose and wiping it directly on his clothes... 2. (Continuing from the previous point) If you keep idling, the game will switch to first-person view. At this time, if an attractive woman walks by on the street, you will see the protagonist's gaze follow her closely... 3. Some high-end places in the game won't let a slovenly guy like Trevor through the front door. Once, when switching to Trevor, he was blocked outside the golf course gates and not allowed in. Trevor threw a tantrum and acted like a hoodlum: "I just took a shit in your pool!" 4. It's quite obvious when driving a convertible: when waiting at a red light, if the car radio is playing rock music or something, the protagonist will rock their body to the beat... 5. When walking up to a pedestrian NPC in the game, pressing the right directional button will make you chat them up. Not only are the chat lines different for different NPCs, but their reactions are also different, and certain NPCs will even have special dialogue (like Trevor's sidekick Ron; the two of them will call each other's names in all sorts of ways). 6. Trevor's initial home (yeah, that trailer): there's a canister of "gasoline" by the door. Smelling it every time you go over there will knock Trevor out cold, and then he wakes up somewhere unknown every single time... 7. While Michael's family has run away, Michael will act absent-minded—for example, when coming home he will deliberately shout loudly, "Is anyone home?", or have nightmares alone in bed, or smoke alone by the river wondering what the hell is on his mind... 8. Sometimes when switching to Trevor, you'll find him riding a Faggio scooter on the highway "cruising" with another NPC also riding a Faggio. He'll even refer to themselves as "Faggio brothers." If you keep riding like this the whole way, Trevor has quite a few witty remarks... 9. (Continuing from the previous point) But sometimes when you switch to Trevor, his ass is driving while being wanted by four or five police cars on the highway!!! You can't switch to other characters during a wanted level in the game, so figure out what to do next... (You earned those cops yourself, you gotta tearfully finish them off...) 10. Trevor has a tattoo commemorating Michael... (True love! This is true love!) 11. In the multiplayer heists, you also get to do a heist with Trevor! Trevor once again showcases his bold yet meticulous command skills. Under his plan, you successfully rob a huge batch of drugs, and Trevor "generously" uses his own money to front your cut before the drugs are sold off. It's just that the end of the mission is pretty tragic for Trevor—he falls into a trap set by the cops. Although he narrowly escapes the encirclement, he loses more than he gains, and in the ending screen, he cries so pitifully and miserably that it makes people feel sorry for him... ====== ABOUT THE ENDINGS [SPOILER WARNING] ======= [spoiler] There are three endings: A. Kill Trevor, B. Kill Michael, C. Team up to take down the FIB masterminds [spoiler] Most people choose Ending C, where after the game ends, the three of them live happily ever after (not really). But Endings A and B, though not perfect, are still thrilling. In Ending A, Franklin decides to take out Trevor because even though Trevor is loyal and has off-the-charts combat power, he is extremely prone to emotional loss of control and is a dangerous ticking time bomb that must be eliminated to prevent future trouble. Franklin calls Michael, and Michael (surprisingly) agrees to help out (from this you can tell that Michael is just a mercenary, opportunistic scumbag). They invite Trevor to a secluded spot. Trevor sees through the trick and runs away (probably because he trusted his friends too much, so he didn't make any preparations or carry weapons or anything). Of course, he couldn't outrun Franklin's street-racing skills, and eventually crashes into a fuel tank. Just then, Michael suddenly appears on the scene. In the end, the once-haughty Trevor dies a miserable death in the raging fire. Right before dying, Trevor realizes Michael has betrayed him once again, and lets out a final, miserable and desperate roar in the fire—talk about dying with an unfulfilled grudge... Afterward, Franklin and Michael tearfully (not really) split Trevor's 20-odd million inheritance. In Ending B, Franklin decides to take out Michael. Although Franklin's current soaring success is entirely thanks to Michael bringing him into the game, Michael's treacherous and mercenary scumbag behavior makes Franklin, who always looks out for his bros, hold him in contempt. Franklin calls Trevor, and Trevor flat-out refuses his proposal (talk about true love for Michael! Talk about a stand-up guy!). They invite Michael to a secluded spot, and just as Franklin is about to make a move, Michael gets a call saying his daughter Tracey is going to college. Michael, who has always been troubled by his family, has finally made it through the tough times (his wife is back in his arms, his good-for-nothing son is slowly straightening out, and his daughter, who has always chased overnight celebrity dreams, is going to college). But those good days come to an end right there. Franklin chases Michael all the way up high. During the scuffle, Michael falls over the railing (whether Franklin chooses to let go or pull him up), Michael ultimately plunges to his death, dying no better than Trevor in Ending A. That desperate and angry look right before he dies will probably give Franklin nightmares for the rest of his life... Michael's inheritance ultimately goes to his family, and Franklin ends up abandoned by everyone. No matter whether you choose A or B, you have to personally kill a brother you used to go through thick and thin with, so both of these endings can be considered bad endings, but they are also considered the "true endings" of the game. GTAV is kicked off by Franklin, and in these two endings, the one who survives never pays attention to Franklin again, leaving him all alone to wander through Los Santos by himself. This brilliant legendary underworld tale of Los Santos begins with him and ends with him. GTAV's portrayal of character traits is reflected at all times in various details, and these two endings push the personalities of the three characters to their respective extremes.

translation_en: Man, there are as many ideas of how Grand Theft Auto should be played as there are players in the world. Don't buy the fairy tales that GTA is only there for chasing hookers with a chainsaw — if it were that simple, Saint’s Row would've put Rockstar North out of business long ago. In Grand Theft Auto V, you'll be watching cartoons and doing yoga. You'll also have to kill and rob, but not by choice. Namaste. Happiness generator As is well known, the fourth and fifth GTAs take place in a new reality where there was no Claude, no Tommy Vercetti, and no Carl Johnson. It turned out pretty much like J.J. Abrams’ Star Trek reboot or comic book series reboots: the names are the same, the places are the same, but everything else is different. That's why returning to Los Santos is somewhat disorienting. Remade for a new generation, the city has kept some external features, but overall it has become completely unfamiliar. For example, of the old Grove Street, where Carl Johnson and his gang lived according to the story of San Andreas, only a musty little yard remains, and its former inhabitants as if never even existed. Now the purple Ballas live here, and if you manage to show up here on foot, the whole neighborhood will jump you. An entire era of San Andreas history has simply been erased, and the state itself rebuilt from scratch. Out of the three cities, only Los Santos remains, but it has transformed and expanded so much that it actually feels like a real city. ► The new Los Santos is arguably even more confusing than the new Liberty City. The GPS navigator will be your best friend both in the city and beyond. The entire area (the city itself is the size of the new Liberty City from GTA IV, plus the surrounding countryside twice that size) is, for once, open from the very beginning: no excuses like "the bridges are closed due to a terrorist threat." And everywhere, absolutely everywhere, you can stumble upon something interesting. Every single second, something is happening somewhere. This isn't just set dressing (since you can intervene in any random event), nor is it a Potemkin village built specially for you — Los Santos gets along just fine on its own. GTA is no longer just a territory you have to drive across from point to point for the sake of the story, occasionally breaking for mass murder if you get bored. Rockstar, having walked the thorny path of evolution, has achieved an almost ideal game space, creating a real ecosystem with almost no rules and conventions. And on top of that, it's very beautiful and cozy. Never before has it been so pleasant just to drive down the highway in GTA. Some Gerry Rafferty is playing on the radio, cars rush past in a solid stream, trees and some shacks blur by, the sunset peeks out from behind the mountains, the car bounces on road bumps, and you feel like you can even sense the wind resistance — not a game, but a happiness generator. The last time it felt like this was in last year's sunny Forza Horizon, but that's still a narrowly specialized racing game. So you could say GTA V has no competition when it comes to generating happiness. Franklin is your typical righteous "nigga," with a clear system of values and a hyper-inflated sense of gang loyalty. He is young, inexperienced, but surprisingly sensible, steals cars to order, and dreams of hitting a big score. He doesn't like to take unnecessary risks, but for friends, he's ready for anything. Michael is a seasoned bank robber who has retired and lost himself at the bottom of a bottle. Unlike the previous protagonists, he has long settled into adult life: a mansion in Vinewood, a garage full of cars, an unhappy wife, a daughter hanging out with porn moguls and lustful showmen, and a post-pubescent son who does nothing but smoke weed, troll people online, and play the local equivalent of Call of Duty. And Trevor... Trevor is just a psycho (he's even got paperwork to prove it). He lives in a dirty trailer, cooks meth, yells profanities for no reason at all, wipes out bikers, and at the first opportunity — punches people in the face (and women, women too!). Completely out of control, insolent, quarrelsome, and socially dangerous. Everything best from the previous parts is in GTA V, and most of the series' standard flaws have been gotten rid of, even if sometimes not in the most elegant way. More jokes, more sun, more possibilities, more living world. More pleasure. Just a little bit more — and it would be perfection. My rating: 9.5/10

translation_en: GTA5 and GTAOL are great games, but Rockstar is a piece of shit company. Why am I complaining like this? Because of their ban system. Quite a few friends have been speculating about how the GTAOL ban system works. So let's briefly analyze the various theories: Theory 1: Players get banned because the PC they use to play the game has pirated game files or residual trainer DLLs, which get detected as abnormal data. Case analysis: Quite a few friends switched from pirated versions to legitimate ones. Because the game download is 60GB, and internet speeds in some parts of China are still pretty bad, some players directly imported the pirated files into Steam. I'd say this theory is about 40% credible, but there are still some players who imported pirated files and are playing happily. Even worse are the rumors that if you've ever played any pirated game or used a trainer, any residual DLL files left on your PC will be detected. I completely scoff at this because they don't have the right to scan your entire hard drive; they can only scan DLL files related to critical game files. Of course, if your trainer or pirated game was infected with a virus or bundled with adware that tries to modify critical DLLs on its own and you get banned, you can't blame them (so just support legitimate copies). Anyway, better safe than sorry (after all, you gotta take responsibility for what you pay for). Within ten days of a ban, you might as well back up important files, reinstall the OS, clean up your computer, and format the hard drive. Credibility: ★★★ Theory 2: Data anomalies caused by using a VPN, leading to frequent IP address changes during login. Case analysis: Two of my friends have been playing Steam games using VPNs for years, and their GTAOL ranks are both in the 200s or 300s. And when I got banned, I was running the exact same VPN as them. Doesn't this clearly mean it's not the VPN's fault? Credibility: ★ Theory 3 (Hard facts): Save file errors caused by network issues. Case analysis: GTAOL's save system keeps one copy of the save on your local machine and another on the server. When logging in and during gameplay, the game automatically uploads the local save to the server for comparison. Because of the Great Firewall, many players have pretty bad internet. Sometimes the save upload fails, meaning the server can't sync your local save. At some point, your network suddenly gets better for a second, and your local save gets uploaded to the server. The server compares it and goes, "How the hell did you suddenly get so much money and cars? You must have used a glitch or third-party money drop, banned!" And just like that, you're banned. What the fuck, this isn't my fault, why do I have to take the fall?! But oh well, what can you do when their only response is those six magic words [T/N: referring to Rockstar's automated support replies]. Therefore, we just gotta do our part and buy a VPN—you're gonna need one for Steam games sooner or later anyway. When the game prompts a save sync error, just quietly log off and wait until your internet is good again before logging back in. Trying to force a login is just pushing your luck. Also, newbies shouldn't jump straight into Pacific Standard; ranking up and making money is fast, and playing with homies is fun, but having an email pop up in the bottom right corner of your screen while you're having a good time is a huge buzzkill. For now, just stick to contact missions and read up on newbie guides written by veterans. Credibility: ★★★★★ Theory 4: Rockstar is racist. Case analysis: Quite a few friends said that right after their 10-day ban was up, they changed their nationality flag to the Stars and Stripes, and then went back to playing happily. (WTF?) But to be fair, this wave of mass bans mainly hit players with five-star red flags next to their names. Whether it's an issue of player behavior actually crossing the line, or genuine racism, we have no way of knowing. But racism is pretty damn obvious in the GTA universe—Michael and Trevor can carry four to five thousand rounds of ammo, while Franklin only gets four to five hundred. As for whether Rockstar is objectively reflecting racism or holds those views themselves, I'll leave that for you guys to decide. Credibility: ○○○○○ Theory 5: Settling scores after the fact. Case analysis: Rockstar's game system relies on save synchronization. Whatever shady shit you pulled in the past thinking you got away with it, who knows, maybe they found out about it later. To this I just say: you totally fucking deserve it! Do whatever you want to your own single-player game, but if you bring that toxic bullshit into multiplayer, getting permanently banned is fully justified. In public lobbies, you still see Chinese players shouting "Can someone drop me some money?" You're humiliating Chinese gamers in front of the whole world. Please, if you're gonna say that shit in English, at least more people will understand it. Stop using Chinese, stop making us look like clowns. Credibility: THREE STARS So those are the five main theories going around right now. All in all, some of these bullshit bans are genuinely not our fault, but right now, compared to Rockstar, we players are at a disadvantage. If you can't change the environment, change yourself. During this wave of bans, those of you with bad luck should just lay low for a bit. Writing all this is basically just trying to minimize the risk of getting banned. Finally, a specialty from the Heavenly Empire: Resist bad games, reject pirated games. Practice self-protection, beware of scams and swindlers. Moderate gaming stimulates the brain, excessive gaming harms the body. Manage your time wisely, enjoy a healthy lifestyle.

Who the fuck comes up with the brain-dead decision to make the PC online experience absolute garbage and essentially herd players online? Shows what kind of amateur company you fucking are when it comes to running [PC Online], leaving a mountain of issues unresolved and just pressing on anyway. R.I.P. OpenIV. At this point, GTAV story mode is [strike]NO Mod[/strike] and online mode is a complete fucking mess. July 15, 2016 Review: The company's current attitude toward PC online players: "If the ruler wants you dead, you have to die." Even if you play by the rules, obey the law, keep a low profile, and run an honest game, it doesn't fucking matter. The moment that piece-of-shit garbage anti-cheat detection system flags you, your online privileges get restricted. There's a 3-strike limit: 10 days for the first, 30 days for the second, and permanent for the third. Once you get flagged the first time, there's a huge chance you'll get hit a second and third time. After a ban, your online character data gets completely wiped and reset to zero. And no matter how you contact customer support, all you ever get back is a dead, automated canned response. I just love fair game, I very hate cheats, but FYRS banned me from gta online for no reason!!! If you genuinely love the game and only want to play single-player on PC, it's still somewhat recommended. If you genuinely love the game and are mainly looking for the online experience, please click the [←] in the top left or the _□[Ｘ] in the top right of your browser to leave this page, and buy a console instead—either a PS4 or an Xbox One. If you don't own either, you'll need to go out and buy one of those home consoles. I've been a law-abiding PC player for over a year. 730 hours? Yeah, that's my playtime, because I work days and go to school at night. Knowing public sessions are full of hackers, I always stayed strictly in invite-only sessions. If friends tried to drag me into a public session and I refused, risking falling out with them over it, I'd rather sever ties than touch that goddamn risk. From April through June of this year, seeing more and more false ban reports pop up, I made sure my game folder stayed completely clean every time before going online. Recently, with the Summer Sale, a friend finally got the game so we could play together. On the early morning of 6/25, we played around for two, three hours in an invite-only session, went to sleep, and woke up around noon to check my email. Found out I got slapped with a random 10-day ban. I was completely baffled—I played strictly by the book, so why the fuck was I banned? Naturally, I contacted support and instantly got hit with a canned response. Before the ban lifted on 7/6, I completely deleted the game, reinstalled it fresh, and shut down as many background processes in Task Manager as possible just to avoid getting banned again. After the ban lifted on 7/6, I played with my friend for a few more days, doing some minor work and the simple Fleeca Job heist. On the night of 7/12, I came home and couldn't even connect online. The error kept blocking me: "GTA Online session failed to sync catalog data with server." Lost a whole day because of that bullshit. Later on the night of 7/13, I saw on the Bahamut forums that changing your IPv4 DNS to a static IP (209.244.0.3, 209.244.0.4) finally let you log into a private friend session smoothly. Logging on that night, I saw the new vehicle update, so I figured I'd join a random group to grind out the Pacific Standard heist for some extra cash. The heist leader was solid and gave me a 40% cut. The team coordination and chemistry felt great, giving me a real sense of accomplishment. That finally pushed my level 169 character's savings up to over 965,000—one step closer to buying a new car. Right after finishing it, I went back to the invite-only session to mess around with my friend, driving all over the map. Mid-session, a prompt popped up: banned until 8/12. Hit with a second ban for absolutely no fucking reason. I just stared at that warning screen in a daze for a full minute. My game folder was completely clean. There is literally no combination of keys I could possibly press while playing that would violate any GTAO rules. Where the fuck are the game company's ban criteria? PC players have to play by the rules while walking on eggshells, terrified of getting banned. When legitimate players get banned, they don't get a single fucking explanation, and when you report it to customer support, you just get an instant canned response closing the ticket, treating PC users like absolute fucking idiots. Thank god I hadn't bought a Shark Card to stock up on in-game money for cars before my first ban on 6/25! I've been playing for over a year, why the fuck would I even need to cheat? Exactly. The way these engineers designed this detection program is just based on rigid code to decide if a player is cheating. At this point, I can only say that these anti-cheat programmers aren't putting enough effort into fixing the bugs in their own software, resulting in a bunch of innocent PC players getting screwed over. The core game itself easily scores a 10/10, absolute perfection. But the scumbag engineers who wrote this piece-of-shit detection system and the robotic corporate attitude get a zero from me. And sending you all the way back to your 18th-generation ancestors with some passionate Taiwanese Hokkien curses would still be letting you off easy! You fucking morons think you can write a detection system once and never have to check or update it again? Are you seriously sure a garbage standard detection system written once has zero issues? Why do operating systems need frequent updates for security flaws? Why do computer hardware drivers and all kinds of software need updates? Why do phone apps need updates? No antivirus software is 100% complete and perfect; every single one of them throws false positives sometimes, which is why antivirus software is constantly updated. Software like this isn't something you just write once and it's fine forever—you update it precisely *because* there are vulnerabilities! I remember back in June 2014 when you guys were preparing to release the PC version. You should have had the mental preparedness to deal with online cheaters and modders on PC. If you're going to half-ass your measures for the PC online version, you shouldn't just completely abandon it, and then quietly pick off random innocent PC online players starting in 2016 to squeeze out some extra cash. And then you aggressively slap a second ban on players who've already been banned once. Why? Could it be because your detector found some anime doujins and porn on the user's computer, so you decided to ban them a second time? If that's how it is, you should've just kept it exclusive to consoles instead of scamming people by releasing a PC version. If you can't handle the fucking heat, stay out of the kitchen. This is no way to handle things. Honestly, even if I had a console and a GTAV disc sitting right in front of me right now, I wouldn't even want to play it. Fuck you, Rockstar. o_O The game company used to actually listen to player feedback last year, but now they just send automated replies. Witnessing history: the absolute shittiest anti-cheat detection system ever made, paired with the most irresponsible corporate attitude. FYRS!

translation_en: WARNING! This review only applies to the current version of GTA Online. If you're thinking about buying the game just to play the single-player campaign by yourself, or at absolute worst, the co-op heists with 4 friends — it's a thumbs up, hard as a petrified mammoth's dick. So let's begin. When the game first hit our wonderful platform — the online was intriguing, because let's be honest, it's a AAA game with free DLCs! And what DLCs they were! Heists, one of the best co-op modes I've seen in gaming, especially since I played them with friends. Varied, with single-player campaign-level production values, demanding teamwork, and mostly unique objectives for each player. Just awesome. And so, sucked into this swamp, playing heists over and over, I waited for more. But it never came. Car packs came out, useless modes and tons of clothes came out, the game started getting boring. And then, lo and behold, they announced a freemode expansion, with missions for the whole lobby and stuff like that. Turned out to be complete bullshit. Boring events like "deploy your parachute last," plus broken by cheaters (more on that later). Then came the update with bikers and more meaningful freemode missions, a bunch of adversary modes nobody asked for, and the quintessence of Rockstar's total misunderstanding of their own game's concept and target audience — Further Adventures in Finance and Felony (what a fucking name, wow). And here's the problem. All these troubles stem from three things: 1) The DLCs are free, so the game's main monetization right now is selling shark cards for in-game cash. The game literally feels like a f2p grinder. Maximum money payout is about 20k every 10-15 minutes. 100k an hour. To buy a single decent supercar you need to spend 20-25 hours of pure grinding on the same missions, boring ones in a closed lobby or "fun" ones in an open lobby where you can safely divide the payouts by 2 or 3, but we'll get to that. Every new DLC eats money like there's no tomorrow, the game is designed so that you're always dropping a shitload of cash on who-knows-what, with no option for even a 5-minute trial. You can't even look inside an apartment before buying it. Basically, a normal person won't touch even half the features unless they buy microtransactions or cheat. Or beg hackers to drop them money, which is what the bums in the chat constantly cry about. 2) The latest DLC was forcefully shoved into open lobbies. And here's what happens. You, in a group of maximum 4 people, are doing your missions. 26 (!) other people in the city see a huge-ass notification telling them to ruin your day. In the end, it all turns into pure madness. Real-life example: you need to deliver a truck with a trailer from the port out of town. 2 Hydras fly in, 5 Insurgents with machine guns drive up, a couple more guys run over with rocket launchers, the truck gets blown up. Someone brings a new one — it gets blown up. After dying, everyone respawns right across the street. Fun? Hell yeah. And it's like this constantly. You simply have no way to get rid of other players. Unless you search for a dead lobby where everyone doesn't give a fuck about you, or there are just few enough people that you can fight back. Against two Hydras that will show up in a minute. Fuck, even in Battlefield vehicle respawns take longer than that! I should also clarify — you can not only lose what you've earned because of other players, but actually go into the negative. So this is no longer fucking GTA. It's some kind of absolute fuckery and bacchanalia. It's an alien invasion simulator in LA; the only thing missing is a flying Tony Stark, he'd fit right into the atmosphere of the hell happening in open lobbies. And all this with zero balance, shitty netcode, and... 3) ...cheaters. There are more of them here than regular players. After a patch, there are always a couple of days while the kids wait for cheat updates when you can play in peace. A couple of days later, the lobbies get even "funnier." Because cheaters here can: be godmode, blow up everyone on the server, turn players into objects, forcefully drop money on you (by the way, you'll get banned for 2 weeks for that), lag the lobby down to 1-2 fps, and a bunch of other cool stuff. And most importantly, these aren't paid subscription cheats. These are public script hooks that any kid can download with a Google search. No registration or SMS required. To sum it all up. I would gladly pay another 2,000 for a season pass, even 3,000. But for good, unique content, for a normal economy without grinding, for an anti-cheat, for the things I'm used to in AAA games. The gameplay itself is gorgeous, no matter how you spin it, but it's draped in f2p trash designed to suck out your money, nerves, and time. Grind millions just to grind millions. Pay money to get fucked over ©

translation_en: [h1][b]A true gift from Rockstar to its fans![/b][/h1] Grand Theft Auto V, a third-person action game set in an incredible open world. Developed and published by Rockstar Games. Released in September 2013 for Xbox 360 and PS3, getting a remastered version in November 2014 for XOne and PS4, and finally arriving on PCs in April 2015. In the plot, we are introduced to three protagonists: Michael and Trevor, two old friends who used to rob banks together in the past, and Franklin, a young member of the Grove Street gang—yes, the very same one from classic San Andreas. The three characters team up, living through countless situations involving the mafia, the FBI, heists, car thefts, and even movie production, in the gorgeous and revitalized Los Santos. It maintains the narrative quality expected from Rockstar, with plot twists, charismatic characters, violence, and a whole lot of action. For the first time in a GTA series game, we have the opportunity to control three protagonists, each with their own narrative arc that intertwine to develop an even bigger plot, and Rockstar somehow manages to develop all three characters in a very well-balanced way. First, we have Michael, a retired criminal who theoretically "made it" in life, living in a mansion with his wife and kids, but who finds himself in a crisis upon realizing he's failed as a father and husband, finding a way to vent all his frustration by returning to crime. Second, we have Franklin, an ambitious young man who realizes his gang's petty crimes won't get him anywhere and, upon meeting Michael, sees an opportunity to achieve his goals. Finally, we have Trevor, an insane, sadistic, and violent character, but one who exhibits a certain code of ethics that makes him one of the most charismatic characters in the entire franchise. Undeniably, Rockstar uses the exact same formula as their previous games, featuring criminals who aren't exactly villains, who are "forced" to return to the criminal underworld and get themselves into even bigger trouble. However, the developer manages to make their stories engaging and memorable, with charismatic characters and grand conclusions. It's impossible not to get caught up in Michael's family dramas, or Trevor's madness, or even to hate the corrupt FBI agents who screw the protagonists over at every turn. And if that weren't enough, aside from the main plot, there are dozens of side stories, like the "Strangers and Freaks" missions, that make the game even more immersive. GTA V's plot alone is worth the experience, but the game reaches a greater dimension due to the sheer amount of content on offer. First, we have a gigantic map featuring not only urban areas but also rural areas, mountains, rivers, and deserts, all of them with incredible life and simply stunning visuals. The rain, the sunset, sunny days—everything is presented with impeccable graphic quality that impresses even on the lowest settings. It's almost impossible not to stop at least once to admire the sunset from atop a mountain, or watch the moonlight reflect on the ocean water. On top of that, the gigantic map is crammed with countless activities. The player can take part in off-road, street, and even jet ski races; play sports like golf, tennis, or even triathlons; go to the movies, play darts, or do yoga; complete parachute jump challenges or airplane stunt challenges; customize their vehicles; and still spend hours exploring the map to find collectibles ranging from murder clues to pieces of a possible UFO. Basically, it's endless content that guarantees a significant boost to the game's lifespan. The gameplay remains very similar to the previous game, with a significant improvement to the cover system and the excellent addition of special abilities for each protagonist. While Trevor can take more damage, Michael can slow down time in true Max Payne style, and Franklin slows down time while driving vehicles, making getaways and chases much easier. Each of these abilities is used to great effect during the campaign and adds a fresh feel to the gameplay. Another point that was noticeably improved is vehicle handling, which now feels much easier to control, making the gameplay way more intuitive and enjoyable. In terms of customization, the game brings back features from previous games. Now we can once again heavily customize the protagonists' appearance with haircuts, tattoos, and clothes. Furthermore, vehicles and even weapons can be modified with a wide range of customization options, further boosting the sense of freedom. And as if the already massive single-player mode wasn't enough, we have the multiplayer mode, which gives the player even more freedom by allowing them to create a unique character who arrives in Los Santos to make a name for themselves in the criminal underworld. GTA Online includes everything the single-player mode offers and goes beyond, featuring new heist missions and diverse game modes, favoring not only traditional competitive matches but also players who just want to have fun with friends. It's almost like a game of its own, and the best part is that the Online mode receives constant updates to this day, always with new content and game modes. One important thing to note is the excellent optimization the game received on PC. Even on a quite modest machine running everything on minimum settings, I got great results, with the game running very fluidly and a constant framerate above 30 fps. This was a pleasant surprise since GTA IV had a miserable and lamentable port. Rockstar learned its lesson, made the two-year wait worth it, and delivered an excellent PC version. Grand Theft Auto V is an outstanding game that manages to extremely competently expand everything best about the franchise's history. With a great plot, three extremely strong and engaging protagonists, and a ton of content that appeals to all types of players—not to mention the Online mode, which is practically another game inside the game itself. GTA V is as grand as the franchise's fans could have ever wanted, and we will be eternally grateful to Rockstar for gifting us this unforgettable game. [i]"I feel like I can't kill both of them." - Franklin[/i] [b]Additional information:[/b] Overall rating: 10. Time dedicated to the game: 160 hours. Achievements unlocked: 38 out of 68. Difficulty: Moderate, neither hard nor easy, just right, guaranteeing both challenge and fun. Tip: Simply get lost in Los Santos. Gameplay: [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/luishq2010] Coming soon. [/url] Screenshots during gameplay: [url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/luishq/screenshots/?appid=271590&sort=newestfirst&browsefilter=myfiles&view=imagewall] Click here. [/url] Is it worth the price? Yes, buy it with or without a discount, it's worth every penny. Game mode: Singleplayer and multiplayer. Language: In English, with PT-BR subtitles. translation_en: [spoiler] Got no games to play so I'm writing a review instead. Fuck. [/spoiler] I knew I'd have to write a review for GTA5 someday, just didn't think it'd be this soon (originally planned to do it after 1000+ hours, but looks like that's not happening). GTA—Chinese names include Grand Theft Auto, Grand Theft Auto, Auto Thief, Grand Theft Auto, Wild Driving... call it whatever you like. Not just for me, this series probably has the biggest impact on most players, right? So I can't just slap this review together. Let's break it down into three parts? [h1] Compared to previous titles [/h1] Some people say it's not as fun as San Andreas or Vice City. Are you fucking stupid? You're all grown up now, understand? Why don't you go play San Andreas for 500 hours right now and see how that goes? The only thing GTA5 fails to beat is GTA4's story, even though GTA4's mid-game plot was also an absolute mess. But GTA4's immersion and character writing brilliantly satirized the unreality of the American Dream. Liberty City, overflowing with greed and corruption, makes you feel the helplessness of dreams getting slapped in the face by reality. Even though GTA4's optimization still sucks balls today, and Rockstar still hasn't gotten rid of GFWL, but... Goddammit, aren't I talking about GTA5? Anyway, as the greatest game series of this century, I have every reason to believe Rockstar has handed in a satisfactory answer sheet. [h1] Single-player [/h1] Since everyone's already familiar with the story of the three guys and a dog, I won't bore you with the details. The replayability should be extremely high. Believe it or not, I can spend all day just pressing Spacebar and R (PC controls)? I seem to remember vaguely that Rockstar said they were going back to San Andreas's variety. Clothes and car modding go without saying—even electric bikes can get turbochargers now, and I'm pretty sure no other game has the balls to do that. Apparently, someone vaguely mentioned being able to change body types, right? Don't you dare tell me adding a few stat numbers counts as changing body types. I really wanted to see a big-fat-belly Trevor and a skin-and-bones Michael, fuck! Goddamn it, I forgot about mods. The single-player alone is worth the ticket price. Rockstar, why the hell did you have to go and make a frustrating-ass online mode? [h1] Online [/h1] Without a doubt, all the negative reviews are because of Online—and of course the people who can't even launch the game. Have some mercy, guys. It was Rockstar's first time making a large-scale online game—that's what people on Tieba were saying when it first launched. After all, I spent 500 hours hanging out in the sky (loading screens), got ripped off on missions where I didn't get paid, and on top of that, the network I used most for GTA5 was campus Wi-Fi. I probably don't even need to mention how shitty the network was. If! If anyone still wants to play Online, take my advice: get a paid VPN/accelerator, it should fix most of your problems. Cheats I admit it, I used cheats. Spare me and don't drag me through the mud! I was in the second wave of bans! After that, I never cheated again! I can post my gaming resume right here: GTAOL Level 1–20: Constantly getting griefed by people with SMGs, getting hunted down by NPCs while trying to grind missions in online lobbies, scraping my way to level 20 with no house and no car. GTAOL Level 20–40: Bought an Armored Kuruma, started soloing some minor missions, slowly got the hang of it, and sometimes rolled out into the streets in the Kuruma to slaughter noobs. GTAOL Level 40–70: Could no longer farm cash from tiny little missions, so I decided to just find random people to do Heists with. From Prison Break, Humane Labs, Series A to Pacific Standard, I ground out the progression step by step, and met one of my future Criminal Mastermind teams... Ko... forgot the name...(*/ω＼*) GTAOL Level 70–97: The golden age of my online playtime. Formed my own heist crew with three other people, conquered the hardest heist missions, had Kuruma shootouts in free roam, and drove up Mount Chiliad just to look at the scenery when we were bored... "Hey, let's do Criminal Mastermind together?" "Hell yeah, when are you free?"... A few young guys, tempted by the 10 million payout of Mastermind, started the journey of tackling the hardest challenges in Online. translation_en: A year ago, I came to this prosperous and beautiful city—Los Santos. Here I met Franklin, a neighborhood youth riding a Bati motorcycle and taking Chop out for a spin. Michael, a veteran criminal sitting at home peacefully watching TV with his kids. And Trevor, a lunatic with a hangover on top of a mountain, wearing a women's slip dress. Remember when you were collecting trash in Funding The Riot and getting hunted down by gangsters? Remember when the heist leader drove an Armored Kuruma in The Pacific Standard to help you make your getaway? It's been a year, and I've already left this city with my friends. Goodbye, familiar yet stranger city—Los Santos.

translation_en: I've played for around 100-something hours, so let me quickly share my thoughts on this game. Players who haven't bought it yet, look over here; those who already bought it don't need me to say much. This is actually a pretty good game in all aspects. It's an open world with no loading screens or waiting times. But the operators are a bunch of incompetent, trigger-happy retards. Why do I say that? A few days ago my account suddenly got banned for 10 days (from April 30, 2016 to May 9, 2016). Since I couldn't play on my own account after the ban, I started playing on my friend's account. The day I logged on, I was playing in a public session the whole time, and then I ran into a cheater. My character was in the garage and suddenly couldn't move, then water spouts randomly burst out of the ground, then I got burned by fire, then my character got teleported to another place, got hit by water spouts again, burned by fire, and then died. Feeling like it was pointless, another friend and I teamed up to do the only mission of that night. When using auto-invite for the team, we got matched with a level 36 player who was carrying a minigun that you can only buy at level 120. Drawing from my experience with my previous account getting banned, I took screenshots right then and there to keep as evidence. As a result, the next day, the friend's account I was playing on got banned, and the friend I teamed up with got banned too. Then I started appealing to Rockstar and attached the screenshots. But the result was the same as how my own account was handled—they completely ignore whatever actually happened to you. I wrote countless appeal tickets in both English and Chinese, and they were all the exact same canned response. Rockstar's way of dealing with cheaters is: As long as a cheater throws money at you, sorry, account banned. If a cheater participates in a mission through auto-invite or auto-matchmaking, sorry, account banned. If you want to kill people and go to a public session, and someone uses cheats, sorry, every single player in that session gets banned. Rockstar lacks the ability to properly investigate, so they just use a scattershot approach against cheaters and take down normal players right along with them. It would be fine if they actually got the cheaters too. But the real situation is that normal players get banned, and as I'm writing this review, cheaters are still online killing people like crazy. This makes my brain hurt trying to figure out what kind of detection system Rockstar even has. Whether it's the official Rockstar forums or the Steam community, players from all countries first tried appealing in broken English, and when they realized English appeals were useless, every language under the sun came out. I honestly have no idea how many languages Rockstar's customer support speaks. Even if Rockstar's support is fluent in every language, Rockstar still has this attitude of "my game is amazing, if we banned your account we banned your account, take it or leave it," knowing full well that once your account gets banned, you'll just go buy a second one anyway. If anyone who hasn't bought this game still wants to buy it, or if anyone whose account got banned still wants to buy a second one, add me as a friend and let's talk about life. Update (May 10, 2016) My account got unbanned at around 2 AM on May 10. Right after getting unbanned, I immediately logged back in to play in a session. When I noticed people in this session chatting, saying, "Can you give me some more money?", I realized someone was modding money. So I hopped in my Hydra and went to find these guys by the beach. Of course, I was up in the sky. Then, when I came back after opening my video recording software, I found a bunch of money bags piled up on my plane (while I was still in the sky—smh). So I started recording their money-modding process. While I was recording, the plane I was driving—even in passive mode—got blown up out of nowhere, and I died. After respawning, I checked and saw my money hadn't increased at all, so I safely logged off, planning to send the video to official support. But because it was too late, I stopped sending it and decided to send it after I woke up. The crazy thing is, around 10 AM, I logged on again and found out my account got banned once more. How amazing is that, truly fucking amazing. Rockstar, a whole-ass company, is worse than a cheat developer—they manage to ban innocent players while the actual cheaters get to keep playing.

translation_en: The first few hours, or rather about 20-30 hours, Rockstar's work blows your mind – the level of detail and scale is off the charts. It's no joke – a full-fledged mega-city with skyscrapers, alleys, suburbs, a port, an airport. But wait, there's more – the territory of the entire island features deserts, mountains, forests, small provincial towns, military bases, the ocean, wind turbines, radio telescopes. At night, standing on a mountain, you look into the distance – and Los Santos is shimmering with myriads of lights, a stream of cars endlessly moving along the highway, the Moon reflecting on the water's surface, and in the distance a storm is gathering or the Sun is getting ready to peer over the horizon. In short, visually and technically the game is striking, generating hundreds of breathtaking landscapes or massive urban panoramas. The story features three main protagonists – Michael, Franklin, and Trevor, whom you can freely switch between. The overall plot revolves around these characters interacting to solve their problems and raise hell across the state. Because back in the day, these guys were a skilled bank-robbing gang. But the past won't let go. Out of all the GTA games, this one has the most cohesive and consistent plot, with very solid directing. A multitude of diverse, unique missions contributes to this. The heists stand out in particular – there are setup phases where we choose the approach for the heists, recruit a crew, and prepare gear. Then come the heists themselves, directed to all Hollywood standards in the spirit of Michael Mann's movie "Heat". The added first-person mode does a great job of enhancing immersion. This mode isn't just tacked on, and gunfights in it feel like a normal first-person shooter, with cool guns and reload animations. Driving cars is also thoroughly adapted for this mode. It's fun to cruise around the night city – you feel like a badass driver, just like in Winding Refn's movie "Drive". Rounding out this monstrously detailed picture of everything and anything are such "small touches" as television, with its own channels and real shows. Very funny shows, I might add. And the internet, which you can surf for hours. Or going to the movies, where they show both art-house films and blockbusters. And nobody forces this on you – you can play the whole game without even knowing all this stuff is in there. And that's not even all – there's also a well-developed multiplayer that is constantly expanding. Dozens of engaging modes and activities, cooperative and unique online heists with their own story and cutscenes. The game is truly rich in content and possibilities, and you'd think, here it is, the game of your dreams. But no, we must mention the flaws that really ruined the aftertaste. The game has a disgusting ending. It feels like the head of the studio walked in and said – "Wrap it up, we're going gold next week." The finale is so abrupt and rushed – it's like speeding down the highway in a sports car and suddenly hitting a concrete wall! You have to ask, what the hell did the main protagonists suffer through a good half of the game for, if all their problems could be solved just like that, out of nowhere. Boom, and it's over! Totally disappointing, no doubt about it. Also, starting from the second half of the game, I clearly started noticing that the game desperately lacks difficulty. Catastrophically so. It's like playing on very easy. Why couldn't they include a difficulty setting? But hardcore gamers weren't considered – all problems are solved almost with your eyes closed. There is no feeling that you pulled off a genuinely risky job – everything happens too fast, missions are short, there are no challenges at all. Balance clearly wasn't a priority – a bunch of guns, but what's the point if you can wipe out crowds of enemies left and right with even the starting pistol? I really missed long, intense firefights. Just as you get into the shooting groove – the action sequence is already over. The plot, for all its initial appeal, loses steam and depth in the second half, heading toward the finale on autopilot, and I already wrote about the finale. Meaning, the overall impression of the story got smeared and it turned into a forgettable filler. You won't remember it as a benchmark for good gaming stories. So, Rockstar still has room to improve. At the same time, it's hard not to appreciate the titanic amount of work put into the game. Therefore, despite the significant flaws, you remember the many dozens of pleasant hours, the sea of details and content. So, 9/10. I couldn't bring myself to give it any less. But there's definitely room to grow and things to fix.

translation_en: After more than 650 hours of playtime I feel I have to leave a review for this game (pros, cons and finally a short summary of what I think about it). PROS: - Very good optimization and a solid port, good graphics (though they don't rival brand new games) - An open world where you really can do whatever you want - An interesting and pretty cool single-player story - Long lifespan (almost infinite with online, otherwise for solo: 15/20 hours rushing, 50/60 hours for 100%) - A world packed with tons of details and pretty well-hidden Easter eggs - Heists, whether in online or solo, are really cool - A wide variety of weapons (around 50) - Mods Online mode: - All the perks of solo play but with your friends, so a lot of good laughs - Lots of customization options (varying in price) - Loads of updates, about one every month CONS: - Missions are often set up in a "go from point A to point B, then cutscene" style - Loading times Online mode: - The game's economy is way too expensive. VERY VERY VERY long to get rich in the game (10 million = about 50 hours of gameplay), with 6 million being the price of the low-end yacht, so I'll let you do the math. But why is that? Well, so you'll buy rather pricey Shark Cards—75 euros (more than the price of the game itself) for 8 million in online. - Uninteresting missions with not much of a story in online - PvP is unequally balanced based on player level; a player level 120+ has a huge advantage in their weapons (especially the heavy sniper, which one-shots levels 1 to 100, and the minigun) and health compared to level 90 and under. - Passive mode needs to be reworked; players abuse it by toggling passive on and off just to backstab you and leave you unable to retaliate. - Modders/hackers—on this point I'll explain: basically, you can get more or fewer modders depending on the time period. You find tons of them during those damn Jordan mod updates (it's the most well-known but there are others) until Rockstar drops a minor update (sometimes invisible) to fight the new mod version (and ban the cheat users). However, between the time the mod update drops and Rockstar steps in, online is infested with modders (almost impossible to play without running into a godmode guy who teleports, kills everyone, etc.). Outside of those windows, there are either no modders in online or very few (the ones you see during quiet periods usually get banned instantly). To wrap up on this point, you just have to learn to live with these fucking hackers and whatever new features they come up with. - No private server system where you could play with mods with your buddies, which is a real shame. We could have seen RP mods pop up, for example. To me, GTA V is a game everyone should play at least once in their life; it's a very good AAA title. Despite a few flaws, it hits the spot when you don't know what to do, whether you're playing alone or with friends. It's better suited for casual gamers, but you can tryhard it if you care about your K/D ratio, getting gold medals on solo missions, or doing the Criminal Mastermind heist challenge (which is genuinely difficult and meant for the best players). For me, the biggest con of this game (aside from the modders) is the online economy—it's impossible to make massive amounts of money, whether easily or grinding hard (aside from the Mastermind challenge which gives 10 million, but you can only do it once). NB: Someone's still gonna have to explain to me why modders actually enjoy going around killing everyone in godmode on an endless loop.

translation_en: As a player with over 2,000 hours, I feel like I'm finally qualified to review this game a little bit. Anyone who says the game is absolute garbage with less than 500 hours, or trashes it just because they got banned for their own stupid reasons, is being completely biased. First off, GTA V is an incredible game, whether you're a veteran of the GTA series or a total newbie who's never touched this kind of game before. It's modeled after Los Angeles and recreates it with incredible detail (since a lot of things in GTA are parodies, many elements like cars, place names, or landmarks have their own twist added, sometimes fusing two cars into a brand new one). The biggest impression it left on me is that GTA V finally added a first-person perspective. Being able to use first-person especially when driving cars and flying planes makes it totally worth playing for a lot of people. GTA V is split into single-player and online modes. Single-player is different from past GTA games or other RPGs (like Assassin's Creed) because you cycle between three protagonists, and many missions require you to constantly switch between all three to complete them—which is a pretty cool innovation. The offline mode is super detailed, with way too many small touches to list out one by one, you just have to experience them yourself. For example: a pedestrian crashes their car into a utility pole, it falls down and can literally crush you to death; if a car engine takes a heavy hit, it blows up, and so on. Plus, offline mode has a lot more mysterious stuff than past games, like aliens, the three cults corresponding to the three protagonists (especially the Epsilon Program for Michael), and cryptic symbols written on Mount Chiliad that still haven't been properly solved to this day (almost 4 years later). Then they added GTA Online, which is the main reason GTA V is so popular. Online mode is a whole different experience—exploring Los Santos and Blaine County everywhere with your friends in your own rides. Online mode gets periodic updates, and these updates don't cost you any real-world money. Of course, if you're broke and desperate to get a certain item fast, you can buy Shark Cards, but for God's sake don't be stupid and go looking for modders for modded money (which is why so many people get banned). I think the biggest highlight of GTA Online is the Heists. Heists are cooperative missions for 4 players to pull off a series of jobs (robbing banks, prison breaks, infiltrations, etc.). If you love heist games like Payday, you seriously cannot miss this. Besides heists, GTA Online has tons of other modes. My second favorite is Adversary Modes, which come in all kinds of types—like a few players trying to avoid a serial killer in a pitch-black house, or Beast vs. Slasher (players hunt down the beast, while the beast has to hit designated checkpoints). Of course, there's a ton of other stuff in GTA Online like races, parachuting, golf, tennis, the list goes on forever. And once you know your way around GTA V, you can use the Online Creator to make your own race tracks, deathmatches, Last Team Standings, and more. Map making is a huge source of fun too. Everything I just mentioned about GTA V is still just the tip of the iceberg. With so much stuff worth exploring and so much fun to be had, doesn't that make it an amazingly fantastic game? *** It's been almost half a year since my last review, and in these past six months GTA got several major updates: first was "Further Adventures in Finance and Felony" on June 7th, followed by the "Bikers" DLC on October 4th, and then the "Import/Export" update on December 13th. These were all massive updates, something unprecedented compared to the second half of 2015 through the first half of 2016. These updates drastically changed how players play and experience GTA Online. Before this, everyone made money by grinding Pacific Standard over and over, but after these updates dropped, people gradually shifted to CEO cargo, biker factories, and importing/exporting cars to make cash. Personally speaking, new updates bring new highlights and new ways to make more money, which is obviously a good thing. But the new grinding methods are so repetitive, and a lot of the time you're just bored out of your mind driving across half the map, so it slowly loses its fun. Sure, a lot of people might say the old Pacific Standard was boring too, but that's just because you didn't know how to play and only relied on the "Kuruma glitch." Pacific Standard actually had tons of different ways to play and was super efficient. During the finale you could drive any car you liked without losing money, and on Convoy you could choose different ways to hijack it. Bottom line: the teamwork and coordination with your squad was way more fun and enjoyable than these new grinding methods. On the other hand, the new items keep piling up, but the price inflation is getting ridiculous. For the last update alone, buying everything cost $60M or even more (which is equivalent to a few months of my grinding). Then out of nowhere they dropped a 60-car garage (meaning they literally doubled all garage spaces prior to the update). So for the average player grinding daily in GTA, no matter how much money you make, it's never enough. I guess that's the negative impact of these new updates. *** Half a year has passed, and I've put in another nearly 1,000 hours. I'm closing in on 4,000 hours now. Because of Red Dead Redemption 2 and rumors of GTA VI being in development, GTA V hasn't had many updates in the first half of this year. We got Cunning Stunts: Special Vehicle Circuit and 4 cars (back in March), plus the long-awaited "Gunrunning" DLC. With less development focus, GTA V has started losing the vitality it used to have. The best money-making method went right back to Pacific Standard, which means the CEO cargo, Bikers, and Import/Export updates from 2016 were basically just temporary novelties. Because the Pacific Standard Kuruma method (the most common escape strat back then) got patched, players started finding new ways to do the Pacific Standard finale escape. Among them, the plane glitch let people finish the finale even faster and simpler than before, and you could get the $100K Elite Challenge bonus every single time (meaning doing 10 Pacifics gave you an extra $1M—it's like doing 10 runs now gives you the efficiency of doing 12.5 runs back in the day). And as the blank stretch of April and May rolled out, Rockstar went all out: first they ran a 15-day double cash and RP period on Contact Missions (note: back in early 2016 it was only for a single day), then double cash on Biker Contracts, and then they blew everyone's minds with double cash on *all heists* (back in 2015 there was only one Pacific week, and in 2016 there was none). During this time, every weekly update featured specific items on discount, with discounts bigger and more frequent than ever before. Rockstar was hoping to use sales and promos to get more people playing GTA Online, but with competition from other games and their own lack of fresh innovation (updates), GTA Online is starting to show signs of decline. *** **January 2021 Review of GTA:** GTA was my very first Steam game, and the one I've played the most. That alone shows how much I love it. But in the two years since my last review, I've only put in about 200 hours, and my playtime is still stuck in the 4-thousand range. This is heavily tied to some of the game's updates and the release of other new games. In late 2017, GTA dropped the Doomsday Heist (maybe a lot of people really liked this heist), but that's when GTA missions started getting all sci-fi and magical. The story was pretty trendy, dealing with AI, but that's also when invisible armored enemies showed up (even though they only appeared in that mission and weren't that hard to fight), along with flying DeLOREANS (though paying homage to *Back to the Future* is cool as hell), which left series veterans (or players who stuck around specifically for GTA's classic grounded style) feeling totally lost. From 2019 to 2021, GTA kept pumping out content, and all of it was free. But the missions just didn't have the same life as before. Missions went from requiring 4 people in the old heists, down to 2 for Doomsday, 1 for Casino Heist prep work, and finally just 1 person for the Cayo Perico Heist. (This evolution is actually a blessing for players, because even a few years ago rounding up 4 people was a pain in the ass, and if even one person dropped you had to restart the whole damn mission). But if you really think about it, those fun, memorable heist moments filled with multiplayer teamwork and coordination (like the Prison Break or the Pacific Standard) feel like they're gone for good. (Because finding people for old heists is a hassle, and the payouts can't keep up with the post-update inflation). In my eyes, I've always felt that GTA, MAFIA, and even later WATCH_DOGS are three games cut from the same cloth. Even though their themes and historical settings are completely different, these three games are the closest to reality. GTA gives us LA, New York, and Miami; WATCH_DOGS gives us Chicago, San Francisco, and London; MAFIA gives us old New York and old New Orleans. Their rich radio music, vehicles, billboards, and shops (I can't think of a single word to encompass all of it—just everyday life) all carry a very strong sense of era and theme. But over the past couple of years, more and more similar or comparable games have flooded the market, completely overwhelming us. And honestly, that's the exact reason why people are leaving Los Santos to go sightsee everywhere else in the world.

translation_en: [spoiler]The Game of Dreams![/spoiler] It's honestly hard to even start this review, since this game is so absurd (in a good way) and massive that it's complicated to know where to begin. But let's go. The Grand Theft Auto franchise has always been a worldwide success, and this is obviously due to the fact that it puts the player in an open world, something that had never been seen before. Furthermore, the player isn't the "hero" of the story, which also wasn't common, but what I'm trying to say is amazing, even though GTA III changed gaming history forever, Rockstar manages to make the franchise even more impressive with every title, and that was no different with GTA V, which is simply a game that for a while was nothing more than a fan's dream. Rockstar made a game that genuinely makes other companies jealous. GTA V was made without rushing, taking no less than 5 long years of hard work to be ready, and those 5 years resulted in the most ALIVE game I've had the pleasure of playing in my life. Walking through Los Santos is simply an experience you haven't seen in many games, maybe never seen at all. Every inch of the game's map was made with care and you can see details in everything. In the city you can witness a police chase, a mugging that you can interfere in, an accident, a fight, a homeless person begging for change, someone talking on their phone, another eating something, and much more. It's all so alive and beautiful, and all of this on a gigantic map, and unlike GTA IV's map which was smaller and entirely urban, GTA V's map is very varied, featuring a city, desert, forest, mountains, beaches, all frightfully gorgeous, with an abundance of details. It's a sight for sore eyes for both gamers and non-gamers; at this point, the game's quality is unquestionable. The story of this game wipes the floor with many Hollywood movies. The script is wonderful. I myself questioned before the game's launch if 3 playable characters would actually work instead of ruining the main story, and thank god I was so wrong! Franklin, Michael, and Trevor will without a shadow of a doubt be remembered for a long time in gaming history. These 3 characters work together extremely well, each has their own characteristics, they are completely different from one another, and it's very hard not to get attached to them. The arguments, the banter, missions, celebrations, tense and fun moments between them—and there are quite a few—make whoever is playing get emotional easily. The plot twists are impeccable, it simply never gets boring. Each mission, sometimes without a super strong motive, is still spectacular, and that doesn't just go for story missions, I mean overall, everything was very well thought out. GTA V unfortunately isn't perfect. Like every open-world game with a massive map, it also suffers from bugs. I can't name many here, as incredible as it seems I didn't witness many, but you can definitely see them: cars getting swallowed by the ground, textures disappearing, falling from a silly height and dying, among other things. Bugs are without a shadow of a doubt much more common and varied in the online mode. GTA Online: You can waste a lot of hours on this. The story mode already has plenty to do, but online you definitely have a lot more. Besides simply having the entire story mode map available for you to explore, online you can do it with your friends and with tons of activities scattered around, races of everything you can possibly imagine, deathmatches, heists, missions, and many other things. But what stands out are the Heists, very complex and long robberies that require a team of 4 players, each with their own objective. Cooperation between players is essential, especially since nobody can mess up. You really spend hours on this, but it's always worth it since the reward and satisfaction at the end are huge. Hackers are unfortunately very common online, and Rockstar often bans even people who don't use them, but even so it doesn't help. It's really annoying to join a public match; the chance of there being an asshole using cheats is pretty high. Creating a match with just friends is much better and avoids unnecessary disappointment. Grand Theft Auto V is a lesson in how to make a truly great game! Rockstar's 5 years of hard work are genuinely impressive. The game cost no less than $266 million (including marketing), maybe even more, becoming one of the most expensive games ever produced to date. All of this resulted in: the biggest hype without a shadow of a doubt surrounding a game to this day, the fastest entertainment product in history to make $1 Billion, the fourth best-selling game in history, breaking 7 Guinness World Records, and all of it thoroughly deserved. GTA V is a unique game that shows that work done with love, a lot of patience, and by a company that knows how to respect its franchise and its fans—releasing DLCs packed with content and completely for free! May Rockstar's creation serve as an everlasting example to all other companies on how to make a game that will undoubtedly be remembered. Rating: 10
