I didn't even touch it on console. No, it's not like I have a console antipathy. Just being broke. I was also worried about my PC like "what if I can't run it?". At some point I said, "even if I can't run it, oh well," since my PC isn't anything amazing, but I'm saying "thank god it runs it" already. I'm not going to talk to you about the three-character gameplay, the new graphics, the "keep on keeping on" and "we are making Los Santos a global brand" policies that the Los Santos municipality has strictly followed since San Andreas, or how great the optimization is. Did I just talk about it anyway? Oh well, let's just agree and get it over with. Those who played Grand Theft Auto 4 know it had an online mode, which didn't really hook me and didn't have much of a point. In Grand Theft Auto 5, Rockstar Games has built upon that tenfold. Literally a whole new world has been created. The game damn well earns every bit of that 180 TL, especially in the online mode. New features like Heist missions, contact missions, property and vehicle ownership have added a completely different kind of excitement to the game. My personal advice is to grab your friends and throw yourselves into the streets of Los Santos. Dive into the old online modes (races, deathmatches, etc.), and heist missions. Make the money and watch it slip right through your fingers. Then come home, pour yourself a glass of whiskey, and enjoy the view of Los Santos from your window. I don't know what else I could write here, but my advice is that you shouldn't acquire this game through illegal means. I'll give you a few reasons for that, of course: 1) The online mode, obviously 2) The updates Rockstar sends out almost every day 3) The story mode of the offline part (excluding mysteries, stunt jumps, races, etc.) takes 31 hours to finish and can get boring after a while. Finally, Grand Theft Auto promised me about 58 hours in roughly 5 days (midterms are over, I have a week off, otherwise I couldn't play it, yeah). About 28 hours of this was in online. Since I was in constant contact with my friends and constantly jumping into missions and stuff, I didn't get bored at all. By the way, the character creation screen is also awesome, they didn't forget to shout out Niko. There's also the director mode that came for PC, but for some reason I haven't been able to get into it much yet, I'll update the review later. Don't forget to like if you liked it, dislike if you didn't, select the funny option if you found it funny, and feel free to send a message if you want to give any suggestions.[/b] [i]Zenobiaa Los Santos Rio Ave Apt. NO:5[/i]

translation_en: I only play single-player, thanks. 2017.7.4 [h1]To keep my initial review from misleading people, I'm updating it on 2015.8.31[/h1] [b] I have to admit, my original review was way too emotional. GTA V had just come out back then, and looking at all those mind-blowing features, it was really easy to write such a "sentimental" review. Then for a while after that, I just kept playing this game. Until around 50 hours in, right when the single-player campaign was at the setup phase for the final heist, I suddenly felt kind of burnt out. Nothing in the game seemed fun anymore, so I decided to try multiplayer. Because of my connection and running into some toxic pricks, my multiplayer experience wasn't great. Plus, I didn't really care much for multiplayer heists and races. Honestly, I'd rather just hang out in the apartment at 101 Weazel Plaza and watch the view outside. Anyway, for me, this game only has about 50 hours of playtime, which I didn't expect at all. So let me advise you guys: think twice before buying, and figure out whether you're into single-player or multiplayer—like whether you're a story junkie, graphics snob, looking to play with bros, easily triggered, etc., etc. Though the pricing for GTA V in the Chinese region is genuinely fair. [b] So yeah, if you like it, just buy it. Other people's reviews are just for reference. Play it first, then come back and leave a review to help others out [spoiler] Dragging others down with me ←_← [/spoiler] [/b] [/b] [h1] ★★★★★ Unreserved 5-Star Review ★★★★★ [/h1] Six days of pre-loading, six days of arguing with customer support about the meaning of life—every bit of the wait was worth it. The moment I opened the game, I was in tears. From the first trailer three years ago, to the news that there wouldn't be a PC version, to PC players signing petitions while R* played coy and evasive—it's all still vividly fresh in my mind. Back then I hadn't bought into legitimate games yet; I just looked at it as the sequel to some masterpiece that would max out your hard drive. Until last year, when the GTA V page finally showed up on Steam with a release date: Q1 2015, and a little spark of hope lit up inside. Later on, when pre-orders opened, I bought it legitimately on day one with a solid half-price discount. It took me nearly a week to pre-load it, and when I eagerly tried to open it, I realized I'd activated it on the wrong account. Cue another long, endless week of appeals. Until the day before yesterday, when I found out I could finally launch the game. The moment I saw the R* logo, my roommate woke up from my screaming. [h1] Let's talk about the game itself [/h1] Optimization is good. While it's nothing mind-blowing, running it on medium settings still gives you a great visual experience. The attention to detail is full of heart. In GTA V, the mobile phone feature already leaves Saints Row in the dust—all kinds of news, interactive web pages, buying stocks, supercars, planes, yachts, and you can even watch videos in the entertainment section! [At noon I ate takeout while watching an episode of Fame or Shame.] The protagonists have distinct personalities; the three-character setup makes the game infinitely fun. You will never get bored in Los Santos. Different special abilities add variety to combat, and the protagonists aren't superheroes anymore—everything's gotten more realistic. You can get headshot, your jumps can fail, and running out of stamina drains your health. Solid driving mechanics—no bullshit, compared to Watch Dogs, I can actually shake the cops. Above all that, every single word here is straight from the bottom of my heart. My laptop's running low on battery, getting a bit sleepy tonight, brain's not working. I'll fill in the rest when I have time during the day. [b] To be honest, I used to really look down on the GTA cult. Now, well... I'm sorry, I've joined the cult. [/b] What's that? You're asking me "Do you recommend this game?" when writing a review? I just wanna know, can I get a few more of those thumbs-up buttons?

translation_en: Hello violence, drugs, money, accessible women and other joys of the promised life. [h1]Welcome to Los Santos[/h1] The game, no doubt, is very beautiful. And while everyone is choking on enthusiasm over how cool and gorgeous it is, I'll try to quickly outline the actual state of affairs. I'll start with what everyone is going wild over—the graphics and the game world. The developers worked hard on these elements. There is nothing else like it in the gaming industry today. But all of this is just a bright wrapper that blinds you at first, and players rush into Los Santos like moths to a flame, drooling. The PC optimization is so well done that other studios should take notes. In a word—unmatched. The story, as expected from the GTA series, once again won't leave us indifferent. It's original, sarcastic, adventurous... In other words—a great story that complements the franchise. I'll note that in this installment, more than any other, there are crossovers with the plots of past games. For instance, you can run into Packie McReary or the biker protagonist from Liberty City Stories. Now let's tear off the wrapper, cool our heads from the hype, wipe the drool and look inside, examining the bare facts so everyone can make their own decision. What do we have: 3 types of clothing stores, with diverse and large assortments for each character. Many types of land vehicles that you can customize, yet each protagonist has their own favorite car, and they couldn't care less that you bought a sports car—as soon as you switch to another character, they'll rush to the garage and jump into their "baby," and you can just cross the money spent on the new car out of your budget. The internet has become smaller than in Liberty City, but more functional, you can buy almost everything through it... And true, why bother rendering car dealerships (which you could rob)? Businesses migrated straight over from San Andreas, run almost the same way with a few minor exceptions. No bars, no restaurants, no shopping malls... boring. I dreamed of robbing a mall (: . Movie theaters have been added, but the repertoire isn't very exciting, and you can't walk around the lobby or stroll through the auditorium annoying the audience... There is tons of transport, including watercraft (submarines) and aircraft, but you can't ride the trains, though there's a weird metro-tram thing, but you can't drive it, only ride inside as a passenger. Buses drive around the city, but there's not a single route. No big blockbuster premieres, streets aren't blocked off for shooting movies or TV shows. There isn't even a mansion shooting a Santa Barbara-style show (or whatever they film nowadays) with fans crowding around outside. Seriously? Los Santos? Vinewood? I don't buy it. There are other minor things like extra garages that you enter and exit via loading screens. But like I said, those are just minor details. It's fun and interesting to play, as well as to explore the updated city, but we've gotten all of this before. So aside from the very (ver-r-ry) beautiful and optimized graphics, the developers didn't manage to surprise us with anything new. We got an excellent sequel to a cult game, and although I personally hoped for something revolutionary, I am immensely satisfied with the game. [h1]Rating[/h1] It's almost a tradition for my reviews to have a rating at the end. And I have to say, giving any definitive score to a masterpiece like this (and despite everything written above, the game claims that title) is very hard. I'll try to be original so as not to offend my favorite franchise. Rating: [b]Priceless[/b]

translation_en: «Masterpiece! An action game with dark humor.» Rockstar have done it again with another worthy masterpiece, gathering the very best from previous games in the GTA series and combining it into one explosive package. A hurricane of positive emotions that I just have to share with you. The gameplay throws you headfirst into a crazy whirlpool of events right off the bat. It kicks off with a bank heist—unlike GTA 4, my friends, where the beginning was kind of boring. The story is wrapped up really cool with unexpected twists and a very good payoff, overall just like always: an action flick with loads of upbeat dark humor. With every mission you get drawn deeper and deeper into the world of GTA 5. It's a shame there are so few story missions; I replay the early missions with pleasure. A new feature for me was playing as multiple characters—there are three of them in the game: Michael De Santa, Franklin Clinton, and Trevor Philips. The characters are super charismatic, each with their own world and interesting backstory that you learn about from the early missions. Character progression lets you improve their stats: stamina, strength, stealth, driving, and flying (strength and stamina don't visually change the characters like in GTA San Andreas, which is probably for the best). Each character also has a special ability. For example, one of the three special abilities lets you slow down time while driving so it's easier to make sharp turns at high speed or dodge obstacles. The dialogue in the game is written and directed in such a lively, well-thought-out way, it feels like a movie instead of a game. There's plenty of dark humor in the dialogue, which is a definite plus. The scale of the huge virtual city of Los Santos gives the player complete freedom of action; the city is truly beautiful, detailed down to the smallest things, making you want to call it "alive." Rockstar really knows how to pull this off, great job, keep it up. The game has Easter eggs referring to previous GTA parts, as well as UFOs, Bigfoot, and sea monsters. There will be plenty to do when you take a break from the main story and Online. There's more than enough ground, air, and water transport to get around, something for every taste—there's even military stuff. I won't list them all, I'll just add that the models look super cool and closely resemble their real-life counterparts. There's an option for vehicle tuning and restyling, which is great news for fans of souped-up cars and bikes. The graphics are gorgeous. On ultra settings, the surrounding world looks as if you're looking out a stained-glass window at a mega-city. Unfortunately, not many players will be able to appreciate all its perks due to the high system requirements, and upgrading PC hardware with the exchange rate back in March 2015 is just absurd. At launch, the optimization was heavily tailored towards Nvidia GPUs, though the situation has evened out by now. The gameplay is good. I want to make a special mention of the controls, since a lot of people complain that the controls are trash and all that... I play with both a gamepad and a keyboard + mouse, and I'm happy with everything. A bad dancer always blames his balls. The game's multiplayer is a blast, plus Rockstar keeps improving it and casually adding new stuff. Folks, I want to point out right away that going into heists without smart players on your team is just a waste of time, effort, and nerves—totally pointless. To get the maximum out of heists and other activities, you need to play with friends or at least not brain-dead noobs. I wish everyone a strong team for pulling off heists and getting the "Criminal Mastermind" achievement that gives you 11 million GTA dollars. Purely a personal opinion—the mission difficulty is casual. I want hardcore, and I mean real hardcore! I dove headfirst into the game!!! Not a single regret about pre-ordering it six months before release. I wish everyone a great time in the world of GTA 5, a hurricane of positive emotions, enjoying the game to the max and feeling it with every cell of your body. PS - There's way too much arguing about optimization, and there's plenty of info online about GTA 5 tests on various setups with different settings. No need to blow that topic up here.

translation_en: This review is only about the Online portion. Not really a review either, just sharing some thoughts. After endless stuttering, reconnects, disconnections, and crashes, I finally busted out the good ol' VPN and smoothly connected to Rockstar's servers. I, naive fool that I was, thought this meant I could happily play with Los Santos residents from all over the world. But alas, I was too young, too simple, tender as a lamb. After finishing the tutorial, I was around level 3. I ran around the session looking for three other players, stalking them like a total creeper (Grand Stalk Auto V?), but those three big bosses were running all over the place completely ignoring me. Fine, if you won't let me ride your coattails, I'll go find someone else. Just then, I got an invite. Wow, a Heist! I clicked join while thinking to myself, *Hmph, watch me totally flex my insane skills in front of you big shots.* Once I joined the mission, I was dumbfounded. In a lobby full of level 70 or 80 pros, my level 3 tag stuck out like a sore thumb. Don't panic. We've got game sense and mechanics, true badass style, fear nothing. Stumbling and bumping my way there, arriving over a minute late to the objective, the pros were already going hard against the enemy. I hatched a plan, slammed the gas, charged straight into enemy territory, bailed out of the car, and started blasting. That was just what I *imagined* would happen. Amidst the shocked stares of the pros, I got riddled with bullets and died. Mission Failed. Did I mention that the car I bailed out of also ran over and killed a teammate? Leaving the mission in frustration, I decided to calm down, play it safe, and keep a low profile. Yeah, for a beginner, Heists are way too hard, so let's start with some races. Shortly after, under the watchful gaze of the top 7 players (out of 8 total), I slowly drove my blown-tire car straight into a river. Did Not Finish. No, I figured stunt plane races should be pretty easy. Throughout the entire race, I tried my absolute best to scatter pieces of my airplane across every corner of the track. Flying planes is way too hard, let's just ride bicycles instead. Yet 20 minutes later, I was still stuck on the very first ramp, unable to jump up. The other racers and I were definitely not riding the same kind of vehicle! Ah, why is this game so hard?! Let's just pick up some guns and do some manly stuff. Versus mode, 2v2. I got teamed up with an orange-haired wavy-haired chick. Seeing the opponents' matching crew IDs, names, and mafia outfits, I couldn't help wondering if we walked into a sweatshop lobby. I wanted to tell her, "Girl, let's play it safe and hide, don't just feed the enemy kills." Turns out this chick was hardcore as hell. She rushed straight at the enemy's gas barrels and went *bang bang bang*, blowing the opponents twenty-some meters into the air. So wild. Girl, do you need a girlfriend? So while the girl was out there dealing damage, I hid behind cover like a absolute coward, stealing kills and mopping up. In the end, our side actually took the lead. Finally, my very first victory in life! After the match ended, I desperately chased after the girl on foot, welcoming the dust storm kicked up by the tires of her pink sports car. But she didn't say a word, stuck her middle finger out the window at me, and drove off toward the setting sun. If I were a straight man, I definitely would have fallen in love. Alright, after all that fooling around, I was almost level 5. Time to buy a house, get a sports car, and live that decadent high-roller life. Bought the apartment and the sports car. Yep, I was broke. Even the pre-order bonus money was basically gone. I stood in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows of my mansion, looking up at this restless, noisy world, then looked down at my empty-ass wallet, and smiled with satisfaction.

translation_en: [b]In my reviews, I express my personal opinion, it might not match yours and that's okay![/b] [quote]I can't guarantee that everything is going to be fine. Maybe I'll have to hack you into little pieces and flush you down the toilet... But I sincerely hope it doesn't come to that. ⓒ Trevor Philips[/quote] [b]From this intro,[/b] I think you realized that the game is packed with a huge amount of cool dialogue. GTA V has always been famous for its hilarious, awesome, and interesting jokes and lines! Which later became cult classics for fans of the series and beyond. Edgy jokes or ones that cross the line completely are totally Rockstar's style. Most of the time they fit the context, which is why they don't feel idiotic or out of place. [b]As for the game's storyline.[/b] Each character — and there are three of them — has their own gimmick. And every character lives their own life. But when it comes to heists, they're a team. While playing through the storyline, there's a really cool option to play as any of the three main characters. Let's briefly bring you up to speed: Trevor Philips is a mentally unstable "redneck." I think you get why he was kicked out of the Air Force. Franklin Clinton dreams of becoming a major crime boss. Michael is a retired bank robber trying to leave his past behind. I guess there's no point in writing a lot about the plot. You all already know everything if you've had even the slightest interest in the game. [b]Let's move on to the gameplay part of the game.[/b] The gameplay is very diverse! Not only is the city super vibrant and wherever you go, something is happening somewhere. The interesting game storyline doesn't let you catch a breath for even a second. This is the first time I've genuinely, truly seen such a lively city. I just like watching the lives of people and animals. Driving around the city while listening to cool music on the radio. By the way, there's a cool feature to add your own music to the radio. Sometimes I can just hop on a train and ride around evening Los Santos. Try it! It's genuinely worth it. Every character has their own individual car. You can tune or upgrade them at Los Santos Customs. Driving cars in GTA V is actually pretty realistic. Later on, you'll be able to grow your business, buy cars, real estate, etc. Shooting is just shooting, I don't really have anything to say about it. The special effects when you land a headshot look cool, and the variety of weapons is at a high level. The phone is made really well! You can use the browser to search for various information! And even here, Rockstar approached it with a sense of humor. [b]As for the graphics settings of the game.[/b] The graphics quality on ultra settings is worthy of respect! The 4K mode is unrealistically beautiful and optimized. I haven't seen this level of graphics in a single game with such a massive open world. http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=426135917 I think many are used to all new releases being poorly optimized, but this isn't the case. Even the new Mortal Kombat X let people down on release day. In GTA V, unlike the graphical part of the game, the technical optimization sucks. There are a lot of complaints that the game won't launch for one reason or another for many users, and that's a minus. [b]I'd like to write about the downsides of this game.[/b] When I'm driving down the road and there's a conversation happening, it's hard for me because I don't know English at a level where I can catch the thought on the fly and drive decently at the same time. Plus, the main chunk of conversations happens precisely while you're behind the wheel. Controlling flying vehicles is awkward on a keyboard, and you have to waste about an hour getting used to it! With a controller, there are no such problems. That wraps up the downsides of this game. [b]Moving on to online.[/b] I think anyone who has played knows its merits. I won't delve into the requirements of GTA ONLINE. I'll just write what I personally like. You can be in a gang. Wear clothes in your crew's style. Thus expressing your individuality. Loads of diverse missions, tasks, just tearing around the city causing absolute mayhem. At any moment, just like in real life, you can call your gang buddy on the phone. For example, to set up the next bank heist! Isn't that cool? You can start your own business, get awesome rides, real estate. You can fly fighter jets! GTA ONLINE is everything! Therefore, if you haven't bought this masterpiece of the gaming industry yet, what the hell are you even still reading this review for. Hurry up, go deposit some cash and buy Grand Theft Auto V. It's worth its money! Believe me!

translation_en: I don't know since when, but some games stopped being just games. Some designers started playing the "games with a message" card, trying to shove certain morals down players' throats; other designers treated games as an art medium, turning the screen into their canvas and code into their paintbrushes; and yet other designers simply wanted to tell a story—no more, no less, just that. Of course, most games are still just games, but in my view, *Grand Theft Auto V* doesn't seem to belong to any of the above categories. Because when Rockstar handed players a massive, exquisitely detailed, and vibrant city the gaming world had never seen before, what they were actually selling was something entirely different. To put it simply, *Grand Theft Auto V* is a city, and you can trash it however you want. Grandeur and extreme attention to detail sum up the biggest selling points of *Grand Theft Auto V*. Hundreds of millions of dollars in development budget, a development team of a thousand people, and four long years of development... Back in the autumn of 2013, Rockstar had already broken numerous gaming industry records with the series of technical milestones demonstrated in this title, and the reward was over 34 million copies sold. While a hefty investment doesn't necessarily guarantee commercial success, in this high-stakes gamble, Rockstar clearly hit the jackpot. As the main artery of the entire game, the script for *Grand Theft Auto V* is also exceptionally brilliant. The lead writer for the story was Dan Houser, one of the founders of Rockstar. This Englishman who came to New York with dreams after graduation probably understands American society more comprehensively than some Americans who are "too close to see the wood for the trees," making the story of *Grand Theft Auto V* feel a lot like a detached, cold-eyed satire. Dan's pen shaped three protagonists with distinct personalities: Michael, a middle-aged man undergoing a midlife crisis who wants to wash his hands of crime but just can't; Franklin, a young Black man who grew up in the ghetto and rose out of the mud, though not entirely untainted; and Trevor, crazy, dangerous, and possessing typical antisocial personality traits. Three men lingering on the fringes of society, three different perspectives. The online mode (known as *GTA Online*) is another world that will make players invest a massive amount of time and passion. In this online gameplay based on the core of *Grand Theft Auto V*, players can create their own characters... From name and gender to genetics, appearance, and so on, players can customize everything themselves. Online characters have independent funds and levels, all of which require players to participate in online gameplay to accumulate. In GTA Online, players can experience almost all the gameplay elements found in the single-player content, except that these features require players to continuously level up their characters to unlock them. When participating in various events and races in this mode, you compete against other "thugs" from all over the world. You can team up with other players to reclaim cargo or vehicles, or plan a crazy heist together; you can compete with other players in motorcycle, bicycle, parachuting, racing, and other events, fighting for the championship within the rules; you can also engage in competitive gunfights with other players to see who is truly the king of gunfights. But *GTA Online* is not flawless either. Aside from some event mechanics—like gunfight matchups—feeling a bit crude and repetitive, the balance of online matches is a rather obvious issue. In many team-versus-team events, players can freely choose their own teams, and the game can start as long as each team has at least one player. This often leads to situations where a single player has to fight against multiple players. If fairness is lost in a match, entertainment naturally cannot be guaranteed either. If we are looking for some kind of explicit gratification when facing most games, then *Grand Theft Auto V* feels more like enjoying some indescribable state. It seems to open a door full of possibilities; while the charming scenery behind the door is certainly moving, more importantly, it demonstrates to us the prototype of a future online community, and once again raises the industry standard for open-world games to an awe-inspiring height. I wasn't really into virtual reality tech like the Oculus Rift before, thinking that current game display technology was already enough to support current gaming products. But after playing *Grand Theft Auto V* in first-person mode, I started eagerly hoping for such devices to become mainstream as soon as possible. Not for anything else, just so I could take a stroll down the streets of Los Santos. In short, *Grand Theft Auto V* is standing right on the boundary between the dreams of game developers and players for the game world and reality. May more game works stand together in this place. And Rockstar should also walk even more resolutely towards the other side of the dream, going further and further.

translation_en: [h1][b]You can walk the dog, and in 1080p and 60fps at that. 10/10[/b][/h1] Alright, alright, jokes aside, now for real! [h1][b]"Grand Theft Auto V" is kind of like Uncharted, except it doesn't suck. pewpewpew! bangbang![/b][/h1] Ok, ok, that's enough of the good stuff before the comedy merry-go-round spins completely out of control. Time for a serious and substantive review, short and to the point. "Grand Theft Auto V" is the newest and most expansive installment in a series that really needs no introduction. There's no denying that the game is masterfully made and I had a great time with it, especially in the multiplayer mode, which is devilishly addictive. Even though it's a product that was built with the 10-year-old PS3 and X360 in mind, you have to say that on PC it looks at the very least very good. While particle effects and graphics are things that can easily be improved when jumping between generations, the design of most missions, locations, and the script is a completely different matter. I quite often had the impression that the game looks a bit archaic, and that's precisely because it was made with very dated hardware in mind. However, Rockstar managed to polish their masterpiece, and if we mentally step back 3-4 years in the gaming industry, "GTA V" could even be considered the best game in PC history. Still, looking at this product a bit more critically, these flaws can be somewhat annoying. Rockstar's policy is a masterclass in making money, but when it comes to their attitude towards players, it's a bit worse. There's no talk of any scams, shady practices, or other swindles though, because the game is worth its price and the user gets enough content to feel satisfied. Even though the PC and PS4 versions were heavily delayed, you have to admit that the time we had to wait for them was largely compensated for. Looking back now from the perspective of those 2 years of difference at how the PS3/X360 versions look, I'm glad Rockstar didn't release the game on PC and next-gen consoles right away. "Gaming" in that quality is a crime against yourself and those around you. Aside from the aforementioned flaws, the game is truly great and it's worth checking out, especially since the multiplayer is still heavily supported and expanded with new elements. [b]Real, honest rating: 9/10[/b]

translation_en: The project is "At long last!". It's a bit shit to call a collection of opinions "reviews", but whatever. 15 years ago, well, maybe I'm exaggerating a bit, [b]GTA3[/b] came out. A revolution! A reimagining of the action genre! An "open world" (the term wasn't even common back then yet)! Tearing down social and other norms. Saturation with satire everywhere and in everything. It was precisely with its transition into a 3D world that the game hit gamers' PCs with vibrant new colors... and wild stuttering. After a while—and you couldn't say we waited long—hardware lines bulked up in power and let us properly appreciate every element of the game. However, discussing what was happening on screen, a group of friends would dream: what if? And that "what if" meant a lot: from basic freedom of movement horizontally and the ability to swim, to things that at the time seemed simply unbelievable, like playing it online, doing missions together (just to be clear, wired internet was only just emerging, most people didn't even have a dial-up modem). A couple of years later, [b]GTA Vice City[/b] comes out. A completely different atmosphere, the disco era, beaches, sun... gangsters, drugs, and all that goes with it. Helicopters appear, playing becomes even more interesting, the plot and character development are more tangible. Technically, the game doesn't differ much from the 3rd part, but it just so happened that this was the exact one I wanted to finish from start to finish. Yet, a lot was still missing. [b]GTASA[/b] was a milestone. Basically, you could do absolutely everything here, and once again hardware limitations... I was only able to play it properly a bit later, when I bought a decent nVidia 6600GT graphics card. Gang territory wars, character leveling, cars, martial arts, endless expanses, and much more. Sometimes I'd steal a plane and just fly around the map. But I wasn't that hardcore of a "sandbox" fan, and I had zero interest in spreading goodness left and right or handing out cuddles. We were still whining about multiplayer... and then, modders slapped SAMP together. Some people still play it to this day. I won't even consider GTA on mobile platforms, not interesting at all. And then, [b]GTA4[/b] – for me, a revolutionary installment. Physics, graphics, story... shitty optimization, that's all GTA4. On top of all that, it also had supported multiplayer where you could raise hell in pseudo-New York to your heart's content, especially thanks to mods. While I played through the previous parts without paying much attention to the plot, here I savored every single mission. And most importantly – the interactivity. It became fun to run into people, watch situations unfold, drop into the local "Comedy Club", play billiards, and so on. Of course, the lack of polish ultimately shows. That annoyingness of the "friends" drives you up the wall in the end. And yet, every time Rockstar raises the bar of requirements for a product without churning out some copy-paste... thing. Yeah, the core concept has been the same since 2D GTA1, but... And then, September '13, the release of [b]GTA V[/b]. The 5th part is a concentrate of the company's best ideas from a decade of painstaking work. As soon as pre-orders opened on Steam (on PC, of course), I rushed to hand over my cash like my ass was on fire. I tried not to watch playthroughs, not to buy a console and all that stuff, just waited, and the wait rewarded me with practically one of the best games out right now. Why practically? I played a bit, and what did I find: that thrill when I accidentally stumbled upon someone's let's play was gone. Everything is taken for granted. The story, the references to "Analyze This" and stuff like that – amazing (within the bounds of its Vinewood-ness). Trevor is very much like Nicholson; all these points have been chewed over thoroughly, so dwelling on them is just a waste of time, everyone knows everything. A pity I haven't reached GTAO yet, but that can wait. Despite the fact that this opinion turned out a bit disjointed – my thoughts are getting tangled because I'm writing this in the break between missions. I really want to get back to it. Do I recommend the game? Of course! Even if you're not a fan of the series, just having the game on your shelf is nice. But not without this point – every GTA release is the embodiment of everything the gaming industry is capable of at a specific period in time (gameplay, AI, etc.). Buy it, see what it's capable of... anyway, it's a far cry from a failing Watch_Dogs, where we were just fed pretty screenshots. Oh right – a separate word on optimization. My hardware only meets the minimum requirements, but even on those the game runs without major stuttering, and what little there is only shows up occasionally. Verdict: I recommend it to everyone, but 18+. Kids won't really understand everything anyway, and they don't need to be playing this.

translation_en: [b]NOTICE: I am writing this review with few hours of playtime because I had already played it on console.[/b] Grand Theft Auto V is a spectacular game, where Rockstar went all out in every aspect to give us many hours of fun and gameplay. Because of this I state, it's a must-have game for fans of the Grand Theft Auto franchise. [h1]Plot and missions[/h1] The missions in Grand Theft Auto V are spectacular, very well thought out, and taking advantage of the novelty of inserting three protagonists, they not only have solo missions but also group missions, such as heists and robberies. Rockstar knew how to manage the missions for each protagonist and how they would complement each other. I have to admit that Grand Theft Auto V's campaign has a very weak plot compared to its predecessors, but it's made up for by the wonderful missions (which are better than the predecessors'). [h1]Graphics and optimization[/h1] Unlike its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V was very well optimized, running even on rigs below the minimum requirements with reasonable performance. Now we have many more graphics settings options, being able to reduce or increase them to the extreme. The game's graphics itself are flawless, it was already gorgeous on consoles, it's way more beautiful on PC, for sure. There are so many details in the scenery, wind action, water, reflections, leaves, dust, etc. I can't complain about that at all. [h1]Online mode[/h1] Grand Theft Auto Online came to give players many more hours of fun, and it's here to stay, since this gamble by Rockstar paid off big time. In online mode, besides the open world, we have racing missions, deathmatches, heists, robberies, etc., with content created by Rockstar and by players through the Creator. It's possible to transfer your character from console to PC, like I did, which is good for those who want to keep their progress, but it's bad because of console glitchers who are over level 2000, this puts other players at a disadvantage. [h1]New features[/h1] Compared to the consoles, Grand Theft Auto V for PC has some new features, such as many more NPCs/cars in online mode, more detailed grass/bushes (previous generation didn't even have it), reflection details, more intense weather, the game running at a framerate above 30fps, Director Mode (I'll talk about it below) and much more. [h1]Director Mode[/h1] Rockstar likes modders to work on the game, besides liking players to create new things with it, and keeping that in mind they made Director Mode exclusively for PC Grand Theft Auto V, which is a mode where you can do anything, from messing around on the map with superpowers to making movies/videos out of the game. Yes, this mode gives you the freedom to be any character in the game (you need to unlock them by playing the campaign) or even animals, if you prefer you can also create programmed actions and lines for NPCs and execute them (hence the name Director Mode, since the NPCs will be your actors). You just have to play in this mode to get an idea of how fun it is. Not to mention the game has its own video editor, where you can add effects, change cameras, and export to watch on any device. [h1]Conclusion[/h1] It's a game that I recommend buying and enjoying, without a shadow of a doubt.

translation_en: [h1]"It's finally happened!" or "more than just GTA!"[/h1] Attention! This review is written through the prism of my own impressions and emotions. Its main task is to talk about my own impressions and feelings as sincerely and honestly as my writing ability will allow, and also to talk about how and why this little game won me over. So, like the "last of the Mohicans," having prepared myself for a long wait—namely, as long as it would take—I tried to find out as little as possible about the project before its release on personal computers, and that was really difficult! I'll make a reservation right away: I bought GTA V primarily for the single-player game. And you know, the game was worth the candle! After playing for a few hours, I was radiating exclusively positive emotions and experiencing full satisfaction, the endorphins in my blood were through the roof, and I could compare this feeling only to my state at 10 years old, when I first got my hands on a computer and, in particular, the game NFS: Porsche Unleashed! And my expectations fully matched reality! The only thing I regret is that its release didn't coincide with my vacation. Having played it, I can't speak negatively about a single aspect of the fifth part, I am unable to list and squeeze out even the slightest cons, so I'd rather leave that to the people who like to suck them out of their thumbs. GTA V has gathered all the best from all the previous parts, and has also added a lot of things that are radically new or improve the series' concept. The world here is as alive as it gets; you want to leisurely explore every corner of the current Los Santos, allowing yourself to savor every minute spent in it. Every mission I've managed to play through is staged amazingly, everything happens extremely dynamically and with all sorts of variety. [list] [*]First-person view; The task set before the developers was accomplished with flying colors, shootouts become harder, and driving a car leaves unforgettable impressions. [*]The fauna really fits into the big picture, the kitties and doggies brought a certain cuteness. [*]The city is not just the biggest, it's unique; every street, every piece of architecture, every landscape—god, how much effort and time has been invested in this, the terrain, the design, and most of all life is boiling, it's as if it's breathing! Someone is busy with business, someone is strolling, it's extremely interesting to watch all this! [*]The internet network equivalent! The innovation from part 4 has settled in great! Only here you will encounter a lot more content, tons of it! Twitters, sweaters, and other inventions of homo sapiens. [*]And have you ever wondered how many Easter eggs and references to events in our lives and art this game can pack in! You will always find something to do, whether it's playing tennis or exploring the underwater world with scuba gear! [*]Epic police chases! The artificial intelligence has been improved, now they won't let you just vanish like that, shaking off the police is now a real, little adventure. [*]The game's characters are presented with extreme depth; each of them has their own everyday problems and life difficulties that seem extremely minor against the background of that huge world that surrounds them, but at the same time so significant. [*]In previous parts of the series, throughout the game, you couldn't shake the feeling that the actors were always overacting or, conversely, underacting, the feeling that something was wrong, sometimes a bit clunky, and only by comparison do you realize what cinematic quality and realism—take even a simple conversation—we've been presented with this time. Everything looks so natural: character traits, dialogues, humor. All in all, in GTA V you're in for a wonderful staging of dialogues and cutscenes! [*]The soundtrack is genius! As for the radio, I've always been thrilled with all the radio stations of this "action game" without exception, regardless of the installment. Maybe somewhere the music and sound components limped a bit, but that's not about "number five," the sound in it is absolutely gorgeous, it makes you listen closely and enjoy yourself. [/list] Of course, you need to see all this for yourself; it's better to play once than read a review a hundred times :D and how after all this can anyone allow themselves to say that the price tag is high? Sorry for the wall of text :D

translation_en: Ah, finally, after so many delays GTA V arrives on PC, even though I already platinumed it on ps3 (for those who only played on ps3 or x360, it's a must play), I had to play the "definitive" version of this wonderful game! Besides the gorgeous graphics, it's very well optimized, and let's wait for the mods xD (I think it's missing a workshop, right Rockstar?) About GTA Online, if you have friends to play with then fun is guaranteed! and I recommend a Headset to play (Especially for the Heists) Overall, it's a complete game, which I believe can please everyone, who likes the GTA series MUST buy it, but if you've never played GTA but like open-world games with plenty of freedom, third-person shooting and FPS, Midnight Club style racing, Ace Combat style flying, being a thief like Payday... or if you've ever dreamed of playing as a family man, a modern CJ, or a psycho... What the fuck are you waiting to buy it???

translation_en: My long experience on PS3 with Grand Theft Auto V and GTA Online leads me to recommend it, simply because it's a tremendous video game in terms of story, gameplay, graphics, music, dialogue, voice acting, etc. But, today I've been called to write this review based on my experience with this long-awaited PC version. Before I start, I must say my expectations weren't clear, since I knew Rockstar would do a great job, but at the same time, the lack of communication about the PC version, the delays, and past experiences (poor optimization of GTA IV) made me somewhat apprehensive regarding GTA V. [h1]Technical Details[/h1] - Takes up 65 GB on the hard drive (currently). Let's remember there are quite frequent content updates, which takes up more hard drive space. - Works properly with both keyboard and mouse, and the Xbox 360 controller for Windows. - Slight fps drops present with my current PC. If you want to see my PC specs, check the info on my profile. [h1]What did I like?[/h1] [olist] [*][b]Performance and required hardware:[/b] As I mentioned before, if the game was going to be as poorly optimized as GTA IV, this wasn't going anywhere. But the big surprise is that, with quite high graphics settings (not maxed out, since I don't have an extremely powerful PC), the video game looks spectacular and, on top of that, I get 60fps all the time. It's simply marvelous, I still can't believe they did such a good job on the optimization. If I have to compare with GTA IV; GTA V looks and runs 100% better than GTA IV. [*][b]New content:[/b] I like that there are more radio stations, more animals, and that, as usual, we can access a ton of car models. [*][b]First person:[/b] One of the things I wanted to try the most was riding around on a bike, but in first person. I think many wanted to do the same thing. It's a formidable experience (until you crash). [*][b]Configuration/Settings:[/b] As the folks at Rockstar mentioned in a recent interview, they've learned that people want to configure the video game to their liking. And GTA V provides a pretty flexible options/settings menu. Because of this, lower-end rigs will probably be able to enjoy this tremendous video game too. [*][b]GTA Online:[/b] If there's one thing many of us suffered with playing on consoles, it was getting into GTA Online. Connecting was truly an odyssey. But in this PC version, I had zero problems from day one, being able to play for about 2 hours with my character transferred from the PS3. I didn't have high latency either, and I was able to waste several players who were just starting out (just to test things like which key activates the c4). [*][b]Character transfer:[/b] I transferred my PS3 character, and something I feared was either that the things I could bring with me to the PC version wouldn't be explained in detail, or that it would fail for technical reasons. Pleasant surprise: Transferring a character was a success, and at each step it explained in detail what things were allowed and what weren't, what would happen to the money I got this way or that way, and what would happen to any previously created character on the PC version. Excellent. [*][b]Rockstar Editor:[/b] Awesome, very user-friendly with great capability and plenty of options to give us an interesting content creation tool. The bad part: In one of the latest updates, a few achievements were added, one of them being uploading 10 videos to YouTube. Seemed a bit exaggerated, but oh well... The Rockstar Editor itself is very polished. [*][b]Steam integration:[/b] Even though it was confirmed there would be achievements, they weren't activated until the game launched. Therefore, some thought maybe there wouldn't be Steam achievements. Well, I'm glad this time we are using the platform where we bought the game in an optimal way. [*][b]It's GTA:[/b] It doesn't even need an introduction. I won't even list what I didn't like next, because there's nothing I didn't like. As someone out there said, when a game is truly good, it'll be a sales success just like it has been on PS3/Xbox360, then on PS4/XboxOne, and now it's being on PC. The reputation speaks for itself, nothing more to add :) [/olist] [h1]What didn't I like?[/h1] [olist] [*][b]Modder detection:[/b] It's very sad to run into some guy, miscalled a "hacker" (since he just uses a mod, he doesn't have an ounce of a hacker in him), with god mode. It's worth noting that I haven't seen this in months, and I hope it stays that way. [/olist] Without a doubt, a total blast. If you want an entertaining story, with charismatic characters and a lot of variety in missions, you have the Grand Theft Auto V campaign. If you want to have a good time with friends, and enemies (why not?), a lot of action, missions, and everything an open-world multiplayer has to offer: Grand Theft Auto Online. If it hooks you, you'll easily spend over 200 hours playing GTAV. I say: [b]Recommended[/b]. Thanks, Rockstar.

translation_en: How can I put it? I played this game on the PS3 for a long time back then. The content is super rich, and you could say it has way too many pros to even list (including all sorts of Newton-crying, anti-physics absurd possibilities that turned what should've been flaws into meme moments players rush to try and even record videos for). Anyway, even though IGN gave it a 10/10, this game isn't "completely without regrets." Overall, it breaks down into pros and cons: Pros: 1. The online mode is full of sincerity—you'll see what I mean once you play it. 2. Honestly, the PC optimization is really good. 3. Even though the game is a few dozen GBs, it's genuinely well-made, and the graphics live up to the file size. 4. The China region pricing is genuinely fair, I'm not even lying. 5. The single-player main story is logical and fun, with well-portrayed characters (especially Trevor, let's count how many times he says FU*K in a day 2333). 6. The single-player side quests also ooze sincerity; all sorts of bizarre and weird missions give players the urge to keep playing. 7. There are three endings for players to choose from. While this kind of setup isn't rare, it's a first for the GTA series. 8. The first-person perspective is a great addition, you can play it like a shooter. 9. There are way too many other pros to list in detail. Cons: 1. The game environment is worrying. Steam turning into Baidu Tieba—is that really okay? 2. The game's physics aren't that amazing, but the super high replayability makes up for it (might be kinda hard to have great physics with a map this big though). 3. No Steam trading cards, huge thumbs down. I wanted that wallpaper of Trevor banging a white chick for my background 2333. 4. Maybe it's just my crappy internet, but the Online mode seems to need a VPN/accelerator to run smoothly. Anyway, this game is definitely worth the money, though I'm guessing a lot of people are gonna fall down the Steam rabbit hole because of it. Gabe Newell's conspiracy is a total victory!

translation_en: Great, great, great. The first time I ever touched Steam was because of this game. It was so insanely popular when it first came out. Great, great, great. Back in 2017, I was a sophomore in high school. A friend introduced me to Steam, and it was the first time I realized you actually had to *pay* for games. My allowance back then was 20 bucks a day—ten for lunch, ten for dinner. I hardcore saved up. Stashed away my lunch money for a week, got 98 bucks, and bought it right away. My friend and I excitedly hopped into the game. Back then, I didn't even know what a smooth framerate was. Playing on integrated graphics at 40 FPS, my friend and I stubbornly pushed through 490 hours. Flipping vehicles on flat ground, blowing myself up with my own grenades—if you can think of a retarded way to die, I’ve done it. But man, back then I actually thought it was so much fun. Sometimes I'd play a whole match, die without firing a single shot, and I was still happy. I just kept playing. Couldn't hit shots? I went and practiced recoil control. I spent so much time watching streams, videos, and playing the game. I flexed being the "Pochinki God at 40 FPS" all through high school, hahahaha. After playing for a while, I wanted to mess around and create some content myself. Alright, so I googled and downloaded a voice changer—called Diamond Voice Changer—planning to troll guys and make some funny moments. Motherfucker, who would've thought that piece of shit had a virus in it? Got me banned instantly. When a bunch of English text suddenly popped up on my screen: "You Have Been Banned From Steam," it honestly scared the shit out of me. I didn't even use hacks! Just think about it, with 40 FPS, how many kills could I possibly get? What kind of high-tier plays could I pull off? At best I’d hit some lucky-ass twitch shots, but what do you do when you're banned? I had no idea what went wrong. I borrowed a friend's account to test it out and see what was up. Logged in, played for a bit, and *bam*, banned again. Appeal failed. Basically said there was unauthorized software running in the background. That narrowed it down and I finally figured it out—fucking voice changer software was the problem. Uninstalled it. Still paranoid, I even wiped and reinstalled my whole operating system. I couldn't borrow friends' accounts anymore either; if those got banned too, I'd have to pay them back. What do I do? Save up again the hard way, scraped together enough for a second, smurf account. My internet was trash back then, 3MB/s, took a whole afternoon just to download. Downloaded it, nervously logged in, and played for a bit—no ban. I finally breathed a sigh of relief. But my heart ached. I barely had any allowance to begin with, and just like that, I threw two 98-buck games down the drain. Sigh. Thinking back on it now, it's still pretty funny. Played nearly 1,000 hours on that smurf account too, but eventually better games came along and I quit. Today I glanced at PUBG in my library, looked at the reviews—mostly just people begging for points with "pet the cat to grow your dick" copypastas. Boring as hell. Figured I'd write one myself. I'm not really good at writing reviews, so I'll just write about my own experience instead, hahahaha. Here's to my lost high school life.

translation_en: [h1] A flawed 2017 PUBG knock-off [/h1] This sh1tshow becomes more and more impossible to play every single time I queue into a new match. And the funniest part is, in DUO, matchmaking can take up to 2-3 minutes + on top of that I have to hang around on a map where a bunch of bots with [b]retarded[/b] AI run all over the place, waiting for more (sub)humans to join. [b]Starting from the top, the cons of this[/b] [strike]magnificent[/strike] [b]game:[/b] [b]1)[/b] I started playing PUBG pretty much right at release and even back then there was a massive amount of cheaters. Has anything changed during the periods I played in 2018/2019/2020/2023? [b] NO, no, and f#ckin' no.[/b] Moreover, everything got even worse, new types of them appeared. From cheats that remove recoil to subtle map hacks showing all players and loot, and of course cheats that let you instantly heal yourself and revive teammates. Yeah, why ban anyone at all when you can throw dust in people's eyes with endless weekly news about how "We have banned a [b]GAJILLION[/b] cheaters, aren't we great." [b]2)[/b] Continuing on the subject of cheaters, there's the magical report system and PUBG's equally mind-blowing support. Throughout my whole playtime since 2023, a report has only worked a couple of times, handing out a ban duration of................ ... [b]3 days.[/b] And that's to someone with a name like HJKDFKSLGG2281337. And what does it cost such people to create a new account now? [b]That's right, nothing, since the game is F2P now[/b]. [b]3)[/b] PUBG used to compete with Fortnite, two battle royales with essentially the same mechanics. Only while Fortnite's style appeals to 10-12 year old kids, PUBG used to be a serious tactical shooter tailored to a military style for an older audience. What do we have now? The exact same garbage skins, emotes, everyone's [strike]beloved[/strike] battle pass system with the most sh1tty recoil and not designed for the average player at all. The skins themselves are naturally made female 99% of the time, as revealing as possible so that some horny kid can beg his mom for money, dump cash into this sh1t, and gawk at a pixelated ass. [b]I guess they only have to milk money this way now.[/b] [b]4)[/b] An absolute degenerate teammate matchmaking system. Why the f#ck do I need a guy with level 20, or even level 1, on my team when I'm level 200? And it works the other way around too, you might get someone with level 800-1400. You'd think, what's wrong with that? Well, the fact that in that case a good half of the players are now the exact same unhinged 800-lvl no-lifes. Furthermore, [b]the same system might throw you into a match with no team at all[/b], despite you choosing to play DUO or SQUAD. Which raises a reasonable question - WHAT THE F#CK? Are bots overloading the system so much that they had to throw in humans instead, or what? Absolute nonsense that I will never understand. [b]5)[/b] A bunch of useless guns and other tactical trash. Those brain-dead Chinese devs added their nation's weapons, plus tactical gear, sh1t-grenades, and... chips... Starting with the guns. There are 5 different shotguns in the game, or 6 if you count the sawed-off. And why? Not only do most kills happen with assault rifles and sniper rifles according to their own stats, but this is also completely unbalanced sh1t that can one-shot you from almost 50 meters away. Then there are another 5 assault rifles in 7.62 caliber and 8(!!!) in 5.56. Who even needs this kind of "variety"? There are basically no differences between them, and some are just outright diarrhea. A mortar that is the pinnacle of uselessness, an autistic panzerfaust, 4 motherf#cking useless melee weapons, a decoy grenade that does practically no damage, a sticky bomb that ruins the whole setting, a "zone" grenade, and C4 that kills everything except enemies while beeping across half the map with a radius from 0.1 meters to 2 trillion light years, depending on your luck (which you don't have). As for the tactical gear, I don't get it at all; this was supposed to be a battle royale, not Rainbow Six Siege or some f#cking CoD. And chips that let you revive people, I think that's complete madness. Now it's not enough to just kill a guy, you actually have to wipe out his whole squad or reach his corpse and carry this chip away with you, which by the way takes up inventory space. And you can't even always pull that off for many reasons. [i]I'm not against variety, but what I described feels like complete nonsense to me, an attempt to artificially create choices in a dying game.[/i] ------------------------------------------------ Honestly, I could go on forever. Describe the bugs, the game's community, the fact that hit registration doesn't always work, and so on and so forth, but I just don't have the energy for it anymore.[b] Any pros that might be left wouldn't outweigh the cons no matter what.[/b] Friends got me back into the game, but who knows for how long. Personally, I'm going to try and finish the remaining achievements and drop it forever. Although considering everything written above, either I'll run out of energy to play this, or my patience will snap from yet another headshot death by an 800-lvl guy shooting with zero recoil and instantly snapping to targets. [b]It's a real shame that a game with such potential was sold to Asians for pennies, and now they're just milking a dead cow named PUBG[/b]

[/h1] [hr][/hr] After 2800 hours in this wonderful game [spoiler](dumpster fire)[/spoiler], I can tell you with confidence how things actually work here: [list] [*]Cheaters have been here since 2017, with waves coming and going in 2018/2019/2020/2021 and up until January 2022 (back when the game was a paid version for 900 rubles and ~700 rubles on sale), followed by the transition to a free-to-play F2P model with an additional premium version for new players costing 929 rubles, while those who bought it earlier got the premium version for free. If you accidentally kill such a player knowing they are cheating, oops, you can't report them during the fight anymore... The game doesn't have an option to report a player after you've killed them. You have to record the match, find a forum, submit a report somewhere on there so they might get banned later... Who the fuck needs to waste time on that? [*]However, if you regularly donate to the game and use cheats at the same time, you are not considered a cheater. I went flying into space on a motorcycle. Bugs. A lot of bugs. But it was fun. Servers are struggling. December 2017 - January 2018 Official release out of alpha. 3M+ online. No, wait. A very weird map, didn't vibe with it, but Asians are happy (shocker, right?). For New Year's, Vikendi was added. Cold, but interesting. Still fun. 2019 Very many cheaters. Parkour added. Not as fun anymore and matches get way sweatier. Skins that you can't even sell or trade. 2020 Cheaters. Cheaters. Cheaters. In every single match there are übermenschen who have been playing PUBG all their lives, know what's going on where, and give you no room for error. New (v2) ranking system, you can't choose your map. Bots in normal mode. The game is dead. Some indie garbage like Fall Guys or Among Us pulls in more concurrent players during prime time than once-beloved PUBG. The devs shit the bed completely and preferred to invest money in golden pools and PUBG Mobile rather than developing the desktop version and fighting cheaters. All that's left is a bad aftertaste, the realization that a game I spent 1,100+ hours in is unplayable if you just want to kick back and relax. Or actually get any enjoyment out of it. 10/10 until 2019 3/10 now. Do not recommend. But it's worth a try. After all, only a true samurai can endure such pain and suffering) Ps. Didn't play 2021-2023)

translation_en: I think it's time to say goodbye to PUBG! I first came across this game back in 2017, and it had a huge pull for me. I was a college sophomore back then, and after hearing about it from a classmate, I fell madly in love with it. The tense lobby music from back then is still echoing in my ears. My laptop at the time couldn't handle this masterpiece at all, so that entire summer I went to the internet cafe downstairs every single day. I remember the game wasn't even standard in internet cafes yet, so every time I went I had to spend half an hour installing it myself. That half-hour was pure torture, but at the time I felt it was totally worth the wait. What I loved about the game was the realism and the thrill. The realistic physics engine they built back then was their pride and joy—the near-realistic ballistic trajectories, weather changes, vehicles, and so on were just so damn charming. What was also unforgettable back then were the official apologies from the PUBG devs. Because the game was so insanely popular, a massive wave of players like me flooded in and crashed the servers. This even made someone like me who never used Weibo download it just to hound the devs every time it crashed, hahaha. I remember the devs apologizing every single day back then, but we were still happy as hell to keep playing. I took on a part-time job just to earn money so I could play PUBG every day and bought a new laptop. Why did I quit the game later on? First of all, it's the overwhelming amount of hackers. They've been getting more and more brazen, and of course, a lot of that is due to the devs doing jack shit and letting it happen. On top of that, I don't know what the fuck is wrong with the game's developers nowadays—instead of properly optimizing and developing the game, they've actually started selling skins! To put it simply, the PUBG devs have gotten just as shitty as Tencent! Today's PUBG has lost the vibe it used to have! Don't have much time, just wanted to put my angry feelings into words!!!

translation_en: Everybody remembers when PUBG blew up and the servers were bursting with millions of players. Here is what has happened to the game over more than 5 years: Originally, the game had a ton of problems that came straight from the alpha, but they kept feeding us breakfast bullshit, promising that "we'll fix everything, we'll patch everything up, blah blah blah." It never went past talking because no matter how hard the developers supposedly tried to fix bugs, new outfits kept showing up in the store instead. Now we know what they were busy with all this time. If you dig a little deeper into the technical side, PUBG is made on UE4—an incomparable, beautiful engine where multiplayer can be made enjoyable for both the client and the server (take ARK, Fortnite, Insurgency). Having played all three of the aforementioned games, I can say that engine limitations have nothing to do with it; what matters is how data replication between the client and server is handled to create the illusion of playing with each other (yeah, right). So. Ever since the alpha, PUBG was a garbage implementation of this, but it was forgivable because the project didn't have to explain its smallness. But even in the alpha, a million players rushed in, they couldn't open servers fast enough, and the game was NOT DESIGNED for that kind of concurrent player count. Okay, they patched it up with duct tape and crutches, it was playable, even though you constantly had to restart the lobby, the game itself, and put up with packet loss and a kiloton of bugs both visual and technical. From the minimum system requirements, you'd think we're launching a satellite into space and all calculations are going to be processed locally. Why? Because the client side of the game will eat all your resources, yet it's still limited by the server's response. My hardware is three times better than recommended, but I still frequently drop to 40 fps, and I'm far from playing on max settings. Well, let's get back to the game: Now the project is no longer small, players brought in enough donations to remake the game properly from scratch. That didn't happen. They decided to tweak the current project instead of remaking it right. But they did find great managers who handle microtransactions and are in charge of the money. Well, okay, let's fix what we have, it's gonna take a while, but it's necessary—those were the words spoken back in 2018. After saying that, the devs realized it was pointless and, although they put up a front of working, NOTHING changed. They managed to fix one thing, and another broke. They improved and optimized player connections to sessions, but made life hell for people with connection errors (the game JUST crashes). There are countless examples like this, but look at what happened to the game over the past year: The company realized nobody is gonna put up with this shit they call a game, so they poured money into the mobile version and abandoned this one. BUT to hide it, they played it very smart—players left, and to attract new ones... Let's make the game free-to-play! There are still not enough players and you have to wait a long time for a match on a specific map... The conclusion—remove map selection. Still not enough players filling up a full lobby within a certain time frame? Let's throw in bots. Even in normal matches. This project is on the verge of death, but they're still trying to squeeze the last pennies out of it by adding battle passes, crates, keys, skins, anything except real actions to improve the gameplay. I didn't even touch upon the topic of cheaters, whom they've also given up on—that hurts even more, but even the cheaters have left this game. What do we have now? The only people left in the game are those who make money off it—streamers, esports players, check it out, a couple of beer-drinking factory Joes, and bots. A metric fuckload of paid skins in the store, loot boxes, and other crap. I'm waiting for PUBG to die. If you want to start playing, don't. This project was born with good intentions, but was sold out for money to make even more money. The game is trash*

Of course, ruining your life over shit like this is a low-probability event anyway. What I care about more, comparatively speaking, is: if the game I bought becomes unplayable, who do I go to for compensation? Perfect World or Tencent? But I guess in the end, it'll just mean we players who insist on buying genuine games take a total loss for nothing. Take the 2018 WeGame version of *Monster Hunter: World*, for instance. The game was delisted, a bunch of players supporting domestic industries insisted on not getting refunds, and in the end, Tencent swallowed the money, probably leaving them to be heavily mocked by real-life pirating snobs. Games belong to the ninth art. Any blockbuster game inherently contains the author's thoughts and philosophy. Amidst the collision and blending of various ideological cultures, foreign reflections on the future and countless bizarre fantasies are simply unacceptable to the SARFT and the Ministry of Culture. If the authorities won't accept them, the real question is whether the players can accept them. As things stand right now in the domestic gaming market, constrained by Steam and various console factors, you can still make a boatload of cash by just making trash. They know that as long as the game's quality is barely passable, and they design some flashy "micro-operations" to show off, along with all sorts of horny character art, edgy character models, and cringy dialogue, they can scam people out of their money. The game's plot has to be nonsense, without any depth—simple and easy to understand. It's even better if you stir up a bunch of drama, good or bad, to trigger public outcry. A typical example would be *Tower of Fantasy*—you guys must have gorged on that gossip, right? At the same time, pump out some ads and push a marketing campaign. This kind of production actually makes way more money than a game you spent serious time plotting and making. Even though a lot of people in China seem to know about Steam now, back before *PUBG* came out, if you walked down the street, hardly anyone knew what Steam even was. Back in the day, a domestic single-player game developer made a martial arts game and submitted it for review. Because they were a domestic developer, they knew the censorship mechanism inside and out, so before submitting, they removed blood and dismemberment effects, and turned all the corpses black. But even so, it still failed review. The censors said that the player character in this game only had to serve ten days in prison after killing someone, which could easily cause a negative social impact. Later on, through endless revisions, it basically turned into a martial arts game where you can only ride horses. Meanwhile, Tencent's *Moonlight Blade* has zero consequences after slaughtering human enemies; you can just keep on butchering them. Doesn't that create a worse social impact? Yet *Moonlight Blade* passed review. Why does this happen? Tencent makes a fortune every single day; they can afford the fees and can keep making mistakes through trial and error. But that small developer had no money left after finishing the game, and just dropped dead on the spot. Therefore, the development of Chinese single-player games doesn't depend on your production quality, nor does it depend on whether your marketing is on point—it depends first on whether you can afford to pay off the gatekeepers. The original intention of the Great Firewall was good: to resist the output of Western ideology, consolidate the ideological high ground, and reduce the invasion of harmful culture. But unreasonable policies have made it difficult for the domestic gaming industry to develop. And precisely because of this reason, many people have come to take this shit for granted. Now, thinking about it carefully, has the function of the Firewall deviated from its original purpose? The wall was meant to block decadent culture, but now, it also blocks out excellent games, allowing certain domestic decadent capital to effortlessly suck the blood of all players without any pressure. The wall has been used by some as a tool for reaping exorbitant profits, and this country's gaming market has been turned by a certain group into a breeding ground for corruption. As an ordinary gamer who loves Steam and loves the joy Steam brings: a one-size-fits-all approach is fast, but it treats the symptoms rather than the disease.
