translation_en: Hello everyone. Today I've decided to write my first review for a game like PUBG. I've played this game for 950 hours. I won't say I play amazingly, but I still understand a thing or two about this masterpiece. Right off the bat, I suggest looking at the pros and cons of this project separately. Let's start with the pros: 1) As for me, it's the ability to play with friends in a squad. Thanks to this mode, you can get a pretty hefty dose of fun and memorable emotions. 2) The game mechanics, thanks to which you can shoot realistically with all types of weapons (I mean the presence of recoil). Unfortunately, I can't name any more pros. Cons: 1) The game is full of bugs and flaws. 2) The presence of a huge number of "cheaters" in the game. 3) There are 4 maps in the game, but you can only play without issues on "Erangel" and "Sanhok". To get into "Vikendi" or "Miramar", you have to wait a long time until it finally puts you in a match there. Honestly, I consider these 2 maps dead. 4) During your playtime, you might experience constant game crashes to the desktop, or alternatively, you might get hit with the message: "Connection lost". Personally, this pissed me off a lot. 5) Now regarding the weapons: god knows how damage registration works in this game; sometimes your hits with any weapon just won't register, sometimes you randomly take a headshot—in short, it's an inexplicable mess. 6) Sometimes it happens that, for example, you drive up to an airdrop, arrive, sit down to loot, and you get run over by your own car, which decided to keep driving instead of obediently stopping next to you. 7) It happens that when you drop and start looking for a weapon, you never find it after looting a significant number of rooms, while your enemy finds one right after landing. 8) It happens, and quite often at that, that you jump to one end of the map, and the zone constantly pulls to the complete opposite end. 9) All the extra content in the game is paid; players who bought this game and just play it have never been given anything for free and, as it seems to me, never will be. Anyway, this list could go on for a very long time, but I'll probably stop at the fact that yesterday I got hit with a permanent ban for reasons unknown. Let me just say straight away that I'm not a cheater, and I didn't do anything forbidden or illegal in the game. I wrote to support, but I don't think it'll help. So draw your own conclusions—whether to buy this "Korean masterpiece" for 900 rubles or live and play other normal projects in peace is entirely up to you. If you think my review is amateurish, or conversely, if you liked it, write it all in the comments. That's all from me, thanks everyone for your attention.

Half a year ago, my long-time Steam account got banned because it was hacked and used for cheating. I hadn't set up Steam Guard (that's on me for lacking account security awareness, I take responsibility for that), but my appeals to official support were rejected three times. Game ID: PHyyy- Three months ago, my girlfriend logged into the game at an internet cafe and got instantly banned. We later found out it was a hardware-ban by association because someone had cheated on that exact PC at the cafe. Multiple appeals to official support went nowhere. She had nearly 2,000 hours of playtime and a huge inventory (I bought her a ton of skins). Game ID: LHyyy- Just the day before yesterday, seeing the Steam Summer Sale, my girlfriend said since it was on sale and she hadn't played in a while, we should buy new copies to play. So my girlfriend and I each bought another copy of this trash game, *PUBG*. Last night (July 1, 2019), we played for a few hours. When I logged on during the day today, I was banned for absolutely no reason. In one of the matches, I was caught in a pincer attack between two players. Within a few seconds, I turned around and killed the enemy behind me, then snapped around to kill the enemy in front. I guess that must be the reason for the ban, because apart from that, I can't think of any other possible reason. Game ID: Lidexun-Daddy I have submitted another appeal to official support. To add one thing: neither my girlfriend nor I used any cheats, mouse macros, or any other kind of illegal software bullshit. If we did, my whole family can drop dead. Regardless of whether this appeal does anything, I am sick to death of *PUBG*, and I find the ban measures of Korean company Bluehole and BATTLEEYE utterly laughable. No matter what, I will never touch this absolute trash game again. I can understand that during a sale, a ton of cheaters buy new accounts to ruin the game environment (I despise cheaters with a passion myself), and that Bluehole steps up cheat detection during this time. But I genuinely, truly cannot understand Bluehole’s "tyrannical," "dictatorial" ban policy of "better to wrongfully execute a thousand than let one escape." Comrade Deng Xiaoping said it best: "It doesn't matter if a cat is black or white, as long as it catches mice, it's a good cat." Seeing many friends with similar experiences to mine—regardless of whether those friends actually cheated or not—I am willing to give them the benefit of the doubt. We are just tiny, insignificant consumers. If we really wanted to protect our rights over tens, hundreds, or thousands of bucks, or just to vent our anger, most of us don't have the time or energy. That is why Bluehole is so arrogant. I hope someone will step up and sue this company, just like the person who once sued China Mobile over a dozen yuan, and I will definitely give whatever support I can. translation_en: Friendly advice to China: The internet is full of games that scam kids out of their money and walk away, and you do nothing. Look at the images on web ads all over the domestic internet—every single one of them is more exposed than Steam, and you don't give a shit, yet you come after Steam. You've got the time and leisure, why don't you manage the Chinese film industry? It's more deformed than Lu Benwei. Look at your CCTV, then look at someone else's BBC. What a gap. You stomp on the cultural confidence you built up yourselves, and why? Because you refuse to reform your management style, and instead drag a huge platform down with you. Even though many Chinese players just treat Steam as a game launcher, it at least gave everyone some awareness of buying legit. Just as we're finally making some progress, we're about to be knocked back to square one. Are you encouraging people to pirate games? Not even talking about so-called democracy, why can't you have a rating system? A rating system would solve most of these issues. Do you think this is fun? You experts are truly galaxy-brained. But I guess in the end, it'll just mean us players who insist on buying legit take a total loss, and then we'll get mocked by some real-life pirating superiority-complex grandpas. Galaxy-brained. Fucking awesome, my country, hehe. Emperor Qin, this prosperous era is just as you wished. Some people and their friends grew up playing Legend and CS as kids, and none of them went around hacking people to death or committing crimes. Nowadays, bratty kids watch Pleasant Goat and roast other kids—is that really the fault of games and anime, or is it the fault of irresponsible parenting and schooling? Everyone knows the truth in their hearts. Just like that, you've abandoned the goal of 100 years of socialism? What is the Chinese Dream? Study hard and get the fuck out of the country. Games belong to the ninth art. Any blockbuster game inherently contains the author's thoughts and philosophy, but for our country's currently closed-off values, foreign reflections on the future and bizarre fantasies are just unacceptible to the SARFT. As for domestic games right now, due to Steam and console factors, you can still make a ton of cash just by making garbage. They know that as long as the game quality is barely passable, and they design some "micro-operation" flexing mechanics, all kinds of softcore horny character art, and various chuunibyou character models and lines, they can scam people out of money. The game's plot has to be trashy, it can't have any depth, it has to be simple and easy to understand. That kind of production makes way more money than a game where you actually put serious thought into the plot and execution. Steam might seem like a lot of people know about it in China, but honestly, before PUBG came out, if you walked down the street, hardly anyone knew what Steam even was. In fact, China's real-name verification is already ahead of foreign countries. UnionPay and WeChat Pay both require an ID card, so why hasn't a rating policy been rolled out yet? Because right now, whether something passes review is entirely up to the Ministry of Culture and the SARFT—there are no relevant laws or regulations to determine whether a game passes review. There was once a domestic single-player game developer that made a wuxia game and submitted it for review. Because they were a domestic developer, they knew the censorship mechanism very well, so before submitting, they removed blood and dismemberment effects, and turned all the corpses black. But even then it couldn't pass. The censors said that the player character in this game could just go to prison for ten days after killing someone, which easily creates a bad social impact. Later on, through edits and more edits, it turned into a wuxia game where you can only ride horses. Meanwhile, Tencent's Moonlight Blade lets you slaughter human enemies without facing any consequences, letting you just keep on butchering them. Doesn't that create a much worse social impact? Yet Moonlight Blade passed review. Why is that? Tencent makes a fortune every day; they can afford to pay. That small developer didn't have much money left after finishing the game. So the development of Chinese single-player games isn't about how good your production quality is, nor is it about whether your marketing hits the mark—it's about whether you can afford to pay up first. And what do relevant Chinese departments claim their basis for censorship is? It's the so-called social mainstream, the Socialist Core Values. What does this kind of thing feel like? Ancient monarchs would always find a statement that sounded legally and theoretically sound to justify their power: the Mandate of Heaven, "I am the True Dragon," all my power is bestowed upon me by the heavens. And the Socialist Core Values act as a tool for that exact purpose—giving themselves an outwardly reasonable statement for illegitimate, unlawful power and the benefits they acquire. Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Macao are Special Administrative Regions. Their social, economic, political, and cultural systems are all different from the mainland. Has everyone ever thought about why that is? It's actually very simple: the crying baby gets the milk. Take Hong Kong, for example—if they had adopted the mainland system back when it returned in '97, they would have had massive strikes and school boycotts, bringing normal society to a halt. Plus, at the time, many eyes both domestic and international were watching Hong Kong, so they became a Special Administrative Region. And what about us mainlanders? When they blocked foreign websites, we endured it. When they censored World of Warcraft, we endured that too. We've never spoken up for our own rights. And now they're escalating further: the Steam China version is about to come out. The best-case scenario is that we get a Chinese store version, and all existing CN region payment methods and regional pricing discounts get transferred over there. If we silently endure this time, what about next time? I'm afraid we're going to turn into the North Korean Gwangmyong network. A lot of people treat all these things as a matter of course—whether it's blocking foreign websites, censoring games, *Baozou Dashijian*, or now the Steam China version. But the reality? In Europe, there are terrorist activities happening on Instagram and Twitter. Did they just simply build a firewall to block these social media apps? No, they wage cyber warfare against those terrorists and drive them off those social media platforms. If that's the case, why can't the CCP do it? Is it just because building a firewall is cheaper? Are our rights and our places for entertainment and leisure worth less than the cost of a cyber battle? Do Chinese people just have to compromise and endure while foreigners get to protect their rights? Please spread these words far and wide. Speak up for your rights and for Steam. I don't know which version of "being represented" is better: the kind where they ban and censor World of Warcraft, *Baozou Dashijian*, and other free media, social apps, and single-player/online games, and then claim it's the will of the people and the players; or whether the stuff I'm posting today represents the interests of Steam players. But I know that everything I'm saying here comes from the bottom of my heart, spoken with mixed feelings after going through all this shit. I'm speaking with a clear conscience, whereas they aren't necessarily doing the same. I hope everyone spreads these words. I know 9/10 times it won't do anything, but how can you not cry out just because your voice is small? As an ordinary resident living in China who loves Steam and loves the joy Steam brings, this is all I can do. Thank you everyone. Actually, being an obedient subject has zero benefits and all downsides. Because if you show obedience, they need to provide you with even less. Since you've already expressed your submission, why would they give a shit about your needs? But so-called unruly rabble? To maintain their rule and appease the populace, the things they have to provide are naturally a lot more. We see this domestically: when they blocked foreign websites and censored games, we submitted. And the result? The Steam China version is about to drop. Because you've already expressed your submission, they definitely figured, "Just release it, they'll keep submitting anyway." Whenever I think about the First Amendment of the United States and how Steam, this platform of free speech, allows me to voice my thoughts here, while the CCP is about to launch Steam China and take all of that away, I get mixed feelings. Honestly, the things I want by speaking out aren't much. I'm not delusional in thinking that capitalism means life will magically get better or whatever—you still gotta work hard yourself, you still gotta grind for a dozen years to buy a house and a car. All I want are fewer restrictions and controls, and for the government to respect citizens' rights. But even something as simple as that is so fucking hard. A hundred years ago in Beijing, Qing dynasty subjects were helping foreigners set up ladders to climb over the wall, and a hundred years today, foreigners are helping Chinese people set up ladders to climb over the wall. Because saying I don't like it after 1100 hours would be bullshit; it definitely has things that drew us in. But I just can't stand the company's practices anymore. Bad optimization? We upgrade our hardware. High ping? We use accelerators. Even when it comes to shooting games having cheaters, which is totally normal and I'm sure many of you are the same, this is the most **cheater**-coddling game I have ever seen, completely abandoning and leaving the Asian region unmoderated. (As for the ones they ban, my ass they can't recover their accounts. Besides, those were reported by us players, because the game's own detection system is a complete joke to me.) NA and EU players might still have a nice, scenic environment, but I'm done playing babysitter in this Asian breeding ground, with black-market accounts everywhere, flying orphans all over the damn place, and a dev company that only knows how to pump out skins. Let's talk about the journey with this game. Got hooked starting from H1Z1 (of course, PUBG now is walking down the exact same dead end as H1Z1). Back then it was still really fun; even if you couldn't get a chicken dinner, four people rolling together was a blast. Then cheats and hacks started showing up. Back then they weren't too rampant yet, and cheaters were just as mentally retarded as always, so "immortal cultivators" could still be dealt with. Later on, friends I knew started leaving one by one—either quitting because of cheaters, or joining "them" and then quitting. I'll just use a timeline for this transition period (to avoid repeating myself), mainly to see if many of you are just like me. Asia server falls → Korean/Japanese servers → Japanese server shuts down → SEA server → back to Korean server → Russian server about to open → changing IP to enter Russian server → Russian server falls. That's basically how it went. ---------------------------- The last paragraph is pretty pissed off, purely to vent. If you don't want to read it, you can leave. I've been wanting to say this for a long time: if I were hacking, I wouldn't even deserve to be called a man if I didn't wipe 80 of you motherfuckers in a single match. Stop fucking acting, that single-point gunshot sound, abnormal fire rate, impossible angles—you might fool some noobs, but that's it. Like those huya-numbers/letters, douyu-numbers/letters, and those awkward Chinglish names, pinyin + birthday. When they are spamming the kill feed back-to-back (let me add a qualifier here so I don't generalize too many players, that's not what I mean, it's just that most cheaters are like this), I don't even fucking want to watch the replay! Anyone with an asshole can see what their real skill level is. Without cheats, they're dumber than dogs; the least they could do is at least be in my scope, right? I'm begging you guys, stop humiliating the Chinese, go learn from the great Korean nation next door instead. Someone's probably gonna wonder why I didn't list QQ numbers—at least those guys are fucking blatant! Instant-killing everything in sight the moment they see you, true men don't pretend, fucking legends!

translation_en: I'm pretty much an early adopter of this game. This is already my third account to get banned, absolutely fucking laughable. The first two times were honestly just soul-crushing, but my friends asked me to squad up so I bought it again. I'm a CSGO player, and when I first started playing, with around a hundred hours in, PUBG felt pretty easy to me. But later on, I started dying right after landing all the time. Back then I had no idea what cheats were, but I eventually found out—all sorts of aimbots, bullet tracking, wallhacks, completely frying my brain. My first account had around 1,000 hours, and back in July 2017, I got hit with a 100-year ban. I played at home, never went to internet cafes, didn't use mouse macros or plugins, and never once cheated or used any third-party software. My K/D over 100 matches was around 3.8. I mean, I'm a 3-year veteran of CSGO, so anyone who plays CSGO should get where I'm coming from. Fine, I got banned. Back then there was no appeal channel, so tough shit, I had to swallow the bitter pill. Three months later, I bought another account. That was when skins started coming out, and I was obsessed with outfits, so I topped up and bought the trench coat, red sneakers, red scarf, and various weapon skins, spending around 10,000 RMB. When I hit 1,136 hours, it was during one of Bluehole's massive ban waves, so there were fewer cheaters those few days. Playing as a 4-man squad, our win rate was around 60%, getting 15+ kills almost every game. We played for two days and must have racked up 300 or 400 kills. On the third morning, after breakfast, I turned on my PC and got a permanent VAC ban. My heart was utterly crushed. I used to see people spamming "false ban" on PUBG's official Weibo and thought they were just in denial. Now I finally get how they feel. My account worth over 10,000 RMB just got ruthlessly banned like that. I can't even describe the feeling. I couldn't believe my eyes. I launched the game and the screen told me I was permanently banned by Steam. My whole body went limp. I quit the game for seven months. Then in 2018, I bought another account to squad up with my old teammates, and started buying skins again, dropping a few thousand RMB on gold AKM, SKS, M416, various gun skins, and scarves. Until around 600 hours in, boom, another permanent VAC ban. I just let out a bitter chuckle for a few minutes. I guess this is just Bluehole's way of a cash grab—banning normal players, then dropping new modes to lure you into buying a new account. Not this time. From two years ago up until now, cheaters still exist, they're just not as rampant as before. But when it comes to the final circle, you gotta die. Two years ago when the game first launched, I could understand the anti-cheat mechanics being immature, but it's been two years. And do you guys at Bluehole have any fucking clue how much pain it causes the countless people whose accounts get hacked, used for cheating, and then get banned by the time they recover them? You'll never get those days back. Those fun times fighting for airdrops, hot-dropping, playing hide and seek, and trolling people. Back then this game was super lively, everyone loved to talk. Now everyone's tight-lipped. Why is that??? People's mentalities are dead. Goodbye, trash PUBG. Hope you fucking die early. Keep running your business like this, and the world will forget you even sooner.

translation_en: I want to keep this review very open, to express my opinion, so to speak. I'm writing it because this was the absolute last straw. I've simply run out of patience. Previously I didn't want to leave any review for this game, since it's super addictive and I play it a lot, I like it, but it doesn't deserve a positive review. So yeah. My patience snapped after the release of the latest updates for this game. We all already damn well know about the huge amount of bugs and unfinished garbage in this game, but I'll still mention them a bit below. In the latest update, which introduced the ranking system, something went wrong. First of all, the developers removed the ability to choose a server, meaning it automatically connects me to the server that supposedly suits me best. I don't know if it's because of this or not, but my ping jumped from an average of 60 ms to an average of 110-120 ms. Even though the ping went up, I didn't notice any drastic changes in connection stability, but as we know, in games of this type every little detail matters. Second of all, I don't understand what kind of dumbassery went into making it take 4-5 minutes to find a match. That's way too long for a game with this player base. Yay, the next day they fixed it somehow, but my ass was burning furiously from the long matchmaking times. Third of all, the fps tanked really hard. Playing is sometimes completely impossible, at the most crucial moment fps drops to 20-30, especially in gunfights or just in cities. With every update the average fps gets lower and lower, even though when I first bought the game, everything was great with fps. So great that I played on medium graphic settings and with almost no stutters, and now things are so bad that with the exact same PC setup I've squeezed graphics settings down to absolute minimum and I get severe stuttering. These three points forced me to write a negative review for this game. Now let's move on to the overall cons. The game has been out for a year and a half, and it looks super raw. I bought this game in January 2018, as soon as it left beta. Playing it was an absolute pleasure and without stutters, at first. Plus major crates used to drop that paid for the cost of the game within a week. But then they started rolling out updates that made things worse and worse. It would've been better if they hadn't introduced anything and just left it as it is, at least there would've been stability. As the main cons I can highlight the following: lack of optimization, terrible game code, and a huge number of cheaters. A game with this kind of player scale and cash flow, yet everything looks so sad. It seems like they're fighting cheaters (or making it look like they are), but in reality their numbers aren't decreasing. Yeah, I agree, this is a pretty standard problem for all modern online games. But if they at least fixed the first two main problems that would be great. I can also highlight the pros of the game, which make me want to play it. First of all is the execution of the game itself. The concept itself is implemented really coolly. No matter what I play, what mods or games like battle royales, PUBG surpasses them. Secondly, I really like the weapon system (though not the hit registration system - it's awful). Namely, gun shooting, reloading, fire modes, various weapon quirks (for example, the ability to release the spoon on a grenade). I get a massive rush from shooting bolt-action rifles (Kar98k, M24, AWM), specifically from the shots and reload animations. In that regard, the gun system really hit the spot for me. Thirdly, the hit point system, a huge amount of various heals and boosters, the implementation of a partial HP bar if the player was wounded, and reviving a player if you're in a squad. Fourthly, everything else - the interface, the maps (not including the vehicle driving system here because it's garbage), solo and squad modes (you want to play alone, you want to play in a party - it mostly depends on you, not on the team like in most online games), the training mode (implemented really coolly) and so on. In conclusion I'll say, I really didn't want to leave a review like this. But what can you do? How else do you get through to the developers? Who have a shit ton of money, but no one wants to do anything, for a year and a half already. They do everything just for show, very clunkily and unfinished. If this game gets polished, it has potential, people will play it, if all the holes and bugs are fixed, or even better, some aspects are completely redone (instead of adding skins and skin-farming systems). Of course, if your nerves are more important to you, I by no means recommend buying this game at this price. I hope that in the distant, distant future this game will be reworked for the better and I'll edit this review. Yeah, I hope for that, even though deep down inside I understand that's hardly ever gonna happen. I give the game 5 shit-sitting Uzi-wielding sons out of 10.

translation_en: I hate to say it, but I was hoping the game would change over the last 6 months. That never happened and because of that I also believe it never will. At first, the fun and satisfaction of killing a few enemies was the reward for putting up with its many flaws, poor optimization, and horrendous server performance, but after these months, things are still the same or worse. Sure, it's fun, but only if you don't take it seriously, if you jump in and are willing to die—sometimes without even knowing where you got shot from—and repeat it over and over again. Simply put, this game has every single evil a multiplayer game can have: - Bad optimization (Even if you have a 1080ti the frame drops are huge and sometimes it crashes) - Server lag (The most absurd I've ever seen) - Hackers (They run rampant and I doubt they get banned) - Bugs that can be annoying or sometimes even kill you (And they've been there since the beta) - No level-based matchmaking (In fact, there is no level system at all) - There are loot boxes you earn with in-game points (And you have to pay to open them, but you can get any piece of shit) - They already shoved a $10 pass down our throats, <<just to unlock>> some crappy clothes (And they're sure to keep selling us more) - Character customizations and faces are the exact same as the beta. Anyway, I repeat, I dreamed of a PUBG that actually worked well, like any paid game with millions in the bank, with innovation in its gameplay elements, with passion from its developers, with a game that was a pleasure to play, and where every time you die you aren't left with that feeling that the game just does whatever the fuck it wants. As pros, I could say that the gunplay feels really good, the visuals are quite pretty, and the hits and animations are well done. If all of that worked the way it should, I'd encourage you to buy it, but... I cannot recommend this game if you want to have fun shooting people. Look for any other Battle Royale or Shooter, because there are actually some really good free-to-play ones running even better than this. If all of the above doesn't seem like enough to you, go ahead, but you've been warned.

translation_en: First of all, I want to say one thing. Right now I'm abstracting myself from the game's problems and will say why this game is good. -The battle royale mode is implemented very well in the game, the feeling of anxiety and danger never leaves you (mostly in solo, in squad you're a bit more relaxed, more on that later). The enemy can be anywhere. -Head-on clashes with an opponent are always a game of cunning (if it's a skilled opponent), who will outflank, trick, and confuse whom, unfortunately the gunfights themselves aren't all that interesting (more on that later too). -Many publications, reviewers, and players say that this game breeds cool, funny, and dumb situations, and they are right. It doesn't happen in every single match, but definitely in every third one: either some dude drives a UAZ onto a roof, then climbs down and starts tearing circles around the courtyard honking, or you chase a guy with a frying pan for three minutes, or run around a church with a shotgun after someone (at moments like these "Yakety Sax" plays in my head), or you're left with two other people and they have better weapons than you while you only found a Colt and you come out of the fight victorious, or you're ramming cars with another player Mad Max style, or half the server shows up at a drop and complete fucking chaos ensues. -The feeling of victory. I'll be totally honest, I've never won in all my time, but I was veeeery close to it, and what happens to you when you're left one-on-one... Your heart beats like crazy, you sweat as if you're in a sauna, not every game can give you emotions like that. -The game is capable of paying for itself, for example I've already paid off half of mine. No matter how hard you try, you just can't turn a blind eye to the problems. -Oh, this problem gets beaten to death forever... You see, the kicker is that when you look at the game's system requirements you expect a corresponding level of visuals, but not in PUBG's case. Graphics are straight out of 2012. Someone will say: but this is a multiplayer game and such games are hard to make. You're right, but when you look at the graphics of Arma 3 or, say, Battlefield 4 and you can play on high-medium without frame drops, you realize someone here is drop-dead clumsy. Yes, I know they've even launched a campaign and a FIXPUBG website now, which is commendable, but the latest update that adds minor optimization raises a ton of questions. After patch 19, many players couldn't go anywhere past the lobby, it just froze. Yeah, they fixed it quickly then, but what's next, did optimization increase? And here's the most interesting part: some people actually got a higher FPS, some by 10, some by 5, some by 15 (there were funny people who had 145 FPS and thought it was optimized so much it went up to 200, even though the devs increased the max FPS cap), but for others, things got way worse, and I was one of them. Now I have a new graphics card and it plays fine, but before patch 19 everything worked more or less okay on the old GPU, after the update everything went to shit – long loading times, stuttering while aiming, while opening inventory, frame drops became more frequent, textures and objects started loading slower. To make the game playable, I had to drop all settings to absolute zero, every single parameter, after which playing became both comfortable and uncomfortable at the same time: the FPS became stable, but I can't see shit, everything is a blurry, jagged mess. Why such discrepancies? It's not clear. I thought it was because the game re-downloaded the game client (and here's another funny fact: for some players the update weighed differently, for some 10GB, for some 9.5 or 9.3, for me it was 16.9 altogether, moreover, initially it was 9.5, after downloading it decided to download again but already 16.9... And then it decided to download again :D). I thought that uninstalling and re-downloading the game would fix everything, but alas, I can't say if that helped. I don't know if it helped at all, I already had a new GPU by then, maybe it helps some people. -The servers are shit, all lag also depends on the server. Even on the new graphics card there are sometimes drops, and I can tell by how fast the game loaded – if it loaded right at the moment of the plane flight, then expect lag. Mmmm, and the netcode – hit registration is not always working, often bullets land when you are ALREADY behind cover (feels like bullets are made in Estonia, they don't trigger right away). What can we even talk about when the connection drops in the LOBBY, this is just the game menu but an error can pop up right there. And now for the problems that aren't as critical, but some of them are infuriating. -Explain to me please, which dumbass came up with the idea that when you pick up a weapon, it's unloaded, and auto-fire is still set to single shot? Because of this, you'll die early on more than once. -Shooting in the game is extremely uncomfortable, you'll take a long time getting used to it, it took me 50 hours to at least shoot somewhat normally. The recoil in the game is just wild, if you hold down the trigger and don't control the recoil, the barrel literally shoots up into the sky – and countering it seems simple just because there's no ammo, but it's 50/50 here. Also, leading shots is slightly inadequate too, even from 20-30 meters you have to aim a centimeter past the character model. -For some this will be a con, but I took it for granted: the game is not fair to all players, a lot depends on luck – what weapon and attachments you get, how close you end up to the zone or its center, how much ammo or healing items you find. Once Brendan Greene said: "that all online games have a random factor." In this game, it's the highest. -Imagine a situation: you and another player land in the same spot, and there are only two houses here. Both of them run to the same house and one of them grabs the weapon first, he got lucky. Now imagine the exact same thing, but they run to different houses, and it's logical to assume both have weapons. Fair? Quite. But not in this game, depends on your luck. Sometimes it happens that one house has a weapon and the other doesn't. Now you understand, the loot distribution in the game isn't fully balanced. It happens that in one room three pistols can be stacked on top of each other. -In a squad you feel more or less safe, your teammates will always cover you and tell you if an enemy is somewhere, and head-on clashes are business as usual here. In solo it's completely different, this is one of the hardest modes to win in, everything depends only on you (there's a mode, by the way, where you can play solo against squads), and because of that you will be killed from all sides, and in solo hiding is always a priority. Head-on clashes aren't always successful, since a third player might kill you, and getting killed from behind or around a corner is business as usual here. But this isn't a con for me, just par for the course. -Fucking grenade spammers, I dream of the day the carry limit for grenades is reduced. There are some degenerates who don't want to shoot, they just gather a dozen grenades and start tossing them, hoping it kills someone. -Physics... No comment here, cars here are like soap in a bathtub. I can recommend it to people who have very good PCs, and even then only with a 50% discount (that's how it worked out for me financially, the 30% discount plus money from selling trading cards), but as for everyone else... Better not, wait until the game is finished (will it ever be?), and for now the developers promise to finish the game by early November, will they pull it off? We'll see. As for me, I'll take a break from the game until November, and we'll see how things go. For now, I don't recommend it.

translation_en: [h1]PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS is a Battle Royale style game where up to 100 players fight to reach first place[/h1] Well, first of all, the game is pretty acceptable, it has several game modes (Solo, Duo, Squad, 1-Man squad) either in first-person (FPP) or third-person (TPP), and it has servers for South America (SA). As for the gameplay, I found the game pretty smooth, dynamic, and balanced in most aspects. To sum it up, the game still has 3 maps, Steam achievements, and inventory items where you can get several crates a week by using the battle points you earn from playing. In this game, you can still have fun even as a beginner, but the game isn't very friendly when it comes to helping new people, so get ready to die a lot before you manage to get a win or at least get close to one. As for performance, which is the most important thing based on my observations, here's the deal... at the time of this review, I have a pretty weak PC that basically meets the minimum requirements for this game, and I have almost no performance issues (only in certain parts, like when opening the inventory, which stutters for 1 or 2 seconds). So yes, the game probably has poor optimization and graphical issues, but from what I've read, it was apparently way worse back in the day (the first year of release) and doesn't apply as much nowadays, since not only me, but several people manage to play the game on an acceptable PC without sudden frame drops or freezes. As for the cheater problem, at least on SA servers I apparently never had issues, even though on a few occasions I noticed certain weird situations, but that might just be me crying about it, so I don't think the situation is as bad as people say it is (maybe on other servers on other continents the situation is worse, but I don't think it's the majority like people try to make it seem). Well, as for the price, I think R$ 55.99 is expensive. A lot of people miss out on playing because they don't want to pay that price, and the game has already lost a large player base. I think they should rethink this price, but it doesn't look like that's their intention anytime soon, seeing as they released the Sanhok Battle Pass costing R$ 34.99. So if you're very picky about what you spend your money on, maybe this isn't the ideal game for you. Well, basically that's it. In my opinion, even though the game is losing players, [b]it's still great[/b]. But before buying, look into the game to make sure you won't regret it, because what I reported in this review was based on my experience, which tends to be almost always positive even in bad games, and because of that, maybe you won't have the same experience I did... (and mind you, I'm not even that big a fan of this Battle Royale genre, man).

translation_en: [u]March 23, 2017.[/u] PUBG releases in Early Access on Steam. It's not the first or the last game to come out in Early Access. Everyone probably still has that bad taste in their mouth from buying DayZ (give me back my grand). What does this "Early Access" even mean? Long story short, get ready for bugs, crashes, lag, and optimization issues. Want to complain? You bought the game yourselves, so deal with it. [u]August 22, 2017.[/u] The game is already gaining popularity, but the "boom" is going to happen a bit later, after the tournament at Gamescom. No, you heard that right, a tournament for an unoptimized game with a $350,000 prize pool. [u]August 27, 2017.[/u] That very same "boom". PUBG overtakes CS:GO and Dota 2 in player count. At that point, 8 million copies of the game have been sold. [u]September 8, 2017.[/u] There were 1,300,000 concurrent players in the game. [u]November 7, 2017.[/u] The game sells 20 million copies, and the concurrent player record hits 2,500,000. [u]December 21, 2017.[/u] The developer kept their word and released the game by the end of the year, but the problems didn't go anywhere. So what do we do? That's right, announce it for XBOX. Couldn't optimize it on PC, let's try on consoles. [u]February 9. March 18, 2018.[/u] PUBG on mobile. Today is July 5th. They've added a massive amount of content in the form of crates... Well, okay, okay, they also added 2 new maps, vehicles, weapons, attachments, and stuff like that (probably was tough, considering PUBG's stats). Has PUBG become playable in 1.5 years? Yes and no. All the problems stayed, and cheaters were added on top of them. The fight against them is ongoing, but the demand for cheats is huge (again, PUBG's stats and numbers). Is it worth buying this game? No. It's got 2003 textures, and the system requirements are lying. You'll be able to launch it, but play it? No. My advice to you, steer clear of Early Access games. Oh, wait! PUBG has fully released, but it sure as hell doesn't feel like it.

translation_en: Edit of my 2020 review: Some of the things I complained about have been fixed. It only took 3 years. I'm going to test ranked, it brings competitive zones and rules and I hope I can get that tournament feeling back. However, I remain very disappointed by the meta switch on AR HTKs to try and appeal to CS:GO players and get them to come back. Numerous tweaks were implemented to move away from "tactical" gameplay and fall back on gameplay that leans more towards aim skill. Before, with a shorter HTK, whoever positioned themselves and opened fire first had a high probability of winning the engagement. This situation heavily favored those who played positioning and the circle intelligently. Now that they've removed knockback on hits and you need 2 headshots to kill, guys who rely purely on their AIM have a much higher chance of turning the fight around. I'm a competitive player, +1600h, between 3 and 9 KDA depending on how seriously I play FFA. To give you an idea, look up DarrickS on OPGG and XPULZ (50% podium finishes across 24 tournaments). Here is my opinion: Don't buy it anymore. I bought this game casually in 2017 because I just had to play with the buddies. I had no ambition with it and then I realized I was doing well so I got super invested. I wasted 1600 hours of my life, because in the end it's impossible for me to go any further since the devs stop us from doing so. The state of the game is a disaster. The devs don't listen to the players. In the list of requests that are still pending: - Region lock to stop Chinese players (and people who lag in general and who have quite an advantage) from squatting EU / NA servers. On the other hand, the devs installed 3 (!!!!) anti-cheats to regulate the cheater problem and all players are penalized (shitty performance after 2 years with a 1080 and an I5-8500K 6 Core OC) whereas with a region lock, 90% of the problem would be solved. Besides, if you go on OPGG, you'll quickly realize that the leaderboard (the best players) is 95% made up of people cheating without hiding it... - Change the play zones to make the "standard" experience more interesting. Outside of tournaments, you'll be far from a true BR experience since there's no point in winning and trying to stay alive as long as possible. So people play like headless chickens and unless you do the same, you quickly get bored for 30 minutes since the server is empty after 5 minutes. On top of that, MMR doesn't work / casts too wide a net. In the same match you'll be mixed with the worst and the best alike. So if you're good, you get bored slaughtering noobs, if you're bad, you spend your life playing shitty games and getting wrecked by guys who are 10 times your skill level. That said, I don't think they do it because in competitive, where justement we are very numerous, the servers are struggling hard due to the high proportion of survivors for a relatively small zone. I couldn't fully play competitive until I got a 1080 and it barely holds 60 FPS in a slightly tight late game. - No training center: No way to practice unless you're known, have access to a custom server and play within the tight circle of streamers / competitive players. translation_en: 08.07.2018. Thought I bought a Battle Royale game, but ended up in some sort of sci-fi horror. You can walk up to an item and try to pick it up, but it'll just stay put or straight up vanish. Or maybe it'll show up in your inventory 5 seconds later. Items might actually have a mind of their own in this game. Your enemies sometimes glitch around in jumps. I don't know if this is some chrono-shift or if the enemies just can't sync up with our reality, but it's gonna be a pain in the ass to damage them. By the way, this can happen to you too. Vehicles in this game have a mind of their own, too. If you park near some object (a fence, a barrel, a wall, etc.), the car won't like it and will start freaking out, attacking the offender, or just roaring its engine. The game also features a "Springboard" anomaly just like in S.T.A.L.K.E.R., and if you miss it while driving, you can go flying several meters up into the air even while driving on a flat road. Don't believe that everyone in the game is human. Actually, there are beings from another dimension who only mimic human behavior. But when they're in danger, they use their powers. Here is an incomplete list: immortality, homing bullets, wallhack, teleporting anywhere the owner wants, turning any land vehicle into an aircraft, and speed-running (Sonic mode). Also, even though these creatures lack brains, they are driven, evolving, and multiplying so fast that even the developers can't handle them. To keep you from thinking you can easily win just by coming up with survival strategies and knowing the ins and outs, the game pumps you with a special poison. This poison distorts your visual perception of the world, making it look like the picture is lagging or stuttering, makes you suspect every distant bush is an enemy, and makes you think you're safe lying in the grass when you're actually just lying out in an open field. This poison can also feed you false grenade trajectories so you throw it into a wall instead of a window, give you false hope of dealing damage to an enemy when you're not even hitting them or not even shooting at all (a hallucination), and periodically you'll feel like physics just stop existing in the game. As the cherry on top, the game has its own jumpscare. It's called "Bad Module," and it can pop up at any moment (no quiet scary music to warn you). Although it's hard to call it a jumpscare since it mostly just makes you pissed off. There are other "weird" things in the game, but I wrote about the ones I run into the most. Even though this game constantly pisses me off, I still play it (maybe that "alluring poison" was used on me). But the game still gets a thumbs down because I just want a battle royale without any of the above bullshit. 07.10.2018. 3 months later. PUBG is like a crappy wife—you hate her most of the time, but you don't leave her. The game is changing. Some of the stuff from the list above doesn't happen to me anymore. That's cool. However, the heaviest issues are still there. BUT. It's still unclear what the devs actually want. And almost every single update just raises questions. The decision to remove region lock, who the fuck knows. Flooding players with untradeable items that you can't even sell, because how dare you sell something you were gifted (that's the BLUE team's mindset). Adding a little window detailing how the anti-cheat works, dropping news about a shitload of banned accounts, and still running into "gods" in almost every second match (I specifically check the replays)—yeah, what a thrilling experience. Personally, I'm only annoyed by the occasional server issues and the supernatural people (cheaters, if you didn't catch that). For this reason, the thumb stays down for now, but I'll keep playing just to spite the commenters. By the way, reading some of the comments, I loved the "tech pros" verbally attacking my beloved potato PC. Kids, just for you, I have screenshots on my profile where you can see how it looks on medium settings. My fps fluctuates between 50 and 120, and it doesn't stop me from pulling off wins. So my internet and potato are doing just fine. Someone might say I'm flexing my wins, but in my defense: yeah, I am flexing playing on a potato. Next review update in 3 months if I don't forget or just give up.

translation_en: I've been playing PUBG since the closed beta in early 2017. When it first came out, I thought it was a well-made game that compromised between realism and casual play by taking H1Z1, adding more realism, improving the quality, and giving it more weight. It had a lot of issues at first, but since it was an Early Access game, I thought it was really great how they took a lot of feedback to fix things quickly. However, even after the official release in December 2017, there are still unresolved issues and new ones popping up. Setting aside management and other out-of-game issues, the core gameplay is really good. But from a player's perspective, since this is a multiplayer game and not a single-player one, you can't just look at the gameplay—you have to look at other aspects too. In that regard, PUBG has a lot of serious problems. As of June 24th, the problems with PUBG in my opinion are: 1. The rating system is fucked (first-time players get matched with sweatlords, and it's too easy to drop rank, making it easy to smurf and stomp newbies). 2. Way too many cheaters (you think it's only bad on Asian servers? There are tons of them on Korean servers too). 3. All sorts of bugs running rampant (getting stuck in walls, scopes unzooming by themselves, Molotovs not extinguishing, etc.). 4. Server status is garbage (bullet registration issues, items not picking up, doors not opening). 5. Constant crashes (crashes that you'd rarely see in other games happen to me at least once a day). 6. Lack of optimization (it doesn't require a 1080-tier GPU as the recommended spec anymore, but it still demands pretty high specs and the frame rate drops and spikes wildly). As of June 24th, the pros of PUBG in my opinion are: 1. The sound quality is pretty good (it's not perfect, but gun sounds and directional audio are of high quality). 2. Good gun balance (it used to be all about AR supremacy, but after balance patches, SMGs and DMRs rose up so you can use all kinds of weapons. Though shotguns suck now, and pistols and melee weapons still aren't used). Most of the problems are out-of-game issues like cheaters, bugs, the rating system, servers, and optimization. Assuming the AI was human-level and this was a single-player game instead of online, I’d give it a solid 9 out of 10 because it's that well-made. But I hope you don't forget that this is an online game.

translation_en: My first review goes to those motherfucking cunts at Bluehole. This obscure little company got insanely lucky and made a killing off a 100-player survival shooter that was at least somewhat novel a year ago. Probably because this absolute truckload of money fell right out of the sky, this little Korean company got happy, got cocky, and got way too big for their boots. They don't have the tech or the attitude of a major studio, but they've got the ego of one, and they even pull off moves that major studios wouldn't dare to make. Maybe I just don't play enough games, but PUBG really opened my eyes: a year after release, the devs raised the minimum system requirements—bumping the minimum GPU requirement from a GTX 660 1GB to a GTX 960 2GB. Even cards more powerful than a GTX 960 2GB would suddenly turn the game into a slideshow. This shit went on for weeks, and a flood of negative reviews poured in, turning the game's overall rating to Mixed in just a few weeks. But Bluehole doesn't need to give a shit about trivialities like that; after all, countless gamers from all over the world will keep mindlessly buying the game until it's dead, and they can just sit at home sipping coffee while mountains of cash roll right in. Who wouldn't love that? Whom the gods would destroy, they first make mad. Bluehole got super lucky, raking in a massive player base—especially in China—and counting money until their hands went numb. Even so, Bluehole's greed still wasn't satisfied. After making staggering profits off their first new cosmetic crate, Bluehole smelled blood in the water like a starving wolf and started constantly pumping out new skins and crates. The players were happy because when a new crate dropped, they could use the BP they'd saved up to buy crates, sell them on the market, and turn it into real cash. If you got lucky and unboxed a rare, expensive skin that made everyone jealous, you could make some extra pocket money while playing games, and you'd be in a great mood. If Bluehole had just kept that win-win relationship going with the players, they probably could've made even more money, but Bluehole's greed apparently wouldn't allow that; Bluehole wanted all the money for themselves. So Bluehole shut down individual player trading, kept right on pushing new crates and skins, and sat back on their couches sipping coffee, thinking about how filthy rich these new crates and skins were gonna make them. But players weren't having it, and purposefully stopped buying any keys or skins at all, because real cash you could actually spend in the real world got turned into dead money stuck on Steam to buy games and other skins. Who the fuck wants to trade real money and time for dead money? As a result, the profits from these new crates and skins didn't even hit a third of any previous crate. Bluehole didn't get what they wanted. Bluehole achieved their goal of hoarding all the money, even though the actual amount was way fucking lower than they planned. As a consumer, as a player, I am beyond sick of Bluehole. Elsewhere, when I spend money I actually get the treatment I'm owed, but in PUBG all I've experienced is Bluehole's bottomless greed. A few months ago, a massive frame-rate drop for every player chased off a huge chunk of the community, but at least you could fix it by turning off replay mode—I could live with that. They shut down player-to-player trading; fine, at worst I'd just miss out on a little side cash—I could live with that. Community: An urgent need to clean up the community, something that would be solved quickly with region locking, given that 90% of hackers come from China. Optimization: textures that don't load, shadows that don't appear, anti-aliasing that wrecks the performance of any processor (i5-7600k). Events: Promises of weekly events to compete with Fortnite, only to see them happen or not depending on the week, whenever the fuck they feel like it. Content: content is announced way too early and delivered at an exasperatingly slow pace, I've been waiting three months for the new map which feels like it's never going to arrive. Oh wait, that would prevent them from taking their 10% commission on Steam market transactions tax-free, a fucking disgrace. In short: Good idea, abysmal execution. But the approach is completely wrong. Drastically increased reload times, recoil, and damage debuffs for ARs, paired with damage buffs for SMGs. Even Shroud was cursing the M416 at one point. In short, if I have an M416, M16, or Scar-L in my hand, I typically leave them behind for a UMP, Vector, or SKS (for close combat) because the recoil is fucked. How could this have been solved better? Damage buff for the SMGs, can even be a hard one, but introduce a damage drop-off over range. The further the shot, the less damage, and SMGs should deal heavy damage under 100 meters, but after that (also because realistically it's mostly subsonic ammo) little to no damage at all (bullet drop could also be made harsher for that). All in all, it's a pre-release game that is no longer labeled as pre-release. I'm sorry that PUBG's success threw Bluehole for such a loop, but please Bluehole, or others, if something like this happens: WORK ON IT AND WORK HARD so that the designed game actually reaches a proper 2.0 status. translation_en: PUBG. A game that caught my attention thanks to Shroud. I was so eager to play and try out this new game that was part of the battle royale genre. I actually liked the Hunger Games theme (though it's originally from an Asian movie with the same name as the genre) with a realistic (not entirely) and military style. To start with, [b]DO NOT BUY THE GAME[/b], I don't recommend it. I mean, I fell in love with this game, I like it a lot, but it has a ton of problems that stem from the developers, who are complete assholes. The game mechanics and everything are sensational. The game has been on Steam for a year and some months since it came out in early access, it has raised [b]700 million dollars[/b], which is a shitload of money and allows the company in charge of the game to expand and put more people to work on it to improve it, but that's not the case here. I'll start with [h1]OPTIMIZATION[/h1] I think it's the point to criticize that everyone puts in their reviews, and at the same time it's one of the problems the game has had since early access. The optimization of this game is fucking trash. Despite having been on Steam for a long time now, with a lot of feedback from users, just 1 week ago the developers confirmed they would work on the optimization of the game, fixing issues they could have identified at the very beginning of the game, but no, they didn't. Even though the whole community has been talking about this for over a year, they haven't done shit against it. In my experience, when I bought the game (in January of this year) the optimization looked fine to me, there were tiny fps drops but it wasn't a problem. I mean, optimization was the reason I didn't buy this game before, and seeing the reviews after version 1.0 of the game where it supposedly [b]improved a ton[/b], I had no choice but to finally buy it and start playing. During updates, the optimization would get worse, or if it improved, it was by very little. I had situations where I could kill an enemy in a face-to-face encounter, but when shooting in full auto, my fps would drop so much to the point that the game would freeze, stop shooting, and I'd end up dying. This ruined my gaming experience for several matches where the exact same thing happened. I even remember using a UMP9 with a 4x ACOG scope, I shot at an enemy who was running and the game literally froze for 5 seconds. The same thing kept happening, I had to close the game. Another point to highlight: I used to have the option enabled to render the character when pressing Tab (which shows your inventory and your character). This option just makes your character's model show up in that menu with their clothes and everything. I remember opening it several times and the fps would drop from 60 to 55 or 40. I had a situation where I decided to open it to check how damaged my vest was and out of nowhere my fps dropped to 25 and stayed like that (an enemy found me and I died), just for pressing Tab. I disabled that option after that issue. Curiously, in update 1.14 they claim to have fixed this issue, and unfortunately... No, they didn't. It still drops frames. Honestly, you're going to go through a lot of bad times because of this issue that will ruin your gaming experience. [h1] CHEATERS/HACKERS [/h1] Another problem the game has been carrying around since it came out in public early access. If you want to know something funny, Bluehole released this game into public early access without [b]any anti-cheat system[/b], yeah, none, which is why people could use free open-source [b]cheating[/b] programs. The game doesn't have any program of this kind for the moment and relies on reports to punish. The problem with reporting is also that the death cam in this game (the one that shows you how you were killed from the player's perspective) in first person is useless. If I tell you about my experience with it, I honestly think I've reported people who didn't deserve it because I trusted that their death cam worked. Seriously, the death cam would always show me in all playbacks that my killer had no recoil, when shooting me while moving, it showed that the crosshair was behind me, and I ask you, how the fuck do you hit someone who's moving if you aren't aiming towards where they're moving? That's why the death cam is only good for detecting hackers who don't even hide it and are obvious. Plus, playing this game on the NA (North America) server in third-person perspective in solo mode is literally suicide, because it's swamped with hackers. That's why I only play in FPP mode, since this one has fewer players, matches take a bit longer, and well, hackers just want to jump into quick matches to farm [b]Battle Points[/b]. Bluehole claims that [b]they are winning the war against cheaters[/b], but in reality, that's not the case. [h1] UPDATES [/h1] To start with, I don't know why, for what reason, God only knows, but this game updates 26MB 3 times a day, I haven't the slightest idea why. Also, I don't know why patches that don't make that many changes to the game tend to be so heavy. The minimum you can download for an update in this game is 5GB, for an update that doesn't apply many changes. Big updates with content take too damn long to arrive, the game's development team takes ages to put out content for the game, plus many of their updates that claim to balance and fix the game, don't do it. There was a case which was an update before 1.14, I think it's 1.13, where it said it buffed the M16 and removed the sound of being hurt when winning the match. Then a YouTuber proved that everything they did to the M16 was the exact opposite, and the winning sound still played. Another thing these developers tend to do is apply changes and not put them in the patch notes. An example would be that the AKM was buffed in this weapon update (where the FAL was added) and this change wasn't added to the patch notes. I don't consider this action bad since it encourages playing and discovering if they added a hidden change, adding to the fact that most big updates come with way too many microtransaction crates. [h1] REWARD FOR PLAYING [/h1] Every game gives you a reward for playing it, whether it's level progression, story progression, items for playing, or in-game money to buy objects, something that actually makes you feel like it was worth playing. For example, Team Fortress 2 gives you weapon drops for playing or a small chance at a cosmetic while you play. Even if it's random, it's something you earn for playing and you can enjoy it. The point is PUBG used to have this and now it doesn't have it anymore. The game itself becomes tedious. Sometimes matchmaking fails and it never finds a match, so you'll have to keep restarting it (my case for FPP perspective). When you find a match, you'll then have to wait for it to fill up. The game will unfortunately decide when to start the countdown for the match. It's happened to me that it's taken 3 minutes to start that countdown with [b]90 people[/b] waiting, then they make you wait an additional minute for the countdown plus waiting for the plane to fly over the place where you want to land and loot. This becomes a routine in this game and a very tedious one, adding to a problem of this battle royale genre, which is spending minutes and minutes in the match without finding a single player and then dying out of nowhere. The routine, added to the fact that this can happen to you, creates a formula to wear down your patience very effectively. The game initially had 3 crates that didn't require paying for a key to open them and 1 paid one, so you could unlock something through your own hard work. I happened to unlock an item worth 50 dollars and boy did it feel good, but now the game is plagued with crates that need a paid key so it's impossible to unlock anything for free despite the fact that you paid $30.

translation_en: As one of the earliest players to get into PUBG, let me tell you what it means for a game to get more and more trash with every update. My passion for this game was at its peak around March and April of last year through the summer vacation. I played squads with my classmates (every single day, on all sorts of servers, even when we had no classes, a couple of matches right after lunch, and on weekends from 9 AM to midnight). My leaderboard rank was pushing four digits (no big deal, though). Those were our happiest times. But ever since the summer vacation ended, PUBG blew up completely, and with it, the cheaters blew up too. At first, it wasn't too bad; when you ran into a hacker, you'd basically die right as you landed. Later on, the hackers developed a routine: they’d let you loot a whole city, let you waste your time scavenging everything, and only then come and torture you. I've run into all sorts of shit like giant players, Gomu Gomu no Mi stretching powers, flying, burrowing underground—you name it. Plus, two of my friends got falsely banned. After the summer of 2017, I basically stopped touching the game. Now I play occasionally, and they've updated it with a bunch of fancy, useless attachments, 3x scope airdrops, and armored airdrop UAZs—just a bunch of game-breaking nonsense. I am honestly speechless. I heard that fucking Sanhok is returning to the original version (haven't paid attention in a while, don't know if it's true), and I'm actually pretty happy about it. After all, I was drawn to this game by the pure, authentic battle royale experience. Do I recommend it or not? If it really goes back to the original version, I recommend it! If they keep updating with all this fancy bullshit, all I wanna say is wcnmb (fuck your mom).

translation_en: My first ever review goes to those motherfucking pieces of shit at Bluehole. This obscure little company struck gold and made a killing thanks to a 100-player survival shooter that was actually somewhat innovative a year ago. Probably because this absolute mountain of cash fell right out of the sky, it made this little Korean company happy, arrogant, and stuck-up. They don't have the tech or the attitude of a major developer, but they sure have the ego, pulling off moves that even AAA studios wouldn't dare to make. Maybe I don't play many games, but PUBG really opened my eyes: a full year after release, the devs actually raised the minimum system requirements—bumping the GPU requirement from a GTX 660 1GB to a GTX 960 2GB. Even graphics cards more powerful than a GTX 960 2GB would suddenly turn the game into a slideshow. This shit went on for weeks, and a flood of negative reviews poured in, tanking the game’s overall rating to "Mixed" in just a couple of weeks. But Bluehole doesn't need to give a fuck about trivial shit like that. After all, countless gamers worldwide will keep mindlessly buying this game until it's dead, meaning they can just lie back at home sipping coffee while truckloads of cash roll right in. Who wouldn't love that? Whom the gods would destroy, they first make mad. Bluehole got super lucky, raking in a massive player base and counting endless piles of money from all over the world, especially China. Even so, their greed wasn't satisfied. After dropping their first new clothing crate and making insane profits, Bluehole smelled blood in the water like starving wolves and started constantly pumping out new skins and crates. The players were cool with it at first, because when a new crate dropped, you could spend your saved-up BP to buy it, sell it on the market, and turn it into real cash. If you got lucky and unboxed a rare, expensive-ass skin that made everyone jealous, you could make some extra pocket change while playing the game, which felt awesome. If Bluehole had just kept that win-win relationship going with the players, they probably would’ve made even more money, but their bottomless greed just wouldn't allow it—they wanted all the cash for themselves. So, Bluehole disabled the Steam community market, kept right on dropping new crates and skins, and sat back on their couches sipping coffee, dreaming about how much bank these new items were gonna make them. But players weren't having any of it, and purposefully refused to buy any keys or cosmetics. Why would anyone trade real, spendable cash for dead money that can only be used to buy more games and skins on Steam? As a result, the profit from these new crates and skins was less than a third of any previous crate. Bluehole didn't get what they wanted. They achieved their goal of hoarding all the money themselves, even though the total was way the fuck below expectations. As a consumer and a gamer, I am completely fucking done with Bluehole. When I spend money elsewhere, I actually get treated like a customer, but in PUBG, all I get to experience is Bluehole's bottomless abyss of greed. A few months ago, a massive frame-rate drop drove tons of players away, but at least you could fix it by turning off the replay feature—I tolerated it. They disabled individual trading—fine, at most I just lose a bit of extra pocket money—I tolerated it. Another massive FPS drop update—wait, it should get fixed soon, right?—I tolerated it. Every single time I put up with their shit, it just killed my hope for the game. When I turn on my PC, what I want more than anything is to see patch notes and bug fixes for PUBG, not updates for pointless emotes and weapon skins. Bluehole's bullshit has completely alienated their user base. The FPS drop issues went unaddressed for weeks, while they quietly raised the hardware requirements and updated all sorts of useless garbage. I don't know about anyone else, but I am done with Bluehole for good. 98 RMB thrown away to feed some stray dogs, 200 hours wasted sleeping through matches—uninstalling to keep my IQ intact. Finally, I hope Overwatch gets better and better, and I hope the Shanghai Dragons get their first damn win soon. Overwatch will always welcome back any former agents.

translation_en: Hi! To start from the beginning, people generally fall into two groups. Some play PUBG, others Fortnite. It's the same with Pepsi and Coca-Cola, McDonald's and KFC; I didn't like the look of Fortnite so I chose PUBG. I knnooow there are patient and impatient people, if you're in the second group scroll straight to the bottom :) To the point, if you're starting your adventure with this game you're in for a disappointment, the same one that hit a lot of people giving a thumbs down after 10 hours of gameplay. Unfortunately, it's tough at the start, you die practically right after landing or just above the ground. And this story repeats itself very, very often, which unfortunately people don't have the nerves for. But once you master flying, landing, looting, driving vehicles, choosing a convenient location, the world is your oyster, yeah! And you choose which one :). Why? Because you jump out of the plane yourself and fly wherever you want. But if you land in big cities you have a higher probability that you won't make it out unless the zone happens to favor you. But the game has great sound design and even if you stay in a building, the enemy will track you by your stomping. I honestly recommend starting in secluded places, and weapon first! Armor and the rest later. And now, if for example you have friends and want to play together, awesome! There's a duo option (two of you), 3-man squad (three of you) and squad (four of you). I recommend choosing either the duo option or squad because in 3-man you're kind of one man down and you play against 4-player squads. That's enough theory, personally I like the game mega much, I put in 300 hours, won and lost many times :) But the fun and sometimes funny moments make up for all the failures or stupid mistakes, just like the coveted chicken dinner! As for the shooting mechanics itself, you have to get used to it but I think it's good. And here I recommend, there are a lot of cool materials on YT about all the weapons, how they behave, how they shoot, as well as how to move, hide, etc. To sum up: Is it worth paying 72.99? I think it's worth it if you actually intend to play for a bit, because with in-game points we can buy crates with skins and then sell them or open them; if we sell them, the game will pay for itself after some time. Personally, I got around 200 PLN back towards the full refund. Pros: + Engine + Variety of weapons and their upgrade/modification possibilities + Adventure! + Graphics + Vehicles, it's also cool that there are several of them and they differ in their properties + Ability to play together with friends + You decide for yourself where you jump out of the plane and where you start your adventure! Cons: - Bugs, they happen but they are working on it all the time - Cheaters, although here I actually think there is more strictness than in CS and a lot of accounts are being banned on an ongoing basis. Best regards and I encourage you, I had a great time! K.

I get unlucky and get blown up by the red zone when I was about to win, should the red zone be deleted too? Aren't you contradicting yourself with this change? The reason this game was instantly accepted by the masses is precisely because of its randomness. Fine, go ahead and increase the recoil for all ARs, other than making the game harder to pick up for beginners I can't think of any other point. Anyway, I don't see how this relates to what you said about preventing players from using specific overpowered weapons (M416). Besides, the M416 is strong, but it's strong because of its attachment slots, while also facing the issue of being hard to fully kit out. I can say it's still balanced. No matter how you change it, its 4 attachments still make it stronger than other ARs, so this change of yours is totally pointless. What, you say you're increasing the usage rate of the AK? Sorry, but the AK's single-tap muzzle jump, bullet muzzle velocity, drop-off, and the backpack space 7.62 ammo takes up mean its pick rate still won't be very high. 3. New attachments: the 6x is okay, can be used as a transition when there's no 8x for sniping. Once I find an 8x I'm still dropping it. That 3x scope, designer what were you thinking? Go on, try using those crosshairs yourself and see if you can even spot a person, could it possibly be any more exaggerated? Is the 3x scope really necessary? I'm not exaggerating when I say this game now has 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, 5x, 6x, 7x, and 8x scopes (6x and 8x have variable zoom). You could say it's pretty comprehensive. Grips, five in total. Oh my god, what are you thinking, a survival game and I'm walking around a mall having to pick and choose which grip to use??? I shit you not, just reading the descriptions of the 5 grips already made my head spin. Some even give you +1 stat while deducting 3 stats. What, can I just not equip a grip at all? You tell me different grips have different playstyles, some grips focus on single-taps, some enhance spraying. Bro, there are only so many rifles that can take grips. Later on, when I'm scoping in with a red dot to fight enemies at a distance, do I have to temporarily swap out my 4x scope and also temporarily swap grips? Aren't weapon attachments supposed to provide positive buffs to guns? What's the point of making it all so fancy and overly complicated? I still can't accept that this game actually has 5 different grips, not to mention the art style of these 3 new grips. Anyway, I feel like it totally clashes with the game. 4. Designer, I really want to split hairs with you on this one: "DMRs can now equip AR magazines and attachments." I tried it out. Rifle suppressors and mags can be used on DMRs (SKS, Mini, SLR). Sniper suppressors and mags can be used on DMRs, and the effects are 100% identical. But, but, but, sniper suppressors and mags CANNOT be used on rifles. I honestly can't wrap my head around this logic. Logically speaking, if rifles can take DMR parts, that means the caliber is the same, right? Then why the hell can't it work the other way around? Are there any hardcore gun nuts out there who can explain this binary-brained mechanic? 5. I hope you don't mess with the holographic sight. Your original intention was good: making the circle bigger and color lighter so the red dot doesn't block your vision when aiming at people. But you made it way too faint. You changed it so it's basically like the red dot, where you still can't see the reticle against the light, and the holo's bulky housing already blocks plenty of vision as it is. With this change, its only advantage over the red dot is gone. Secondly, adding the ability to change reticle color and style is totally pointless. I don't know if the designer even plays this game, but in a match, you constantly have to swap scopes on a gun to fight enemies at different distances. I slap on a red dot, adjust the brightness, change the style, then take the scope off and put it back on, and it resets. What, I gotta adjust it all over again? Being able to adjust reticle brightness has been out on the live servers for ages, yet just like the test server now, if you adjust the brightness, take the scope off and put it back on, the brightness resets. ■ Stay true to the original concept. The core of Battle Royale is survival of the fittest; if I have a Level 3 helmet and Level 3 vest, I'm going to wipe you out and get even stronger. If my gear sucks and I run into a fully-kitted gigachad, I'm going to use my brain and tactics to kill them and steal their loot. Do you really think everyone having a Level 2 helmet and a 98K and just raw-dogging aim duels and reaction times is the standard gameplay for this game? You guys at Bluehole keep pushing towards e-sports, completely ignoring the casual fun experience for the rest of us. Overall, this test server update is extremely lazy and completely unprofessional. I'm not going to be arrogant and say "if these updates get pushed to the live servers I'm quitting" or anything like that, but if they really push it over like this, I believe it will leave the vast majority of players deeply disappointed, extremely disappointed. It completely loses the flavor this game is supposed to have. Also, I suggest firing the designer in charge of this update.
