translation_en: **That’s it. Enough. Personally my (and maybe not only mine) patience has run out. I’ll try to describe this "creation" as constructively as possible and why I don’t recommend buying it. But despite a fair amount of hate, I’ll start with the pros after all:**[list] [*]Sound design. I’ll give the game credit - everything sounds pretty realistic and pleasant here, shooting has a good impact. Thumbs up; [*]I personally consider the "battle royale" concept near-genial. First of all, it’s unforgettable emotions, and second, an endless generator of various interesting situations on the battlefield, where tension and interest remain even after n-hours of playtime; [*]Basically, leaving aside the FPS issues mentioned below, quite enjoyable gunplay and bullet ballistics. It’s not uber-hardcore like, say, Arma, but that’s a good thing, because the difficulty of hitting targets stayed at the right level while keeping a low barrier to entry; [*]It’s quite fun to spend time in it with a company of friends. (Although any shit seems more fun with friends. Friendship is magic?); [*]The marketplace. Yes, you can actually make a decent buck here, and unlike, God forgive me, CS:GO, you don't need an initial investment. You just play the game and earn points to buy crates: some can just be opened, some require a key. Points are farmed pretty quickly. You can easily make back the cost of the game.[/list] [b]And now get ready for the cons, where an immense amount of accumulated hatred will be poured out: [/b] [*]The main con, in my opinion, is optimization. Yes, it still has significant issues. The way the game behaves even on medium settings with hardware like a GeForce GTX1060 6GB, Core i7-4770, and 16GB RAM with such shitty graphics (which we'll talk about a bit lower) is just unacceptable. I would understand if the image quality was at least on par with high settings in Arma 3 (which runs just wonderfully on the aforementioned configuration), but no - the picture here looks blurry and crappy. With all that, I want to note that in a normal routine situation where there's no one around, the game behaves normally, but when a shootout involving at least 5 people starts - FPS drops begin. Therefore, dealing with the local gunplay (which was made a bit harder after a recent update due to increased recoil) at 20-40 FPS is pretty tough. So I currently see only one way out - either get used to playing with FPS drops, or play on minimum graphic settings (WHY DO I HAVE TO TORTURE MY EYES WITH LOW FRAMERATE AND SHITTY GRAPHICS?! Because it's all made through an ass, that's why). It feels like the game is only tested on high-end PCs, while everyone else has to play on medium (maximum, high) settings and "enjoy" the wonderful blurry mess. Want to play with V-Sync? Forget about it, otherwise you'll get so-called input lag. Just fucking wonderful (no). To be fair, I'll note that they are trying to patch the game and sometimes performance even improves (remembering the beta test times, but this is still Early Access, so it's forgivable), but personally, I don't quite understand how this "piece of code," which somehow managed to compile at all, dares to call itself a release. Again, this game does NOT have next-gen graphics even on ultra settings, so it should NOT allow itself to demand such PC power. [*] The second most significant problem is servers. But it's not as bad as it might seem. Among the annoying glitches: at the start of a match, items are picked up with a delay (here I can understand, almost 100 people are looting simultaneously); poor hit registration with the shotgun, when you can kill with a "one-shot" or just slightly wound an opponent under the exact same conditions. Not cool, but tolerable. [*]This is more of a nitpick, but still - a scanty character creator. I'll just say I'd like a bit more variety. [*]Another very annoying problem is cheating. No comments here. Cheaters just exist, the anti-cheat can't cope. That's it. [*]And lastly, crashes. I don't know about anyone else, but the game regularly likes to just crash on me for no particular reason.[/list] [i]CONCLUSION: As stated above, the game still has room to grow because it's way too raw for a release version, has a bunch of bugs and problems. And what a shame. Because it's growing in not quite the direction it should be ("our optimization suffers and we have n-bugs multiplied by the cheater problem? WELL LET'S MAKE MORE CLOTHES AND WEAPON SKINS, IT'S SO FUCKING FASHIONABLE AND YOUTHFUL! AT THE SAME TIME, WE'LL RAKE IN EXTRA CASH! COOL, RIGHT?!") I don't recommend buying it at the moment, unless you're playing with a squad of friends.[/i]

translation_en: Battlegrounds is a game with a peculiar, almost accidental success story. Its creator didn't expect sooooo much hype behind his definitive version of the Battle Royale gamemode, and for sure I didn't either when I first saw this game. The main reason is probably because of the livestreams wave of success, and this game works perfectly for them. In short: the game's creator (the famous PlayerUnknown who's in the product's name) used to make Battle Royale mods for other games, and PUBG was going to be his ultimate Battle Royale, published by Bluehole. Interesting, right? PUBG established itself so well in the market for being the first standalone Battle Royale game, and there are several reasons why it acquired its temporary hegemony, and its subsequent and slow loss of players. For those who don't know, games of this style work like this: you usually drop into an open map with 99 other players, and you'll have to find gear while the map shrinks closer and closer to the center. The last player alive wins. There's also the possibility of joining a squad and playing with your friends, which honestly is one of the most fun ways to play. Starting a match is remarkably easy. You won't have to deal with annoying lobby systems. It's practically pressing a button, and at most you'll have to invite a friend to a party. It's one of the best lobby systems I've ever seen. The first few hours are frustrating, the shooting system is very unique and there's no way to practice and get used to the basics. This, while several players have a much better knowledge of the map and how the weapons work than you do. It's literally a pain in the ass, and I strongly recommend playing with more experienced friends to REALLY get used to the mechanics. From then on, you'll REALLY start playing. Another cool impression is the game's sound design. The gunshots actually have a very realistic and immersive sound design, you'll probably even be able to guess the distance of a firefight as your experience with the game grows. The bullets also have a really cool drop to observe, even if maybe it's not that realistic, it works well. Is it fun? Yes it is. Several unusual situations will certainly mark your playthroughs, and the thrill of the match is guaranteed. From the moment you hear the sound of a footprint, to seeing the last member of your squad trying to win the match. At least, when I got used to it, I had fun and really saw the potential behind the game. But that ran out over time: after about 25 hours, I was more dragging myself to play with my friends than actually having fun. There's a certain general consensus that "battle royale doesn't get old because no matter how much it involves repetitive tasks, the situations that happen in matches are different," and I strongly disagree with that. Generally, it's as if there's a template of various possible events, and they happen in a chaotic way. It's as if the game really had fresh situations, but since it's a videogame and the number of interactions is limited, because it's LITERALLY just a gamemode, it gets very tiresome. Especially because the game has an immense amount of time just looking for gear, and personally: I HATE repetitiveness. It's what makes franchises like Dynasty Warriors and survival games not exactly my thing, and PUBG is by its nature an extremely repetitive game. Even though SOMETIMES you have one different moment or another in certain matches, you'll have a ton of the same boring moments. You'll still have to look for loot, you'll still have to walk or drive long distances, you'll still have to watch your surroundings. Sometimes, the variables only change the way you'll execute these tasks: maybe you'll have to walk less because you got lucky, or you'll feel safer in the spot you're in. And the more you get used to it, the more frustrated you might get: the game's shooting system, maybe for server latency reasons, or maybe because of its own mechanics, doesn't always seem to register your hits. A lot of the time, whoever wins is whoever shoots the most, and if you're someone who loves precision shooting, you might have a very frustrating learning curve. It's so frustrating that on the forums they recommend calculating latency when you shoot as a variable. Even though the game is paid, you can still get lootboxes, which opening can cost you money. Interesting right? You pay 50 bucks for a game with just one gamemode (and events), and you still have content locked behind crates. To make matters worse, this content is literally cosmetic items in the game, which can be acquired in the middle of a match but unfortunately only count for that match. So maybe even for those who pay, it's not that useful. At least, selling drops can earn you some extra cash on the Steam market. And to make matters worse, the game is still EXTREMELY poorly made. Expect some server lag, assets that can be found on the Unreal Store (which is okay, but even proves there wasn't that much aesthetic care), the updates are almost LITERAL TECHNIQUES the size of the game and even with a good PC, expect some frame drops. Not to mention physics bugs everywhere. And that's not all. The game is FULL of hackers. I even understand that it's a consequence of reaching a massive audience, but the problem doesn't end there: Fortnite has WAY less with similar popularity and Bluehole refuses to implement Region Lock, preventing Chinese hackers from entering the South American server (which is quite common). On top of everything I said, these problems have been persistent since the game's open beta, and Bluehole hasn't done anything to fix it, with only minor improvements and additions of minor mechanics and content. Congratulations on destroying a game with potential! So, at the end of the day: it's hard to recommend PUBG. Fortnite is much better in SO many ways and the loss of players makes total sense when a game gets such poor support. Still, it's my favorite Battle Royale. Its immersion factor is a lot of fun and I can't stand messing with Fortnite's building, but honestly: if a clone comes out that keeps the immersion but treats the player with more respect, I'm dropping PUBG right away. Pros: + Unpretentious and simple fun. + Great team communication: it's one of the only games where you REALLY end up acting like a squad. + Easy and intuitive to start. Makes the game addictive. + Functional level design. + Gameplay manages to be both casual and hardcore, depending on your learning curve. + Extremely immersive sounds. + Remarkably interesting bullet physics. + Full of interesting situations to witness. Cons: - Unnecessarily heavy updates. - Full of physics bugs. - Excess of hackers. - Horrendous support. - Crappy optimization. - Lack of any basic training mode. - Tedious repetition loop after some experience. FINAL SCORE: 53,3 Verdict: Does the game have its pros? Yes it does. But it's pretty obvious that the name is bigger than the content it presents. I strongly recommend trying Fortnite, H1Z1 and all the other games of the style that are Free to Play before getting PUBG, because even with potential, the product CURRENTLY wasn't quite what satisfied me. I played about 30 hours and nowadays I think I'm extremely fed up with the game's lack of variety. It's a game with many qualities, but the flaws are enough for me to have temporarily given up on it.

translation_en: First of all, I love this game. But I'm still giving it a negative review, and this is the first time I've ever given a negative review to a game. This negative review is aimed at the "PC 1.0 Version Update #3". 1. Everyone's talking about how Level 3 helmets only spawn in care packages. For an aggressive player like me, that's great—I've got a sniper rifle, the enemy has a Level 2 helmet, I'm having a blast. But, but the reason you gave for this change is that Level 3 helmets affect the overall match? That luck dictates success or failure?? What about Level 3 vests? Tell me, in a close-range encounter, doesn't the guy with a Level 3 vest have a massive advantage? We shoot at the same time, he got lucky and found a Level 3 vest so I died and he lived—isn't that also luck deciding life or death? Should Level 3 vests be put in care packages too? Well, you might say, "You can just aim for the head, then it doesn't matter what level vest they have." Fine, let's look at it another way: we both have Level 2 helmets, he gets lucky and finds a 98k, I only find an SKS, and we shoot each other in the head at the same time and I die. Is this also a death caused by luck? I get unlucky and die to the red zone in a game I was supposed to win—should you delete the red zone too? Aren't you contradicting yourselves with this change? This game was rapidly accepted by the masses precisely because of its randomness. Noobs can get #1 because of this randomness, which closes the gap between them and the pros. Don't forget that, Bluehole. 2. I am beyond baffled by these weapon adjustments. Fine, go ahead and increase the recoil on all ARs. Aside from raising the learning curve, I can't think of any other point to it. Anyway, I don't see how it has anything to do with what you said about preventing players from using specific overpowered weapons (the M416). Besides, the M416 is strong, but it's strong because it takes a lot of attachments, while also coming with the problem of being hard to fully kit out. I'd argue it's still balanced. No matter how you change it, 4 attachments are still going to be better than other ARs, so this change of yours is totally pointless. What, are you saying you want to increase the pick rate for the AK? Sorry, but the AK's single-tap muzzle jump, bullet velocity, drop, and the fact that 7.62 ammo takes up so much inventory space mean its pick rate still isn't going to be very high. 3. The new attachments: the 6x is okay, you can use it as a transitional scope for sniping when you don't have an 8x. Once I find an 8x I'm still gonna throw it away. That 3x scope—what were the devs thinking? Go on, try using those crosshairs yourself and see if you can actually spot anyone. Could it be any more exaggerated? Is the 3x really necessary? I'm not even exaggerating when I say this game now has 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, 5x, 6x, 7x, and 8x scopes (counting 6x and 8x zoom). You could say the lineup is pretty comprehensive. Grips—there are five of them in total. Oh my god, what goes through your mind? This is a survival game, why do I feel like I'm wandering around a mall having to pick which grip to use??? To be honest, just reading the descriptions of the 5 grips has made my head spin. Some of them buff one stat and nerf three. What, am I just not supposed to run a grip at all? You're telling me different grips lead to different playstyles, like some grips are better for tapping while others buff spraying. Bro, there are only a few rifles that can even take grips. Am I supposed to be running a red dot for long-range fights, and then every time I temporarily swap to a 4x I also have to temporarily swap my grip? Aren't weapon attachments supposed to give a net positive to your gun? What is even the point of making things this overly complicated? I still can't accept that this game actually has 5 different grips, not to mention the art style of these three new grips. Anyway, I think they look totally out of place. 4. Devs, I really want to be nitpicky with you on this one: "DMRs can now equip AR magazines and attachments." I tried it out, and rifle suppressors and mags can be used on DMRs (SKS, Mini 14, SLR), sniper suppressors and mags can be used on DMRs, and the effects are 100% identical. But, but, but sniper suppressors and mags *cannot* be used on rifles. I honestly cannot wrap my head around this logic. Logically speaking, if rifles can take DMR attachments, that means the caliber is the same, right? Then why the hell can't it work the other way around? Can some hardcore gun nut explain this binary-brained mechanic to me? 5. I hope you don't mess with the holographic sight. Your original intention was good—making the circle bigger and the color lighter so the red dot doesn't block your vision when aiming at people—but you made it way too faint. You changed it so it's practically the same as the red dot, where you still can't see the reticle against a bright light, and the holo housing already blocks enough of your view as it is. With this change, it's lost its only advantage over the red dot. Secondly, adding the ability to change reticle color and style is totally pointless. I don't know if the developers even play this game, but in a match, you constantly swap scopes on the same gun to fight enemies at different distances. I put on a red dot, adjusted the brightness, changed the style, take the sight off and put it back on, and it resets. What, am I supposed to adjust it all over again? You could easily just add a scope preset option in the settings. Ever since they added reticle brightness adjustment to the live servers, it's still like the test server where taking off a sight and putting it back on resets the brightness. ■ Sticking to the source material, the core of Battle Royale is survival of the fittest. If I have a Level 3 helmet and Level 3 vest, I'm going to run you over and become stronger. If my gear is trash and I run into a fully-kitted gigachad, I have to use my brain and tactics to kill them and take their stuff. Do you really think the standard gameplay of this game should just be everyone running around with Level 2 helmets and 98ks, pure-aiming and twitch-reacting each other to death? You guys at Bluehole keep pushing towards e-sports, completely ignoring our casual player experience. Overall, this test server update feels very lazy and extremely unprofessional. I'm not going to be arrogant and say "if these updates go live to the main servers I'm quitting" or anything like that, but if they really push these changes live as they are, I believe it will disappoint the absolute vast majority of players—very disappointed. It completely loses the flavor this game is supposed to have. Also, I suggest firing the designer in charge of this update.

translation_en: [h1][u] PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS [/u][/h1] It is a [b]First-Person[/b] and/or [b]Third-Person[/b], [b]Multiplayer[/b] game, "innovating" with the [b]Battle Royale[/b] theme. The game consists of 100 players who parachute onto an island (Erangel or Miramar) in search of weapons and gear with the objective of killing other real players, while trying to survive against the others who have the same objective as you. The playable area progressively shrinks, "trapping" the survivors in a smaller and smaller circle, which in turn forces all remaining players to encounter each other until the end. Whoever (Solo) or whatever team (Duo-Squad) stays alive until the last wins. [b]PUBG[/b] was born in the hands of [b]Brendan "PlayerUnknown" Greene[/b], who had previously developed mods in the same style for the game ArmA, and later created his own game. Brendan was inspired by the movie [b]Battle Royale[/b] to do so. [b]Pros:[/b] [list] [*] Graphics [*] Physics (read addendum!) [*] Immersion [*] Limitless [*] Event Mode [*] Solo, Duo & Squad [/list] [b]Cons:[/b] [list] [*] Optimization [*] Physics (read addendum!) [*] Cheaters [*] Bugs [*] Server - Duo FPP [/list] [h1]Addendum:[/h1] [b][u]Pros:[/u][/b] [b]Graphics:[/b] Very well-crafted graphics, always with lots of detail. The only problem is the saturation; on the Erangel map the colors aren't vibrant, quite the contrary, which can even make playing harder. In other words, saturation isn't merely a graphical aspect for visual satisfaction, but it helps when playing competitively and aiming to win. [b]Physics:[/b] Fluid movements, you feel the movement work, it's not stiff. And this applies both to vehicles and outside of them. An example I can cite of how spectacular vehicle movement physics is, is that in a certain car in [b]Miramar[/b], depending on which way you turn the steering wheel and straighten back out, it might pull to the side you were forcing it toward earlier, making it clear that the cars in that city urgently need an alignment shop ~hahahahah~... [b]Immersion:[/b] From pure relaxation while looting and gearing up your backpack, vest, and level 3 helmet, to the maximum distress and stress when you realize you're surrounded from all sides, or when there are only a few left so you can secure your [b]Chicken Dinner[/b]. [b]Limitless:[/b] You can go from 10h to 10000h played or maybe more. Who dictates the limit is you, and only you. The game manages to be and not be repetitive at the same time. It will always be the same basic things, looting, killing, healing, winning (or losing), but each battle in the field is something different, every shot is a new thrill whether it's good or not. [b]Event Mode:[/b] Unfortunately for a limited time, but it brings much more fun and action to what used to be monotonous. So far we've had two types of events (which can be played in Customs at any time): [b]War[/b], where you and nine other people on the same team drop into a very small, randomly chosen region of the map against other teams and must score the highest points until the time runs out, or reach the maximum score. Note: The only loot is done through airplane drops. As soon as you spawn you already get weapons, ammo, bandages, and maybe something else, which is random. Furthermore, it's worth noting that respawn is constant, roughly every 1 min. [b]Flare Gun[/b], you as usual spawn in the plane and choose with your team (another 4 people) where to drop and loot. The thing is, it's not that simple, the loot isn't the best and everyone is - just like you probably are - looking for flare guns, the ones that will call the plane and deliver the loot drop in the crate. Here's the problem, EVERYONE will be after these flares, or drops coming from planes, meaning in a drop region the firefight will be frenetic. Note: Using the flare outside the Safezone calls an armored car, while shooting inside the safe zone brings equipment like weapons, ammo, medkits, vests, etc. [b]Solo, Duo & Squad:[/b] Maybe it wasn't even necessary to put this here, but I think it's really great to have the freedom to play Solo, Duo, and Squad whenever you feel like it, and not need friends for it. I can play alone in either Duo or Squad, or with random people, and thus maybe make new friends. [b][u]Cons:[/u][/b] [b]Optimization:[/b] And here we are, blessed optimization. Want an optimized game? Stay far away from this one! There's not much to talk about here, unfortunately the game is completely poorly optimized (despite having improved a lot in recent updates). There are reports of people who can't run it without FPS drops using a GTX 1080, I7 7700k, and those who with a GTX 1050 TI run it smoothly. Maybe bad luck, maybe poor optimization for certain cards or drivers, maybe conflict with third-party apps running in the background, anyway, infinite possibilities. The thing is, you can get FPS drops, freezes, and crashes with anyone, whether you have a 550 or a Titan Pascal. [b]Physics:[/b] Damn the vehicles! How many times have I died because my car simply decided to grow a mind of its own and fly away? Or when I hit a tiny bump in the terrain with a motorcycle at full "health" and it exploded? To be honest, I've lost count of how many times this has happened to me. Don't get it? Look it up on YouTube after you finish reading here =P. Or better yet, I'll make it easy for you, just click [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Txl_TV3BuK0]HERE[/url] and you'll see this wonderful compilation of other people's misery with vehicles in PUBG! [b]Cheaters:[/b] Another heavily talked about point here (and rightfully so), the game used to be infested with cheaters (mostly Chinese), who still use them blatantly, without even trying to look legitimate. Fortunately, the number has decreased considerably in the last few months, and, it's not impossible, but it's much harder to find players using cheats or macros. That's not even mentioning the new DeathCam, and the option to report the player, which came to make banning those who are impure easier. Let's be real, it's no fun at all when you're full of loot, aiming at a player 1 km away with your Kar98k 8X tracking their movement and waiting for the opportunity to shoot, when suddenly they eliminate you with a burst from a Scar-L. That's why whenever you believe someone is actually using a cheat or macro, report them! [b]Bugs:[/b] Have I told you about the physics of cars and motorcycles yet? Well, I think so... Yeah, there's not much to say, the biggest problem right now is vehicles with their wonderful bugs. Other than that I think that's it, there are no other bugs that get in the way, not that I remember at least! [b]Server - Duo FPP:[/b] Basically, at the time I'm writing and publishing this review, there are no First-Person servers for Duo. In other words, play Third-Person, or go to the NA server and if you or your friend don't have good internet, suffer with lag. [b]Final Consideration:[/b] I was extremely hesitant about whether or not to recommend this game, but let's be honest, it's amazing. The only problem is the lack of maps (only two) and worst of all, the optimization. Otherwise there's nothing that bad (considering that cheaters are disappearing). I won't tell you that it's worth buying at the current price and under these conditions, but if you have cash to spare, and found it interesting, just buy it and be happy! [h1]Rating: 7/10[/h1] [code] Please, if I helped you with this review, check the "Yes" box in the recommendations. That way I can help more people and I'll be very grateful.[/code]

translation_en: About the April 12, 2018 update, seriously, changing the blue zone mechanic like this makes the whole game experience absolute garbage. It completely turned into an RNG zone game?? Whoever gets the buildings inside the circle is god tier. If you're outside and don't run into anyone, fine, you can manage to get in with decent health, but you're still gonna get shot at. If you do run into enemies, basically if a teammate goes down you can't even revive them, you kill someone and can't even loot their box, and you have to rush into the zone before you can heal up. No matter how high your skill is, if someone camps you, you're dead! Not to mention you can't even fully loot up anymore. A game with so many playstyles has been severely reduced to a pure deathmatch, and do you even die feeling satisfied? (Getting slaughtered by people sitting safely inside the RNG zone while you're driving or moving in—that kind of luck has zero to do with skill.) These players need a certain amount of time to think about tactics, but alright, you don't even give them time to think anymore, so these players just die in all sorts of ways with zero gaming experience. Did PUBG just pander to sweaty pros and abandon the mid-to-low-tier players? Are they trying to kill their own game? Let me just say, I have 950 hours in PUBG. I wouldn't dare call myself a pro, but I'm at least average, and I genuinely love this game. But this update completely broke my mental. Just driving all the way into the zone, spending most of the match inside a vehicle, to the point where once you get in a car you can't even get out. At first I thought there were still so many people alive with such a small circle because it was just updated and there were no cheaters yet, but I finally realized even cheaters have to drive to rotate, you can't outheal the blue zone, and there's no time to even shoot people. If they can't change this zone timing, I feel like quitting for good and just playing Rainbow Six and Battlefield. Bye-bye to this game. If you want hard gunfights and kills, those two games are way better. Don't we play PUBG to experience the thrill of looting high-tier gear? Well now they don't even give you time to loot, and there's no time to kill people and loot their boxes. This is just my personal opinion, if any of you guys think I make sense, please help reply and upvote this to the top!

translation_en: April 12, 2018 This is gonna be a long review. But a good one too. When it hit early access with its beta version around March 2017, it was so fucking terrible it was unplayable. It was terrible all the way until the desert map came out in early 2018. Just like all over the world, in Turkey it was hyped and loved by gamers who barely let 2 or 3 different games into their lives. Gaming and tech websites ran articles every single day with headlines like "PUBG breaks records." Every twitch streamer, every YouTuber loved the game in its trash state or loved the crates worth 5000 TL each that were showered upon them. Various organizations held tournament events. Along with all this, fanboys crawled out of the woodwork. They defended the game like their dads had made it. To anyone who said "this game is shit," they'd say "what the fuck do you know about games." PUBG clearly shows us one thing from a year ago when it launched until today: Marketing is what matters, not product quality. A year ago, a low-quality but well-marketed product was breaking records, yet today, even though it's become much higher quality, it's not marketed as well as it used to be. Some people pop up with irrational arguments like "Fortnite passed PUBG, I guess that means it's better bro." Of course Fortnite passed PUBG, because it's free. League of Legends passed Dota at least 5 years ago, for example. So I guess "that means LoL was better than Dota even 5 years ago, bro." Dota 2 had to go free-to-play so it wouldn't perish against its free rival LoL. LoL and Dota are comparable games. Their genres are the same, their gameplay, graphics, maps are almost identical. Hell, even their heroes and strategies are largely the same. Now, have you ever thought about what's the same between PUBG and Fortnite? Only the battle royale part. Trying to compare them just because they're both Battle Royale games means you don't understand the first damn thing about games. If streamers/YouTubers, and especially the gaming press, make this comparison and declare one of the winner, either they don't understand a single thing about games either, or they're part of the marketing. Don't get me wrong, I got nothing to say to people who just go "I like this, I have more fun playing that." My beef is with those who say Fortnite is higher quality than PUBG (or vice versa). If you're thick enough to compare Fortnite and PUBG, you can also compare DayZ and Rust. Because they're both Survival games. Hell, you can even compare an apple and a watermelon and say which one is higher quality. At the end of the day, they're both fruit. It just doesn't fucking work like that. An apple can only be compared to another apple. One is fresher, riper, or tastier. Don't be fooled by greengrocers / marketers who tell you watermelon is higher quality than an apple. Eat whatever the fuck you want. My thoughts on PUBG's current state are as above. As a game, the current state of PUBG, which has been constantly developed since its release, is more than enough to have a good time. The development process is ongoing and new content is being added. The best part of the game that hooks the player is being under constant risk of death, the resulting adrenaline rush, and the pressure it creates. The relief you feel when you shoot your opponent, the happiness of accomplishment when you win. Also: Well-designed maps. Enjoyable gameplay close to a simulation. Extra fun when played with teammates. Let's not skip the negatives either. Especially poor server-client performance at the start of the match. High system requirements for smooth gameplay. Big cities being way too big and detailed. The lack of a single-player training mode for players to improve themselves. Simple bugs sometimes not being fixed by the developers for a long time. For example; ridiculously loud airplane, vehicle, and explosion sounds. Red zones appearing way too often and in the same area. Bullets shot into water reacting as if they hit a wall. Finally: PUBG is not bleeding out. It's still played by 2.5 million different players simultaneously at certain times of the day.

The numbers already show that the game was/is a success, even with all its past and future limitations. So, I am 102% sure everyone already knows what game this is about (as of 21/03/18). I'll start with two questions, and answer them right after. Is the game good? Yes. Is the game bad? Not anymore. [i]But hold on, that's just my opinion, it doesn't mean it has to be yours too, alright?[/i] [b]But why is the game good?[/b] Well... due to my personal taste for FPS and PVP styles, it's a game where I can have fun and spend a few hours of my month (since lately it's been complicated to spare many hours of the day for an activity I like so much, which is gaming). Right now the game has decent performance on mid and high-end machines. I believe they (the developers) are actually working on improving their product to deliver a better user experience. And of course there are a few other factors that make me consider the game good; graphic quality and sound effects are two things worth pointing out, even though it's not the best game in the world in those aspects, not to mention the profit I've made from it to this day lol [b]And why did I ask if the game was bad and answered with "not anymore"?[/b] Basically because for me it no longer has some of the problems from before that made me consider it a bad game. I'm not saying PUBG doesn't have problems. Of course it does, normally, like all other games, and I hope they are always working to fix them. And if you ask me... "Leo, do you recommend the game?", my answer is kind of obvious. Yes, I recommend it. Just don't own a toaster and expect the game to run smoothly lol You'll have a lot of fun with this little online game, especially if you play with one or more friends. Fun and frustration are guaranteed, it depends a lot on the skill level of those involved. I tried to write around 1000 words but it's not gonna happen, so I'll just stick to the 387 words. [h1]Overall score: 9/10[/h1]

translation_en: HELL YEAH! For just 900 rubles (or less if you're a masochist and want to buy it on GAMESmail.sru), you get a massive range of new emotions. You thought you knew what having your ass on fire felt like? Nope, this game will show you. It'll burn always and everywhere for various reasons: - The game is drowning in cheaters with varying degrees of up-their-ass-bottle depth. Wallhacks, maphacks, aimbots, loot highlights, instant healing for themselves and teammates, teleports, no recoil. - The servers. Ohhh, it's just a fairy tale. There are zero Russian ones. None. Mail.sru promised to make them, but judging by recent data leaks, they didn't even sign up for it because Bluehole demanded quality servers, and our beloved distributor doesn't want to spend money. So what happens is — you land on a house before your opponent and start furiously tea-bagging over a weapon, but your character stupidly won't pick it up. Some dude runs up who is lagging behind the server, picks up the gun you've already stroked 50 times trying to pick up, along with the ammo for it. "No big deal," you think, and leap off the roof to bail somewhere and find a weapon. Fuck you. While you're in mid-air, the guy shoots at where you were 5 seconds ago and hits you dead on. Not to mention the fact that even if you find an assault rifle, you can get outgunned by a pistol because your bullets don't register, and instead of 5 hits, it counts 1. But every hit on you gets registered, and I repeat, in the killcam you might not even be on screen because you left ages ago, but nope. - Loot economy. You can search an entire house and only find an empty bottle for interesting personal use, while an opponent rolls out of a shed on a hoverboard in full level 3 gear, with two fully kitted ARs, and helps you figure out what to do with that bottle. - Vehicle physics. Oh what fun. Slightly better than in Total Overdose (c). You're riding a motorcycle, wind in your face, hair blowing in the breeze, everything is super. But God forbid you run over a 0.5 cm by 0.2 bump. You'll start pulling off such acrobatics. You'll fly up, do every known somersault, invent new ones, land right on your head no matter how hard you try to level out, and die. Or you're driving with the boys to a disco in the next village, and guys from another village come driving out to your disco. Collision. You get launched into flight. Literally punching through the clouds, the sky, and Allah, you fly to the other side of the map and then explode. Or cars can just glitch into each other and blow up, just because. - Cool textures, I've never seen anything like it. The cliffs on Miramar look like sliced butter with a stretched-out texture. Some of them aren't even solid, so you can glitch inside them and shoot everyone while nobody can hit you because they can't see you, and the rock isn't bulletproof. - (This downside is outdated, but I'll leave it for history) Optimization. Well, they seem to be working on it, but even on top-tier PCs you have to play on low settings because your FPS commits suicide the moment it sees a plate made of 22 polygons in an attic of a house you can't even enter. 10 scorched asses out of 5 chicken dinners

translation_en: Oh, this PUBG. A game worthy of praise, a simple idea, clunky execution, millions of players online every day, and a mountain of cash that fell on the developers. About the developers: The guys got insanely lucky, the idea hit the mark and took off like a supersonic missile. With that much cash, the devs lost their minds so hard that they don't even put the game on sale during Steam sales. What can you do, greed will be the death of them. People bought it and will keep buying it, with or without a discount. Over 32 million copies sold at $29.99 a pop. Not to mention the sales of crates, keys, etc. I feel like with that kind of money, they could have expanded the team by hiring talented developers who could have helped polish the game and make a working anti-cheat. About the game: The first few games were amazing, a storm of emotions, wins and losses, joy and anger. But then they came... Players with the hand of God, shooting from any position at any distance, through any obstacles, on the move, doing 360s, jumping no-scopes, with their eyes closed, with the pinky toe of their left foot, straight to the head. Oh yeah, cheaters—at this point, they're in every single game. There are clumsy-handed cheaters who, even with cheats, die at the start of every third match; there are those who try to hide their cheats by playing more realistically; and there are those who just put their tiny "you know what" right on me, on you, on the anti-cheat, on EVERYONE! The ones who have every cheat imaginable: Want top loot? Here you go. Don't want to sweat and want to run around like the Flash? No problem. Want to shoot with zero recoil? Easy. Want aimbot? Got that too. Don't even want to bother moving your mouse? Here's a cheat that sends all bullets straight to the target, just shoot in their general direction, plus homing grenades as a bonus. Someone dared to damage you? There's instant healing. From personal experience: I only play Duo with my brother. Once, the two of us were shooting at a single guy from 300 meters away, hitting him every other shot—a total of 6 hits! 1 hit to the body with an M24 and 5 more hits to the body with a Mini14, but by some miracle, he survived. I don't know how, but he survived, it wasn't a bug, we were shooting non-stop and it took about 7 seconds. Then, from the exact same distance, using a red dot sight, he dropped both of us with headshots. There were guys driving around the map in a car, shooting at everything within range. No hesitation, right through obstacles, one drives and the other shoots. What can I say, straight to the top. The only escape from cheaters is to dive underwater—bullets don't penetrate water. Too bad you eventually run out of air and have to surface... By the way, cheats cost money too, and the developers aren't even fighting them. Which raises the question: aren't the developers the ones selling these cheats? Cheaters buy the game, buy cheats, buy keys and crates, sell items, and pad the game's player count. Why fight them? It's a goldmine. Very suspicious... Optimization: It used to be absolute garbage, now it's gotten a bit better. Yeah, you need better hardware—hell, The Witcher 3 on high settings runs dozens of times better than this. P.S. The game is worth buying, it's fun to play, but not right now—cheaters will ruin the whole experience. I won't take this review down, even if they get rid of all the cheaters, because I've just had enough...

translation_en: [h1]A story of an unexpected encounter and a silent stranger.[/h1] My game takes forever to load. I only load into the match just as I'm already free-falling out of the plane. Usually, there's a couple of other guys dropping near me. Though maybe those are just AFKers? This time, there were 9 such bodies circling around me. Diving down, I spotted a car. A brilliant idea popped into my head: run all these poor bastards over. Landing, I hopped into the ride. It was an old-school minivan, the kind hippies drive in movies. Slow, but sturdy. As I rolled closer to the site of the upcoming carmageddon, I heard the roar of a second engine. My first thought was either lag, or someone just deciding to drive past. I was wrong. The second car didn't drive past. It started running the poor bastards over too. The stranger and I were taking out the AFKers with two cars. After squishing the last one, I got stuck in a ditch. The driver of the other car tried to ram me. But he stopped right next to me after the first try. Probably figuring it was pointless, or maybe because he got stuck in the ditch right next to me too. I got out of my car next to his. Tried to make contact using the video game sign language for mutes. For example, jumping means "apple," and crouching twice means "I'm friendly. Don't shoot." So that's what I did, crouched a couple of times. Started waiting for his reaction. Thought he didn't understand me. I was ready for him to show some kind of aggression toward me. I looked at him, and he knew I was waiting for some kind of response. He slowly stepped out of his car. Looked at me one more time, then crouched a couple of times. Yeah, he answered me, even with a bit of a heavy accent in mute language, but contact was established. After that, we took off running down the road, ditching our cars. We ran, maybe because there was still no trust between us. Whoever stops first takes a fist to the face. Maybe we were both thinking that, or maybe it was just me. But my thoughts were scattered by the sound of gunshots. Someone was shooting at us. While we were running, someone opened fire on the two targets. Totally predictable. Two unarmed people running along the road are great shooting gallery targets. We got lucky, didn't even get hit, and made our escape. Reaching a small cluster of houses with a motorcycle parked nearby—either out of distrust and a desire to ditch each other, or because we were far from the zone and running out of time—we both hopped on the bike. One was the passenger, the other the driver. We rode down the road until we hit some kind of suburban settlement I didn't know the name of. Split up into the houses. Scavenged through the trash for any gold that could help us survive. I found a UMP among all this junk. Time was running out and we'd looted everything in the houses, so it was time to get back to the vehicle and relocate. The thought crept in to ditch him and take off. But thinking it over again, I decided to wait. About 30 seconds later, he showed up. I aimed my SMG at him, he aimed his shotgun at me. The moment had come that could shatter our fragile friendship, requiring just a single left-click from either of us. Nothing happened. We both slung our guns back over our shoulders and got on the bike. That's when I knew I could trust him. We rode down the road. The wind was blowing through my hair and I was waving my gun left and right. My passenger and I were tearing it up. But as it usually goes, this couldn't last forever. Because sooner or later, one of us was going to betray the other anyway. After all, there could only be one survivor left in this bloody and brutal game. A game where you can't trust anyone. But we managed to break those rules, we were like Katniss and Peeta from The Hunger Games. We had this pure idyll going on, but it had to come to an end sooner or later. And then something happened that neither of us expected. We were betrayed by the motorcycle. Motorcycles are the most treacherous things in the game. You never know for sure if you're gonna die just trying to get on one, or if it's gonna clip on some random shit in the road and flip over? Or maybe it'll actually decide to work normally and get you where you need to go? Who even knows with these bikes. Dying on the road, I died with a smile on my face. I was glad it ended this way. Neither of us had to make the hard choice of shooting the other in the back. I thought about that during the final seconds of the round and hoped he was happy with this outcome too. We never exchanged a single word with each other. The sad part is that in the next incarnations of our avatars, the chance of us ending up in the same match is super low. Even if we do get matched, the chances of us meeting up are even lower. But even if we did meet, one of us would just kill the other without ever knowing it was that exact same "silent stranger."

translation_en: The internet was blowing up for a few days and the reply button wouldn't load at all. After it got fixed today, I noticed there were a ton of replies, and coincidentally I felt like a lot of parts were poorly phrased or had weak arguments, so I'm revising it. Heard Nuomi cleared his name, so I'm back to add to my review. Back when the whole thing with Old Immortal Huang calling out Nuomi happened, Bluehole swiftly banned Nuomi's account. As soon as Nuomi's account got banned, the associated streaming platform quickly followed suit and shut down his stream. While domestic players cheered, it kicked off a nationwide witch-hunt against cheaters, which eventually culminated when the famous streamer Lu XX was called out by state television. However, more than half a year has passed since this massive cheating war, and not only have the cheaters in China not been wiped out, there are only more and more of them. On top of that, the crisis of trust caused by cheaters has started to permeate the Chinese PUBG community. At this point, arguing over who is cheating and who isn't is completely pointless. Because whatever official statements Bluehole puts out are the only standard we accept. In other words, if you guys say someone is cheating, they're cheating; if you don't say anything, they aren't. I'm starting to feel bad for the people hunting down cheaters, risking getting doxxed and receiving offline threats, only to get zero forceful, official responses. Instead of roasting Bluehole's anti-cheat for so long, let's take a look back. How has Bluehole's anti-cheat performance been over the past half year? Based solely on the public info released, what left the deepest impression on me was that after Tencent announced they were publishing PUBG, they made an example of a few prominent cheaters. Most of the time, what we see is that right after servers go down for a new version update, the cheats just rise from the ashes. Compared to how other game companies handle anti-cheat, Bluehole is seriously way behind. Take Blizzard as an example. Their sworn enemy, Bossland, recently had to shut down all their cheats for Blizzard games worldwide. After Bossland developed the "Overwatch Bro" and completely crossed Blizzard's bottom line, it took only a year and a half for the District Court in Zwickau, Germany, to issue a final ruling ordering Bossland to stop infringing on Blizzard's copyrights. After that, Bossland switched to developing PUBG cheats instead. (Seriously Bluehole, you're turning into the town bicycle). Even though Blizzard isn't a totally perfect game company, when it comes to anti-cheat, Blizzard would rather piss off players than let up. Bossland's total collapse wasn't actually because they lost to Blizzard in court; a bigger reason was that the cheat developers couldn't guarantee the account safety of people using their cheats. In December 2017, Blizzard updated their game launcher and embedded a system in the background that constantly scans for suspicious programs (according to the farewell letter when WoW-Brother went down). You could say this is a severe violation of user privacy, but I gotta admit, it works. To this day, a lot of World of Warcraft cheat makers still haven't come up with a foolproof way to protect their customers' account safety. As for the current situation in China, we have to admit that the difficulty of protecting intellectual property and enforcing regulations here provides fertile ground for cheats. Usually, cracking down on cheats relies entirely on game developers taking the initiative to report the case to the police before law enforcement will strike down the cheat creators. For a company like Bluehole, which has no branch office in mainland China, cracking down on cheats probably relies entirely on this "unstable partner"—Tencent. In other words, if Bluehole hands the publishing rights of PUBG over to Tencent, Tencent will help you fight cheats. Conversely, Tencent can also sit back with a "not my problem" attitude and watch your reputation among mainland players go down the drain day by day. But then again, if your own product isn't solid, nothing you say matters. Right now, PUBG cheats are blooming everywhere, to the point where it's as bad as the game's source code being leaked (though some say the source code was leaked a long time ago). Actually, what players want isn't for you to just slap a simple ban on people using cheats; they want them to be stopped *before* they can use cheats and ruin other people's gaming experience—like failing to load into the match, or getting forced out of the game when abnormal activity is detected. So as things stand right now, Bluehole is nowhere near good enough. (Irresponsible conspiracy theory: Tencent has already started dipping its toes into battle royale games, like the old-school H1Z1 and the rising star Fortnite. After state TV called out PUBG in early 2018, there's a good chance the review process for the national server of PUBG will hit some roadblocks. If Tencent finds it too hard to launch the national server of PUBG, they might just pivot to recommending Fortnite to domestic players instead, since it's already localized and much easier to get approved under the battle royale mode.) As for region locking, well, every player knows what's up. The day Tencent announced they were publishing this game, rumors were already flying that Bluehole would region-lock mainland IPs in the future to ensure the national server ran properly. As for whether mainland players who already bought the Steam version of PUBG will still be able to play normally? Just look at Rocket League next door. However, what really pissed me off is Bluehole contradicting and slapping themselves in the face. Since you can't handle the wave after wave of attacks from Chinese cheat developers, then just own up to it fair and square. Don't go doing interviews saying, "Even though most players using cheats come from China, we can't generalize and paint all Chinese players with the same brush," while on the other hand messing around with ping-based matchmaking and dedicated regional servers, effectively penning the cheaters up so Chinese players just digest them among themselves. If you think 98 RMB isn't worth the price of your game, then raise the price. We Chinese players don't want to be treated like second-class citizens. If you think we players who bought your game for 98 RMB are on the same level as those foreign players screaming to region-lock China, fine, then step up your efforts to crack down on actual cheaters instead of banning us. These Chinese players using cheats are making the honorable and proud word "Chinese" carry the stigma of being "cheaters" in this game, and in this game, I don't acknowledge them as Chinese. Talking about this, I even feel a bit bad for H1Z1. Back then, they just looked down on Chinese players and region-locked the game even if it meant getting cursed out. They didn't want to offend either side and ended up offending both, but at least their region lock had more spine than you do. Today, I am roasting Bluehole in this review not just because your anti-cheat is weak and made me lose my patience, but because of your actions. You don't act like a company with a product that has tens of millions of players; instead, you act like some newly founded garage startup. Haven't you guys grown at all as a company since releasing PUBG on Steam? Ever since I bought this game, the things you've done have steadily lowered the floor of my expectations: A game developer advertising "Xunyou Dedicated Accelerator" right inside their own game. Two streamers having a beef, so you hastily ban an account yourself, only to be forced to unban it later. Where is your company's credibility? What's even harder to believe is that a gaming company actually had scandals leaked about its regional director taking bribes because of a falling out with his girlfriend. I guess Bluehole really set a first in the gaming industry. Today, Nuomi cleared his name. Good for Nuomi, I wish him smooth sailing in his future career. If Lu Wei can clear his name in the future, I'll wish him smooth sailing too. Even though I've edited my review quite a bit, if your anti-cheat system is truly beyond saving, then just give up on PUBG already and get so bloated that you go develop AAA titles instead. Either way, I still hope every single game your company puts out bombs hard. Fxck You Blue Ass♥hole

translation_en: I have nearly 500 hours in PUBG. I guess that's not super long, but it's definitely not short either. I got into the game around June of last year, back when those rare 10,000 RMB crates only cost 100 RMB. Man... My classmate and I grinded this game for the entire summer vacation. All summer long, I was dreaming about getting a full squad together. But sadly, with such trash optimization and servers, nobody wanted to play it. After the summer ended, the game blew up. It went from having fewer players than CS:GO to hitting all-time highs on Steam. The game got popular, and I was stoked! Because a lot of people around me stopped playing trash Honor of Kings and started playing PUBG. A lot of people got introduced to Steam, and many even bought new PCs just for PUBG. Back then, I thought with a market this huge, it meant better optimization and servers. Maybe this was going to be the next LoL or Overwatch. But what happened next totally caught me off guard. Everyone knows it's hard to completely get rid of cheaters in FPS games, but PUBG just amplified that shit infinitely. Before PUBG, seeing a top streamer get caught cheating was a once-in-a-blue-moon event. After PUBG blew up, you'd see three in half a year. Bluehole, I think you might as well just take down the Asian server's top 10 leaderboard. No matter when you open that leaderboard, 9 out of 10 are QQ/WeChat group promos. Every time they talk about updating the anti-cheat system, you log in, check the leaderboard, and well, it's fucking useless. How out of hand has the cheating in this game gotten? Averaging dozens of kills a game and shooting straight into the top 10 of the Asian server. What does that even mean? It's like a few serial killers slaughtering civilians and then breakdancing right outside the police station—and the cops still don't arrest these criminals! Later, Bluehole added a killcam feature. I have no idea if it even does anything, but out of all the people I reported, I didn't get a single feedback message. But I refuse to believe not a single person got banned. What does it mean when these guys still don't get banned? It's like someone clearly videotapes the criminal's face right before getting killed, catches the entire crime on camera, and even hands the perpetrator's name over to the cops, yet the police still can't catch them. I don't even want to talk about the optimization and servers, because Bluehole is a small company, and they need time to fix those things. But the cheaters and fatherless Red Zone armies are genuinely fucking destroying this game. The Red Zone army hides behind retarded patriotic slogans to team up maliciously, and their pathetic little chants of "China No. 1" sound so weak. They aren't patriotic at all; they're an embarrassment to our country. They make foreigners associate China with malicious teaming and cheaters. It even makes me wonder if Chinese people aren't meant to use Steam and should just stick to Tencent and NetEase. I won't even mention the behavior of Chinese players in PUBG. I've seen a foreigner say "hello," and Chinese players would immediately start screaming abuses at them, using really nasty language. Seriously, I don't want to swear, but I just keep wondering how the fuck Chinese people's basic decency can drop this low—cheating, malicious teaming, hurling abuse at random. And here we are still bragging about 5,000 years of Chinese culture and being a civilized capital, when this single game completely invalidates all of it. Chinese PUBG players, please stop bringing up each other's mothers the second you meet. Stop dragging patriotism into a fucking game. Stop constantly trying to code and hack your way through a game. It's just a game to be played for fun, alright?

translation_en: Alright let's be clear, it's a very good game (on paper), but I'm writing this review because at some point you have to stop treating people like morons. Let's start with the positives: The game is very immersive, you plunge right into the BR vibe, you're playing for your life. The graphics aren't too shabby. translation_en: I'll try to write this down as detailed as possible and people can say whatever or trash me for it, but I'm still going to list aspects that I managed to deduce after 50 hours of gameplay. The PUBG phenomenon itself: Players have always been starved for this kind of game, and the whole theme has become pretty hyped, especially since the first survival games and the movie creation and books called "The Hunger Games". No wonder this genre and name suddenly became hyped, because it's wrapped in a clean and pretty package... plus they're fast-paced... faster-paced than say a LoL match, and if you die, many times you're into the next game within moments. Literally, it was created in a simple yet brilliant way. From this perspective, 8/10 is my score for the game. "Be faster than anyone else": This is supposed to be one of the main mottos and driving forces of the game, but that's not how it is. This is really only 50% true because the luck factor is heavily present there. Actually, if I want a game based on luck, there are card games for that where, of course... you build the deck yourself, but how the cards are dealt... you don't decide that anymore. And yes... this is a virtualized card game. Many times you drop down to a place with multiple people... everyone gets a house and oops... you happen to pick the exact house where you find at most a single magazine or a helmet. Since it's 50% luck... and 50% how much you really immerse yourself in it... how skilled and fast you are... it deserves 5/10 points... not a single bit more. Hit box... aka... it's there, but it's not there: I watched a lot of videos and sometimes I scratch my head as to why a bunch of good shots don't register for me that most of the video makers hit, let's say. Well... after some head-scratching and hair loss, I realized that the vast majority of the videos... came out well before 1.0, and lo and behold... as the game expanded, the overall picture comes together more and more painfully. You see it right... somehow the more content and options there are, the more the existing things slip away. If you try it, you'll figure out what I'm talking about. So the bottom line. The surface to shoot at is not always where you see the enemy character. Sometimes before it... sometimes after it. Or by coincidence, right where it needs to be. Completely random. Sometimes it really hits... other times you rewatch the Killcam and you see that you didn't hit it even once, from your perspective it even bleeds... showing that "you hit it"... This ruins the experience a lot... a whole lot. 3/10 Lack of optimization: This game only runs FLAWLESSLY from start to finish for someone who has already sacrificed quite a bit of time and money into their rig. Heavy FPS drops and sometimes the servers lag really hard too. 3/10 And absolute despair. Cheaters: Yes... unfortunately, this game has also been reached by the masses of cheaters, because you can "farm money" with this game to no small extent. You can get accessories for your character that only beautify them but give no advantage... but there are clothing items that go for 150-200-300 Euros. Yes... which can ultimately be credited to your Steam account. Well... then I don't even need to explain what kind of a farm that means if you're successful... and a lot of people... are capable of a lot of things for this profit, and its Anti-Cheat system is currently dead weak. 1/10. The scores are as follows: 8, 5, 3, 3, 1. Total score: 4 / 10. This is dead weak and only enthusiastic fanatics, farmers, and beginners who hopped on the hype train are the ones keeping it alive right now. My review is that no one should buy this for now. That 30 Euros is still too much for a game with a 4.3 average score. But it's worth keeping an eye on it because if they focus heavily on these issues and points... then it could become a really good game.

translation_en: Feeling hopeless and ashamed as a Chinese player. I'm not ashamed of being Chinese, but of the behavior of other Chinese players. First off, this game genuinely blew me away—the intense pace, the thrilling competition, teamwork... it all got my adrenaline pumping. However, cheaters are rampant and the devs can't stop them, and recently the "Red Army" slaughtering foreign players made me realize the flaws of certain Chinese players: self-righteousness! A game is not a competition between countries, nor between races. The moment everyone parachutes down, they are fighting for themselves and their squad. That was the developers' original intent. Now, destroying the game environment under the banner of patriotism is genuinely something we Chinese players need to reflect on. This game isn't a charge led by army legions; it's backstabbing survival. I hope those in the Red Army see this and repent. Secondly, the cheating issue. Us poor folks call cheaters "Immortals," which is the foreigners' "GOD." But we don't have an ounce of respect for them; instead, we despise and spit on them. We will do our utmost to resist cheaters, and I hope Bluehole steps up too and crushes them. After all, a game's quality is decided together by the players and the developers. Also, regarding the optimization, I hope they can buff the servers because Chinese servers lag every night around 8 PM, I hope they take this seriously. To the foreign players crying for region lock, I can only express my sympathy and apologies. Here, on behalf of all Chinese players who just want to play normally, I want to say SORRY to you guys. We originally hoped to play together with you, hoped for interactions without borders, yet this incident that angers all players happened. This mistake legitimately stems from the ingrained bad nature of some of our players, bringing so-called patriotism into the game. From the bottom of my heart, to all foreign friends and all normal Chinese players, I want to say one thing: I'm sorry, my apologies.

translation_en: **I have a 2,000-word character biography due next Tuesday, but here I am writing this review instead. Have a heart, guys, and smash that like button quq!** Alright, jokes aside, to be honest, my first impression of this game can be summed up in two words: **fucking retarded.** That's a very subjective review because back then I hadn't even bought the game. Mainly influenced by games like H1Z1, it gave me the impression that both the players who play these games and the games themselves are total retards. [spoiler]In my opinion, cheaters = retards, any objections?[/spoiler] I bought this game last September because I wanted to play with my roommate. Ended up closing it after just a few minutes. Anyone who's been around for a while knows why; the early flaws of this game were just too many. (Especially since I had PvP anxiety back then.) But last week, my badass roommate and I played a duo match [strike]which was basically soloing for him[/strike], and with only 8 hours of playtime, I got my very first chicken dinner. By last night, at my 13th hour of playing, I experienced a 4-man squad chicken dinner. Team coordination feels amazing, doesn't it? These experiences started to change my perspective on the game. I realized the game itself isn't retarded, **the only retards are those Hackers.** I found myself starting to enjoy the tension brought by PvP and the thrill of victory. (Though my PvP anxiety was actually cured by Rainbow Six.) The beginner R6 skills I had gave me an advantage in reaction time and awareness during close-quarters firefights, which greatly improved my gaming experience. Having tasted my first chicken dinner, I slowly started to accept the game. I started trying out solo queue, which I used to be very resistant to. My ranking kept getting higher and higher, slowly ratting my way from outside the top 50 into the top 15, even the top 10 [spoiler]anyway I've never won a solo match, winning a solo chicken dinner is impossible, absolutely impossible in this lifetime, you can only survive by ratting your way into the top ten[/spoiler]. Dying right off the drop seemed further and further away, and I started having my own favorite playstyle [spoiler][strike]probably some sort of peaceful Zen/Daoist rat playstyle[/strike][/spoiler]. I started getting used to the game's ballistics, and I started learning how to control recoil [spoiler]though controlling the C8 with an extended barrel and 2.5x is never gonna happen.[/spoiler] Seriously, when I got the first blood of the match with a pistol, when I looted my first airdrop, when I first saw those words "Winner Winner Chicken Dinner", those subtle feelings were unlike anything I'd ever felt. Ever since I first played CS 1.5 when I was five years old, up until now, I have never had such an enjoyable gaming experience. (Cheaters excluded.) This game has an irresistible charm. It's not like the game's foundation is that great; PUBG is still just a pure PvP game. It doesn't have the nostalgia of CS, the storyline of Mafia 2, or the worldview of Dark Souls and Elder Scrolls. All it has is constantly running from the blue zone and shooting. But yet this monotonous content gives me a sense of joy and accomplishment that other games don't. Alright, enough praising the game, time to rant. 1. Cheaters, seems like there's some improvement? Hope they keep cracking down. 2. Optimization, a 1070, 1700x, 12GB RAM, all settings on high and I'm barely getting 60+ FPS (Okay, maybe my standards are a bit high here, but optimization is still important, right?) 3. Content, red zones, airdrops, blue zones, looting houses, driving cars, opening crates [strike]teabagging teabagging QEQE pressing T to trash talk[/strike]. Once you've done these, you've pretty much experienced 80% of the game. I hope they add some more gameplay-enhancing content in the future. 4. Handling, meaning vehicle handling here, just keeping the formatting neat. While vehicle handling isn't exactly terrible, it's pretty shit. I'm not asking for NFS or GTA 5 physics, but at least when driving over some rough terrain, can you not make the car emit that scraping chassis sound? It's really fucking grating. (Don't give me that realism bullshit, this is a game.) 5. Servers, nothing much to say, they've improved but still need more work. 6. Oops, looks like I'm running out of bullshit to write? But the formatting has to stay neat. That's pretty much what my first 50 hours of gameplay felt like. I'm starting to look forward to this game, hope they don't let the player base down. =====================2018.11.13========================== The teacher who made me write that 2,000-word character biography passed away. Feeling kind of sad. Though aside from the new map, it doesn't seem like there have been many gameplay updates? Server quality is still a joke, hackers are still running rampant. Well, they are a small indie company after all.......

This game used to be a gacha where you rerolled until you got the super rare old map, but updates evolved it into a gacha where you wait for a match without cheaters. Light players like me don't run into cheaters very often when playing solo, but the second you play with someone who plays every day, you're suddenly swarmed by cheaters. On top of that, when you watch streamers and pro gamers, there's almost always a cheater, and the conversation always assumes a cheater is present—like, "Is this cheat level something we can actually beat?" Please make it so people can never buy the game again once they get banned for cheating. What's the deal with players from a certain country getting a refund even after getting banned for cheating, and then using that money to buy the game again? What's up with internet cafes in a certain country having cheats pre-installed? Are you just letting them run wild? [h1]A certain country... certai... IT'S CHINA, DAMMIT![/h1] Queue up for random squads and 90% of the time you're stuck with 3 Chinese players. Even if you use voice chat to tell them you're Japanese and don't understand Chinese, they just yell at you in Chinese. Well, it's not even necessarily that they're yelling, but they're so damn loud all the time that it feels aggressive. When I occasionally run into English or Korean speakers, a small spark of friendship is born. And I have literally never run into a Japanese player in random matchmaking. I queued up auto-matchmaking with 2 friends, and the random fill was a Chinese kid. He only spoke a language I didn't understand, but ignoring that I cheered him on with a "Go go!", and out of nowhere the kid team-kills me and steals my loot. When my surviving friend avenged me, the kid yelled "Motherfucker!" and disconnected. Oh, so you *can* speak English after all! I tried talking to you in all sorts of ways earlier and you completely ignored me. [b]I D O N O T R E C O M M E N D I T[/b] [h1]I don't know if it does anything, but I signed the petition too[/h1] I'm sure many of you already know, but the dev team's news posts are being flooded with comments saying "RegionLockChina." Or instead of just blocking players when cheats are detected, why not silently drop the detected players into their own dedicated server so they only play against each other? Why not try isolating them for about a week? I know you guys are working hard on countermeasures, but isolation is the cleanest and most effective solution. The core fun of the game is top-tier, so I've got high hopes. If things turn out for the better, I'll happily change this to a positive review. Peace out.

translation_en: Welcome to Playerunknown's Hackergrounds!! Well, 250 hours played and probably quite a few more will drop, but I don't recommend the game at all because of the invasion of the Chinese community and their culture regarding hacks and derivatives. The game is based on constant randomness, but it obviously leaves room to achieve your objectives, so once you accept that the game sets the pace and forces you to make decisions you would never make, besides dying quite a few times in situations where you can never defend yourself, it will get much better (no sarcasm, you truly need a perfect attitude, if you manage that the game is really good). I won't go too much into the aspects of the game, because the game itself has a high quality (except for the damn fall damage when you fall out of the parachute, or getting stuck in a couple of rocks falling into infinity...), but I will put emphasis and deeply focus on the subject of hackers, which is a long story. First of all, trying to do duo or squad with randoms from Europe is impossible, you're only going to get Asians with Chinese as their language, so communicating with them isn't very possible. Every now and then when you try to communicate with them they just murder you and take all your items, otherwise they completely ignore any directions and it's all the same anyway. Apparently the massive arrival of people from China and surroundings to all servers in the world is tremendous, our friends are truly causing havoc. All the hackers, or 95% of them, are Asian. I've recently discovered a little bit more about the motives that can lead someone from those countries to carry out this type of action systematically. At first, the earnings considering the time invested were ridiculous, but with the new crates a rot of power takes over these people in the form of an apparent necessity, because it's obvious they aren't having fun, I think that's something we're all clear on; maybe for the first 5 games they find it curious, but then with absolute certainty an infinite boredom hits them, even so, they keep up those practices, and the reason ** is that now they can earn about 4-7 dollars a week if they are lucky and depending on the price of the crate at that moment (at first you could earn up to 25 dollars, but now prices have stabilized). There is a limit of 6 crates per week. China's monthly minimum wage, depending on the region, goes from 150 dollars to 300 dollars. We're talking about being able to make 4-7 dollars a week, so every month 16-28 dollars, which considering their minimum wages is not bad at all. If you add to that that they probably have many accounts to be able to reach the crate limit with each of them and cashing out the money from steam to other means through various ways that I won't say because they'd be considered illegal conduct... you get the answers to the hackers. *** The developers comment that they ban huge amounts of people, but it's a joke to see how 50% of the matches when you reach the end, they kill you with zero recoil, from the hip, and with 100% precision, and with an abysmal wall hack. The combinations are fun, sometimes they carry aimhack, sometimes wallhack, sometimes one of the two, sometimes some variant that makes it more complicated to distinguish with different nuances, like making it look like there is recoil but actually there isn't, modifying the recoil to be slightly less or directly having no recoil but without having aim hack, making the crosshair not move at all 100% of the time as if you were holding your breath (but there is recoil), making breath recovery instantaneous, not having to zero for bullet drop, seeing 100% of objects through 1km around, and depending on their rarity they emit a certain color. 75% of hacker teammates carry all the combinations, and it's insulting, but some truly know how to hide it, only by watching the replay of their game can you get to know if they have something. There is a truly huge amount of mods, very varied and extremely difficult to know if they have hacks, but some are very subtle and complicated to perceive, only the typical aim hack is the obvious one, but there are dozens and dozens, the aim hack is not the most abundant hack. As I was saying, in 50% of the matches that reach the end I encounter hackers, I don't want to imagine the ones I don't reach, considering that the hacker obviously is always going to reach the end of the game, and until you reach that end you have less chances of encountering him, probably in 80% of the games there are hackers (although as I was saying, there are many types of hacks). It's a true scam the absolute indifference that our friends at Bluehole feel, it's no use banning when they can get the game for 10 dollars, you can report people on their forum, but after weeks of posting a report they don't even deign to look at it, they must be overwhelmed... They've already taken the money, I deduce they don't need anything else from us anymore, what a shame. All hackers have Asian names, or with numbers, which is basically the same, Asians have an incredible fixation with names composed of numbers, regional locking the game would improve it infinitely, because it's not only the systematic hackers of that origin, but all the lag that can be produced by their tons of ms that they are giving away everywhere. I do not recommend buying it, until they do something, as soon as the patch came out the hackers came out of their caves. EDIT: 05/23/2018 Well, I don't know how the game is currently regarding the third-person mode and its relation to cheaters, but in first person I have never perceived with any certainty all the problems I mentioned in the review. I could re-do the review and adapt it to certain current aspects where the game fails miserably, but overall it's a game that is worth it and I don't think it's necessary to beat to death its main premise: The developers constantly fail in their perception of what it means to add content and in the very meaning of the word, you just have to take a look at the direct competition (Fortnite) to realize what the word content truly means, besides pacing correctly (I must say that personally there has been no game like Fortnite that has called my attention less, that doesn't take away from knowing that what they have done with that game is worthy of admiration, and has formed an entity of its own that one must undoubtedly look at).

Also, they do ban cheaters, but if I were a company, I'd probably let the cheats be sold, and once the user base grew, ban them to force people to buy the game again and make money. Honestly, PUBG feels like it's doing exactly that right now. Server management is a joke too. Plus, the textures and rendering for long-range fights look even worse. Does a game with zero progress really deserve to be called a "god game" just because it's Korean? If you're thinking of buying it, wait until the official release, after the test server updates go live on the main servers, and listen to what players with mid-to-low-tier setups have to say before you buy.
