translation_en: Because of this review, I pissed some people off. Some flamed me in the review section, some left hate comments on my profile, some added me on friends just to flame me, and some threatened to shit on me on Baidu Tieba. I am seriously sick of being harassed.......... Let me reiterate: many people like CF or H1Z1 and think my review was hating on them. I want to state: the only thing I'm hating on is the quality of these games themselves and their publishers, not the players who play them. Players aren't above or below each other, but games definitely range from excellent to trashy, and publishers range from conscientious to scumbag. Take H1Z1, for example. I don't hate it just because its popularity is slowly dying down now—I hated it even when it was at its absolute peak. I will hate it forever. What I despise is Daybreak's discrimination against Chinese players: on one hand, they added localized Chinese, but on the other hand, they region-locked buying but not playing, teamed up with VPN providers to run cheap, tacky marketing using cheap patriotic gimmicks, and started that whole "China No.1" circlejerk. Their business practices are downright ugly. So! Fucking! Shameless! Any game might hold too many emotions and memories for players, their passion and dreams, the good times spent with friends, countless late nights pulling all-nighters at internet cafes, their fading youth and memories..... But people gotta grow up eventually, people gotta experience a wider world out there. When you play better games and meet more honest publishers, you inevitably look back at the games you used to play. Strip away all those emotional factors and just look at the game's quality, and you'll realize what absolute trash those games and publishers actually are. I respect your youth and memories, I understand your genuine affection for any game, but there are just some games and publishers whose practices I cannot respect. The End. ======================================================== The comment section is not a toilet or a cesspool. So anyone coming in here just to greet my family or throw mindless abuse will have their comments deleted without exception. I hope everyone can discuss games rationally and avoid personal attacks. ======================================================== A bunch of people left negative reviews for this game just because it didn't go on sale during the 2017 Summer Sale......... For fuck's sake! This is the most retarded reason for a negative review I've seen all fucking year! I can't take it anymore, I can't忍, I gotta speak up, I gotta start ranting! You have the right to bitch about the game not going on sale—that's your freedom of speech. But I feel like giving a negative review *just* because there's no sale might end up burying a good game! Please!!! This is the review section, alright?! Not fucking Baidu Tieba!!! Reviews are supposed to be about your personal gaming experience, not a place to shitpost and chat bullshit! Do some fucking homework before you hate on games, will you?! Your arbitrary and brutal reviews are not only useless, they're likely to mislead newbies, okay? Most people reading reviews aren't looking for your shitposting or smartass remarks; they genuinely want to know if the game is right for them. I hope there'll be fewer of these brain-dead reviews in the future, and more rational, objective analysis. List out the pros and cons one by one so everyone can make up their own minds. Whatever, I didn't even want to comment, but I just had to get this off my chest. Let me say a few more words. As of July 2017, the game has only been released for a little over 3 months and is still in Early Access, but as of July 21st, it has topped the global Steam weekly sales charts for 17 consecutive weeks. That's a new record for Steam games. PUBG and H1Z1 belong to the same battle royale genre. PUBG is more expensive than H1Z1, has worse optimization, and came out more recently, yet it sells better than H1Z1, has more players, and is more popular. This clearly proves that its quality has stood the test of time!!! But because it's in Early Access, the game still requires massive amounts of effort, manpower, and money to polish. Most players are willing to pay for it because they have higher expectations and want a better gaming experience. The fact that this game is so popular right now shows that everyone recognizes and loves it. For a developer that actually makes games seriously, one that is willing to interact with players, listen to their feedback, and constantly improve, one that works hard to optimize the game—not going on sale is totally reasonable. Besides, I know developers are out to make a profit, and when a game is this hot, "only an asshole wouldn't make money," but in a way, doesn't keeping the original price also have the effect of increasing the cost of cheating? Also, the base price of this game is 98 RMB. I want to ask those people whining about negative reviews over no sale: how much do you think this game should cost? 69? 49? 29? 19? 9 bucks? How about free? If you think even 98 RMB is too expensive, then I suggest you stop playing games and figure out how to make some money instead. Some domestic players have gotten so used to being raped by "free-to-play" web games and Tencent games that they've practically developed Stockholm syndrome. They bitch and moan about a 98 RMB buy-to-play game, but they drop 888 RMB on a Fire Kirin weapon or reload a 20 RMB/month QQ Super VIP subscription for half a year without a single complaint. Haven't you guys seen how in CrossFire you even have to pay extra real money just for a bulletproof vest? Games that wave the flag of "free-to-play" while setting up in-game purchases or items that mess with game balance—*those* are the fucking most expensive games out there!!! I feel like the essence of gaming is fair competition, so everyone can enjoy the fun of competing on a level playing field. But in China, it turned into: "Want to get stronger? Top up your account, bitch!" How many domestic players have been pinned to the ground and face-rolled by cash-sharks just because they couldn't afford to pay or didn't pay enough! Don't you feel any anger towards game companies or publishers (yes, I'm talking about company T) that don't treat regular players like human beings and divide players into different tiers? I remember a web game publisher once said: "Free-to-play players or those who refuse to spend money are actually just part of our game content, equivalent to NPCs in the game. They exist so that paying players can experience the joy and sense of achievement of crushing and curb-stomping them." The wording is crude, but the point stands. I hope you guys don't forget how to fight back just because you're so used to being oppressed and squeezed by domestic online games!! Alright, I'm done venting. Let me calm down, get back on topic, and talk about the pros and cons of this game. Since the game is still in Early Access, players planning to jump in need to pay attention to the following points: ① The biggest issue right now is game optimization. The game had a major update at the end of June 2017 which noticeably improved optimization and gave a nice boost to frame rates, but many mid-range PCs still run into stuttering, slow model loading, low FPS, and random crashes to desktop during gameplay. You just have to communicate with the devs to help them polish it and give them some time. If your PC specs aren't good enough, I suggest playing on the lowest graphics settings. I often play on very low or low settings myself, and honestly, once you get used to it, it doesn't affect winning or losing all that much. I'll explain why below. ② Cheaters. All online shooter games inevitably face this headache—games like Battlefield 1, H1Z1, and even Counter-Strike, which has been out for nearly 20 years. But the officials are also working hard to improve things. Over the past 3 months, they've banned a total of 25,000 game accounts. They've definitely shown the attitude and determination to fight cheaters; now it's just a matter of technical execution. While the current BattleEye anti-cheat system isn't perfect, apart from VAC, it's currently the best solution available (fun fact: Rainbow Six Siege also uses BattleEye, and it works pretty well). Please understand. Also, please start with yourselves and work with your friends to build a fair and harmonious gaming environment. You absolutely cannot "fight fire with fire," otherwise that's just the pot calling the kettle black. ③ The "China No.1" issue. Compared to H1Z1, this issue is a lot better in this game, and I don't want to comment on it too much. Just one sentence: Anyone seeking a sense of self-worth in a game, anyone hiding behind patriotism while making remarks that damage the nation's image or engaging in inappropriate behavior, and anyone trying to achieve psychological gratification by putting down, slandering, or even insulting others—they are all absolute losers in real life. Even though this is a Chinese review, this applies just as well to foreigners. I hope everyone focuses more on enjoying the fun of the game itself and cuts out the pointless trolling. ④ The gameplay here is different from other battle royale games. Gunplay and graphics aren't actually the most critical factors for getting a chicken dinner. Sometimes you gotta be a coward to survive, coward your way to the top. The longer you play, the more you'll realize this game is crawling with rat bastards (especially on the Asian servers), and their various rat tactics will piss you off to the point of coughing blood. Of course, sometimes luck is also a major factor (like whether the safe zone randomly spawns close to you or far away). But if you think about it, out of 100 players only one gets a chicken dinner, and the other 99 are destined to be courier boys, so keeping a recreational and relaxed mindset might make it much more fun. Don't stress too much if you keep failing to get kills or chicken dinners. If you're really that pissed off, go to KFC and grab a couple of chicken leg burgers, order some McNuggets from McDonald's with an iced cola, and life is still pretty sweet! ⑤ VPNs. I suggest using a VPN. If you choose to play on a direct connection, high ping will seriously ruin your gaming experience. It might vary depending on region; coastal Guangdong is probably a bit better. I'm in North China and I've always used NetEase UU. It's relatively cheap at 29 RMB a month, and overall pretty stable. I hope that once the domestic player base hits a certain threshold, the devs will add some servers in mainland China (rumor has it that domestic company Three Hundred Dreams is going to publish this game?). Like I said, game publishers are out to make money. As long as our domestic player base is large enough and the demand is loud enough, I believe that—just like the Steam Chinese localization—it will catch the official's attention and things will improve. ⑥ The green blood issue under the Chinese UI. Once you get familiar with gun attachments and gear (after about 50 hours?), you can change your game language settings to something other than Chinese (like English or Japanese), and you'll be able to see red blood in the game. ⑦ Strongly recommend teaming up with your good bros for duos or squads. You'll find way more fun that way!!!! ⑧ The game has a custom match mode (essentially privately hosted servers). You can find plenty of interesting modes and settings in these servers (including Zombie Mode), and by the way, you can also practice your aim there. Just keep in mind that playing in these custom servers won't record your stats or rankings, and you won't earn any BP coins either. ⑨ The game getting stuck on the loading screen. This is usually caused by the UI freezing or a slow internet connection. If the UI is frozen, you can click the first refresh icon in the upper right corner of the game to reload it. If your internet is too slow, try switching your VPN node. Lastly, have fun gaming! See you in the game!

[h1]Pros:[/h1] [*]very good gunplay that rewards tactical play (run and gun as well as constant hip-firing should be avoided) [*]nice animations (e.g. picking up items, switching weapons, and parachuting) [*]many different weapons (everything from sniper rifles to AKMs, M16s, handguns, and submachine guns is represented and is fun) [*]weapon mods are useful and easy to use (suppressors, buttstocks, and various sights) [*]the map is versatile, large, and has many places worth seeing [*]realistic movement animations and mechanics (no, I can't jump out of moving cars and start shooting immediately or even expect to still be alive - looking at you H1Z1) [*]weather and sound effects are very atmospheric (in the rain it's easier to sneak around, giving you tactical advantages) [*]no microtransactions so far (although these are planned to be introduced after the EA phase) [*]there are various cars and also boats [h1]Cons:[/h1] [*]melee combat (currently very inaccurate, but also too strong, e.g. with fists) [*]currently too few rewards (you can use in-game currency earned through playing to buy crates containing random rewards like a mask or a shirt, but these are purely cosmetic) [*]sometimes desync and poor performance due to server issues (though this only happened very rarely for me) [*]sound bugs involving vehicles and your own footsteps (often you think there's an enemy right next to you) [h1]Conclusion:[/h1] I am generally very satisfied with the gameplay, but the game is still a long way from being perfect. Performance causes a few issues from time to time, but overall it runs very well on my PC (which is high-end). Still, in its current state it's already a lot of fun and is a definite recommendation if you're a Battle Royale fan and can tolerate a few small bugs. Jump out of a plane, grab a weapon, and with plenty of tactics, luck, and skill, become the true 'King of the Kill' ;-) [h1]Join our Steam group: [url=http://steamcommunity.com/groups/Diamond-People#]Diamond People💎[/url][/h1]

translation_en: After fixing the LSP issue in the first step, I got into the game. I didn't buy it at launch, and I saw that most of the negative reviews were about optimization. The "3D church waiting" loading screen does indeed sometimes freeze the first time it loads and when returning to the game. The game uses Unreal Engine 4, and there aren't very many in-game graphics settings. Even with my GTX 980Ti, it's the same—sometimes framerates suddenly drop (both High and Ultra settings are the same). When waiting in multiplayer, having too many players on screen does indeed make the framerate unstable, hovering around 50 to 60 FPS. Also, the green enemy blood effect makes me feel really uncomfortable; I wish I could change it or turn it off. I still really like the game, it's just that the optimization is indeed not very friendly. If the game could run stably, capturing the footage for my stream would be even better. The replayability is actually pretty decent. If you and your squad don't have a strong advantage, you can adopt a "don't fight unless you have to" tactic (thirty minutes of waiting, thirty seconds of combat). If you're forced to take them on head-on, I suggest making good use of nearby cover. In most cases, if a squad without good gear manages to wipe another squad and take their gear, their advantage becomes massive. Also, newbies shouldn't rush to drive the first vehicle they see on the map; most of the time, someone is probably camping nearby, and that applies to airdrops too.

translation_en: First of all, I want to address those reading this to decide whether to buy the game. If you have a group of friends to play with, it's absolute bliss (you can sometimes make friends on various streamers' discord servers). However, for those who say, "Bro, I roll solo, I'll still play," it might get boring because the game automatically pairs you with duos or squads, but having good English is an absolute must. Let's get to the mechanics; I'll examine the game mechanics in 2 stages: 1) Looting: The game starts by dropping and gliding from a plane, and there are a ton of locations you can go to. You open your parachute when you get close and land. There are a few spots where everyone frequently drops and good loot spawns. The first person or group to find a weapon there does some cleaning house, and the player count drops to more or less 80. From this minute on, the goal is to find good gear as fast as possible, take the right position, and be among the last players standing. There is a shrinking circle; if you stay outside of it, you take damage per second proportional to which circle it is. Things you need to acquire: --Helmet and vest (Level 1 to Level 3) --One close-range and one long-range weapon Close---} M416/Scar-L/AKM Long---} SKS/Kar98 --Med kit (first aid kit) --Ammo After finding these for good loot, we add attachments like scopes, etc. Up to this point, I liked it quite a lot. Weapons and scopes can sometimes cause issues; not every weapon spawns everywhere, or you might loot a million places and not get a solid gun, but generally, the looting system is manageable. We can get stuff from every house, etc. 2) Let the fights begin: Fighting, especially if you're playing with a team, gives you an advantage if you fight from a distance and from a place where you can take cover. Because if someone on your team is alive, you don't die instantly; you get knocked down, and your teammate can revive you within 10 seconds. Other than that, apart from headshots, there are no weapons you can get one-shotted by (dying in a single bullet), except for shotguns—which is a good thing. Other than that, we follow the classic survival game logic; you can find vehicles and use them to get to the zone. OVERALL I recommend it because I enjoy it a lot, the adrenaline is through the roof while playing. BAD SIDES *PUBG is still in Early Access, so it's full of bugs *There are optimization issues *Graphics can change gameplay; for example, while a guy might be invisible on Ultra, he might be more visible on Low *Lobbies crash frequently As a result, this game is gonna kick some serious ass when it's finished...

translation_en: [h1]PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS - a successful game.[/h1] [b] DESCRIPTION [/b] Let's start from the beginning, what does this game offer us? PUBG is a game that's only been out for a couple of months, so you have to expect bugs (early access), poor optimization and MASSIVE REPLAYABILITY. How's that? A game that's a couple of months old is beating H1Z1, which has been out way longer than PUBG, how did that happen? Well, if you're wondering whether to buy the cheaper H1Z1 or the more expensive PUBG, I'd choose the latter. You can get H1Z1 for half the price of PUBG, so why are more people playing PUBG? PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS (CAPS OFF!@~!) is a typical battle royale where our task is to "survive" and get 1st place, which rarely happens, but whatever. The game is focused on solo as well as duo/squad play (squads up to 4 people), where tactics matter, not just stupidly spamming LMB like in H1Z1. The game offers us both 1st and 3rd person perspective, most of the time you use 3rd person anyway -> you see more. Want to play H1Z1? Here's what it will offer you: jumping like a maniac, jumping out of moving vehicles like a wizard, getting disconnected from the game as cool as Obelix falling into the cauldron, very few weapons like Mario, and the devs giving the finger to the players aka crates, no way to earn any currency while playing (not counting betting which is pathetic in my opinion), oh and if you run into some guy who stored all the helmets in his inventory, you've got a problem. Alright, time for pros, cons and my opinion about this game. [b] PROS [/b] +++++ In duo/squad mode there is a knockdown mechanic (you don't kill right away, you just knock them down) and you have to FINISH THEM OFF, if you fail, their teammate can pick them up :) ++++ Trying to get out of a vehicle while it's moving drains HP (In H1Z1 you're a wizard) +++ Ability to choose where you want to jump down on the map (jumping from a plane flying over the map) +++ Huge variety of weapons +++ Weapon attachments (scopes, magazines, grips and others) +++ NO WAY TO PUT VESTS, HELMETS, OR WEAPONS INTO YOUR INVENTORY ++ Levels (1,2,3) of vests, helmets and backpacks (You don't upgrade them, you just find them, higher level = more durability, backpack = more capacity) ++ Diverse airdrops ++ Bombardments (red zone) (though they could make bombardments happen only within the zone instead of randomly) ++ Variety of vehicles (Hey John, did you see the motorcycle in H1Z1? Heck, even a German 3-seater motorcycle, go play PUBG :)) ++ Earning coins for kills and reaching a certain placement (You use them to open crates that drop character outfits) YES, FOR FREE + The smaller the zone, the more HP the barrier drains + We slow down when jumping (better physics than in H1Z1) + Grenades, including smoke bombs + No bandages at the start + More healing items (Bandages, first aid kits, med kits, energy drinks) + Frequent UPDATES (Since game launch, the best new additions are motorcycles and new weapons) + Huge player base [b] CONS [/b] -- Poor optimization (The game is young, let's give it time) On i5-4460 and R9 390 on very low 50-60 fps (max 60 fps capped) ps. it's best to play on very low (you can see more) -- More and more cheaters (1.11.8) -- More and more bugs (1.11.18) - Physics act weird sometimes - Once I got bugged inside a wall after getting out of a vehicle - Once I got my motorcycle stuck in map textures [b] MY OPINION [/b] In my opinion, the game is better than its competitor with a brighter future. The devs take care of the game, weekly updates and monthly ones (bigger changes) are being released, which is also a plus. If you like battle royale, this game is for you, I guarantee you'll get hooked. The game is worth its price. Best regards, ???trem0

translation_en: COMPREHENSIVE PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS REVIEW! Review update date: November 22, 2018 "" JUNE 27 | JULY 4 - 13 - 26 UPDATES "" (I WRITE AS UPDATES DROP) With this update, 2 new weather conditions (Sunset and Clear Sky) were added and optimization issues were pretty much sorted out. My friends who were getting 32 FPS told me they are now getting a stable 60 FPS. This update—which is 5 GB (June 27) + 1.7 GB (July 4) + 440 MB (July 26)—didn't just bring those; now you can even attach scopes like Red Dot to Pistols and 2 new weapons were added. Item drop rates were balanced. The Southeast Asia server was added and bugs in the game menu were fixed. Also, the inventory issue for players playing in 4:3 was fixed. Interface and General improvements were made. Plus, you can now always see your teammates in color. You will no longer need to press the F key to get through doors destroyed by grenades or the Red Zone. You will now be able to use healing items when you open your inventory while reloading your weapon. I'm talking about PUBG—short for PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds, a survival game made by Bluehole and Nfinity Games—which made $12 million in 3 days and sold 1 Million copies 2 weeks after its release. DayZ has been in our lives for so long that everyone is kinda done with it, and since the developers have been pushing updates at a turtle's speed even though the game came out in 2013, nobody is playing it or can stand it anymore. Then DayBreak rolled up their sleeves and released H1Z1. Seeing that H1Z1 was catching on, they split it into 2 separate modes: King Of the Kill and Just Survive, and those who bought them beforehand didn't have to pay extra. But let's be real, we cursed Daybreak plenty of times because of the bugs in H1Z1 KOTK, we all know this. Actually, the game turned out to be like Miscreated in terms of realism and H1Z1 style, throw in a bit of ARMA 3 controls and boom. There you have PUBG :) When we enter the game, just like in other games, we create our character, select our server and enter the match, then it drops you and all the other players in the corner of an 8x8km World where you can wander around aimlessly and find weapons to practice your aim until the match starts. Once the required number of players is reached (which usually takes like 30 seconds), you find yourself inside a C-130 Airplane with other players, you pick the spot you want to drop and start gliding in the open air, and the moment you land, naturally, since you have no gear other than your Fists, the weapon hunt and game of tag begins. If you don't get randomly offed in the first 1 Minute, it means you've survived the initial chaos :D As the game goes on, a circle called the Circle constantly shrinks and kills anyone outside of it, so you'll either need to find a car or a long marathon awaits you to get to the safe zone. The only thing you need to pay attention to isn't just the Circle; while looting outside in randomly spawning Bombing Zones or driving through them, it's highly likely you'll suddenly take a bomb to the head, so if you're inside a bombardment zone, definitely find somewhere to take cover. Since PUBG progresses extremely fast, it's a game that will punish you the moment you stare blankly around. Guys camping in houses and rocks while running from the Circle can sometimes be annoying. Don't neglect to watch your surroundings. After all, this is a 100-player battle, you never know what's gonna pop out and where. One aspect that makes the game different from others, in my opinion, is the Knock mechanic. If a guy has 100 health, he doesn't die instantly; first he gets knocked down, if he has a teammate nearby he goes towards him to pick him up or waits for him to come after getting to a safe place. After a 9-second revive process, you become mobile again with 10% health and the firefight continues. BAM BAM BAM Useful info: If you're playing as a squad and 3 out of 4 guys on the opposing team are knocked down, if you knock the 4th player too, logically since there's no teammate left to revive the other 3 fallen players, all of them instantly die. If you died, depending on the guy you killed or your team, you can return to the Lobby with a certain amount of in-game cash and enter a new match. If you entered in Squad or Duo, you can spectate your other friend. If you won, you'll obviously get your cash and return to the lobby :) Now let's get to the good and bad parts (The bad parts are steadily decreasing with weekly updates.) [h1](+) PROS[/h1] [list] [*]The game can be played in 3 ways as Solo, Squad or Duo. Squad consists of Max 4 people and if you enter with 3 people, whether another guy joins or not is up to you. This is actually a good option to prevent trolls, because you queue as a 3-man pre-made and the other guy just wanders around doing nothing, better off queuing as just 3. [*]We have customization options like Rifle - Pistol - SMG. From silencers, scopes, extended mags to grips needed to improve recoil control. There's even a FlashHider to hide the muzzle flash when the weapon fires. Scope varieties are also in a pretty good state, separated into Holo - Red Dot - 2X Magnified - 4X Magnified ACOG - 8X Magnified CQBBS - 15X PM II scopes. Higher magnification scopes can be used for snipers. [*]There is a hot combat feel, meaning you aren't just sitting around doing nothing. [*]Vehicles are at a sufficient level, there are plenty of vehicles ranging from motorcycles to boats. [*]The game is realistic and honestly a lot of fun, it really makes you want to play despite its cons. [*]You can drive the TOROS in the game, our grandpas' car, and hilarious dialogues happen regarding that car: [*]It has TURKISH Language support! [/list] [h1](-) CONS[/h1] [list] [*]When we first enter the game, it lags a lot. (I'm saying this keeping in mind that I have a high-end system) [*]There are a lot of complaints that the game lags while parachuting down (Rumor has it that opening the inventory fixes it) [*]While all players suddenly jump from the parachute and rush to loot, there's a weapon-grabbing chaos where you try to enter a house and open the door, but the door won't open. Yep, I'm talking about LAG! There are 10-15 second lags at the very beginning, but if you don't die during that process, you're fine. [*]Don't be surprised if a car flies right over your head while you're running down the road. Even while driving on a flat road, it has happened to me many times that I suddenly flew up into the sky, took a short-range tour, and then fell back down and exploded along with the car. The physics engine needs improvement. [*]If you played H1Z1 and started playing this game, DO NOT GET OUT OF THE CAR BEFORE IT STOPS! take it from me, otherwise you'll find yourself on the ground on your knees. [*]Even though we open crates with the money we get at the end of the game, new crates need to come out; the content seems okay for now, but after a while, it gets boring. Constantly opening the same crate with 30K cash feels pointless to people :( [*]There's an issue with hitboxes, but I think it's getting fixed, sometimes the bullets we fire don't register on the guy, etc. [/list] Even though this game might intimidate you with its high price tag and so many flaws, it's a game you can have a insane amount of fun with. Moreover, considering how fast the updates roll out, we can foresee that all those shortcomings I listed here will be resolved in a short time. translation_en: Best game to come out of Korea in years. The best game of 2017. I've been playing PUBG since the beta, and I've played H1Z1, DayZ, and RUST. Among them all, if we're talking highest quality, PUBG is easily sitting at the top right now. This game is a 100-player survival game where you kill or be killed on a Russia-themed island. When you load in, you wait on a remote island, hop on a plane, drop wherever you want, and beat the living crap out of each other until only 1 person is left standing—the classic "Battle Royale" style. Also, to stop "campers" from just sitting there waiting for people to come to them, there's a shrinking play zone that drains your health and forces the map to get smaller. It’s got a ton of strengths: customization using various gun attachments like flash hiders, suppressors, and optics; a game system that doesn't require pay-to-win microtransactions; and fast patches. Unlike DayZ, you don't need to spend ages looting, and the gun balance is so well done that people don't just use one specific weapon like in H1Z1. Now let's look at the cons. The downsides are optimization and server issues. These problems have been around since the beta. When you try to pick up an item, your character hesitates for 3 seconds like they're having an existential crisis before finally grabbing it. Depending on the server status, you'll rubberband 1 to 2 seconds back in position, which can actually decide whether you win or lose. Also, the physics engine is weird as fuck—if a car gets stuck, it starts breakdancing and then flies straight up into the sky. Let's talk about graphics. If you drop the foliage setting to very low, bushes just stop rendering, so there's literally no reason to turn the graphics up. Also, optimization is so scuffed that unless you have a high-end PC, you have to play with low-quality textures. Since it's an Early Access game, there's room for improvement, but looking at DayZ Standalone which stayed in Early Access for years, Early Access isn't a free pass for being broken. The choice is entirely up to the buyer. But from my experience playing since the beta 3 months ago, it's still better than other survival games that fail to fix random bullsh*t deaths and become literally unplayable during peak hours. Also, it's improved a lot—frames are good now, and even during peak hours, the servers run smoothly. If there are any of you who still haven't bought it, I'm totally down to recommend it.

translation_en: I was thinking about buying Playerunknown's Battlegrounds for a long time. At the very beginning, I noticed more and more streamers starting to play it. All in all, that's normal - a game comes out, they promote it and then everyone forgets about it anyway. Standard. In this case, we're dealing with an Early Access version, meaning a game that is still being polished. [i]To this day I kick myself for letting someone talk me into buying DayZ back then, because since 2013 the game has still been in beta.[/i] But getting back to the point, I took a risk. I thought - cool, I'll buy it and see what happens. [b]At worst, a refund[/b]. I watched a bunch of videos, read reviews, and followed a few streams. [b]It looked pretty good[/b]. I'll add here that I was getting it mostly for [b]SOLO[/b]. Because my friends were either not interested or already had people for Duo/Squad. The game offers three matchmaking modes: SOLO / DUO / SQUAD. The first mode is standard - you queue solo and play against people without teams. Just like you. The second mode is similar to other games - you queue with a buddy and play against other players in duo. The third mode is like team vs team - you queue with 4 people and play against teams made up of the same amount. It's worth mentioning here that if you don't have anyone to play with, there's a "matchmaking" option. Meaning it will pair you with randoms for your team, whether in duo or squad. The game has a voice chat that is activated with the [T] button, but you need to set in the options whether you want everyone to hear you or just your team. Because sometimes this can lead to a quick death. As for optimization, it's pretty so-so. It's not like it's tragic, but you can forget about playing on Ultra. The commonly used trick here is to set everything to Very Low + Textures High/Ultra + View Distance to Ultra. Thanks to this, it'll be easier to spot the enemy, and the game will gain those few fps. And now the most important thing, the game is in Early Access so you should expect: - random fps drops - crashes to desktop - memory leaks - display driver crashes - freezes upon entering the lobby I'm not scaring you by any means, just giving a heads-up. Because on the forum there are sometimes several topics about why the game runs this way or that. Because it's in Early Access. All the problems I described above may or may not occur in your case. However, it's worth keeping in mind rather than crying later that the game crashed or I suddenly have frame drops. Summing up... The game is worth buying, whether solo or in a team. It will provide hours of good fun that you often want to return to. Despite the issues, it's a well-optimized EA that will run even on a potato.

translation_en: For an Early Access it honestly wipes the floor with H1Z1 without a doubt. Naturally they need to improve many aspects, for example: 1) THE OPTIMIZATION. I have a GTX 1080 (and a really good PC) and I suffer some FPS drops throughout the matches, though of course it's not something that prevents me from playing the game well, but if with a beast of a graphics card I get drops I don't want to imagine for those who have a worse card (or a computer that isn't all that good). 2) THE LAG. This is indeed an important point, although recently I've been playing smooth matches in this regard that doesn't mean there is no lag, and many, MANY times it's extremely annoying lag that is a royal pain in the ass during matches, something that for example H1Z1 doesn't suffer from, matches are always smooth (or at least in my case they are). It's lag that screws you over from the moment you parachute down, when you open doors, when you want to pick up stuff, when you shoot, when you get into vehicles, etc, etc, etc. I think this would be the important point the developers need to focus on. 3) THE GAMEPLAY (Well, some things). All in all the gameplay is very really good, but there are things that make you say "come on, seriously?", for example: When you parachute down and you're almost touching the ground you go from 20-25 Km/h to 0-1 Km/h, YOU FALL SUPER HYPER SLOW and you waste time for nothing (They could at least add the option to cut the parachute). They could also let you perform actions while inside vehicles, I don't see the logic in why if you're in a car as a passenger you can't use a fucking med kit. Another thing is that the character is extremely clunky when you need to vault certain walls, rocks, etc. you get stuck on any stupid thing, and on top of that it takes ages to sprint and without that insignificant speed boost you don't stand a chance of jumping over tons of things (that is a supreme pain in the ass). 4) A MAP THAT'S TOO BIG FOR TOO FEW PEOPLE. I don't know if later on the game will allow matches with more than 100 people, it would be cool since many times you get fucking bored, you spend 15 minutes running just to die. It would be cool to have a bit more action, even like 200 people and have the plane take a wider route. Beyond the previous points, the game is excellent and is on a good path. You shouldn't cry about an Early Access when it has problems, it's obvious that these kinds of games come out with a thousand bugs at first, but it's more than certain that it's going to end up being the best Battle Royale by far. (See The Forest as a game that in Early Access was absolute garbage and now it's an amazing game). To wrap it up, if you played H1Z1 (or ARMA 3) and liked it, you're going to love this one. You need to give it a little time to get the hang of it and properly understand the mechanics, afterwards you get addicted. That said, if you have a shitty computer I don't recommend it, not for now. You'll have to wait for a couple more patches (They pushed one out with optimization but it still runs kinda so-so), unless you want to spend money and look at it lovingly in your library without being able to play it xD I'll comment soon if patches come out. Kisses on your little buttocks.

translation_en: [Game Overview] It's a game where about 100 people drop onto a deserted island and kill each other. There's no such thing as respawning. Once you die, you just get sent back to the lobby. In a situation like that, you keep fighting until you're the last person or team standing. Because of this, it has a unique kind of tension you can only really get by playing it. [Review by a beginner playing an FPS/TPS for the very first time] [Scroll down further for my review after playing 400 hours] As expected, I just can't win at all. Absolutely cannot win. I get excited if I can even manage one kill in a match. My aim is all over the place, and my bullets hardly ever hit. So whenever I run into an enemy, I get ruthlessly slaughtered without mercy. When I get killed, I naturally lose all my gear and have no choice but to queue up for the next match, which is SO frustrating. However, it's not frustrating in a painful way. For some reason, it's fun. Oh, it's not like I'm a masochist or anything. It's just that in this game, fighting and cooperating with teammates isn't the only source of fun. Your heart rate spikes, you can actually hear your own heartbeat, and you push hard for the win. I recommend this to anyone who wants to experience that kind of thrill. Of course, the joy of getting a chicken dinner (winning) is head and shoulders above any other game. There are all kinds of fun things about it that you can't put into words, so you should definitely give it a try. Just keep in mind that it requires a fairly decent PC setup. [6/1] [[After that, I played for 400 hours.]] It's been over half a year since I started playing, and chicken dinners have become pretty easy to grab. My K/D has definitely gone up, and I think I've finally shaken off beginner status. The old map is more popular, but a new map has been released, and it looks like large-scale pro leagues are starting up now too. Seriously, a game with an active dev team and community is a great thing. However, those hackers (cheaters) I heard rumors about right when I started seem to be on the rise lately, and things are so tense that some people in the community have somehow started taunting regular players. Still, it's a fact that cheaters are around, so if you're just starting out now, you might want to keep your expectations in check and dive in with a mindset like, "I guess I'll check out this trendy game." (Actually, most of them are in the high-tier brackets, so it doesn't really affect beginners or bad players all that much.) I've had this much fun, so I definitely think it was worth 3,300 yen. [1/28, Personal opinion]

translation_en: First of all, I want to address those reading this to decide whether to get the game. If you have a group of friends to play with, it's fucking amazing (you can sometimes make friends on various streamers' Discord servers). However, for those who say, "Bro, I play solo, I'll manage," it might get boring because the game automatically matches you with duos or squads, but having good English is an absolute must. Let's talk about the mechanics. I'll examine the game mechanics in 2 stages: 1) Looting: The game starts with you gliding down from an airplane, and there are tons of locations you can go to. When you get close, your parachute opens and you land. There are a few hot spots where everyone drops and good loot spawns; the first person or group to find a gun there goes on a cleanup, and the player count drops to around 80 or so. From this point on, the goal is to find good gear as quickly as possible, take up the right positions, and make it to the end. There's a circle that shrinks frequently; if you stay outside of it, you take damage per second proportional to which circle it is. Things you need to acquire: --Helmet and vest (Level 1 to Level 3) --One close-range and one long-range weapon Close---} M416 / Scar-L / AKM Long---} SKS / Kar98 --Med kits / First aid --Ammo After finding these for a good loot run, we add attachments like scopes and whatnot. Up to this point, I like it a lot. Weapons and scopes can sometimes be an issue; sometimes certain weapons don't spawn anywhere, or you can loot a million places and still not get a solid gun, but generally, the loot system is manageable, and you can find stuff in every house, etc. 2) Let the fights begin: Especially if you're playing with a team, fighting from a distance and from a place where you have cover gives you an advantage because if someone on your team is alive, you don't die instantly—you get knocked, and your teammate can pick you up within 10 seconds. Other than headshots, there are no guns that can one-shot you (except for shotguns, that is a good thing). Other than that, we follow standard survival game logic; you can find vehicles and use them to drive into the zone. OVERALL: I recommend it because I really enjoy it; the adrenaline is through the roof while playing. CONS: * PUBG is still in Early Access and full of bugs * Optimization issues * Graphics can change gameplay—for example, a guy might be invisible on Ultra while being much more visible on Low * Lobbies crash frequently As a result, this game is gonna kick some serious ass when it's finished...

translation_en: PUBG is a super addictive BR game: At the slightest sound (even in your own house) your adrenaline starts pumping! The map is huge and (for me) really well made (in terms of buildings, scenery in general). Matches all start the same way: You're in a transport plane and you choose when you want to eject to go to whatever area you want. The cool thing is that the plane doesn't take the same path every time, it flies in a straight line from one side of the map to the other, different for every match! Once on the ground, you have to loot what you can and fight the other players (especially in the towns, hostilities kick off really fast right from the start!). Over time the play area shrinks (thanks to a zone system), forcing players to move (and exposing them). And this goes on until the end of the match when there's 1 player or 1 team left depending on the game mode! For me it's a great game!, addictive, stressful and at the same time not too much of a "bastard" (in the sense that at the start of the game, everyone has the same chance of winning). I'm really glad I bought it and I strongly recommend it! On the other hand, there is a BIG downside! : As you might have read in other reviews, optimization isn't great for now, so to play I'm forced to turn the graphics way down. Except at one point, a prone player looked like a half-rendered bush because of the game (except when the bush shoots at you and moves, you figure it out pretty fast. During the shooting, the other player becomes "normal", meaning body and head). So if your PC isn't very recent or very powerful, be careful before buying it. Right now on Steam they recommend a GTX 660 as a graphics card, but for now I'd recommend at least a GTX 960 minimum (so you don't feel like you're playing a retro game). If this review was helpful, a little thumbs-up button is available right below :) EDIT : Still plenty of players and updates, active development (Just as well honestly! :) ) Over 130 hours and I'm far from getting bored of it! Playing with friends adds endless replay value and loads of good moments! (and major rage moments like: "Aaargh, what the f***, I had so much gear!!!"). But given how fast you jump back into a match, the little moments where you're disappointed fade away very quickly for the action to come! Anyway, uh, what are you waiting for to buy it? It's not going Free To Play anytime soon you know^^ :) See you in-game !

translation_en: Pro & Contra + Comparison to H1Z1/Conclusion + Update Settings -----------------------------------[b]Pro & Contra[/b]--------------------------------------------- + visually it definitely makes a better impression than similar games + tactical gameplay is totally possible + versatile gear (different weapon mods, 3-tier helmets/vests/backpacks) + multiple ways to get around (on foot, car (5 seats*), motorcycle (3 or 2 seats), strand buggy (2 seats)) + damage from vehicle accidents + no excessive healing possible, since there isn't too much handed out + circle gets smaller irregularly and is unpredictable + multiple paths lead to 1st place (rambo gunfights, circle runners and camping with a little umbrella in your drink ;)) + throw trajectory indicator for your own grenades + effect of the weapon in hand on running speed + currently CLOTHES are free / no in-game purchases with real money + huge map + compass lets you know exactly where you are / your mates / precise callouts of "enemy movements" possible + playable solo, duo or squads (you can still play 3 vs 4 for example, with or without randoms) - vehicle handling is clunky (currently the Dacia feels like a bus) - the 100x mentioned lags (yeah yeah I know, early access) - the player model is personally too close to the screen (fov) - movements, especially when prone, are very wooden - you can't manage to jump over the tiniest walls ------------------------------------[b]Comparisons[/b]----------------------------------------------- Comparisons to H1Z1 are a bit far-fetched. Only three facts connect both games. You get dropped out of an airplane (1) you have to gear up (2) and whoever is left standing at the end wins (3). The rest differs, though. For one, in H1Z1 you get your gear thrown at you right away and for another, that game is all about speed. A fundamental difference starts right at this point. BG forces its players to move from house to house due to less equipment. To gear up and relies more on lots of small fights. So the offensive hunting like in H1Z1 is often missing. Also the map in BG is bigger and the players are more scattered. Which favors the many small fights. H1Z1 has the smaller map and pushes players together faster. Even though H1Z1 offers quite a bit more healing (amount), the fights in BG often feel much longer-lasting. Sure, in both games you can hand out souvenirs with shotguns and beat defenseless victims to a pulp with blunt objects with growing enthusiasm, but only BG has the universal frying pan. People often complain about the lags, but I'd like to remind everyone of the beginnings of H1Z1. After all, that game has a head start of over 2 years when it comes to bug fixes and changes. So I think if you're going to make a comparison, you should also look at the launch of H1Z1 and not years of work. If you ask players who have been playing H1Z1 for a long time, you'll also hear that the bug fixes for the lags happened at most half a year ago. Generally, I also think it's pretty retarded to want to compare games with completely different graphics in terms of performance. A glimpse of how I play H1Z1: I gear up at some random spot (I have little clue about the map, which isn't necessary either, since everything lies around everywhere). Afterwards I run as a gas runner nicely along the edge and pick flowers. Usually don't see a damn soul. Eventually someone comes speeding by in their car (not too many players left alive), jumps out of it while moving at full speed and Captn Noob is down. The whole fun takes about 10 minutes. The whole thing again for BG: You generally loot continuously until the late game, since you simply always lack heals somehow as long as you haven't had any enemy contact yet, or precisely because you already had enemies right in front of you. Houses are checked and taken, and you slowly move towards the safe zone. I am much more on guard, since the ranges are much further due to the mods. Usually I also make it to the late game here with the more tactical playstyle. But I'm constantly busy re-equipping and on guard. And happily for 30 minutes + ------------------------------------[b]Conclusion[/b]----------------------------------------------- In short, one could say that H1Z1 is faster and more about pure warfare. BG on the other hand brings more fun to tactical players. So it's not about which game is "better" at all, but rather which playstyle you personally prefer. ------------------------------------[b]Settings[/b]----------------------------------------------- Personally, I play with the following launch options since I had lags when shooting at first: -USEALLAVAILABLECORES -malloc=system -sm4 In-game settings can be set as low as possible. Same for view distance. Currently that doesn't seem to have any effect, except that the game runs smoother. I kept model design on medium, otherwise it looks horrific to me. But that's a matter of taste. It's also important to just clear the temp folder once. (Press Windows key + R, click "Appdata" there, go further to Local, further into Temp and generously empty the folder) For all non-SSD users, the program [url=https://www2.razerzone.com/de-de/cortex]Razer Cortex[/url] can also help. (free) The program [url=https://bitsum.com/parkcontrol/]Parkcontrol[/url] (free) gives you the ability to access your cores and also utilize them 100%. For example, I have 8 cores and on my PC 2 cores were parked at 5%. In other words: out of 8 cores, only 6 were running for me and 2 were painting their nails. It still doesn't always run lag-free for me, but the difference, especially during gunfights, is like night and day. *Source: LeutnantKibaGER

translation_en: 10.05.2017 I really like the game! Pros: +++ Every match is different: you land somewhere else, loot different items, a lot of like randomness... bad or good luck with items. ;) +++ Playing with a friend/friends is even more fun, interesting or hilarious. :P ++ Great gunplay, I feel like I'm holding a weapon that poses a threat, not some toy. ++ Weapon attachments that make the guns even better and cooler. ++ Tactical and more realistic gameplay, you gotta use your brain, not just rush in or go for kills only - (H1Z1) ++ Good sound design, e.g., footsteps (though a bit too quiet for me... probably depends on the headset), or when someone is crouching, reloading, etc. + Clothes, just a cool little extra, but nice to have, well-made, hoping for more :) + Huge satisfaction when you reach a high placement, or when you take down an enemy one way or another. Or when you and your friend pull off a nice bit of teamwork or coordination. ;) Cons: --- Optimization: i5 7500, 8gb RAM 2400Hz, XFX RX 480 8gb - the game runs at 50-60 fps on high settings, I play on medium-high and get 60-80 fps, but the game still feels clunky, random-ass fps drops, lag, some minor teleports, texture flickering, weird lighting sometimes, using a scope also causes fps to drop, or when the red zone is active, or when there are a lot of players nearby (excluding the lobby) you have to click a dozen times just to open a door or loot something... the devs have a lot of work ahead of them. But I believe it'll only get better ;) updates fix things often. I don't know if it's the same issue, but sometimes the screen goes black and comes back after 1-2 seconds or resets the game/PC. -- Camera mode, it's cool that there's both FPP and TPP, but in my opinion it would play much better as FPP-only, because TPP gives you a huge advantage when it comes to exploration, being able to observe surroundings without even exposing yourself... I play both modes, but TPP is unfair sometimes (I had a situation where a guy was lying behind a counter, and even with TPP I couldn't see him, yet he could watch me). I hope that when queuing for a match there will be an option to choose (FPP, TPP, or both). -- I also hate the free-look with ALT, I'm running and I can just look straight behind my back? Pretty stupid in my opinion. I'd understand if the free-look was limited (like our actual head movement in real life), but oh well... - Few weapons and attachments, it would be cool to see new ones in the future. - Sound, I said it was good, but a few things are annoying, like when we're in the plane, rain, or parachuting - they are super loud, and turning down the volume makes footsteps harder to hear... but I think that's more of a hardware issue than the game itself, though I feel like it could be somehow improved. Meh, feels like a 50/50. Neutrals: ¤ Nice graphics, but because of the game engine, textures load weirdly in my opinion, they take time to reload like when you land with a parachute, and a bit further on the horizon trees and grass look poor, sort of blurry... hard to put into words... ¤ Big map, vehicles - but it would be cool to have more islands like that to make truly diverse locations, more weather conditions or snow, dynamic weather during the match, a day-night cycle or playing once at night and once during the day... you know what I mean :) ¤ I don't get how it happens that an enemy eats a whole rifle mag and nothing happens, while I lose all my health or die from a single shot of a crappy pistol..... I understand helmets, body armor, I don't know... maybe distance, accuracy, where the bullet hits, whether it's the head, leg, or chest etc. (if that's even a thing), but sometimes it's really over the top. ¤ Melee combat is completely garbage xD, but you don't really use it anyway. ¤ This was supposed to be a con, but because it happens very rarely, I put it in neutrals: I'm talking about door destruction. I had a case where the doors were destroyed, only the hinges remained, but I couldn't walk through them, they became invisible walls. Same when shooting through them, it's a total lottery, either you kill or you get killed through them, doesn't matter if you shoot into open space (where the door was destroyed) or at the remaining parts of the door... But like I said, I'm very rarely in that situation. ¤/- Poor character customization, really poor... I think the game is worth the price, especially if it keeps getting updated, polished, and improved. No need to be afraid of playing solo, because playing alone is super fun too. A game is a game, sometimes it pisses you off, slightly or majorly, but that's how it is everywhere. The game is addictive, does it get boring? Well, I'd say not really, though I think it could sometimes be more interesting just by adding more weapons, locations, a night mode, etc. I recommend the game, encourage you to give it a try :) My rating: 8/10 6.10.2017 The game is still fun! Even with low hours played. Performance on my rig has improved, new weapons, cool plans for the future (new map, weather). Overall, still recommend!

translation_en: A while ago, that video of "foreigners and Chinese people screaming at each other in H1Z1" went totally viral on Weibo, and out of nowhere, *H1Z1: King of the Kill* was on most people's radar. It let more people know that a game where you shit-talk and tear into foreigners even existed, and some people even jumped into Steam specifically just to play this game. *Battle Royale* is a horror novel written by Japanese novelist Koushun Takami, which tells the story of an entire class of students forced into a death game. The rules are simple: participate in a mutual slaughter until only one person survives. The theme was later adapted into both films and games. In the early days of its adaptation into a game, the "Battle Royale" mode was an Arma 2 mod created by the fan "PLAYERUNKNOWN (Brendan Greene)." As the game continued to evolve, this mod also carried over into Arma 3. Then came the widely known H1Z1. To develop a true battle royale game, the mod creator is currently at Bluehole developing *PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS*. Today, I'm bringing you a review of this game. [h1]A Dark Horse in the Battle Royale Genre[/h1] Why do I call *PUBG* a dark horse in the battle royale genre? I think its current player counts and sales figures already speak for themselves. More than a year after its release, *H1Z1: King of the Kill* had sold around 5 million copies globally. Meanwhile, *PUBG* hit a staggering 2 million copies sold in just one month after release—and this is with *PUBG* priced 30% higher than *H1Z1*! Aside from sales, the concurrent player counts for these two games are also neck and neck. Given these numbers, *PUBG* must have some exceptional qualities to win over so many players. So next, let's take a look at the game's quality. [h1]Retention of the Core Mode[/h1] As a game personally spearheaded by the founder of the battle royale mode, *PUBG* retains the most fundamental rules of the game. 100 players will participate in a match together, air-dropping onto a massive island to start killing each other. In each match, the plane flies across the island on a random flight path, and players can choose which area they want to drop into. This setup is genuinely eye-catching, but it has both pros and cons. On the one hand, players now have control over their own "destiny" instead of spawning randomly somewhere on the map. On the other hand, because landing areas tend to be clustered, competition between players right at the start of the game becomes insanely fierce. When I first started playing, for example, I'd often land with three or four people right around me, and I usually wouldn't last five minutes. As time passes in-game, the safe zone on the island gradually shrinks, and players have to push toward the safe zone to survive. Because the in-game map is enormous, if you're unlucky and the safe zone spawns far away from you, you'd better find a car ASAP. Otherwise, the late-game circle shrinks so fast that running on foot just won't cut it. [h1]Abundant Weapons and Modification System[/h1] If you ask me, the biggest feature of this game is the huge variety of weapons available for players to use. Weapon types are mainly divided into shotguns, assault rifles, submachine guns, sniper rifles, machine guns, pistols, crossbows, and melee weapons. Just in the official recent update, the "Vector" submachine gun was added to the game, and I'm sure the pool of usable weapons will only grow over time. The diverse weapon choices make the game much more replayable. Besides the rich selection of available weapons, the game also lets you mod your firearms. While scavenging for "loot," players can find various attachments, and equipping them boosts weapon performance. Take weapon scopes, for example: there are red dots, holographics, 2x scopes, 4x scopes, 8x scopes, and 15x scopes—though those last two are extremely rare in-game. Because there are so many optional attachments for every slot on a weapon, it might take a long time of searching just to get the setup you actually want. [h1]Built on Unreal Engine 4, Optimization Draws Flak from Players[/h1] The game is built using the Unreal Engine 4, which seems to have become standard for new games these days. But the optimization issues that came with it have drawn widespread flak from players, with most people unable to keep the game running at a stable 60 FPS. When the game first launched, my rig (6700K + 1070) only managed around 40-something frames indoors on high settings. But I gotta hand it to the developers—after a few updates, the game's optimization has improved massively. With the exact same graphic settings, my 1070 now keeps the game well above 80 FPS. So whenever I post *PUBG* news and see players in the comments whining about optimization: if your rig hits the official recommended specs, this game will definitely run, and 8G of RAM is pretty much a must. Putting optimization aside, the graphics under Unreal Engine 4 are still gorgeous. The overall art style leans more toward realistic, with detailed and bright visuals. The developers also did a fantastic job with the firearm models; you can tell a lot of effort went into them just by looking at the scopes players interact with the most. The game's lighting effects and building details are also pretty much flawless. Strip away the in-game UI, and the surrounding environment reaches photorealistic quality. Aside from sunny days, there are also rainy days, and the feeling of raindrops splashing against the screen glass is especially awesome. At the same time, the sound of the rain drowns out nearby enemy footsteps, forcing players to be way more alert while looting. That little detail is pretty neat. The chilly, overcast weather on rainy days instantly sets a grim tone for the cruelty of the battle royale. [h1]A More Hardcore Battle Royale Mode[/h1] Unlike H1Z1's instant gratification of running into people and starting a bloodbath, *PUBG*'s game pacing is slower, more tactical, and emphasizes squad coordination. The overall gunplay feels great, especially the shooting mechanics—players no longer feel shackled by H1Z1's clunky shooting system. Of course, you can also queue solo, though it's a bit less fun compared to rolling with friends. The in-game map lets you see the exact locations of yourself and your teammates, saving you from constantly double-checking your position while running from the blue zone. In the final phases of the game, because the play area gets so tiny, make sure you're safe and don't make any reckless moves. Patiently wait for someone else to fuck up, and then strike. Media outlets recently exposed two brand-new maps the developers are working on, and I think dropping new maps like this is a smart move to constantly feed players fresh experiences and keep the game alive. My first "Winner Winner, Chicken Dinner" was won playing with friends. People who haven't played the game always ask what "chi ji" (eating chicken) means, so let me explain it here. It's a translation of the English idiom "Winner winner, chicken dinner!" which dates back to 1970s casinos—if someone won, the dealer would shout this phrase out. Basically, it means you've won so you can afford chicken for dinner tonight; it's a celebratory saying. The official localization affectionately translated it as "Chi Ji" (Eating Chicken). [h1]Conclusion: A Battle Royale Game Marching Toward Perfection[/h1] I call *PUBG* a battle royale game marching toward perfection because, as of right now, the game certainly still has a few minor flaws. But for a game that's only been out in Early Access for two months, its current performance is completely stunning! The speed at which the developers are currently updating the game also shows how much they value this project. To borrow a quote from the official tagline: "NOT JUST A GAME, THIS IS BATTLE ROYALE." It looks like the devs want to make this game the gold standard of the battle royale genre, so let's all keep our expectations high for this one. translation_en: PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS, more commonly known as PUBG, is a Battle Royale game that involves dropping a certain number of players (100 max) all over an island with the goal of becoming the last survivor: you have to kill all the other players and be the last one standing! (You get dropped from a plane, and you decide where to jump). Of course the system is well thought out because throughout the game there are fewer and fewer competitors since players get killed, and since the island is too huge, the combat zone shrinks progressively (which brings the players closer together), and if you're outside the combat zone, you lose health! So you really have to keep an eye on the game map. You can play in "duo" or "squad", which means teams of 2 to 4 players with friends, so this time it's not the last survivor who wins, but the last team! You scavenge for weapons, armor, ammo, etc., which are scattered randomly around the map, so it's also about looting in addition to fighting—it's pretty dumb to rush a player with your fists if they already have firearms. There are also vehicles you can use, thankfully, as it's often happened to me that I was stuck outside the combat zone and it was located on the other side of the map! So I’d panic looking for a ride, and when I finally find one, I yell MIRACLE! And I'm pretty damn happy :P You can play in TPS or FPS view, and it's easy to switch between the two, it's totally up to you! It's pretty handy; when you want better all-around visibility (and to hide), you go to TPS view, and when you want to get a good aim on a player, you switch to FPS view. That's not a strict rule of course, you just manage it however works best for you. Regarding optimization and updates: The developers really listen to the players and they do their job; we get weekly updates that bring extra content and heavy optimization work. When I first got the game I struggled a bit to run it on my current setup, but with the latest update, the game runs way smoother, I'm super happy! Optimization is progressing pretty fast :) It's not ideal yet, but I'm optimistic for the future, I'm even convinced this game could leave early access pretty quickly if it keeps going at this pace. PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS is very promising, don't hesitate to buy it, for me it's worth the price.

translation_en: Hello everyone, I'm SF Express Courier No. 76, and this is my story — I dropped out before finishing middle school and chose to become a courier. Back when I delivered in City Y, sometimes I'd skip lunch just to wait for the recipient, sitting right outside their door. Occasionally, recipients would be home but inconveniently unable to open the door, so I had to keep waiting outside until they finished whatever they were doing before I went in. Back then we were all so innocent, everyone's face would be blushing when the door opened. Alright. I admit, my concept of love was stuck back when I delivered to a girl for the first time, delivering to that same address over and over until the very end. Until one day I dragged that man out of her bed, and she raised a shotgun, pointing the barrel at — me. I forgave her, after all, I'm just a delivery guy. That memory wasn't a pretty one. When I grew up and became independent, I realized I didn't believe in any of that bullshit love anymore. The older I got, the more I felt my first love shouldn't have been given away so casually. I am much more proud than you think. Today is Monday, I checked the logistics info like I always do. There are quite a few packages, mostly heading to City P. Don't know who pissed off the heavens, but the sky outside the window suddenly turned dark. "Clouds rise over the stream, the sun sinks behind the pavilion; mountain rain is about to come, sweeping through the tower." I casually recited a line — couldn't memorize the text in 8th grade, had to copy just this line 20 times, so it stuck. I feel like a lot of the stuff people spend half their lives learning in classrooms is pretty much useless for a lifetime. I make at least a dozen trips to City P a week, I could deliver a package blindfolded without denting it. I put on my sunglasses and threw on my raincoat. I thought, I must be happy. That sense of satisfaction city folks get when receiving a package, I could see it right in their eyes. And they all love talking to me in this weird, excited tone: "China, number one!" They said this means "Hello, thank you" in English, the universal language of the world. I never doubted it. When I got back, my boss told me I was wrong, and that even the "cao ni ma" I understood earlier didn't mean "thank you for your hard work." I smiled and told him: I'm just a courier, uncultured, severely nearsighted, clumsy, and bad with words. I get scared even a slightly delayed delivery will ruin their mood. The only thing I can do is wait by the door, hoping the recipient comes to pick it up soon..... Now I'm tired, speak a little softer.....

translation_en: Review after 120.7 hours of experience: Pros: Weapon variety: There are 22 weapons in the game. You can get 4 different weapons from drops. The strongest weapon is the Awm, which is a sniper. Also, new weapons will be added to the game with updates. (vector, groza, mk14 added) Weapon customization: Besides attaching a red dot or holo to weapons, you can also attach scopes like 4x, 8x, and 15x. The 15x only drops from crates. Apart from these, you can attach many attachments to weapons like magazines, muzzles, stocks, and recoil-reducing parts. +2x added. Spectator mode: This game offered us the ability to watch your teammate after you die right when it came out, something H1Z1 couldn't manage to do for years. Vehicles: Besides 3 types of vehicles, you can also be active on the water with a boat. In the last major update, a 3-seater motorcycle was added to the game. +A 2-seater motorcycle was added too. Cons: Optimization: The review is based on a 144hz monitor and a gtx 970 graphics card. Especially when entering Georgopol and Polyana, dropping to 30 fps drives you crazy. While generally getting 70-80 fps, in some places I even see 110-120. (fixed after update) Server problems: Although rare, server crashes and lag issues are annoying. Considering that the developer improves the game based on players' feedback and fixes issues by listening to the players, it would be safe to say that the game will be much better in the future. Even in its current state, it's a game played with a lot of enjoyment. I definitely recommend it. Review after 155 hours of experience: After the 20.04.2017 patch; The fps drop in cities has been fixed after the new patch. We can now go above 60 fps in cities where we used to get 30 fps. With the new small additions, the game has become fully playable. The fps issue is not completely fixed. You can get 30 fps in the most ridiculous place on the map. We can say this is the only con for now. Review after 246 hours of experience: We've gotten totally used to the game by now. We're at a point where we can't even see its flaws, if any. The fps issues and server crashes that used to be annoying are no longer there. Since the 2 most important problems are fixed, the rest is bullshit anyway, so we can say it's ready now. In addition, the fact that it keeps getting constantly updated and brings new content increases our confidence in the game even more.

This is my bad, not passing the buck. Also, I am not accusing "all" Chinese players. On the contrary, I believe most players won't actively start any trouble. A friend asked, "We get cursed at, and when we curse back we're the ones with bad manners? We're supposed to just take it and not fight back?" It's really not like that. As my friend @·别拉我玩游戏 said, "When someone flames you, flaming back proves nothing except your own helplessness." Since we're all playing online games, wouldn't it be best to solve it in-game? If you play better than them and crush them a few times, isn't that the most satisfying venting method? "I love watching you get so pissed off yet helpless against me" — isn't that the best solution? Of course, I totally agree with what @Let's together said: "Enjoy the game, enjoy life. Relax your mindset." GG ------------------------------------- Original Review: Aside from optimization issues, it's still a good game. What I want to talk about is the community atmosphere, which is just utterly disgusting. Call me a snowflake if you want, but some players are just an absolute embarrassment. Some random monkey yells out "TAIWAN NO.1" and it sets off a bunch of Chinese players. All kinds of Chinese profanities endless to the ear, turning on mics and blasting the national anthem only shows how unqualified certain people are as gamers, not how patriotic they are. "Fxxk your mother." "Your mother boom boom." "F*** those little Japs to death." "Korean dumbasses" ... Everybody tell me, if someone is constantly screaming profanities on public voice chat, can you keep playing this game? My mental hasn't been tempered to the point where I'm immune to all evil and unfazed by everything. Trying to get some people to calm down makes me a coward being cursed at? Is shouting slogans and acting tough against the world supposed to be brave? I really don't get it, does screaming harder mean your spit travels through the Ethernet cable to f*** the other guy to death? During the game, I heard a Japanese player say something to his friend while the Chinese players were screaming profanities that made me want to cry: "ほらね、これが中国人。笑うでしょう。" (Translation: Look, this is the Chinese. Hilarious, right?) PS: I am not generalizing all Chinese players. Among the trash-talkers, you can't rule out certain streamers trying to stir shit up for attention. Games have no borders and no politics. Steam provides us gamers with a platform for nearly zero-distance communication, and what we communicate shouldn't be filled with biases and discrimination. Finally, as gamers, I believe we only have one common enemy, and that is: HACKERS. That's all, GG.

translation_en: I’ve sworn a million times never to buy early access games. And here I am stepping on the exact same rake again... But, weirdly enough, this time the rake hit my level 3 helmet and didn't even leave a bump) We have before us yet another incarnation of the Battle Royale, which started with Koushun Takami's novel of the same name, later broke into Japanese cinema, and now it's the gaming industry's turn. As many know, the pioneer was ARMA with a special mod. Then again, as a mod for H1Z1 (King of the Kill). And now the creator of those very mods decided to make his own game with [strike] blackjack and hookers [/strike] an emphasis on realism and a cool atmosphere. The game has been in early access for only 3 weeks, but every Wednesday the devs drop a huge patch with a bunch of fixes (hello H1Z1) + they roll out another massive patch every month. Right now, judging by the reviews, you can play normally even on potatoes like GTX 660+ 2GB, i3 + 8 gigs of RAM (not my setup). Now, about the game itself and why it's so damn good: [list] [*]Realism in everything – from car physics to bullet trajectory. [*]A wide-ass arsenal of weapons ranging from machine guns to frying pans (by the way, melee weapons aren't just ballast here, you can beat a guy to death with your bare hands in 2-5 hits, and if you need to do something silently, well, you know). [*]Lots of weapon attachments, from standard red dots/scopes to flash hiders and sniper rifle cheek pads, for example. [*]There's tons of loot; landing in an area with 2-3 houses guarantees you'll find at least a pistol and ammo for it. The trouble is you won't be able to carry much without a good backpack, though))) [*]You choose where you want to start your battle. Implemented via an airdrop from a plane, but unlike the aforementioned competitor, you can steer your free fall. [*]Instant matchmaking – 99 people gather in 1-2 seconds. [*]The ability to play in duos or squads – you're matched against duos and squads accordingly. [*]The graphics look nice (waiting for optimization, yeah...) [*]The sounds are just goddamn divine. The game relies heavily on sound in general – the sound of footsteps, gunfire, moving vehicles, a flying plane, etc. All these sounds will help you survive (and kill someone else). [*]Vehicles – 3 are already available (UAZ, Dacia, and buggy) + they're adding the motorcycle any day now. [*]A wide range of tactical opportunities, from standard camping to sneaky tactics and flanking maneuvers with decoys. [*]I've heard people whining about cheaters – bullshit. Haven't run into a single one, though I play on EU... [*]And lastly, what I personally like. You can't just sit tight for long in a fortified bunker picking off everyone who approaches. The game has an exceptionally well-implemented shrinking play area system... [/list] I'll wrap up my brief review here, hope it helps someone decide whether to buy or not buy this game. And may the best man win! Upd. 26.04.17 Everything is still good, the devs keep pleasing us with weekly patches, straightening out the optimization. And they don't forget about cosmetics (for example, cars now come in different colors and there's an open-top UAZ). The sidecar bike is certainly adorable, but imo useless). More guns, more attachments. Keep it up, Bluehole! P.S. Forgot to mention another plus – for every match you are awarded in-game currency, which you can use to buy a crate (surprise))). It opens completely for free and contains purely cosmetic items to change your look. Some items are so rare that you can sell them on the market for several times the price of the game itself (test your luck). P.P.S. Massive thanks to those who leave constructive criticism instead of just downvoting the review. P.P.P.S. I strongly recommend anyone having issues with stutters and FPS drops to check out the community guides. There are some very good builds there that will boost your performance big time.
