translation_en: The game is insanely superior to its genre competitors. With graphics and a gameplay fluidity that is much more focused on the mode, this game has a lot to offer for those who like Battle Royales. Pros: - Gorgeous graphics - Variety of weapons, equipment, scopes, grips... - Considerably large map with loot spots everywhere - The developers' attention to detail is noticeable (like weapons having more than one firing mode, and when switching between them you can even notice the fire selector button position change) - Very well-balanced weapon damage - Simple and complete controls (even though at first the camera and movement might feel a bit weird) Cons: - Main and most obvious one, the 56 reais price tag for a game still in EA - Vehicle mechanics need to be adjusted - Bugs and exploiting low graphic settings to gain a vision advantage (like people disabling grass effects, for example) I've always liked the genre, and I pinned my hopes on H1Z1 to play something really cool, but its sort-of-PS2 graphics and totally "washed-out and colorless" scenery made me lose interest. PUBG brought what H1Z1 failed to deliver. Tactics, fluidity, and combat realism! I give the game a 9 basically pending bug fixes, other than that it's one of the best purchases I've made in recent times. Highly recommended!

translation_en: One after another, cheaters that anyone with eyes can see are blatantly obvious face zero penalties, and famous streamers like You Tiao, Da Guan Ren, and Wu Wu Kai do it publicly. I have no idea what the developers' stance on cheats is. Is this really a game where you buy it for 98 RMB and then pay a monthly subscription for hacks? Turns out this game really is pay-to-win. Back then, I thought PUBG was a treasure. As an RPG lover, I've rarely played games from childhood to adulthood where you couldn't lock onto targets with the Tab key, so my aim is absolute garbage, and I never had any idea what recoil control was. But PUBG was different. Even with terrible aim, I could make up for it with tactics and positioning. Many people think PUBG is just CS on a big map, but I feel like PUBG is Commandos or Assassin's Creed on a big map. I explored every corner of the map, knowing inside and out which house corners people could hide in, which flanking routes were the most concealed, and which stairs and bridge undersides you could crawl into. I knew all these strategies like the back of my hand. After 500 hours, I was in the top 10,000 on the Asia server and top 1,000 on Oceanian. Now, having played for almost a thousand hours, my heart is completely dead. Because the hack sales groups and cheat QQ groups have arrived, and against their wallhacks, I have nowhere to hide. When the foggy weather came out, I thought it was my home turf, but turns out removing fog and grass only costs 150 RMB for a permanent pass. Maybe the guys with great aim find ways to fight back against hackers, but strategic players like us—commonly known as "LYB" (crouching/camping cowards)—truly have nowhere to hide in front of cheaters. Now I realize that players like us who only spent 98 RMB are just targets set up for the tech bigshots. High-rank matches on the live servers are full of cheaters, and there are plenty on the test servers too. Being able to watch the death cam on the test server and witness yourself getting one-tapped by a 98K without even scoping in—that feeling is pure, unadulterated bliss. Bluehole, are you going to do anything about the cheating players? Bluehole, are you going to do anything about the streamers who act as promoters and role models for everyone? What a damn waste of this game. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- **Part I** My name is Kira067, and I'm a prisoner. I only know how to kill; killing is the only reason I'm still alive. Kira067 isn't my real name; the name I was born with was forgotten long ago. Fading away right along with it is the sunlight filtering through the curtains in the afternoon, the blueberry pie my mother baked, family prayers around the dinner table... All those so-called moments of happiness gradually blurred away in the bloody stench of war and slaughter. I'm starting not to remember my mother's face, and I've long since forgotten my original name. My memory consists only of killing and blood, to the point where it makes me wonder if I ever truly existed in this world at all. War, everything is war. War has destroyed almost everything in the world: food, energy, water... everything related to survival. The Earth can no longer afford to sustain everyone. Naturally, the ones who performed the worst in the war—thieves, swindlers, cowards, traitors—were all sent to a military tribunal. Waiting for them is a deserted island and 99 other people who went through the exact same terrible things. A plane drops them by parachute onto the island, but in the end, only one person is allowed to leave alive. Yes, I, Kira067, am one of those who committed grave sins in the war. The funny thing is, I've even forgotten how I committed my crimes; my memory holds nothing but the slaughter across more than forty islands. The energy crisis has occurred forty-three times, and I've been to that island forty-three times. Forty-three times, every time I was the one covered in blood, coming back alone. **Part II** Forty-four. This is the forty-fourth time stepping onto this island. I stroke the forty-three scars on my left forearm, looking around the boarding airstrip. There are ninety-nine other people waiting at the airstrip; they are manic, uneasy, all newbies. Nearly half of these ninety-nine will die upon landing; the rest will either die to the island's poison gas, get sniped by someone hiding in the grass, or die by my dagger. And I, after killing the very last person, will carve the forty-fourth scar onto my forearm—the medal of the forty-fourth victor. Sitting not far from me is a girl with fire-red hair and a cuckoo tattooed on her shoulder. Ever since the first parachute drop, all my desires regarding girls dropped to zero—on the first island, a muscle-head tried to finish off another drenched girl right after landing, only for a Uzi popping out of the grass to blow away every single hair from his groin two seconds later. "My name is Tina129," the girl noticed me looking at her and actually spoke up. "How long do you think you'll survive?" she asked. Such a newbie, I thought. I knew her name; long-term slaughter has made my eyesight sharp. "Tina129" is engraved on the dog tag hanging around her neck. People like this won't even last past the first circle of poison gas. The girl seemed to sense my disdain and stopped talking to me. In the distance, a piercing foghorn screamed, and the airplane cabin door opened like a bloody, gaping maw. I stood up and walked toward the plane. **Part III** This time I landed in Water Town again. The terrain in Water Town is complex, and the field of view is narrow; newbies go into houses and get trapped so hard they can't even crawl out. I jumped and sprinted across the rooftops. Today I got lucky, scoring a Level 3 helmet, Level 2 vest, a Vector for close combat, and an M16 for long range. The M16 is a bit crappy, but any tool that can kill is a good tool. Amshushing, looting, killing, running from the poison—all these actions were as skilled as if they were carved into my brain. Having danced at the gates of hell forty-three times, I know every single routine for killing and being killed. The poison circle is getting smaller, about the size of a soccer field now. The electronic watch on my wrist tells me there are still twenty-some people alive. Such a bunch of newbies. I can't forget my twelfth time on the island, when a dozen people were proned inside a poison circle the size of a living room. Everyone ran out of ammo, crowbars, machetes, and frying pans flying everywhere. The bones in one of my arms were shattered, and I used my teeth to end the last person's life. This time there's a tall building inside the poison circle. It's both safe and dangerous. All four sides of the tall building are bulletproof glass, making it hard for outsiders to hit anyone inside. But all eyes from every direction are focused on the tall building, with two dozen murderous eyes staring at the temporary residents inside. For instance, I caught a glimpse of red hair sticking out by a first-floor window, red like fire. I think I know who the owner of that hair is. I crept up next to the window. Since people outside can't shoot into the house, and people inside can't shoot out. "Tina," I softly called out her name. "How about a trade? You don't shoot me, I'll watch the outside of the building for you, and later you throw me a first aid kit." The hair inside the window quickly pulled back, and after a moment, I heard the girl's voice. "Okay." **Part IV** What followed was more forgettable crouching and slaughter. The poison circle grew smaller, and the living people grew fewer. Finally, the remaining number was 3: me, Tina129, and one other lurking assassin. "Tina," I shouted, "come out quickly, the gas is coming. Go out the front door, not the side door. There's a guy prone in the W direction of the side door." Rustling footsteps came from inside the house. The front door opened, and Tina, holding a UMP and pointing it in my direction, crouched along the base of the wall toward another large boulder acting as cover. How naive. Either you completely trust me, or you don't trust me at all. Then, someone stood up from the grass in the S direction, dumping a full magazine of a SCAR into Tina's body. Sorry, but I needed a decoy. I raised my gun and put a few bullets right into that person's head. I had been aiming at the S direction the whole time, but I needed a decoy to make him show himself. The electronic watch on my wrist made a ticking sound. Surviving players: 1. I walked over to Tina's corpse, covered in blood, eyes wide open. Ha, little girl, go get reincarnated in another world. I pulled out the dagger she wore and carved the forty-fourth scar onto my forearm. **Part V** Mechanical killing, waiting, killing, waiting. The energy crisis happened dozens more times, I dropped onto the island dozens more times, and there was almost no space left on my left forearm for me to carve another medal. This is the eighty-third time stepping onto the island. The poison circle surrounded a building; downstairs was me, upstairs was some other lucky bastard. Nobody is more familiar with how to push a building than I am. In eighty-three bouts of life and death, I can't even remember how many people I've killed on the second floor. I threw a fragmentation grenade up the stairs, fired my gun blindly a few times, threw another frag grenade, fired blindly a few times, and then pulled out a flashbang and tossed it up. The flashbang popped with a crisp bang, and I rushed up with my gun—at this point, the guy upstairs was either cowering in a corner too scared to move or blinded by the flashbang, leaving him completely at my mercy. The moment I went upstairs, I saw that person's face—it was a delicate-looking girl, and underneath a bulky helmet, fire-red hair was exposed. T... Tina? I froze immediately. I remember this girl. Out of thousands of kills, she was the only girl who had ever spoken to me. I remember how she died—she died because she trusted me. After snapping out of it, I hurriedly fired, but the muzzle of my gun shook violently like a newbie holding a weapon for the very first time. A bullet hit her shoulder, stripping away her body armor, and a cuckoo bird lingered on her shoulder. I stood there in a daze, trying to adjust my crosshairs, only to find that the entire magazine was already empty. Her vision had recovered, her gaze cold and merciless, nothing like that naive rookie anymore. I saw the dog tag on her neck, engraved with—Tina130. The last sound I heard was the firing of an SKS, right beside my head. **Part VI** I woke up from the darkness. I don't know my own name. "You're a prisoner, you've committed heinous crimes," a person in a white lab coat sitting across from me said. "This is a time of war, and killing is the only reason you're going to survive." I tried hard to recall my prior memories—complete blankness. There seemed to be some fragments about afternoon sunlight, but those fragments were so distant and unreal, as if they were mass-produced. I didn't remember anything about the war, nor what unforgivable crimes I had supposedly committed. The white coat tossed me a dog tag. "Put it on, this is your name." I looked at the dog tag, the brand-new dog tag shining brightly. Kira068. That's me, Kira068. I stroked the dense, packed scars on my left forearm. I don't know where those scars were left behind. I only know that killing is the only reason I'm still alive.

translation_en: [h1]The Game / Gameplay[/h1] PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS is a classic "Battle Royale" game, much like what you already know from H1Z1: King of the Kill, for example. 100 players drop in at various points over an island and then have to take care of looting and finding weapons, vehicles, and other gear. The winner of a match is the last one surviving. Due to the ongoing and increasingly faster shrinking of the so-called "safe zones" on the map, things soon get pretty interesting to hectic. PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS can be played solo or teamed up with friends as a 2-man team or as a squad (up to four players). [h1]Pros[/h1] + Very good graphics + huge game world + many different weapons with different handling + large selection of armor and accessories + quite effective protection against campers thanks to the faster-shrinking zone + fast and good support + everything on the map can also be reached and entered [h1]Cons[/h1] - Servers are still quite unstable at times (rubberbanding, lags, disconnects) - Controls are pretty clunky and imprecise every now and then - sometimes catastrophic vehicle physics with obstacles like bumps and fences - currently still little content in the reward crates - monotonous interiors of houses and bunkers [h1]Conclusion[/h1] If the publisher keeps their promise and consistently supports the game with updates and patches, this will be a game that you will have a lot of fun with for a very long time. An absolute buy recommendation, especially when playing with friends in duo or as a squad! :-) 9/10

translation_en: After putting a good few hours into this, I think I've got enough material to write a proper review. First of all, I gotta say the game is a lot of fun, both solo and with friends. If you go with buddies, you can be a 4-man squad, running the show in your little car (if you manage to grab one of those good old Dacias) shooting guns like it's a hunting trip. If you play solo, the vibe is more about playing invisible to your enemies and trying to catch them off guard, because your only companion on this journey is Madam Ambush. I played it with friends at a lan party, and we had some damn good laughs. I'm playing it solo now, and I still have a good time, because the game keeps you on edge the whole time when you play solo, seeing the circle close in and having to choose your next move very carefully. That feeling of being in a house, hearing noises on the floor below, and hiding with your weapon ready waiting for some clueless bastard who has no idea what's coming to him to show up on the stairs, is totally priceless, honestly. Does it lack content? Of course, maybe add more weapons, items, maps, etc. Although the most important thing right now would be game optimization, that's the main priority in my opinion. PROS: - Fun, addictive both solo and with friends. - The gun system is really good, you have different attachments you can slap on that make them handle differently. - The sound ain't bad either. - Gunplay feels good, weapons even have bullet drop, which helps improve the experience. - Graphically it looks nice, the overall textures and effects are well done. - In-game items are cool because it doesn't take long to get new gear, which you can also sell on the Steam market and make a few bucks, which at the end of the day is what we all like. $$ dOLlARS $$ CONS: - The price. It's in development and 29.99€ feels a bit steep for the content and the current state of the game. - Optimization. Depending on your PC it'll run better or worse, but you need a decent rig to get it running more or less smooth. - Content. It falls a bit short maybe, just one map, and a few weapons and stuff. This last point is forgivable since, like I said, it's still in development and I understand (I want to believe) they'll add more content over time. Alright, back in I go. See ya later.

translation_en: Comparing the game to "H1Z1", "PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS" definitely wins. To talk about the "+" and "-" sides of the game: +3x and 6x scopes have arrived, now it's very easy to find scopes, there are all sorts of scopes. +We can choose which map we want to play. +You can zoom in and out with 8x and 15x scopes. +Car sounds were changed with the 1.0 patch, way better than before. +Gun sounds are really nice and realistic. +There is a huge variety of guns, and they keep adding more to the game with updates (The "VECTOR" gun was added with the April 20 1st-month update, the "VSS" was added with the 2nd-month update). +You can attach 3-4 mods to guns and the mods are actually useful, not just for show. +All guns in the game (except pistols) have 2 modes, one is single-fire and the other is full-auto, which is a good feature. +Looting and camping in the game are even fun (Of course, once you play the game for 300-400 hours, looting becomes torture). +You can place markers on the map, which is a pretty cool feature (If you play duo or squad, not only you but your teammates can also see the marker). +When you crash with a car, both the car's health and your health go down. +Daily, weekly and monthly updates are coming to the game. +Turkish language support is available in the game. +When you die, you can spectate your team (It came to H1Z1 after who knows how many... years, months, days, whatever, let me not trash it too much). +You can jump from the plane whenever you want, wherever you want. +You don't just drive cars on land, you can also drive motorcycles, and even boats in the water! +If you get out of a car while it's moving, you die or get injured, entirely depending on your speed. +There is a chance of rain in the game and they made it really realistic, the sounds and atmosphere are quite nice. Likewise, there is a chance of foggy weather and the atmosphere etc. is quite nice. -[IMPORTANT] I bought the game when it first came out and there were no cheaters at all, or at least I didn't see any, but right now there are a lot of cheaters in the game. If you play 10 matches, you'll inevitably run into 1-2 cheaters. -When you land with the parachute, the game can bug out and your health can drop in a ridiculous way. -The moment we go over a small bump while driving on the road, the car flies way up into the air, flips over, etc. -Playing without a scope is seriously hard, especially you can't hit guys far away without a scope, at least I can't. -Skins are few and not good for now in the game. -Punching does way too much damage in a ridiculous way! -In duo or squad mode, even if you hit enemies with a headshot, they just get knocked down (Meaning even though they got shot right in the brain, they can get back up). -There is no crafting system, I wish we could craft simple things like bandages. Quick info about the game: -I played 400+ matches, it only crashed to desktop twice. -If your FUP (Fair Usage Policy data limit) is exceeded and you are using the internet (Facebook, YouTube, etc.) and playing the game at the same time, there is enough lag to annoy you. But if you are not using the internet, just opening the game and nothing else is open, it lags very rarely. If your FUP is not exceeded, you can play comfortably whether you use the internet or not. -One of the most important things in the game is scopes! But unfortunately they are hard to find (With the update on April 20, a 2x scope came to the game and it's easier to find). -The learning curve isn't long, I got 2 kills in my very first match. -When you land with the parachute, the game can bug out and your health can drop in a ridiculous way. ------------------------------ My system specs: Gtx 970 16gb ram Intel Core i7 6700K I play on "Ultra" settings with this system. Inside and outside buildings, fps is +90 (With the update on April 20, there was a +10 increase in fps and fps doesn't drop in cities like before, or if it does, it drops much less) (With the 2nd-month update the game became smoother, fps increased by 5-10) (With the 3rd-month update optimization was improved quite a bit) [NEW] (With the 1.0 patch, the game's optimization was improved a lot, I can play the game comfortably on ultra) ------------------------------ Note: There is a thing called BP in the game, which is the game's currency and you can buy crates with it, skins drop from the crates and you can sell them too. In +30 days I opened +40 crates and made 20.09 TL. Goal is 20.23 TL! Note: New crates and skins were added to the game with the 3rd-month update, and thanks to that, I made 100 TL within 3 weeks. Note: I played the game for +350 hours, got a bit bored and took a break, but it has more replayability. If you don't want to miss the updates coming to the game, you can visit the official "playbattlegrounds.com" website or follow the official Facebook page "Playerunknown's Battlegrounds Türkiye". The price of the game is a bit steep, but it's definitely worth your money! (I've had the game for 5-6 months and I've already made my money back, I earned about 200 TL). If you have questions you can ask below the review or add me. Thanks for reading my review, if it was helpful clicking "Yes", if not helpful clicking "No" would be a contribution to me. translation_en: [h1][b]1st Person Update![/b] PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds[/h1] At first, it's a United Airlines simulation. But after jumping out of the plane, things really get started. Pick your destination and steer there using "WASD+Shift". The ripcord can be pulled manually or by the "we won't let you hit the ground assistant" at about 200m altitude. On the final meters down to earth, take another look around (hold down the "alt" key) to make sure who else decided on this exact patch of land. Just like in H1Z1, everything that breathes is poison to your own survival. Once arrived at your starting point of choice, you need to scavenge everything that can somehow cause pain as quickly as possible. Whether pans, knives, or lead-spitters, having is always better than needing! Besides the right tools, everything that can mitigate externally inflicted pain is essential. Helmets, vests, bandages, energy drinks... everything that stops your guts from spilling out gets picked up. All this junk finds shelter in a backpack on our back. Once the bare necessities are hoarded, the real fun can begin. The meaning and purpose is to shoot the crap out of everything that crosses our path. Your own ambition is to leave a trail of devastation and earthly shells within the ever-shrinking circle/map. To figure out where you currently are, you simply have to study the inclination of the lichen. Alternatively, you can just press the "M" key. Now the infantryman is faced with a map that shows his own position, the surroundings, the viewing direction, and the sphere into which you are supposed to stroll. Due to your own and others' activities, the number of targets steadily decreases. If you and a handful of adversaries find yourselves together on the green at the end to bash each other's brains in, you've pretty much done everything right. Now it's time to keep calm. With surgical precision, you need to make the projectiles impact where the temperature is about 37°C. If you pull this off and only your own sludge-pump is still ticking at the end... Well then, "GGWP!" Everyone who played gets rewarded with points that they can trade for in-game items in the main menu. [b][u]OMG! Unpacking my sweet little bees![/u][/b] Let's all chill out together before we can deal with this! [i] (*sniiiiifff&exhaaaale very slowly)[/i] Real file story! Rumor has it that it's not toasters, but actual existing high-tech servers processing our gaming experience! "No shit, Captain Obvious!" And why does the time continuum always tear when I'm just trying to bury someone? Think about it! Just Early Access, but the guys up top are working on it. If you're sick of your own [b]marker on the map[/b], you can now delete it with "del". To leave only scorched earth for the following enemy, vehicles can now be stripped of their tires and left behind at a doneness of "Well done". Previously monogamous attachments can now also be used multiple times[i](Vector can be fitted with a tactical stock; SKS now digitizes with a cheek pad)[/i]. Lead-bean-shooters now do a bit less damage and assault rifles suffer less from Parkinson's while working. For the clueless among us, a dashed line is now supposed to reveal the way to the center of the next chillout area! Nice! In addition, you can delight in the [b]VSS[/b], a suppressed, 9mm-firing, 4X-magnifying rarity defined as a sniper[i]("very rare loot")[/i]. Last but not least, suicide on wheels was added - [b]"Added Motorbike" O.o[/b]. So little bees, stay cool and keep an eye on your blood pressure! [b][u]OMG! Little bees, let's spin a Fidget Spinner together![/u][/b] It's not a NERFy weekly update, it's a super extremely rare bee-subscriber-follower-special update! After the last updates, the servers are running real tight. Loot now disappears much smoother into our vegan carrier bags made from recycled cookie skins. On top of that, there are two new mugs and haircuts you can treat yourself to. But who gives a shit about haircuts when you can have an Mk14 EBR for it?! The natural habitat of that 7.62mm-firing rarity is known to the neutral observer as a red box with a parachute/swinging-tit magnet. Anyone who already suffers from an Mk14 allergy from CoD is advised to stock up on enough glycerin ASAP. Once you hold the holy grail in your hands, you can look forward to an extremely effective flyswatter. For all those who are sick of getting cowardly snacked from behind by some 5-face, there's now a solution (No way! Yes way!). "Added 1st Person server options to NA and EU Solo" ... No! Yes! Ohh! Gone are the days when everything seemed pointless. Gone are the days when we sobbed alone in the shower. Gone are the days when suspicious little thinkers could blow us away without us having to fear them afterwards. If your opponent's *one-click feels too suspicious, you can now report them. Yay! Now swing that ban hammer diligently, little bees! (Formal protest: "Not everything that kills us is a cheater!" YES IT IS! Solely and exclusively because all of us, each and every one of us, is actually an absolute PvP machine. Deep down we always knew it. Elo hell, noob teams, disconnects & ping are the only things keeping us gods in the flesh from winning every single time! So if the above factors don't apply... then CHEEEETArrr!!! REPORT!) Reducing the waiting time when using the First Aid Kit/Painkiller & Med Kit/Adrenaline will soon let us get back into the action faster. With "Ctrl+M" you can now mute anything capable of using a microphone. Winter is coming my dear bees, survive it unscathed! [u] FUBAR Index[/u]: [list] [*]Annihilation by squatters through hypocritical exploitation of inappropriate lingering in buildings. [*]Failure to locate lead-spitters (You could of course claim you got nothing from the Easter bunny. Or you testify that it was simply hidden unfindably! So it's ALWAYS the game's fault! Never ours!). [*]The acquaintance of our organs with dozens of alloyed lead beans. [*]A direct hit from the BOOM-BOOM. [i]This list can be extended by any events perceived as ungracious in general.[/i] [/list] PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds is an alternative for everyone who wants to escape the fast-paced, arcade-heavy H1Z1, but still likes Battle Royale. It's playable in both solo and multiplayer modes, features a [b]spectator mode[/b] in team play, and looks pretty damn good graphically. Still, it should be mentioned that it's an Early Access game that does a lot of things right. But it isn't perfect yet. [b]The gaming experience is recommended[/b] and effortlessly makes up for minor gameplay flaws. [b]9 out of 10[/b] trolley dollies would recommend PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds. [i]Suggestions, criticism, or something completely different?[/i] Spit it out! <3 -> PUBG we call it love!

translation_en: [Update Dec 22, 2017] BattleGround is a Battle Royale in Alpha [u]that I give a lukewarm recommendation to.[/u] I hesitated for a long time before leaving a positive review. [u]The pros:[/u] - The concept is really well made, when it's [truly] finished, it's simply going to be the best game in the genre. -- The "blue zone" is an area that shrinks (in stages) as the match goes on. Being outside this zone damages you and forces you to move toward the center. Plus, the final center of the blue zone is random and never ends up in the same spot. This stops campers from abusing it and adds a lot to the strategy and gameplay. -- The game is "speedy", it's dynamic, you don't have time to get bored, matches last around 30 min. -- The anxiety, the paranoia, the insane sprints with the blue zone breathing down your neck, it's really gripping and addictive. -- The primal scream of joy you'll let out when you finish first is worth all the little bugs and annoyances currently in the game. - The graphics are pretty nice, easily on par with Arma 3 on ultra. - And speaking of Arma 3, the hitboxes are flawless.... it's such a huge change, it feels so good... you have no idea!! - You can play in squads, duos, or solo. The balance is well struck, solo matches only pit you against other solos and that's a smart move! - You can choose when to eject from the plane and therefore influence where you spawn, which adds a huge amount to strategy and gameplay. - Very decent weapon selection. - Weapons are customizable, nothing original, but at least it's well done and bug-free. - The inventory and interface are well made, ergonomic and bug-free, which is rare enough to be worth pointing out. - VoIP is pretty decent. - Updates [strike]every week[/strike] pretty often. (with visible improvements... mostly audible) [u]The cons:[/u] - [strike]It is REALLY very poorly optimized right now.[/strike] Even though progress has been made, it remains a very resource-heavy game, optimization isn't ideal yet. It'll get improved later on. Since the 1.0 release, fps are clearly up, but server rollback issues have popped up. - There are still some cheaters.... not as many as I expected after reading the reviews before buying it, but there are definitely some. By my personal estimate, there's always at least one cheater every 8 to 10 games (which is actually pretty low, but when you run into one... well there you go... Ragequit). [strike]The devs were very clear about this: There is currently NO complete anti-cheat system, it will be added after optimization.[/strike] [Edit Dec 22, 2017] The devs have added a few protections against cheating. And they ban cheaters pretty quickly when detected and reported by players using the in-game report system. They even added a KillCam, which lets you confirm a suspicion. - The sound is much better than at the start, especially vehicle noises. Gunshot directional audio isn't quite there yet. Artillery sounds a bit like a bad TV series, not very credible. The only positive thing about the sound: weapon noises are pretty well done. And enemy footstep audio is finally balanced. - It lags a little bit too much for my liking. Now it's hard to tell the difference between lag and optimization issues, but there are still 3-4 big Lags/Freezes/Rollbacks lasting 0.5-1 seconds per match. On the other hand, it's really way less severe than I expected after reading the reviews. In fact, to be honest, [u]it's very playable[/u] and even way more so than certain other games in the genre... (no need to call them out, you know the guilty parties...) Since the 1.0 release there are tons of rollbacks at the start of matches, which wasn't the case before. Can't wait for a patch or better servers. - The gaming experience really varies a lot from one player to another. For example, some complain about repetitive disconnects, in 200 hours of play, I've only had 10. Earlier I said the hitbox was perfect, but some people clearly have issues with it. I also said I had sound clipping issues with explosions, some people don't have this problem at all. Some have major lag issues, I have very few. Some have building deformation problems, like "play-doh", I don't have that problem at all. A lot of problems in this game seem pretty random and clearly depend on your rig.... or just luck. So if you buy this game, it's a bit like Russian roulette... annoying. [strike]even for a beta.[/strike] - Personal nitpick: I'd like the blue zone to leave us alone longer... but hey, that's a personal preference, and since the game balance is just perfect, best not to touch anything.

translation_en: So, I've spent 30 hours ingame by now. PUB is definitely (only) for fans of tactical/realistic shooters. I think most people know what it's about. You jump out of a plane, collect gear and weapons, and then head into a constantly shrinking zone. I'd say I'm relatively successful, I actually make it into the top 20 at least 9 times out of 10 (in solo). Jump out of the plane and then fly relatively far to a distant, small cluster of houses. Loot there, ideally find a car, and then head off to a bigger city where there are no enemies hanging around. Personally, I can't wrap my head around why so many players so often drop directly over a big city. That frequently leads to 50% of the enemies being eliminated right at the start of the first zone. PUB is not for fans of fast-paced shooters. Especially in Duo/Squad mode, it often means: looting, sneaking, hiding, waiting, and observing. If things go "badly"—meaning you have a good position well inside the first zone—you can easily end up waiting 10 minutes for enemies without ever spotting one. In general, you can say that enemy contact is definitely "scarce," depending on how you play. Sure, if you hang out in a big city that was flown over directly by the plane at the start of the round, you'll make the acquaintance of one or more enemies relatively early on. If you play rather smart, meaning you actually want to win, you prefer to stay out of enemies' ways. Especially when there aren't many left alive. Keeping your trigger finger under control is extremely important in PUB. Whoever shoots gives away their position to all other enemies. Gunshots can be heard from extremely far away and are extremely easy to pinpoint. Anyone starting out fresh will definitely die a few times because they go weak. It's not that easy to ignore that inner FPS voice that screams "Shoot! Shoot!! SHOOT!!!!!!!!!1!11" when spotting an enemy. You will—have to—learn to deal with it. Personally, I really like the game immensely, but I'm also a fan of tactical shooters. Anyone looking for fast action is in the wrong place here, as are people with a low frustration tolerance. It's possible you play perfectly for 20 minutes, have great gear and weapons. One mistake and you're dead, possibly without ever having seen the enemy. As for the general state of the game: good in my opinion. Other publishers would officially release the game like this and then chuck patches after it. Of course there's still a lot of room for improvement. Picking up items is a bit "laggy," the plane at the beginning is deafeningly loud so that communication with team members is impossible, there are no team waypoints for the map, occasional bugs/glitches, lagging enemies... nevertheless, you can already play it very well. If you like sneaking from tree to tree and looting house to house, if you're up for properly getting into the survival atmosphere, if you enjoy staying put in the exact same spot for minutes and not shooting immediately upon first visual contact with enemies, then this is the right place for you and you can/should buy it right now in my opinion. If you like fast action and just want to shoot shit for half an hour in the evening, you're in the wrong place.

translation_en: "A game about being ready to kill your teammate for a 4x scope." I tried getting into H1Z1 and even The Culling, but only PUBG managed to hook me and won't let go. This is probably due to the solid execution of the Battle Royale mode itself, which follows all the right rules and focuses on balance rather than milking people for cash via skins or microtransactions. WHY DID I BUY THE GAME? I won't list all the perks of the genre; I figure if you're interested in this game, you've 100% already played H1Z1, Miscreated, Arma 2, Arma 3, DayZ, The Culling, or something similar. There's no character needs system (food, water, and stuff), nor is there a deep injury system (fractures, bleeding), so the whole process is focused entirely on making it to the center of the zone and killing enemies. This is a great move for this kind of mode. Maybe in the future, the developers will complicate certain elements for hardcore fans and separate them into a "hardcore" mode so they can break their legs, bleed out, or just starve to death. NOBODY HAS EVER HUMILIATED MY PC LIKE THIS As for optimization, the game has no concept of it. Unless, of course, you're a fan of slide shows and playing at 10-20 fps is normal for you, then you won't lose anything. But if you're used to playing at 60 fps and have a pretty good PC, then sorry, go suck on your graphics card somewhere else. Here, it will sodomize your computer to the fullest, though it's unclear with what and how. The game runs on the Unreal Engine, which is well-optimized and has long been used in the gaming industry, but apparently the developers' hands are growing straight out of their asses. OH YOU SLY BASTARD! Unfortunately, playing games like this on high graphics settings isn't always helpful or comfortable, because an abundance of detail gets in the way and camouflages your enemy. Therefore, even if you have a PC that costs as much as a Formula 1 car, there's a high probability you simply won't see the enemy lying in the grass, sitting in the shadows, or next to some dark object. But if you have low graphics settings, spotting that little shit in the grass is a breeze, because the amount of it is minimal, textures are muddy, and shadows are way too bright. It's a guaranteed win. I WALK IN AND THERE'S FUCK ALL The most important thing in survival games is loot, and everything's fine with that here—in almost every match you'll have an assault rifle, armor, and a helmet. Sure, there are times when you run into a house and there's only an orphan frying pan, but that's more of an exception than the rule. WHERE WE DROPPING? Overall, I'm happy with the game. Having bought it for 800 rubles, I got 10,000 rubles' worth of emotions, impressions, and just a great mood. I recommend the game to all genre fans. My rating: 8 scopes out of 10 (I climbed to the very top of the plane's tail, and you?)

translation_en: Remember never to use Dolphin Booster, it's an absolute scam. It's even worse than not using anything at all. The Tieba forums are full of Dolphin shills. I wouldn't disconnect if I didn't use a booster, but after using it, my old problems like not being able to open doors or reload weapons didn't get fixed at all, and on top of that, I keep disconnecting. Dolphin is just trash. Dolphin is just trash. Dolphin is just trash. Dolphin is just trash. I was really pissed off when I wrote this, so it was very short and emotional. Let me add some context about what happened back then. I'm on a 100M China Telecom broadband connection, located in Suzhou, Jiangsu. I bought a 3-month Dolphin Platinum subscription (the official website didn't have a 1-month option, at least not back then, I don't know if they do now). Under Mode 1, the game wouldn't even launch. Mode 2 let me in, but I'd disconnect, get back in, lag, gun-swapping wouldn't work, I'd walk through a door only to rubberband right back outside—just all kinds of issues. I tried switching to all sorts of nodes (tried all the East China ones). Completely useless. I have to point out that no matter which node you pick on Dolphin, Dolphin's own displayed PIN is always under 30 and packet loss is 0%!!! Then I went on Baidu and the forums, looking everywhere, trying things like turning off antivirus and firewalls. Including the CMD command suggested by my man Martinv•Ni, all completely useless. I contacted customer service, and they sent me two files, a Ping.cmd file. After running the test, the CS rep checked it and said everything was fine (their file showed under 20ms every time, what kind of problem are you gonna spot with that when my game is lagging like a dog?). Anyway, I was still lagging. CS said, "There's an abnormality with the game's matchmaking server, I'll help report this for the tech guys to handle tomorrow." The next day, I contacted CS again. Went through the Ping.cmd test all over again. Submitted the generated data, and CS once again said everything was fine and told me to test it again. The magical thing is, this time I actually didn't lag *as much* (for example, you only had to try reloading your magazine 3 times for it to actually work). Went out for dinner, came back, and the lag started up again. It was lagging so badly I couldn't even play, so I had to shut the game down and watch a game stream instead. When I saw how smooth the gameplay was on the stream, I realized that time in the afternoon still counted as mild lag. Finally, I switched to another booster, and not a single damn issue. Anyway, I definitely had problems using Dolphin, just leaving this here as a reference for the bros out there. Maybe, like the guy below said, this VPN just wasn't right for me.

translation_en: 2017.7.27 Update Current playtime 450h+ K/D 2.5+ Everything I said before is bullshit, I just wanna quietly collect and deliver loot. Also, I take back my previous point, I now think this game is heavily based on luck. Luck 8 : 2 everything else. Oh and one more thing, the optimization is now 100000000000 times better than when it first started, so if your PC is decent, don't hesitate. -----------------------------------------Divider----------------------------------------------- Bought the game yesterday (2017.4.13), here is a summary after 7 hours of playtime. (The following is purely personal opinion and experience) 1. Gameplay / Content ★★★★☆ Lots of ways to play, diverse tactical details, you could say it's more creative than H1Z1's base mode. But as for the current game content, the choice of gear and items is a bit "monotonous". By monotonous I mean: guns are basically all assault rifles (M4/M16/AK/SCAR), some players might keep a shotgun or sniper rifle as a backup, while pistols and submachine guns have become pretty useless, only good for the very beginning when you just land. Thrown items are even rarer to see people use, smoke grenades pop up occasionally, but as for the others, I don't know if there are too few or if they're just so useless that you might as well just gunfight directly, anyway throwables also seem kind of pointless, and melee weapons (like machetes, crowbars, etc.) go without saying. 2. Game Optimization ★☆☆☆☆ Although this game has only been out for barely a month, we shouldn't be too harsh on its optimization, but since it's already on sale and cost 98 RMB, shouldn't we get a normal gaming experience? (Rant over, now down to business) [Hardware requirements (for reference only)] [u] Graphics card gtx660 / amd7850, RAM 8g [/u] This is the starting configuration if you want to play this game. Do not consider it if your specs are lower than this, wait for optimization or just upgrade your rig accordingly. This entry-level setup can run basically smoothly on lowest settings right now. Of course, one requirement is to make sure you don't have too many background programs running before starting the game. This game eats RAM way more than you think, and with the same specs, adding more RAM makes a massive, massive difference for this game. Also, I won't recommend any game accelerators; the current mainstream ones all have an acceleration option for this game, but since I haven't compared them, I won't make blind comments. 3. Advice for wanna-be players / newbies Solo players enter with caution! Most of the fun in this game comes from teaming up and cooperating with teammates (basically looting together, sorting the items, and playing delivery boy 2333), to be honest, solo mode is pretty boring. The game has solo, duo, and squad, so it's best to drag your buddies along if you want to play. For newbies parachuting, I suggest jumping to places away from the flight path. The areas directly along the flight path are basically filled with experienced veterans. Also, camping and ratting are always more useful than pure gunplay. In this game, wanting to get a chicken dinner (winning the game gives you "Winner Winner Chicken Dinner", so...) Tactics : Teamwork : Aim : Luck = 3 : 3 : 3 : 1 The above is purely personal opinion, and might be limited due to time, for reference only. ——April 14, 2017, 10:06:05 -----------------------------------------Divider----------------------------------------------- The following is my experience after 100 hours of gameplay (May 4, 2017, 23:06:33) Before I knew it, I've played over 100 hours, so I'm writing something while having some free time. After 100+ hours of gameplay, I've clearly graduated from a noob to a veteran. I gotta say, ever since the first monthly update, the game's framerate has become way too stable. Buddies with decent specs can buy it with peace of mind (though if your PC isn't top-tier and you're a graphics snob, you can wait a bit longer). Moving on to the game content, looking at the items and guns added with each update, you can really see the developers' sincerity, and it also shows that future game content—especially firearms and items—will be even more diverse. After playing for 100+ hours and looking back at some of the things I said before, they were actually kind of inappropriate. Below is a rough overview of weapon choices. 1. Weapon and Attachment Choices Rifles (Primary Weapon): ① AK: The only one using 7.62 ammo, high damage, but poor stability. Spraying at very close range feels amazing, but tapping at mid-to-long range is a bit of a struggle, depends on your feel. High spawn rate (I'll prioritize it when I can't find an M16 or 5.56 ammo is low). ② M4: With full attachments, it's the all-around best gun. If you can't find attachments, use something else. Very low spawn rate. ③ M16: Very balanced, strong overall capability, only downside is no full-auto mode. (Pro tip: set it to burst mode, and then keep spamming the left click, it's basically full-auto). ④ SCAR: Excellent at close and medium range, struggles a bit in long-range combat. After 400 hours of playtime, I really like using this gun. Aside from the M4 requiring a stock and grip, and the SCAR requiring a grip, all guns can take a muzzle attachment and a magazine. Dual mags are definitely best; extended or quickdraw comes down to personal preference, I personally like extended mags. Suppressor > Compensator > Flash hider. Secondary Weapon Choices: Comes down to personal preference Shotguns: You MUST pick up a choke! The shotgun's god-tier item! Massively reduces bullet spread. ① S686 Double Barrel: Two shots, rapid fire, recommended for people with good flick aim. ② S1897 Pump Action: 5 shells, single shot. ③ S12K: 5-round semi-auto shotgun, takes rifle attachments (becomes 8 rounds with an extended mag). Snipers: ① 98K: One-shot headshot against Level 2 helmets and below. ② SKS: Designated marksman rifle, decent damage, but massive recoil (unless I have a muzzle compensator and cheek pad, I won't touch this gun). SMGs: Whatever, they're all pretty much the same. I occasionally use the Vector or Uzi. Too lazy to write anymore, going to go get a chicken dinner first. If I have free time later, I'll write about the game's mechanics~ PS: Buddies who want to play together can add me on Steam or come to YY 23253151 (not guaranteed anyone will be there).

translation_en: It's March 30th. Since buying the game till today, I've probably played around 80-something matches, all solo queue across various modes, mostly SOLO. I've won a few chicken dinners, with my highest rank being Asia SOLO #48. The optimization has issues, I don't need to elaborate on that. 1. My setup meets the recommended specs: E3v3 + GTX 660 + 8GB RAM + 1TB HDD, running Windows 7. 2. My experience: Even with all settings on very low, parachute dropping is seriously laggy. Dropping in the wilderness is okay, but if you drop into a town or somewhere with a lot of buildings, it drops to 1 FPS for about 2-3 minutes while it loads the graphics, which is super frustrating.... Afterward, it stays around 40 FPS with occasional stuttering, basically playable and you can experience the game normally. 3. Network-wise, I'm on Shenzhen Telecom, and playing with a direct connection is basically impossible. I've tried Dolphin and UU, and I recommend UU. Dolphin is a total trap, whoever uses it knows, but UU is very stable and I'm very satisfied. Hope the above helps those who haven't bought the game yet but want to play. The content below is to help newbies who love the game. 1. Don't drop hot spots. After the second blue zone, don't go into houses. Ride the edge of the blue zone to sneak up on people, pay attention to finding cover, don't shoot if they're too far or you're not sure you can kill them, and press X to put your gun away to run faster. 2. The few SOLO chicken dinners I got were won using shotguns. Pros use snipers, one shot per kid; noobs use shotguns, one blast per pro, specialized in killing the top 2. My weapon recommendation for noobs is: a red-dot assault rifle + a fully-kitted 5-round shotgun. Why this recommendation? Because my aim is bad, I basically lose straight-up gunfights, and when I win, it's by ambushing people and after firing tons of bullets... so shotguns are my best friend. No matter who it is, in the final one or two safe zones, 2 shots solve the problem. Finally, I have one suggestion, I hope the next optimization adds a kill cam feature!!! How many times have I died not knowing what hit me~~~ I was so geared up. Too many tears to mention. Hope you guys upvote this so the devs can see it, thanks. April 24th: After switching to an SSD and adding another 8GB stick of RAM, my FPS is stable at 40-50. But after the monthly update, aiming down sights with various scopes feels really awkward to get used to. My peak Asia SOLO rank was 2150, highest I got was top 300, couldn't climb any higher than that, the latency is just too real... can't take this abuse. Any squad of 4 with a decent rank looking for teammates? You can contact me. I practically live in Georgopol, military base, camps, bunker, and Ferry Pier. My gunplay is solid and I know how to flank.

translation_en: [b][Early Access reviews are subject to change after the official release version][/b] [h1]Into the Battle Royale[/h1] Before I begin, I want to clarify that I haven't played the ArmA Battle Royale mod or H1Z1: King of the Kill, so it's hard for me to write a comparative review. [b][u]Meeting Battle Royale[/u][/b] PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS (hereafter PUBG) is a battle royale game made by Bluehole in collaboration with PLAYERUNKNOWN, the creator of the battle royale mode. Since the concept itself is quite familiar thanks to the original battle royale and numerous media spin-offs inspired by it, getting your hands on a decent battle royale game actually wasn't easy. And finally, the answer came in the form of PUBG. [b][u]Only for Survival[/u][/b] The rules of PUBG are very simple. 100 players skyfall onto their locations of choice, loot weapons and survival gear, and become the last survivor. You are free to do whatever you want in this process. You can overwhelm others with sheer firepower right from the start, or you can farm up a ton of gear, secure a spot, and play for a late-game advantage. You can even rat it out and just run away like a coward without firing a single bullet. No one's going to call you a coward. The losers who died first are already queuing up for another survival match anyway. [b][u]For a Dramatic Match[/u][/b] PUBG didn't forget to include mechanics to make this short film unfold dramatically, just like the original battle royale. First of all, since the start involves dropping from an airplane, it requires strategic movement right from the get-go. If you're dropping into a city overflowing with loot, you're going to want to think twice. Other people will have the same idea, and you'll see a bunch of parachutes floating around you. There's also a zone restriction system to prevent excessive item farming, handled by a gradually closing electromagnetic field like a blue zone. Unlike the original, it doesn't kill you in one hit, but that actually cranks the tension up even more. Aside from this restricted zone, red zones with random bombardments add yet another layer of tension. In addition, ballistic trajectory elements, gear limits to prevent excessive looting, weapon attachment systems, the presence of vehicles, strategically well-designed maps, zone timer systems, and the wildcard airdrop—systems that are well-balanced so the game doesn't get too loose or too overwhelming really add to the fun. Also, besides going solo, duo (2-player) and squad (4-player) modes offer a different kind of fun compared to solo mode, almost like playing a real survival game. Make sure you use a mic! [b][u]Major Issues[/u][/b] But there are still walls to climb. First of all, even considering that it's early access, the server and game optimization status are bad enough to cause discomfort while playing. The level of annoyance you feel when the blue zone is closing in normally, but your character keeps walking in place like Tracer, is immense. The optimization is also pretty poor, and the fact that certain graphic options (foliage, shadows) directly affect balance is a serious problem. Another issue is the sound. In a game where sound whoring has to be the main focus, the spatial awareness of sound is way too terrible. When you get ambushed by gunfire, it's damn hard to figure out where the enemy is based on the gunshot sounds, and you can't really tell exactly where an enemy is just by hearing footsteps either. Walking on carpet making dirt footsteps sounds is just a bonus (not sure if it's a bug). [b][u]Since it's still Early Access...[/u][/b] However, the devs are aware of the flaws above and other minor issues and have promised patches as quickly as possible, so I think we can still look forward to it. One thing is for sure, though: the game itself is a lot of fun. The joy of getting good loot, the thrill of stabbing an unsuspecting enemy in the back and downing someone in urban combat, the relief of barely escaping the restricted zone, the emptiness of getting caught off guard, and the euphoria of seeing your record land you near the top. I think this fun is the driving force that keeps me enjoying PUBG. Can you survive? Welcome. To Battlegrounds. translation_en: If I had known about this before it came out, I wouldn't have bought H1Z1: King of the Kill (which I bought not too long ago). Now about PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS itself :) I consider this game the best Battle Royale representative at the moment! I didn't play the Arma mods, but I played H1Z1, and I also used to have high hopes for The Culling, which, alas, didn't pan out :с The combat system in this game is done really well. First of all, the fights are dynamic, in my opinion. And the gunplay itself is done very well, there is no hardcore RNG in the shots. Plus, there's a big selection of weapons and, most importantly, you can modify them! Put all sorts of attachments, scopes, extended mags, and so on. This was a very pleasant surprise and I loved it :) About vehicles. There's plenty of vehicle presence and variety in this game, and most importantly, these damn vehicles handle pretty well. The map is huge too. I don't know the exact size, read somewhere that it's 8x8 km (might be wrong). The main thing is that there's plenty of room to roam, and the terrain itself is diverse: forests, clearings, rivers, towns, countryside, beauty :3 though... the forests aren't very dense here (hear the camper crying). Plus, we choose the spot to parachute ourselves: at one end of the map, the other, or right in the middle. Small thing, but nice :3 And you can plan some kind of tactics while falling :D At the end of a match, you get coins. The coins themselves are free and you get them no matter what (hope it stays that way). And with the coins you can open crates containing cosmetic items that transform your character (or at the very least you can dump them on the Steam Community Market :3). The only downside to this game is optimization! (Though, probably nobody is surprised by that nowadays). Initially, the game set me to high settings, I was happy at first because even in the menu I had 60 fps. Started the game, fps dropped to 45. "Well, tolerable," I thought, but it got worse. The fps started dropping horribly to 18-25, I had to set everything to low quality and make do with what I have (basically, even on low the game looks quite nice). Although, if you believe the developer news, the first few months they're gonna be working precisely on optimization and an update should drop in April that will get rid of these wild fps drops. The game should run more stably too, so we wait, believe, and hope :) I definitely recommend buying this game! It just came out in Early Access, but it already has everything your heart desires (except optimization). So if you have "sensitive eyes" (only high settings and stable fps), I advise holding off on buying for now and waiting for future updates. But if the gameplay itself and the thrill of the game matter to you, go ahead and buy it! It's worth it :) ---------------------------------------------------------------- (08/07/2017) Well. A few months have passed and I want to say that they are actually working on the game. The graphics got better, optimization was tweaked, now I play with nice graphics at 50-60 fps, which is very pleasing, they brought in new animations, cases, and cosmetic items. The devs are sticking really well to their update roadmap and the game is genuinely getting better and better. Anyway, I'm glad I bought the game. That rare case when buying an Early Access game wasn't a waste :3 -------------------------------------------------------------- (30/09/2017) I noticed a second wave of angry negative reviews and for the second time most of these reviews are because the game servers started crashing. Guys, are you serious? I love people who write reviews like this :) If they like the game and it works fine, everyone stays silent and plays instead of writing a decent review. But if suddenly something breaks, that's it, everyone awakens their inner angry reviewer and furiously starts writing a negative review about what a piece of shit the game is... Guys, DON'T BE LIKE THAT! ---------------------------------------------------------------- (21/12/2017) RELEASE OF VERSION 1.0 Well, the game is finally out (although many tried hard to prove it would never release and would just be eternal Early Access). What conclusions can I draw? The game has been very well polished: a new map was added, parkour, new weapons, all sounds and the UI in the game have been remade, vehicles look different too, the graphics got a noticeable upgrade and at the same time optimization became much better (so you get it, right? graphics are cooler, fps is higher — just a fairy tale). Basically, it feels like playing a totally different game and the positive vibes from playing have increased) BUT! Minor (and for some not so minor) bugs remained, some people rage at them, and some find them funny (like me :)), so be careful :D ---------------------------------------------------------------- 21/06/2018 SITUATION IS GETTING WORSE Anyway, things are pretty sad now: no content (cases don't count), events are meh, optimization is added then removed (tired of tweaking settings, one day I'm playing on medium-high, the next on low-medium), they haven't even added any new modes... The new small map "Sanhok" and the battle pass with rewards are coming out soon, I hope the situation improves.

translation_en: Hello! My first impressions after about 7 hours of playtime: Parachute on and let's go! POSITIVE: - Relatively fast matchmaking. Mostly under 1 minute. - Camping is getting harder and harder because the moving blue zone makes constant movement and/or repositioning necessary. - Terrain detail / shaders / graphics in general are nice to look at. - Mostly smooth gameplay. - Duo/Squad team-ups. It's way more fun to get thrown into a random bunch of like-minded people. (Unless you already brought friends along) - Vehicles are quick to learn how to steer with a little bit of practice. - Vehicles like the Dacia, Jeep, and even a boat are steerable and can be found all over the game world. - Huge variety of weapons. Besides the AKM, M16, M416, Uzi, UMP, pistols, and shotguns, there are also various hunting rifles and sniper rifles, though all of them only reach their devastating potential once you slap the right attachments on them. - In general, there are many different ways to modify your weapons with attachments you find. NEUTRAL: - Grass textures very often clip into houses and onto other flat surfaces. This means pixelated shadow textures form inside houses and shelters. This definitely needs improvement so it doesn't ruin the realistic playground. - Teammates without microphones = unfortunately still a widespread problem, just like in other MMO/Survival games. If your squad or team partners can't give out warnings, it frequently leads to a team wipe. - Controls. It takes some instruction just to figure out how to aim properly. By the time I figured out how to use my red dots and stuff, I had already suffered through quite a few painful rounds. For me, it's a double right-click on the mouse. Of course, you mustn't forget that at ranges of 100+ meters you have to aim differently to get the lead to hit your target. - The equipment crates you can buy in the start menu can be bought with score points. Maybe the price difference to the previous crate should be a bit smaller. (NOT P2W!!!!) NEGATIVE: - Footsteps. It makes no sense that I'm still making a goddamn racket when I crouch-walk. This definitely needs to be adjusted! - Sounds in general - weapon sounds are good, but the noise a car makes, as well as the supply drop, are definitely way too loud and mess with the gameplay. Plus, you can hear a car from over 500 meters away. This needs better balancing. - Some game crashes even with plenty of hardware power. (8gb gpu / 16gb ram / hexacore 3.8ghz) CONCLUSION: If you're looking for a game where you can test your skills against other players in looting, tactics, aiming, shooting, and more, this is the absolute right place for you. It's also a blast to team up with your gaming buddies and wipe out an enemy squad before your whole team accidentally gets into a car crash where everyone dies. ;D Seriously though, it's genuinely one of the few Early Access games that has insane potential. I'm sticking with it, it's a lot of fun. Therefore: CLEAR BUY RECOMMENDATION FROM ME Suggestion: It would be nice to have a shooting range where you can try out all the different weapons without having to play PvP. EDIT 30.03.2017 The first big update is here and really addresses the adjustments demanded by the gaming community - here's a look at the patch notes: Week 1 Patch Notes This patch will be deployed for both clients and servers Thursday, March 30, 5PM KST/1AM PDT/8AM UTC Out-game Added Oceanian & South American servers Server Performance/Stability Resolved an issue where game server performance would degrade over time Resolved several server crash issues Client Stability Resolved several client crash issues Client Optimization Added View Distance setting to graphics options Gameplay Adjusted movement speed of endgame play zones Adjusted weapon sound volume in the lobby UI Removed crosshair while in a vehicle and not in the aiming state Added ability to see item durability state directly in vicinity pane Bug fixes Fixed a bug with the volume of crouch walking Partially addressed performance degradation when opening inventory Fixed a problem which would allow characters to go under the map in certain areas Removed the depth of field effect when spectating in team-play modes. Fixed a bug with the character creation system Fixed an issue in the REVIVE system where a player would get stuck in the revive animation when the downed player died Fixed a bug which would cause the PLAYERUNKNOWN hi-top trainers to render incorrectly Fixed a bug where a character would receive damage from vehicles while behind trees/walls

Given the immensity of the map, and as happens in other games of the genre, a circular energy field will force us to move to an increasingly smaller area until only one player is left standing. translation_en: To keep it short - the game is top tier in its genre. If anyone's interested - here's a highlight reel of our noob gameplay and drunk PUBG: https://youtu.be/JtY0udkNHzo UPDATE 2018: The game has left early access. Since many people keep checking this review, here is what the devs did during early access and after release: + They actually released the game, despite prophecies of perpetual early access (a rarity these days) + 2 new maps + A shitload of guns + Custom servers + Events + Improved ballistics + Added vehicles + Russian servers + It's not Fortnite Controversial point: +/- Optimization - it's still a bit fucky, but compared to the early access launch, it's night and day. After release - feel free to rage all you want about it, but for now don't ruin the game's rating over the technical side. It's fucking obvious it needs work and let's hope the devs understand that. Pros: + Adrenaline-fueled gameplay + Graphics are nice, not without flaws, but overall very decent + Weapon attachments - red dots, compensators, grips, and other dope accessories + Vehicle physics are better than in all Ubisoft games combined + A huge amount of weapons, you can have a frying pan showdown + Gunplay is well-made, guns feel great + Huge and diverse map + A nice and convenient UI FINALLY! + Price (in rubles - compare it to other similar games and you'll realize the devs aren't greedy, the rest is just the exchange rate) Cons: Standard early access problems - optimization. i5 4570, radeon 480 - everything on high except post-processing (on medium) - mostly 50-60 fps, but there are drops to 30 when using a flashbang for example, 37-40 fps in the lobby, drops to 27-30 in the plane. None of this is critical, but it'd be better without it) - Laggy servers, though not constantly - Items don't always pick up on the first try, rubberbanding, etc. - Price (in Euros - a bit pricey for EA) CONCLUSION: Definitely the best battle royale, h1z1 doesn't even come close, and don't even get me started on the rest. translation_en: > I will share the update details at the very bottom of my review < I participated in the game's beta tests and what I will say is that even though the game just came out, it made a great entry and made us happy. The game turned out better than I expected, in a bit I will give recommendations, and examples of positive and negative aspects. - Getting into the game is really easy, you can log in very quickly, find a server and start playing. It doesn't have the constant next next next and waiting around like in h1z1. - The lobby is a small island with weapons, no cars etc., which I don't think is necessary anyway, the game starts fast. - Everyone starts in a plane, the plane moves along a certain route on the map, you can jump out of the plane wherever you want. - For the sake of realism, picking up items on the ground takes a little long, the character bends down and picks it up from the ground, which is actually nice but puts you in a tight spot during combat. - The game takes up around 15 GB, the size you need to download is 8.7 GB. Recommendations - Don't worry, you won't crash into the ground if you don't open your parachute after jumping from the plane :) it opens by itself after a certain distance. - Controls / Z go prone / C crouch / F pick up item on ground / B change weapon mode - If you hold down right-click while holding a weapon, weapon recoil decreases, but you slow down. If you click right-click once, the game switches to first-person fps mode. - Attachments can be added to weapons, red dot- holo scope / extended mag / 4x-8x scopes etc. If you find attachments, don't forget to add them to your weapons. Positive Aspects (+) - As much as the game resembles h1z1, the way aiming works is similar to ArmA, and this feature really feels like you are comfortably hitting the opponent. - When you turn the graphics to max, they are actually as good as you wouldn't imagine, but since there are optimization issues right now, you can't play stably on high settings. - Server conditions are good, no ping spikes etc. occur. - Apart from the gas release outside the circle on the map, red zones appear and those areas get bombed, this is a good method for elimination, cars and sound effects are really good. - You can swim in the game and there are speedboats, this was something that really needed to be in it. Negative Aspects (-) - Optimization issues have been largely fixed, but I suppose they will be fixed even more. - The gas in the final area deals too much damage. - I think more than 100 people should be able to enter the matches because the matches end very slowly and you get bored due to the low player count. Because there are few people, airdrops are also few. - Some close-range weapons (shotguns) deal high damage to distant opponents too, I suppose this will be fixed. I started translating the game's page into Turkish so you can get information about the game faster. I will edit my review every time the game gets an update. ---> Thanks for reading. // Last edit 11.12.2017 //

translation_en: I think this is one of those rare successful moments when someone tries to make a clone of an already existing game! Yeah, I know that the whole thing originally started as an Arma mod, but the mode settled into H1Z1 really well, the guys implemented everything pretty well and got people genuinely interested in their game and this mode. I played the H1Z1 battle royale enough and I liked everything about it, for me it was a very interesting game to kill time in a cool way. Just recently before PUBG came out, I found out about it as yet another battle royale game on the way. After watching a couple of reviews, I realized I was interested and wanted to buy this game. After release I realized my purchase was WORTH IT! Next up, I'm gonna compare it to H1Z1 since it's now its main competitor: - First off, graphically PUBG is a much prettier game, reminds me a lot of Arma 3 (personally), looks great! - Secondly, the character movement and shooting mechanics here are WAAAAAY nicer, - Thirdly, there's a ton of diverse weapons and different cars (even boats), whereas during all of H1Z1's existence they only managed to add the AK47... and that's it. A couple of vehicles and 3 types of weapons is definitely cool for several years of H1Z1's existence. - Moving on: you can put all sorts of attachments on weapons, the interface is way more convenient, picking up weapons or swapping helmets/body armor is way handier than in H1Z1 (though I'm still waiting for design tweaks). The feature where you choose yourself when to jump out of the plane onto the map is also interesting (don't know if that was a thing in the Arma mod). Overall, I think this is a genuinely SUCCESSFUL battle royale game. If you've been wondering whether to get H1Z1 or not, forget about it! Get PUBG and don't sweat it, it's an awesome battle royale that I'm sure will actively develop and get even better. I can't say anything bad about optimization, the game runs fine for me, averaging 55-60 fps. I know many people complain, so look into that yourselves. Thanks for reading my opinion, hope it helps someone when buying the game. Good luck everyone!

translation_en: I took part in all the Closed Beta weekends, so I think I can already add some kind of review. PLAYERUNKNOWN'S BATTLEGROUNDS (PUBG) has quickly claimed the top spot in the Battle Royale genre. It's no wonder at all, because standing behind this project is PLAYERUNKNOWN himself, aka the god of Battle Royale games. Everyone knows that this genre first came with him in ARMA, and then he also worked on the "competitor" H1Z1: KotK. Unfortunately, H1Z1: KotK went a different way and compared to PUBG the game feels arcade-like. The PUBG developers stick more to the ARMA style, which means more simulation than arcade. The game contains relatively fast action for this genre and gunfights feel very professional and satisfying. So few games offer you such a good feeling for killing another player or even winning the whole match. [b]Pros:[/b] + More simulation than arcade + Beautiful weapon and ambient sounds + Excellently modeled weapons + Content (clothing, weapons, cars) already offers more than the competition in an extremely short time + Spectate mode (the competition can only be jealous again) + The game can be played solo, with a friend in duo mode, or best of all in the so-called SQUAD mode. In this mode you can play in up to 4 players and the fun is multiplied many times over + Developers who know how to use what they have on their shoulders + PLAYERUNKNOWN [b]Cons:[/b] - The game is in the first phase of Early Access, so optimization is lagging behind, but since the right people are taking care of the game, I believe that with every update it will be noticeably better and better - Sounds regarding their position, where shots are coming from, etc., still need a few tweaks, because often it's really hard to tell where the shots are coming from and whether they're shooting at you or not - Currently, due to the extreme rush of players, servers are relatively overloaded (logically), so you can run into occasional lags There would be much more to say and the review could be even more extensive, but I got tired of writing. :D I hope this review helps newcomers decide on buying the game.
