translation_en: 1. Better not touch cases. (This kind of luck-based shit is just like gambling, once you start opening them you just can't stop. Unless you think you're God's favorite, you'd better stay away from cases and just buy skins the normal way!) 2. The XP needed to level up is fixed. No matter what level you are, it's always a flat 5,000 points per level. Every weekly rank-up gives you a random drop, either a graffiti (which has limited charges) or a weapon skin, though they're mostly worthless, and you only get one per week. Once you hit level 40, you can prestige, reset back to level 1, and you'll get that year's Service Medal. For example, if you hit max level and prestige in 2017, you get the 2017 Service Medal. Basically, the medal is just for flexing. 3. Balance. I don't even need to explain this one—skins give zero stat boosts, so you don't have to worry about running into any pay-to-win whales. 4. CTs and Ts both have their own faction-exclusive weapons, like the CT's M4A1 and the T's AK-47. (I'm only mentioning this to clown on my noob friend who grabbed me and asked why CTs can't buy an AK-47 and Ts can't buy an M4A1. Honestly, I'm gonna roast him for this for a whole year, lmao.) 5. You can play Competitive as soon as level 2 now, and placement matches don't just make you play 10 games—they make you *win* 10 games. Only after 10 wins are your placements complete. Every 2 wins, your Competitive matchmaking gets locked and you can't play, which is the game evaluating your skill level based on those 2 wins and your previous losses. Once the cooldown ends, you can play Comp again. Only after finishing your placements can you play Comp to your heart's content! 6. You gotta watch out for random strangers. translation_en: Since the last update (07.12.18) the whole community has basically jumped with anger. Valve made changes to their game, namely a new mode - danger zone, as well as switching to f2p. While introducing a new mode is spot on, the second change is a shot in the foot. If this doesn't change, I give this game a month to live at most from today. From now on, when a cheater gets banned, they lose nothing, just 10 minutes to make a new account and then boom, all over again. To me, this is some kind of unfunny joke from Valve. On prime servers, which are paid, it will still be possible to play normally, though on free servers it's going to be a total massacre. A new player downloading the game and entering it for the first time will see tons of shit and the cream of the community, and after 3 hours of playing they'll have had enough. It probably won't encourage them to buy the game, only scare them off. This move would make sense if the anti-cheat caught cheaters faster than they can create accounts, or if it banned computers instead of accounts. I secretly believe this is some 200iq bait to catch all the cheaters because I don't want what used to be undisputedly the best game on the market to die in such a way, I'd love to be able to help but barely anything gets through to Valve. Introducing danger zone is a bullseye. Players wanted a 180° change so they got it, and yet 90% of them are complaining. Obviously nobody would return to the game just for a tickrate change to 128. Everyone would hop in, play 3 matches, decide there's no difference and out. Source 2 would be better, although introducing it requires a lot of time and thought, but the coming month might be the best time for it. An operation would give Valve profit and also joy to players who would play more than just one ranked game a month to keep their rank. That's why I'm surprised we still don't have a new operation in the game, it seems pointless to me, but I guess uncle Gabe knows better. In its history CS has been through many ups and even more downs, and maybe we are witnessing the final one. Players left after the release of pubg, fortnite and also after the market changes, but sooner or later they always came back. I hope it will be similar now and that one update will put this game back on its feet. It's hard for me to judge whether I recommend this game or not. Overall yes, but after recent events no. The next month will be very important and all we can do is wait. Let's hope it's not the end because it's kind of stupid to lose everything over such an ill-considered and stupid move. To sum it up, yes, I recommend this game, I recommend logging in and playing at least the new mode, especially since this is practically the last chance for normal CS. We'll see in a month

translation_en: **[b][h1]Let me tell you a story;[/h1][/b] Back when I was sweating my ass off trying to reach DMG... Every time I finally hit DMG, boom, there's a cheater in the lobby, or my rank gets wiped just because I didn't play for 2 days (for reasons I still don't get). I kept deranking until I just gave up caring. Now, while I was still trying hard to stay in DMG, I met a Global Elite. Gotta give credit where it's due, he was a really cool guy to talk to. We queued up and played together, and thanks to him I made it to LE. Time went by, we had a friendly chatty relationship for about a month or so. By the way, he had a crazy amount of hours, a ton of pins, and even 8 knives—over 20,000 TL worth of skins. One day I was spectating his game, looked closely, and honestly it kinda looked like cheats, but since I wasn't that great of a player myself, I figured I shouldn't judge him :) While we were chatting in private, I joked that he played like a cheater, and he just laughed. I joined his next game as a spectator again, and I thought to myself, "Yeah, he's definitely cheating." Anyway, I casually dropped a hint in chat, joking around that he must be cheating because it was impossible, stuff like that. He said, "Yeah, I'm using cheats, they have 'VAC Ban Protection'." I reacted like, "What the hell, how does that even work?" He told me the name, if I remember right it was a cheat called "ATOM". Anyway, I said, "Aren't you worried about your hours and all those items, what happens if you get banned?" He said, "No way I'll ever get banned, it's a very advanced cheat." I was still mind-blown, so I went to the cheat's website (might be remembering the name wrong, but it was a Turkish cheat site) and checked it out. Lifetime access was like 100 TL or something. I hit up live support and asked, "What is this VAC Ban protection?" and they started explaining: "It's a cheat with fully professional in-game awareness. If you can see an enemy's location and go kill them, it tells you whether it'll look like cheating or not. For example, if the enemy made a tiny sound, but nobody with normal settings or an average headset could have heard it, and you use Wallhack to go kill them, it's fine. The cheat tells you when you're allowed to shoot, but if something like that [suspicious scenario] happens, the cheat pops up a warning telling you *not* to shoot." Stuff like that. I told him to go fuck himself and logged off. Anyway, sending my regards to the Valve family. I also sometimes wonder why the hell I still play despite all this. I'm someone who really values time, and I can't even tell you how much I miss those 30-40 minutes wasted every time a cheater ruins a match. I just hope they step up the solutions, even just a little bit, for this game we inexplicably and unconditionally love, so we can finally play in peace. So yeah, that's my story...

translation_en: Counter-Strike: Global Offensive is the best fps game, it's both so fucking awesome and totally fucked up. Up to 1000 hours played it'll bring you joy, the only thing that might annoy you sometimes are trolls and underage players who claim they are fucking you, your mother, father, girlfriend, dog, cat, hamster, and anything else closer related to you that is a living creature. These professional "fuckers" unfortunately fuck everyone, despite the fact that the only place they've dipped their little dick is in a cola bottle. If you get through this period, pass those magical 1000 hours and decide that yes, this is your calling and you want to achieve something more in it, your first goal will be to hit global. You'll spend hundreds or maybe even thousands of hours playing the most serious 5v5 matchmaking in the world, which will fully show you what team play is all about. Yes, team play. After some time of running around the map together with 4 retards picked for you by the system, you'll start muting them right from the start of the match, going everywhere by yourself to avoid magical flashes in your face and constant blocking in every situation from your boosted teammates. Wanting to take over a given bomb site on the way to winning the match, you'll have to take out every enemy on it by yourself, plant the bomb and defend it too, same goes for retaking. Your team in the meantime will be waiting somewhere in the distance admiring the beautiful textures and skins, occasionally calling out some info, fake info, then so you can show off even more, they'll drop like flies chasing a frag, giving you a chance to hit an ACE or lose the round. With each passing day of combat, you'll start to learn the reality that playing so-called mms is just plain rank farming. If you're good, you're just good, because whether in silvers or globals, it's just retarded FFA 5v5 running around the map and you won't find advanced tactics or full info here, just fucking flame on the way to rushing A or B. Just like with each passing day you'll start to meet a mass of talented young players who don't have more than 200 hours played on their profiles and will still be better than you. Their gamesense, prediction, aim, is sometimes greater than top 10 HLTV pro players. You will meet them in every match, because there are more and more of them and there will only be more. 70% of the time, these talented players end their careers on those accounts within 1/2 months, when a message suddenly appears on their profile - 1 VAC ban registered. The game's developer of course does literally everything, daily updates, new cases, skins, putting bunny ears or pumpkins on chickens, all just so you can finally see that they don't give a fuck, and CS:GO is starting to resemble its predecessor 1.6, where on every server you'll find more cheaters than slots on it. Wait! It's not like that after all! Valve introduces non-prime and prime! Awesome! It looks like this: on non-prime, 90% of matches are cheaters playing against cheaters, and on prime you'll find them a little less. Instead of eliminating them, the developer prefers to throw them into another bag. Over time, the rank system becomes more and more ruined and meaningless, because it is no longer an indicator of anything. Not everyone cheats, but in every match regardless of the level you will encounter a complete mix of skills, at low ranks you will play against globals with golds, and at higher ranks you will play with golds against globals, because you will never get a smurf or a competent player in your team, just boosted fucking pieces of shit. The charm of our beloved game is added to by the fact that we have to blow some cash on hardware otherwise we can forget about any goals. Anyone who thinks hardware doesn't matter is an idiot. A person with normal fps + a 144hz monitor might be way worse in skill than you, but if you're hovering around 60 unstable fps on a normal monitor, they're going to have way too much of an advantage over you despite your skills. With each update the game's fluidity decreases, which is already so annoying that you don't even want to play it anymore, because it should be the other way around. If the gameplay itself hasn't convinced you yet, you can think about collecting skins, flexing with them in front of others and showing off how awesome you are because you have some pink bayoneted knife and everyone gets a hard-on at the sight of a regular pixelated skin sometimes worth more than your 4-month income. You can of course make nothing out of nothing, go the gambling route, only if you get lucky and don't sell it in time, the next day you'll blow everything, because every game of chance is constructed so that a moment like that will come, even if it seems unreal, it will happen 100%. If I've convinced you with my opinion about this game, the whole community, you can go on grinding your high rank, preferably getting 5 frags per match and only looking for people to carry you, because a promotion will satisfy you more than your mediocre gameplay which you won't do shit with anyway, because according to you what you have on your profile defines how you play. In the future, I'll surely run into you and once again you'll make me realize not to play matchmaking with a bunch of retards on a 64 tickrate, because the wonderful ranking system places you in such a way that if I want to win, I have to hit an ACE every round while additionally playing against magical new accounts, because in my team out of 100 played games I don't have the honor of getting any once. Fortunately, I don't care about it, because for me winning some tournament, taking some good place, having a lot of knowledge about CS and improving my gameplay every day on a pathetic 50 fps is an achievement, not some rank that's just a picture.

translation_en: Good day to you, dear Steam users and CS:GO players. I’m writing this review from my own point of view. Whether you agree or not is up to you. I hope my review helps at least someone :). So, let's begin. An interesting, cool time-waster (evidently not just wasting time, but your nerves too). We have two sides: Counter-Terrorists (basically SWAT), and the terrorists themselves. We can choose either team. Then the actual action starts, which I think there's no point in describing. Let me start with my criticism. Players, the community. Oh dear God, hearing this makes my heart stop. Why is that? I go into a Public server / MM (makes practically no difference), and I greet everyone. Most of the time it sounds like this - "Good evening\morning\day everyone." What do I hear in response? - "Sup b*tch" - "Fuck off" - "Shut up." Oh yeah... translation_en: This is probably the first review I've ever written, and maybe the last one too, because I'm lazy. But I'm seriously about to quit this game, so I wanted to write something. A friend recommended this game to me back when I started college, and in the end, even my friend stopped playing, leaving just two of us, including me. CS:GO isn't really popular in China; PUBG blew up, and even classmates who don't play games started trying PUBG, while the only ones still playing CS:GO were just the two of us. After the Perfect World server came out, I basically stopped playing international matchmaking. After all, the network advantage is there, and using a VPN for international servers isn't as smooth as the national server (shitty dorm Wi-Fi). But the release of the national server didn't actually make CS:GO popular. And to be blunt, the national server lowered the cost of cheating. CS:GO cheats on Taobao are dirt cheap, feel free to look it up yourself if you're interested. The national server meant cheaters didn't even have to shell out those few dozen bucks to buy the game. Today, when some motherless level 1 smurf account arrogantly told me that it only cost 3 RMB to wreck us, I just felt like there was no point anymore. I don't think anyone wants a game they love to be disrespected so recklessly, where the effort you put in isn't even worth 3 RMB, not even worth a bottle of Coke. I came from CrossFire, and back then my fastest typing speed was practiced from flaming cheaters. To be honest, one of the reasons I played CS:GO was because I ran into cheaters less often, and it wasn't as frustrating. Today, I was genuinely completely disgusted. In Casual, I ran into two or three cheaters on the other team. At least they tried to hide it a little bit, though their acting was so pathetic I won't even mention it. By the second map, most of the cheaters left, except for the top guy on the other team who immediately started rage-hacking—using a Krieg 553 to wallbang lock, smoke lock, face-to-face snap lock, talking trash the whole time: "Yeah, I'm cheating, report me," and all sorts of other nonsense about destroying us. Judging by his voice, he wasn't a kid either. He's a motherless, unraised asshole, so I won't say anything else. CS:GO's casual kick system is interesting—you can only kick players on your own team, whereas in CrossFire, VIPs could vote-kick across teams. So I had to join the cheater's team to vote and kick him, and it was all F2 (no), not a single F1 (yes). It instantly reminded me of those days in CrossFire; it seems the gaming environment for Chinese FPS games is just like this. I won't say things like "the quality of Chinese players is low" because that easily invites hate, but the current state of the national server environment is pretty much just like this. Right, one of the cheater's teammates had a level 2 2018 Service Medal. With 100 profile ranks, you'd think he knows right from wrong, but after three rounds of watching him stay silent and rim the cheater's asshole just to get a happy little win, it made me sick to my stomach. It’s a bit disgusting to say, but with 100 ranks, that’s his level of character. Looking at my own matching Service Medal, I almost want to delete the damn thing. What's the point of playing for so long? It's not even worth 3 RMB, not worth a bottle of Coke. One of the cheater's teammates typed in all-chat: "Carried to a win, I love it." Yeah, sure, whatever floats your boat. In the third round, I went to the other team again to vote-kick. Thanks to a bunch of newly joined players, we finally kicked the cheater out. Yay, congratulations. I won't even mention how many people voted no this time, I just won't mention it. Finally, I wish all CS:GO players a pleasant gaming experience (motherless cheaters excluded). I won't ramble too much about what the gaming experience and environment are like; I guess everyone already knows. If you're cheating, your experience must be awesome, while the other team's experience... well, if everyone cheats, the gaming environment... alright, I'll stop there. PUBG has a pretty interesting urban legend where cheaters get matched with more cheaters; a "War of the Gods" is actually a lot of fun. I'll just wait and see when CS:GO ever reaches that kind of spectacle.

translation_en: It's not just a game, it's a state of mind. CS originally started as a Half-Life mod. It caused quite a stir among players back then, and eventually Valve just hired the mod creators and made CS an official Valve product. I still remember back before CF (CrossFire) came out, internet cafes were filled with either Legend of Mir, Warcraft, or a bunch of people playing CS. After CF came out, CS slowly faded out of Chinese gamers' sight. In 2011, CS:GO burst onto the scene, breathing new life into this old franchise. Honestly, I've played a lot of shooters—that demolition game (R6 Siege), farming and fighting in the fields (Battlefield), phone of duty (Call of Duty), hackers' unknown battlegrounds (PUBG)... I'd get super into them at first, but slowly lose interest, and after coming full circle, I always end up back at CS. A friend once asked me, "You play CS:GO all day, how do you keep going?" To be honest, I don't know how I keep going either. Every time the music kit kicks in at the start of a round, for some reason my blood just starts pumping, and before I know it, I've finished a whole match. Later I thought about it: "Maybe it's the power of nostalgia." CS was my gateway FPS game. Back then I didn't know how to play online, so playing against bots every day was still a blast. Later I found out about some platform and went on there to play online, starting off by getting absolutely wrecked in various deathmatches. Then I switched over to playing CF (since everyone around me was playing it at the time). Later CF started releasing all these "flashy" guns and screaming squeakers, and right around then I found out about CS:Source—the great physics engine, the graphics that blew people away back then. I didn't even know what a legit copy was back then, I just downloaded a cracked version straight to play online on a platform. Played it for about half a year, and then got dragged back by friends to play various online games. The first time I heard about CS:GO was when its esports tournament showed up on TV. I really wanted to play it, and that was also when I found out about Steam. But then I found out it cost money, and since I had zero concept of buying legit games back then, I just didn't buy it. Went right back to comparing dicks in domestic online games. Now, I'm back. Walking past that familiar mid doors, slowly creeping up A-short. So many memories.

translation_en: After a long time in the CS:GO community, I'd like to share my opinion here. I've made a list of pros and cons. Let's start with the good stuff. Pros: - You can make money through in-game items (that do NOT change the gameplay), like weapon skins, cases, etc. (This is completely optional and nobody forces you to do it) - Maps from the classics like de_inferno or de_dust2 are still around (new textures etc., but still the same map) - There are custom servers (Community servers/Dedicated servers) - There is an active community with lots of German players too - Compared to the predecessors, there are new game modes, whether you like them or not is up to you (they aren't under pros for nothing in my case) - The game gets regular updates that result in a functioning game and actually make sense - A lot of attention to detail - The community can decide on suspected cheaters themselves with enough matchmaking wins - You can like "Operations" or not (allows for new maps and weapons etc.) Cons: - Hackers are rarely kicked in matchmaking because they win the game for people - Few maps in the new game modes (Workshop maps not included) - Every now and then you run into hardcore cheaters who ruin the game - Some bugs exist, but they get fixed quickly (pixelwalk etc.) - The servers run on 64-tick, so some actions aren't registered properly - New recoil patterns etc. annoy hardcore veterans Conclusion: I bought the game at full price and haven't regretted it for a single second. For a Counter-Strike fan from day one, it'll definitely take some getting used to, but everyone will find something to enjoy here. Thanks for your attention, I'd appreciate a rating.

translation_en: CS:GO is hands down my absolute favorite game, no exceptions. My PC is pretty trash and can't run any of the popular games out there. I bought OW, bought PUBG, tried out R6, and Dead by Daylight back then too, but even on the lowest settings I only got around 20fps, so I ended up having to refund or quit all of them. Then by chance I came across CS:GO, and thanks to the 1.6 nostalgia from back in elementary school, I picked it up really fast. With my unstable 60fps PC, I managed to grind to 1,500 elo on 5EPlay (though honestly I could've gone higher!). As a student, and one from a strictly middle-class family, at first I never planned on spending real money on this game, let alone opening cases. Next thing I know, my AK goes from Poverty-Spec to Redline, and then to Asiimov; the M4 goes from The Emperor to Buzz Kill; the AWP goes from Worm God to Atheris; the USP from Torque to Next Level to Kill Confirmed; the Deagle from Bronze Deco to Printstream (still wanna get that Light Rail red Deagle sometime). The only regret is that I still don't have a knife, even a cheap one. [spoiler]I just couldn't f***ing help it! They look so damn good! Definitely not buying any more after this, inventory locked for good. F***ing classic.[/spoiler] Thinking back, that Silver life when I first started playing was so much fun—auto-snipers, shotguns, Negev, trolling with foreigners, and sometimes trash-talking Koreans or Vietnamese players. Pulling off an ace meant you could brag about it for a whole year, and winning a 1v5 meant you couldn't sleep from the hype. Now I've lost count of how many times I've done that, but honestly, the higher your rank gets, the fewer chances you even get to show off. Then the Perfect World server dropped. I originally swore I'd never touch the Chinese server, but eventually got driven away by the communication issues on the global servers. Plus, because of some issues with the CN server environment, I ended up switching to 5EPlay. Most of the friends from my starting Silver stack have drifted apart, and the ones who were meant to stay in Silver are still in Silver, sigh... Thinking about all this, it always hits me how fast time flies. It ain't that long, yet I've spent a little over a year on this game, clocking in 892 hours. But right now, I'm forced to quit this game. Because I'm a high school senior. For the next year, I won't touch it anymore. I won't care about skin price trends, new cases, skins, or new operations. I won't care about team news, whether TYLOO will finally win a championship trophy, or whether Jw1 (Scream) will still be throwing every single round...... Sigh. Next year after the Gaokao (college entrance exam), I'm getting a new PC and making a push for 2,000 elo! Hope my friends will still be waiting for me! Wish me good luck on my exams! See you in the jianghu! Good luck with the Gaokao!

translation_en: 2023/9/28 Twenty years to sharpen a sword, just waiting for today! [This was the first game I ever bought, and I'm only just leaving a review now...] Back then the Chinese server wasn't out yet, and every time I had to play competitive with over 200 ping and 40% packet loss, which naturally meant getting vote-kicked by high-class players from Southeast Asia and certain island countries and regions, sometimes even getting trade-banned from matchmaking. It was hopeless and helpless, but it still didn't stop me and my friends from experiencing the unique joy it brought. "Standing in the smoke on Dust 2 A-long, mowing down two guys on A-site and a sniper in pit with a Negev." That was my first 1v3 clutch, and I was happy all night, thinking at the time: This really is a great game, 45 RMB was totally worth it. [Yet that 45 RMB was just a microtransaction entry fee] Later, the Chinese server was announced. I bought an activation code, queued duo with my friends at an internet café, communication was so much easier, latency and packet loss were basically gone, and the officials even designed two sticker capsules specifically for the Chinese server, so touching. When the Chinese server actually launched, it became a free-to-play game. I didn't really look into whatever that 88 RMB buy-to-play thing was, but anyway, it was free to play now. I started to worry about the existence of little squeakers; after all, back then 45 RMB was just enough to act as a ticket to properly keep the kids out, would making it directly free... Turns out that worry was unnecessary. The environment for Chinese players in CS:GO is actually pretty good, with basically no one screaming music down the mic the whole time or flaming people in public chat. Sometimes the fun of awkward small talk and bantering with random teammates even surpassed the anti-terrorist gameplay itself, something you could never do on international servers. However, an even more severe issue happened------the handling of cheaters on the Chinese server. Yeah, every game has cheaters, but when cheaters don't get the punishment they deserve, it just lets more cheaters run rampant. From wallhacks at the very start, to aimbots, to spinbots, and now even instant bomb-defuse hacks. Maybe because I'm pretty trash, I haven't run into such high-level cheats in Competitive mode, but in Casual, especially Wingman, cheaters are just way too out of control. The hatred for cheaters has made a lot of normally decent veteran players impatient, and some CS:GO public communities have just turned into places to dox cheaters' IDs. Let's keep it factual: whether this guy is cheating has nothing to do with their anime profile picture, nor which province they're from. Some internet scum in these communities even use our hatred for cheaters to provoke regional discrimination and generalising, which just adds to the chaos of the public communities. Of course, online discourse has its own logic, I won't get into that. I just hope the game developers and publishers actually take players' thoughts into consideration, properly step up the anti-cheat, and make VAC no longer stand for "Valve Allow Cheat", but Valve Anti-Cheat. I hope you'll actually read my first long review, thanks. PS: The 7-day trade lock on skins is fucking retarded

translation_en: After a long time in the CS:GO community, I'd like to share my opinion here. I've made a list of pros and cons. Let's start with the good stuff. Pros: - You can make money through in-game items (that do NOT change the gameplay), like weapon skins, cases, etc. (This is completely optional and nobody forces you to do it) - Classic maps like de_inferno or de_dust2 are still around (new textures etc., but still the same map) - There are custom servers (community servers/dedicated servers) - There's an active community with lots of Germans around - Compared to the predecessors there are new game modes, whether you like them or not is up to you (there's a reason I put them under pros) - The game gets regular updates that result in a working game and actually make sense - A lot of attention to detail - The community can decide on suspected cheaters themselves with enough matchmaking wins - "Operations" - you may or may not like them (they introduce new maps and weapons etc.) Cons: - Hackers are rarely kicked in matchmaking because they win the game for people - Few maps in the new game modes (Workshop maps not included) - Every now and then you run into hardcore cheaters who ruin the game - Some bugs exist, but they get fixed quickly (pixelwalk etc.) - The servers run on 64-tick, so some actions aren't registered properly - New recoil patterns etc. annoy hardcore veterans Conclusion: I bought the game at full price and haven't regretted it for a second. For a Counter-Strike fan from day one, it will definitely take some getting used to, but everyone will find their fun here. Thanks for your attention, and I'd appreciate a rating.

There are no relevant laws or regulations to determine whether a game passes review. There was once a domestic single-player game developer that made a wuxia game and submitted it for review. And what do the relevant Chinese departments claim their basis is when reviewing? It's the so-called social mainstream ideology; it's the Socialist Core Values. What is this kind of like? I'm speaking with a clear conscience, whereas they aren't necessarily doing the same. I hope everyone spreads these words. I know that nine times out of ten it won't do shit, but how can you refuse to shout just because your voice is small? As an ordinary resident living in China, I love Steam, and I love the joy Steam brings me. This is all I can do. Thank you, everyone. Actually, being a docile subject has zero upside and all downsides. Because if you show obedience, they need to provide you with even less. translation_en: So, I'm gonna speak my mind. A massive amount of problems completely overshadow all the positives. Let's start by listing the main flaws: 1. Cheaters. 2. Hit registration issues. 3. Terrible matchmaking. 4. Non-working anti-cheat. 5. Bans for no reason. 6. The developers' attitude towards the players. ... Yeah, the list is long. And now one by one ↓. Cheaters: Almost every game you'll run into a cheater with an empty profile that only has one game on it. While back in the day you'd occasionally find normal players with decent profiles among them, nowadays absolutely every player who plays suspiciously has a zeroed-out profile with a single game. It’s sketchy, and for good reason. They don't ban for cheats here, judging by how many of them there are. Heck, a guy can literally join right into a game and start advertising cheats. You're walking crouched, making no noise, and BOOM, an enemy pops out, already knowing where you are, and kills you. You're heading towards a win with your team and suddenly, the enemy gets salty, turns on cheats and you lose. Maybe he'll get banned someday, but the match is already over and your time is wasted. This just makes you wanna puke, I'm putting this problem at number one on the list. Shooting players: An equally annoying phenomenon is when you shoot a player, they are right in your sniper crosshairs (and not just sniper), you pull the trigger — and the bullet just flies right through without doing any damage. Meanwhile, the enemy already kills you. This just makes you endlessly pissed off and kills any desire to play. Involuntary gestures kick in: "What the FUCK", or the trendy: "WTF Man, r u srsly?". :D Situations like this happen in every single match, maybe that's why all players are so high-strung. :/ Matchmaking: Has gotten long. You have to wait like 5 minutes, sometimes up to 20. It just throws random garbage into your team. Turks screaming God knows what the whole game, some Poles who are also screaming, hell everyone is screaming, it's impossible to play normally. Haha, the funny thing is you can actually get a good laugh out of these guys, they pull off some crazy shit sometimes :), you don't even need to go to the zoo :). There is no sorting by country or ping, you just have to play with whoever. If you're not talkative, people will just look down on you, swear at you, and all that stuff. Get used to eating shit. Anti-cheat: Like that joke: "A guy comes in to apply for a job at a state firm. They tell him: - Well, we've got this, this, and this here (various perks, implying bribery :D), the salary is 5 grand. And he replies: - What, you guys actually pay a salary here too?". Yeah, the anti-cheat is surprisingly here. But it's apparently just for show, just for the picture. Like putting up "CCTV in operation" signs so people don't piss in the hallway. But everyone can see there are no cameras). Same with CS:GO, it's seemingly there, but you can't see it. Yeah, bans go out sometimes, but it feels like the anti-cheat has nothing to do with it, because in all my time playing I've never once seen a situation where the anti-cheat banned a cheater right in the middle of a match. BANNED? For what? For getting kicked by four swearing 9-year-old cocksuckers because you didn't clutch an ace. Bought the game, logged in to play, BAM, it freezes, kicks you to the menu. WHOOPS, a pop-up — ATTENTION ATTENTION, you've been banned. Shocking, right. This kind of thing happens too, and it's the final blow to this game's reputation. There are tons of YouTube videos showing and proving all of this. Yep, people get banned for no reason here. Still wanna play? :). How the developers treat the players: They don't even talk to the players, they just toss updates on the floor like dogs: "Here, eat up." That's how arrogant the attitude is. No news, everything just happens spontaneously. They don't listen to the players at all, they just do whatever the fuck they want. It's just straight-up disrespectful. Conclusion: Is it even worth listing the pros if there are this many problems? I think not, so I won't. Terrible anti-cheat, cheaters, bullets not killing!!!, all of these are such obvious things to every CS:GO player that you can't help but laugh. I am just mind-boggled by this game. Hope this review was fun, useful, and informative, and that you'll close the CS:GO store page and find yourself something normal. Don't play this piece of shit, save your time, nerves, energy, and money (70 rubles on sale, haha, it's 70 now, while it used to be all 500, well it's pretty obvious how people buy the game if they run sales like that :D). UPD: I have 500 hours played in total, 78 on this account because I forgot the password to my old one :0

translation_en: Once a great game that interested many has turned into who knows what. It feels like it’s been forgotten and is only being used to milk money. A huge amount of problems outweigh all the positives. Let's start by listing the main flaws: 1. Cheaters. 2. Hitreg doesn't work. 3. Terrible matchmaking. 4. Broken anti-cheat. 5. Bans for no reason. 6. The developers' attitude towards the players. ... [h1][u]Yeah, the list is long. Now one by one[/u] ↓ [u].[/u][/h1] [h1]Cheaters:[/h1] Almost every game you'll run into a cheater with an empty profile that only has one game on it. Even though back then you could still find normal players with decent profiles among those, nowadays absolutely every player who plays "suspuriously" has a zeroed-out profile with a single game on the account. That's alarming, and for good reason. People don't get banned for cheats here, judging by how many cheaters there are. Hell, a dude can literally join right in the match and start advertising cheats. You're walking crouched, making no noise, and BANG, an enemy flies around the corner already knowing where you are and kills you. You and your team are heading for victory and suddenly the opponent gets tilted, turns on cheats and you lose. Maybe they'll get banned someday, but the match is already over and your time is wasted. This just brings total disgust, I'm putting this problem at the very top of the list. [h1]Shooting at players:[/h1] An equally annoying phenomenon when you shoot a player, they are right in your sniper crosshairs (and not just sniper), you pull the trigger — and the bullet flies right through without dealing any damage. Meanwhile, the enemy already kills you. This just makes you utterly pissed off and kills any desire to play. Involuntary gestures kick in: "What the FUCK", or fashionably: "WTF Man, r u srsly?". :D These situations happen in every single game, maybe that's why all players are so nervous. :/ [h1]Matchmaking:[/h1] Got long. You have to wait like 5 minutes, sometimes even 20. It throws random-ass people into your team. Turks screaming God knows what the whole game, some Poles who are screaming too, everybody is just screaming, it's impossible to play normally. Ahah, the funny thing is you can actually get a good laugh out of these guys, the shit they pull sometimes :), you don't even need to go to the zoo :). There's no distribution by countries or ping, you just have to play with whoever. If you're not talkative, people will just despise you, curse you out, and all that stuff. Get used to eating shit. [h1]Anti-cheat:[/h1] Just like the old joke: [i]"A guy comes in to apply for a job at a state firm. They tell him: -Well, we got this, this, and this here (various perks, implying bribery :) ), the salary is 5 grand. And he replies: -What, you guys actually pay a salary here too?"[/i] Yeah, the anti-cheat is here, surprisingly. But it's apparently just for show, to keep up appearances. Like putting up signs saying "Video surveillance in operation" so people don't piss in the hallway. But everyone can see there are no cameras). It's the same in CS:GO, it's supposedly there, but you can't see it. Yeah, bans drop sometimes, but it feels like the anti-cheat has nothing to do with it, because in all my time playing I've never experienced a single situation where the anti-cheat banned a cheater right in the middle of a match. [h1]BANNED? For what? Just because.[/h1] Bought the game, logged in to play, BOOM, it freezes, drops you to the menu. BAM, a popup window — ATTENTION ATTENTION, you have been banned. Surprising, right. This shit happens too, and it's the final blow to this game's reputation. There are tons of YouTube videos showing and proving all of this. Yes, they ban for no reason here. Still want to play? :). [h1]How the developers treat the players:[/h1] They don't even talk to the players, they just toss updates on the floor like dogs: "Here, choke on it." That's how arrogant the attitude is. No news, everything just happens spontaneously. They don't listen to players at all, they just do whatever the fuck they want. It's just straight-up disrespect. [h1][u]Conclusion:[/u][/h1] Is it even worth writing about the pros when there are so many problems? I think not, so I won't. Terrible anti-cheat, cheaters, bullets don't kill!!!, all these things are so obvious to every CS:GO player that you can't help but laugh. I am just mind-boggled by this game. I hope this review was entertaining, useful, and informative, and that you'll leave the CS:GO store page and find yourself something normal. Don't play this piece of shit, save your time, nerves, energy, and money (75 rubles on sale, haha, already 75, while it used to be all 500, well it's pretty fucking obvious how they sell the game if they do discounts like that :D ).

translation_en: Sometimes, I keep wondering, why do we play CS? Why? Let me tell you a story here. Because I liked a hardcore, extremely niche FPS game, I created a group chat. At first, there were only 9 people in it, and besides me, everyone else was an admin. Then, through our slow promotion and accumulation on Baidu Tieba and Steam, the number of people in the group gradually grew. That day, I was just planning to casually chat and bullshit in the group as usual, when the topic randomly jumped to the "beggar's edition" of Rainbow Six. In this version, if you want to unlock all the operators, you have to grind like crazy. Then, a bro said that the thing he lacked the least was the will to grind. He felt a bit tired from playing a dozen games a day, and while playing on his computer, he'd have his phone right next to him playing a mobile game. To play games, he bought 5 phones and 3 computers, and his computers hadn't been turned off for almost two months. He had two computers set up in his office, and whenever the boss wasn't around, he was playing games. Out of his 5,000 RMB monthly salary, he only kept 300 for himself and dumped all the rest into Tencent games. He had to go to work at around 6 in the morning, and often played games until 5 AM. Because of all this, the girlfriend he was ready to marry ended up breaking up with him. At first, we found it incredible, not even knowing where to begin making fun of it. When we asked him why, he first said he liked playing games, and then mentioned that it was like he was poisoned—the first thing he thought of when he woke up every day was rushing to grind the game. Then we brought up how domestic mobile games use crazy p2w tactics and disgusting events to boost user retention. This so-called gaming doesn't serve any recreational or entertaining purpose. Once you take these mobile games as goals to pursue in your heart, you become their captive. You aren't playing the game; the game is playing you. These practices that prey on human psychological weaknesses are truly disgusting, just like exploiting a gambler's urge to break even. After that, the topic shifted back to that bro, and we started advising him to give up gaming, pay more attention to reality, stop sending all his money to Tencent, or save up to go traveling—road trips were best. Then he said he once got into a car accident while driving and looking at his phone, so he only rode a bicycle ever since. But after buying a phone mount for his bike, he got distracted by his phone again, flew down a flight of stairs, and ended up hospitalized for several days. We, who were just advising him, fell completely silent upon hearing about his "epic achievements," not even knowing where to start roasting him. Someone resignedly said that only military service or Professor Yang could save him. If the story ended here, it would just be another typical example of the media constantly shitting on how "video games ruin people's ambitions." But the twist was unexpected: he said he used to be in the military. He started talking about his past, serving in Xinjiang as a second lieutenant and platoon leader. But shit went down during his very first patrol leading a team, and 3 people died. He could never forgive himself, and afterward fell into severe depression. The military doctor said he wasn't fit for service anymore, so he was honorably discharged with deep regret. He slowly recounted how he had led a squad on patrol, not expecting a large truck to barrel toward them. At the time, he noticed the truck was acting abnormally, but he didn't pay much attention to his teammates' warnings, and then the disaster happened. He felt like he had killed his own comrades, because among the three of them, the youngest was only 18. Seeing his comrades' parents arrive at the base and seeing what they looked like when they saw their son... it just shattered his heart. So he took his severance pay and some of his own savings, scraped together about 100,000 RMB, and handed it to his comrades' parents, telling them it was the official death compensation. After being discharged, he cut off all contact with everyone from the military; he didn't even dare to have any contact. Whenever he saw his own parents, he couldn't help but think of the scene of his comrades' parents coming to the base, and then he couldn't stop blaming himself. He said with agonizing sorrow that he wished he had been the one to die instead. That vivid memory constantly tormented him. Right after leaving the army, he pulled quite a few stupid stunts trying to "release" himself, but seeing his heartbroken parents made him give up. At this point, another group member chimed in with his own past military experience. Back in 2002, there was an accident where his squad was dispatched, not knowing the explosion was a terrorist attack. In the end, he was the only one who survived, and he watched with his own eyes as a comrade was blown to pieces. He said being a special forces operative isn't all that great. When you first become one, you feel pretty badass, but gradually you realize you're the actual sinner because you've killed so many people, your hands stained with human blood, with no way to seek redemption, leaving you utterly lost. His tone was slightly self-deprecating as he tried to help the previous bro look on the bright side. Honestly, just hearing it felt profoundly shocking. I don't know how he climbed out of that shadow, or if he even ever did. Maybe time blurs everything, or maybe even a decade later, he might still wake up terrified from nightmares recalling the miserable deaths of his comrades. Only those who have experienced war understand how precious peace is—much like how German and British soldiers walked out of the trenches on Christmas night to celebrate together and exchange gifts. I didn't quite understand these truths before; I was obsessed with all kinds of war games, and felt completely confused by the confusion, fear, guilt, and madness of the characters in *Band of Brothers*, *Hacksaw Ridge*, or *The Pacific*. But contact with these guys seemed to connect those lingering, fragmented shadows in my mind. I thought of a movie directed by Ang Lee, *Billy Lynn's Long Halftime Walk*. To be honest, this movie doesn't have any grand scenes, nor any thrilling plots; it even looks like a low-budget, indie film. But ordinary people probably find it hard to understand the film's sense of loss regarding where soldiers belong. Not every hero needs to be burned to death, and not every hero has to sacrifice themselves to plug a machine gun nest. On the battlefield, redemption is always infinitely more precious than slaughter. And behind the scenes, where the lights and flowers cannot reach, there are even more unsung "heroes" and less-than-glamorous sides, a truth that we ordinary folks might never understand. This reminded me of a video I watched before, mentioning that many US soldiers in the Middle East suffered from a psychological illness called Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). For effective treatment, experts would use electronic devices to constantly replay the traumatic scenes right before the eyes of the recovering soldiers. I remember the scene replayed to the patient was him driving a Humvee armored vehicle, when suddenly an RPG hit the vehicle right in front of him, and the instantaneous explosion directly flipped that Humvee up into the air. To be honest, some experiences, when replicated through secondhand text, images, or audio, can never truly reach the feeling of experiencing it yourself. We will never be able to empathize with the mindset of these unsung heroes at the time, and it's best we never get the chance to feel it. But when they are emotionally fragile, when they leave the military, they don't just magically vanish from this unfriendly world. I also hope more people pay attention to this issue, so that at least after suffering trauma, they can feel that the limited world they touch isn't entirely about slaughter and loss. After understanding all this, honestly, it's hard not to question the meaning of life. Ordinary people fight over trivial interests in this world like ants fighting over a withered leaf, hurting each other over scraps. Deception, hypocrisy, apathy, jealousy, hatred—can these really withstand the test of real life and death? Are they really worth fighting over? Is there really any point in crying, laughing, rejoicing, and getting angry? When a portion of this world is fighting desperately for responsibility and duty, aren't we wasting our lives away just surviving like parasites, doing a huge disservice to them? Then what the hell is our shit-tier life even for? So, why do we play CS? Because we only have to face a virtual electronic world, venting our violent desires at will without having to bear the consequences; because we don't have to experience the pain of parting through life and death, nor face the daily dread and anxiety; and even more because we don't have to make a choice—the choice to become the soldier General Patton talked about. That soldier might be you, and your best destination is to be shot dead by the very last bullet in your final battle, because you are the last one, and after you die, the war will end and no one else will have to sacrifice. Otherwise, if you survive the brutal struggle among your own kind, you will spend a life plagued by illness, nightmares, confusion, and pain with blood-stained hands, just like the people in the stories. Peace does not come easily. Treasure your gaming while you can. Hoping that the scenes in games never appear in reality, and saluting all the brave soldiers fighting on the front lines of counter-terrorism.

Even later, when I was a bit older, I started liking duelling people, going head-to-head with other delinquent youths at the local LAN cafe, totally destroying their confidence. Then even later than that, I played deathmatch on 175 and DouKe for about a year, getting pounded into the dirt by all sorts of pros. translation_en: Back when we were kids, the two of us would happily ditch school and run off to the internet cafe to play CS, totally carefree like we didn't have a single worry in the world. But after starting middle school, everything changed. Some guy in our class bragged about his CF skills every single day, and to flex his wealth he even bought her a battle axe, stealing her away from me. So, she switched to CF, leaving me all alone. After school, the gloomy sky had already started raining, and upon finding out she went to play CF, I was practically breaking down. I walked home in the rain, only to get completely splashed with muddy water by some asshole on a bike. It was that guy riding the bike. "Country bumpkin, keep playing your dumbass CS!" he yelled, and sped off. There was no emotion on my face, but it hurt like hell inside. That night, I cried for hours. ----- Eight years later, she'd grown tall and hot, but seemed to have given up on her education and was playing in some internet cafe CF tournament. She'd lost several matches in a row, and a few beads of sweat hung on the tip of her cute nose. Her teammate next to her was a squeaker playing on a Private Second Class account who didn't even have a single RMB-cash item. They were gonna lose this round. I saw her, walked over and sat down, and chased the kid away. But she was too focused to even notice me. Four people were already dead on the field, leaving just me, a SAS holding an AK-74, in a clutch situation. I peeked out, one-tapped an enemy sticking their head out, and continued spraying down the enemies coming to pinch me. Then, relying on my movement, I dodged Fire Kirin bullets and one-tapped him with the Glock's 12 remaining rounds. I picked up the Fire Kirin and clutched the round for them. She took off her headset, looked at me with eyes full of surprise, and asked, "Where have you been all these years? You've gotten so good, I've been waiting for you in CF." I looked at her, deadpan, and said, "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive (CS:GO) expands upon the team-based action gameplay that it pioneered when the franchise launched 12 years ago. CS:GO features new maps, characters, weapons, and delivers updated versions of the classic CS content (de_dust, etc.). In addition, CS:GO will introduce new game modes, matchmaking, leaderboards, and more. 'Counter-Strike took the gaming industry by surprise when the unassuming mod became the most played online PC action game in the world almost immediately after its release in August 1999,' said Doug Lombardi at Valve. 'For the past 12 years, it has been one of the most-played games in the world, headlining competitive gaming tournaments and selling over 25 million units worldwide across the franchise. CS:GO promises to expand on CS' award-winning gameplay and deliver it to players on the PC as well as next gen consoles and the Mac.'" Tears streamed down her face, and she came with me to CS:GO. Then she opened cases and lost all her fucking money.

translation_en: Uh, I'm honored to do a review for CS:GO. I'm post-00s, yep, exactly 18. I probably first got into the CS series when I was 5 or 6. Back then, we lived in a single-story house, my sister was in high school, and we had an old PC at home. Besides built-in games like Minesweeper, it had CS 1.6 on it. Yeah, I was an annoying kid back then, playing CS every day. Then we moved and got a new computer. But you know what? I still remember. In CS 1.6, there was a bot named Cavin. He was special, really special. Back in elementary school, I used to get bullied a lot and looked down upon by my family. So, I liked to talk to this bot. Why him? Because all the other bots bought guns randomly—this round they buy an AUG, next round a UMP45, and the round after that, an AWP. But this bot named Cavin was different. As CT he buys an M4. Someone's probably gonna ask, "What if you play as T?" Yep, he buys an AK, and if he finds an M4 he'll drop the AK. What if he's broke? Yep, a P90!!! So, for a while, I thought he wasn't a bot, he was an actual person, and I'd pour out all my miserable feelings to this bot. And back then, I'd press Y and type out Pinyin, letter by letter. I still haven't forgotten him. But what creeps me out is that other post-00s kids around me have no idea what CS even is. Even worse, some think it's software like PS or AE. They said they only knew CF. And I went through a period of being ostracized by these people. Yep, in elementary and middle school, I was treated like a joke, so I had no choice but to blend into the CF scene. Yeah, getting isolated just because you play a different game—it's that simple and brutal. Then I almost forgot about CS, forgot that period of venting my bitter tears to a bot. But now, I'm in high school—well, not quite high school, it's a "3+2" program. And now there are one or two like-minded friends around me. I'm so damn grateful I didn't miss out on my current school. Even though it's not a real high school, I'm having a good enough time. But I also have a friend who's always trash-talking CSGO, saying how bad it is. But he hasn't been through what I have, so of course he doesn't get it. Now, I've got a lot of friends, including some foreign ones. Days playing CSGO are just really different. When playing CF, almost nobody tells jokes, and you've got people looking for "husbands," "wives," or "big sisters," and every single one of them is just after WeChat red packets. In CSGO, there aren't that many toxic flamers—though they exist, just don't take it to heart—or people messing around ruining relationships for loot, and no random kick-happy assholes. Just yesterday, some guy said something toxic, and not just the Chinese players, but even the foreigners, all started chewing him out. That toxic dude got too embarrassed to keep playing and left. After that, all 13 people in the lobby just started cheering. I switched teams and could hear cheers all over the voice chat. It just feels really different. But playing competitive, you occasionally run into some pretty trash teammates and enemies. When you pull off some insane kills, they don't really react, but when you suddenly drop a massive amount of kills, they think you're cheating. But whatever, if you start arguing with them, then you've got a huge problem—it always ends on a bad note. Look at it from another angle: you're not cheating, but people think you are—doesn't that make you feel like a badass? Besides, no matter how much they report you, it's useless; the innocent stay clean, the guilty stay dirty. Now, if you actually *are* cheating and refuse to admit it, well, you can't blame them for coming after you. I bought it when it was 24 bucks, and now it's free. I'll just pretend I bought a prime global version. But you know, I wanna ask Gaben, does he not plan on making L4D3? CSGO is free now, so why not release L4D3 and keep milking our money?

translation_en: He was a Global Elite in CS:GO. Skilled, with insane game sense. P90? One-tapped a SG 553 across the map. AK-47? Running one-taps straight to the head. AWP? Anyone caught in his scope didn't stand a chance. Negev? Ever seen a 1v5 clutch? Desert Eagle? Used only the Deagle all game, got MVP every round, and a 16:0 sweep. Countless people fell to his gun, countless people called him a hacker, but he knew it was his true skill. Because other than himself, nobody knew the hours he spent practicing his aim, nobody knew how he played against a dozen bots to train his game sense. Going from a negative K/D to over 3, almost 4—only he knew the blood, sweat, and tears behind it. He had a 100-game win streak in competitive. Yet, he couldn't stay lost in the game forever. Pushed by his parents, he finally got a girlfriend. At the same time, he got a job. Since he only got home at night and was exhausted from work, he stopped playing competitive mode entirely. His record froze at a 100-game win streak. Every day when he got home, he'd only play CS:GO for an hour—only by playing with his "brothers" could he shed the stress and misery of the day. His girlfriend never understood why he locked himself in the room every night, laughing and chatting. Since they had two computers at home, one each, she had no idea what he was actually doing. Normally, he wasn't that nice to her because he wasn't a talkative guy, and she wasn't one either. But the way he silently took care of her when she was sick, and laid out her heavy clothes and umbrella when it got cold, really won her over. Just like that, a few months passed. Until one day, she learned that because of work, he had to work overtime for a whole month, couldn't come home at noon, and wouldn't get back until midnight. She took a month off specifically to take care of him. After all, her salary wasn't much, and she genuinely felt bad for him. She brought him lunch every day, and at night she'd wait until 11:40 to start cooking, serving him until he went to sleep. Yet, she was always curious about the laughter coming from his room every night; she wanted to know why. Finally, one noon, she turned on his computer and found only one game on the desktop—CS:GO. Driven by curiosity, she opened the game... A month later, he opened CS:GO for the first time in forever, but something felt off—his rank had dropped from Global Elite to Silver I. He checked his match history and found that his most recent games were all losses. His K/D had plummeted from 3.8 to 1.2. He knew only he used his account, so all of this had to be the work of the woman cooking in the kitchen. "Did you do this?" he pointed at the Silver I icon on the computer screen. She looked a bit nervous, twisting the hem of her shirt with both hands: "I—I did it..." "Why were you messing with my computer?" She sensed a hint of seriousness and anger in his tone—he was always exceptionally gentle with her. "Because—because I wanted to understand you... I wanted to make you happy too... I didn't want you to only be happy when you were with your friends." By the end, her voice was so soft she could barely hear it herself. "Ah!" She was startled by the sudden move—he pinned her against the wall (*kabedon*), using his left index finger to lift her chin: "Does that mean you've met all of them? Chatted with them?" "Y-Yeah..." She looked a bit flustered. "How many competitive matches have you lost?" "Probably 100..." She lowered her head as low as it could go, feeling as though the next moment a slap would sting across her face. "Did you get flamed really bad?" She was a college graduate of course she understood words like "noob," "f*ck you," and "f*cking noob" coming from foreigners, not to mention domestic insults. She refused to back down; she wanted to fight back and prove she could, but she couldn't even see the enemies before she died. Every time she lost, she would secretly cry for a bit to vent her frustrations. Thinking of this, she nodded. "Wanna play and prove to them you can do it?" "Yes!" For once, her answer was unusually loud. "Fine, I'll teach you then." Just like that, he started training her in CS:GO, teaching her aim, map layouts, and everything he could possibly teach. Along the way, their relationship grew even closer. He changed his ID to NoobTeam No1. She changed hers to NoobTeam No2. Every time, he only used 50% of his skill, letting her be the main character. Finally, she successfully ranked up to Double AK. Until one day, she asked him, "Where'd you get this knife? It looks so cool!" "Oh, this? I unboxed it!" "How do you open them?" "Remember the cases that drop after matches? You just buy keys and open them. Like this. But it's all RNG." "Oh! Is that how it works? I've got over a hundred cases here, let's open them all!" Just like that, the two of them opened cases and blew their entire life savings. "Welcome to Counter-Strike Derank: Global Case Opening!" That was reportedly what the two of them told the bank teller while withdrawing their very last bit of savings.

translation_en: [h1][b] Counter-Strike: Global Irritation.[/b] [/h1] [code]Attention! This review is merely the author's opinion, which he is not forcing upon you! You're free to stick to your own. If you disagree with anything, leave a comment and we'll discuss it! [/code] [h1] ✎ [u] Foreword: [/u] [/h1] It's hard to find someone in the gaming world who doesn't know about it or hasn't heard of it. A legendary game that made the journey from a "Half-Life" mod to one of the biggest esports titles. It has always been wildly popular – I remember playing CS 1.6 on LAN with friends for hours on end, getting a ton of emotion and enjoyment out of it. With technological advances, they decided to improve the outer shell of "Counter-Strike" as well. "Source," released a bit later, was met quite coldly by most of the audience, but it was still a solid product. And then in 2012, "Global Offensive" came out, which is what this is about. It brought some improvements, but it has more than "enough" flaws. [h1] ✔ [u] Pros: [/u] [/h1] ➜ Graphics. The game looks good, although for games like this, top-tier graphics aren't even necessary. ➜ Gameplay. Still as simple, but so addictive. You can play every day and you won't get bored of it! When did killing an enemy ever become a boring activity?) ➜ Sounds. The weapon sounds are good and realistic, and the ambient sounds are great too. The only thing that sometimes misleads you is the volume of footsteps, even if the enemy is running from very far away. That is, assuming you have good headphones and aren't deaf. ➜ Foreign language tutor. While playing, you're bound to pick up some foreign words. The variety is huge: Turkish, Polish, German, and some of you might even brush up on your English. [h1] ≈[u] Controversial Qualities: [/u][/h1] ➜ Skin cases. Now, to make your weapon look nicely painted, you don't drop textures into the root folder, you have to buy them. Sure, it looks nice, but overall it's useless. And if you find out the price of some of them, you might start doubting the mental faculties of the people who buy them (that same "Howl" or "Fire Serpent" – essentially it's just a piece of code that won't improve your aim by a single bit) or get disappointed in your own financial situation. Plus, now you have to pay for graffiti and it runs out, they introduced gloves... Waiting for colored smoke! ➜ Operations. Pretty fun events where you can test yourself and get a reward. Except they come out extremely rarely and they cost money. ➜ Ranking system and matchmaking. The idea isn't bad. Only the players don't always match them: boosters, derankers, smurfs – the game is chock-full of them. But sometimes you actually get players of your own level. It's also worth noting the matchmaking. Playing at "Gold Nova Master," I frequently got "LEM" and "Silver" players on the same team (I could understand it if they were in a party, but no – just totally random people). And way too many people are obsessed with ranks. ➜ Modes and maps. They removed some game modes (VIP) and a whole bunch of maps, which really bums me out as an old-timer and 1.6 veteran. But they added a couple of new ones that slightly make up for the sting. [h1] ✘ [u]Cons: [/u][/h1] ➜ Cheaters and non-working VAC. I often ask myself – is there even an anti-cheat? Every other game – you're playing against some life-crippled loser whose eyes are so crossed and fingers so crooked that they can't play without cheats. Reports don't do shit anymore. Although back in the day, when the grass was greener, I actually saw bans being handed out, but that was a long time ago. ➜ Hitboxes and wallbangs. Shot someone in the leg, but got a headstone? Landed 12 hits for 99hp? Welcome to the club! You can shoot through a concrete wall, but not through a barrel. Or completely by accident, wallbang a jumping enemy in the head from 3km away, right through your teammate's leg. ➜ Community. Behold – the most repulsive thing about this game! These are the people who got tired of Dota and came to ruin lives in CS: ● Cheaters; ● Inadequates and autists; ● People who know your family members better than you do; ● Kids; ● Kick-happy assholes. (They vote-kick everyone and for everything. Play well / Play poorly. Nice skin / Ugly skin. Liked your nick or picture / Didn't like it, and other illogical reasons); ● Wannabe streamers with ten subscribers just like them (who will definitely report you); ● Commandos (people with a score of 0-0-17 who tell you why you're a NOOB!) ● Babysitters (people who start punishing you for a wrong move or word by shooting you in the head); ● People with cheat-phrenia (they see cheats everywhere they aren't and live by the rule "If you play better than me – you're a cheater!"); ● Melomaniacs (doesn't matter if it's competitive or not, you'll be forced to listen to this wannabe DJ's favorite tracks); ● Foreigners. Finding out you're from Russia ("SUKA BLET!!!"), they start shitting on you and straight-up tilting you, blaming you for all sins even if you're single-handedly carrying the whole circus – "You stupid Russian!" But overall, nationality doesn't matter, because CIS region players aren't any better. ● Billy Milligan. And remember – you can easily run into all of these personalities comfortably coexisting in a single person. To save myself a five-page rant on this topic, I'll just say this to you: "Welcome to the Zoo!". There are decent players, but their percentage is negligible. It's better to play with your own trusted team so your nerves don't fry from the sheer incomprehension. [h1] ➥[u] Conclusion.[/u][/h1] Valve has every opportunity to turn this game into a masterpiece, yet they don't do it! They only release cosmetic updates that nobody asked for and mostly just make you laugh. I get it, making money off everything is profitable, but you also need to consider what the players want. I can't wholeheartedly recommend this game, but I can't say it's complete shit either (I play regularly, even though I get severely disappointed sometimes). Give it a try, and then you can decide for yourself whether the game is worth your time and nerves or not. Wishing you adequate teammates and opponents, but don't forget about your own behavior. And don't use cheats!) [h1][b] Easy-peasy, lemon squeezy! [/b][/h1] [url=steamcommunity.com/id/your_nevermore/recommended/570/] ➜ Dota 2 Review. translation_en: Do I like the game? Do I like Counter Strike? YES, SO MUCH. I've been playing it since version 1.3. Do I recommend this Counter? Global Offensive? Much to my regret... no. After almost 1500 hours of gameplay I don't even know where to start with this review. The game is BROKEN. 1. The anticheat. A fucking joke of an anticheat. WH, spinbots, aimbot, autobunny, and I won't go on because it makes me want to bang my head against the keyboard. 2. Wonderful servers that swallow more bullets than a trucker smokes cigarettes. 3. This game is more of a multi-language insult simulator than a shooter (cyka blyat, filho da puta... one, two, three, name them all). 4. Matchmaking is garbage and the ranking system is too. One match it pairs you with people 3 or 4 ranks below and the next it pairs you against the best in the world. They should take notes from other games; seasons, a points system that's simple and understandable for all players... This is a game where RANK MEANS NOTHING. I've played with and against Global Elites who haven't held an AK in their life, and then I've run into Master Guardian Sheriffs who played insanely well. Smurfs? Hacks? There'll always be that distrust because of the great anticheat the game has (point 1 of the review). 5. Valve doesn't give a shit about the game. They focus more on dropping loot boxes with skins ($$$$$$$$$$$$$$$) and shit maps nobody plays (like CANALS) than on fixing the game. And this last point is the worst. Valve DOES NOT care about the game. Every now and then they drop some patch like: "we changed some shit sound that didn't affect anything... We tweaked a map nobody plays... Let's nerf this pistol because it's too much... (for Valve, nerf = take it out of the meta and make it completely useless) BASICALLY, BEATING AROUND THE BUSH." A game that is so popular right now, generates so much money, has more and more impact and major competitions. It's really sad that the people making workshop content invest more time and "care" for the game than the actual developer. I play it, I like it, and I keep playing it, but it's not as fun as it used to be. Something that already happened to me back in the day with LoL and I ended up quitting it. And it's just a pile of bullshit that makes every match I enter fill my head with thoughts like: "will there be a cheater ruining the match? Will I get a toxic team? Any trolls? AFK? A server that works worse than the Windows troubleshooter?" I understand more and more why people completely quit this game to move on to others, like PUBG or Rainbow Six Siege. Some people will have the exact opposite opinion of what I'm saying in this review, and I respect that. The game is cool and I like it, I'm not saying it's not. I'd love to give it a thumbs up, but I can't; I guess the bad outweighs the good. Besides, nowadays there are better shooters, more original, more fun AND ABOVE ALL BETTER CARED FOR, and since we spend money on the game the bare minimum is for it to work properly. I've been playing Counter Strike for almost my whole life (for better or for worse I'll keep doing it) and I think this is one of the worst versions. Where have those wonderful times of 1.6 gone...

translation_en: Hello community. I don't even know how to start. I now have something like 1300 hours in this game and for the first time in my life I'm ashamed of having spent time on a game. + The game principle of combining the simplest character animations with the simplest hitboxes is top-notch. Germans who basically wish you the worst things in life or insult you otherwise, wishing you the shortest life possible and all diseases that don't even exist yet. Oh, and everyone is retarded, of course. EVERYONE! Except the one doing the insulting. Russians who basically do the exact same thing as Germans, just with a bamboo internet connection and a €5 headset. Since Valve manages to sell knife skins for $700+, there apparently isn't enough money to do something about hackers. No! Quite the opposite, the community itself then gets to decide via a so-called Overwatch whether a reported player gets banned or not. But first you need a certain number of competitive match wins to even do that. And when you've finally managed that and think you can make a difference, you end up in a window where a match plays out in real-time. This means if someone is using a subtle aimbot, you wouldn't even be able to recognize it. BUT HEY! There's always the beloved console. You open it, type *demoui* and then you can watch the whole thing in slow motion and control the time yourself. But even that is a fight every time. Sometimes the console won't open during it and you have to restart the game. And repeat that until it works by sheer luck. So, you assume you've spotted a hacker and reach the end of the *Overwatch*. You can then select what you think the person is using and what not. Once you submit this report, you get slapped with the same little text every time: thank you for stepping up as an Overwatch investigator. No reward, no nothing. NOTHING. This means you're doing the work for a game that makes millions and you don't even get anything for it. No XP, no luck with weapon skins, no, absolutely nothing! And in the end, 90% of the players don't get banned because nobody bothers with this shit anymore. Understandably. And to top it all off, that's exactly why the game is unplayable. In competitive, there is almost always a hacker. Even on so-called community servers, there are people using aimbots just to look cool. You can only hope that the admin of the respective community server is active and bans hackers. Now you have to put yourself in the shoes of honest players who have 2000+ hours and practice every day to master the game even better. And then some fucking 8-year-old kid comes along screaming: BLYAD, BLYAD, BLYAD, RUUUUSKKYYYY, BOOY, RUSKYYY, VODKAVODKAVODKAAA and just wipes that player out, just like that. And afterwards an EZEZZEZEZEZEZEZEZEZEZEZ (Easy) follows in the chat. Reporting does fuck all anyway since there's no real anti-cheat. And 2 hours ago he just got kicked from a TS and insulted as the son of a sex worker because he didn't fucking kill the whole 5-man team by himself. Afterwards, he quickly wants to play a cozy match on a community server because things still seem fine over there. But no. As soon as he joins, people start insulting each other in chat in all kinds of languages. Fine, voice chat off, he carries on anyway. He gets a few sick kills, is pretty high up on the scoreboard, everything is going well. And then it starts. A: A hacker totally destroys him and then spams the chat with EZEZZEZEZEZEZEZEZ NOOB BLYAD. B: People start wishing him all sorts of diseases again and send him friend requests just to tear him apart on Steam afterwards (because people don't get banned there either, by the way). C: It stays at A and he just puts up with it until his nerves are completely shot. You want a game you can only endure on alcohol and hard drugs? You've come to the right place! You want a game that drives you to suicide? BUY IT!! And while you're at it, buy all the crates Valve keeps releasing with great new skins inside. The keys only cost €2 and a few cents because otherwise it would be too cheap. And when you've dumped €200 into it and opened all the crates, your best drop is worth €4. I've already pumped €600+ into this game and look at my inventory. No knife. No cool weapon skins. NO, I had to plaster my weapons with so-called stickers so they wouldn't look too boring. (Those only cost €1 a piece, after all). The game is simply a nightmare. Thanks for reading, I'm gonna go hang myself now.
